text.enUS: A Bloodstained Journal Page. A torn, bloodstained parchment examined during the investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle. A few words remain legible through the thick blood, and Commander Althea Ebonlocke asks that its handwriting be checked. Commander Althea Ebonlocke keeps a vigilant watch over Darkshire and asks for the handwriting on this torn, blood-spattered page to be examined. Despite the thick blood, a few words remain legible enough for Clerk Daltry to compare with the Town Registry.

A Bump in the Road. Trackmaster Zherin looks after the track at the Mirage Raceway, and the animals out on the Shimmering Flats have grown big enough that their numbers must be kept down before they wander onto it. You are asked to thin out Saltstone Basilisks, Crystalhides and Gazers. A basilisk once collided with a racer belonging to the goblins, the Red Thunder, and in the aftermath Kronkrider took Zherin on to look after the track. Zherin cannot say what the animals out on the Shimmering Flats are eating to get so big, only that their numbers have to be kept down, or one will stray onto the course mid-race. Clearing wreckage is bad enough, and Zherin would rather not pick it out of burnt animal parts as well.

A Bundle of Hides. Jahan Hawkwing sends cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff for leatherworking. The delivery takes you across central Kalimdor and introduces the Crossroads wind rider roost. Hunters bring game hides and meat to the Crossroads, where Jahan Hawkwing gathers pelts from across the Barrens. The outposts cannot process every raw hide, so he asks travelers to carry them west to Thunder Bluff. Master leatherworkers there can turn the pelts into gear for the Horde.

A Bundle of Trouble. At Eastvale Logging Camp, A Bundle of Trouble begins with timber left in the woods and a deadline near. Supervisor Raelen needs the cut wood brought back before the shipment falls behind. Supervisor Raelen has a shipment of timber due soon. Eastvale Logging Camp cuts wood for Stormwind, and her crew has fallen behind schedule. With the deadline close, Raelen needs the timber sent on its way.

A Clue to Sanders' Treasure. In Westfall, a weathered parchment carries the trail of notorious pirate Captain Sanders. It marks the second step in a treasure hunt across the bluffs and coastlines. After you follow Captain Sanders' first treasure map, you find a parchment that points farther inland into Westfall. The scrawled note sends you east from the coast, up the bluffs toward the main road. Near crumbling stone ruins and an abandoned chimney, an old barrel marks the next place Sanders hid a clue, drawing seekers deeper into the troubled farmlands.

A Curious Pair. A Curious Pair begins when Trevan Rol notices an unusual duo passing through the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Under the banner of the Earthen Ring, a tauren was seen traveling alongside a high elf—an alliance rare enough in Horde territory to prompt immediate suspicion. The Sepulcher is a grim waystation where strangers are scrutinized carefully, especially those claiming diplomatic business. When two representatives purporting to belong to the Earthen Ring passed along the road, local scout Trevan Rol caught sight of them. While a tauren walking under the shamanic order's mantle surprised no one, his cloaked companion struck the Forsaken as exceedingly bizarre: an unmistakable high elf.

A Dark Threat Looms. Suspicious of sabotage at the Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII dispatches a courier north into the perilous Wetlands to have a sample of volatile powder examined. The courier must navigate the treacherous highway past the Algaz Gate to deliver the sample to demolition expert Ashlan Stonesmirk at Dun Modr. Following disturbances around the Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII is brought a strange smelling powder from a suspicious barrel near the dam's eastern ramp, where he had spotted Dark Iron sappers. Recognizing the potential for catastrophic sabotage, Hinderweir suspects the substance is a refined explosive designed to shatter dwarven masonry. Lacking specialized chemical testing equipment at the dam site, he insists on consulting a military demolitionist before jumping to conclusions.

A Dark Threat Looms. This quest marks the moment an investigation into sabotage at the Stonewrought Dam uncovers physical evidence of foul play. After discovering a suspicious barrel hidden near the massive dwarven structure, adventurers retrieve a sample of strange smelling powder to bring before Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. The Stonewrought Dam stands as a monumental triumph of dwarven engineering, holding back the vast waters of the loch. However, whispers of sabotage have drawn scrutiny to the surrounding shoreline. Tucked away near the water's edge, an out-of-place barrel holds an ominous substance—a strange, pungent powder that clearly does not belong to standard dam maintenance supplies.

A Dark Threat Looms. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII fears that the Stonewrought Dam is the next target of Dark Iron dwarf aggression following attacks in the Wetlands. With most of the dam's defensive garrison reassigned elsewhere, adventurers are sent to investigate Dark Iron sappers lurking around the eastern ramp. The Stonewrought Dam is one of the crowning engineering feats of Ironforge, holding back the vast waters of Loch Modan. However, with the ongoing conflicts across Khaz Modan and beyond, much of the dam's security detail was reassigned to the Alliance Front. This troop shortage leaves Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII and his skeleton crew largely defenseless against coordinated assaults, right as enemy activity creeps closer to the colossal structure.

A Dark Threat Looms. Following the discovery of suspicious powder at the Stonewrought Dam, Ashlan Stonesmirk in Dun Modr identifies the substance as unstable Seaforium. Capable of catastrophic destruction if it comes into contact with water, the powder poses an immediate danger to the region and the nearby dwarven realm. Stonesmirk concocts a disarming colloid and sends word back to Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII to defuse the disaster. Examining the samples brought from the Stonewrought Dam, Ashlan Stonesmirk immediately recognizes the telltale silver crystals and distinct odor of Seaforium. While inert in dry conditions, Seaforium reacts violently with moisture—a terrifying reality for a dam holding back the waters of Loch Modan. Ashlan warns that an unchecked explosion from such a compound could blow Ironforge out of the mountain.

A Dark Threat Looms. This quest is a critical step in defending the Stonewrought Dam from a suspected Dark Iron plot. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII tasks adventurers with gathering rare chemical and organic reagents from across Loch Modan to concoct a defusing mixture. Without these components, the defenders will be unable to neutralize the explosives planted beneath the massive stonework. To counteract the volatile explosive concoctions used by Dark Iron saboteurs, Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII relies on an unorthodox chemical neutralizer. Rather than simple water or dampening sand, neutralizing Dark Iron blast powders requires a potent slurry made from indigenous Forest Lurker venom, a tear extracted from the crocolisks inhabiting the Loch, and a Mo'grosh crystal. Each component brings unique reactive properties necessary to render dwarven demolition charges completely inert.

A Dark Threat Looms. A desperate emergency mission given by Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII to prevent the destruction of the Stonewrought Dam. Dark Iron saboteurs have planted an explosive Seaforium charge deep below the waterline, threatening to shatter one of the greatest engineering marvels of the dwarven kingdom. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII spotted Dark Iron Insurgents swimming toward the base of the Stonewrought Dam carrying a massive keg of explosive Seaforium. Without Mountaineers nearby to intervene, the infiltrators secured the weapon directly against the dam's underwater foundation. A breach would unleash the entire volume of the loch into the lowlands below, causing catastrophic flooding and crippling dwarven trade and travel across the region.

A Difficult Path. A Difficult Path marks the formal beginning of a Forsaken paladin's training in Deathknell. After dealing with the mindless undead rising from the crypts, newly awakened champions of the Light are directed to Aramis Hammerhand within the village church to confront the agonizing reality of wielding holy energy in undeath. When a freshly awakened Forsaken paladin finishes culling the feral undead outside the crypt, Shadow Priest Sarvis hands over an unexpected delivery. The Consecrated Scroll radiates holy energy so intensely that the shadow priest visibly recoils, bluntly asking the bearer to step aside. To a practitioner of shadow and decay, the very aura of the Holy Light feels like an open flame.

A Donation of Wool. A Donation of Wool is a material requisition organized by the Gnomeregan Exiles to gather essential textile supplies. Displaced from their technological home city, the exiled gnomes rely on sixty pieces of wool cloth from generous adventurers across the realm to sustain their community. Contributing to the drive grants formal recognition among the gnome refugees. Following the fall of Gnomeregan to trogg invaders and radioactive contamination, the surviving gnomes found themselves displaced from their high-tech metropolis. Operating as refugees primarily hosted by their dwarven cousins in Ironforge, the Gnomeregan Exiles face severe logistical strain. Routine material drives for basic goods like cloth are essential to keep their people clothed, supplied, and organized while surviving outside their ancestral halls.

A Dusty Unsent Letter. A Dusty Unsent Letter is a forgotten parchment recovered from an old footlocker in Westfall. It offers vital proof that the elusive Stalvan Mistmantle lived in Moonbrook before his disappearance. While searching for the past of the mysterious Stalvan Mistmantle, investigators discover this unsent letter tucked away inside an old footlocker in Moonbrook. Darkshire's town registry still listed his last address as the Moonbrook Schoolhouse, and Clerk Daltry wanted word on whether he had truly lived there. This unmailed correspondence provides the missing link, confirming that Stalvan resided in the Westfall township for a time. Yet its presence also raises ominous questions, as retrieving it disturbs a vengeful Forlorn Spirit that guards the remnants of Stalvan's past with bitter malice.

A Dwarf and His Tools. Prospector Ryedol warns that Dark Iron dwarves, looking like the Shadowforge clan, are all around. They just attacked the dig site where Ryedol worked, and Ryedol wants the lucky pick back. Dark Iron dwarves of the Shadowforge clan, by Prospector Ryedol's account, have attacked the excavation site where Ryedol worked. They killed nearly everyone, Ryedol's boss Hammertoe among them, and Ryedol barely escaped with life intact. The site lies to the north of Ryedol's position.

A Dynamite Plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket is eager to put dynamite to work in Stormwind. The inventive tinkerer in the Dwarven District has heard talk of industrial sabotage and wants a supply of coarse dynamite to begin her plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket, a gnome engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District, welcomes talk of industrial sabotage. Rather than urge caution, she asks passing mercenaries to bring her a bundle of coarse dynamite.

A Faded Journal Page. A Faded Journal Page is an old parchment retrieved from an upstairs chest in Marshal Haggard's secluded home in Elwynn Forest. It serves as a vital clue in unraveling the dark history surrounding Stalvan Mistmantle. Left behind inside an old trunk when retired Marshal Haggard took residence near the eastern border of Elwynn Forest, this weathered parchment sat undisturbed for years. With Haggard's failing eyesight preventing him from deciphering it, the page remained neglected until adventurers digging into the legend of Stalvan Mistmantle retrieved it.

text.enUS: A Favor for Evershine. To secure a cask of Evershine for Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot, an adventurer must first lend a hand to Brewnall Village. Brewer Rejold Barleybrew refuses to part with his liquor until the dangerous predators roaming the nearby snowdrifts are thinned out. Rejold Barleybrew has the cask of Evershine that Pilot Bellowfiz requires, but he is in no hurry to surrender his prized brew for free. Rather than asking for coin, Rejold asks for protection. The wild beasts of western Dun Morogh—ravenous Ice Claw Bears, thick-hided Elder Crag Boars, and prowling Snow Leopards—wander uncomfortably close to Brewnall Village, creating constant distraction and peril for the locals.

A Fine Egg. Curgle Cranklehop speaks of the fine egg, which stands a chance of hatching free of the Gordunni ogres' evil incantations. Curgle Cranklehop describes a fine egg as one with a good chance of hatching untouched by the wicked chanting of the Gordunni ogres, provided conditions are ideal.

A Fine Mess. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan, an injured goblin named Kernobee lies battered among troggs after being ambushed by Dark Iron dwarves. Rescuing him uncovers unsettling intelligence about Dark Iron involvement in subterranean drilling machinery, which must be relayed all the way to Booty Bay. While navigating the dangerous inner chambers of Gnomeregan, adventurers discover Kernobee stranded in the dormitory area. Severely beaten and groggy, the goblin survived capture by Dark Iron dwarves who left him behind to perish among the feral troggs. Finding a friendly face is his only chance of surviving the trek back through the contaminated corridors.

A Firm Response. "A Firm Response" is a Horde quest on Zephras Isle issued by Ayessa Dawnsinger. Tensions are boiling over as the mysterious High Order intrudes upon the territory and dealings of the local Windshapers. Ayessa orders a preemptive strike against Belathaan Brightwish on the road to the Shrine of Akir to establish clear boundaries through force. The Windshapers of Zephras Isle do not tolerate uninvited scrutiny, especially from an organization as secretive and calculating as the High Order. Prior warnings have gone unheeded, forcing Ayessa Dawnsinger to escalate the matter. To safeguard their interests, she chooses to intercept Belathaan Brightwish in the isolated stretch of road leading north toward the Shrine of Akir, ensuring the altercation stays away from prying eyes in town.

name.esES: Un peligro con olor a pescado

text.enUS: A Fishy Peril. In Goldshire, A Fishy Peril begins with reports of murlocs moving inland through the waterways. Remy "Two Times" asks travelers to alert Marshal Dughan, whose guards are already stretched thin. Remy "Two Times" grows uneasy over a new threat while seeking business in Goldshire. Murlocs are creeping up the streams and into inland shallows, disrupting fishing and menacing innocent travelers. Remy fears the local guard is overlooking a danger that is still growing, so he asks passersby to carry word to the heart of the township.

A Free Lunch. A Free Lunch is an Alliance errand originating in Lakeshire, where the inn cook Darcy asks an adventurer to take a prepared meal to Guard Parker. Parker patrols the perilous southern road heading toward Duskwood, keeping Lakeshire's approaches clear of hostile gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Daily life in Redridge is fraught with tension, but Darcy, a local of Lakeshire, tries to support those defending the town in her own way. Having packed a hearty meal for Guard Parker, she finds herself unable to deliver it personally. The wilderness just beyond the town gates swarms with aggressive Redridge gnolls and roaming orc warbands, making travel outside the town perimeter far too dangerous for an unarmored civilian. Instead, she relies on passing travelers to carry the ration out along the road toward Darkshire.

A Friend in Need. Iverron lies bitten and in danger in Shadowglen. The young night elf calls for Dirania Silvershine, whose help may save him from Githyiss the Vile's venom. Iverron lies weakened after a bite from Githyiss the Vile. He ignored warnings and went too near the webwood caverns, where the vicious spider struck. Dizziness and failing strength leave him unable to reach safety alone.

A Friend of the Family. A Friend of the Family is an urgent courier task originating from Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Fearing local threats like the Dragonmaw orcs, the harbor authorities entrust an adventurer to deliver the priceless Menethil Statuette directly to Highlord Bolvar Fordragon in Stormwind Keep. Menethil Harbor serves as a crucial naval gateway linking the northern reaches of the Eastern Kingdoms to the south. Named in honor of the late King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron, the port stands isolated among treacherous marshes and aggressive enemies. With local threats mounting, harbor leadership recognizes that priceless relics associated with the fallen northern kingdom cannot remain safely in such an exposed outpost.

A Friend of the Family. In Stormwind, A Friend of the Family carries a rare likeness of King Terenas to the Cathedral of Light. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon entrusts the Menethil Statuette to an adventurer for Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker, who will keep it safe. King Terenas Menethil II helped shape the Grand Alliance during the Second War and lived with deep personal devotion. Though he held great standing among humanity's kingdoms, he was humble and disliked monuments made in his honor. Few likenesses were commissioned, and fewer survived Lordaeron's ruin and the Scourge's devastation.

A Gnome's Respite. A Gnome's Respite is an Alliance quest offered by the eccentric tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Overwhelmed by the Venture Company's rapid industrial push into Windshear Crag, Gaxim hires adventurers to cull their loggers and deforesters so he can buy enough breathing room to invent new deterrents. Gaxim Rustfizzle represents the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences. Stationed among the ancient groves of Stonetalon, his stated duty is proving to the nature-worshipping night elves that modern gnomish invention—blending magic, chemical brews, and mechanics—can actively protect their threatened lands. However, the relentless pace of the Venture Company has left him with barely any time to prototype his defensive devices.

A Good Friend. At Aldrassil, Dirania Silvershine grows worried when Iverron misses his daily visit. She asks travelers to search the hills near Shadowthread Cave, north of Shadowglen. Dirania Silvershine waits beneath Aldrassil for Iverron, who visits her every day. Hours pass without him, and she asks travelers heading into Shadowglen to look for her friend.

A Grand Adventure. A Grand Adventure marks a turning point for the crisis on Zephras Isle within Skywall. Led by Ayessa Dawnsinger and the Windshapers, it outlines a bold plan to seek salvation for their home by journeying down to the mortal realm of Azeroth. Zephras Isle faces an escalating crisis as wind spirits have vanished without explanation. In response, the Windshapers have been investigating these disturbances, uncovering unexpected revelations about their missing kin and the fate of their elemental home. Ayessa Dawnsinger seeks capable adventurers to heed their findings and prepare for an unprecedented undertaking.

A Green Sample. A Green Sample is an errand offered by Shylamiir in Stormwind City, directing adventurers to infiltrate the secluded magical city of Dalaran. Expecting a pristine specimen of mana-infused vegetation from the central garden, the expedition uncovers unexpected demonic taint among the Kirin Tor's flora. In Stormwind City, the enigmatic Shylamiir seeks an adventurous traveler willing to run a discreet errand into restricted lands. Intrigued by the Kirin Tor's unusual pursuit of botany, Shylamiir desires a living specimen of the mana-infused vegetation cultivated within Dalaran's central garden. Because the secretive sorcerers keep their borders closed to outsiders, obtaining such flora requires someone adept at slipping into places uninvited.

A Grim Discovery. Krueg Skullsplitter in Camp Mojache is startled to hear that you met tauren in Feralas, and more so on learning they are Grimtotem. Belgrom, one of Krueg's masters, has put a bounty on their kind. Krueg wants you to go back and bring him twenty Grimtotem horns. You tell Krueg Skullsplitter of tauren you came across in the area, and Krueg is quick to name them as the Grimtotem clan. Belgrom, one of Krueg's masters, takes a keen interest in their kind and has put a bounty on them. Krueg tells you the Grimtotem are not to be underestimated, and that they are evil. You go back, slay them and bring twenty horns to Camp Mojache, so the first blow falls before they can raze villages or pilfer land.

A Grim Discovery. Krueg Skullsplitter admits to having mentioned a bounty, and says the one who did the work deserves the best of the payoff. The horns are put in a crate for you to carry to Belgrom Rockmaul, found in the Valley of Honor in Orgrimmar, who will want your account. This follows the first A Grim Discovery. After the first A Grim Discovery, Krueg Skullsplitter is taken aback, then admits to mentioning a bounty. You did the work, so Krueg feels it only right that you take the best of the payoff. The horns are packed into a crate for you. The crate goes to Belgrom Rockmaul, found in the Valley of Honor, who wishes to hear what you saw and will make your hard work worth it.

A Grim Task. Following the devastating Dark Iron assault on Dun Modr and the Thandol Span, Longbraid the Grim seeks vengeance for fallen kin and lost soldiers. He tasks brave travelers with tracking down and slaying the elusive Dark Iron warlock Balgaras the Foul, taking his ear as proof of the deed. The northern reaches of the Wetlands have seen intense fighting between the Mountaineers of Ironforge and infiltrators from the Dark Iron clan. During the siege, the town of Dun Modr was overtaken, and the western bridge of the Thandol Span was shattered. Longbraid the Grim lost not only many loyal soldiers in the assault, but also his own brother, leaving him determined to see the enemy paid back in kind.

A Hero's Welcome. Ginro Hearthkindle tells you that General Shandris Feathermoon wants a word with you in person. Gratitude for what you have done for the Stronghold is surely part of it, but she also means to discuss the insect creatures you and Raschal met in the south of Feralas. Ginro Hearthkindle passes the word: General Shandris Feathermoon wants to see you personally, and she is waiting in the main compound of Feathermoon Stronghold. Ginro admits the reports about the Zukk'ash insects are frightening.

A Humble Task. A Humble Task is an early rite of duty given by Chief Hawkwind in Camp Narache. As the Chieftain attends to pressing tribal concerns on the Red Cloud Mesa, he asks a young adventurer to venture southeast and check on his elderly mother at the local water well. The request emphasizes communal responsibility, elder reverence, and the daily harmony essential to the tauren way of life. In the shadow of Camp Narache, every member of the tribe is expected to pull their weight and share in the harmony of life. For young tauren coming of age, tribal duty is not measured solely in battle prowess against quilboars or predators; it begins with basic social responsibility. Chief Hawkwind demonstrates this ethos directly: bound to his post by administrative and defensive leadership, he places his trust in novice adventurers to watch over the community's vulnerable elders.

A Humble Task. A Humble Task is an introductory rite of service in Red Cloud Mesa, where an elder tests a fledgling adventurer's humility and diligence. By carrying fresh well water across the plains to Camp Narache's leader, young tauren learn that serving their people starts with the simplest duties. Greatmother Hawkwind has walked many trails in her long life, and while her spirit remains steady, her legs no longer carry her across the plains with the speed of her youth. Stationed near the water well on the southern edges of Red Cloud Mesa, she tends to her responsibilities with patient resolve. When aspiring tribal defenders cross her path, she redirects their youthful energy toward practical community needs, offering them a chance to prove their worth through service rather than violence.

A Hunter's Boast. A Hunter's Boast is a timed hunting challenge issued by Daryl the Youngling at Farstrider Lodge in Loch Modan. Eager to flaunt his supposed mastery, the arrogant young human dares adventurers to track and slay six mountain buzzards before his fifteen-minute timer expires. Farstrider Lodge serves as a gathering ground for some of Khaz Modan's finest trackers and marksmen, but not everyone under its roof possesses veteran humility. Daryl the Youngling—who fancies himself 'Daryl the Bold'—is quick to dismiss wandering adventurers. Convinced that greenhorn outsiders cannot hold a candle to his own hunting prowess, he lays down a brash wager: bag half a dozen local mountain buzzards within a quarter of an hour, or admit defeat.

A Hunter's Challenge. A Hunter's Challenge is a timed hunting trial issued by the brash human Daryl the Youngling at Farstrider Lodge in southeastern Loch Modan. Annoyed by his own inability to belittle your previous success, Daryl wagers the shirt off his back that you cannot track and fell five elder mountain boars within twelve minutes. The task tests an adventurer's swiftness against the rugged terrain and dangerous wildlife of the highlands. Daryl the Youngling resides among the seasoned huntsmen of Farstrider Lodge, yet he carries none of their quiet patience. Instead, Daryl compensates for his lack of years with bluster and exaggerated hunting tales, including rambling yarns about how he earned his 'famous' scar. Unwilling to acknowledge anyone else's competence, he continuously botches his fellow hunters' names and devises strict trials meant to humble newcomers and restore his own inflated standing among the lodge's residents.

A Husband's Revenge. A Husband's Revenge is the conclusion to a tragic tale of past betrayal carried into undeath. Raleigh Andrean, a Forsaken residing in the Undercity, charges travelers with tracking down his former friend Valdred Moray, who murdered his wife in life. When Raleigh Andrean received the engraved ring carried from Silverpine Forest, it rekindled memories of his mortal life that undeath had mostly withered away. Among those memories was a profound betrayal: his close friend, Valdred Moray, had murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. While the chill of the Scourge and subsequent Forsaken existence dulled Raleigh's capacity for grief and love, his thirst for retribution remained entirely intact.

A King's Tribute. A King's Tribute is an Alliance quest offered by King Magni Bronzebeard in the High Seat of Ironforge. Deeply moved by the grief of Sara Balloo, whose husband Sully fell defending the Thandol Span, the King decides to honor the fallen soldier with a lasting monument. He dispatches an adventurer to relay his royal commission to Grand Mason Marblesten. When King Magni Bronzebeard receives the plea of Sara Balloo, he does not dismiss the grieving widow. While he acknowledges that common folk may struggle to understand the brutal necessities of war, the loss of every soldier fighting beneath the Alliance banner weighs heavily upon his conscience. Unable to reverse the grim finality of death on the front lines, Magni chooses to ensure Sully Balloo's sacrifice is never forgotten.

A King's Tribute. King Magni Bronzebeard has commissioned a monument to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who perished defending the Thandol Span. To honor the fallen warrior with enduring dignity, Grand Mason Marblesten dispatches travelers to Hillsbrad to retrieve pristine Alterac Granite. When King Magni Bronzebeard decided that fallen soldier Sully Balloo deserved a lasting memorial, the task fell directly to Ironforge's finest craftsman, Grand Mason Marblesten. Balloo lost his life during the disaster at the Thandol Span, a vital artery connecting the dwarven lands to northern kingdoms that has suffered brutal attacks by Dark Iron saboteurs. To Marblesten, fulfilling the king's royal decree means creating a sculpture that will withstand both time and war, ensuring that dwarven sacrifice is neither overlooked nor forgotten in the Great Forge.

A King's Tribute. A King's Tribute marks the final step in honoring the sacrifice of the fallen dwarven soldier Sully Balloo. After fine granite is gathered from the ruins of Lordaeron, Grand Mason Marblesten sculpts a solemn memorial monument in Ironforge on the orders of King Magni Bronzebeard. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned a permanent monument to honor Sully Balloo, a brave dwarf who lost his life in service to his people. Crafted by Grand Mason Marblesten using high-quality granite transported from the war-torn lands of Lordaeron, the finished memorial stands in Ironforge as an enduring testament to fallen soldiers whose sacrifices preserve the dwarven kingdom.

name.ptBR: O medo é para os fracos

text.enUS: A Lack of Fear. A Lack of Fear is a rite-of-passage summons for dwarven priests, calling promising disciples back to the grand halls of Ironforge. High Priest Rohan awaits in the Mystic Ward to test their discipline and bestow teachings tailored to their growing resilience. Priests serving the Alliance abroad are routinely directed by their local mentors to report back to their order's senior clergy. For dwarven disciples, that guidance leads straight to High Priest Rohan in the heart of Ironforge's Mystic Ward. The summons marks a turning point where basic spiritual practice gives way to deeper, trial-tested applications of holy magic.

A Lack of Virtue. A Lack of Virtue is a delivery quest involving an enduring petty grudge between two card-playing sailors, Tom Half-fish and Bart Tidewater. Travelers carry a packaged gift across the sea to Menethil Harbor, stepping right into the middle of a mutual cheating accusation over how the Maiden's Virtue was won. A Lack of Virtue centers on an acrimonious rivalry between two salty seafaring gamblers: Tom Half-fish and Bart Tidewater. Tom recruits passing travelers to deliver a packaged parcel across the water to Bart in Menethil Harbor, using the delivery as a petty spiteful jab against his former companion. Along the way, Tom warns that Bart is no true sea dog at all, but rather a former actor who cheated his way through card games to purchase his command.

A Last Request. A Last Request begins upon discovering the corpse of a fallen peacekeeper in the field. Clutched in the dead guard's hands is a bloodstained note containing vital clues about his final moments. Reading his dying words offers the only way to carry out his unfinished duty and bring closure to his fate. A Last Request begins with a grim discovery in the field: the lifeless body of a fallen peacekeeper. Slumped in death, the guardian still clutches a bloodstained note that slips free upon inspection. In these turbulent days on Zephras, peacekeepers often pay the ultimate price trying to maintain order, and recovering their dying words is frequently the only way to uncover what befell them.

A Lesson to Learn. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends young druids from Darnassus to Moonglade to learn the ways of water. There, they meet an elder of the Cenarion Circle and begin training in their aquatic aspect. Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides young night elf druids as they practice among Darnassus’s boughs. When an initiate shows a firm bond with nature and readiness for greater responsibility, Mathrengyl sends them toward mastery of the waters. Cenarius’s gifts demand focus, and learning to cross the depths without drowning calls for guidance from the Cenarion Circle’s elders.

A Lesson to Learn. A Lesson to Learn is a rite of passage for young tauren druids ready to claim command over the water. Issued atop the heights of Thunder Bluff by Turak Runetotem, the quest directs students to Nighthaven in Moonglade to begin their trials under the tutelage of the Cenarion Circle. After gaining command of raw physical might through the bear, a druid's studies turn toward adaptability. The waterways of Azeroth present perilous hazards to landbound travelers, demanding an aspect suited to cold depths and crushing currents. Turak Runetotem watches his students closely, choosing only those who have proven their dedication to nature before sending them north to study the aquatic form.

A Letter Undelivered. A faded, bloodstained missive found among the skeletal ruins of Agamand Mills, addressed to Yvette Farthing. It reveals a tragic parting between two lovers as the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, offering a glimpse into what the Forsaken left behind when they traded life for undeath. Written by Thurman Agamand, the eldest son of patriarch Gregor Agamand, this unsent parchment never reached its intended recipient before the family estate collapsed into ruin. When the Plague of Undeath consumed Tirisfal Glades, Thurman refused to abandon his ancestral home and kin. Amid the horrors of the onslaught, he took up quill to write one last message to Yvette Farthing, whom he had loved before the kingdom turned to ash.

A Letter to Grelin Whitebeard. This sealed correspondence is addressed to Grelin Whitebeard, an experienced dwarf stationed out in the snowy wilderness of Coldridge Valley. Sent from the mountain capital of Ironforge, it serves as a rare dispatch of news and instructions reaching the remote frontier. Life in the snowy basin of Coldridge Valley can be isolated, especially for those stationed beyond the safety of Anvilmar. Letters like this represent the crucial link connecting scouts and scholars in the field to the halls of Ironforge. Carried southward along the mountain paths, the missive brings word from the capital to Grelin Whitebeard's wilderness campsite.

A Light in the Darkness. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this quest tasks Forsaken adventurers with rescuing newly raised undead trapped in Night's Web Hollow. It highlights the delicate relationship between undead wielders of the Holy Light and a populace that deeply distrusts them. By aiding their fallen kin, these holy practitioners hope to prove their loyalty to Sylvanas and the Forsaken cause. The Holy Light is notoriously agonizing and hazardous to the undead, yet some Forsaken retain their connection to the sacred magic they wielded in life. In Deathknell, figures like Aramis Hammerhand strive to demonstrate that their faith has not turned them against their people. To combat the suspicion that holy practitioners will turn on other undead as monstrosities, they actively use their abilities and compassion to safeguard their kin.

A Little Beauty. A Little Beauty is a local task in the Shen'dar Highlands where travelers gather soft hippogryph down feathers near Zephras. The colorful plumes are used by the Skyborne to adorn their hair, bringing a touch of simple joy and beauty to the village during challenging times. On Zephras Isle, southwest of the village, wild hippogryphs have established nesting grounds in the Shen'dar Highlands. While these territorial beasts can be an unruly nuisance to nearby travelers, they shed exceptionally vibrant and silky soft down feathers. For the local Skyborne, collecting these discarded plumes presents an opportunity to craft exquisite ornaments woven directly into their hair.

text.enUS: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. In the bustling halls of Ironforge, the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle seeks to uncover the evolutionary secrets of Azeroth by studying oozes and slimes. Curious about the Royal Apothecary Society's strange fascination with these vile puddles, he tasks Alliance adventurers with journeying to tainted Felwood to bottle up specimen samples. While most scholars of the Explorers' League concern themselves with ancient titan relics or buried dwarven genealogies, Laris Geardawdle has set his inquisitive mind on a squelchier subject: oozes. Ubiquitous across wetlands, cursed woods, and damp ruins, these living puddles defy standard biological classification. Having witnessed Forsaken apothecaries scooping up slime samples across Lordaeron, Laris has resolved to understand what makes these gelatinous horrors so uniquely interesting to the Undercity's alchemists.

text.enUS: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. Following his initial study of tainted specimens, the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle seeks untainted ooze samples to understand how these strange creatures adapt to their environment. Having realized that oozes absorb the corrupted nature of places like Felwood, he sends adventurers to discover and gather pure, unpolluted specimens from across Kalimdor. Laris Geardawdle's preliminary experiments in Ironforge hit an immediate stumbling block: the oozes he previously examined were thoroughly polluted by the dark energies of Felwood. While this demonstrated that oozes absorb and reflect the traits of their surroundings, it left him without a control group. To understand the baseline nature of ooze life, he needs specimens untouched by demonic taint or urban filth.

A Lost Master. In Auberdine, Terenthis prepares to help find Volcor, a night elf lost in Darkshore. He can weave a camouflage cloak to protect the searcher, but needs pelts from the coast's fiercest moonstalkers. Terenthis in Auberdine fears for Volcor and his companion, Grimclaw, as danger closes around the coast of Darkshore. The southern wilds hold aggressive predators and corrupted wildlife. Rather than send an unprotected scout into that danger, Terenthis plans a cloak woven with wild illusions.

A Lost Master. In Darkshore, you follow Grimclaw’s trail to find the missing scout Volcor. You carry the Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak Terenthis made from fine moonstalker pelts. Terenthis in Auberdine has woven the Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak, and the search for Volcor begins. Grimclaw, the missing night elf scout’s loyal bear, waits on the road south of the settlement for help sent by Terenthis. Give Grimclaw a familiar greeting, and he leads you off the road toward the cave where Volcor is hiding.

A Man About a Murloc. A Man About a Murloc is an errand undertaken on behalf of a fisherman named Jason who is troubled by local murlocs raiding his fish. Jason sends adventurers to consult Remy "Two Times", a local eccentric harboring a deep grudge and schemes of his own against the creatures. A local fisherman named Jason has grown fed up with murlocs raiding his catches. Knowing that Remy "Two Times" harbors a mutual hatred for the amphibians, Jason directs travelers to confer with Remy to see if he has devised any practical ways to drive them away from the waters.

A Missing Hand. A Missing Hand is a quest in Durotar concerning the sudden disappearance of Heglan Shadeeye, a Shattered Hand scout tasked with keeping watch on Tiragarde Keep. When her regular intelligence dispatches abruptly cease, an investigator is sent to find her post and uncover what silenced her. A Missing Hand begins with growing concern over Heglan Shadeeye, a scout belonging to the Shattered Hand. Stationed in Durotar to monitor the hostile human garrison occupying Tiragarde Keep from afar, her steady stream of intelligence reports suddenly vanished without explanation. Her superiors doubt the human soldiers managed to detect and capture her, raising fears that an unexpected and more dangerous hazard intervened. Adventurers are dispatched north of the keep to locate her post and determine whether the disruption is merely a delay in communication or something far grimmer.
A Mysterious Message. A courier's intercepted message gives the People's Militia proof of who directs the Defias Brotherhood in Westfall.

A Net Disaster. A Net Disaster is an Elwynn Forest quest centered on an unusual disruption at Crystal Lake. With hook-and-line fishing yielding nothing and even minnows disappearing from the shallows, adventurers are dispatched to check overnight traps. The ruined traps reveal that hostile neighboring intruders are actively wrecking local fishing gear. At Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest, local fishermen face an alarming drought in their daily catch. Empty hooks are common enough, but when not even minnows appear in the shallows, everyday angling turns into a serious mystery. To salvage what they can, overnight traps are set in hopes of pulling in basic stock.

A New Cloak's Sheen. Krueg Skullsplitter has come down to Feralas with companions, sent by their masters in Orgrimmar. Krueg plans a cloak for life-mate Korrin and asks you for ten Iridescent Sprite Darter Wings. Krueg and companions came down to Feralas, sent by their masters in Orgrimmar. Krueg's life-mate Korrin loves new clothes, so Krueg plans a cloak adorned with the delicate wings of faerie dragons. The sprite darters with the beautiful wings Krueg wants live west of Camp Mojache, and Krueg asks you for ten Iridescent Sprite Darter Wings.

A New Ore Sample. Tatternack Steelforge seeks new ore in Thousand Needles to strengthen the Horde’s arms. The blacksmith in Camp Taurajo sends you south to bring back a sample for testing. Tatternack Steelforge works as a blacksmith in Camp Taurajo, under Orgrimmar’s direct scrutiny. He has already supplied weapons made from local centaur armaments, but still wants to prove his craft to Warchief Thrall. Travelers passing through showed him a strange piece of ore taken from a kobold to the south. When they refused to sell it, Tatternack took their refusal as an insult to his craft and the Horde.

A New Plague. A New Plague is an introductory task in Brill that reveals the Forsaken's overarching strategic ambition. Apothecary Johaan tasks recruits with harvesting the blood of wild darkhounds to lay the groundwork for a virulent pathogen commissioned directly by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. In the damp village of Brill, Apothecary Johaan works on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society under a mandate directly from the Dark Lady. Sylvanas Windrunner has charged her alchemists with crafting a disease unlike anything Azeroth has ever seen. While the original plague of undeath served the Lich King by slaughtering humanity and binding their souls, this new creation is explicitly designed to annihilate Arthas Menethil and lay waste to his Scourge legions.

A New Plague. Tasked by Apothecary Johaan in Brill, this errand requires gathering scales from the local Vile Fin murlocs prowling the Tirisfal coast. The Royal Apothecary Society aims to harness unique biological reagents to refine their budding new contagion, ensuring it can spread beyond isolated victims to engulf larger populations. Poisoning a single target is simple alchemy, but formulating a plague capable of sweeping across entire lands demands more complex components. Apothecary Johaan's ongoing research in Brill hinges on creating a disease that can self-propagate and endure in the wild. To engineer this transmissibility, he turns his attention toward the shoreline wildlife of Tirisfal Glades, identifying the resilient biology of the coastal Vile Fin murlocs as a promising source of raw material.

A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan turns his attention toward developing a potent new biological agent for the Forsaken. By studying ancient texts, he discovers that a historic, deadly plague survived through the venom of eastern Tirisfal's night web spiders, prompting an urgent retrieval effort. While pursuing his alchemy for the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill, Apothecary Johaan scours aged tomes in search of deadlier mixtures. He uncovers records of an ancient pestilence that once ravaged thousands of lives. Crucially, the texts indicate that the deadly pathogen survived across generations by harboring within the local arachnids of Tirisfal Glades, making their venom an invaluable biological reagent.

A New Plague. This quest marks the grim culmination of Apothecary Johaan's initial research in Brill on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society. Having harvested venom, blood, and vile concoctions across Tirisfal Glades, Johaan sends you to the cellar of Gallows' End Tavern to test his lethal brew on a captive dwarven mountaineer. Throughout your time aiding Apothecary Johaan, your efforts have steadily built toward refining a lethal toxin. The Royal Apothecary Society pursues an ambitious and shadowy agenda on behalf of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner: crafting a new plague that bypasses undead biology while annihilating the living. In this final step, Johaan brews what he euphemistically calls a 'special drink' and tasks you with administering it directly to an imprisoned enemy of the Forsaken.

A New Threat. A New Threat is an early combat assignment issued by Balir Frosthammer in Coldridge Valley. Dwarven mountaineers have been caught off-guard by a sudden surge of troggs bursting out across Dun Morogh, threatening local settlements and camps. Coldridge Valley was long regarded as a protected haven for young dwarven warriors and mountaineers training in Dun Morogh. That peace shattered when subterranean Rockjaw troggs began clawing their way to the surface in startling numbers. Reports quickly reached Anvilmar that troggs were swarming the frozen lake and surrounding foothills, disrupting daily patrols and cutting off vital supply routes through the valley pass.

A Noble Brew. Zardeth of the Black Claw schemes against Stormwind's nobles from beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. Lord Wishock's call for an investigation puts the hidden warlock coven at risk. Beneath the Mage Quarter streets, warlocks gather in the Slaughtered Lamb and keep their coven hidden. Lord Wishock, a member of the House of Nobles, has heard of the dark magic below the city. He is urging his peers to launch a full investigation, which could bring the city guard and royal scrutiny down on the coven.

A Noble Brew. In Stormwind, a courier carries Black Claw Stout to Lord Baurles K. Wishock in the Royal Keep. Zardeth of the Black Claw has arranged the delivery from the cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. Lord Baurles K. Wishock spends time in the Hall of Petitioners in Stormwind Keep, speaking of his own importance and the kingdom’s future. Patrons of the Slaughtered Lamb know another side of him. At night, he drinks in the tavern’s upper rooms and leaves large bills unpaid. By day, he petitions to have the tavern shut down.

A Peon's Burden. Ukor waits on the trail outside the Valley of Trials with a load he cannot carry home. The recruits in the red canyon refused his provisions, and now he asks travelers to return them to Razor Hill. Ukor set out from Razor Hill with provisions for the fresh recruits training in the red canyon. He believed they needed the food, but the taskmasters turned him away. They keep supplies lean because they believe meager rations teach young Horde warriors discipline and endurance. Innkeeper Grosk later explains that this hardship is part of their training.

A Pilot's Revenge. Following the trail of a missing dwarven siege engine pilot leads to a frozen corpse in the wilds of Dun Morogh. Found among the remains, Hildelve's personal journal details his fatal struggle against a notorious predator known as Mangeclaw, leaving behind a dying wish for vengeance. Pilot Hildelve did not survive his time stranded in the rugged snowy crags. When travelers locate his remains, they discover his journal resting beside him. In his last penned words, Hildelve recorded a savage encounter with a massive Ice Claw bear he named Mangeclaw. Though he managed to fend off the monstrosity initially, the injuries proved severe, and the beast eventually returned to finish off the weakened pilot.

A Portable Power Source. With the ectoplasm in hand, Mux Manascrambler needs a stable, portable source of energy to keep it active. He has heard rumours of Magma Lord Bokk, an elemental in the Burning Steppes whose heart is a Magma Core, and wants that core brought to him in Gadgetzan. After Hunting for Ectoplasm, Mux Manascrambler wants a steady, movable source of power to keep the ectoplasm active. Rumour has it that Magma Lord Bokk, a mighty elemental, carries a Magma Core for a heart, an endless supply of heat. The Magma Lord is said to dwell in the Burning Steppes, to the south of Blackrock Mountain and west of the Pillar of Ash. Mux wants that core brought to Gadgetzan, so the extra-dimensional ghost revealer can run.

A Putrid Task. A Putrid Task is an early military assignment offered by Deathguard Dillinger in Brill. It directs adventurers to push back the mindlessly aggressive Scourge encroaching upon the old bridge west of the settlement. Collecting proof of the monsters' destruction secures the road and eases pressure on Tirisfal's defenders. Brill sits at a critical crossroads in eastern Tirisfal Glades, making any enemy approach a direct threat to the Forsaken power base. Mindless Scourge constantly seep westward across the waterways, clustering around the broken remnants of the old stone bridge. Without regular patrols beating them back, the shambling corpses would quickly choke transit between Brill and the western farmsteads.

A Recipe For Death. A Recipe For Death is an alchemical errand commissioned by Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Tasked with gathering grizzly bear hearts and arachnid blood, adventurers transport the volatile biological reagents to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity to aid in formulating the Forsaken's lethal New Plague. Positioned on the front lines in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel recognizes the grim arithmetic facing Sylvanas's people. Surrounded by the relentless legions of Arthas and enduring remnants of humanity, conventional warfare offers little hope. The Forsaken's grand ambition lies in developing a New Plague—an engineered contagion potent enough to rot both living humans and undead Scourge alike. Renferrel's field research determined that combining arachnid venom from the Skittering Dark with toxins concentrated in the hearts of native bears yields a virulent foundation.

A Recipe For Death. Master Apothecary Faranell tasks Horde adventurers with recovering the lost research of Apothecary Berard from Pyrewood Village. Berard fell victim to Archmage Arugal's shadow magic, leaving behind critical notes on an ancient blight that wiped out Lake Lordamere's aquatic life. Before his downfall, Apothecary Berard was considered one of the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising researchers. Stationed in Pyrewood Village, he investigated past ecological disasters to aid the Forsaken's alchemical pursuits. However, when Archmage Arugal unleashed his dark sorcery over Silverpine Forest, Berard succumbed to the curse, degrading into a mindless servant under the mage's thrall.

A Recipe For Death. A Recipe For Death concludes an investigation into the findings of a fallen researcher, directing adventurers to gather rare biological reagents across Lake Lordamere. By recovering harvested mosses and a strange tumor, the Forsaken bring essential components to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. This work directly supports the Royal Apothecary Society's overarching goal to develop a New Plague. The loss of Apothecary Berard to Arugal's curse struck a blow against the Royal Apothecary Society, but his field journal left behind crucial insights into the blighted biology of Silverpine Forest and Lake Lordamere. Stationed at the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel parsed through Berard's recovered notes and discovered that Berard had documented promising properties in local freshwater organisms. Rather than let Berard's sacrifice go to waste, Renferrel tasks champions of the Horde with fulfilling his lost colleague's vision.

name.ptBR: Um dia na vida de um refugiado

text.enUS: A Refugee's Quandary. Following the disastrous fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and radiation, displaced gnomes have fled into the snowy wilds of Dun Morogh. Outside Anvilmar, an engineer named Felix Whindlebolt lost his vital belongings and tools to Frostmane troll scavengers during the panicked evacuation. When subterranean troggs overran the high-tech city of Gnomeregan, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his advisors authorized the release of radioactive gas in a desperate bid to eradicate the invaders. The gambit backfired catastrophically, slaying thousands of innocents, mutating survivors into mindless leper gnomes, and forcing the remaining populace into a frantic exodus across Dun Morogh.

A Righteous Cause. A Righteous Cause witnesses a conversation between Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr as they reflect on the defense of the Undercity against Naxxramas. Their exchange highlights the memory of Garek Bandarion, an undead hero who rediscovered how to wield the Holy Light as a paladin. The quest illuminates the rare Forsaken who strive to maintain their connection to the Light despite the skepticism of their kin. A Righteous Cause centers on a poignant reunion between two veteran defenders of Lordaeron: Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr. Having survived the harrowing assault when Naxxramas unleashed the Scourge upon the Undercity, the two reflect upon their fallen comrades and the difficult path walked by Forsaken who still revere the Holy Light.

A Rogue's Deal. A seemingly casual favor for Calvin Montague in Deathknell sends a traveler on the road to the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. The errand involves ferrying a mysterious, unaddressed message to Innkeeper Renee under the guise of an ordinary courier run. Lounging amidst the solemn graves and ruined chapels of Deathknell, Calvin Montague presents himself as an exhausted fighter burdened by too many Scourge zombies and creeping spiders. Claiming he simply needs a hand delivering a message to Brill, he entrusts passing adventurers with an unmarked letter. His breezy demeanor and promise of generous coin make the task appear as nothing more than a harmless favor meant to point freshly awakened Forsaken toward the region's main town.

A Sacred Burial. A Sacred Burial is a quest entrusted by Lorekeeper Raintotem, tasking Horde adventurers with protecting Red Rocks in eastern Mulgore. The sacred ancestral burial grounds have been overrun by marauding Bristleback quilboar who are defiling the graves of esteemed tauren warriors. Driving off these interlopers restores honor and peace to those who gave their lives founding and defending Thunder Bluff. Red Rocks serves as one of the most revered sanctuaries in all of Mulgore. Tucked into the crags beneath the eastern mountains, it is the final resting place reserved exclusively for the most valiant tauren. The heroes interred here are legendary warriors who shed blood to protect their tribes, uphold their chieftains, and carve out a permanent homeland atop the mesas of Thunder Bluff. To the Shu'halo, disturbing their rest is an affront not just to tradition, but to the Earth Mother herself.

A Scribbled Letter. A Scribbled Letter is a summons delivered to adventurers at Northshire Abbey following their early clashes with nearby kobolds. Sent under the seal of Tordrin Stemblade, it directs promising recruits to seek out his training and guidance. The letter marks a crucial step in preparing defenders to face the escalating perils threatening the kingdom of Stormwind. Upon returning from skirmishes with the kobold camps infesting the valley, adventurers at Northshire Abbey receive a hasty missive. Marked with the seal of Tordrin Stemblade, the note requests their prompt attention before attending to other business. The letter serves as an urgent summons to connect budding champions with formal mentorship within the abbey's protective grounds.

A Scroll from Mauren. Gaxim Rustfizzle needs arcane help to trigger his NG-5 explosives from afar. He sends you to Collin Mauren in Stormwind, where gnomish ingenuity meets human arcane craft. Gaxim Rustfizzle seeks a safer way to set off his NG-5 explosives. Mechanical fuses cannot give him the remote trigger he wants: one button should ignite the charges while he stays at a safe distance. He turns to arcane magic to bridge that gap.

A Sealed Crate. A Sealed Crate is a turn-in task involving recovered trade goods that have fallen into the hands of highwaymen or were lost along commercial routes. Adventurers return intercepted cargo to trade handlers to secure regional supply lines and receive payment. Wagon trails and shipping lanes have become treacherous due to a sharp rise in ambushes by bandits and thieves targeting trade caravans. Unsuspecting haulers and couriers frequently lose their shipments when caught unawares, leaving heavy sealed crates abandoned along wild roads and wilderness paths until someone recovers them.

A Shifty Merchant. Mux Manascrambler has the core to power his device and now needs a rod able to carry that power without melting. He once met an imp in Winterspring selling exotic goods, and wishes he had bought the elemental rod on offer. You look for the imp in a cave at the entrance to Darkwhisper Gorge and buy the Fel Elemental Rod. After A Portable Power Source, Mux Manascrambler turns to the next problem: a rod able to carry the core's power without melting. Mux met an imp in Winterspring selling all manner of exotic goods, and the imp's elemental rod would have done perfectly. Mux is kicking himself for not buying it. The imp lives inside a cave at the entrance to Darkwhisper Gorge in southern Winterspring. You find the imp, buy the Fel Elemental Rod, and bring it back to Mux in Gadgetzan. Mux insists the imp charge only forty gold, the price quoted to Mux.

A Short Incubation. Quentin, waiting in Thousand Needles, hears that the Moonweavers gave you the sprite darter egg. The egg looks almost ready to hatch, so Quentin wants to be sure it is healthy and undamaged, and asks you for two elixirs of fortitude. Quentin finds it intriguing that the Moonweavers looked after the egg and thinks both are quite capable. Since the egg was a gift to you, it is yours to be responsible for as long as you wish. It appears almost ready to hatch, but it should first be checked for health and damage. A small spell to protect it will do the job, and Quentin has every component on hand except two elixirs of fortitude. Quentin admits to growing tempted by the races while waiting, and will return the egg for you to keep once its health is known.

A Sign of Hope. A crumpled map bears a few words scrawled in chalk: a plea to Ryedol from Hammertoe, who says they are taking Hammertoe to Uldaman and asks for help. Prospector Ryedol should hear that Hammertoe Grez lives. Roughly scribbled in chalk on the crumpled map is a short note signed by Hammertoe. It is addressed to Ryedol and says only that they are taking Hammertoe to Uldaman and that help is needed. The word to carry to Prospector Ryedol is that Hammertoe Grez lives.

A Simmering Storm. A Simmering Storm begins when an adventurer recovers a strange, spark-emitting relic known as the Dull Stormy Orb from the harpies of Drygulch Ravine. Bearing the swirling miniature storm to the goblin tinker Rezlak provides insight into the harpies' odd trinkets and earns the interest of Ratchet's enterprising salvagers. While contending with the aggressive Dustwind harpies nesting throughout Drygulch Ravine, travelers may come across an unusual curiosity: the Dull Stormy Orb. Though its outer surface appears muted and worn, holding the object reveals a steady vibration of raw electrical current. Inside the sphere, dark mist churns endlessly, illuminated at random intervals by sharp internal sparks. It is unmistakable proof that the harpies were manipulating storm magic through strange relics.

A Simple Compass. At the burned Alexston Farmstead in Westfall, A Simple Compass waits in a small chest. It belonged to Baros Alexston before he became Stormwind's City Architect. Baros Alexston grew up working his family's farm in Westfall. His simple compass was his first navigational instrument, and may have stirred his interest in geometry, drafting, and exploration. The Defias Brotherhood raided and burned the farmstead, leaving the compass in a sturdy chest among the ruins as bandits overran the farmland.
