name.ptBR: Com os agradecimentos da Fazenda Bosque Defumado

text.enUS: A Smokywood Pastures' Thank You!. Great-father Winter waits in Orgrimmar to thank those who recovered Smokywood Pastures' stolen holiday treats. Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive a token of appreciation for bringing the supplies back. In Orgrimmar, Smokywood Pastures sells treats, recipes, and seasonal cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. Their shipment was stolen in the snowy hills of the Alterac Mountains, and business stalled. With the treats recovered and the Abominable Greench dealt with, Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive the company's thanks.

A Solvent Spirit. Master Vornal tests would-be pupils in Sen'jin Village as his eyesight fades. He asks them to gather makrura eyes and crawler mucus along Durotar's coast. Though he scoffs at taking an apprentice, the work tests patience and resolve. Master Vornal lives in Sen'jin Village, where age has dimmed his sight. Primal magic once came readily to his fingertips, but now he relies on alchemy to sharpen his perceptions and weave his arts. Though his body weakens, the stubborn troll refuses an apprentice. He says neither the Darkspear nor Durotar's orcs have produced anyone worthy of his teaching.

A Stack of Letters. A Stack of Letters is a small bundle of correspondence brought through the mountain pass into Coldridge Valley. Though initially believed to belong entirely to Talin Keeneye, the bundle holds communications meant for multiple scouts stationed in the freezing wilderness. Reaching remote camps within Dun Morogh's rugged mountains is grueling work, and postal runners often rely on passing travelers to carry mail out of Anvilmar. This bundle of letters arrived through the pass destined for scouts stationed deeper in Coldridge Valley. While thought to be solely for Talin Keeneye at his lakeside camp, sorting through the parcel reveals missives meant for other outposts across the snows, including mountaineer Grelin Whitebeard.

A Sticky Situation. Gilveradin Sunchaser holds the original packaging for the Hinterlands Honey Ripple that Dran Droffers is after, and will help package it for a fee of two extra bottles. The bottles are in crates around the abandoned Horde base near Skulk Rock. Dran Droffers seeks the ripple, and Gilveradin Sunchaser has the original packaging for it. The help is not free: Gilveradin wants two additional bottles for the trouble. Ten bottles of Hinterlands Honey Ripple are to be gathered and brought back to the camp.

A Strange Request. Witch Doctor Uzer'i needs a concoction that Neeru Fireblade in Orgrimmar has mixed up. Uzer'i hands you a shrunken head, promised to Neeru in exchange for the herbs, and sends you to the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar to deliver it. Witch Doctor Uzer'i says Neeru Fireblade in Orgrimmar has what is needed to get started in Feralas: a concoction for something Uzer'i will not yet explain. Uzer'i gives you a shrunken head, promised to Neeru in return for the herbs. It is the head of some poor dwarf Uzer'i came across in the forest. Neeru can be found in the Cleft of Shadow.

A Student of Nature. A Student of Nature marks a fledgling druid's introduction to formal training on Zephras Isle. After helping restore local harmony, novice druids are summoned by Xyton Silverwind beneath the boughs of Thendal Grove. It serves as the opening gateway into understanding the deeper balance between flora and fauna on the isle. Following the resolution of local disturbances caused by overzealous wildlife, Rorian the Dayseeker delivers a personal summons to young initiates. Left behind by the local mentor Xyton Silverwind, the folded parchment invites aspiring druids to step forward and dedicate themselves to the deeper mysteries of the wild. It signals that an initiate's natural talents have caught the eye of the grove's elders.

A Student of the Arcane. A Student of the Arcane is an introductory trial and summons for novice spellcasters on Zephras Isle. Initiated by Rorian the Dayseeker after newcomers prove their basic mettle, it directs budding mages to review a Glowing Recall Crystal and report to the local mentor, Dorii Brightwhisper. After helping manage the troublesome vuldren lurking near Thendal Grove, fledgling mages are entrusted with a curious artifact: a Glowing Recall Crystal. Left behind by Dorii Brightwhisper, the island's resident arcane instructor, the crystal serves as a magically recorded missive designed to test an initiate's aptitude and welcome them into deeper mystical study.

A Supernatural Device. Deliana is looking for a way to speak with the ghost of Anthion Harmon. An engineer with a peculiar fascination for the supernatural says he can build a machine for talking to the dead, and you bring him the blood you collected, in Gadgetzan, as his payment. Deliana is searching for a way to reach Anthion Harmon, or more exactly his ghost. The engineer Deliana has in mind is Mux Manascrambler, who boasts of a machine for conversing with the dead. That blood of yours was meant for him from the start, so carry it to Gadgetzan in Tanaris and give it to Mux in exchange for his services.

A Supernatural Device. Mokvar has a use for the venom samples you collected: they are for an acquaintance, Mux Manascrambler, who is in Gadgetzan. Mux is working on a device for speaking with the dead, and Mokvar hopes it will help reach Anthion. Mokvar remarks that you must be brave to have stayed on, and says there is more armor to be had for anyone still willing to help. The venom you gathered belongs with an acquaintance, Mux Manascrambler, an engineer who takes an interest in the supernatural. Mux's current project is a device for talking to the dead. Mokvar pins a last hope on it: reaching Anthion to learn more about Mokvar's own situation. You take the sealed container to Mux in Gadgetzan, in Tanaris.

A Swift Message. Quartermaster Lewis at Sentinel Hill needs urgent armor shipments from Stormwind to equip the People's Militia. Because Westfall receives almost no official military aid, he sends you to Thor the gryphon master to carry an urgent requisition note to the capital by air. Sentinel Hill stands isolated against a rising tide of Defias outlaws and gnolls, starved of direct military aid from Stormwind. Quartermaster Lewis relies on private contacts in the capital to keep the People's Militia supplied with weapons and armor. With gear running thin, his only lifeline is Osric Strang, an armorer located in Old Town. Getting an urgent requisition to him requires swift travel, leading Lewis to enlist travelers to contact Westfall's gryphon master, Thor.

A Task Unfinished. A Task Unfinished is a simple delivery quest highlighting the strain young tauren endure during their coming-of-age rites on Red Cloud Mesa. Overburdened by the demands of their trials and a filial chore, an exhausted youth asks a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down to Innkeeper Kauth in Bloodhoof Village. High upon Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren face rigorous trials of passage to prove their readiness for the wider world. Balancing traditional rites against ordinary tribal chores can push a youth to the brink of physical exhaustion. Faced with an unfinished Rite of Strength and an urgent chore from their father, one young tauren seeks the aid of a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down the mesa.

A Threat Within. Volunteers are answering Stormwind's call in Northshire Valley, where local defenses need help. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride explains that the kingdom's forces are spread thin abroad, leaving garrisons short-handed against trouble at home. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and monastic study. Now it is Elwynn Forest's first line of defense against unrest at home. Stormwind's regular forces serve on distant fronts, leaving the heartlands short of soldiers. With few guards nearby, the Stormwind Guard must call on every willing volunteer who reaches the abbey.

name.zhCN: 一张被撕破的日记书页

text.enUS: A Torn Journal Page. A Torn Journal Page is a tattered piece of parchment recovered from an old shipping crate along the Stormwind City canals. It serves as an essential physical clue into the identity and dark history of Stalvan Mistmantle, connecting the grim happenings in Duskwood to records preserved in Elwynn Forest. Discovered hidden near the bottom of a sealed storage crate beside Stormwind City's canals—tucked beneath old books, family heirlooms, and a ceramic vase—this fragment was left behind among forgotten personal effects. Though damaged and worn, the handwriting upon the page carries a distinct script that points directly to Stalvan Mistmantle's past, prompting investigators to seek out those who might still recognize the hand that penned it.

A Troubling Breeze. Athridas Bearmantle waits for word from Starbreeze Village, but the reports have stopped. Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren watches over the sleeping Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, and his silence points to danger in Teldrassil. Athridas Bearmantle depends on regular word from Gaerolas Talvethren, the Great Warden watching over the Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The druids sleep there to keep their sacred pact with Ysera in the Emerald Dream. Their sanctuary matters to the spiritual balance of the young World Tree. Now reports from the east have ceased, and unease spreads through the forest.

A Visitor to Dun Morogh. A Visitor to Dun Morogh is an investigative task offered by Beldin Steelgrill outside Kharanos. Mountaineers reported an unfamiliar campfire high on the cliffs overlooking Gol'Bolar Quarry, prompting a scout to check whether the stranger poses a threat to the local dwarves. Dun Morogh's mountaineers keep a diligent watch over the crags and snowy valleys surrounding Ironforge. When a campfire suddenly appeared high above Gol'Bolar Quarry, it raised eyebrows in Kharanos. Beldin Steelgrill, concerned by the unusual encampment situated directly above a vital dwarven excavation, recruits travelers to scale the ridges and determine whether the mysterious stranger is a benign traveler or an intruder.

A Warden of the Horde. In Orgrimmar, Children's Week ends with Grunth's return to Orphan Matron Battlewail. After seeing the world with his guardian, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself. After the adventures of Children's Week, Grunth thanks you for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. He remembers his parents' advice to rise above hardship and hopes to become a hero like you. His final request is to return home and tell the matron about your time together.

A Warrior's Training. In Goldshire, A Warrior's Training sends young warriors to Stormwind for lessons in battlefield endurance. Lyria Du Lac directs them to the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Old Town, where veteran Harry Burlguard offers seasoned instruction. After aspiring fighters show reliable command of the fundamentals against threats across Elwynn Forest, their trainers see little more for Goldshire drillmasters to teach. Lyria Du Lac sends recruits into Stormwind, toward the gritty district of Old Town. Veteran fighters gather there to share combat experience far from the royal garrison’s rigid ways.

A Watchful Eye. Theocritus watches Morganth from the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest. He sends travelers east into Redridge Mountains to place an enchanted glyph at an old lion statue near the Tower of Ilgalar. Theocritus watches the hills from his tower in eastern Elwynn Forest. His rival, Morganth, is a powerful sorcerer who has claimed the Tower of Ilgalar in Redridge Mountains. Theocritus fears Morganth's dark magic may cross the border, so he made the Eye of Azora to watch the rogue wizard from afar.

Abercrombie. Abercrombie appears to be a feeble, eccentric hermit dwelling in a dilapidated shack in western Duskwood near Raven Hill Cemetery. Claiming to be a harmless recluse plagued by the horrors of the woods, he readily enlists sympathetic travelers to gather peculiar reagents and supplies on his behalf. Tucked away in the rotting shadows near Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie cuts a pathetic figure. He presents himself as an old man merely trying to survive the terrors of Duskwood, asking travelers to run modest errands into Darkshire for supplies, herbs, and thread. To those unfamiliar with the history of the region, he seems like just another unfortunate soul left behind as the province fell into decay.

Abercrombie's Crate. Abercrombie's Crate is a lost container of delicate tools and collected herbs belonging to the eccentric hermit Abercrombie. It rests abandoned near the entrance of the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound in southern Duskwood after the old man was chased off by marauding ogres. While wandering far from his shack in western Duskwood to gather vegetation, Abercrombie crossed paths with a hostile gang of ogres. Fleeing for his life, the old hermit dropped his crate of precious instruments and harvested botanicals. The ogres hauled his belongings back to their stronghold at the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, leaving the heavy chest sitting carelessly near their cave mouth.

Abominable Creatures. Abominable Creatures is a quest given by Captain Truman, a human loyalist desperately awaiting reinforcements on the outskirts of Lordaeron's fallen capital. Believing his commander—a revered Grand Marshal—is still valiantly fighting in the nearby Ruins of Lordaeron, Truman implores a capable adventurer to track him down. The mission exposes the grim fate of the kingdom's lost defenders and the bitter hostility smoldering among surviving loyalists. Captain Truman stands vigilant at his post, anxiously awaiting long-overdue reinforcements to support the defense of Lordaeron. Confident in the martial prowess of his superior—a renowned Grand Marshal whom he describes as a tall, statuesque hero—Truman remains bound by duty after being commanded to hold the line while his commander charged into the ongoing fray. Harboring deep suspicion toward outsiders and openly scorning those he considers lesser breeds, the captain refuses to trust local irregulars. When a capable traveler approaches, Truman seizes the opportunity to enlist aid, pleading for someone to venture into the ruined territory to check on his master's well-being and assess the battle.

Addle's Stead. Addle's Stead is an abandoned farmstead in southwestern Duskwood, lying quiet under the forest's gloom south of Raven Hill. While its original homesteaders fled long ago, the farm has become a hidden staging ground for the Defias Brotherhood. Like many of the forgotten homesteads scattered across Duskwood, Addle's Stead fell into disrepair when darkness and ruin enveloped the region. Rather than remaining empty, the farm has been repurposed by the Defias Brotherhood. Agents prowl the perimeter, lurk within the decrepit farmhouse, and stash supplies in the barn, using the shadowy cover of southwestern Duskwood to escape the notice of both the Night Watch and Stormwind authorities.

name.zhCN: 普罗德摩尔将军的命令

text.enUS: Admiral Proudmoore's Orders. Kul Tiras forces keep their coastal positions in Durotar, and Admiral Proudmoore's Orders lay out their plans. The documents were written before Daelin Proudmoore fell at Theramore and describe a campaign against the Horde. Admiral Proudmoore's Orders show that the Kul Tiras forces at Tiragarde Keep still mean to fight. Lieutenant Benedict's garrison holds the papers, which detail long-term maneuvers and fortifications against the Horde. The plans show that Daelin Proudmoore's offensive in Durotar was an organized campaign, built to continue after his death. For the Horde, the documents reveal Kul Tiras operations and possible reinforcements threatening its borders.

Ados Fragment. The Ados Fragment is an inscribed piece of stone recovered from the Whelgar's Excavation site in the Wetlands. Together with three companion shards, it forms the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic bearing enigmatic Titan inscriptions. Unearthed in the muddy trenches of Whelgar's Excavation, the Ados Fragment is one of four missing pieces required to reconstruct the Goaz Stone. Prior to raptors overrunning the dig site, Prospector Whelgar began translating the primary tablet, only to discover that the inscriptions broke off at crucial moments. The scattered pieces—named Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru—were lost across the ruins, concealed within ancient containers and dirt mounds amidst prowling beasts.

Aelthalyste. In the Undercity's War Quarter, Aelthalyste trains Forsaken priests in the power of Shadow. She guides their spiritual discipline and sends troll acolytes to their own elders in Orgrimmar. Aelthalyste trains Forsaken priests in the power of Shadow. While many priests across Azeroth revere the Holy Light, her students have turned from it. She rose as an incorporeal banshee and shares the spectral agony and relentless resolve of Sylvanas Windrunner's followers. From her chamber in the Undercity's War Quarter, she calls aspiring priests from distant outposts to master their darker arts. She teaches them to harness suffering as a weapon.

Aetheen of the Gales. This quest marks a rite of passage for young adventurers on Zephras Isle, directing them to report to one of the island's leading authorities. After completing early trials under Rorian the Dayseeker, promising youths are sent into Thendal Grove to meet Aetheen of the Gales, an elder who reads the winds and evaluates the next generation. The early tasks set before novitiates on Zephras Isle are not merely mundane chores; they serve as informal tests to evaluate whether rising youths possess the grit and spirit needed to defend their homeland. Recognizing that island life faces growing trials, mentors such as Rorian the Dayseeker keep a watchful eye on candidates who prove capable of handling greater responsibility.

After the Ambush. After a Dark Iron assault disrupts the delivery of blasting powder to the southern excavation site in Loch Modan, Huldar splits the duties with his partner Miran. Unwilling to risk another ambush alone, Miran requires a sturdy escort to carry the remaining supplies safely to the dig site. Transporting explosive mining powder through the hills of Loch Modan was never simple, but the open hostility of the Dark Iron dwarves turned routine labor into a lethal undertaking. Following an ambush spearheaded by Saean and his conspirators, the haulers Huldar and Miran find their routine shattered. With barrels scattered and the road perilous, the pair must divide their efforts: Huldar guards what remains behind, while Miran prepares to push forward with the next load.

name.deDE: Und wieder unter den geschrumpften Riesen

text.enUS: Again With the Zapped Giants. Zorbin Fandazzle knows you have already gathered residue, but can always use more. The Ultra-Shrinker is yours to use once more on the giants of Feralas, and Zorbin waits by the Forgotten Coast docks. Zorbin cannot pay nearly as much this time, but promises to spread word of your service. Zorbin Fandazzle admits you have gathered residue already, yet calls this an encore performance and says there is always room for more. Zorbin asks you to zap giants in Feralas once more with the Ultra-Shrinker and bring ten miniaturization residues from the shrunken giants to the docks of the Forgotten Coast. Since Zorbin cannot offer nearly as much in return, the offer is to praise your service among goblin friends, who have quite large ears.

Against Lord Shalzaru. Latronicus Moonspear at Feathermoon Stronghold tells you that scouts have identified one of the crueler naga royals, Lord Shalzaru. He asks you to put a stop to Shalzaru and bring back the relic the naga lord uncovered. New scouting reports have given Latronicus Moonspear a good picture of how the naga are led. Royals sit among their ranks, and it is they who give the orders. One of the crueler of them is Lord Shalzaru.

Against the Hatecrest. Latronicus Moonspear at Feathermoon Stronghold wants to meet the Hatecrest naga head-on rather than wait for them. He asks you for ten Hatecrest Scales in good condition. Whatever the naga are up to, Latronicus Moonspear assumes they will eventually try to claim the island for themselves, and aggressive steps are needed before it is too late. He wants ten Hatecrest Scales in good condition, and expects you to see for yourself how to get them. He counts on it weakening the naga presence on Sardor Isle and on it being your first time cutting your teeth on the naga.

Against the Hatecrest. Having reported back, you are sent on by General Shandris Feathermoon to Latronicus Moonspear, the general's second, in Feathermoon Stronghold. Shandris would like to commit a full force against the naga but will not leave the stronghold open to the Horde, or worse. General Shandris Feathermoon sends you on to Latronicus Moonspear, the general's second, who has been keeping a close watch on the naga forces so far. Shandris will assess the wider situation with the naga here. Much as a full force against them is wanted, leaving the stronghold open to a direct attack from the Horde, or something worse, seems less than ideal. Latronicus awaits you in Feathermoon Stronghold.

Agama'gor. Agama'gor stands north of the road from Camp Taurajo toward Mulgore. Bristleback quilboar hold this encampment in the southern Barrens, keeping pressure on the nearby Horde outpost. Agama'gor is a Bristleback stronghold in the southern Barrens. Its huts, brambles, and crude totems lie close to Camp Taurajo. The quilboar threaten travelers moving between the Barrens and Mulgore’s grassy hills, and Horde scouts and hunters fight to contain them.

Agamaggan. Agamaggan the Great Boar was one of the colossal Ancient Guardians who walked Azeroth in its earliest days. He fell ten thousand years ago fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients, and his sacrifice helped save Azeroth from ruin. Where his blood and body crashed into the earth, vast networks of thorny vines arose, creating the Razorfen and granting life and purpose to his descendants, the quilboar. Ten thousand years ago, during the War of the Ancients, the mighty demigod Agamaggan came forth to battle the Burning Legion. The colossal boar fought with terrifying ferocity, and though he ultimately fell in combat, his actions helped save Azeroth from ruin.

Agamaggan's Agility. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a blood shard ritual. The captive quilboar channels the power of his ancient boar god, blessing those who bring him shards from the Barrens with swift movement and sure aim. Crimson blood shards jut from the Barrens soil, especially near quilboar encampments and colossal brambles. Quilboar tradition says the crystals formed from Agamaggan's spilled blood. The Great Boar Ancient fell fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Even locked in a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo, the elder quilboar Mangletooth knows how to channel the stones' dormant divine power for anyone who brings them.

Agamaggan's Strength. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde travelers Agamaggan's Strength in return for Blood Shards. The captive Razormane shaman draws on his people's reverence for the ancient boar demigod and his hatred of the rival Bristleback tribe. The quilboar honor Agamaggan, an ancient boar demigod whose spilled blood is said to have formed the red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. They treat the crystals as sacred, drawing on their power to strengthen their front-line fighters. Mangletooth, an elder Razormane shaman held captive in Camp Taurajo, offers this strength to Horde champions. He claims your foes will cower as they do before the Razormane's mightiest champions.

Agamand Family Axe. The Agamand Family Axe is an ancestral heirloom preserved within the Agamand family crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a martial symbol of the wealthy mill-owning dynasty, it is sought by Coleman Farthing to strip the undead family of their remaining dignity. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty reigned as prosperous landowners across the northern hills of Tirisfal Glades, maintaining vast mills and a private family crypt. The Agamand Family Axe rested among the ancestral arms entombed alongside deceased patriarchs and warriors, kept intact on underground weapon racks even as the Scourge overran the estate and slaughtered its inhabitants.

Agamand Family Crypt. Tucked into the hills just north of Agamand Mills, the Agamand Family Crypt is the ancient resting ground of one of Tirisfal's wealthiest farming dynasties. Now claimed by the Scourge under Captain Dargol, its tombs have been ripped open, and the slumbering ancestors raised as mindless terrors. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held expansive estates across northern Tirisfal Glades, entombing their forebears within this hillside mausoleum. When the Plague brought ruin to the kingdom, the crypt fell into the clutches of Captain Dargol, an agent of the Scourge. Rather than letting the wealthy lineage rest in peace, Dargol employed dark necromancy to awaken the entombed skeletons and vengeful apparitions, transforming a sacred burial ground into an aggressive Scourge foothold right on the edge of Forsaken territory.

name.esES: Daga de la familia de Agamand

text.enUS: Agamand Family Dagger. The Agamand Family Dagger is an ancestral heirloom of the fallen Agamand dynasty, resting on weapon racks within their ancestral crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Coleman Farthing seeks this blade alongside the rest of their family arsenal to strip his former masters of their remaining legacy and honor. Before the Third War, the Agamand family maintained vast estates and grain mills across the rolling meadows of Tirisfal Glades. Like the rest of their lineage's armaments, the Agamand Family Dagger survived the devastation wrought by the Scourge, locked within the family crypt north of Agamand Mills. Protected by the restless, undead remnants of the household and mindless minions of the Lich King, the dagger represents the prestige and martial heritage that once elevated the family above their servants and tenants.

name.esES: Maza de la familia de Agamand

text.enUS: Agamand Family Mace. The Agamand Family Mace is an ancestral heirloom preserved within the Agamand Family Crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a symbol of pride for a wealthy dynasty of northern Lordaeron, it has become an object of spiteful retribution sought by their former servant Coleman Farthing. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held extensive farmlands and windmills in the northern reaches of Tirisfal Glades. Like the rest of the regional aristocracy, they fell before the plague of undeath. The Agamands were reanimated as mindless thralls in service to the Lich King, wandering their ruined estate while their ancient family treasures remained locked within the depths of the family crypt. The Agamand Family Mace is stored among these weapons, an emblem of a forgotten lineage now reduced to shambling Scourge.

name.esES: Espada de la familia de Agamand

text.enUS: Agamand Family Sword. The Agamand Family Sword is a tarnished ancestral blade kept inside the Agamand Family Crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a proud symbol of the wealthy mill-owning dynasty, it is sought by the Forsaken Coleman Farthing to erase the final vestiges of his former masters' legacy. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty held immense wealth and influence across the rolling mills of northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, the family met a gruesome end, their bodies raised into mindless thralls of the Lich King. Their ancestral weapons, including the ceremonial family sword, were sealed away in the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern edge of the mills. Stripping these blades from their burial racks serves not merely as looting, but as a deliberate act to break whatever memory and noble standing remains of the fallen household.

Agamand Heirlooms. Coleman Farthing tasks adventurers with plundering the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern end of Agamand Mills. Driven by bitter resentment over his mortal demise, he seeks to strip his former masters of their ancestral weapons and erase their final remnants of dignity. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Coleman Farthing served the wealthy and influential Agamand family at their expansive mills in Tirisfal Glades. Whatever occurred during the fall of their estate, Farthing blames his former lords entirely for his death. Now raised into undeath among the Forsaken, he views the Agamands' downfall with spiteful satisfaction, rejoicing that the once-proud dynasty has been reduced to mindless minions enslaved to the Lich King.

Agamand Mills. Agamand Mills is a sprawling farm and windmill complex nestled in the northern heights of Tirisfal Glades. Once the proud estate of the wealthy Agamand dynasty, it has fallen into ruin and stands as the largest Scourge stronghold in the region. The wealthy Agamand family built their estate around a vast milling network across northern Tirisfal. When the Third War broke out and the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the patriarch Gregor Agamand refused to flee, fortifying the compound and convincing his retainers and laborers to make their stand. Their provisions and stone walls might have held, but their youngest son, Devlin Agamand, betrayed his blood. Devlin slaughtered the estate watchmen and let the walking dead into the sleeping quarters. Crippled from within, the remaining defenders were wiped out, and the family joined the mindless ranks of the undead.

Agathelos the Raging. Agathelos the Raging is a colossal armored boar penned within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. To the quilboar, whose god and progenitor is the great boar Agamaggan, a beast of his size carries considerable spiritual significance, and he grows even more fearsome when enraged. His sheer mass and strength make him one of the most dangerous beasts lurking under the southern Barrens. The god and progenitor of the quilboar is Agamaggan, a titanic boar. A beast the size of Agathelos—standing roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard—therefore carries considerable spiritual significance among the Razorfen tribes.

Aggem Thorncurse. Aggem Thorncurse is a living quilboar shaman in Razorfen Kraul, bearing the title Death's Head Prophet. He calls a boar spirit to his aid when threatened. Aggem guards a part of Razorfen Kraul occupied by the Death's Head tribe. His shamanic powers include summoning a boar spirit, reflecting the quilboar's reverence for Agamaggan.

Aggressive Encroachment. Aggressive Encroachment is a task issued by Valreaa Valewind to protect the local settlement from desperate wildlife. Ursera from a nearby den have grown increasingly bold, wandering into the village and threatening its inhabitants. The ursera population nesting southwest of the village has become an urgent safety hazard. Recently, a hungry adolescent beast strayed right up to the base of the village's central elder tree, nearly mauling a young child playing nearby. The settlement's rangers were forced to cut the creature down before tragedy struck.

name.frFR: Des agitateurs, des provocateurs, des animaux

text.enUS: Agitators. Agitators is an early task on Zephras Isle issued by Yala Windwatcher. The aggressive Al'Aketh cult has pushed into Thendal Grove, agitating the peaceful native wind sprites into hostile elementals. Adventurers are sent to disperse the roiling winds and clear out the cultist converts threatening the area. Thendal Grove has fallen under the shadow of the Al'Aketh cult. Known for their unsettling designs on Zephras Isle, the cultists have encroached on the grove and actively riled the delicate wind spirits dwelling there. Once peaceful sprites have turned violent, forming volatile roiling winds that threaten anyone passing through the region.

Agmond's End. Agmond's End is an abandoned dwarven excavation site tucked into the southern hills of the Badlands. Once a hopeful exploratory dig led by the prospector Agmond, the camp turned into a slaughterhouse when burrowing troggs overran the operation and killed its leader. Like many sites in the arid Badlands, Agmond's End began as a dwarven venture to uncover ancient relics and delve into the earth's buried history. That dream ended abruptly when savage troggs surged from the surrounding crevices and overwhelmed the miners. Agmond himself was cut down during the attack, giving the site its grim name. Today, the ruined dig remains utterly infested by Stonevault troggs, with shattered crates and abandoned tools left exactly where they fell.

Ahanu. Ahanu is a tauren merchant operating within Hewa's Armory on the lower rise of Thunder Bluff. He crafts and trades leather armor to travelers and young braves setting out across Mulgore and the wider plains. He also helps newly arrived couriers navigate the bluffs when delivering messages from nearby settlements. Situated amidst the leatherworking stalls and armories of Thunder Bluff's lower rise, Ahanu provides vital equipment to those who make their living across Kalimdor's grasslands. Working hides sent by his friend Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads, he represents the everyday tradesfolk who keep the tauren capital supplied with durable cured and tanned hide gear. For travelers fresh off a wind rider from the Crossroads, Ahanu frequently serves as a first point of contact in the grand city, receiving deliveries and directing messengers toward the local flight roosts.

Ahanu's Leather Goods. Ahanu's Leather Goods is a bundled consignment of finished leather armor and supplies crafted atop the mesas of Thunder Bluff. Prepared by the leatherworker Ahanu, the parcel is bound for the Crossroads in the Barrens to supply wandering hunters and adventurers. The supply lines of the Horde depend on practical trade between established strongholds and frontier outposts. In Thunder Bluff, the artisan Ahanu works raw hides into finished apparel and gear, preparing this consignment specifically for trade beyond Mulgore. The bundle is destined for Jahan Hawkwing, a merchant operating in the bustling heart of the Barrens at the Crossroads. Because overland travel across the plains is slow, transporting the bundle introduces messengers to the aerial courier network maintained by the tauren, relying on Tal and Devrak's trained wind riders to ferry goods swiftly across long distances.

Aid For The Refugees. Aid For The Refugees centers on the displaced survivors of Ban'aethal, a settlement deep within Shadowgale Forest that was suddenly evacuated in the middle of the night. With their home falling into the sky and the surrounding wilderness grown far too perilous to enter, the refugees rely on brave travelers to recover the belongings they had to leave behind. Aid for the Refugees is an appeal for assistance from Ealaane and her fellow displaced villagers. Having narrowly fled their homes deep in Shadowgale Forest, the survivors have gathered together with almost nothing to their names, hoping a passing traveler will brave the dangers they left behind.

Ak'Zeloth. Neeru Fireblade sends you from Orgrimmar into the Barrens after signs of demonic corruption emerge. His contact waits near the border. Neeru Fireblade says the Burning Blade still threatens the Horde with demonic corruption. After you bring him a Burning Blade insignia collar from Durotar, he sends you into the Barrens. A cult gathers around the Demon Seed, an artifact of vile power, and Neeru wants you to find his contact near the border.

Akiris by the Bundle. Privateer Bloads in Booty Bay is looking to acquire bundles of valuable akiris reeds for an associate named Groy. The plants have to be taken from the naga, who were last spotted on the northern beach. Privateer Bloads offers work in Booty Bay for anyone willing to tackle a seaside venture. An associate named Groy pays handsomely for bundles of akiris reed, a reed that grows by the sea and that the naga call by that name. Bloads does not know why Groy wants them, only that ten stalks are needed and that the naga were last spotted on the northern beach.

Akiris by the Bundle. Privateer Bloads in Stranglethorn Vale needs a fresh bundle of akiris reeds transported across the sea to Dustwallow Marsh. A contact named Privateer Groy has a client in Theramore Isle who wants more right away, and Bloads himself will not be heading there for a week. Word has arrived from across the sea while you were away. Privateer Groy in Theramore Isle sent word to Privateer Bloads expressing satisfaction with the prior shipment of akiris reeds, noting that an interested client demands more immediately. With Bloads not scheduled to sail for Dustwallow Marsh for another week, he entrusts you with the packaged parcel of reeds to deliver by hand.

Aku'mai. Aku'mai is a monstrous, three-headed hydra dwelling in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps along the Zoram Strand. A servant of an Old God, it rose from the waters when that Old God's corruption tainted the temple's sacred Moon Well. The Twilight's Hammer cult has gathered in the Deeps and sacrifices innocents to it for power. Blackfathom Deeps was once a great temple of Elune, until the corruption of an Old God seeped up from beneath the earth and tainted its sacred Moon Well. Aku'mai, a gargantuan hydra and servant of the Old God, rose from the waters. Rather than an ordinary denizen of the tides, Aku'mai is a living blight upon the Zoram Strand that has taken up residence in the submerged ruins of the night elves' fallen temple, poisoning the waters with its malice.

Aku'mai's Lair. Aku'mai's Lair is the deepest and darkest cavern within Blackfathom Deeps. Located beyond the Moonshrine Sanctum, this submerged hollow serves as the nesting ground for Aku'mai, a monstrous hydra venerated as a servant of the Old Gods. Sealed away behind the Moonshrine Sanctum, Aku'mai's Lair represents the culmination of the corruption sweeping Blackfathom Deeps. To enter the cavern, dark rituals must be engaged by igniting the four brazier fires flanking a naga statue, awakening guardians sworn to defend the threshold. Beyond these heavy double doors lies a sunless, flooded grotto. Here, both the Twilight's Hammer cultists and invading naga gather in reverence of Aku'mai, an ancient three-headed hydra considered a living servant of the Old Gods.

Al'Aketh Thugs. The peaceful roads around Thendal Grove are threatened by a violent band of Al'Aketh cultists occupying the nearby temple ruins. Dispatched from the Shrine of Akir under orders to harass wayfarers and force recruits into their ranks, these zealots pose an immediate danger to local travelers. Hanaa Nightwind tasks adventurers with breaking their hold and slaying their brutish commander. Just southwest of Thendal Grove lie ancient temple ruins that should offer quiet shelter to wanderers. Instead, the grounds have been overtaken by the Al'Aketh, an aggressive cult driven by fanatical ambition. Far from peaceful worshipers, these cultists act as highwaymen and enforcers, preying upon those traveling along the outskirts of the grove. The Rangers stationed nearby suspect these ruffians were sent directly by High Priestess Lorthuna from the Shrine of Akir to bully and coerce the populace into bowing to the cult's influence.

Alamar Grimm. Alamar Grimm is a gnome warlock trainer stationed in Coldridge Valley at Anvilmar. Bitter over the tragic loss of Gnomeregan, he distrusts outsiders and focuses on teaching fledgling warlocks how to harness dark arts and summon their first demonic minions. While most gnomes in Coldridge Valley channel their energies into recovery and tinkering, Alamar Grimm harbors a deep resentment over the fall of Gnomeregan. He holds a cynical view of standard adventurers and even the host dwarves of Ironforge, grumbling that their allies care more about diplomacy with humans than reclaiming the fallen techno-city. Operating from Anvilmar, he seeks kindred spirits who understand that ruthless power may be what his people truly need.

Alanndarian Nightsong. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong tends to Darkshore's sickened wildlife. She works with travelers to ease the afflictions spreading through the region, especially among its deer. Alanndarian Nightsong watches over Darkshore's wildlife from the coastal settlement of Auberdine. Taints in the soil and water have left creatures of the ancient woods sick and strangely aggressive. She seeks ways to ease their suffering and restore their strength.

Alaric's Remains. Alaric's Remains are the recovered bones of an individual once interred in a shallow grave along Silverpine Forest. His lingering spirit bids travelers to carry what is left of him past the Rot Hide gnolls into the towers of Fenris Keep. Unearthed from an unremarkable shallow grave in Silverpine Forest, the remains belong to Alaric, a former resident of Fenris Isle. Rather than linger in an exposed pit, his spirit yearns for the place he cherished in life. He asks whoever unearths his bones to leave his ill-fitting boots behind and bring his skeletal remains directly into the keep, seeking quiet sanctuary far away from the scavengers prowling the mainland.

Aldrassil. Young kaldorei gather beneath Aldrassil’s vast boughs in Shadowglen. The settlement shelters trainers, merchants, and local leaders in hollows carved through the great tree. Aldrassil shelters young night elves in Shadowglen. Ramps wind through its immense trunk, passing trainers and artisans on the way to the high roost. Tenaron Stormgrip watches over the glade’s protection from there. Beyond the tree, Teldrassil stretches across the horizon, while novices learn their arts beneath Aldrassil’s canopy before venturing into Kalimdor’s troubled wilds.

Alexston Farmstead. At Alexston Farmstead, wild Harvest Watchers prowl the ruined fields. Baros Alexston grew up here before becoming Stormwind's city architect. Alexston Farmstead lies amid Westfall's dry plains, abandoned like the neighboring estates. Its caretakers fled when banditry spread across the countryside. Now the fields have grown wild, and the Harvest Watchers left to tend the crops attack anyone who comes near the barren farmhouse.

Algaz Station. Algaz Station is a dwarven military outpost situated in northwestern Loch Modan, directly south of the fortified pass of Dun Algaz. Manning the approach to the northern tunnels, its garrison of Mountaineers helps safeguard travelers and watch the frontier leading toward the Wetlands. Perched just east of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, Algaz Station serves as a vital strategic watchpoint for the kingdom of Ironforge. A cadre of dwarven Mountaineers maintains a permanent vigil here, keeping the vital road between Loch Modan and the northern lowlands open to trade and troop movements. Given the frequent threats in the surrounding hills, from wandering beasts to encroaching troggs, the outpost provides respite, repairs, and martial support for weary travelers before they venture through the mountain tunnels.

Alien Egg. The Alien Egg is an unusual and mysterious clutch found guarded by local wind serpents across the canyons of Thousand Needles. Despite its unfamiliar appearance, the native serpents protect the egg fiercely as if it were their own. Its presence has aroused the curiosity and concern of the tauren scouts stationed atop Freewind Post. Discovered resting at the base of the towering spires south and northeast of Freewind Post, the Alien Egg stands out dramatically from the typical fauna of the canyon floor. Rather than abandoning or destroying the odd clutch, the native serpents of the needles fiercely guard it alongside their own nests. Hagar Lightninghoof, a tauren brave keeping watch from the heights of Freewind Post, sought to retrieve the specimen to determine whether it represented a threat to the mesa settlements or merely an unusual variation of local reptilian life.

Alien Egg. Rumors among the tauren of Freewind Post speak of a bizarre, foreign egg guarded fiercely by wild serpents on the canyon floor. Hagar Lightninghoof tasks Horde adventurers with tracking down and retrieving the specimen before whatever lurks inside breaks free. Word reached Freewind Post of an unusual egg spotted deep in the serpent dens that dot the canyon floor beneath the towering stone needles. The serpents native to the canyon watch over the egg as though it were their own brood, striking out at any traveler who ventures too close. Intrigued and wary of what might threaten the local hunting grounds, Hagar Lightninghoof asks brave scouts to locate the clutch, bypass the slithering sentries, and secure the oddity for study.

Allegiance to the Old Gods. Allegiance to the Old Gods is a Horde quest initiated by recovering a waterlogged message from the naga inside Blackfathom Deeps. Delivering the note to Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost uncovers a sinister ritual plot unfolding deep within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. While battling the naga of Blackfathom Deeps, Horde scouts discover a damp, crumpled note bearing frantic handwriting. The scribbled parchment details instructions directed toward the naga priestesses, ordering them to gather elemental water crystals. Far from random pillaging, these crystals are being collected to fuel the summonings of naga aquamancers, marshaling elemental forces for a far darker objective.

Allegiance to the Old Gods. Allegiance to the Old Gods is a Horde quest tasking adventurers with eliminating Lorgus Jett within the depths of Blackfathom Deeps. Directed by the Darkspear seer Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost, the mission aims to disrupt the Twilight's Hammer cultists who seek to awaken ancient forces of destruction. Striking down Lorgus deals a direct blow to the cult's subversive operations beneath Ashenvale's coast. Perched on the strand of Ashenvale, the Horde outpost at Zoram'gar keeps a nervous watch over Blackfathom Deeps. The submerged temple complex has become a breeding ground for dark sorcery, overrun by naga, corrupted beasts, and the cloaked fanatics of the Twilight's Hammer. Je'neu Sancrea, an earthen ring seer stationed on the coast, recognizes that the cultists do not revere the natural balance or spirits of the land. Instead, they pledge their servitude to the Old Gods—monstrous beings of chaos defeated in ancient eras whose malign touch still lingers in Azeroth's forgotten places.

Alliance. The Alliance is a grand coalition of mortal races bound by shared ideals of honor, duty, and the defense of order across Azeroth. Born out of the ashes of the northern kingdom of Lordaeron, its current heart beats in Stormwind City, united alongside the dwarves of Ironforge, the exiled gnomes, and the night elves of Kalimdor. The modern Alliance descends from the original Alliance of Lordaeron, founded when Sir Anduin Lothar led Stormwind refugees north during the Second War to unite the Seven Kingdoms, dwarves, and high elves against the Old Horde. While the Scourge and the Third War decimated the north—leaving Lordaeron in ruins and driving the survivors into scattered resistance—the restored Kingdom of Stormwind rose to fill the void. Today, Stormwind stands as the preeminent seat of human leadership, carrying the banners of honor and faith into a fractured world.

Alliance Relations. Thrall seeks a careful hand to preserve peace with the Alliance. In Orgrimmar, Craven Drok sends seasoned Horde adventurers to find Keldran near the western exit. The work calls for quiet diplomacy and intelligence to protect Thrall’s fragile peace. Thrall knows war with the Alliance could ruin his young nation. Raised in human captivity, the Warchief learned human statecraft and military strategy. Craven Drok watches for warriors and champions with patience for a subtler path, one that looks beyond raw force.

Alliance Relations. In Orgrimmar, Alliance advances across Kalimdor raise fears of dangerous political fallout. The Horde sends orders to Desolace to purge demons before the Alliance can accuse Thrall's people of renewed ties to the Burning Legion. Alliance scouts and expeditions crossing Kalimdor put the Horde in a delicate position. Demonic remnants across central Kalimdor could confirm old suspicions that the orcs and their allies still serve the Burning Legion. With Warchief Thrall's sanction, Keldran oversees operations from Orgrimmar to clear those remnants before hostile Alliance factions can use them to justify war.

Alliance Trauma. Alliance Trauma is a summons directing accomplished field medics to report to Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh. Dispatched by first aid instructors across Alliance capitals, it invites skilled practitioners to study under Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen, the chief physician of the Alliance's elite medical corps. Once a medic masters the fundamental techniques taught in the great Alliance cities, local instructors can teach them little more. For those who demonstrate exceptional aptitude with needle, cloth, and triage, word is sent directly to Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen. Operating from the frontier stronghold of Theramore Isle, VanHowzen oversees Alliance Trauma, the organization charged with saving lives in the most brutal warzones of Kalimdor and beyond.

Alliance of Lordaeron. The Alliance of Lordaeron was the historic grand coalition of the seven human kingdoms, Khaz Modan dwarves, Wildhammer gryphon riders, gnomes, and high elves formed to resist the Old Horde in the Second War. Led militarily by Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and diplomatically by King Terenas Menethil II, it shattered the invading orcish forces and secured the Eastern Kingdoms. Though political fractures and the devastation of the Scourge tore it apart during the Third War, its legacy laid the foundation for the current Alliance. Following the horrific sack of Stormwind in the First War, Regent Lord Anduin Lothar brought the battered southern refugees across the Great Sea to Capital City. Pleading their cause before King Terenas Menethil II, Lothar convinced him to gather the rulers of the human nations in council. Old rivalries and border tensions ran deep, but the threat of the Horde outweighed them. Choosing Lothar as their Supreme Commander, the seven human nations bound themselves together in a desperate pact.

Alpha Strike. Hadoken Swiftstrider has a plan to break the impasse with the Woodpaw gnolls: strike down several of their leaders, who call themselves Alphas, in quick succession. Hadoken wants you to be the one to carry it out. Hadoken reasons that if the gnoll leaders, who call themselves Alphas, fall one after another, their ranks will be thrown into chaos. It might also send the message that the Horde can and will destroy them. You are to carry out Hadoken's will: five Alphas down inside a single hour, or the stalemate stays.

name.esES: Altar de la Tempestad (Las Estepas Ardientes)

text.enUS: Altar of Storms (Burning Steppes). Perched in the jagged crags of the Burning Steppes, the Altar of Storms is a dark monument dedicated to fel rituals and demonic power. Blackrock clan warlocks occupy the sinister site, performing foul magic beneath the shadow of Blackrock Spire. Its dark aura draws ambitious practitioners of the shadow from across Azeroth. Constructed during the earlier wars to channel corrupting fel magic, the Altar of Storms stands as a grim monument to dark pacts. In the Burning Steppes, hostile warlocks of the Blackrock clan control the grounds, conducting occult rituals and drawing upon demonic forces. Nearby, the encampment of the hermit Gorzeeki Wildeyes and his master Mor'zul Bloodbringer overlooks the site, where renegade practitioners study its violent energies and concoct demanding rituals for ambitious spellcasters seeking greater dark power.

Alterac (kingdom). Alterac was one of the seven historic human kingdoms, nestled high in the rugged Alterac Mountains. During the Second War, its ruler, King Aiden Perenolde, made a treacherous pact with the Old Horde to spare his realm, leading to the kingdom's military downfall and total collapse. Today, its ruined capital lies abandoned in the snow, while dispossessed nobles and outlaws wage a guerrilla war under the banner of the Syndicate. Alterac arose thousands of years ago as an Arathorian city-state following the Troll Wars. Settlers capitalized on strategic mountain passes and trading outposts, eventually establishing an independent realm when the empire fractured. Though rugged and mountainous, Alterac bordered the prosperous lands of Lordaeron and Stromgarde. Historically, it fielded tough mountain fighters, but enduring border friction with Thoras Trollbane's Stromgarde left the kingdom politically isolated from its neighbors long before the Dark Portal ever opened.

Alterac Granite. Alterac Granite is a prized, durable stone quarried from the mountainous terrain of northern Lordaeron, specifically around Darrow Hill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Revered by master stonecutters for its exceptional resilience and grain, it is chosen by King Magni Bronzebeard's royal mason to carve an enduring tribute for fallen soldiers. When King Magni Bronzebeard ordered a monument to commemorate Sully Balloo—a brave dwarven defender who perished in the tragedy at the Thandol Span—ordinary quarry stone would not do. Grand Mason Marblesten, tasked with sculpting the memorial in Ironforge, insisted on obtaining Alterac Granite. Renowned as one of the finest stones available across the Eastern Kingdoms, its legendary durability ensures that the likeness and memory of a fallen hero can endure untarnished for generations.

Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, snow-capped range rising directly above the rolling pastures of Hillsbrad. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the slopes now harbor ruined settlements, bandit factions, and dangerous wilderness where travelers rarely walk unguarded. Long before the hills fell into chaos, these highlands formed the sovereign nation of Alterac, one of the seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. That legacy shattered during the Second War when King Aiden Perenolde struck a clandestine pact with the Old Horde, allowing orcish forces passage through the peaks in exchange for his kingdom's safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed Perenolde, leaving the region fractured by martial law and territorial disputes.

Alterac Mountains (Classic). The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, overcast highland rising sharply north of Hillsbrad Foothills, crowned with permanent snow and jagged peaks. Once the home of the human kingdom of Alterac and the scholarly redoubts of Dalaran, the region now lies largely in ruins, fought over by brutal ogres, noble-born bandits, and the opposing armies of Alterac Valley. Rising high above the Hillsbrad lowlands, the Alterac Mountains are a harsh realm of rain, pine, and high-altitude snow. Once anchored by three major human powers—the mountain kingdom of Alterac, the magocracy of Dalaran, and the fortified town of Strahnbrad—the region collapsed under betrayal and war. Today, the ruined capital of Alterac is squatted by the Crushridge ogres, Strahnbrad is occupied by outlaws, and among the shattered remnants of Dalaran its surviving wizards work tirelessly to restore their ruined sanctuary.

Altered Beings. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem studies strange changes in the Barrens' oasis waters. Fissures beneath the pools may be changing the creatures that live there, and he asks you to bring him shells from altered snapjaws. Tonga Runetotem is searching for the cause of strange changes in the Barrens' oases. Though the savanna is dry, a handful of pools support fertile ground. Tonga found peculiar fissures beneath those waters, sending out potent energies. He does not know whether the force came from outside or rose from deep within the earth. Now he studies the creatures that drink from and live in the pools, hoping to learn what the fissures are doing to them.

Altered Snapjaw Shell. At the Lushwater and Stagnant Oases, snapjaws bear altered shells that draw a druid’s attention. Their carapaces may reveal what the fissures beneath the Barrens are doing to local wildlife. Oasis snapjaws have changed in ways that trouble those who study the land. The freshwater turtles of Lushwater and Stagnant Oases are believed to drink from springs fed by mysterious underground fissures. Their altered carapaces have caught the attention of researchers at the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem, a tauren druid, gathers the shells as he seeks to understand the land’s health. He wants to learn whether energies rising from deep below are an unnatural blight or something stranger.

Althea Ebonlocke. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads the Night Watch, the beleaguered town guard protecting Darkshire from the terrors of Duskwood. A relative of Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, she shoulders the defense of an isolated region abandoned by Stormwind's regular military. She organizes patrols, tasks adventurers with culling local horrors, and coordinates the town's survival against constant monstrous threats. While her relative, Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, handles civil governance within the town hall, Commander Althea directs Darkshire's thin line of physical defense. When Stormwind failed to deploy royal troops to guard Duskwood against creeping horrors, the citizenry formed the Night Watch. Under Althea's steady, unyielding command, these volunteers patrol the fog-shrouded roads, keeping skeletal undead, ferocious wolves, and spiders from overrunning the town perimeter.

Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a pivotal training assignment given to Alliance rogues by Lucius in Lakeshire. Dispatched to the nearby mill with a set of thieves' tools, initiates are tasked with infiltrating an area under Blackrock orc scrutiny to crack a locked chest and retrieve a token of thievery. In Lakeshire, rogue instructors do not bother with abstract lectures when a locked chest can teach the lesson faster. Lucius sends promising operatives northeast along the road to Alther's Mill, equipping them with their first set of thieves' tools. To earn their formal Certificate of Thievery, novices must slip into the abandoned mill, pick open Lucius's personal lockbox, and bring back the token cached within.

Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a Redridge Mountains quest given by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire. The foreman needs adventurers to clear out a dangerous tarantula infestation at the nearby lumber mill so workers can safely retrieve the timber required to finish the Lakeshire bridge. Foreman Oslow has his hands full attempting to keep bridge repairs on schedule in Lakeshire. Between hostile Blackrock orcs, encroaching gnoll packs, and aggressive murlocs along Lake Everstill, his workforce is pushed to the limit. The latest disruption strikes directly at his supply chain: Alther's Mill, the lumber operation to the east, has been overrun by giant tarantulas, halting timber shipments needed for the town's bridge.

Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a ruined lumber mill tucked into the rugged hills northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital source of processed timber for local builders, the abandoned grounds have deteriorated into a haven for feral scavengers and prowling predators. For adventurers traveling east toward Stonewatch, the dilapidated structures serve as a grim landmark marking the boundary of safe frontier territory. Before the region fell prey to invading predators and orc raids, Alther's Mill bustled with timber trade that supplied the construction of Lakeshire and surrounding settlements. Its quiet clearing northeast of Lake Everstill provided ready access to mountain timber stands. As turmoil mounted across the kingdom of Stormwind and the Blackrock clan pushed down from the heights of Stonewatch, local millers abandoned the facility, leaving the dry timber buildings and wheel to decay into rot.

Altsoba Ragetotem. Altsoba Ragetotem is a tauren weaponsmith stationed at Bloodvenom Post in Felwood. From this remote Horde outpost, he keeps passing champions armed with reliable maces, staves, and axes to face the blighted horrors of the forest. Bloodvenom Post is a treacherous outpost, situated in the heart of Felwood amidst demonic corruption and tainted wildlife. Maintaining a supply line out here is a grim necessity, and Altsoba Ragetotem does his part by outfitting Horde scouts and travelers. Whether someone requires a sturdy crescent axe or a heavy war maul, Altsoba ensures warriors heading into the corrupted timberlands do not enter the fray unarmed.

Alyissia. In Aldrassil, Alyissia trains young night elves to fight with strength and discipline. She teaches warriors how to defend the young world tree. Alyissia trains young night elves inside Aldrassil, where they learn to fight with steel and shield instead of nature magic or the priesthood. Kaldorei forces are known for their Sentinels and stealthy archers, but danger across Kalimdor also calls for fighters who can hold the front line. Alyissia teaches the first techniques: how to direct battle fury, master a stance, and withstand the wild creatures and corrupted grells that press into Shadowglen.

Amber Kearnen. In Westfall, Amber Kearnen watches the Defias Brotherhood for SI:7. From a hidden vantage point, she tracks their unlawful activity for Master Mathias Shaw. Amber Kearnen scouts for SI:7 in Westfall, far from the halls of Stormwind Keep. She watches an abandoned tower the Defias Brotherhood has taken over. Master Mathias Shaw leads her work directly. Kearnen briefs covert operatives sent to stop Defias threats and gather intelligence across the contested countryside.

Ambercorn. Ambercorn is a sacred nut that falls from the tall, ancient trees scattered across Mulgore. Infused with natural magic, it serves as a vital reagent in tauren shamanic brews, most notably used to induce spiritual visions during youth trials. Gathered from beneath the sturdy boughs of Mulgore's great trees, ambercorns are more than ordinary nuts to the tauren. Rich with the spiritual vitality of the land, they hold latent magical properties that tauren mystics have understood and utilized for generations. Young hunters and wanderers learn early to keep their eyes on the grass beneath the canopy, honoring the Earth Mother's gifts that fall freely from above.

Ambermill. Ambermill is a fortified human settlement in southeastern Silverpine Forest, situated just southwest of Lordamere Lake. Once a quiet lumber village, it is now occupied by surviving wizards and apprentices of Dalaran. Their presence represents a dangerous outpost of human resistance on the southern borders of the Forsaken realm. Before the Third War, Ambermill was a quiet lumber town of little importance. In the chaotic aftermath of Lordaeron's fall, the surviving wizards of the Kirin Tor moved in and fortified the settlement. Dalaran spellscribes, conjurors, and apprentices now patrol its buildings and stables, using Ambermill as a forward redoubt against the undead.

Ambermill Investigations. Ambermill Investigations is a Forsaken mission assigned by Shadow Priest Allister from the Sepulcher. With Dalaran wizards weaving magic in the nearby town of Ambermill, the Forsaken must disrupt their spellwork and strip their magical foci to keep hold of Silverpine Forest. The human town of Ambermill sits nestled in the hills of eastern Silverpine Forest, firmly occupied by wizards and defenders pledged to the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. As the mages engage in a vast, concerted ritual to weave magical energies, Shadow Priest Allister and his companion Dalar recognize an immediate peril. If the Kirin Tor are permitted to channel their power unchecked, the Forsaken risk being swept out of Silverpine entirely.

Amberstill Ranch. Amberstill Ranch is a tranquil dwarven homestead nestled along the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, directly north of Gol'Bolar Quarry. It serves as the primary breeding and training grounds for Ironforge's celebrated mountain rams. Adventurers visit the ranch to acquire hardy dwarven mounts, train in riding, or help the family defend their livestock from local predators. Tucked against the crags of Dun Morogh, Amberstill Ranch is renowned throughout Khaz Modan for raising the sturdiest mountain rams in the Eastern Kingdoms. The Amberstill family manages the stables and paddocks, training these sure-footed beasts to navigate treacherous snowy passes and steep alpine cliffs. Outside of supplying riding mounts and domestic livestock, the family often contends with the savage fauna of the hills, particularly wandering wendigos drawn by the scent of fresh flock.

Ameth'Aran. In Ameth'Aran, broken colonnades mark the ruin of a once-great Highborne city in southern Darkshore. Queen Azshara's nobles practiced arcane sorcery here before the Great Sundering shattered the ancient world. Now the vengeful ghosts of the elves who died here haunt the stones. Before the Great Sundering, Ameth'Aran and its sister settlement, Bashal'Aran, were twin centers of Highborne influence along the ancient coastline. Favored by Queen Azshara, Ameth'Aran's ruling nobles devoted themselves to unrestrained arcane experiments. The sorcerer Athrikus Narassin governed from afar in the Tower of Althalaxx. The city thrived until the Well of Eternity collapsed and tore the Kaldorei Empire apart.

Amethyst Phial. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the Amethyst Phial to travelers in Dolanaar. They carry it to the Oracle Glade to gather water from the moonwell beneath the Oracle Tree. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the Amethyst Phial to travelers on Teldrassil. It is the final vessel used in the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage. They carry it to the far northwest of the boughs, to the Oracle Glade. Beneath the ancient canopy of the Oracle Tree lies the island’s first and most potent moonwell. The phial is dipped into its radiant waters to gather the essence of Elune’s grace. Druids and priestesses study and tend to the World Tree’s unpredictable growth with that water.

Ammo for Rumbleshot. Gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot is running low on shot and powder for the riflemen practicing outside Anvilmar. A missing crate of ammunition was abandoned in the snowy wilds near the Grizzled Den when a courier was routed by hungry wendigo. Loslor Rudge at Steelgrill's Depot keeps steady supply lines flowing to tradesmen across Dun Morogh, but the valley's wildlife often interferes. His latest shipment of heavy ammunition never reached Hegnar Rumbleshot's roadside workshop. While camping near the cave system known as the Grizzled Den, the terrified courier crossed paths with local wendigo and fled for his life, abandoning the heavy wooden crate in the snow.

Among the Faithful. Among the Faithful follows an undercover investigation into the Faithful of Al'Akir stationed at Falaath Village in the Shen'dar Highlands. By blending in as a prospective recruit, an adventurer learns that the cult's supreme leadership is secretly gathering to launch an imminent offensive against local settlements and outposts. Posing as an eager recruit among the Faithful of Al'Akir, an infiltrator enters Falaath Village in the Shen'dar Highlands. The cultists openly celebrate their growing ranks, boasting that their collective devotion lends shape and fury to the storm itself. New arrivals are typically sent directly to Skypriest Aanders for scrutiny, but an unexpected meeting at the local inn disrupts normal protocol.

Amongst the Ruins. Tasked by Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost, Horde adventurers delve into the flooded temple of Blackfathom Deeps to recover a fathom core. The Earthen Ring seeks this relic to uncover the dark elemental plots of the invading Twilight's Hammer cult. The ancient night elven temple of Blackfathom Deeps, once sacred to Elune, has fallen under the dominion of sinister forces. Deep within its submerged passages, the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer have established a stronghold. Stationed at the windswept shore of Zoram'gar Outpost in Ashenvale, the Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea observes the growing taint with rising alarm, recognizing that the cult intends to subjugate the local elements against the land and its defenders.

An Aggressive Defense. An Aggressive Defense is an Alliance quest given by Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar. Faced with rampant furbolg corruption along the central thoroughfares of Ashenvale, the night elves are forced to mount an active cull against the maddened Foulweald tribe. The road running east from Astranaar toward the Falfarren River serves as a vital lifeline through Ashenvale, but it has grown exceedingly dangerous. Furbolgs driven mad by demonic corruption have begun raiding travelers directly off the main trail. Rather than simply manning barricades and waiting for the next ambush, Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner dispatches capable adventurers to break the Foulweald camps located just south of the highway.

An Alarming Request. Emissary Jacques in Southshore brings bad news out of Dalaran: the city's ley lines have been thrown off, and its constructs have turned erratic and destructive. Archmage Modera sent Jacques to find outside aid, and you are told to seek her image near Dalaran, beside Lordamere Lake. Emissary Jacques says Dalaran's ley lines have been disrupted, and the city's constructs now behave erratically and destructively. The cause is not yet known. The high council has ordered the matter kept private so as not to bring shame to the order, but Jacques says the charade cannot go on forever, for the city is being overrun. Archmage Modera sent Jacques to seek outside aid, and you are to find her image near Dalaran, beside Lordamere Lake.

An Ambassador of Evil. Historian Karnik wants Ambassador Infernus of Angor Fortress put down. You are to go back into the Badlands, and carry proof of the kill to Advisor Belgrum in Ironforge. Ragnaros himself sent Ambassador Infernus to Angor Fortress to oversee the Shadowforge as they hunt for lost artifacts in Uldaman. The toll in dwarven lives has already been heavy and is worsening. Karnik dares not guess how many artifacts the Shadowforge might find and use against Ironforge. You are to go back to the Badlands, destroy Infernus, and bring Belgrum proof of your victory. Time presses, since Ragnaros will not wait for them to prepare.

An Ancient Grudge. Deep within the historic Hall of Thanes, an ethereal attendant pleads for an end to the torment of a fallen ruler. The spirit of Faldrim Anvilmar lingers on, consumed by an old grievance and denied eternal peace. Adventurers are tasked with putting the restless thane to rest. Within the stone vaults of the Hall of Thanes, death offers no immediate respite. A ghostly attendant of Faldrim Anvilmar lingers there, barely able to muster the strength to speak across the mortal veil. Rather than seeking freedom for itself, the phantom's only concern is its master, begging travelers to quiet the turbulent spirit of the thane.

An Apprentice's Enchantment. Apprentice Kryten has enchanted the agate you brought him from the Boulderfist shaman. Touched to a pedestal at the foot of the tower, it will wake the tower's defenses. Before you leave, he sends you to Skuerto for the rest. Kryten hands you the enchanted gem. He explains that touching it to a pedestal at the foot of the tower will wake the tower's defenses, and that you should use it when you are ready to go in after the rest of Trelane's items. He will await your return at the camp. First, speak to Skuerto, who will fill in whatever else you need to know.

An Audience with the King. At Stormwind Keep, An Audience with the King brings the Defias report before the Crown. After the long investigation across Westfall and the Deadmines, the heroes carry City Architect Baros Alexston's findings to the capital. Edwin VanCleef has been defeated, and the conspiracy beneath Moonbrook has been dismantled. City Architect Baros Alexston prepares an official report for the Crown. He believes the adventurer who broke the guild's criminal enterprise should be honored before the monarch. You carry the detailed findings across Stormwind's grand canals to Stormwind Keep, expecting to meet the realm's sovereign.

An Enticing Offer. 'An Enticing Offer' is a local initiative aimed at repelling encroaching murlocs using bait concocted from toxic duskweed. By harvesting the noxious weed directly from nearby farmland, the plan simultaneously assists local growers and establishes a deterrent against shoreline pests. Dealing with pervasive murloc infestations often calls for inventive pest control rather than endless frontline skirmishes. 'An Enticing Offer' proposes a clever solution to address two local nuisances in a single stroke: crafting a specialized bait laced with duskweed to deter murlocs from encroaching onto settled lands, while clearing encroaching weeds from neighboring crop fields in the process.

An Extraordinary Egg. Curgle Cranklehop has rarely seen an egg from Feralas in extraordinary shape. Such eggs are the rarest of all. Curgle Cranklehop says that very few eggs come out of Feralas in extraordinary shape, and that these are the rarest of all. An egg of that kind is what Curgle is looking for.

An Old Colleague. An Old Colleague is an Alliance quest given by the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looking to construct an extraordinarily potent device, Gaxim sends an adventurer all the way across the sea to Ironforge to track down an old acquaintance capable of synthesizing a hazardous explosive concoction. Completing this errand opens the door to procuring the volatile chemical compound known as Nitromirglyceronium. While stationed among the peaks of Stonetalon, Gaxim Rustfizzle conceives of his most ambitious engineering endeavor yet. Creating a mechanism of that scale requires specialized fuel far beyond typical gunpowder or crude oil. Specifically, Gaxim requires Nitromirglyceronium, also designated as NG-5, an explosive mix potent enough to guarantee destructive results should everything go according to plan.

An Old History Book. In Stormwind, a lost chronicle returns to the Royal Library. Titled The History of Stormwind, the battered book bears the library’s seal and vanished before the kingdom was rebuilt after the First War. Its return gives Head Librarian Milton Sheaf a chance to preserve the history of southern human lands. Duskwood’s undead and ogres roam among the ruins where this mud-caked volume was found. The book is a rare relic from before Stormwind’s destruction. Its opening page bears the kingdom’s formal library seal. Someone checked it out decades ago, before the Horde razed the capital, and the book was presumed lost in the fall of the south.

An Ordinary Egg. Curgle Cranklehop works with ordinary hippogryph eggs, which are a coin toss: about half of them hatch. Curgle tends them and hopes for luck. An ordinary hippogryph egg hatches only about half the time. Curgle Cranklehop does their best to nurture each one, and with some luck it will hatch.
