text.enUS: An Orphan Looking For a Home. After Doling Justice, Kindal Moonweaver greets you on your return from Darnassus with news: a nest full of eggs was saved, though the mother died. Kindal offers you one of the eggs as a pet and sends you on to Quentin, who waits by the race tracks in the Shimmering Flats of Thousand Needles. Kindal Moonweaver is glad to see you back from Darnassus and reports good progress while you were away. A nest full of eggs was saved, though the mother died before help reached her. The eggs look set to hatch soon, so they will need a good keeper, and Kindal offers you one as a pet. If you are truly interested, carry an egg to the race tracks in the Shimmering Flats, where Quentin will tell you more.

An Undelivered Letter. An Undelivered Letter is a piece of long-forgotten mail left behind in Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Penned years ago by the elusive Stalvan Mistmantle, it serves as a critical clue in unraveling the dark tale of his past. Years ago, a storm drove a traveling courier into the Lion's Pride Inn looking for dry lodging. Near midnight, the terrified messenger fled down the stairs in his sleeping clothes and vanished into the pouring rain, never to return. He abandoned a chest full of belongings on the second floor, including a letter written by Stalvan Mistmantle addressed to an estate in Stormwind City's Canal District.

An Unwelcome Guest. An Unwelcome Guest is a local task in Lakeshire where resident Martie Jainrose seeks retribution against Bellygrub, a destructive wild boar. The beast has rampaged through her garden and trampled her seasonal daffodils, prompting a bounty on the creature's tusk. In the lakeside town of Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose tends to her domestic grounds amidst the gathering shadows over the Redridge Mountains. Her quiet routine is shattered by a persistent local terror: a notoriously aggressive wild boar that has repeatedly invaded her garden. Having trampled her prized patch of daffodils beyond recovery for the season, the distraught resident turns to capable travelers to put an end to the rampaging animal.

name.zhCN: 安娜斯塔西娅·哈特威尔

text.enUS: Anastasia Hartwell. Anastasia Hartwell is a prominent Forsaken mage trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. She guides fledgling and developing spellcasters in mastering the arcane arts and oversees vital magical research and field missions across Lordaeron and beyond. Standing within the dark, echoing chambers of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Anastasia Hartwell instructs Forsaken and Horde mages in channeling arcane energies. Though the kingdom of Lordaeron fell to ruin, former human practitioners like Anastasia have preserved their scholarly traditions in undeath. She maintains that magic demands strict discipline, warning any traveler she meets that careless incantations will quickly consume the untrained.

Anaya's Pendant. Across Ameth'Aran, Anaya's Pendant remains with the restless ghost of Anaya Dawnrunner. Cerellean Whiteclaw carries grief for the love he lost when the Sundering shattered their world. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the ancient kaldorei city of Ameth'Aran fell into ruin. Cerellean Whiteclaw believed his beloved Anaya had perished, and carried his grief into a long sleep beside Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage. After waking, he wandered Darkshore and found Anaya's tormented apparition still drifting through Ameth'Aran, bearing the pendant. Cerellean cannot raise a hand against her himself, so he asks travelers to free her spirit and recover the heirloom.

name.frFR: Ancien sceau de pierre de lune

text.enUS: Ancient Moonstone Seal. The Ancient Moonstone Seal holds Asterion captive in the ruins of Bashal'Aran. Forged by the Highborne long before the Sundering, it binds his spirit with arcane magic. The Ancient Moonstone Seal binds Asterion's soul to the pillars of Bashal'Aran. His former master, the Highborne sorcerer Athrikus Narassin, forged it as an unbreakable anchor while the Well of Eternity still stood and Queen Azshara reigned. More than ten millennia later, Asterion remains a spirit bound by its magic. No strength or spell he commands can break the ward.

Ancient Statuette. The Ancient Statuette is a sunken relic recovered from the shores of the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Sought by the night elf Talen, the small effigy originates from the submerged ruins of the ancient city of Zoram. The waters off northwestern Ashenvale conceal the sunken remains of Zoram, a pre-Sundering night elven city lost beneath the waves ten thousand years ago. In recent days, the explorer Talen surveyed the submerged ruins from a small craft, seeking lost historical relics. When a vicious assault by naga drove him ashore, Talen abandoned most of his belongings in his flight, dropping the ancient statuette he had dredged up onto the tideline sand near his scuttled skiff.

Andorhal. Once the thriving agricultural heart of northern Lordaeron, Andorhal became ground zero for the Kingdom's destruction during the Third War. It was here that Kel'Thuzad tainted the grain with the Plague of Undeath, unleashing horror across the region. Today, the ruined town is held firmly in the iron grip of the Scourge. Before the Third War, Andorhal was the prosperous granary of the Eastweald, gathering grain from across Lordaeron and distributing it eastward to Hearthglen and Stratholme. Because of this vast distribution network, Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned chose Andorhal as the staging ground for their horrific plot. By tainting the grain crates with the Plague of Undeath, the cult turned the breadbasket of the kingdom into an engine of necrosis, infecting countless citizens before the Crown even understood the threat.

Andron Gant. Andron Gant is a reclusive, frequently intoxicated Forsaken residing in the murky depths of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. He handles occasional research commissions for local mages. Lounging amidst the noxious fumes of the Apothecarium, Andron Gant rarely ventures beyond the safety of the Undercity's stone walls. To the casual observer, he appears to be little more than a drunken scholar, occasionally hiring adventurous couriers to retrieve obscure relics like the Tablet of Markri from distant shores on behalf of local mages.

Andron's Ledger. Andron's Ledger is an intelligence document obtained from Andron Gant in the Undercity. The Deathstalkers seek it as part of an operative's early work gathering information for the Forsaken.

Anduin Lothar. Sir Anduin Lothar, known as the Lion of Stormwind, was the last descendant of the ancient Arathi bloodline and the Supreme Commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron. A childhood companion of King Llane Wrynn and the Guardian Medivh, Lothar led humanity through the horrors of the First War and rallied the northern nations during the Second War before falling at Blackrock Mountain. Carrying the ancient bloodline of the Arathi kings, Lothar grew up within Stormwind's royal court alongside Prince Llane Wrynn and Medivh. The trio embarked on reckless excursions into the wilderness, skirmishing with Gurubashi trolls in Stranglethorn Vale. Lothar rose rapidly through Stormwind's martial ranks, joining the King's Honor Guard and earning renown as an Armsman of the Brotherhood of the Horse.

Anduin Wrynn. Anduin Llane Wrynn is the ten-year-old crowned King of Stormwind, reigning in the absence of his missing father, King Varian Wrynn. Due to his young age, the true administration of the kingdom rests in the hands of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and the royal court. Born in the peaceful interlude following the Second War, Prince Anduin was named in honor of both his grandfather King Llane and the legendary knight Sir Anduin Lothar. Following the mysterious disappearance of his father en route to a diplomatic summit in Theramore, the child was abruptly crowned to maintain stability throughout the kingdom. Though intelligent and empathetic beyond his years, the ten-year-old monarch has little actual say in state affairs, leaving rule of the realm divided between Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and royal councilor Lady Katrana Prestor.

Angerfang Encampment. The Angerfang Encampment is the primary stronghold of the Dragonmaw clan in the central Wetlands. Led by Chieftain Nek'rosh Skullcrusher, these renegade orcs use the sprawling camp as a staging ground to threaten nearby dwarven settlements and plot the destruction of Menethil Harbor. Sprawling across the muck of the central Wetlands, the Angerfang Encampment serves as the fortified heart of Dragonmaw power in the region. Unlike the scattered raiding parties found wandering the marshes, this compound boasts heavily defended barricades, watchtowers, and a formidable host of warriors, bonewarders, and dark spellcasters loyal to the old ways. From here, the Dragonmaw project military force across the marshlands, raiding travelers along the roads and menacing nearby dwarven digs like Whelgar's Excavation Site.

Another Clue to Sanders' Treasure. In Westfall, a scrap of Captain Sanders' parchment points the way to his next hidden marker. Captain Sanders hid his stolen riches across Westfall, using riddles and buried markers instead of one map that could be seized. This scrap continues the trail from the previous hiding place. It tells the finder to turn north and look for a discarded jug near a lonely windmill above the sea cliffs.

name.deDE: Eine weitere Botschaft an die Wildhämmer
name.esES: Un nuevo mensaje para los Martillo Salvaje
name.frFR: Encore un message pour les Wildhammer
name.zhCN: 又一个给蛮锤部族的警告

text.enUS: Another Message to the Wildhammer. After the first message, Otho Moji'ko at Revantusk Village says the Wildhammer and their gryphons are as close as a troll and a mate. Disgusting, but it can be used against them. Otho wants gryphons in the Hinterlands killed for their feathers. After the Highvale high elves, Otho Moji'ko has another message to send. The Wildhammer and their gryphons are said to be as close as a troll and a mate, which Otho finds disgusting, but useful. Kill the gryphons you meet across the Hinterlands and collect their Long Elegant Feathers. Gryphons are known to live in every region there. From the feathers, Otho will make the final message.

Another Power Source?. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan has more power sources and will sell you another one, at a price of ten Wastewander Water Pouches. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle guesses the first power source from Slake That Thirst ran out of time, or perhaps got lost in the sand. Whatever the reason, Bilgewhizzle has additional power sources to sell. This time the price is ten Wastewander Water Pouches, because times are tough all around and power sources do not grow on trees.

Ansirem's Key. Following his magical examination, Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver points toward an ancient troll dagger capable of disrupting the focal altar empowering the Stone of the Tides. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay. Ansirem Runeweaver determines that an altar or focal point amplifies the power of the Stone of the Tides. Overpowering that magic calls for another troll relic: an ancient dagger he found while researching in Stranglethorn. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay.

Anvilmar. Anvilmar is a fortified dwarven outpost nestled in the snowy depths of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. Centered around a massive stone forge, it serves as the primary training grounds and rallying point for young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomish refugees beginning their adventures. Tucked away in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley, Anvilmar stands as an enduring symbol of dwarven perseverance. Dominated by a roaring central forge, this sturdy masonry complex houses class mentors, supply vendors, and veteran mountain mountaineers who drill recruits before sending them out into the wider kingdom. Though sheltered behind towering drifts, the settlement remains on constant guard against the hostile Frostmane trolls and aggressive wild beasts prowling the frozen valley.

Apothecarium. The Apothecarium is the southwestern quarter of the Undercity and the headquarters of the Royal Apothecary Society. Within these noxious laboratories, Forsaken alchemists labor tirelessly under Master Apothecary Faranell to concoct virulent plagues, toxins, and engineered horrors. It stands as the grim heart of Undercity's biological research, vital to Lady Sylvanas's campaign against the living and the Scourge. Occupying the southwestern terrace of the subterranean capital, the Apothecarium is a labyrinth of bubbling vats, dissection tables, and pungent chemical fumes. Led by Master Apothecary Faranell, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes this district to advance their understanding of mortality and rot. Here, alchemists and surgeons experiment on tissue grafts, vivisection, and the assembly of mighty abominations. Their overriding purpose, mandated by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, is the formulation of a new plague capable of eradicating both the Scourge and the lingering human presence across Lordaeron.

Apothecary Helbrim. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim studies the Barrens for the Royal Apothecary Society. Sent to Kalimdor, he gathers unfamiliar reagents for the Forsaken. Apothecary Helbrim works beneath the harsh sun at the Crossroads, far from the Royal Apothecary Society's quarters in the damp undercity of Undercity. Sent across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he searches the Barrens for useful plants, fungi, and other natural specimens. He depends on travelers to bring him samples, including local fungal spores, and works with Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. Through Helbrim, the Forsaken's alchemists reach beyond the ruined borders of Lordaeron.

Apothecary Johaan. Apothecary Johaan is an alchemist and researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Brill. Tasked by his order and Lady Sylvanas, he conducts lethal experiments on local flora and fauna to develop the Forsaken's new plague. Working openly out of the Forsaken settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, Apothecary Johaan represents the scientific ambitions of the newly formed Royal Apothecary Society. Like his colleagues across Lordaeron, Johaan operates under direct orders to craft biological and alchemical weapons capable of securing the Forsaken's fragile future against the living and the Scourge alike.

Apothecary Lydon. Apothecary Lydon is a morbid researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Tarren Mill. Chronically depressed and intensely bored, he finds joy only in refining lethal concoctions and watching the living suffer. He spearheads the research into potent new toxins aimed at securing Hillsbrad for the Forsaken and furthering Sylvanas's New Plague. Stationed inside the chapel turned laboratory of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon represents the cold, calculating ethos of the Royal Apothecary Society. He is afflicted by a profound, languid melancholy, disgusted by the blooming flowers and crisp air of Hillsbrad Foothills. The only diversion that lifts his perpetual gloom is the art of deathcraft. When left unattended, he passes the time poisoning, dissecting, and reanimating his unfortunate pet frog, Umpi, repeatedly waiting for new reagents to arrive.

Apothecary Renferrel. Apothecary Renferrel is a prominent member of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Tasked with advancing the Forsaken's alchemical endeavors, he coordinates extensive field research into the region's corrupted wildlife and undead threats. Travelers through Silverpine frequently assist him with gathering volatile reagents and investigating dangerous Scourge remnants. Operating out of the Sepulcher, Renferrel serves as one of the Royal Apothecary Society's chief field researchers in Silverpine Forest. While Undercity houses the grand laboratories and high leadership of the society, Renferrel handles the practical, muddy work of securing native biological specimens, refining potent concoctions, and analyzing the grim ecology of Lordaeron's western border.

Apothecary Zamah. This errand sends an adventurer racing from the arid Barrens to Thunder Bluff carrying a volatile, rendered fungal emulsion. Apothecary Helbrim needs the potent mixture delivered swiftly to his colleague, Apothecary Zamah, tucked away in the shadowy depths beneath Spirit Rise. After studying the peculiar fungal blooms thriving across the oases of the Barrens, Apothecary Helbrim cooks down a batch into a delicate emulsion. The unstable brew degrades rapidly once prepared. Lacking the time to travel to Mulgore himself, Helbrim entrusts the flask to a reliable runner to make the climb up the bluffs before the solution loses its chemical potency.

Apothecary Zinge. Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, Apothecary Zinge works for the Forsaken. She studies biological specimens and arranges research shipments across Horde lands. Apothecary Zinge works in the Apothecarium beneath the Undercity. Under Master Apothecary Faranell, she searches for chemical and biological compounds that can advance the Forsaken's aims. Her work connects her with field researchers and scouts far beyond Tirisfal Glades, including at distant outposts in Kalimdor.

Applejack Still. The Applejack Still is a distillation apparatus used to process fermented apples into high-proof liquor. Approaching the device reveals a stinging vapor of concentrated fruit, which the machine condenses and dispenses as a clear spirit. The Applejack Still is a functional distillation device constructed to refine fermented cider into high-proof spirits. Anyone stepping close to the apparatus is immediately greeted by a pungent aroma of concentrated apples sharp enough to sting the nostrils. Its piping and condensing coils efficiently extract and concentrate the essence of the orchard harvest into potent liquor.

Apprentice's Duties. Apprentice's Duties is an Alliance contract offered by tanner James Halloran in Menethil Harbor. After sending his young apprentice into the marshes only for the boy to be mauled by giant crocolisks, Halloran hires a capable adventurer to finish the dangerous harvesting job and settle the score. Tradesmen in frontier ports like Menethil Harbor must rely on local raw materials, but the surrounding bogs are unforgiving. James Halloran sent his young apprentice into the marshes to skin giant Wetlands crocolisks. When the youth failed to return, Halloran tracked him down and found him horribly mauled by the predatory beasts.

Aquatic Form. This quest marks the final step in a young Horde druid's journey to master the waters. After proving their worthiness and attuning to the sea lion aspect in Moonglade, the druid returns home to Thunder Bluff to receive formal recognition and master their aquatic form. Having braved the trials in the sacred haven of Moonglade, an aspiring tauren druid is directed back to Mulgore by Dendrite Starblaze. Bearing the Pendant of the Sea Lion, the initiate carries physical proof of their balance and dedication across Kalimdor's waters. It serves as tangible evidence that they have respected the ancient traditions required to adopt an aquatic aspect.

Aquatic Form. You return to Darnassus with the restored Pendant of the Sea Lion. The rite teaches Alliance druids to attune their spirits to deep waters. For Cenarion Circle initiates, shapeshifting joins the druid’s spirit to the wild aspects of Azeroth. After enduring trials in the dark coastal depths and in Moonglade, young night elf druids receive the assembled Pendant of the Sea Lion from Dendrite Starblaze. They carry the sacred token back to Teldrassil as proof of their respect for the laws of air, water, and breath.

Arachnophobia. Arachnophobia is a Horde bounty quest targeting Besseleth, an ancient and colossal predator haunting southern Stonetalon Mountains. Posted on a roadside notice near Windshear Crag, the bounty directs adventurers into Sishir Canyon to claim the spider matriarch's fang for Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat. Putting an end to her reign makes the mountain roads safer for night travelers. Travelers along the main thoroughfare south of Windshear Crag will spot a weathered wanted poster warning of the dangers to the west. Sishir Canyon and Webwinder Path have been completely overrun by eight-legged predators. At the heart of this webbed menace sits Besseleth, an unusually large, orange-hued spider who commands her brood and ambushes anyone daring to stray off the path after sunset.

Aramis Hammerhand. Aramis Hammerhand is an undead holy warrior situated within the desecrated chapel of Deathknell. As a Forsaken paladin trainer, he instructs newly risen dead who seek to reclaim their bond with the Holy Light. Walking this path in undeath requires immense discipline, as wielding such radiant energy inflicts agonizing pain upon their decayed flesh. Standing within the somber walls of Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand represents an anomaly among the recently awakened Forsaken. In life, many citizens of Lordaeron answered the call of the Silver Hand, only to perish when the Scourge swept across the north. Aramis survived the fall only to be raised into undeath, yet he chose not to abandon the martial and spiritual teachings of his former existence. Now, he offers guidance to others who refuse to surrender their devotion.

Arcane Feedback. In Stormwind, Arcane Feedback prepares priests to face hostile spellcasters. High Priestess Laurena teaches the rite in the Cathedral of Light, where faith is shaped into a defense against arcane power. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena warns acolytes that arcane magic remains a danger. The Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order, while raw magic can turn volatile and lead to corruption or catastrophe. Warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts threaten the faithful. Priests learn that faith can become an active ward against spells around them.

Arcane Feedback. Arcane Feedback is a priest quest given by High Priest Rohan in Ironforge to human acolytes visiting Khaz Modan. Rohan directs the developing priest home to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind to receive teachings tailored specifically to the traditions of humankind. It marks a key moment of progression where young disciples begin mastering racial manifestations of their faith. When a human priest seeks advanced spiritual tutelage in the halls of the Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan greets them with reverence but sets a boundary. While dwarven and human priests share devotion to the Holy Light, each civilization nurtures its own particular rites, disciplines, and defensive prayers. Rather than imparting Ironforge's unique secrets, Rohan sends human clergy back to their cultural roots in Elwynn, ensuring they master their people's distinct heritage.

Arcane Feedback. In Darnassus, Arcane Feedback sends human priests back to Stormwind. Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon reluctantly honors the Alliance summons. There, High Priestess Laurena prepares the acolyte for deeper instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. She recognizes the formal alliance between the kaldorei and Stormwind, yet distrusts human magical and spiritual practices. Night elves see arcane power as volatile and dangerous, a view shaped by ten millennia of grief since the War of the Ancients. Even human divine rites trouble the night elf clergy when they blur radiant faith with arcane workings.

Arcanist Doan. Arcanist Doan is a master human mage residing within the Athenaeum of the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing. He serves the Scarlet Crusade as one of its most lethal arcane specialists and guardian of key crusade archives. While the fanatical ranks of the Scarlet Crusade lean heavily on martial fury and holy fervor, Doan remained convinced that raw arcane power was essential to purging the Scourge from Lordaeron. Stationed deep inside the Athenaeum of the Monastery's library, he was entrusted as both a lorekeeper and an operational gatekeeper, safeguarding the Scarlet Key that secures crusade sanctuaries across the northern kingdoms.

Archaeologist Flagongut. At Menethil Harbor, Archaeologist Flagongut keeps in touch with field researchers across the Great Sea. The dwarven scholar of the Explorers' League is staying at the Deepwater Tavern while bound for the Whelgar Excavation Site. Archaeologist Flagongut rests with a mug at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Like many members of Ironforge's Explorers' League, he traveled west across Khaz Modan to help with discoveries near the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. Though far from the high halls of the library, he keeps ties with field researchers, processing lost relics and reports carried across the Great Sea from distant expeditions.

Archaeologist Hollee. In Auberdine, Archaeologist Hollee tracks dwarven research across Darkshore. The ancient ruins draw Ironforge scholars to the coast, where she keeps in touch with prospectors searching for relics and unusual geological formations. Archaeologist Hollee works from Auberdine, among the night elves who guard and settle Darkshore. The dwarven scholar is a regional contact for surveyors and expedition teams crossing the wilderness. The Explorers' League sends its people across the sea to uncover traces of ancient history, and Darkshore's ruins give them ground to study.

Archaic Rune. The Archaic Rune is an introductory quest given to fledgling dwarf Shamans in Dun Morogh. Imbued with elemental power from ancient Wildhammer inscriptions, this sacred tablet introduces young initiates to their elemental heritage. Delivering the stone to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar marks the formal beginning of their training in the ways of earth, air, fire, and water. Fledgling adventurers in Coldridge Valley discover the Archaic Rune after assisting local allies near Anvilmar. Bearing distinctive script carved in the style of the Wildhammer clan, the stone is visibly and palpably charged with ancient elemental power. The rune serves not merely as a relic of stonecraft, but as an elemental test: only those who possess a nascent attunement to the primordial spirits can comprehend the markings etched upon its weathered surface. For those capable of reading the script, it provides clear guidance to seek out proper instruction within the nearby dwarven outpost.

Archbishop Benedictus. In Stormwind City, Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church of the Holy Light from the Cathedral of Light. He guides the faithful and the Alliance through uncertain times. Archbishop Benedictus took the Church’s leadership after his mentor, Archbishop Alonsus Faol, died. He had seen the First and Second Wars devastate the kingdoms and helped oversee the building of the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. He vowed to uphold the virtues of the faith. After Lordaeron fell and the Scourge rose during the Third War, the human kingdoms looked to him for spiritual guidance. From the Cathedral, he counsels the royal court, trains newly initiated priests, and directs holy crusades against the undead and demonic forces threatening Azeroth.

name.zhCN: 大法师安斯雷姆·鲁因维沃尔

text.enUS: Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver. Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver is a senior human wizard and a ruling member of Dalaran's Council of Six. Having survived the Scourge's destruction of Dalaran in the Third War, he oversees Kirin Tor operations from the Violet Citadel as Dalaran is rebuilt. Though dedicated to the rebuilding of his city, he also maintains discreet interests abroad—including a willful daughter who ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate. A veteran mage who helped defend Dalaran across decades, Ansirem Runeweaver sits on the Council of Six, the ruling magocracy of the Kirin Tor. He survived the devastation when Arthas Menethil and the Scourge marched upon the city and Archimonde was summoned. In the wake of Dalaran's fall, Ansirem has aided the efforts to rebuild the arcane city, whose protective shield was lifted early, and now works from the Violet Citadel.

Archmage Malin. Outside the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind City, Archmage Malin directs arcane affairs. A former pupil of Archmage Trelane, he coordinates field agents seeking magical artifacts and rare reagents across the Eastern Kingdoms. Archmage Malin is the central contact for Stormwind's arcane practitioners, stationed beneath the Wizard's Sanctum in the Mage Quarter. He learned magic under Archmage Trelane, and now works to protect the scattered legacy of his former master. While acolytes study inside the tower, Malin watches over matters across the realm that need magical oversight.

Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal. Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal is an arcane volume documenting the investigations of the master mage of the Tower of Azora. Delivered to the scholars of the Ironforge Library, the journal adds valuable magical insights to the great dwarven archive. Archmage Theocritus is known throughout the Alliance as an esteemed spellcaster stationed at the Tower of Azora in the eastern reaches of Elwynn Forest. Over years of solitary study, Theocritus has investigated curious artifacts, ley line anomalies, and nearby magical threats, recording his findings within detailed journals. Recovering such a volume represents a rare opportunity to study the personal observations of a senior Kirin Tor archmage.

Archmage Xylem. Archmage Xylem is an eccentric and reclusive human wizard dwelling in an isolated tower atop the cliffs of northern Azshara. Known for his volatile temperament and dangerous experiments, he has withdrawn from worldly affairs to pursue esoteric arcane research. Reaching him requires magical teleportation, and he only entertains adventurers who can assist in his peculiar studies or aid his personal vendettas. Perched high upon the jagged cliffs of northern Azshara, Archmage Xylem makes his home in a secluded spire overlooking the ruined elven coastline. Rather than building a road or trail, the wizard isolated his sanctuary entirely, relying on his servant Sanath Lim-yo to magically transport approved visitors up the cliff face. Observers across Kalimdor consider him profoundly eccentric and perilous to deal with; even fellow scholars treat him with deep caution, noting that he behaves unlike almost any other human mage.

Arena Master. Is there more to mastering the arena than this? Short John Mithril, the Pirate behind the Gurubashi event, may have the answer, and you will find him in the Stranglethorn Arena. Whatever you have gained at Gurubashi, it seems that mastering the arena asks for more. Short John Mithril, the Pirate who organizes the contests there, may know what. Look for him inside the Stranglethorn Arena.

Argent Dawn. The Argent Dawn is a neutral, knightly order dedicated to stamping out malevolent threats across Azeroth, most notably the Scourge and the Burning Legion. Formed by survivors of the Knights of the Silver Hand who rejected the fanatical zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade, they welcome champions of any race or faction who honor the cause of the Light. From their fortified sanctuary at Light's Hope Chapel to far-flung outposts across Kalimdor, they stand on the front lines against darkness. When Highlord Alexandros Mograine fell and Lordaeron collapsed into ruin, the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand broke into bitter disagreement. Many survivors surrendered to grief and paranoia, morphing into the xenophobic Scarlet Crusade. Yet veterans like Lord Maxwell Tyrosus recognized that their former comrades had abandoned the true tenets of the Holy Light. Refusing to succumb to madness or abandon the dead kingdom, they split away to form the Argent Dawn—an order committed to defending Azeroth alongside anyone willing to fight, whether Alliance or Horde.

name.ruRU: Страж Манадос из ордена Серебряного Рассвета

text.enUS: Argent Guard Manados. Argent Guard Manados is a night elf sentry stationed in Darnassus on behalf of the Argent Dawn. Resting at the Craftsmen's Terrace, he keeps watch over Kalimdor's growing corruption and directs adventurers toward the sinister forces lurking in Blackfathom Deeps. While most of the Argent Dawn focuses its vigilance on the blighted lands of Lordaeron and the Scourge, Argent Guard Manados represents their watchful eyes in the night elf capital of Darnassus. Standing among the artisans and tradefolk of the Craftsmen's Terrace, Manados monitors emerging threats that menace the balance of northern Kalimdor. When rumors reach him of the Twilight's Hammer cult establishing a foul foothold beneath the waves of Ashenvale, Manados enlists capable heroes to strike at Blackfathom Deeps and recover artifacts of their dark devotion.

Argent Guard Thaelrid. Argent Guard Thaelrid is a wounded night elf scout sent by the Argent Dawn into the submerged ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. Trapped near the Pool of Ask'ar, he bears witness to the dark alliance taking root between the naga and the Twilight's Hammer cult. When strange reports trickled out of the Zoram Strand concerning foul rites deep beneath the sea, the Argent Dawn took interest. Dedicated to watching for rising evils and unnatural corruption across Azeroth, the order dispatched Scout Thaelrid to slip inside Blackfathom Deeps. His mission was simple: assess the depth of the threat, observe the movements within the flooded temple, and report back so the Dawn could decide where aid was most desperately needed.

Argos Nightwhisper. In Stormwind's Park, Argos Nightwhisper guides Alliance travelers toward Darkshore. His brother Gershala studies the corruption spreading there. Argos Nightwhisper lives among the night elves gathering in Stormwind's Park. The district's quiet groves recall the kaldorei's ancestral woodlands. Like others of his kin stationed in the human kingdom, Argos connects the new allies across the Great Sea. Reports from across the ocean trouble him. He urges capable Alliance champions to travel to Auberdine in Darkshore, where his brother Gershala needs help against the spreading corruption.

Ariden's Camp. Ariden's Camp is an abandoned encampment nestled just north of the path threading through Deadwind Pass. Left decaying in the shadow of Karazhan, it stands as an eerie, quiet anomaly amidst the desolate canyon winds. Travelers between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows often pass it with unease, wondering who once pitched a tent here. Tucked against the crags north of the gorge road connecting Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows, this dilapidated campsite looks like an ordinary transient stop long forsaken by living men. Yet in the oppressive gloom of Deadwind Pass, nothing remains unmarred by dark sorcery. Whoever named the camp Ariden's and whatever fortune its owner sought in Karazhan's orbit, the pass's lingering horrors swallowed it, leaving only weathered cloth, cold ashes, and an enduring mystery.

Arikara. "Arikara" is the culmination of an ominous task given by Magatha Grimtotem in Thunder Bluff. Warning that an ancient wind serpent may be stalking High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the elder shaman sends Horde adventurers to summon and slay the beast upon the burial spires of Thousand Needles. After securing refined Incendia powder, Magatha Grimtotem enchants the reagent to serve as a summoning catalyst. She warns that ancient tauren traditions have shifted too rapidly under the new Horde alliance, provoking the vengeance of Arikara, a ferocious wind serpent spirit. Magatha directs heroes southward into the windswept canyon of Thousand Needles, instructing them to throw the powder onto a ritual pyre situated among the elevated burial sites of Darkcloud Pinnacle.

Arikara Serpent Skin. The Arikara Serpent Skin is the scaled hide taken from the mythical wind serpent Arikara atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Carried back to Whitereach Post, it serves as tangible proof that the vengeance-seeking beast was summoned and slain. Arikara is a formidable wind serpent tied to ancient tauren legend, rumored to seek retribution against Cairne Bloodhoof amid shifting cultural ways. Using enchanted Incendia Powder prepared under the direction of Elder Magatha Grimtotem, champions light the sacred fire atop the burial bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle to force the spirit-beast into the physical realm. Stripping the serpent's hide yields the Arikara Serpent Skin—an unmistakable relic of the beast's demise.

name.frFR: En armes et prêt au combat

text.enUS: Armed and Ready. You carry Morbent's Bane back to Sven Yorgen, the weapon forged to strip away Morbent Fel's unholy defenses. Morbent Fel's hold over Raven Hill cemetery resists ordinary steel. Blades shatter or glance off the dark wards around the necromancer. A weapon made to break those wards is now ready. Grimand Elmore shaped the metal in Stormwind's Dwarven District, and sacred power consecrated it. Morbent's Bane can now sever Fel's tie to unlife.

name.esES: El ejército de los dragones Negros

text.enUS: Army of the Black Dragon. In Brackenwall Village, the ogre Tharg wants vengeance on the army of the black dragon. Tharg resents Overlord Mok'Morokk for telling the ogres to run rather than fight, and asks you to strike at the Firemane. Black dragons killed many ogres, and Tharg's wife was among the dead. Mok'Morokk, whom Rexxar made Overlord, told the survivors to run, and that is how they came to Brackenwall Village. Tharg says ogres are poor at running and ought to fight, and he believes Mok'Morokk cares only for Mok'Morokk. Tharg also says that Mok'Morokk tells all ogres to stay put and keep this place safe.

Arnak's Hoof. Arnak's Hoof is the macabre proof of death taken from the criminal Arnak Grimtotem. Hunted down on the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arnak was marked for execution by the defenders of Freewind Post after murdering a fellow tauren and kidnapping his sister. Arnak Grimtotem earned notoriety throughout Thousand Needles as an outlaw whose brutality crossed even the contentious lines of tauren clan politics. After murdering another tauren and abducting the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong, a formal bounty was posted for his death. Arnak holed up on the heights of Darkcloud Pinnacle, surrounded by Grimtotem guards. Slaying him and claiming his severed hoof serves as undeniable confirmation for Cliffwatcher Longhorn at Freewind Post that the murderer has finally answered for his crimes.

Arthas Menethil. Once the golden prince of Lordaeron and a celebrated paladin of the Silver Hand, Arthas Menethil fell from grace during the Third War while pursuing the demonic orchestrators of the plague. After claiming the cursed runeblade Frostmourne in the frozen north, he surrendered his soul, murdered his father King Terenas, and spearheaded the destruction of his own homeland as the Scourge's dark champion. Born to King Terenas Menethil II, Arthas was raised to embody the ideals of the Alliance of Lordaeron. Trained in combat by Muradin Bronzebeard and inducted into the Order of the Silver Hand under the tutelage of Uther the Lightbringer, he was revered by high and low alike as the future of humanity. Bold, skilled, and fiercely protective of his people, he fought tenaciously against Blackrock clan orc incursions and forest troll warbands. Yet beneath his radiant exterior lay an uncompromising pride and an obsessive dread of failure.

Arugal. Archmage Arugal is a former wizard of Dalaran who unleashed the feral worgen upon Lordaeron. Overcome by madness and grief, he now rules from the heights of Shadowfang Keep, treating the savage beasts as his beloved children while menacing all of Silverpine Forest. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Arugal was a member of the Kirin Tor, though some peers like Dalar Dawnweaver dismissed him as a charlatan whose weak spellcraft relied heavily on enchanted trinkets. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Arugal sought a weapon powerful enough to stem the tide. Drawing upon the esoteric research of the late Dalaran mage Ur, Arugal pierced the veil between realms and summoned the worgen into the mortal world. The ravenous beasts tore through the undead legions as intended, but their feral ferocity could not be contained, and their savage hunger swiftly turned against innocent mortals.

Arugal Must Die. Arugal Must Die is a decisive Horde mission issued by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. It tasks brave champions with storming Shadowfang Keep to slay the rogue archmage Archmage Arugal and claim his severed head. Eliminating Arugal is critical for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner to break the worgen menace and secure Silverpine Forest for the Forsaken. While the Forsaken have carved out a base in the Sepulcher, Silverpine Forest remains treacherous and deeply contested. Perched high upon the cliffs overlooking the woods sits Shadowfang Keep, the lair of Archmage Arugal. Driven mad by guilt and dark sorcery, Arugal unleashed the feral worgen upon Lordaeron. His ravenous beasts roam the forest paths, directly hindering Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's efforts to establish a fortified strategic hold over the region.

Arugal's Folly. Assigned by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, this quest tasks Forsaken agents with securing Arugal's earliest spellbooks from a nearby farmstead. Uncovering the magic behind the worgen curse is vital for the Forsaken to turn it against the mad mage and secure Silverpine Forest. Recovering the Remedy of Arugal marks the first step in unraveling the threat looming from Shadowfang Keep. Dalar Dawnweaver, an ambitious Forsaken mage residing in the crypts of the Sepulcher, holds no respect for Archmage Arugal. To Dawnweaver, Arugal was an unremarkable practitioner whose inclusion in the Kirin Tor was baffling and whose magical understanding seemed amateurish. However, the monstrous beasts now roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver intends to deconstruct the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

Arugal's Folly. This task sends Forsaken agents to collect enchanted shackles from Moonrage worgen roaming Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver, analyzing Arugal's notes, aims to unravel how the renegade mage artificially reinforced his unstable magic. Studying these bindings brings the Forsaken closer to dismantling the worgen threat plaguing the region. Upon inspecting Arugal's recovered research, Dalar Dawnweaver expresses utter contempt for his former peer. According to Dalar, Arugal was never fit to serve Dalaran, let alone handle high sorcery during the kingdom's direst hour. To compensate for his mediocre talent, Arugal relied on enchanted relics and hardware to bolster and bind his summoned worgen beasts. Dalar requires physical samples of these items to dissect the magical tether holding the monsters together.

Arugal's Folly. Arugal's Folly is a key quest in the Sepulcher's ongoing campaign against the mad archmage's influence across Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver tasks Horde adventurers with infiltrating Deep Elem Mine to execute the corrupted foreman, Grimson the Pale, securing vital mineral wealth for Varimathras's forces. While unraveling the dark enchantments Archmage Arugal unleashed upon the forest, Dalar Dawnweaver receives urgent intelligence from the Forsaken Darkstalkers. The feral sorcery spreading from Shadowfang Keep has reached the Deep Elem Mine in the southeastern hills, where worgen now make their lair. The mine holds crucial ore needed to fuel Undercity's militarization, but its current occupants render it completely unusable.

Arugal's Folly. Arugal's Folly culminates in a dangerous investigation into the curse gripping Pyrewood Village. Dalar Dawnweaver tasks Horde operatives with obtaining enchanted shackles from the villagers to decode Archmage Arugal's twisted handiwork. Unraveling these bindings exposes the tragic magic holding the settlement under the shadow of the worgen. South of the Sepulcher lies Pyrewood Village, a settlement caught in an uncanny state of existence. Under the daylight sun, its residents go about their lives as ordinary human peasants, fearful and insular. Yet as twilight falls over the forest, their human forms tear apart into savage Moonrage worgen, roaming the streets under Arugal's sway. Dalar Dawnweaver seeks to unravel the exact arcane bindings causing this diurnal horror.

As Water Cascades. Sacred water is brought to bear on the red crystal in Darkshore. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea hopes moonwell water from Auberdine will reveal what lies beneath its opaque surface. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea seeks a safe way to study the red crystal high on Darkshore's eastern cliffs. Moonwell water holds divine, restorative magic, blessed by the night elves' devotion to Elune. Glynda believes water from Auberdine's moonwell may react with the strange stone and pierce its opaque shell without destroying it.

Ashenvale Outrunners. Ashenvale Outrunners is a Horde patrol-interception mission issued by Kuray'bin in Ashenvale. Night elf scouts have fanned out from Silverwing Outpost to gather intelligence on nearby Horde encampments, prompting a preemptive strike to keep the outpost's defenses hidden. By hunting down these stealthy scouts, the Horde blinds the local Alliance forces and discourages future incursions. The forests of Ashenvale remain a contested frontier where every path and ridge is fiercely watched. Intelligence is as deadly as an axe, and reports reaching Kuray'bin confirm that night elf scouts known as Ashenvale Outrunners have slipped out from the Alliance stronghold at Silverwing Outpost. Operating in the dense wilderness east of their base and south of local Horde holdings, these scouts stalk the woodland paths to map out fortifications and track troop movements.

Ashlan Stonesmirk. Ashlan Stonesmirk is a dwarven explosives expert assigned to the regiment guarding Dun Modr and the Thandol Span in the northern Wetlands. From there, he keeps a vigilant eye on regional dangers threatening the realm of Ironforge. Positioned at Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands, Ashlan Stonesmirk serves the regiment guarding the Thandol Span. His expertise with explosives makes him a useful contact when suspicious materials threaten dwarven defenses.

Assassin's Contract. A Shadowy Assassin in Hillsbrad Foothills carries a contract that orders the killing of Magistrate Henry Maleb. Red wax seals it, pressed with a distinctive signet ring, and you are to bring it to Maleb in Southshore. The paper orders the killing of Magistrate Henry Maleb. A seal of red wax closes it, pressed with a distinctive signet ring. A Shadowy Assassin in Hillsbrad Foothills carries it, and Maleb in Southshore is the one to show it to.

Assassination Plot. Assassination Plot is a Horde quest initiated by recovering intercepted centaur orders in Thousand Needles. The orders reveal an impending strike targeting the tauren Kanati Greycloud at his hunting camp by Whitereach Post. Thousand Needles has long been contested terrain dominated by warring centaur clans and dangerous wildlife. When the tauren brave Kanati Greycloud set up a hunting camp at Whitereach Post, the small post southwest of the Great Lift, the local centaur viewed it as an audacious intrusion into their territory. Rather than merely driving game away, the centaur resolved to eliminate Greycloud entirely to discourage any further Horde expansion through the canyon.

name.esES: Asalto a la Isla de Fenris

text.enUS: Assault on Fenris Isle. Assault on Fenris Isle is the climactic military directive issued by High Executor Hadrec to eradicate the Scourge stronghold in Silverpine Forest. To break the Lich King's grip upon Lake Lordamere, Forsaken agents are sent to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. For weeks, Fenris Isle has stood as a poisonous blister in the heart of Lake Lordamere. While the Forsaken secured the western roads and established their presence at the Sepulcher, the Scourge entrenched themselves inside Fenris Keep. Commanded by the powerful necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, this island outpost threatened not only Silverpine Forest but the southern waterways leading toward the Undercity itself. High Executor Hadrec recognizes that the Forsaken will never truly hold Silverpine while a servant of the Lich King conducts vile experiments right off their eastern shores.

Assault on the Kolkar. After Brutal Politics, Warug in Magram Village wants proof that you can kill Kolkar the way the Magram do. Head north and slay Kolkar centaurs, scouts and maulers. Warug sneers that the Kolkar believe themselves strong while the Magram laugh at them as they kill them. Warug wants you to prove you can kill Kolkar as the Magram do, so you head north: twelve Kolkar centaurs, twelve scouts and six maulers are to fall.

Assessing the Threat. Assessing the Threat is a defensive scouting operation commissioned by Deputy Feldon in Lakeshire. With the local garrison stretched thin and denied reinforcements from Stormwind, adventurers are hired to cull encroaching gnoll packs along the southern road and measure the strength of the growing menace. The town of Lakeshire is fighting for its survival on multiple fronts. Between Blackrock orc warbands descending from the heights and aggressive gnoll packs harassing the valleys, the local defenders cannot spare troops for standard reconnaissance patrols. When initial reports confirmed gnolls encroaching on the border, Deputy Feldon turned to outside help. Rather than committing regular guardsmen to the wilderness, the town pays traveling champions to test the enemy's strength firsthand.

Asterion. Asterion is an ancient Highborne spirit bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran in Darkshore. Once the trusted second to governor Athrikus Narassin ten millennia ago, he was mysteriously imprisoned in a magical moonstone seal that held him through mortal life and into the afterlife. Today, his specter remains shackled to the ruined shrine, surrounded by demonic beasts and dreaming of liberation. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara herself. Azshara appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern the twin settlements, and Asterion served as his right hand. Respected for both his physical combat prowess and his command of arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among the people of Bashal'Aran while frequently traveling between the sister cities to manage the needs of their citizens.

Astor's Letter of Introduction. Astor's Letter of Introduction is a document carried by Astor Hadren, a courier traveling between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. Taken by aspiring Deathstalkers, the letter serves as cover to infiltrate a suspected conspiracy involving the shopkeeper Andron Gant. Astor Hadren served as a discreet courier moving between Silverpine Forest and the capital. His personal letter of introduction establishes the bearer's bona fides to illicit contacts in the city. When Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad needed to investigate suspicious leaks within the Undercity, Astor's travels made him an immediate target. By eliminating or robbing Hadren of his papers, an operative can assume his identity and intercept covert communications meant for Astor's eyes alone.

Astral Knot Garment. Wynne Larson works fine spider silk into a garment in Stormwind City. An adventurer brings her rare silk gathered from the wilds, and she tailors it into a magical weave for dangerous journeys and high-society gatherings. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, tailors serve arcane elites and visiting nobles. Wynne Larson is known for weaving pristine spider silk into durable, enchanted garments. Her playful humor comes through when she jokes about saving a few precious scraps for her own wardrobe before handing over her finished work.

Astranaar. Astranaar is the primary Night Elf settlement in central Ashenvale, built across a serene lake island straddling the ancient forest road. Serving as the beating heart of Alliance operations in the region, it provides vital refuge to travelers facing encroaching threats from hostile furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde. Situated atop an island in the middle of a forest lake, Astranaar stands as the largest night elven settlement in Ashenvale. Connected to the mainland by wooden footbridges spanning the waters, the town houses sentinels, priests, and artisans who keep vigil over the woodlands. In addition to offering basic comforts such as an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker, its elevated perches host a flight master providing hippogryph travel to distant outposts across Kalimdor.

At Home in the Shadows. "At Home in the Shadows" is an introductory rogue quest on Zephras Isle. After aiding Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Grove, budding rogues are directed to read a summons and meet their local class mentor, Akeri Duskblade. The quest marks the moment young rogues transition from general village chores to serious stealth and combat training. While handling basic threats around Thendal Grove, young rogues draw the attention of Akeri Duskblade, the grove's resident rogue trainer. Rather than mingling openly in the settlement, Akeri passes a simple note through Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian recognizes that despite Akeri's suspicious demeanor, the mentor understands the practical skills needed to survive outside the grove's sheltered boundaries.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Executor Zygand directs Forsaken champions to strike down Captain Perrine and his garrison stationed at a ruined tower southwest of Brill. Using intelligence recovered in Deathknell, the Forsaken aim to push back the zealous crusaders threatening their borders. Documents recovered from the Scarlet Crusade in Deathknell by Executor Arren revealed active troop movements across Tirisfal Glades. Rather than waiting for the fanatics to mount an offensive against the newly fortified town of Brill, Executor Zygand uses this captured intelligence to orchestrate preemptive strikes against their field commanders.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. This military operation tasks Forsaken defenders with striking at the Scarlet Crusade encampment near the Balnir Farmstead in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. Under orders from Executor Zygand, players eliminate Captain Vachon and his accompanying friars to stall Crusader raids threatening the Dark Lady's domain. As the Forsaken strive to secure the perimeter around Brill and the Undercity, the Scarlet Crusade maintains fortified pockets across the countryside. Reports funneling into town from Executor Arren alert the military command to active Crusader incursions operating out of a crumbling guard tower in southeastern Tirisfal Glades, uncomfortably close to the abandoned Balnir Farmstead.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. This mission represents the culmination of Executor Zygand's early campaign to secure Tirisfal Glades against Scarlet Crusade incursions. Operating out of Brill, Forsaken agents are directed to strike directly at Captain Melrache and his personal vanguard at a ruined watchtower past Faol's Rest. While the Forsaken consolidate their hold over the ruins of Lordaeron, the Scarlet Crusade relentlessly probes the borders of Tirisfal. From an elevated watchtower situated in northern Tirisfal past Faol's Rest, zealous crusaders have organized raiding parties against Forsaken patrols and territory. Rather than waiting to repel another assault, Executor Zygand chooses decapitation: eliminating the command structure that directs the local raids.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Executor Zygand in Brill coordinates the Forsaken campaign against the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Using intelligence recovered by Executor Arren, you are dispatched to eliminate Scarlet Warriors stationed at a guard tower west of the Solliden Farmstead. This assault marks the Forsaken military's opening offensive to purge the zealous crusaders from their borders. The fledgling Forsaken state under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner faces simultaneous threats on multiple fronts. While the Deathguard keeps a wary vigil against the swelling armies of the Lich King, the fanatical mortals of the Scarlet Crusade contest Forsaken dominance over their former homeland. The Crusade considers all undead abominations to be purged with fire and blade, blind to the fact that the Forsaken have broken free of the Scourge's control.

Ataeric's Staff. Ataeric's Staff is a powerful magical conduit wielded by Archmage Ataeric, a senior Dalaran wizard in Silverpine Forest. It serves as both a focus for manipulating local ley lines and physical proof of the archmage's defeat for the Forsaken at the Sepulcher. Alarmed by Dalaran's magical expansion, Shadow Priest Allister ordered Ataeric's assassination and demanded the recovery of the staff. With Ataeric slain and his staff recovered, the concentrated ley energies collapsed back into dormancy. Bringing the staff to the Sepulcher marked a decisive victory against Dalaran's ambitions, though the Forsaken remain watchful of the latent power remaining in the earth.

Athridas Bearmantle. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle works to protect the settlement and its wilds. The night elf druid sends young adventurers to investigate corruption among local wildlife and the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle helps defend night elves arriving from Shadowglen. Teldrassil, the newly grown world tree, shows unnatural signs of decay and unrest. Athridas organizes local scouting and guards the township against threats from the surrounding wilds.

name.zhCN: 埃瑟里克斯·纳拉辛的头颅

text.enUS: Athrikus Narassin's Head. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Athrikus Narassin's Head proves the ancient warlock's death. The coven's demonic activity in northern Darkshore has been disrupted.

Attack on Camp Narache. Attack on Camp Narache is a vital discovery made within the quilboar den of Brambleblade Ravine. A dirt-stained map reveals that the aggressive Bristleback tribe is actively plotting an organized siege against Camp Narache. Delivering these plans to Chief Hawkwind alerts Camp Narache in time to summon aid from Bloodhoof Village. While scouting deep inside the caverns of Brambleblade Ravine, young tauren adventurers uncover a crude, dirt-stained map laying on the rock floor. Upon closer inspection, the parchment reveals deliberate tactical markings made by the Bristleback quilboar. Rather than engaging in mere opportunistic skirmishes, the quilboar are coordinating a full-scale, prolonged siege against Camp Narache.

Attack on the Tower. With the tower's defenses awake, Skuerto at Refuge Pointe sends you into the ogre-held tower for Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. They should lie in chests inside, and Skuerto says Malin will be more than pleased if you bring them back. After Kryten's enchantment, Skuerto tells you what to look for: Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. The three should be sitting in chests inside the tower, and you should have no trouble opening them yourself, though the ogres call for care. The tower's defenses will not deal with them on their own, and if the ogres find you stealing from them, they will put the hurt on you.

Auberdine. Ships crowd Auberdine's docks, linking Darkshore with Teldrassil and the Eastern Kingdoms. The night elven town is the Alliance's main port in northern Kalimdor, set between the Veiled Sea and pine-covered bluffs. Auberdine sits on the Veiled Sea, the only major settlement still thriving in Darkshore. Its ships sail to Stormwind Harbor and, by way of Southshore, to Menethil Harbor. Ferries cross to Rut'theran Village beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Unlike Teldrassil's secluded treetop cities, Auberdine welcomes travelers from across the sea. Lamps light its stone streets, and dwarves and gnomes mingle with merchants among low, arched timber houses.

Austil de Mon. Austil de Mon is a Forsaken warrior trainer stationed in Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Based out of the Gallows' End Tavern, he instructs newly risen warriors looking to hone their martial prowess in service of the Dark Lady. Found inside the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Austil de Mon serves as one of the earliest instructors for Forsaken warriors venturing out of Deathknell. While the living once populated the inn to drink and rest, Austil now uses the gloomy refuge to teach newly liberated undead how to channel raw martial discipline and ruthless combat techniques against the kingdom's surrounding foes.

Avenge My Village. Makaba Flathoof barely survived a vicious assault when raiders from the Grimtotem clan fell upon his village in the southeastern Stonetalon Mountains. Cut off from his kin and surrounded by the dead, he asks Horde travelers to strike back at the encampment of Grimtotem ruffians and hired sellswords to avenge his fallen people. Near the border between the Barrens and the red stone passes of Stonetalon, Makaba Flathoof stands as a lone survivor of a brutal massacre. Raiders flying the dark banners of the Grimtotem clan descended without warning, slaughtering nearly everyone in his settlement. Though Makaba fought back fiercely and brought down several of the attackers, he was eventually driven into hiding with little more than his life and his wrath.

Avenging the Fallen. Huntsman Markhor of Revantusk Village says the Wildhammer train gryphons to slay trolls, and he wants the elder gryphons of the region, the Skylords, wiped out. You are to slay a Razorbeak Skylord and bring its plume back to him. Markhor, a huntsman of Revantusk Village in the Hinterlands, is bitter that the Wildhammer train gryphons to slay trolls. Justice will come for them, he promises, but first he wants you to turn on the elder gryphons of the region, the Skylords. Slay one and return with its plume. The Razorbeak Skylord is a rare breed that tends to keep to the wilds of the Hinterlands, and Markhor blames it for breeding murderous young.

Ayanna Everstride. In Shadowglen, Ayanna Everstride trains young kaldorei in the hunter’s way. Stationed in Aldrassil, she teaches marksmanship, tracking, and survival beneath the World Tree. Ayanna Everstride trains newly awakened kaldorei hunters inside Aldrassil, in the heart of Shadowglen. To the night elves, hunters are indispensable guardians of the sacred forests, not merely trappers or sharpshooters. Ayanna teaches novices early martial skills, ranged combat, and how to survive Teldrassil’s perilous woods.

Ayessa Dawnsinger. Ayessa Dawnsinger is a Skyborne leader found in Valanaar on Zephras Isle. She leads the Windshapers, guiding the Skyborne aligned with the Horde through their trials and politics. Standing within the settlement of Valanaar on Zephras Isle, Ayessa Dawnsinger serves as the paramount guide for the Windshapers—the faction of Skyborne aligned with the Horde. From this vantage, she directs critical efforts across the island, managing external threats, internal fractures, and the overarching survival of her people as they navigate alliances in Kalimdor and beyond.

Azar Stronghammer. Azar Stronghammer is a dwarven paladin stationed at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Having completed his own training in the holy arts, he guides newly awakened dwarven champions of the Holy Light and directs promising recruits toward higher instruction in Ironforge. While paladins are more commonly associated with the great cathedrals of humanity, the dwarves of Khaz Modan have fully embraced the virtues of the Holy Light. Stationed at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Azar Stronghammer watches over newly inducted dwarven paladins finding their footing amidst Dun Morogh's freezing slopes. Having mastered his own martial and spiritual vows, he serves as an approachable mentor. When a novice shows enough dedication and spiritual maturity, Azar directs them up the mountain path to Ironforge to study under veteran champions such as Tiza Battleforge.

Azuregos. Azuregos is an eccentric blue dragon stationed along the coast of Azshara to protect ancient Highborne relics. Entrusted with safeguarding immense magical power by the Spell-Weaver Malygos, he prefers quiet study over violence, but he will readily swat aside any adventurer foolish enough to disturb his vigil. Drawn to the magic-soaked shores of Azshara, Azuregos chose the ancient ruins of Eldarath as his sanctuary. Countless relics survived the Great Sundering along these shattered coasts, and Azuregos considers it his sacred duty as a servant of Malygos to keep such powerful artifacts away from careless mortals. Rather than lurking in a dark cave, he freely roams the crags and beaches, proudly dubbing himself the lord of all magic in the region. Though blessed with a sardonic sense of humor, he fiercely defends Azshara's treasures against the endless stream of adventurers seeking fame or plunder.

Azurelode Mine. Azurelode Mine is an active Alliance iron mine nestled in the southwestern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by Southshore's militia and worked by human laborers, its steady supply of ore fuels the local human war effort against the Forsaken of Tarren Mill. Situated southwest of the open farmland and just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine has long tapped into the mineral-rich ridges along the coast. Today, human miners labor deep underground under the watchful eye of Foreman Bonds, extracting iron to forge arms and armor for the Alliance defenders holding the region against the Undercity.

Back to Billy. You carry Bernice Stonefield's freshly baked pie across the road to Billy Maclure, who has information about her missing necklace. The delivery continues the feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families in central Elwynn Forest. The old feud between the Stonefields and Maclures leaves little room for kindness. Auntie Bernice Stonefield baked a pork belly pie because Billy Maclure would not share what he knew about her family heirloom without it. She hands you the pie with plain irritation and hopes Billy chokes on every bite.

text.enUS: Back to Booty Bay. Kravel Koalbeard trusts you to get a job done and to keep quiet about it. He has a new scheme, risky but with the promise of a bundle for you both. You carry his letter to Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay. This follows Rumors for Kravel. Kravel Koalbeard, the dwarf at the Mirage Raceway, calls you someone he can trust, both to finish a job and to hold your tongue about it. His new scheme carries risk, yet if it pays off the two of you stand to make a bundle. He apologizes for sending you back to Booty Bay, where his last job took you, and asks you to find Crank Fizzlebub there and hand over a letter. If Crank needs help, Kravel wants you to do your best, and says it will be worth the effort.

Back to Darnassus. After meeting the Great Bear Spirit, a young night elf druid returns to Darnassus. The initiate has left Moonglade and now reports to Mathrengyl Bearwalker in the Cenarion Enclave for practical shapeshifting trials. Dendrite Starblaze sends the initiate from Nighthaven back to Darnassus after the meeting with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade. The journey joins two sanctuaries: Moonglade, where the young druid has communed with the spirit, and the unsettled world beyond. In Darnassus, local mentors watch over Teldrassil and guide the next stage of training.

name.ptBR: De volta ao Penhasco do Trovão

text.enUS: Back to Thunder Bluff. "Back to Thunder Bluff" is an essential rite of passage for young tauren druids returning from the sacred glades of Moonglade. Having communed with the Great Bear Spirit, the initiate is sent by Dendrite Starblaze back to Elder Rise to continue training under Turak Runetotem. Moonglade stands apart from the factional divides of the mortal world, serving as a sanctuary where night elf and tauren practitioners of nature magic gather as the Cenarion Circle. After communion with the Great Bear Spirit, night elf mentor Dendrite Starblaze sends the young tauren back to their people. While night elves often view tauren as fledglings in the formalized teachings of Cenarius, Starblaze readily acknowledges the profound wisdom and balance maintained by Turak Runetotem.

Bad Medicine. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks to blunt Colonel Kurzen's military advantage by targeting his medical support. The renegades rely on powerful remedies and toxins concocted by their practitioners, leaving the resistance fighters desperate to turn those same concoctions to their own advantage. Colonel Kurzen has bolstered his jungle force with numerous medicine men who heal his forces and poison Yohwa's fighters with venom fern extracts. To turn the tide of the conflict, Sergeant Yohwa directs adventurers into the Kurzen Compound to scavenge those vital supplies. Securing their jungle remedies will help treat wounded fighters at the Rebel Camp, while capturing a sample of their venom fern extract will enable the resistance to study the toxin and manufacture their own cures.

Badlands Reagent Run. In the outpost of Kargath, Jarkal Mossmeld, an alchemist of some note, needs reagents found out in the Badlands to replenish stocks. Coin is promised, but only to someone who brings the goods. Jarkal Mossmeld is short on ingredients: gizzards from five buzzards, fangs from ten crag coyotes, and shards from five rock elementals. All three can be taken from the creatures themselves. Anyone who is not the fighting type is told to find friends who are. Jarkal pays in coin, but only once the reagents are in hand.

Bael Modan. Dwarven crews blast into the red earth at Bael Modan, searching for Titan relics. Their fortified outpost has driven the Stonespire tauren from their sacred land and kindled a bitter fight. Bael Modan's walls guard Bael'dun Keep, siege cannons, gyrocopter landing pads, and a deep excavation pit. Dwarven prospectors came to Kalimdor convinced an ancient Titan facility lay beneath the red earth. Their blasting tore through sacred ground of the Stonespire tauren. The expedition answered no call to negotiate. Gunfire and explosives drove the tribe from its ancestral lands, leaving survivors scattered and vengeful.

Bael'dun Digsite. The Bael'dun Digsite is a dwarven excavation carved deep into the mountains along the western edge of Mulgore. Established by Prospector Khazgorm's team out of Bael Modan, the quarry is viewed by the local tauren as a direct desecration of their ancestral homeland and an insult to the Earth Mother. Perched on the mountain slopes of western Mulgore, the Bael'dun Digsite represents the southernmost reach of the dwarven Explorers' League expedition based out of Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Unconcerned with territorial borders or the spiritual traditions of the newly settled tribes, dwarven prospectors arrived with picks, shovels, and blasting powder to unearth ancient Titan relics buried beneath the plains.

Bael'dun Keep. Dwarven forces hold Bael'dun Keep above the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens. Under General Twinbraid, this imposing fortification anchors the Alliance's controversial presence in the region and brings it into violent conflict with the surrounding Horde territories. Bael'dun Keep rises over the Bael Modan excavation as the fortified military heart of Ironforge's presence in the southern Barrens. Dwarven architect Haggis Boatmurder designed the stronghold to protect the Prospectors and archaeologists searching the trenches for ancient titan artifacts. Ironworks and artillery arm its garrison, which keeps a vigilant watch, secures dwarven supply lines, and projects Alliance military power into Kalimdor's heartland.
