text.enUS: Bottom of Gelkak's Key. Along Darkshore, the Bottom of Gelkak's Key is one of three fragments of a shattered winding key. It belonged to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast, and reef crawlers scavenged it from the shore. Threshadons sank Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore, casting the gnome and his belongings ashore. Among them was the winding key that activated his mechanical first mate. The key broke against the coastal rocks into three pieces, and local scavengers descended on the debris. Reef and tide crawlers seized the bottom fragment as they searched the tideline.

Bough Shadow. Bough Shadow is a secluded grove tucked away in the far northeastern corner of Ashenvale, east of Forest Song. It centers around a colossal Great Tree rooted over an ancient portal leading directly into the Emerald Dream. Bough Shadow houses one of the rare Great Trees, its roots plunging deep into the earth around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. Today, the tranquil yet imposing grove is heavily guarded by the Green Dragonflight. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy, while patrols of Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles keep a vigilant, unyielding watch over the swirling green portal at its base, turning away any mortal who approaches unbidden.

Boulder Lode Mine. In the northeastern Barrens, the Venture Company tears into Boulder Lode Mine for its riches. Orcish banners and watchtowers mark a claim the Horde once held. Weathered orcish works frame the mine mouth, signs that the Horde once held or founded the claim. Now Venture Company overseers and enforcers answer to Boss Copperplug. The goblin syndicate strips the canyon for minerals, gems, and machinery, with little care for the land or its workers.

Boulder'gor. Boulder'gor is a rugged hill in the western Arathi Highlands, situated directly north of the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. It serves as an active encampment for the Boulderfist ogres and their unusual allies among the Witherbark forest trolls. Rising just north of the crumbling ramparts of Stromgarde Keep, Boulder'gor is a steep bluff claimed by the Boulderfist clan. Within its shadows sits the Boulderfist Outpost mound, making it a central bastion of ogre power across the highlands. Uniquely, the ogres here share their fires and fortifications with forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe, including shadowy spellcasters who lend their dark magic to the clan's brute force. This mutual cooperation poses an ongoing danger to any travelers passing along the central roads of Arathi.

Boulderfist Hall. Boulderfist Hall is a heavily fortified ogre mound nestled in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just north of Thandol Span. It serves as the local stronghold for the Boulderfist ogres, who exert their brute influence across the neighboring trade routes and valleys under the command of Kor'gresh Coldrage. Carved into the rugged southern bluffs of the Arathi Highlands, Boulderfist Hall is the principal redoubt of the Boulderfist clan in the region. Sheltered within its earthen ramparts and deep caverns, ogre brutes and magi maintain a fortified settlement mere steps from Witherbark Village and the strategic bridge at Thandol Span. Deep within the mound lurks their regional chieftain, Kor'gresh Coldrage, alongside enforcers like Phalanax. From this stronghold, the ogres project violent control over the surrounding roads, making any peaceful transit between Arathi and the Wetlands perilous for travelers and supply caravans alike.

Boulderfist Outpost. Boulderfist Outpost is a fortified mound nestled deep within the ogre settlement of Boulder'gor in the Arathi Highlands. Serving as an interior den and holding area, it houses aggressive Boulderfist ogres alongside a few Witherbark trolls. Carved into the earth and stone of western Arathi, Boulderfist Outpost functions as the heart of Boulder'gor. While brute enforcers dominate the settlement above, the outpost's interior concentrates the clan's core strength and provides a dark subterranean shelter. A handful of Witherbark troll witch doctors occasionally mingle among the ogres here, hinting at tenuous tribal cooperation.

Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide Cavern is a subterranean warren tucked at the deepest end of Boulderslide Ravine in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as the primary den and excavation site for the local Boulderslide kobolds, who obsessively tunnel in search of glowing mineral formations. The Boulderslide kobolds have burrowed deep into the crags of Stonetalon, establishing Boulderslide Cavern as their stronghold. Unlike ordinary vermin merely seeking shelter, these kobolds mine frantically for resonite, a rare glowing purple crystal embedded throughout the stone. The crystals pulse with lingering earthen magic, driving the creatures into a defensive frenzy against any intruders who approach their dig.

Boulderslide Ravine. Deep in the Boulderslide Ravine of the Stonetalon Mountains, local kobolds have begun frantically mining a rare subterranean mineral known as Resonite. Sensing a growing tension in the earth, the tauren Mor'rogal sends Horde adventurers to explore the ravine's cave system and retrieve mineral samples to uncover what lies buried beneath the rock. From his post at Sun Rock Retreat, the tauren Mor'rogal watches the peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains with deep concern. The land itself feels disturbed, an unnatural agitation radiating from the southeast. There, within the crags of Boulderslide Ravine, the local kobolds have abandoned their ordinary foraging to aggressively excavate a rare, subterranean mineral known as Resonite. To determine why these superstitious vermin are mining with such desperate frenzy, Mor'rogal enlists Horde scouts to push past their defenses, plumb the lowest depths of the cavern, and bring back unrefined mineral samples.

Boulderslide Ravine. Boulderslide Ravine is a rugged, secluded canyon tucked away in the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via Webwinder Path. Largely spared from the direct clashes between the Horde and Alliance, it serves as the rocky approach to Boulderslide Cavern and remains home to wild mountain beasts. Tucked away off Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine is a narrow cut of rock in the Stonetalon heights. While loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades throughout the region, this craggy pass remains relatively undisturbed by military forces. Wild mountain rams and roaming crag beasts like Cliff Stormers make up the local fauna, navigating the treacherous ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors also keep an eye on the ravine, as rich mineral veins frequently crop up along the rocky slopes leading deeper toward the cavern network.

text.enUS: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. In Northshire, an Alliance bounty names Garrick Padfoot, a notorious local thief. Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey calls for recruits to hunt him near the vineyards. Northshire Valley once offered a safe place to train recruits and tend its sacred vineyards. As order falters across Elwynn, thieves have reached the valley. Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat, quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, he and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants on the roads, and threatened local farmers.

Bounty on Murlocs. Murlocs are spreading through eastern Elwynn, and the Stormwind Army has put a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear the shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before the murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers now attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a minor nuisance has grown into a threat across eastern Elwynn, while the western roads remain comparatively secure.

Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg. Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg is an Alliance quest authorized by the Sentinels to curb the aggressive furbolg population corrupting Teldrassil. Shayla Nightbreeze recruits adventurers outside Darnassus to hunt the corrupted beasts and collect their fangs as proof of deed. On the road outside Darnassus, Shayla Nightbreeze acts on direct orders from the Sentinels to place a bounty on the Gnarlpine furbolg. Once peaceful inhabitants of the ancient forests, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading corruption that stripped away their reason, turning them into vicious threats to the safety of travelers and the natural sanctity of Teldrassil.

Bracers of Binding. Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill says the Magus, busy with the stone tokens you gathered, will eventually want their counterpart: bracers of binding. You are to collect four Bracers of Earth Binding from elementals among the ruins of Dalaran. While the Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, Bel'varil expects a further wish: samples of the matching piece, bracers of binding. Worn on an elemental's wrists, they tie it to a mage's service. Among the ruins of Dalaran, elementals wear them. Bel'varil wants four Bracers of Earth Binding brought to Tarren Mill.

Brackenwall Village. Brackenwall Village is the primary Horde outpost in Dustwallow Marsh, nestled among the bogs in the northwest corner of the zone. Founded by surviving Stonemaul ogres after dragons devastated their original settlement to the south, the village serves as a tenuous stronghold surrounded by Alliance spies, deserters, and the black dragonflight. When black dragonkin drove the Stonemaul ogres out of their ancient home at Stonemaul Village in the southern marsh, their leader, Overlord Mok'Morokk—successor to Rexxar—led the survivors north into the swamp to build Brackenwall. Formed around traditional earthen mounds, huts, and an old watchtower, the settlement gave the battered clan a defensible haven. Though aligned with the Horde, the village suffers from internal rot: Mok'Morokk sits idle, hoarding supplies and refusing to confront the draconic threat, leaving the clan's spiritual and tactical guidance to figures like the ogre mage Draz'Zilb and Horde emissaries.

Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Defias brigands have taken over Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in southeastern Elwynn Forest. The farm once belonged to the Brackwell family, but now its cottage and fields serve as a hideout where conspirators meet and stolen mine gold is received. You find the Brackwell farm southeast of the Stonefield homestead, its fields no longer tended. The Brackwell family has vanished, driven away or worse as crime spread through the area. The Defias Brotherhood now occupies the sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. Brigands regroup here beyond the reach of Goldshire's patrols. Morgan the Collector and other prominent conspirators use the isolated farm to receive illicit gold taken from the forest's mines.

Braelyn Firehand. Braelyn Firehand is an elusive elf residing quietly among the Horde at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. While presenting herself as an arcane practitioner seeking to clear mystical obstructions in the highlands, she pursues a deep personal grudge against the grove keepers of Stonetalon Peak. Standing out amidst the tauren lodges and rustic orcish tents of Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand is a rare sight: a blood elf dwelling openly within a remote Horde settlement. The shaman and chieftains of the retreat tolerate her presence, seemingly oblivious to her true loyalties. Braelyn presents herself as an observer fascinated by the flow of regional magic, eager to hire passing Horde mercenaries to handle dangerous field assignments across the crags.

Braenna Flintcrag. Braenna Flintcrag is a dwarven priest trainer stationed within the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. She instructs devout followers of the Holy Light, guiding dwarven acolytes as they develop their spiritual disciplines and healing arts. She also passes word to visiting night elf priests when they are called home to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Residing within the quiet alcoves of the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Braenna Flintcrag serves the Alliance as a dedicated priest trainer. While Ironforge is renowned for its roaring forges and martial warriors, devout dwarves like Braenna tend to the spiritual welfare of Khaz Modan. She mentors novices answering the call of the Holy Light, teaching the dual disciplines of restorative mending and defensive warding required to survive in an increasingly dangerous world.

Brainwashed Noble. Deep in the caverns outside the Deadmines, Brainwashed Noble remains captive under Defias control. Magical manipulation has stripped him of his will, and he serves the Brotherhood alongside undead minions instead of walking Stormwind's grand halls.

Brambleblade Ravine. Brambleblade Ravine is a rugged canyon cutting into the northeastern edge of Red Cloud Mesa. It serves as a fortified den for the Bristleback quilboar tribe, who persistently raid the nearby tauren settlement of Camp Narache. Young tauren braves are sent here to prove their strength and protect their homeland from these fierce interlopers. Carved into the sun-scorched earth of Red Cloud Mesa, Brambleblade Ravine is choked with dense, thorny briars and quilboar encampments. The Bristleback tribe uses this natural fortress as a staging ground for raids against Camp Narache, threatening the safety of young tauren coming of age. Bristleback shamans and warriors, led by Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, dwell deep within the ravine among trained battleboars. For the Shu'halo, striking into the heart of the canyon is a crucial rite of passage and a grim necessity to secure the plains.

Bramblescar. Across the southern Barrens, Bramblescar's Razormane wage war with the Bristleback across the Gold Road. Thick brambles fortify their settlement. Bramblescar is carved into the jagged briars of the southern Barrens. The thick, sharp thorns make a vital redoubt for the Razormane quilboar and deter casual wanderers. The tribe is fiercely territorial and hostile to outsiders. They skirmish with anyone who approaches, treating all who are not quilboar as intruders on land blessed by their ancient boar gods.

Branch of Cenarius. The Branch of Cenarius is a sacred dryad relic stolen by the vile satyr Geltharis in eastern Ashenvale. Recovering this heirloom was the dying wish of the dryad Anilia, who perished defending it from the woods' corruptors. Revered by the daughters of Cenarius, the Branch of Cenarius represents both the blessing of the Forest Lord and the deep connection his dryads maintain with Ashenvale. The branch was held in high regard by the dryad sisters Anilia and Illiyana until a band of corrupt satyrs ambushed them. The satyr leader, Geltharis, seized the relic and mortally wounded Anilia near the tainted ruins of eastern Ashenvale. With her dying breaths, Anilia pointed northward toward the arch where Geltharis lurks, pleading for a champion to wrest the sacred bough from his claws and restore it to dryad hands at Forest Song.

Brandur Ironhammer. Brandur Ironhammer is a dwarven paladin trainer residing in the Hall of Mysteries within Ironforge. He guides aspiring champions of the Holy Light through their early rites, testing their devotion and dispatching them across the Alliance. Stationed within the quiet alcoves of the Hall of Mysteries, Brandur Ironhammer serves the Alliance by instructing novice paladins in the ways of the Holy Light. Alongside his peer, Tiza Battleforge, Brandur keeps a watchful eye on young dwarven champions, guiding them through the trials of the Tome of Divinity. While deeply committed to his holy duties, he has acknowledged personal flaws under Tiza's frank counsel, working diligently to temper his envy and maintain the inner purity demanded of a warrior of the Light.

Brann Bronzebeard. Brann Bronzebeard is the youngest brother of King Magni and Muradin, who is believed dead, renowned throughout Azeroth as a peerless explorer, archaeologist, and founding leader of the Explorers' League. Driven by an insatiable curiosity for titan ruins and ancient history, his wanderlust has led him deep into the deadly wastes of Silithus. His field companions in southern Silithus await news of his latest expedition. While his eldest brother Magni rules Ironforge from the throne and Muradin served on battlefield frontlines, Brann took to the open wilds. He was a veteran warrior of the Second War. Yet peacetime turned his formidable constitution toward uncovering the forgotten past. As a leader of the Explorers' League, Brann charted vast swathes of the Eastern Kingdoms—from Elwynn Forest to the untamed jungles of Zul'Gurub—before turning his gaze across the Great Sea to the mysteries of ancient Kalimdor.

Branstock Khalder. Branstock Khalder is the priest trainer stationed at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Friendly and grounded, he introduces novice dwarven priests to the Holy Light while keeping a watchful eye on the growing trogg threat outside. Inside the bustling hall of Anvilmar, Branstock Khalder serves as a patient mentor to aspiring priests embarking on their spiritual journey. An easy-going dwarf with a deep devotion to the Light, he helps new acolytes master their early prayers and sacred runes. While his primary duty is spiritual instruction, Branstock is acutely aware of the valley's mounting perils—most notably the aggressive trogg infestation menacing the local mountaineers. Once a novice demonstrates sufficient command of the Light, he directs them through Coldridge Pass to seek further guidance from his superior, Maxan Anvol, in Kharanos.

Brass Collar. At the Brackwell pumpkin patch, Princess wears a brass collar that Ma Stonefield wants as proof the sow is gone. Princess is a huge, prize-winning sow owned by the Brackwell family. She roams their pumpkin patch east of the Maclure homestead, and her appetite leads her into the Stonefield Farm’s crops. After losing valuable vegetables to the sow, Ma Stonefield seeks someone willing to slay her. Princess wears a brass band around her neck, and the collar proves she will not raid the Stonefield fields again.

Brave Moonhorn. Brave Moonhorn is a tauren scout stationed at the top of the Great Lift on the southern border of the Barrens. From this precipice, he keeps watch over the entry to Thousand Needles and alerts travelers to the local dangers ahead. Perched above the sheer drops of Thousand Needles, Brave Moonhorn stands guard where the northern plains meet the canyonlands. His primary role is keeping watchful eyes on regional threats moving through the canyon floor below, particularly the hostile centaur clans. Anyone looking to descend into the needles often crosses paths with him first, receiving crucial warnings before they step onto the massive platforms of the Great Lift.

Break Sharptusk!. Break Sharptusk! is a decisive rite of passage issued by Brave Windfeather on Red Cloud Mesa. To secure the tauren homeland against ongoing raids, young champions are sent east into Brambleblade Ravine to slay Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle. Eliminating the Bristleback chieftain strikes a severe blow against the quilboar encroaching upon Mulgore. The grassy heights of Red Cloud Mesa have long served as a peaceful sanctuary where young tauren learn the traditions of the hunt and attunement with the Earth Mother. However, this peace is constantly contested. To the east lies Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked gulch claimed by the hostile Bristleback quilboar tribe. The quilboar view the tauren as invaders stealing sacred ground, launching relentless skirmishes against the tribes attempting to establish a stable life in Mulgore.

Break a Few Eggs. Break a Few Eggs is an errand assisting a harried cook who must keep up with endless meal preparations. Securing fresh, fragile ingredients without breaking them keeps the kitchen running and the cooking on schedule. Feeding a crowd is an exhausting, never-ending endeavor. Between breakfast, lunch, and dinner, there is scarcely any time to step away from the stove, let alone leave the kitchen to scrounge for raw provisions. In Break a Few Eggs, a hard-pressed cook turns to passing adventurers to secure fresh eggs before the next meal service falls behind.

Breaking the Keystone. Once the Stones of Binding were opened, much of the voice's confinement eased, yet a lock still holds it. That lock is the Keystone among a ring of stones, and the stone watcher Fozruk, one of the voice's captors, holds the key, known to the watchers as the Rod of Order. With the Stones of Binding opened, the voice's confinement has eased a great deal, but one lock remains: the Keystone, among the circle of stones around you. Its key is held by a captor, the stone watcher Fozruk, and the watchers call it the Rod of Order. Taking the rod from Fozruk and carrying it to the Keystone is how the lock will open. The voice promises that its gratitude, if you manage this, will shake the earth to its roots. The Keystone itself is charged with immense geomantic energy.

Brewer's Trade. A trade has been worked out with the Dun Garok brew-kin, who miss the Fallrook family's vineyards as much as anyone. A case of Fallrook Varietal travels to their fort in the southeast of Hillsbrad Foothills, and a sack of their Homebrew Hops comes back. Most of the best bottled years of Fallrook wine are long since drunk, but cases of the Fallrook Varietal still sit in the cellars. The Dun Garok brew-kin miss the vineyards of the Fallrook family too, and a trade has been worked out with them.

Brewmaster Drohn. Above Ratchet's docks, Brewmaster Drohn tends his brewing craft. The orc lives just uphill from the port, making potent drinks with methods tied to the wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout. Travelers who find discarded kegs across Kalimdor are sent to Drohn's porch. Brewmaster Drohn brews from his home on the hill above Ratchet's goblin docks. Rather than devote himself to combat, the orc has given his craft to brewing. He lives peacefully in the neutral haven established by Gazlowe's Steamwheedle cartel. While many orcs favor coarse grog or simple spirits, Drohn works with rare ingredients, carefully balanced flavors, and methods seldom practiced among his kin.

Brewmeister Bilger. Brewmeister Bilger is an intoxicated dwarven brewer residing in the cellar of the inn at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He whiles away his hours tasting potent spirits and waiting on deliveries from distant lands. Bilger spends his days pacing the cool cellar beneath Southshore's inn, nursing hiccups and seeking out the strongest brews Azeroth can offer.

Brewnall Village. Brewnall Village is a small dwarven settlement nestled in Chill Breeze Valley near the entrance to Gnomeregan. Established by the Barleybrew family, this outpost serves as a proving ground for bold brewing experiments and regional defense against wild beasts. Despite being called a village, it functions largely as a rustic encampment in the snowy gnomish lowlands of Dun Morogh. Tucked away in the snowdrifts of Chill Breeze Valley, Brewnall Village lies squarely within the traditional gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. The settlement is home to the Barleybrew clan, stalwart dwarven brewers devoted to perfecting age-old recipes and crafting the ultimate stout. Though dubbed a village, the outpost consists mostly of tents and outdoor brewing equipment rather than permanent stone architecture. Between testing experimental batches of ale and defending against the ferocious local wolves and bears, the Barleybrews rely heavily on wandering mountaineers to gather rare ingredients and keep the valley secure.

Bride of the Embalmer. "Bride of the Embalmer" is a perilous task assigned by Lord Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire. Having pieced together the disturbing truth behind the legendary Embalmer, town leadership sends you into the haunted cemeteries of Duskwood to find his resurrected wife's resting place. By tearing the alchemist's living heart from Eliza's cursed remains, you aim to strip him of his unholy power. For years, parents in Duskwood told their frightened children the tale of the Embalmer. According to the folktale, he was once a kindly alchemist whose mind shattered following the tragic demise of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to cheat mortality, he turned to foul sorceries and took the ultimate sacrifice: carving out his own beating heart and placing it into his wife's chest. Lord Ello Ebonlocke long dismissed this as mere village folklore, but recent revelations have proven that the Embalmer walks among them, his foul handiwork festering beneath the graveyard dirt.

Brightwater Lake. Brightwater Lake is the largest body of water in Tirisfal Glades, stretching across the mist-shrouded lowlands northeast of Brill. Once a tranquil retreat for the kingdom of Lordaeron, its waters now lie cold and dark, surrounding a central isle where an outcast necromancer conducts his forbidden research. Spanning the northern plains between the town of Brill and the Scarlet Watch Post, Brightwater Lake is a quiet and eerie landmark in the heart of Tirisfal. In the peaceful centuries under the Kingdom of Lordaeron, the lake served as a scenic country haven. Today, like the rest of the glades, its pristine character is long gone. The Plaguelands lie not far to the east, and the murky, chilled waters reflect only grey skies, withered trees, and the constant threat of roving murlocs and hostile undead.

Brightwood Grove. Brightwood Grove is a shadowed expanse of woodland located just west of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once part of the region's serene agrarian landscape, it is now infested with savage Nightbane worgen who make camp among ruined homesteads and attack any travelers wandering too close. Situated within sight of Darkshire's perimeter, Brightwood Grove represents the creeping peril threatening the town's borders. The homesteads and fences that once demarcated peaceful farmland now lie collapsed and rotting. In their place, crude camps have been erected by the Nightbane worgen, who prowl the overgrown clearings. The proximity of these wolf-beasts poses an ongoing threat to the town, forcing the Night Watch and passing adventurers to continually cull their numbers before the settlement is overrun.

Brill. Brill is the primary Forsaken settlement in the heart of Tirisfal Glades, situated just north of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once a prosperous human town, it now serves as the administrative and military hub for newly awakened undead stepping beyond the confines of Deathknell. Before the Third War, Brill was a lively village under the sway of regional nobles such as the Barov and Agamand families. That prosperity ended when Kel'Thuzad chose the area for the Cult of the Damned's earliest experiments with the Plague of Undeath. The devastating blight swept through the population so quickly that local militia were driven out, leaving a sprawling mass graveyard in its wake. Now rebuilt by the Forsaken under the leadership of Magistrate Sevren, the town retains its weathered Lordaeron architecture beneath an atmosphere of grim purpose. Brill functions as the regional command center, coordinating defenses against Scarlet Crusade incursions, roaming Scourge remnants, and native beasts warped by necromantic decay.

Brill Town Hall. Brill Town Hall is the administrative heart of the settlement of Brill in central Tirisfal Glades. Standing as the most prominent structure in town, it serves as the civic headquarters from which the Forsaken govern their local holdings and coordinate the defense of the glades. While much of Lordaeron lies shattered and ruined, Brill Town Hall remains standing as a functioning civic center under undead rule. Inside, Magistrate Sevren directs town affairs from his podium, handing out vital commissions and directives to Forsaken adventurers. Aside from the Defiler's Den in the Arathi Highlands, it is one of the only recognized town halls in the known world actively run by the Forsaken, serving as a bleak parody and functional continuation of old Lordaeron's municipal bureaucracy.

Brine. On Blackthorn Ridge, Brine guides shaman initiates toward the spirits of water. This orc shaman teaches them to commune with the tides and earn their Water Totem. Brine lives on a hill in northern Blackthorn Ridge, far from the Barrens' trading posts. Though dry savannas surround her, she has devoted her life to understanding water. Shaman across the Horde seek her wisdom after mastering earth and fire. She teaches that water calls for patience and perspective, qualities few understand as deeply as she does.

Bring Back the Mug. After delivering a piping hot draught of Mornbrew across the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, one final errand remains: returning the empty tankard. Durnan Furcutter sends the runner back across Coldridge Valley to return Nori Pridedrift's prized mug. It is a simple courtesy, but one the brew seller deeply appreciates. Serving piping hot Mornbrew out in the biting freeze of Dun Morogh is a delicate business. Once Durnan Furcutter has finished warming his bones with the scalding brew, the empty tankard cannot simply be tossed in the snow. Dwarven hospitality runs on mutual respect, and letting good dishware go missing is a sure way to find oneself cut off from future rounds.

text.enUS: Bristleback Attack Plans. The Bristleback Attack Plans are crude maps and tactical notes drafted by the quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine. They outline a coordinated siege aimed directly at overrunning the tauren settlement of Camp Narache. Hidden deep within a dirt cave in Brambleblade Ravine, these scribbled tactical sketches reveal that the Bristleback quilboar are no longer just skirmishing on the borders of the Red Cloud Mesa. Instead, their leadership planned an organized, sustained assault to push into Camp Narache and wipe out the young tauren training there. Delivering this map to Chief Hawkwind allows the tribe to send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements, blunting the impending invasion before it can begin.

Bristleback Belt. A Bristleback Belt is a piece of crudely crafted gear worn by the quilboar infesting Brambleblade Ravine. For young tauren coming of age in Camp Narache, collecting these belts serves as physical proof of valor during the Rite of Strength. The Red Cloud tribe tests every youth who aspires to earn respect in Thunder Bluff through the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. The first trial, the Rite of Strength, requires the initiate to protect the tribe from active threats. Because the hostile Bristleback quilboar repeatedly raid tribal food supplies and ambush hunting parties outside Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind demands the belts of these intruders. Returning twelve belts to the chieftain proves that an initiate can confront danger directly and strike a blow for the tribe's defense.

Bristleback Quilboar Tusk. Across the northern and central Barrens, Bristleback Quilboar Tusks are taken from slain quilboar. Mankrik gathers them as proof of slaughter and tokens of vengeance. Bristleback quilboar defend their territory across the Barrens against Horde expansion. Their jagged ivory tusks serve as weapons in close combat. Mankrik, a veteran orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads, lost his wife in a vicious quilboar ambush. He gathers dozens of tusks as retribution, a bloody count of the suffering he means to return to the Bristlebacks.

Brock Stoneseeker. Brock Stoneseeker is a dwarven mining instructor based in the settlement of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. As the proprietor of Brock's School of Mining and Surveying, he instructs novice prospectors in the craft of extracting valuable ores and minerals from the earth. Operating out of Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker directs Brock's School of Mining and Surveying. In the mineral-rich hills of Loch Modan, seasoned expertise with a pickaxe and an eye for geological veins are indispensable. Brock guides aspiring miners through the foundational techniques of identifying ore nodes, extracting raw metals, and properly surveying subterranean deposits, ensuring Alliance tradesfolk can fuel Ironforge's legendary smithies.

Brock's List. Brock's List is a dispatch compiled by the mining instructor Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar. It contains the names of top mining pupils who have earned honorary picks from the guild halls in Ironforge. Mining is the lifeblood of dwarven civilization, and apprentice diggers must prove their skill before they are entrusted with serious work in Khaz Modan's veins. In Thelsamar, the local mining trainer compiles this parchment to reward students who excel in their lessons. The document records those who have earned honorary picks—coveted symbols of competence forged in the capital.

Broken Alliances. In Kargath, Gorn wants the Horde's honor restored after its alliance with Deathwing. The ogre Boss Tho'grun, hired to help get the Sign of the Earth, turned on the Horde and kept it for himself, and you are to take it back at Camp Boff. During the Second War the Horde stood with the dragon Deathwing. Blacklash and Hematus, a pair of his lieutenants, ended up locked away in Lethlor Ravine, far off to the east. Gorn holds that these depraved allies of old must be silenced if the Horde's honor is to be restored. To open the drakes' prison the Horde needed the Sign of the Earth, and hired ogre mercenaries under Boss Tho'grun to help find it. Tho'grun turned on them, overwhelmed them and kept it for himself.

Broken Alliances. Gorn sends you to Lethlor Ravine in the far eastern Badlands, where the black drakes Blacklash and Hematus lie bound by the Seal of the Earth. This follows the first Broken Alliances. Three runestones keep the Seal of the Earth closed. Each rests in a pillar of Lethlor Ravine: Diamond, Opal and Amethyst. The Sign of the Earth, which Gorn gives you, draws the stones out and opens the seal. Countless drakes make their home in the ravine, and Blacklash and Hematus are formidable. Gorn wants both dead, and their bindings brought back.

Broken Hall. The Broken Hall serves as the flooded outer threshold of the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Shattered when the Great Dragon Aspect Ysera and her flight dragged the grand ziggurat beneath the waters, this ruin now stands deserted as the Atal'ai zealots retreat into deeper sanctums. When the green dragons brought down their wrath upon the Atal'ai priesthood and submerged their unholy ziggurat beneath the Pool of Tears, the outermost architecture bore the brunt of the cataclysm. The floor of the Broken Hall collapsed completely, allowing murky swamp waters to flood the chamber. Because of the damage and submersion, the troll cultists abandoned this entrance hall, withdrawing further into the complex. Adventurers entering the sunken temple must wade through these sodden ruins before mounting the stairs to reach the Hall of Masks.

Broken Pillar. The Broken Pillar is a weathered cluster of ancient troll ruins jutting from the dunes south of Gadgetzan. It serves as an isolated research post for the goblin prospector and scientist Marvon Rivetseeker, who studies the enigmatic artifacts buried beneath the surrounding sands. Rising out of the sands south of Gadgetzan and east of the treacherous Abyssal Sands, the Broken Pillar marks the remnants of ancient troll architecture long swallowed by Tanaris. Despite the desolate surroundings and encroaching desert beasts, the site offers rare clues to the continent's prehistoric civilisations. Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin researcher originally based out of Ratchet, has established a lonely camp beside the shattered stonework to examine curious relics known as Gahz'ridian scattered across the waste.

text.enUS: Broken Samophlange. In the northern Barrens, a broken samophlange draws the notice of curious engineers. Its gears and shifting parts hint at a purpose no one has uncovered. The broken samophlange is a baffling contraption from the northern Barrens. Its moving assemblies and fine gears show careful workmanship, even in ruin. Sputtervalve, a goblin in Ratchet, damaged the delicate device by accident before anyone could document how it worked. The finder hoped to send working results to curious colleagues in Undermine, so they sought someone able to repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket, a clever tinkerer near the border outpost of Mor'shan Rampart, was the one they turned to.

Broken Tears. Warug says the Gelkis foolishly believe the centaur mother, Theradras, protects them. He sends you into the cave in their village to destroy the crystals they hoard there, the tears of Theradras, and bring him three of the broken pieces. Warug scorns the Gelkis for trusting Theradras, mother of the centaur, to protect them. To him no one protects the centaur, and the Magram, being the strongest, need no protection. He sends you to the cave in the Gelkis village, where they keep a hoard of crystals called the tears of Theradras. Smash them and bring Warug three broken pieces. He will only trust you with this if you are no enemy of the Magram.

Broken Tools. Broken Tools are the shattered remnants of dwarven prospector picks, intentionally destroyed at an anvil. They serve as physical proof to Baine Bloodhoof that the invasive dwarven excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has been disrupted. To the northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators have set up operations to delve into the hills of Mulgore. While the dwarves seek buried ancient history, the tauren view their aggressive excavation as a direct defilement of the Earth Mother. The noise and destruction agitate the local wildlife, particularly the roaming kodo herds. Rather than merely driving the excavators away, young Baine Bloodhoof instructs defenders to confiscate the prospectors' iron picks and shatter them upon a forge, rendering the expedition unable to gouge further into the earth.
