text.enUS: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. Chicken Clucking for a Mint is a lighthearted seasonal Alliance quest offered in Ironforge during the Hallow's End festival. To earn a traditional Ironforge Mint on behalf of the young orphan Jesper, adventurers must put aside their battle-hardened dignity and flap their arms while clucking like a chicken for the tavern's amusement. Innkeeper Firebrew gladly rewards anyone willing to swallow their pride to bring holiday cheer to a child. During Hallow's End, spirits run high across Azeroth as folk celebrate the break between harvest and winter with costumed revelry and seasonal treats. While seasoned heroes might normally feel too old to go door-to-door begging for candy, the plight of sick or orphaned children offers an honorable excuse. In Stormwind, young Jesper longs for holiday sweets, prompting visiting Alliance champions to gather iconic regional confections from innkeepers across the Alliance capitals.

text.enUS: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. During the festive season of Hallow's End, Innkeeper Norman of the Undercity offers a piece of candy to travelers helping an ailing child. To earn the Undercity Mint, adventurers must cast aside their dignity and flap about like a chicken. The Undercity is rarely known for laughter or warmth, built as it is beneath the ruins of Lordaeron by the liberated Forsaken. Yet when Hallow's End arrives, even the grim denizens of the Trade Quarter join in seasonal revelry. Innkeeper Norman holds onto a stash of Undercity Mints, designated for those collecting treats on behalf of young Spoops, a sick orphan in need of holiday cheer.

name.zhCN: 首席考古学家杜瑟·灰须

text.enUS: Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker gathers reports from the coast. The Ironforge dwarf works outside the Temple of the Moon, where he coordinates the Explorers' League's research and tracks colleagues in Darkshore. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker works outside the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, far from his home in Ironforge. He represents the Explorers' League, which sent him across the sea to Kalimdor for fieldwork. There, he speaks with night elf scholars such as Tarelvir and seeks knowledge of the ancient lands. In Ironforge, his lectures covered ancient lore and primordial beings, including the Wild God Agamaggan. Now he hopes to learn what the night elves' ancestral lands hold.

name.zhCN: 主工程师辛德维尔七世

text.enUS: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII is a veteran dwarven engineer stationed atop the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Tasked with the upkeep and defense of this monumental feat of engineering, he oversees its delicate mechanisms while keeping watch for sabotage. Those who speak with him quickly discover that grave dangers threaten the integrity of the great dam. The Stonewrought Dam is one of the crowning achievements of dwarven stonecraft and engineering, holding back the massive waters of the Loch. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII bears the immense responsibility of maintaining its structure and operational machinery. Perched along the crest of the dam, he monitors the waterways, sluice gates, and structural stress points against the elements and local hazards.

Chief Hawkwind. Chief Hawkwind is the tribal leader of Camp Narache, the proving grounds nestled in the Red Cloud Mesa of Mulgore. Responsible for guiding the youth of the Shu'halo, he mentors new adventurers as they embark on their traditional rites of passage. Under his watchful gaze, young braves learn humility, respect for the land, and the strength needed to protect their people. Standing at the heart of Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind carries the solemn responsibility of preparing the next generation of tauren for the wider world. Red Cloud Mesa serves as a sheltered haven where fledgling hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors undertake the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. Hawkwind oversees these customs, ensuring that every youth learns duty and endurance before venturing beyond the safety of the mesa.

Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head. Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head is taken as grim proof of victory over the leader of the Bristleback quilboar threatening Red Cloud Mesa. Recovered from the depths of Brambleblade Ravine, it is presented to Brave Windfeather to mark the end of a persistent menace against young tauren braves. The tauren carve their peaceful homeland out of Mulgore through vigilance and strength. The Bristleback quilboar entrenched within Brambleblade Ravine have waged an aggressive campaign against the tribes of Camp Narache, urged on by their ferocious chieftain, Sharptusk Thornmantle. Severing his head serves not out of senseless cruelty, but as definitive proof of his demise and a stark warning to the surviving quilboar clans encroaching upon mesa borders.

Chill Breeze Valley. Chill Breeze Valley is a rugged, snow-covered pass in western Dun Morogh linking the dwarven settlement of Kharanos with the embattled city of Gnomeregan. While its main path is a well-traveled thoroughfare for young travelers and refugees, its secluded recesses harbor dangerous beasts and bloody dens. Chill Breeze Valley forms a T-shaped trench through the mountains of western Dun Morogh. The main east-west trail sees steady foot traffic from novice dwarves and gnomes journeying between Kharanos and the outskirts of Gnomeregan. However, straying into the valley's north-south offshoot is another matter entirely. Strewn with bloodstains and mangled carcasses, these shadowy reaches harbor ferocious predators—most notably savage wendigos that lair in deep ice caves and prey on anyone reckless enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

Chillwind Camp. Chillwind Camp sits at the southern pass leading into the Western Plaguelands from the Alterac Mountains. Manned by an Alliance contingent working alongside the Argent Dawn, it serves as the final safe staging ground before the blighted ruins of Lordaeron. From this precarious outpost, commanders direct strikes against the nearby Scourge strongholds and plague cauldrons. Tucked into the rocky pass descending from Chillwind Point, Chillwind Camp is the first line of defense and primary base of operations for Alliance forces pushing into the Western Plaguelands. Though physically separated from the worst of the corruption by the high mountain ridges, the dead chill of the north hangs heavily over the tents and palisades. Under Commander Ashlam Valorfist, a sparse garrison of soldiers, scouts, and Argent Dawn specialists attempts to contain the horrors lingering along the King's Road and gather the intelligence necessary to reclaim Lordaeron's fallen fields.

Chillwind Point. Chillwind Point is a rocky rise and ancient troll ruin sitting on the high frontier between the Alterac Mountains, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the Western Plaguelands. It gets its name from the freezing drafts howling through the mountain pass out of the blighted north. Today, it serves as a lonely vantage point inhabited primarily by a lone troll mystic. Perched on the borderlands where Hillsbrad gives way to Alterac and the plagued north, Chillwind Point looks out over the mountain ravine leading directly into the Western Plaguelands. Long before Lordaeron claimed these passes, ancient trolls built stone structures upon these heights, the remnants of which still stand weather-beaten against the elements. Today, cold winds blow south through the ravine, carrying the chill of the fallen north into the foothill valleys below.

Chimaeric Horn. As part of the warrior rite to craft the Brutal Helm, Orm Stonehoof tasks an aspiring champion with journeying into the ruined Charred Vale. There, the warrior must hunt a maddened chimaera matriarch to claim her galvanized horn as both an act of mercy and proof of strength. Orm Stonehoof is willing to forge the legendary Brutal Helm for Horde warriors, but martial tradition demands that the wearer prove their mettle first. Orm does not simply ask for raw metal or coin; he demands proof of martial prowess and a willingness to confront the grim scars left behind by devastating conflict.

Chok'sul's Head. Chok'sul's Head serves as gruesome physical proof of the death of the Mo'grosh ogre chieftain. Brought to Magistrate Bluntnose in Thelsamar, it secures a formal bounty placed by local dwarven authorities. The ogres of Mo'grosh Stronghold pose a persistent menace to the settlements of Loch Modan, orchestrating assaults against Thelsamar, the excavation sites, and the vital Stonewrought Dam. Magistrate Bluntnose placed a bounty on the brute presumed to be coordinating these attacks: Chok'sul. Given the chaos of the northeastern hills, the magistrate demands undeniable evidence before releasing township funds. The severed head of the ogre chieftain provides the grotesque certainty the dwarven council needs to mark the contract fulfilled.

Chol'aruk the Ravener. A horror stalks a cave on Thorn Hill in the Barrens, where the Razormane call it Chol'aruk the Ravener. Bainham seeks its severed head to avenge comrades lost to similar beasts. Northwest of Bainham's camp in the Barrens, Thorn Hill rises above the Savannah. Razormane tribes have long fought over the plateau. Now rumors speak of a monstrous abomination in one of its caves, called Chol'aruk or the Ravener by the Razormane. Some travelers dismiss tales that it can swallow an armored orc whole. Those who have seen the carnage know the danger is real.

Christoph Jeffcoat. Christoph Jeffcoat is a Forsaken merchant stationed in the settlement of Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. He supplies local crafters and travelers with essential trade goods, cooking seasonings, and specialty recipes. In an active war zone contested by the Alliance and the Syndicate, his mundane wares keep the northern Horde war effort running. While Tarren Mill stands as the Forsaken's military stronghold in Hillsbrad Foothills, a garrison cannot fight on malice alone. Christoph Jeffcoat handles the quiet, practical side of occupation, vending reagents, tools, threads, and spices to soldiers and traveling artisans. From the soothing spices required for local culinary recipes like turtle bisque to rare schematics and alchemical vials, Jeffcoat ensures that Horde forces passing through southern Lordaeron are fully provisioned for the battles against Southshore and the regional perils.

Chronormu. Chronormu, who goes by the mortal name Chromie, is a bronze dragon disguised as an energetic female gnome. Tasked with safeguarding the flow of time on Azeroth, she often works directly with mortals rather than observing from afar. In the Western Plaguelands, she quietly intervenes in the tragic aftermath of the Third War to right disrupted temporal threads. Though she appears to mortals as an eccentric and cheerful gnome named Chromie, Chronormu is a member of the bronze dragonflight serving under the Timeless One, Nozdormu. Bronze dragons are charged by the titans with guarding history and correcting disruptions in the timeways. In the form of a female gnome, she walks beside mortals as an approachable, optimistic peer.

Church of the Holy Light. The Church of the Holy Light is the dominant religious institution of humanity, guiding mortal souls through the virtues of compassion, justice, and devotion. Originally centered in the lost northern kingdom of Lordaeron, its leadership now resides within the grand Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City following the devastation wrought by the Scourge. The Church's origins reach back over a millennium to the faith in the Holy Light that took root among the humans of Arathor, teaching them to channel sacred power to cure injuries and purge affliction. Driven by tenets of charity, righteousness, and the fundamental belief that the Light resides within all thinking beings, these teachings eventually coalesced into an organized faith. The kingdom of Lordaeron became the religious heartland of this doctrine, establishing revered sanctuaries throughout the north, including Stratholme, Andorhal, Tyr's Hand, and Light's Hope Chapel.

Circle of Aquementas. The Circle of Aquementas is a mysterious ring of upright standing stones positioned along the eastern shoreline of Tanaris, just south of Lost Rigger Cove. It serves as a ritual site where travelers can call forth the elemental spirit Aquementas. Tucked away along the windswept eastern coast of Tanaris, the Circle of Aquementas sits quietly south of the pirate stronghold at Lost Rigger Cove. Composed of weathered, upright stones arranged in a circular formation, this unusual site hums with elemental energy against the desert shore. It acts as a focus for summoning Aquementas, an elemental entity tied to an ancient artifact. While the surrounding beaches crawl with Southsea brigands and roaming sea creatures, the circle itself remains a solemn pocket of ritual power amidst the dunes.

Circle of East Binding. The Circle of East Binding is a mysterious ancient ritual site situated in the eastern reaches of the Arathi Highlands, just southwest of Hammerfall. Anchored by the Stone of East Binding, the site is violently contested and guarded by roaming water elementals known as cresting exiles. Positioned amidst the rugged highlands east of Stromgarde, the Circle of East Binding is one of several ancient sites of power scattered across the Arathi basin. At its focal point stands the Stone of East Binding, an enigmatic monument radiating potent elemental magic. Swirling water elementals known as cresting exiles roam the surrounding earth and fiercely defend the stone against any mortals who dare approach.

Circle of Inner Binding. The Circle of Inner Binding is an ancient ring of ritual stones situated in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just east of Stromgarde Keep. Guarded by hostile earth elementals, it holds the Stone of Inner Binding, the most potent seal used to restrain the imprisoned elemental princess Myzrael deep beneath the earth. Perched upon a plateau south of the main road, the Circle of Inner Binding anchors the strongest of the ancient wards sealing Myzrael beneath Arathi. Towering slabs surround the central Stone of Inner Binding, which thrums with dense geo-magical power. Enormous rumbling earth elementals patrol the stones relentlessly, drawn to the site's resonance or bound as guardians. Despite these potent wards, cracks in this inner seal permit the trapped entity beneath the Highlands to reach out telepathically, whispering pleas for freedom to unsuspecting wanderers who handle shards of its stone.

Circle of West Binding. The Circle of West Binding is one of several ancient ritual sites scattered across the Arathi Highlands, situated near Thoradin's Wall. Centered around the Stone of West Binding, this arcane ring is overrun by fiery elemental entities bound to the site. Tucked against the rugged slopes near Thoradin's Wall, the Circle of West Binding forms part of a wider network of ritual sites dispersed throughout the Arathi Highlands. At its heart sits the Stone of West Binding, an ancient relic tied to elemental containment. The grounds are swarming with Burning Exiles—volatile fire elementals that relentlessly guard the perimeter, making any approach to the stone a perilous endeavor for travelers traversing the western plains.

name.esES: La búsqueda del tesoro de Masatormento

text.enUS: Claim Rackmore's Treasure!. Rackmore's log tells of a ship bound for Feathermoon Stronghold that was set upon by creatures of the sea. To keep his treasure from his enemies, Rackmore hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle, and the silver key and golden key that open it are lost. The log says Rackmore's ship was on its way to Feathermoon Stronghold when seafaring creatures attacked it. Hoping to keep his treasure from his enemies, he hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle. Two keys open it, one silver and one gold, and both were lost. Someone who finds the keys and the chest will find a treasure.

Clam Bait. Mai'Lahii at Shadowprey Village has fished all his life and says the best bait is soft-shelled clam meat, which no fish can resist. He wants ten pieces, to be found around a wrecked ship up the coast to the north. Mai'Lahii has fished all his life, and he swears by soft-shelled clam meat as bait, since the fish cannot resist it. To the north, off the coast, lies a wrecked ship, and soft-shelled clams are scattered throughout that area. He asks for ten pieces of the meat.

Clarice Foster. Clarice Foster is a Forsaken woman residing deep beneath the bluffs of Mulgore within the Pools of Vision. Far from the plagued glades of Lordaeron, she spends her days in contemplation among the tauren seers and mystics. While most Forsaken remain in the northern lands of Lordaeron rebuilding their kingdom under the Undercity, Clarice Foster has traveled to the heart of the tauren lands in Kalimdor. Sheltered within the cavernous Pools of Vision beneath the mesa of Thunder Bluff, she dwells alongside Forsaken apothecaries and tauren shamans who study the spiritual and elemental mysteries of the earth.

Clarice's Pendant. Clarice's Pendant is a small keepsake belonging to Clarice Foster, an undead resident of the Pools of Vision in Thunder Bluff. Once a token from her former husband, Yuriv, the jewelry now serves only as a bitter reminder of abandoned family and misplaced devotion to the Light. Clarice's Pendant represents the fractured human past common to many of the Forsaken. Before the Third War consumed Lordaeron, Clarice's husband Yuriv abandoned her and their children to join the fight against the undead, proclaiming that devotion to the Holy Light took precedence over all else. Instead of saving his home, Yuriv perished, leaving his family behind to ultimately succumb to the very Scourge he set out to fight. For Clarice, the pendant is not a cherished memento, but an insulting trinket symbolizing a lifetime spent coming second to zealotry and duty.

Claw Key. The Claw Key is one of three druidic keys hidden within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Alongside the Barrow Key and Sleepers' Key, it is required to unlock the enchanted Talon Den Hoard. The night elf druids established the Talon Den high upon Stonetalon Peak as a sanctuary and repository for powerful relics. To ensure these treasures remained safe from trespassers, they hid them behind a layered security system. The hoard itself is sealed by three distinct enchanted locks: the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key, and the Claw Key. Each key is concealed inside a specialized druidic cache resembling a torch within the winding tunnels of the barrow den.

Clean Zone. The Clean Zone is a fortified, decontamination enclave nestled inside the ruined city of Gnomeregan just past the upper Hall of Gears. It serves as the sole safe haven within the irradiated facility where uncorrupted gnomish forces hold ground against surrounding troggs and leper gnomes. Here, field medics, technicians, and specialized Sparklematic machines offer respite and salvage operations amid the radioactive ruins. While most of Gnomeregan succumbed to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste, the Clean Zone remains untainted. Positioned strategically between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above, it acts as a fortified forward base. Resolute gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold the barricades day and night, ensuring Alliance expeditions have a stable staging ground to regroup, mend wounds, and maintain machinery.

Cleansing of the Infected. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender faces a hard choice over the infected thistle bears. His attempt to cure one has failed, and he asks you to kill the rabid beasts before they harm other creatures or spread the sickness. Tharnariun Treetender has searched for a remedy to the sickness spreading through Darkshore's wildlife. He tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the thistle bears remain diseased and violent. Now he asks you to put them down. He fears they will maul other creatures and carry the sickness farther into the ancient woodlands.

Cleansing the Eye. Cleansing the Eye is an Alliance quest that sends adventurers from the murky Wetlands south to the human capital of Stormwind. After recovering the cursed orb known as the Eye of Paleth, travelers must seek the aid of Archbishop Benedictus to purge its lingering taint. The Eye of Paleth recovered from the marshlands does not shine with holy clarity. Instead, it is steeped in an unsettling shadow, bearing the residual sorrow and trauma of the terrible tragedy that unfolded where it was lost. The dwarf Glorin Steelbrow recognizes the power of the orb, but admits he lacks the divine craft to lift such a heavy affliction.

Cleft. Gnarlpine furbolgs ambush travelers in the Cleft, northwest of Dolanaar. The Cleft lies off the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, where Gnarlpine furbolgs have made their den. Teldrassil’s spreading corruption has driven them mad, and they have fortified the hollow. From there, they threaten travelers on the main road and risk cutting Dolanaar off from Darnassus.

Cleft of Shadow. Rogues, warlocks, and their teachers gather in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. The caverns give them room to practice their arts under the Horde's watch. Below Orgrimmar, the Cleft of Shadow holds rogues of the Shadowswift Brotherhood and warlocks of the Darkfire Enclave. Thrall's Horde honors shamanism and strength of arms, yet its leaders make room for subtler arts. In these caverns, practitioners of poison and fel energy work away from the valley districts and under Orgrimmar's watch.

Clerk Daltry. Clerk Daltry is the civic record keeper stationed in Darkshire Town Hall in Duskwood. Surrounded by ledgers and registry books, he helps investigate the village's past and track down historical records, even if his archives are somewhat neglected and out of date. While Darkshire struggles against encroaching beasts, undead horrors, and supernatural gloom, everyday civic duties fall to Clerk Daltry. Working out of the Darkshire Town Hall alongside Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the local council, Daltry maintains the town's historical ledgers, property rolls, and census data. In a region fractured by disaster, his records are among the few surviving links to the days before Grand Hamlet fell into shadow.

Cliffspring Falls. Cliffspring Falls pours from Darkshore’s eastern cliffs into the forest below. Its waters feed the Cliffspring River and once supplied nearby night elf settlements, but a foul taint now spreads through the river basin. Cliffspring Falls pours from caves high in Darkshore’s eastern bluffs and feeds the Cliffspring River. The river winds west through the woods before emptying into the sea. Its clear waters once gave nearby night elf settlements their purest drinking water. Now they run murky and foul, spreading sickness and decay through the river basin. Naturalists investigating the falls have found the caves overrun by naga and cultists. They plot in the shadows, while demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood threatens to seep through the highland bedrock.

Cliffspring River Sample. In Darkshore, foul water gathers at the base of the Cliffspring River waterfall. Drawn for Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, the vial shows that corruption is moving toward the coast. The Cliffspring River runs from Darkshore's eastern heights, past ancient stone bridges, and into the sea at Mist's Edge. Its clear waters have turned foul and visibly corrupted. Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine, fears the tainted flow will reach the settlement's shore and water supply. He sent travelers to draw water from the pool beneath the river's lower waterfall. The sample confirms that unnatural rot is moving downstream toward the coast.

Cliffwatcher Longhorn. Cliffwatcher Longhorn is the stoic tauren leader stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Tasked with safeguarding the isolated Horde outpost, he coordinates defenses against encroaching Galak centaur and monitors the suspicious machinations of the Grimtotem tribe. Perched upon the soaring rock spires of Thousand Needles, Freewind Post relies on sharp eyes and steady leadership to survive. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the day-to-day security of this precarious settlement. With hostile forces gathering on the canyon floor below and along neighboring ridges, Longhorn acts as the settlement's primary coordinator for scouting reports and defensive military efforts.

Clockwerk Run. The Clockwerk Run is the main entrance corridor leading into the heart of fallen Gnomeregan. Stretching between the Train Depot and the Hall of Gears, this damaged hallway is heavily contaminated by toxic fallout and overrun with irradiated troggs. Serving as the primary gateway into Gnomeregan from the outer train depot, the Clockwerk Run was once a bustling conduit of gnomish logistics and transit. When High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the venting of radioactive waste to stem the trogg invasion, the corridor became a lethal trap. The blast and subsequent fighting caused portions of the hallway to collapse onto itself. Today, the passage is choked with toxic fumes and prowling irradiated troggs, making it the perilous frontline that any expedition must fight through to reach the upper Hall of Gears.

Cloth Request. At the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, Rema Schneider receives Harlan Bagley's request for fresh cloth and knitted goods. His shelves are emptying quickly. Harlan Bagley asks Rema Schneider for a fresh supply of knitted garments and cloth. Bagley notes a sudden and unsettling surge in trade: citizens and travelers are buying armor and sturdy clothing as if bracing for a brutal season. The rush leaves Rema puzzled and wary. The House of Nobles has announced no open war, so Rema wonders why city folk are quietly armoring themselves and whether the crown's leaders are hiding unrest.

text.enUS: Cloth and Leather Armor. In Goldshire, Cloth and Leather Armor sends a trusted traveler east for gear. Marshal Dughan issues an armor marker redeemable with Sara Timberlain at Eastvale Logging Camp. The trip carries recruits beyond Guard Thomas's bridge to obtain armor for the realm's defense. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern river crossing, where murlocs and gnolls threaten the border. After you carry his report to Goldshire, Marshal Dughan recognizes your service with an official Stormwind Armor Marker. Goldshire's garrison has meager stores, so Dughan gives you a marker instead of drawing equipment from them. The marker is a military voucher that records your service to the crown.

Cloven Hoof. The Cloven Hoof is a mysterious relic guarded deep within Thousand Needles by the Galak centaur tribe. Preserved inside an ancient sacred flame at Splithoof Hold, it emanates an uncharacteristic supernatural energy that tauren scholars are keen to understand. Held within an ancient brazier at the deepest recess of Splithoof Hold, the Cloven Hoof is one of the most treasured relics of the Galak centaur. The artifact is continually enveloped in a magical flame, requiring blessed water to briefly quench the blaze so it can be handled. Centaur society is notoriously brutal and splintered into violent clans, but their reverence for the brazier suggests ritual significance tied directly to their origins. Tauren observers like Rau Cliffrunner at Freewind Post believe the strange aura radiating from the hoof could reveal critical insight into the race that has plagued Kalimdor's plains for generations.

Cold Hearth Manor. Cold Hearth Manor is a blighted farmstead located just west of Brill along the main road of Tirisfal Glades. Once a bustling, hospitable estate known for bountiful crops, the outbreak of the Plague of Undeath wiped out its residents, leaving the surrounding fields choked with mindless Scourge. Today, the Forsaken have secured the main farmhouse as an outpost and waystation for travelers. Before the Third War, this homestead bore a reputation for warmth and hospitality, supporting rich harvests in the heart of Lordaeron. When the Plague swept through the kingdom, the entire family and their laborers succumbed, rising again as husks bound to the Scourge. While feral undead still stumble through the ruined fields, Forsaken forces managed to push the mindless dead out of the main farmhouse, reclaiming the structure to serve as a trading post and foothold along the road toward the eastern glades.

Coldridge Pass. Coldridge Pass is a rugged, snowbound tunnel cutting through the southern mountain ridge of Dun Morogh. It serves as the sole overland route connecting the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley to the rest of the kingdom, emerging near the bustling town of Kharanos. Because hostile troggs have overrun the passage, any traveler attempting the journey must either fight their way through or make a desperate dash for the other side. For young dwarven recruits and gnome novices taking their first steps beyond Coldridge Valley, Coldridge Pass is a harsh rite of passage. Chiseled straight through the rock, this tunnel forms the primary link sending newly trained adventurers eastward toward the frontier hub of Kharanos. What was once a secure mountain corridor has become a perilous choke point, infested with aggressive troggs that have pushed up from dark sub-terrains to menace any soul trying to travel between the sheltered valley and the wider reaches of Dun Morogh.

text.enUS: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery is a simple courier task entrusted to recruits by Sten Stoutarm at Anvilmar. With mountain passes often choked with snow and troggs pressing nearby, carrying fresh correspondence out to the camps along the frozen lake keeps the valley's isolated defenders connected. Life in Coldridge Valley is secluded even in the calmest of seasons. When winter couriers successfully navigate the mountain pass with mail from the rest of Dun Morogh, the missives pile up quickly at Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm, busy managing local supply concerns and security, relies on wandering recruits to carry these bundles down the western road rather than letting vital tidings languish in the hall.

text.enUS: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. This errand completes a courier run across the snowy drifts of Coldridge Valley. Passing the dispatch from mountaineer Talin Keeneye down the southeastern road ensures that Grelin Whitebeard stays connected to the dwarven capital. Even in an isolated basin like Coldridge Valley, news and formal correspondence must travel. While Anvilmar serves as the administrative heart of the valley, field scouts and sentries stationed along the trails rely on foot couriers to relay dispatches between the high passes and Ironforge.

Coleman Farthing. Coleman Farthing is a bitter Forsaken survivor residing in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. In life, he worked for the wealthy Agamand dynasty at their extensive flour mills in northern Tirisfal. Convinced to stay and defend the estate against the Scourge, he died alongside his fellow laborers, and now dedicates his undeath to exacting vengeance on his former masters. Before the Third War, Coleman Farthing earned an honest living as a laborer at the Agamand Mills, the largest milling and agricultural operation in Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge poured across Lordaeron, the aristocratic Agamand family refused to flee their valuable lands. Instead, they urged their household and laborers to take up arms alongside them, promising they could hold the farmsteads against the undead horde. Coleman and his fellow workers stayed, believing their masters—a decision that cost every last one of them their lives.

Collecting Kelp. In Goldshire, Maybell Maclure seeks a way to visit Tommy Joe Stonefield unseen. William Pestle needs rare crystal kelp to brew an invisibility liquor for her. The feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families keeps Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield from meeting openly. Maybell wants to see her beloved without provoking an armed clash between their kin, so she seeks a way to cross the valley unseen. William Pestle, an herbalist and apothecary at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, plans to brew an invisibility liquor. The rare ingredients he needs are not in the inn's cupboards.

name.frFR: À la recherche de cartes du syndicat des mineurs

text.enUS: Collecting Memories. Collecting Memories is a solemn task entrusted by the dwarven miner Wilder Thistlenettle in Stormwind City. He asks adventurers braving the ruined mines beneath Moonbrook to recover the Miners' Union Cards of his fallen coworkers. Bringing these tokens back offers grieving families in the capital closure following a catastrophic cave-in. Before Moonbrook fell completely into lawlessness and the shadow of the Defias Brotherhood, the mines of Westfall were an active source of livelihood for many working-class families. Wilder Thistlenettle survived a devastating cave-in that buried a wing of the labyrinthine tunnels, but many of his friends and coworkers were not so fortunate. Cut off from rescue, those workers perished deep underground, leaving behind mourning kin in Stormwind who never received true confirmation or closure regarding their loved ones' fates.

Collin Mauren. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies practical magic and crafts useful spells from natural reagents. He also makes arcane scrolls for his friend Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome engineer and explorer. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies magic's practical uses. He crafts arcane formulas to solve specific problems, drawing on natural anomalies and raw components gathered across Azeroth. Their properties help him make functional scrolls and reagents for friends and travelers.

Colonel Kurzen. Colonel Conrad Kurzen was once a decorated and noble officer of the Stormwind Army, sent to lead an expedition into northern Stranglethorn Vale. After descending into sudden madness and tyranny, he turned his force into a rogue jungle militia operating out of an armed compound. Today, his former subordinates at the nearby Rebel Camp actively seek his death to end his reign of terror. Before his downfall, Colonel Conrad Kurzen was regarded in Stormwind as an exceptionally capable and noble officer. Trusted by the kingdom's leadership, he was granted command of an expeditionary unit dispatched south into the dense jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. However, deep within the humid wilds, Kurzen began to exhibit erratic behavior and extreme megalomania, declaring absolute sovereignty over the surrounding wilderness and abandoning his allegiance to Stormwind.

Colonel Kurzen. Lieutenant Doren calls upon you to deliver the final strike against Colonel Kurzen and his inner guard. You are sent into the Stockpile to eliminate the rogue commander and his remaining leaders to secure the Rebel Camp's survival. Lieutenant Doren and his band of defectors have reached the climax of their struggle against their former commander. Following the suppression of Kurzen's elite specialists, Doren recognizes that the rebel forces will never truly be safe while Kurzen retains control of his jungle redoubt. He directs you into the Stockpile cave, where Kurzen directs his forces alongside his subchiefs and elites.

Comar's Heart. Comar's Heart is a macabre ritual component carved from Comar Villard, a faithful human wanderer searching the marshes of the Wetlands for his lost wife. Forsaken warlocks in the Undercity seek out this relic of pure devotion to feed the summoning rites of a succubus. To bind a creature as capricious and predatory as a succubus, warlocks must bait the demon with true purity and devotion. Carendin Halgar's disciples in the Undercity identify Comar Villard as one of the few men possessing such unblemished fidelity. While his wife was lost amidst the turmoil sweeping the Eastern Kingdoms, Comar stubbornly wanders the sodden roads of the Wetlands, refusing to abandon his search. It is precisely this unwavering love that marks him for slaughter, turning his still-beating heart into the ideal lure for a demonic servant.

Coming of Age. Coming of Age marks the initial rite of passage for young Skyborne taking their first steps beyond Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Guided by Ailee Farheart, novices report to village leader Rorian the Dayseeker to receive an ancestral relic and formally pledge their aid to the shen'dorei. For every young Skyborne coming into adulthood, the journey begins in Thendal Village. Guided forward by Ailee Farheart, fledglings make their way just west to the greatfather tree where the village elder awaits. Passing into maturity among the shen'dorei is not merely a social milestone, but a ceremonial commitment to serve their community amid rising local troubles.

Coming to Terms. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this quest tasks newly risen paladins with reaching out to a fellow knight struggling to accept undeath. Fleeing into the hills in terror, the newly returned warrior faces the agonizing realization of becoming what she once fought against. Awakening from death into the ranks of the Forsaken is jarring for anyone, but for former paladins of the Silver Hand, the shock is visceral. Having dedicated their mortal lives to destroying the undead in service to the Holy Light, these individuals suddenly find their souls tethered back to decomposing flesh. While some adapt under the guidance of Aramis Hammerhand, others are overwhelmed by horror and confusion, fleeing into the Tirisfal wilderness rather than confronting their grim new existence.

Command Center. In Stormwind's Old Town, the Command Center trains recruits while most of the army serves abroad. Also called the Stormwind Barracks, it houses the city's military officers and a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia. In Old Town, Stormwind's Command Center is a garrison and training ground for the kingdom's soldiers. Its halls are quieter than usual, with much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad. Veteran instructors, including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen, train fresh warriors to strengthen the city's defenses.

Commander Mar'alith. Commander Mar'alith is the stalwart night elf military commander directing the Cenarion Circle's vanguard at Cenarion Hold in Silithus. Clad in heavy armor and wielding a grand glaive, he coordinates the martial resistance against the silithid swarms and Twilight's Hammer cultists. Beneath his resolute leadership lies a deep personal sorrow regarding the mysterious fate of his beloved wife, Natalia. Stationed at the heart of Cenarion Hold, Commander Mar'alith bears the tremendous responsibility of safeguarding the Circle's desert bastion. While the druids unravel the ancient ecological and cosmic anomalies of Silithus, Mar'alith handles the grim, practical necessities of war. He oversees tactical strikes against the bustling silithid hives of Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal, ensuring that the relentless insectoid incursions do not overwhelm the expedition's central foothold.

Commander Springvale. Commander Springvale was once a devoted paladin and a commander at Shadowfang Keep. Slain alongside his men during the feral worgen slaughter orchestrated by Archmage Arugal, his vengeful spirit remains behind to haunt the castle halls. Even in death, his ghost fiercely guards the keep against all who enter. Before the ruin of Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale stood as an honorable paladin dedicated to the Holy Light. Leading the garrison in Silverpine Forest, he oversaw the keep's security during the fraught days following the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge.

Commons. The Commons serves as the vibrant commercial heart of Ironforge, connecting the city entrance directly to its vast caverns. Teeming with merchants, travelers, and bankers, it is the busiest thoroughfare in the dwarven capital and the central marketplace for the entire Alliance. Located just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge, the Commons is the first district that greets travelers entering the mountain kingdom. Carved directly out of the stone, this bustling market street houses the primary Alliance Auction House, the Stonefire Tavern, and the city's central bank within the Vault of Ironforge. Broad avenues connect it seamlessly to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward, ensuring that nearly all foot traffic in the mountain passes through its bustling storefronts.

text.enUS: Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender asks warlocks to find Robes of Arcana for a garment meant to bear powerful enchantments. Menara Voidrender asks warlocks seeking greater power to bring her a set of Robes of Arcana. She wants a garment strong enough to hold dark magic. The strength of a magical relic depends on the skill, rarity, and effort put into its materials. Ordinary rags would fail under deep enchantments, so the robe must be finely made and ready to receive them.

name.frFR: Sous les drapeaux de la Horde

text.enUS: Conscript of the Horde. Along Durotar’s western road, Conscript of the Horde sends recruits toward the Barrens. Takrin Pathseeker watches beyond Razor Hill and gives them a letter for Kargal Battlescar, whose outpost guards the crossing. After proving your strength around Razor Hill, you are called west to serve the wider Horde. Takrin Pathseeker watches the road out of Durotar for his friend, veteran Kargal Battlescar. He gives capable travelers a recruitment letter to carry across the Southfury River. For a recruit, the letter marks a first formal assignment beyond the orcs’ new homeland.

Consecrated Letter. The Consecrated Letter is an introductory summons carried by initiates of the Holy Light arriving in Northshire Valley. It directs the bearer to report to their class trainer at Northshire Abbey to begin their training and embrace their role as a visible symbol of faith. The Consecrated Letter marks the formal beginning of an initiate's journey in Northshire Valley. Addressed to newly arrived wielders of the Holy Light, the document calls the bearer to seek out their trainer at Northshire Abbey to formalize their instruction and accept their responsibilities within the Kingdom of Stormwind.

Consecrated Rune. A Consecrated Rune is an inscribed sacred item passed to fledgling dwarven paladins training in Coldridge Valley. It serves as an introductory summons from Bromos Grummner, directing initiates to report to Anvilmar and begin their formal duties as Knights of the Silver Hand. Novice dwarven paladins proving themselves in Coldridge Valley are handed a Consecrated Rune once they have shown basic martial competence. Inscribed with sacred words and blessed by the Holy Light, the rune originates from Bromos Grummner, the paladin trainer residing inside Anvilmar. Dwarves hold immense respect for the traditions of the Holy Light introduced to them by their human allies. Reading the rune serves as both an official summons and a symbolic rite of passage, confirming the novice's place among the Knights of the Silver Hand.

Consecrated Rune. The Consecrated Rune is an introductory summons delivered to fledgling dwarven paladins in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm on behalf of Bromos Grummner, it marks an initiate's formal induction into the Knights of the Silver Hand. While novice adventurers clear out troggs and wolves around Coldridge Valley, the local leaders keep a close eye on those who display a gift for divine martial prowess. Sten Stoutarm delivers this inscribed rune to young paladins, instructing them to seek out Bromos Grummner inside the warmth of Anvilmar. It serves as both an invitation and an official notice that raw potential must now be tempered with discipline.

Console Key. At the Venture Company digsite in the Barrens, Tinkerer Sniggles holds the Console Key. It unlocks the main control terminal and lets the samophlange be removed once the apparatus is shut down. The Venture Company runs an industrial outpost in the northern Barrens. Its steam-driven machinery depends on a device called a samophlange. The console is locked against unauthorized hands, and only Tinkerer Sniggles, the chief technician on site, carries the Console Key. The key opens the terminal casing so the rig can be powered down.

Consult Master Gadrin. Apothecary Lydon found the venom from the broodguards less potent than the sample you first brought, which points to another kind of spider. Lydon sends you to Master Gadrin in Sen'jin Village, in Durotar, who may know more. Apothecary Lydon found the venom taken from the broodguards weaker than the sample you brought first, so it must come from a different spider. Lydon wants a fresh sample of the stronger kind. To learn where it comes from, ask a troll well acquainted with the Witherbark: Master Gadrin, in Sen'jin Village, in Durotar. With luck, Gadrin can name the source of that venom.

Consumed by Hatred. Mankrik turns his grief at the Crossroads into a campaign against the Bristleback quilboar. The orc was separated from his wife in a violent ambush, and now he calls on Horde travelers to kill the creatures and bring back their tusks. Mankrik carries the grief of a quilboar ambush that left him battered and his wife missing. At the Crossroads, he watches the arid horizon, still thirsting for the blood of the Bristlebacks despite the many he has killed himself. He calls on fellow Horde travelers to help him continue the fight.

Continue Your Training. This quest directs newly risen Forsaken paladins to leave Deathknell and travel to Brill for advanced instruction. Entrusted by Aramis Hammerhand, the journey introduces the fledgling holy warrior to the wider perils of Tirisfal Glades. It also serves as a stark warning about the deep suspicion that holy practitioners face among the undead. Once a newly awakened soul has mastered the rudiments of martial combat and channelled holy power within Deathknell's cloistered graveyard, Aramis Hammerhand sends them east into the broader expanse of Tirisfal Glades. Their destination is Brill, a bustling regional outpost serving as the administrative hub for central Tirisfal. There, Shari Stilwell oversees the advancement of those who dare walk the path of the paladin in undeath.

Continue to Stormwind. You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town. Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note in Sentinel Hill. The local gryphon master Thor offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom's trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and the river border of Elwynn Forest, then over Stormwind City's high white ramparts.

Continued Threat. Katar is pleased that your hatred of the fish men is growing alongside Katar's own, and sends you to hunt further fish men on the beach in the Swamp of Sorrows. Katar tells you to find more of the fish men along the beach, and to return once you have had enough of fighting. Marsh inkspewers, marsh flesheaters and marsh oracles are the ones wanted. Katar will take no pleasure until the sea and every one of her children is silenced, least of all the repulsive fish men.

name.esES: Manual de instrucciones de la consola de control
name.frFR: Manuel de la console de contrôle
name.ptBR: Manual de Operação do Console de Controle

text.enUS: Control Console Operating Manual. At the Venture Company site southwest of Sludge Fen, the Control Console Operating Manual guides workers through the machinery. It explains how to close the valves and disengage the samophlange. Southwest of Sludge Fen, the Venture Company runs a drilling and research site in the northern Barrens. Its machinery links gauges, pressurized valves, and mechanisms to a device called a samophlange. Without the right instructions, working the volatile controls can cause a dangerous failure or lock the system. The manual gives the valve sequence for disengaging the core apparatus without triggering an explosive failure.

Cookie. Cookie is an elite murloc serving as the ship's cook aboard the juggernaut hidden deep within the Deadmines. An unusual recruit among the Defias Brotherhood, he tends the crew's cauldrons beneath the watchful eye of Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. He is the only entirely optional boss encountered within the underground dry dock. Beneath the decks of the towering juggernaut in the Ironclad Cove, cooking duty falls neither to a human outrider nor a goblin engineer, but to a solitary murloc known simply as Cookie. How he came by the position is anyone's guess. Whatever doubts the rest of the crew might harbor about a murloc presiding over their rations, pirates are rarely in a position to be picky, and in the underworld of Moonbrook, a meal is a meal.

Coolant Heads Prevail. Lotwil Veriatus wants a vial of Frost Oil to strengthen the shackles meant to hold a summoned friend in check. Bro'kin, a goblin friend of Lotwil's in Alterac, can teach you to make it. Lotwil Veriatus swears nothing keeps an engine or gears from overheating like Frost Oil, and that its worth as a lubricant is without equal. It also helps magical items hold on to their enchantments. A vial would raise the magical capacity of Lotwil's shackles, making them strong enough to stop the summoned friend from killing everyone.

Corin's Crossing. Corin's Crossing is a ruined human settlement situated at a major crossroads in south-central Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving waystation between Stratholme, Tyr's Hand, Darrowshire, and Andorhal, the devastated town is now utterly overrun by the Scourge. Its crumbling town hall and forge harbor lingering horrors, including invisible spectral watchers. Before the Third War, Corin's Crossing served as a central junction for travel across eastern Lordaeron. Positioned between the shimmering waters of Lake Mereldar and what has now become the blighted chasm of the Infectis Scar, its thoroughfares once bore merchants, couriers, and pilgrims traveling between the great bastion of Stratholme and the southern strongholds. When the plague swept through the province, the settlement stood directly in the path of destruction, collapsing swiftly beneath the sheer weight of the undead vanguard.

Corithras Moonrage. Corithras Moonrage is a night elf scholar and quest giver stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He guides newly arrived adventurers in understanding the nature of the great World Tree and tasks them with maintaining its sacred moonwells. Through his lessons, he reveals both the spiritual importance of Teldrassil and the growing burdens carried by the kaldorei. Residing in the shaded settlement of Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage serves as an instructor to travelers leaving the sheltered bounds of Shadowglen. As young kaldorei venture into the wider boughs of Teldrassil, Corithras ensures they understand the history of their new home. He teaches that survival in this changing era requires vigilance and reverence for the natural order.

Corrahn's Dagger. Corrahn's Dagger is the second ridge among the four mountainous fingers towering over northern Hillsbrad Foothills. This high ground serves as a hideout for rogue Syndicate operatives. Rising steeply in northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Corrahn's Dagger is the second of the four rocky projections known locally as the fingers of Hillsbrad. The ridge is overrun by cutthroats belonging to the Syndicate, who use the elevated perch to overlook the valley below.

Corroded Shrapnel. Corroded Shrapnel consists of jagged metal fragments lodged deep within the corrupted treants of the Stonetalon Mountains. Recovered from fallen protectors like Charred and Blackened Ancients, this debris provides physical evidence of the foul weaponry used by the Venture Company during their retreat. When the Venture Company was driven back from the groves of Stonetalon, the goblins unleashed brutal, reckless munitions to cover their escape. Shrapnel from these explosive weapons tore into the valley's defending treants, embedding jagged metal deep within their bark and core. Rather than healing, the ancient guardians slowly fell to corruption, their wood blackening and their fury turning upon anyone who stepped into the vale. The rusted, tainted fragments recovered from these wounded protectors are sought by Kaela Shadowspear so the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle can analyze the exact mechanisms of the corruption.

Corrupt Manifestation's Bracers. Tainted bracers lie on the coast of Silverpine Forest, remnants of a corrupted water elemental. Shaman initiates recover them during the Call of Water and cast them into the Brazier of Everfount with pure water to cleanse the shrine and summon a pure water spirit. The Scourge's plague reached the spirits of Lordaeron. Along Silverpine Forest's misty coast, west of the Sepulcher, a sacred water shrine fell to corruption. Its water manifestation became an aggressive shade. Shaman initiates must defeat it and recover its bracers. At the Brazier of Everfount, they cast the bindings into the flame with pure water, lifting the corruption and calling forth an unblemished water spirit.

Corrupted Brain Stem. Corrupted Brain Stems are biological specimens harvested from the twisted naga and satyrs inhabiting Blackfathom Deeps and the Ashenvale coastline. Gershala Nightwhisper of Auberdine seeks them to study the physical deformities wrought by reckless magical corruption. By examining these brains, night elf scholars hope to understand and potentially prevent a similar fate from befalling the blood elves. The satyrs and naga of Kalimdor stand as living testaments to the warping power of forbidden magic and demonic pacts. Long ago, reckless kaldorei highborne were irrevocably transformed into serpent-like aquatic beasts and demonic horned fiends. The brain stems harvested from these creatures exhibit heavy physical mutation, providing direct anatomical proof of how deep corruptive energies burrow into the nervous systems of once-elven beings.

Corrupted Kor Gem. Around Blackfathom Deeps, naga rites leave Kor gems corrupted. Spellcasters prize the stones for holding arcane force, but this taint must be cleansed before a gem can be used in righteous smithing. Kor gems can capture and hold great stores of magic, making them prized by sorcerers and enchanted smiths. Near the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, naga oracles and tide priestesses claim the stones for their shadowy rites. Their foul enchantments warp each gem with corruption from the sea. The taint does not drain the stone's latent power, so those who need a potent focus still seek gems among the naga.

Cortello's Riddle. A hidden parchment found aboard the Bloodsail Buccaneer vessels along the Wild Shore presents Cortello's cryptic verse. Deciphering the poem points travelers toward a clue waiting beneath an ornate bridge. Scattered notes aboard the Bloodsail fleet anchored off the southern coast of Stranglethorn Vale carry a rhyme. Cortello's verse describes a finely worked, much-used bridge that lies east of Deadwind and south of Redridge. Anyone seeking to unravel the mystery must follow these poetic directions out of the jungle and into the marshes to find what waits underneath.

Cortello's Riddle. Following the trail begun with a waterlogged parchment found in the Swamp of Sorrows, a second cryptic verse urges travelers to a far-off land in Kalimdor. Deciphering the lines points treasure hunters toward a cave in the southwest of Dustwallow Marsh. The second verse left by Cortello directs searchers toward the far-off land of Kalimdor. The rhyme describes a perilous and gloomy territory situated east of the Barrens: the sodden, treacherous wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh.

Cortello's Riddle. A cryptic musty scroll provides the final set of verse left behind by Cortello. The rhyming instructions direct treasure hunters far north to the troubled continent of Lordaeron, where the trail reaches its conclusion along the coastal waterfalls of the Hinterlands. Following the earlier scrolls, this weathered text points away from the southern tropics toward the embattled lands of Lordaeron. The riddle bids searchers to seek out the great turmoil in the north, promising that the long chase ends by braving that unrest and pursuing the coastline.

Costly Menace. Darren Malvew of Southshore hates losing the town's beautiful horses. Undead, the Syndicate gang and assorted scoundrels have cost plenty, but Darren says nothing threatens them more than the mountain lions that keep coming down from the hills of Alterac. Darren Malvew of Southshore cannot stand losing the beautiful horses there. Quite a few have been lost to undead creeps, the Syndicate gang and the scoundrels poking about the region. By Darren's own word, though, no menace to the horses is bigger than the mountain lions up in Alterac, forever coming down from the hills.

name.esES: Garras de puma de las estepas

text.enUS: Cougar Claws. Cougar Claws are harvested from flatland cougars that roam the central plains of Mulgore. They serve as a vital material in tauren ritual craft, embodying the untamed balance and natural ferocity of the wild predators. The flatland cougar is one of the apex hunters of Mulgore's sprawling grasslands, stalking prey with instinctual grace. In tauren tradition, taking the claws of such a predator is not an act of casual slaughter or trophy hunting, but a way to harness the natural spirit of the beast. When goblin operations begin defiling the ancestral waters of the plains, Mull Thunderhorn calls upon young hunters to gather these claws alongside those of prairie stalkers. The tauren believe that the pure, uncorrupted predatory instincts of native beasts can be woven into a ritual totem capable of scouring unnatural toxins and foul sorcery from the poisoned Thunderhorn Water Well.

Councilman Millstipe. Councilman Millstipe is a member of Darkshire's governing council, residing within the town hall of Duskwood. Deeply resentful of royal neglect and judicial meddling from the capital, he actively seeks retribution against criminals who endanger the darkened region. While Darkshire struggles under the shadow of the undead and ferocious beast attacks, its local council fights an uphill battle against the bureaucracy of Stormwind City. Councilman Millstipe represents the town's growing bitterness toward the crown. When the notorious grave robber Dextren Ward was caught selling freshly dug corpses to the necromancer Morbent Fel, Darkshire's leaders sentenced him to death. Instead, Stormwind's House of Nobles intervened, commuting Ward's execution and locking him safely away inside the Stormwind Stockade.

Count Remington Ridgewell. In Stormwind Keep, Count Remington Ridgewell tends a collection fit for a noble’s pride. A wealthy human in the House of Nobles, he gathers rare artifacts, heirlooms, and fine art. Count Remington Ridgewell favors antiquities over military campaigns or local uprisings. His family’s personal museum holds jewelry and artifacts, and he spends his wealth gathering relics from fallen civilizations and houses across Azeroth. To fill his gallery, he finances adventurers and sends field agents such as Mayara Brightwing to retrieve rare objects from dangerous ruins, from Alterac’s mountain redoubts to the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes.

Counterattack!. At Regthar Deathgate’s outpost west of the Crossroads, Kolkar warriors strike back after their leaders fall. They have crossed from Desolace, and Warlord Krom'zar leads their charge. The Kolkar have suffered a deep humiliation in the Barrens. Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark are dead, leaving the remaining centaur shattered and without direction. Word of their defeat travels west across the mountains to their ancestral homeland in Desolace. There, a fresh force of hardened Kolkar warriors rallies instead of scattering into the scrubland. Burning for blood and retribution, they cross into the Barrens and march against the young Horde encampments.

Courser Eye. Courser Eyes are biological reagents harvested from the antlered coursers roaming the highlands of Stonetalon Mountains. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin seeks a large quantity of them to prepare a concoction he mockingly refers to as forest magic.

Covert Ops - Alpha. Covert Ops - Alpha is an Alliance infiltration mission directed by the gnome tinker Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. While operating out of the peaks, operatives are tasked with penetrating the Venture Company's lumber mill in Windshear Crag to recover proprietary engineering schematics. Securing these blueprints allows the Alliance to decipher the mechanical vulnerabilities of goblin machinery while co-opting their logging technology. Operating from Windshear Crag, Gaxim Rustfizzle conducts a persistent covert campaign to disrupt the aggressive logging operations of the Venture Company. While goblin deforesters fell the primeval timber south of Cragpool Lake, Gaxim recognizes that wanton destruction alone cannot halt the enterprise. Instead of merely detonating industrial hardware, Plan Alpha prioritizes intelligence gathering, requiring agents to slip past goblin loggers and overseers to seize their core technical schematics directly from the lumber mill.

Covert Ops - Beta. Covert Ops - Beta is an Alliance mission organized by the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Building upon previous sabotage against the encroaching Venture Company, this operation sends an agent deep into Windshear Mine to trigger explosive diversions and extract vital operational letters. The retrieved intelligence serves both gnome curiosity and the territorial defense of the regional night elf Sentinels. Following initial strikes against the Venture Company's clear-cutting operations across Windshear Crag, Gaxim Rustfizzle devises a follow-up operation aimed directly at their logistical heart. Plan Beta follows the same fundamental logic as its predecessor: creating an explosive, chaotic diversion to scatter the goblin operators and mercenaries while an operative slips through the confusion to search the mines for written correspondence.

Covert Ops Pack. The Covert Ops Pack is a kit of specialized demolitions gear and operational schematics assembled for Alliance espionage in the Stonetalon Mountains. Designed to dismantle the Venture Company's rapacious presence in Windshear Crag, the satchel equips agents to trigger coordinated sabotage while securing high-value technical intelligence. Issued for clandestine strikes deep within Venture Company territory, the Covert Ops Pack pairs brute destructive power with tactical precision. Inside are color-coded NG-5 explosives matched to remote triggers, alongside thorough instructions designated Plan Alpha and Plan Beta. The strategy relies on triggering high-yield distractions at key infrastructure nodes—namely the Cragpool Lake lumber mill and the eastern mine. While goblins scramble to extinguish blazes and assess mechanical failures, an infiltrator slips past the chaos to pilfer critical documents and schematics.

Coyote Thieves. In the outpost of Kargath, Neeka Bloodscar wants you to hunt the crag coyotes of the Badlands, tough beasts that have dared to sneak into Kargath and steal its food. Thirty jawbones are what Neeka asks for. Neeka Bloodscar asks whether you have spent many days in the Badlands, felt its heat and met the beasts of its dusty plains. Crag coyotes are a tough breed, and they have crept into Kargath to steal from the outpost's food. Neeka wants them hunted and their jawbones brought back. Bring enough, and Neeka may believe you know the Badlands.

Crab Season. Crab Season is an urgent foraging task on Zephras centered on harvesting rare Windsong crawlers during their brief annual window. Because recent cultist activity has made the shores of Windsong Lake perilous, adventurers are called upon to brave both hostile interlopers and aggressive crustaceans. On the shores of Windsong Lake across Zephras, a brief seasonal harvesting window opens for only a few weeks each year. The native Windsong crawlers emerge in numbers along the freshwater banks and tributary rivers, offering a rare harvest of meat to anyone bold enough to gather them before the annual opportunity slips away.

Cracking Maury's Foot. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley has retrieved the foot of his late debtor Maury, only to find that what he is owed is locked inside it. To claim what is owed, he directs travelers to the Mosh'Ogg ogre mound in Stranglethorn Vale to search for the missing key. Following the retrieval of Maury's foot in Voodoo Dues, "Sea Wolf" MacKinley faces an unexpected complication in Booty Bay. The late debtor put a lock on his foot, and the valuables he owes are sealed inside.

Craftsmen's Terrace. Craftsmen's Terrace gathers Darnassus's trades along the city's northern edge. Its workshops, trainers, inn, and Argent Dawn embassy draw artisans and visitors alike. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans work along the northern edge of Darnassus. Their shops bring together many of the trades that keep the city running, using night elven methods for practical crafts. You can also find an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors here. Bridges lead west to the Cenarion Enclave and south to the Warrior's Terrace.

Crag of the Everliving. The Crag of the Everliving is a verdant cavern chamber nestled deep within the Wailing Caverns. Dominated by lush, corrupted flora and predatory plant creatures, it serves as the domain of the Fanglord Lord Pythas. Its towering upper reaches shelter the ancient entity after whom the crag is named. While much of the Wailing Caverns is carved of damp subterranean stone, the Crag of the Everliving bursts with unruly, twisted vegetation fueled by the Nightmare corrupting Naralex's slumber. Towering mossy platforms and winding paths are choked with Deviate Shamblers—living plant hulks prowling the undergrowth. Lord Pythas, one of Naralex's fallen disciples, watches over the crag's central reaches, having traded his noble druidic vows for the venomous rites of the Druids of the Fang.

Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company. Nestled within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company. An enormous wooden structure spans above the water, serving as the vantage point from which Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle oversees operations across the mountain valley. Venture Company workers occupy the platforms overhead.

text.enUS: Crane Operator Bigglefuzz. Crane Operator Bigglefuzz is a goblin dockhand working the heavy machinery at the port of Ratchet. After an overloaded crane mishap scattered cargo across the docks, he finds himself desperate to recover a valuable stolen bottle before his superiors notice. Like many goblin dockworkers, Crane Operator Bigglefuzz prioritized efficiency and haste over basic safety margins. While attempting to hoist an excessively heavy haul from a merchant vessel, his crane buckled, sending crates crashing down across the Ratchet wharves. In the ensuing chaos, opportunistic scoundrels swept in, leaving Bigglefuzz to scramble to clean up the mess and salvage the most precious goods before Gazlowe or the local port masters dock his pay.

Crate With Holes. A portable transport container provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Pierced with air vents, it safely houses a trained Snufflenose Gopher used to track down subterranean culinary delicacies within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul. To acquire rare Blueleaf Tubers from the thorny depths of Razorfen Kraul, goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix relies on trained Snufflenose Gophers rather than blind digging. Because gophers cannot simply follow an adventurer across the dusty trails of the Barrens on foot, Mebok packs each critter into a well-ventilated wooden crate. Once brought into the humid, root-choked corridors of the quilboar lair, the crate is unlatched, allowing the beast within to follow its keen sense of smell toward buried tubers.

Crate of Crash Helmets. A heavy supply shipment of dwarven Siege Engine headgear destined for the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. The sturdy helmets are urgently required by the Brassbolts brothers to protect test drivers from concussions caused by their experimental rocket cars. Out across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, gnome engineers test the absolute limits of mechanical propulsion. Unfortunately for the test pilots, the experimental rocket cars designed by the Brassbolts brothers move far faster than their steering can reliably handle. With drivers routinely suffering violent crashes and head trauma, ordinary leather caps no longer suffice. To prevent their roster of willing daredevils from vanishing entirely, heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets are packed and dispatched across the sea to keep drivers conscious—and alive.

Crate of Horseshoes. In Elwynn, fifty iron horseshoes are bound for Lakeshire. Smith Argus forged fifty fresh horseshoes in Goldshire, then packed the crate and hammered it shut. Verner Osgood commissioned them for Lakeshire, where constant pressure from gnolls and orcs leaves local craftsmen reliant on Elwynn for essential metal goods. The delivery answers Verner's desperate need for equipment, and Argus includes a stern bill of sale so the Redridge craftsman knows frontier survival comes at a steep price.
