name.itIT: I pericoli delle Furie del Vento

text.enUS: Dangers of the Windfury. Dangers of the Windfury is a rite of martial readiness offered by Ruul Eagletalon in Bloodhoof Village. Young tauren and Horde adventurers are tasked with battling the savage Windfury harpies nesting in the southeastern cliffs of Mulgore. Hunting these feral predators serves as an essential test of skill and survival before journeying beyond the tribal homeland. In Bloodhoof Village, the veteran warrior Ruul Eagletalon observes all travelers who pass through the heart of Mulgore. For those coming of age or seeking to prove themselves ready for wider adventures, Ruul demands tangible proof of their combat instincts. Survival beyond the sheltered valleys of Mulgore requires poise against aggressive, cunning foes, and Ruul uses the land's fiercest native predators to measure a youth's mettle.

Daphne Stilwell. On Westfall's cliffs, Daphne Stilwell keeps an orchard above the Longshore. She and her husband Jordan fled the north and now aid the Church of the Holy Light while guarding their home from nearby outlaws. West of Moonbrook and the Deadmines exit, Daphne Stilwell tends a homestead and apple orchard on the bluffs. From the Longshore below or gryphon routes south to Stranglethorn Vale above, the farm looks quiet. But life there is not safe. Bandits and scavengers roam nearby, while Daphne works among the trees and watches over her isolated land.

Darcy. Darcy is a waitress serving drinks and warm meals at the Lakeshire Inn. Amid the constant threats looming over Redridge, she keeps her spirits up by looking after local defenders—particularly Guard Parker. Behind the busy counter of the Lakeshire Inn, Darcy works day and night to keep the town's weary militia fed and watered. Lakeshire sits under constant pressure from gnolls and Blackrock orcs, making the tavern one of the few places of warmth left in the settlement. Darcy takes a personal interest in the guards posted around town, frequently recruiting traveling adventurers to run hot meals and friendly errands out to those stationed along the borders.

Dark Ceremony. After the Gordunni Scroll, Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache reads it as plans for a dark ceremony led by the Gordunni mage-lords. Rok Orhan wants you to take an orb from one of those mage-lords, to learn more about the ceremony and the Gordunni's magic. Rok Orhan has looked over the Gordunni Scroll you brought and reads it as the plans for a dark ceremony. As far as Rok can tell, the Gordunni mage-lords are the ones who conduct it. A mage-lord must be found, and an orb taken from him. A mage's orb holds great power, and it should reveal more about the ceremony and the magic the Gordunni wield.

Dark Cleric Beryl. Dark Cleric Beryl is a Forsaken priest trainer stationed in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. He guides newly awakened undead priests as they learn to wield shadow magic and adapt to their new, unholy existence under the Dark Lady. Residing on the upper floor of the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl serves the Forsaken by mentoring nascent priests. Beryl teaches that a Forsaken priest's power comes from darkness and shadow, yet one must also know the light before mastering the dark. He assists newly risen practitioners as they turn their focus toward shadow and the dark arts, guiding them through early trials like crafting their Garments of Darkness and proving their dedication to the new path.

Dark Council. Magistrate Henry Maleb in Southshore has learned that the letter you brought came from a being who goes by Nagaz and belongs to the Argus Wake. If the Argus Wake is allied with the Syndicate, Maleb says, they must be a threat. You are sent to hunt down Nagaz and the Argus Shadow Mages in the Uplands. After Further Mysteries, Maleb tells you the letter came from a being who goes by Nagaz and belongs to the Argus Wake. Maleb does not know what the Argus Wake is, but an alliance with the Syndicate would make them a threat. Maleb wants Nagaz and the Argus Shadow Mages named in the letter found and killed, and asks for the head of Nagaz. You are to search the Uplands, north of Strahnbrad, where the Syndicate is strongest. Maleb hopes the Argus Wake's envoys are there.

Dark Heart. Talo Thornhoof at Camp Mojache wants the dark heart of Edana Hatetalon, who is queen of the harpies of Northspring, living in ruins to the west. Talo calls her pure evil. Edana Hatetalon is the harpies' queen, ruling the Northspring brood in ruins lying west. Talo calls her pure evil, with no feeling in her except hatred for everyone, and has heard her heart is made of crystal. Talo wants you to face her and bring back her dark heart, because the hatred she spreads must be stopped.

Dark Iron Ambassador. The Dark Iron Ambassador is an emissary of the Dark Iron clan found deep within Gnomeregan. His presence raises questions about the clan's interest in the ruined gnome capital. The Dark Iron Ambassador is found among the dangers of irradiated Gnomeregan. He represents the Dark Iron clan, but the purpose of his mission is not explained.

Dark Iron clan. The Dark Iron clan is an ancient, ash-skinned dwarven faction ruling from the volcanic depths of Blackrock Mountain. Cast out of Ironforge during the War of the Three Hammers, they accidentally summoned Ragnaros the Firelord, who enslaved their empire. Today, under Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, they wage shadow wars against both the Alliance and the Horde while serving their fiery elemental master. Long ago, three dwarven factions lived together in Ironforge under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died, civil war erupted. The Bronzebeards defeated both rival factions, casting out the Wildhammers and Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan's Dark Irons. Vowing vengeance, Thaurissan established a settlement in the Redridge Mountains while his sorceress wife, Modgud, led an army against Grim Batol. When both assaults failed and the united Bronzebeard and Wildhammer armies marched on his stronghold, Thaurissan attempted to unleash an apocalyptic subterranean entity to save himself. His ritual breached the core of the world and freed Ragnaros the Firelord.

Dark Iron dwarf. Dark Iron dwarves are a distinct dwarven sub-race distinguished by their ashen skin, blazing red eyes, and innate affinity for fire. Banished from Ironforge following the civil War of the Three Hammers, they dwell deep within Blackrock Mountain where their society has fallen under the tyrannical rule of the Firelord, Ragnaros. Unlike their Bronzebeard and Wildhammer cousins, Dark Iron dwarves possess dark gray or soot-black skin and eyes that burn like glowing embers. Their history fractured during the War of the Three Hammers, when their Sorcerer-thane Thaurissan sought to conquer Ironforge. Defeated and driven south into the Redridge Mountains, Thaurissan attempted to summon dark powers to avenge his losses, inadvertently releasing Ragnaros the Firelord from the Elemental Plane. The catastrophic summoning shattered the surrounding peaks into the volcanic waste of Blackrock Mountain and bound the Dark Iron race into fiery servitude.

Dark Portal. The Dark Portal is a monumental stone gateway standing at the southern rim of the Blasted Lands. First torn open through the combined sorcery of Medivh and Gul'dan, it served as the fateful conduit that brought the Old Horde into Azeroth, initiating the First War. Before its opening, this region was part of the Black Morass, a sodden wetland that stretched across the south. That changed when Medivh, possessed by Sargeras, joined his Tirisfal magics with the fel sorcery of Gul'dan on Draenor. The ritual drained untold lives and tore the fabric of reality apart. The Old Horde raised massive stone architecture to anchor the rift, marching armies through its threshold to shatter the Kingdom of Stormwind in the First War. The portal's fel emanations fundamentally corrupted the surrounding terrain, reducing lush marshes to the red, petrified wastes seen today.

Dark Riders. The Dark Riders are a band of mysterious, hooded horsemen who terrorize Duskwood. Merciless hunters of magical relics, they strike from hiding and leave only slaughter in their wake. Little is known of the Dark Riders' origins. Witnesses describe hooded horsemen who speak in voices both harsh and shrill, and one was seen using a small gem to take orders from a master it called only its 'Lord'. They hunt objects of magical power across the kingdom, cutting down anyone who stands between them and their prize.

Dark Storms. In Durotar, Burning Blade cultists corrupt the land from Thunder Ridge. Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill has learned that the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm leads them, and asks you to end his threat. Orgnil Soulscar has learned that dark magic has taken hold in Thunder Ridge, northwest of Razor Hill. Burning Blade cultists prowl the ravine while young Horde defenders patrol Durotar’s borders. Their presence brings ruin to the wildlife and land.

Dark Vessels. Primal Torntusk in Revantusk Village says the Vilebranch fight with a supernatural ferocity, the work of Vile Priestess Hexx's foul weavings of magic. Throughout Jintha'alor lie dark vessels of tainted blood, radiating a foul magic that belongs to the faceless blood God. Torntusk asks you to steal them and bring them back, so the taint can be removed. Wherever you walk in Jintha'alor, you will find vessels of tainted blood. They radiate the dark power of the faceless blood God, which strengthens the Vilebranch and drives them to madness. Torntusk believes that taking the vessels away and removing their taint will loosen the blood God's grip on them.

Darkcloud Pinnacle. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified tauren settlement perched atop several interconnected mesas east of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. Held by the aggressive Grimtotem clan, the aerial stronghold serves as a base of operations for regional disruption and shady dealings. Spanning three main mesas joined by rope bridges, Darkcloud Pinnacle commands the canyon basin below. The heights are accessible only by a steep natural slope leading from the canyon floor across wooden bridges, or via a high crossing near Razorfen Downs. From these windswept rocks, the Grimtotem watch the valley, safe from casual assault and isolated from the broader tauren tribes.

Darkcore the Elder. Darkcore the Elder is a seasonal quest encountered during the Lunar Festival within the Undercity. By seeking out Elder Darkcore, travelers pay homage to the ancient spirits honored across Azeroth and receive a Coin of Ancestry in return. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient night elven and earthen ancestors appear throughout the continents to share their wisdom and blessings. Elder Darkcore resides in the shadowed halls of the Undercity, bearing witness to the modern realm while offering remembrance to those who seek out the roots of the world.

Darkened Bank. The Darkened Bank is the northern shoreline of Duskwood, bordering the river that separates the shadowed woods from Elwynn Forest. Stretching from the far west all the way east toward the Redridge Mountains, it marks the boundary between the relative safety of the north and the dark terrors of the forest. Running along the southern bank of the river opposite Elwynn Forest, the Darkened Bank forms the northern edge of Duskwood. It extends from the western riverbends east toward the stone span leading to the Redridge Mountains. While visually gloomy under the pervasive canopy of Duskwood's curse, this shoreline is often the first foothold for travelers venturing south from Elwynn. Near its far western tip sits a makeshift campsite where displaced refugees, including Sven Yorgen and Lars, have taken shelter just barely outside the grasp of the deep woods.

Darkhorn the Elder. At the Lunar Festival, Darkhorn the Elder receives travelers in Orgrimmar. Honored among the ancestors, she embodies age, survival, and ancestral pride. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestors appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within Orgrimmar’s fortified ramparts, watching the young warrior city. You can approach her to honor those who walked the earth generations ago, whether you fight for the Horde or brave the gates as an Alliance traveler.

Darkhound Blood. Darkhound Blood is a foul bodily fluid harvested from the tainted canine beasts roaming the fields and forests of Tirisfal Glades. Gathered at the behest of the Royal Apothecary Society, it serves as an early reagent in their dark experiments to engineer a lethal new plague. Under the command of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Royal Apothecary Society strives to develop a virulent contagion capable of wiping out Arthas and his Scourge. Stationed in Brill, Apothecary Johaan theorizes that local beasts, corrupted by dark energies and resilient to the surrounding decay, possess unusual biological properties. By distilling the blood of wild darkhounds, Johaan aims to uncover biological compounds that can resist or propagate virulent necrotic strains.

Darkmaster Gandling. Darkmaster Gandling is the mortal headmaster of Scholomance, overseeing the instruction and training of necromancers for the Cult of the Damned. Operating from the depths of the ruined Keep of Caer Darrow, he serves the Scourge by orchestrating gruesome magical experiments upon the living and dead alike. Within the dark halls beneath Caer Darrow, Darkmaster Gandling governs Scholomance, the premier academy for the Scourge's aspiring necromancers. A living human serving the Cult of the Damned, Gandling worked alongside the lich Ras Frostwhisper to orchestrate atrocities against countless innocent captives taken from the surrounding lands. Students who enter his classrooms are instructed in plague brewing, reanimation, and flesh sculpting.

Darkmist Cavern. Darkmist Cavern is an abandoned mine tucked into northwestern Dustwallow Marsh, completely infested with predatory giant spiders. Crumbling ruins outside hint at an unfortunate former settlement swallowed up by the marsh's hazards. Locals remain divided on whether the cavern gave its name to the arachnids or the reverse. Situated in the northwest reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Darkmist Cavern appears to have once been an active mining venture. Today, any human presence has long vanished, leaving behind rotting, ruined shacks outside the entrance and a network of tunnels choked with thick webs. The cavern is overrun by Darkmist spiders, predatory horrors whose venom and size make the tunnels deadly to unwary wanderers. Marsh dwellers still dispute whether the cavern was named after the foul brood nesting inside or if the spiders took the title from the misty cave itself.

Darkshire. Darkshire, formerly known as Grand Hamlet, is a battered settlement in eastern Duskwood. Cloaked in an enduring, unnatural gloom and neglected by Stormwind, the town survives only through the vigilance of the Night Watch and the stubborn endurance of its people. Once a peaceful woodland settlement called Grand Hamlet, the village was razed by the Old Horde during the First War and later rebuilt. Its fortune turned truly bitter following the fall of Medivh at Karazhan, whose lingering death throes cursed the surrounding woods into the shadowy wilderness of Duskwood. Despite being a nominal holding of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the town hall receives virtually no aid from the crown. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled, forcing Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council to administer their own harsh, insular justice in the shadows.

Darkshire Town Hall. Darkshire Town Hall stands on the western edge of the town square as the seat of local governance in Duskwood. From inside these dimly lit halls, Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke and his council attempt to administer a settlement besieged by creeping darkness and undead monstrosities. Located directly west of the main town square, the Town Hall is where Darkshire's civic leadership gathers to govern an increasingly isolated territory. Within its weathered walls sits Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke, struggling to preserve civil order and protect the populace while Stormwind offers little in the way of military aid. Alongside the mayor, municipal officials like Clerk Daltry work to track local records and the travelers braving Duskwood's dangerous roads, though keeping ledgers current is a grim and challenging task in such perilous times.

Darkshore Grouper. Along Darkshore, grouper are a familiar catch, though murloc attacks have driven fishermen from their boats. The fish is prized for food and sport, and a good haul is harder to find. Darkshore Grouper are a welcome catch in the cold waters off Darkshore. Anglers around Auberdine value them for the simple dishes they make, and travelers and residents alike enjoy those meals. A fishing line and basic gear are enough to bring one in. For many fishermen, the pleasure of catching a grouper matches the pleasure of eating it.

Darksoul Shackle. A Darksoul Shackle is an enchanted fetter worn by the Moonrage Darksoul worgen stalking Silverpine Forest. Crafted under the direction of Archmage Arugal, these implements are sought by Forsaken mages at the Sepulcher seeking to unravel the feral magic gripping the region. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the worgen upon Silverpine Forest, his own arcane mastery proved insufficient to fully direct and sustain the otherworldly beasts. To compensate for his shortcomings, he bound enchanted implements, such as Darksoul Shackles, to his creations. These fetters channel external sorcery into the Moonrage Darksouls, reinforcing their supernatural strength and anchoring the curse that keeps them thrall to Shadowfang Keep.

Darkspear Islands Clash. Darkspear Islands Clash is an Alliance military call to arms urging champions to defend vital ground against fierce Darkspear Raiders. Without immediate support on the front lines, the Alliance risks losing the contested archipelago entirely. The struggle for control of the Darkspear Islands has erupted into open war between the Alliance and aggressive warbands of Darkspear Raiders. Alliance commanders warning that without urgent reinforcements, their foothold in the archipelago will be overwhelmed, have sounded a call to arms for capable champions to stem the hostile tide.

Darkspear Islands Clash. Darkspear Islands Clash calls upon fighters to rally their companions and defeat the hostile Darkspear Raiders contesting the archipelago. The ongoing battle demands coordinated action to stem enemy incursions across the contested island chain. The Darkspear Islands Clash represents an active military push within the contested Darkspear Islands. Forces deployed to the theater are urged to stand fast against waves of Darkspear Raiders who continue to wage skirmishes across the beaches and interior grounds. Rather than an isolated incident, the clash forms part of a sustained campaign to secure foothold territory in the archipelago.

Darkspear Strand. At Darkspear Strand, the tribe’s refuge begins on Durotar’s southern coast. The trolls came ashore after exile from the Echo Isles and built Sen'jin Village nearby under Vol'jin’s leadership. The Darkspear trolls came ashore here after losing the Echo Isles. When witch doctor Zalazane seized their home, survivors crossed the narrow waters and landed on this coast. They gathered just yards inland rather than scatter into Durotar’s hostile red wastes, and built Sen'jin Village. The strand looks across the surf toward the islands they still hope to reclaim.

Darkspear tribe. The Darkspear are a tribe of jungle trolls who joined Thrall's Horde after being driven from their ancestral home in Stranglethorn Vale and rescued from a sea witch in the Great Sea. Led by Shadow Hunter Vol'jin from their temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village, they now serve as core members of the Horde across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite their alliance, they currently struggle to reclaim their new home, the Echo Isles, from the traitorous witch doctor Zalazane. Originally a smaller, less ruthless tribe within the broken Gurubashi Empire of Stranglethorn Vale, the Darkspear endured centuries of warfare and famine against brutal neighbors like the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes. Driven out to sea, they settled on remote islands, only to face aquatic murlocs, Kul Tiran sailors, and a naga sea witch. Their elder chieftain, Sen'jin, was captured and slain in dark sacrificial rites beneath the sea, but before dying he foretold that the orc Warchief Thrall would lead the Darkspear to a new destiny. Rescued by Thrall's passing fleet, the survivors pledged their undying loyalty to the new Horde and sailed westward to Kalimdor.

Darkwhisper Gorge. Darkwhisper Gorge is a treacherous, demon-infested ravine carved into the southern heights of Winterspring. When Archimonde was destroyed at the climax of the Third War, remnants of the shattered Burning Legion fled down the slopes of Mount Hyjal and entrenched themselves in these jagged chasms. Today, powerful fiends stalk its heights, guarding ancient minerals and dark planar relics. Following the defeat of Archimonde atop Mount Hyjal, surviving demons of the Burning Legion scattered into the surrounding mountain ranges. A disciplined vanguard took refuge in Darkwhisper Gorge, transforming the southern border of Winterspring into a lethal stronghold. Led by Hederine demons—including lethal manastalkers, slayers, and initiates under Lady Hederine—these fiends fiercely defend their subterranean tunnels and fiery camps. Beyond the immediate threat of its elite inhabitants, an ominous, sealed archway stands at the gorge's lowest point, hinting at sealed passages leading higher up the sacred mountain.

Darn Talongrip. Darn Talongrip is an orc scout stationed along the frontier of the Stonetalon Mountains near Malaka'jin. He monitors local threats in the crags and helps coordinate Horde communication between forward outposts and regional commanders. Darn Talongrip watches the rugged ascents leading into Stonetalon from the southern Barrens. Stationed in the settlement of Malaka'jin, Darn directs recruits toward the Horde's new fronts in Ashenvale. His post serves as an early line of contact for travelers winding upward into contested peaks.

Darnassus. Darnassus rises among Teldrassil’s high boughs as the kaldorei capital and refuge. Its tranquil waters and groves make it the night elves’ spiritual heart and the Alliance’s primary bastion on northern Kalimdor. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Archdruid Fandral Staghelm guide their people through the trials of newfound mortality. Darnassus took shape after the Third War, honoring the night elves’ survival after they lost the immortality granted by their sacred World Tree, Nordrassil. Unlike the stone cities of Ironforge and Stormwind, it is an open, tranquil settlement of wood-crafted lodges, glowing shrines, and arched bridges over crystalline lakes. Vigilant Sentinels, towering ancients of war, and druids who shape trees watch the paths and preserve nature’s quiet within the city.

Darnassus Marzipan. At Hallow's End, Darnassus innkeepers hand out festive marzipan to visitors who dance for it. Crafted in the night elven capital for the autumn celebration, this sweet is one of four treats Jesper needs. During Hallow's End, Alliance capitals share a tradition of lighthearted trick-or-treating. Dwarves offer sharp mints, Stormwind makes chewy nougat, and Darnassus innkeepers prepare delicate marzipan for visitors. To receive a piece, you must show some festive spirit and dance when the innkeeper asks. The sweet is one of four regional treats sought by Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind's Cathedral Square who cannot go out to collect sweets himself.

Darrow Hill. Darrow Hill is an elevated expanse of rugged grassland nestled in northern Hillsbrad Foothills directly beneath the Headland. While mountain lions and stags graze across its open slopes, feral yetis lurk inside the Foothill Caverns that pit the hillside. Rich with veins of Alterac Granite, it serves as a treacherous frontier where natural beasts and rival travelers constantly clash. Rising along the base of the northern mountains below the Headland, Darrow Hill bridges the rolling pasture of southern Hillsbrad with the jagged, colder heights of Alterac. Mountain lions and stags stalk through the tall grasses, sharing the rocky slopes with towering yetis that spill out from the Foothill Caverns. Beyond its feral wildlife, the cavern walls hide deposits of dense Alterac Granite, drawing quarry workers, miners, and adventurers straight into harm's way. Caught between contentious regional claims, its trails remain notoriously dangerous for travelers of either faction caught unawares.

Darrowmere Lake. Darrowmere Lake is an expansive freshwater lake situated in the southeastern reaches of the Western Plaguelands. At its heart lies the fortress island of Caer Darrow, whose ruined halls conceal the Cult of the Damned's dread necromantic academy, Scholomance. Darrowmere Lake is among the largest inland bodies of water in the Eastern Kingdoms, bordered by the blight-stricken forests of Lordaeron and fed by the Thondroril and Darrowmere rivers. During the Second War, these deep waters saw intense naval skirmishes between the Horde and Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet. The Horde also struck the island fortress of Caer Darrow at the lake's heart, sacking it and carrying off its ancient runestone. Once a thriving waterway and trade artery for the House of Barov, the lake is now a grim, mist-veiled basin in the heart of the Plaguelands.

Darrowshire. Darrowshire is a ruined village in the southern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands, once a peaceful hamlet of Lordaeron. During the Third War, its residents mounted a desperate, tragic stand against an overwhelming Scourge force. Today, only shattered timbers, restless spirits, and bitter memories linger amid the silence. Before the plague consumed northern Lordaeron, Darrowshire was a humble rural settlement nestled beneath the southern cliffs. When the Scourge marched south during the Third War, a force led by the death knight Marduk Blackpool and the ghoul lord Horgus the Ravager besieged the town. The villagers and local defenders fought valiantly, momentarily holding the line against impossible odds. Ultimately, the defense collapsed, and the town was slaughtered down to the last soul. Rather than finding peace in death, many of Darrowshire's fallen defenders were reanimated as ghouls to bolster the Scourge's ranks, leaving the village an eerie, empty memorial of lost valor.

Darsok Swiftdagger. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern trails for threats. The orc scout directs Horde fighters against Witchwing harpies in the Dry Hills, whose raids endanger travelers and settlements. He is also an old friend of Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin. Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern scrubland from the Crossroads. The roads linking Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens’ northern reaches face raiders and centaur, as well as organized hunters from the sky. Darsok’s anger falls on the Witchwing harpies. Their roosts lie in the Dry Hills, northwest of the Forgotten Pools, where they threaten caravans traveling north.

name.frFR: Recommandation portant le sceau de Darthalia

text.enUS: Darthalia's Sealed Commendation. Darthalia's Sealed Commendation is an official dispatch penned by the Forsaken battle commander in Tarren Mill. It praises a soldier's relentless campaign against the humans of Hillsbrad and delivers word of those victories directly to Undercity's high command. Following the brutal clashes across the Hillsbrad Foothills, High Executor Darthalia drafted this sealed dispatch to officially record victories against Hillsbrad's human defenders and the devastation wrought upon human positions. Sealed to preserve the commander's appraisal from prying eyes, the document is addressed to Varimathras, dreadlord advisor to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. For the Forsaken leadership in the Royal Quarter, such missives offer tangible proof that Alliance enclaves south of Lordaeron can be broken, freeing northern garrisons to focus on the relentless threat of the Scourge.

Daryl the Youngling. Daryl the Youngling is a human hunter residing at Farstrider Lodge in the southeastern hills of Loch Modan. Eager to prove his marksmanship among veteran dwarven trackers, he challenges traveling adventurers to hone their wilderness skills and test their mettle against the local beasts. Farstrider Lodge is primarily a haven for dwarven mountaineers, trackers, and seasoned outdoorsmen who watch over the wilderness of Loch Modan. Daryl stands out as a young human striving to earn his place alongside these veteran stalkers. Rather than relying on mere bravado, he actively seeks to measure his hunting instincts against other travelers, issuing challenges to hunt down the tough wild boars and beasts roaming the crags and lakeshore.

Dashel Stonefist. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist is known for his quick temper and heavy hands. The dwarf called Fist keeps to Stormwind City's rougher alleys, where dangerous connections draw the attention of covert investigators. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist is known as Fist for the street fights that have earned him the name. Locals and city guards see a drunken, combative dwarf ready to throw a punch outside a tavern. His place in the district puts him at the nexus of Stormwind's underworld, where smugglers, cutpurses, and political agitators trade coin and rumors beyond the eyes of Cathedral Square.

Data Hoarders. Data Hoarders is a task given by Jemma Quikswitch, an exiled gnome residing in Ironforge. During the desperate evacuation of Gnomeregan, she copied her family's most prized archives onto punch cards, only to lose several in the freezing drifts outside the city gates. Recovering these lost data cards means salvaging everything from advanced naval engineering schematics to irreplaceable family recipes. When the trogg invasion and subsequent radiation disaster forced the gnomes out of Gnomeregan, thousands fled with whatever belongings they could snatch up in the chaos. Jemma Quikswitch took the prudent step of transcribing generations of family knowledge into physical punch card archives. Tragically, a damaged satchel spilled several key cards into the snowfields surrounding the fallen city. Without these missing punch cards, the remaining data registers as indecipherable gibberish, threatening to erase her family's intellectual legacy.

Data Rescue. When the gnomes evacuated their irradiated capital, massive archives of vital technical knowledge and records were left behind. Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge recruits daring operatives to infiltrate Gnomeregan and retrieve a high-security Prismatic Punch Card. Navigating through layers of computerized clearance, couriers must punch their way through progressively fortified terminals deep within the ruined city. The sudden fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and deadly radiation forced the gnomish populace to abandon centuries of advanced research, schematics, and civic logs. Scattered throughout the technological corridors are Matrix Punchograph terminals, the automated data hubs that regulate security clearances and file storage. For exile leaders like Master Mechanic Castpipe, recovering these punch-encoded archives from the ruined depths represents one of the highest priorities of the refugee community in Tinker Town.

David Trias. David Trias is the Forsaken rogue trainer stationed in Deathknell. He instructs freshly awakened undead in the arts of stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft to aid Queen Sylvanas and the Forsaken. Positioned amidst the tombstones and ruins of Deathknell, David Trias is tasked with identifying and training those newly risen undead who possess a talent for unseen murder. For the fledgling Forsaken, survival requires more than sheer force of arms; it demands precise strikes from the dark. Trias decrypts orders and teaches initiates how to wield daggers, conceal their movements, and turn their reanimated reflexes into lethal precision against the living and the Scourge.

Dawn in the Mountains. Dawn in the Mountains is a quest to deliver a shipment of holy candles to Father Gavin at Misty Pine Refuge. A gentle priest of the Argent Dawn, Gavin maintains this mountain shelter to heal and comfort weary travelers rather than wage war with weapons. While many within the Argent Dawn take up arms to purge unholy horrors from Azeroth, some choose the gentler calling of the Light. Father Gavin, a priest dwelling in the rugged mountain wilderness, has turned away from the blade to focus wholly on healing the afflicted and tending to the weary. Taking an abandoned structure, he restored it into Misty Pine Refuge, a safe stop for travelers facing the perils of the high passes.

Dawning Isles. The Dawning Isles are a cluster of low-lying islets situated within Lordamere Lake along the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest. Once idyllic retreats, they have succumbed to the blight of the Plague of Undeath and are overrun by aggressive murlocs. Before the Third War, the Dawning Isles were known as scenic keys resting on the calm, clear waters of Lordamere Lake. When the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron, corruption seeped into the lake's shallows. The vegetation turned pallid and rotting, driving away idyllic peacefulness. Today, the Vile Fin murloc tribe dominates the muddy shores and tangled brush, aggressively defending their burgeoning colonies from anyone seeking to traverse the lake.

Dawning Wood Catacombs. Carved deep beneath Raven Hill Cemetery, the Dawning Wood Catacombs are a dark labyrinth teeming with the fiercest undead in Duskwood. Those who brave the subterranean tunnels face entrenched swarms of skeletal guardians and flesh-eating ghouls. Long before the twilight curse settled over the forest, the Dawning Wood Catacombs served as a resting place for the dead of the surrounding woods. Now buried beneath the ruined Raven Hill Cemetery, these dark stone corridors hold the most lethal undead in the region. The catacombs feature two distinct subterranean wings: the western passages are held by ranks of animated skeletons guarding ancestral tombs, while the eastern passages descend into a foul warren overrun by ravenous, disease-bearing ghouls. Lone travelers rarely survive deep within their depths.

Dawnwatcher Selgorm. Dawnwatcher Selgorm is a human representative of the Argent Dawn stationed upon the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus. Acting as an observer and liaison in the night elven capital, he monitors reports of shadowy cult activity and dark threats stirring across northern Kalimdor. While the Argent Dawn focuses heavily on the undead scourge festering in the Eastern Plaguelands, their vigilance extends anywhere ancient evil takes root. Dawnwatcher Selgorm stands watch in Darnassus, bridging the gap between the insular night elves and the broader crusade against malevolence. From the Craftsmen's Terrace, he gathers intelligence on emerging threats in Kalimdor's wilderness, enlisting capable Alliance travelers to strike at cultists and dark powers before their influence can corrupt the realm.

Dawnwatcher Shaedlass. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass is a night elf affiliated with the Argent Dawn, stationed within the Craftsmen's Terrace of Darnassus. Acting as a quiet eyes-and-ears operative in Kalimdor, he seeks news of his fellow order members sent on perilous reconnaissance into hostile lands. While the Argent Dawn is most famous for its bitter crusade against the Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands, its vigilance extends far beyond Lordaeron. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass maintains a presence in the night elven capital of Darnassus, watching over the faction's interests in Kalimdor. From his quiet post on the Craftsmen's Terrace, he keeps tabs on covert expeditions against dark cults and corrupting powers that threaten the wider world.

Dazalar. In Dolanaar, Dazalar trains young night elf hunters for the wilds of Teldrassil. He teaches them to aim true and form bonds with the beasts of the great boughs. Dazalar trains young hunters in Dolanaar before they venture beyond Shadowglen. Night elf rangers and sentinels patrol the wilderness, and he teaches newcomers the patience and discipline needed to protect Teldrassil's fragile ecosystem.

Dead Acre. The Dead Acre lies burned and abandoned in southeastern Westfall, near the bridge to Duskwood. The Defias Brotherhood torched the farm during their uprising, and rogue harvest golems now stalk its blackened fields. You find the Dead Acre just north of the road from Sentinel Hill to Duskwood. Once a productive homestead among Westfall’s breadbasket farms, it met a violent end when the Defias Brotherhood rose in revolt and drove out the local landowners. The farm and its crops went up in flames. Scorched timber and smoking earth remain, while mechanical Harvest Watchers still reap the barren soil.

Dead Field. The Dead Field is a blighted, abandoned farmstead situated in northern Silverpine Forest. Once quiet rural farmland, it has been seized by the Rot Hide gnolls and transformed into a forward staging ground for Scourge forces. Repeated Forsaken attempts to clear the area have faltered under the command of the banshee Nightlash. Little remains of the original farmstead in the northern reaches of Silverpine Forest, its previous living occupants long lost to the Third War. Today, the ruined plot serves as a base of operations for the Rot Hide gnolls, who act as willing servants to the Scourge. As their numbers swelled, Deathstalker scouts passing through the region noted signs of imminent military mobilization threatening Forsaken supply lines and outposts. Small Forsaken assaults against the farm have repeatedly failed, turned back by the wailing apparition Nightlash—a banshee who manifests whenever her gnoll thralls are endangered.

Dead-tooth Jack. A stolen badge puts Marshal Haggard's authority in Defias hands. The retired officer lives in eastern Elwynn Forest, where Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into surrendering his official insignia. Jack wore a Stormwind tabard in the dark and posed as Marshal Dughan. Haggard needs the badge back before the Defias Brotherhood can use it to impersonate Stormwind officials. Marshal Haggard lives in an isolated cottage on Elwynn's eastern ridges. One night, a figure in a Stormwind tabard approached, claiming official business and asking for Haggard's old marshal's badge. Believing he was handing it to a fellow officer, Haggard complied. The stranger laughed in his face and vanished into the woods. The thief was a Defias rogue called Dead-tooth Jack.

Deadeye Shore. Deadeye Shore lies windswept along Durotar’s eastern edge, east of Drygulch Ravine. Named for Kilrogg Deadeye, the Bleeding Hollow chieftain, its barren sands are roamed by raptors, scorpids, and feral boars. Deadeye Shore runs beneath central Durotar’s red bluffs, with sand and rocky outcrops that faintly resemble a skull missing an eye socket. The coast takes its name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed Bleeding Hollow chieftain who fought in the First and Second Wars. No major settlement or military outpost holds the shore. It is far from peaceful: aggressive wildlife rules the sands, and Burning Blade cultists from nearby ravine hideouts have been seen prowling toward the water.

Deadman's Crossing. Deadman's Crossing is an ominous junction set within the bleak canyon of Deadwind Pass. Branching between Duskwood, the Swamp of Sorrows, and the haunted tower of Karazhan, it serves as a grim threshold marked by gallows and warning signs. Despite its gruesome appearance, the path remains a vital thoroughfare for travelers moving across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Situated at the eastern crossroads of Deadwind Pass, Deadman's Crossing links the shadows of Duskwood with the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows, while a foreboding southern track ascends toward the haunted tower of Karazhan. The crossing takes its name from the twisted hangman's tree planted at the road's fork, where a pair of rotting corpses dangle overhead as a stark warning to all who pass. Beside the tree, battered wooden signs offer blunt advice to travelers, urging them to turn back and abandon hope. The canyon itself is thick with hostile beasts and dark sorceries, yet travelers moving steadfastly along the packed dirt road will find the crossing itself oddly unmolested, so long as they do not wander into the blighted rocks.

Deadmines. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines lie silent under a ruined town in Westfall. Once the greatest gold producer in human lands, the mines were abandoned during the First War. Now rumors speak of sinister forces in the forgotten shafts, though their danger remains unknown. The Deadmines once led all human mines in gold, with Whitestone oak for timber and supports. When the orcish Horde pushed north, miners fled in haste. Sir Anduin Lothar entered the treacherous depths to recover the sacred Tome of Divinity. Subterranean ogres held him captive for twenty months before rescuers freed him. After the kingdom fell, the shafts went quiet, and people came to say they were cursed.

Deadmire. Deadmire is a hunting rite offered by the tauren hunter Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. The task sends hunters east into Dustwallow Marsh to track and slay an ancient, suffering crocolisk named Deadmire, bringing back its tooth as proof. It serves as an exercise in both challenging tracking and the hunter's duty of mercy. On Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof instructs promising trackers in the deeper spiritual traditions of the hunt. Unlike thoughtless slaughter or trophy gathering, tauren hunting philosophy teaches reverence and connection with the natural world. Melor tasks hunters with journeying far eastward to the murky wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh to seek out Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk of immense scale whose prolonged life has turned into an agonizing burden.

Deadmire's Tooth. Deadmire's Tooth is a trophy taken from the ancient crocolisk known as Deadmire, who stalks the murky waters of Dustwallow Marsh. Bringing it to the hunter Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff proves that the aging predator has been granted a merciful and honorable death. In the traditions of the tauren hunters on Hunter Rise, tracking wild beasts is not merely a test of martial prowess or mindless bloodsport. It is a spiritual covenant of balance, reverence, and occasionally, mercy. Deadmire was once one of the most magnificent crocolisks in Dustwallow Marsh, but his great age turned his final years into excruciating torment. Despite possessing the unyielding spirit and terrifying ferocity of his prime, his massive bones and failing body became a prison of endless pain. Claiming Deadmire's Tooth serves as physical proof to Melor Stonehoof that the beast's prolonged suffering has finally been brought to an end through an honorable hunt.

Deadwood Village. Deadwood Village is a furbolg encampment nestled in southern Felwood. Once a peaceful clan attuned to nature, its residents fell victim to the demonic corruption that blighted the surrounding forest. Driven mad by fel taint, the Deadwood furbolgs now attack anyone who approaches their crude wooden settlement. Situated near the southern border of Felwood, Deadwood Village serves as the primary enclave of the Deadwood tribe. When the Burning Legion's demonic energies washed through the ancient woodlands, the furbolgs lacked the power to resist the creeping rot. Their minds warped by fel malice, they abandoned their ancient traditions and spiritual harmony. Today, the village is a squalid gathering of hostile brutes, shamans, and den watchers who violently defend their polluted grounds against intruders, earning the despair of their uncorrupted cousins, the Timbermaw.

Death Cap. In Darkshore, Death Cap grows in the cave behind Cliffspring Falls. Night elf herbalists seek the scarce fungus, but the Grove of the Ancients warns against approaching the falls. Death Cap grows in the damp cave behind Cliffspring Falls, along Darkshore's northeastern mountain ridges. Scaber stalks carpet the cavern floor, but Death Cap is scarce. Night elf herbalists such as Barithras Moonshade value it for experimental brewing. Finding even one means entering a cavern the Grove of the Ancients warns against, where corruption is taking root.

text.enUS: Death From Below. In the Arathi Highlands, Shakes O'Breen expects the Daggerspine naga to attack from the sea, and the crew cannot sail home to Booty Bay without O'Breen's knowledge of the waters. You stay aboard beside O'Breen, man the cannon and drive the naga back. After Sunken Treasure, Shakes O'Breen sees the Daggerspines gathering to attack. Naga have a name for ruthlessness and will keep coming until O'Breen is dead. O'Breen does not value their own life above those of the crew, but asks you to defend them, since the crew cannot reach Booty Bay without that knowledge of the seas. You wait aboard with O'Breen for the naga to come from the water.

Deathguard Bartholomew. Deathguard Bartholomew is a vigilant Forsaken soldier stationed in the town of Brill. Tasked with maintaining security across Tirisfal Glades, he helps travelers navigate the blighted settlement and assists in enforcing discipline among local defenders. Standing watch in the settlement of Brill, Deathguard Bartholomew represents the stalwart military backbone of the Forsaken. Like his fellow Deathguards throughout Tirisfal Glades, he defends reclaimed territory from lingering Scourge, fanatical Scarlet Crusaders, and any other threats to Lady Sylvanas's domain. In addition to keeping watch, he provides directions to travelers attempting to navigate the town's facilities and participates in maintaining orderly conduct among the newly risen.

Deathguard Burgess. Deathguard Burgess is a Forsaken sentry stationed in the town of Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Standing watch over the settlement, he keeps order and directs travelers to vital services across the hamlet. Positioned in the settlement of Brill just north of the Undercity, Deathguard Burgess serves as one of the town guards maintaining security against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade. Like other Deathguards throughout Tirisfal Glades, Burgess aids arriving Forsaken by providing directions to local tradesfolk, class trainers, and civic services, keeping the vulnerable outpost running smoothly.

Deathguard Dillinger. Deathguard Dillinger is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Standing watch over the town's perimeter, he directs newly arrived undead toward necessary services and tasks recruits with keeping the local Scourge remnants at bay. As a member of the Forsaken Deathguard, Dillinger stands at the entrance of Brill, serving as both a frontline protector and an orienting guide for travelers emerging from Deathknell. He provides directions to town amenities such as the inn, the town hall, and local trainers, helping newly awakened undead navigate their new reality under the Dark Lady's rule.

Deathguard Humbert. Deathguard Humbert is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Assigned to monitor the encroaching Alliance presence, he finds himself in an embarrassing predicament after losing his military gear to the dwarves of Dun Garok. While tasked with maintaining Tarren Mill's perimeter against regional threats, Deathguard Humbert suffered a humiliating setback. Sent by High Executor Darthalia to watch Dun Garok from a hidden camp, he left one morning to gather firewood, and dwarven scouts from Dun Garok made off with his prized sword and assorted equipment, leaving the undead soldier desperate to salvage his pride and armament before high command takes notice.

Deathguard Linnea. Deathguard Linnea is a Forsaken soldier stationed at a Deathguard waystation in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. She helps secure the roads between Brill and the eastern borders, watching for threats posed by the Scarlet Crusade and lingering Scourge. Adventurers passing along the main thoroughfares often assist her unit with patrol duties. Deathguard Linnea stands sentinel at a small fortified post southeast of Brill. Life—or unlife—on patrol in Tirisfal Glades is treacherous, as the Forsaken must vigilantly defend their fledgling realm against Scarlet Crusade infiltrators and mindless Scourge prowling the wilderness. Stationed alongside her fellow guards, Linnea oversees patrol efforts along the roadway, coordinating reports with local authorities such as Magistrate Sevren in Brill to keep the eastern road toward the Bulwark secure.

Deathguard Samsa. Deathguard Samsa is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tasked with maintaining Horde vigilance on a tense frontier, he directs traveling champions to strike at local threats encroaching on the settlement. Standing watch in Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa represents the defensive backbone of the Forsaken in the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Tarren Mill serves as the Horde's primary outpost in the region, facing immediate pressure from Alliance outposts like Southshore as well as savage local wildlife. Samsa's duties involve securing the perimeter and directing capable adventurers to eliminate threats before they endanger the encampment.

Deathguard Simmer. Deathguard Simmer is a Forsaken soldier stationed just outside Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. He sizes up newly risen Forsaken and sends them to raid the human pumpkin farm to the west, patrolled by the Scarlet Crusade, for reagents the apothecaries of Brill need. Posted just outside Deathknell, Deathguard Simmer represents the Forsaken military line holding the border between the safe haven of Deathknell and the wider perils of Tirisfal Glades. The region crawls with living humans—most notably the fanatical Scarlet Crusade—who view all undead as abominations to be purged with fire and blade. Simmer tests fledgling Forsaken by sending them west to the Solliden Farmstead, where the Scarlet Crusade patrols from its nearby tower, to steal ten pumpkins and carry them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

Deaths in the Family. Coleman Farthing, a former mill worker now dwelling in Brill, seeks personal vengeance against the aristocratic Agamand family. Convinced to stay and defend their estates against the Scourge during the Third War, Farthing and his fellow workers perished alongside their stubborn employers, only for the Agamands to rise as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, the Agamand family stood as the wealthiest and most influential agrarian dynasty in Tirisfal Glades. Their sprawling mills and fertile pastures produced bountiful grain, commanding the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crept across the kingdom, the Agamands refused to flee or abandon their ancestral holdings, convinced that stone walls and loyal workers could hold off the horrors advancing from the east.

Deathstalker Faerleia. Deathstalker Faerleia is an operative of the Forsaken intelligence agency stationed deep within enemy territory inside Pyrewood Village. Operating out of the settlement's town hall, she orchestrates covert strikes against the Pyrewood Council, the village leaders Arugal uses as puppets.

Deathstalker Lesh. Deathstalker Lesh is a Forsaken rogue serving as a forward scout at Southpoint Tower in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Operating directly under High Executor Darthalia, she keeps watch over the human farms in the Hillsbrad Fields to gauge when the Forsaken should strike. Perched at Southpoint Tower on the southern road through the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the human farmers and town militia working the nearby Hillsbrad Fields. As an operative of the Deathstalkers—the Forsaken's secretive intelligence and assassination network—Lesh tracks enemy movements and numbers for High Executor Darthalia in Tarren Mill. When the moment is right, Lesh sends word to Darthalia with a coded message, 'The raven's cry from the west doth beckon', signaling that Hillsbrad is ripe for the Forsaken's attack.

Deathstalker Report. The Deathstalker Report is a written dispatch penned by Deathstalker Rane Yorick detailing military reconnaissance in Silverpine Forest. It contains critical tactical intelligence intended for High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher regarding local Scourge movements and the state of the Forsaken's forward scouts. Reconnaissance in northern Silverpine Forest is a lethal duty, even for the undead. After finding themselves ambushed and pinned down by Scourge prowling the pine woods, Deathstalkers Rane Yorick and Quinn Yorick had to consolidate their findings into this hurried dispatch. The report summarizes unexpected levels of Scourge resistance threatening Forsaken territorial ambitions in the region. Because Quinn suffered grievous injuries during their mission, the document is entrusted to passing allies to ensure High Executor Hadrec receives word at the Sepulcher without delay.

Deathstalker Vincent. Deathstalker Vincent was a Forsaken scout sent alongside Deathstalker Adamant to infiltrate Shadowfang Keep. Slain by the mad mage Arugal, his corpse remains inside the stronghold as a grim warning to any who challenge the feral worgen within. Before the Forsaken could launch a full-scale assault against the beasts holding Shadowfang Keep, intelligence on the fortress's interior was desperately needed. Two operatives from the Deathstalkers, the intelligence arm of the Forsaken, slipped past the barricades: Vincent and Adamant. Their mission ended in disaster. While Adamant was captured and locked away in a dungeon cell, Vincent was dragged directly before Shadowfang's master. Refusing to bend the knee or serve Arugal's dark designs, Vincent was executed on the spot, his body discarded on the stone floor to rot as a testament to the mage's fury.

text.enUS: Deathstalkers in Shadowfang. High Executor Hadrec dispatches Horde adventurers into Shadowfang Keep to locate two missing reconnaissance agents, Deathstalker Adamant and Deathstalker Vincent. The Forsaken military relies on their gathered intelligence to coordinate an assault against Archmage Arugal and his worgen packs. Breaching the fortress reveals the grim reality of espionage behind enemy lines. Silverpine Forest remains contested ground, with Archmage Arugal's feral worgen holding the towering redoubt of Shadowfang Keep. Seeking to break this siege on their southern borders, the Forsaken command stationed at the Sepulcher organized an intelligence operation. High Executor Hadrec sent two seasoned Deathstalkers—Adamant and Vincent—to infiltrate the fortress and chart its defenses. When days passed without word, Hadrec grew desperate for their field reports, tasking capable Horde champions with entering the stronghold to recover the agents and salvage the mission.

Deathwing. Deathwing the Destroyer, once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, is the fallen Dragon Aspect of the black dragonflight. Driven mad by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he turned against the other Aspects and plunged the world into fire and turmoil. Though defeated near Grim Batol after the Second War and believed slain or hidden away, the terror of his legacy still haunts the deep places of Azeroth. Before he was known as the Destroyer, Neltharion was granted dominion over the earth and the subterranean vaults of Azeroth by the titan pantheon. Yet dwelling so close to the world's deepest chambers exposed him to the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods. During the ancient War of the Ancients, the madness took complete hold. He deceived the other Dragon Aspects into imbuing a golden disc, the Dragon Soul, with portions of their essence under the guise of halting the Burning Legion, only to turn the terrible weapon against his allies and unleash catastrophic devastation.

Decoy!. Narain Soothfancy has a plan for the ransom: a sack of rocks in place of money, and you in place of him. You carry his disguise to the handover spot the booknappers set down in Winterspring. This follows the ransom letter. The ransom note said Narain should make the delivery himself, and he means to, after a fashion. He fills a sack with rocks, looks you up and down, and decides you will do. His special kit holds a turban, a robe and the sack, and you carry it to the handover spot the booknappers set down in Winterspring. When the booknappers show up for the goods, Narain wants them snuffed out, as a lesson in what comes of crossing him.

Decrepit Ferry. The Decrepit Ferry is a ruined dock on the eastern shore of Silverpine Forest that once provided passage across Lordamere Lake to Fenris Isle. Following the fall of Lordaeron, the ferry was destroyed, its operator murdered, and the shoreline overrun by undead and vicious Rot Hide gnolls. Before the Third War, this dock bustled with daily traffic across Lordamere Lake. Local farmers brought fresh produce down to the water, selling their crops directly to the wealthy lord of Fenris Isle and his household. For a modest fee, the ferryman carried trade goods, messengers, and visiting nobles back and forth between the mainland and the keep. That peaceful commerce ended abruptly when the Scourge swept through the kingdom. The ferryman was brutally killed, the boats were smashed, and the pier fell into decay.

text.enUS: Deep Cover. Shenthul sends a promising Horde rogue to Sludge Fen to contact an agent hidden among the Venture Company. The Shattered Hand has spent a year placing Taskmaster Fizzule inside the company’s drilling grounds, where he watches their plans. The Shattered Hand protects Orgrimmar’s interests through secret intelligence and assassination. For a year, its members worked to place an agent in the Venture Company’s ranks. Taskmaster Fizzule earned a place at their drilling outpost north of Sludge Fen, among the company’s mercenaries.

Deep Elem Mine. Deep Elem Mine is an excavation site nestled in the heart of Silverpine Forest. Once an active operation, it was overrun when Archmage Arugal's dark magic swept through the region, transforming its miners into savage worgen. Situated central to Silverpine Forest, the Deep Elem Mine once served the living inhabitants of Lordaeron as an ordinary resource vein. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the lupine nightmare upon the forest, his feral curse spread deep into the tunnels. The laborers inside succumbed to the affliction, turning into vicious worgen who abandoned their pickaxes to claim the cavern as a predatory lair.

Deep Ocean, Vast Sea. North of Auberdine, the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil lie beneath the waves. Murlocs ambushed both night elf vessels as they sailed into port, and their surviving crews seek a way to mourn their lost captains. Murlocs overwhelmed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as the ships approached Auberdine. Both vessels sank in the shallows north of the settlement. Their surviving crews reached shore, but the loss of the ships and their captains weighs on the port.

Deep Sea Salvage. Following Land Ho!, First Mate Nilzlix asks you to bring back the charts and logs of two sunken ships before anyone leaves the cove. O'Breen led three ships into the cove, certain the treasure lay here. The Harbinger docked safely. Then, as the Maiden's Folly with the Spirit of Silverpine came in, the tides began to lower, and both ships ran aground on a temple-like structure in the reef and sank fast.

Deepfury's Orders. Deepfury's Orders is a crumpled parchment recovered from the body of Ol' Rustlocke beneath the Thandol Span. It contains grim instructions belonging to the Dark Iron dwarves who ambushed the scouting dwarven defender. While scouting the foundations of the Thandol Span, the dwarven bridge defender Ol' Rustlocke was cornered and slain in a sudden Dark Iron ambush. Clasped beside the scout's clenched fist lay these orders, drafted by the enemy leader, Deepfury. The document serves as direct proof of a coordinated plot targeting the bridge that connects the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands.

Deepmoss Egg. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Deepmoss Eggs draw goblin merchants from Ratchet. Deepmoss spiders lay clustered clutches in the crags and canyons, and Booty Bay pirates prize them for omelettes. Deepmoss spiders nest across the Stonetalon Mountains, especially in Sishir Canyon and beneath the surviving trees of Windshear Crag. They leave clustered clutches of viable eggs in thick webbed sacks, sheltered by damp mountain moss. Most travelers have little use for them, but goblin traders see a chance to profit.

Deepmoss Spider Eggs. Mebok Mizzyrix sees a chance to sell Deepmoss Spider Eggs to Booty Bay. Spider egg omelettes have become a craze there, and he sends travelers into the Stonetalon Mountains to gather fresh clutches for the overseas trade. Booty Bay’s wealthy patrons and eccentric pirates have taken to spider egg omelettes, driving demand for rare ingredients across the Great Sea. Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix sees a chance to make a fortune by supplying the southern port. The Eastern Kingdoms have no supply of these spiders, so Mebok looks to Kalimdor’s wilderness for the eggs.

text.enUS: Deeprun Rat Roundup. Deeprun Rat Roundup is an Alliance task in the Deeprun Tram where players assist Monty with pest control. Using a charming musical flute, players round up living Deeprun rats to supply Monty's brother with fresh meat for rat kabobs. Down in the subterranean tube of the Deeprun Tram, a colorful character named Monty struggles to keep the underground transit line clear of pests. Speaking in salty sea slang and treating the tramway like a ship's deck, Monty enlists passing travelers to help round up the scurrying vermin infesting the station.

Deeprun Tram. The Deeprun Tram is an subterranean marvel of gnomish engineering linking the Alliance capitals of Ironforge and Stormwind City. Commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard following the Second War, it allows citizens and soldiers to cross vast distances beneath the earth in mere minutes. The enclosed twin tracks cut beneath mountain and lake, serving as a vital artery for Alliance military support and commerce. Following the devastation of the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard grew increasingly frustrated with how slowly dwarven aid and construction supplies reached Stormwind across the mountain passes. To solve the logistical hurdle and guarantee that dwarven soldiers could rapidly reinforce the human capital in times of crisis, Magni turned to High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque. The master gnomish engineer drafted designs for an enclosed underground railway powered by cutting-edge technology. Despite excavation complications—including cutting right through a vast subterranean lake and battling relentless infestations of underground rats—the tram became a crowning achievement of the Alliance, moving thousands of travelers free of charge between Ironforge and Stormwind.

Deepwater Tavern. The Deepwater Tavern is the bustling seaside inn of Menethil Harbor, nestled in the damp marshlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the primary meeting spot, resupply point, and resting place for travelers and mariners navigating the busy port town. Between hearty drinks and harbor rumors, patrons frequently find work or run into volatile tavern brawls. Standing within the sodden streets of Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern offers travelers a welcome shelter from the perpetually drizzly, treacherous marshlands outside. Sailors, dockworkers, merchants, and weary adventurers gather beneath its timber beams to trade news, share a warm fire, and patch their wounds. Beyond the usual amenities of a harbor inn, it houses a resident first aid trainer and local merchants catering to those bound for the perils of the marsh or embarking across the Great Sea. The atmosphere is boisterous and occasionally hazardous; disputes flare up quickly over spilled ale, with notorious troublemakers like Tapoke 'Slim' Jahn known to spark the occasional tavern-wide brawl.

Defeat Nek'rosh. Defeat Nek'rosh marks the culmination of the Alliance campaign against the Dragonmaw clan in the Wetlands. With their siege engines sabotaged, adventurers are ordered to strike down Chieftain Nek'rosh directly to secure Menethil Harbor. Bringing his severed head back to Captain Stoutfist shatters the orcish threat to the coastal port. The Dragonmaw orcs have long plagued the marshlands of Khaz Modan, entrenched within their fortified encampments and threatening the sea lanes of Menethil Harbor. After discovering and burning the clan's catapults, the defenders of the marsh strike straight at the head of the serpent. Chieftain Nek'rosh, commander of the local warband, stands as the final obstacle to breaking the siege. His demise strips the remaining Dragonmaw raiders of their tactical coordination.

Defias Brotherhood. The Defias Brotherhood is a widespread criminal network of bandits, brigands, and assassins waging an underground insurgency against the Kingdom of Stormwind. Their origins are a mystery to most, and they have grown into violent outlaws terrorizing the southern farmlands. From a hidden redoubt, they aim to overthrow the corrupt House of Nobles and lay waste to the kingdom.

Defias Docket. Defias operatives have hidden their orders at Addle's Stead in western Duskwood. The docket gives Stormwind's search for its missing emissary a lead into the Brotherhood's plans. Master Elling Trias points investigators toward Duskwood as they follow leads on the kingdom's missing diplomat. Watcher Backus has noted unusual Defias movements converging on Addle's Stead, the derelict farm south of the road from Westfall. A strongbox on the property holds the Defias Docket. Its records track the Brotherhood's movements, revealing work that reaches beyond highway robbery and local banditry.
Defias Hideout. Defias thugs and vagrants linger in a ruined house on Moonbrook’s southern edge. Its upper floor hides a route into the chambers beneath the town.

Defias Tower Key. At Klaven's Tower in Westfall, the Defias Tower Key proves an infiltrator reached the guarded perimeter. Stormwind operatives seek it from the malformed drones outside. Klaven's Tower stands on the Westfall coast as a Defias Brotherhood stronghold. Recent shipments from Duskwood brought new guards to its perimeter: malformed Defias drones, undead and covered in spikes. SI:7 operatives watch the grounds and direct field agents to pick the pockets of these sentries. Fighting them head-on is not the way to prove the perimeter has been breached. The key shows an infiltrator got through without raising an alarm.

Deino. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Deino trains Horde mages in the arcane arts. She teaches spellcasters to master arcane and elemental forces, and sends seasoned mages across Kalimdor to study ancient magic and seek remote tutors. Deino trains Horde mages in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Totems, huts, and quiet waters surround the raised platforms where she teaches. Troll spellcasters balance spiritual reverence with arcane mastery, a path Deino shares with fellow instructors Enyo and Pephredo.

Delgren the Purifier. Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post on the northern edge of Ashenvale. Operating alongside comrades Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand, he aids the night elves in cleansing demonic and shadow magic threatening the frontier, with a particular focus on the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand. Human paladins are a rare sight deep within the ancient forests of Kalimdor, but Delgren the Purifier arrived with a mission. Affiliated with the Argent Dawn, Delgren traveled west with a cadre of holy warriors determined to assist the Alliance's new night elf allies against the lingering evils of demons and undead remnants from the Third War. Stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, he maintains a watchful vigil over travelers passing south from Auberdine.

Deliah's Ring. Deliah's Ring is an engraved piece of jewelry recovered from a corpse pile amassed by the Rot Hide gnolls in Silverpine Forest. Bearing the inscription 'For Deliah', the keepsake offers a grim trail tracing back to a plague victim stolen from Tirisfal's mass graves. Discovered upon the pockmarked, relatively fresh hand of a corpse among gnoll mounds in Silverpine Forest, the ring is inscribed simply: 'For Deliah'. The discovery reveals that the local Rot Hide gnolls are not merely scavenging battlefields—they are actively raiding the mass graves of Tirisfal Glades and ferrying human and Forsaken corpses south to Fenris Isle for their own vile purposes.

Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in Elwynn Forest given by Hamish Bergwort at the Tower of Azora. Hamish's sensitive arcane equipment is being disrupted by erratic magical surges radiating from the north. To restore stability, travelers must enter Jasperlode Mine and cull the kobold geomancers responsible for the disturbances. Inside the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort oversees delicate arcane apparatus that requires fine calibration. Unfortunately for the scholar, the surrounding countryside is far from quiet. Repeated surges of uncontrolled energy constantly throw off his measurements, rendering careful magical adjustments impossible until the source of the interference is addressed.

Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest focused on restoring magical stability to the Tower of Azora. Hamish Bergwort's sensitive equipment is being disrupted by erratic spellcasting practiced by nearby Defias rogue wizards. Resolving the disturbance requires putting an end to the amateur sorcery around Stone Cairn Lake. Within the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort attempts to conduct delicate magical experiments, only to be repeatedly interrupted by unexplained ambient disruptions. In an arcane sanctuary where precise measurements are everything, even slight ripples in the local magical weave can ruin hours of careful work. Bergwort suspects the disruptions are not natural, but rather the result of crude spells cast nearby.

Deliver Thomas' Report. In eastern Elwynn, Guard Thomas sends word of two dead guards and rising danger. He asks you to carry the report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, where the garrison has few hands to spare. Guard Thomas watches the bridges into eastern Elwynn, where river traffic meets the wilderness. Guards Malakai and Rolf have been killed by aggressive murloc tribes. With his remaining guards too few to contain them, Thomas sends you down the road to Goldshire with an urgent report.

Deliver the News. Deliver the News is a quest concluding the plight of the Windfield family orchard in Skywall. After helping Aamelia secure the farm, the adventurer travels to Valanaar to deliver tidings of their safety to an anxious Alvarion Windfield. Deliver the News marks the resolution of an ordeal at the Windfield family orchard. Having stepped in to save the farm from an impending crisis, the adventurer receives heartfelt thanks from Aamelia, who is ready to put the danger behind them. With the orchard secured, the immediate priority shifts to reassuring Alvarion Windfield, who fled to the settlement of Valanaar to plead for assistance.

Deliver the Shipment. After Driftwood, Watcher Biggs has one last job for you while the wagon is being repaired. Biggs has packed up the key supplies rescued from the ogre attacks and wants you to carry them to Quartermaster Lungertz at Nethergarde Keep. While Biggs repairs the wagon, the key supplies rescued from the ogre attacks have been packed up for you to carry to Nethergarde Keep. The keep stands in the Blasted Lands' northern hills, watching over the Dark Portal. Biggs gives the route: follow the road east, head south into the Blasted Lands where it branches, and turn left at the next fork, with a warning to be wary.

Deliver the Signet. Deliver the Signet is a quest in which a traveler carries a recovered family ring to High Elder Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. The delivery brings tragic confirmation of his nephew's demise on Zephras Isle, while opening new opportunities to assist the local peacekeepers. When an adventurer journeys toward the settlement of Valanaar, they carry with them the Shadowsong Family Signet recovered from an isolated tower. Entrusted with this grim token, travelers seek out Talaanis Shadowsong, the High Elder of Zephras Isle. Beloved by his people despite widespread local hardships, Talaanis must face the painful confirmation that his nephew has perished, receiving condolences alongside the reclaimed heirloom.

Deliver the Thread. Deliver the Thread is an Alliance errand in Duskwood that ferries a spool of Ghost Hair Thread from Madame Eva in Darkshire across the haunted forest to Abercrombie. The eccentric hermit living near Raven Hill Cemetery claims he needs the enchanted thread to ward his ramshackle hut against restless spirits. However, Madame Eva's dark remarks about the thread hint that there may be far more sinister uses for it. Once Madame Eva finishes spinning spectral hair gathered from the ghost Blind Mary, she entrusts the Ghost Hair Thread to any traveler willing to carry it west. The journey requires crossing the shadowed expanse of Duskwood, slipping past lurking spiders and roaming undead to reach Abercrombie's dilapidated shack just north of the vast cemetery grounds.

Deliver to MacKinley. Stoley hands you a bottle of Steamwheedle bilge rum for MacKinley, the "Sea Wolf" of Booty Bay, to put an end to MacKinley's beliefs about Booty Bay booze. After the help you gave with the shipment, Stoley gives you a bottle of Steamwheedle bilge rum. You are to take it to MacKinley, in Booty Bay, so that he can finally let go of his crazy beliefs about the booze there.

Deliveries to Sven. Deliveries to Sven is an Alliance task given by Elaine Carevin in Darkshire, requesting that vital provisions be carried out to a lonely camp on the northwest frontier of Duskwood. There, Sven Yorgen and his few remaining followers wage a desperate, solitary struggle against the horrors of the blighted woods. The errand connects town folk struggling in the gloom with an isolated band on the edge of the wilderness. While Darkshire barely holds its own walls against wolves, spiders, and the restless dead, some refuse to cower behind palisades. Sven Yorgen and a meager handful of companions established a solitary encampment along the northwestern perimeter of Duskwood. So pressed are they by constant danger that they cannot spare a single man to make the perilous trek back to town for provisions. Elaine Carevin steps in to coordinate aid, relying on brave travelers to ensure these frontier fighters do not starve.

Delivering Daffodils. Delivering Daffodils concludes a small domestic errand running between the guard post and town square in Lakeshire. After fetching lunch for Guard Parker and picking up a bouquet from herbalist Martie Jainrose, you hand over the blooms to Darcy at the Lakeshire Inn, only to stumble straight into an awkward local rivalry. What began as a simple favor delivering a hot meal to Guard Parker turns into a delicate romantic gesture. Grateful for his lunch, Parker asks you to fetch flowers from Martie Jainrose as a surprise for Darcy, the cook who prepared his food. Martie arranges a fresh bouquet of her own favorite blooms—daffodils—unaware of who is intended to receive them.

Delivering the Relic. Latronicus Moonspear asks you to carry the Mysterious Relic to his wife, Vestia Moonspear, at Feathermoon Stronghold. He cannot make heads or tails of the device and hopes she can tell what it is. Latronicus Moonspear could not make sense of the device even with a wager riding on it. His wife Vestia, he says, is a fine priestess for their community and one of the most learned scholars to be found anywhere. If anyone can work out what the relic is, she can, and they need to know. She is only a short walk away and no doubt busy studying.

Delivery for Marin. Sprinkle in Gadgetzan hands you the Violet Powder to carry to Marin Noggenfogger, along with a reminder that Marin owes her a favor. With the Violet Tragan in hand, Sprinkle gives you the Violet Powder to take to Marin Noggenfogger, who is also in Gadgetzan. You are to tell Marin that a favor is owed to her.

Delivery to Mathias. Keryn Sylvius sends a sealed parcel from Goldshire to Master Mathias Shaw in Stormwind. The delivery gives a promising rogue entry into SI:7's inner workings. A parcel from the Lion's Pride Inn to the Stormwind Barracks may look like ordinary courier work. For a budding rogue, it is an audition for Stormwind Intelligence. Local trainer Keryn Sylvius entrusts the package to novice cutpurses, giving them a direct introduction to Master Mathias Shaw. The delivery tests whether they can cross the capital quietly, keep a low profile, and follow discreet orders without asking questions.
