text.enUS: Delivery to Silverpine Forest. This errand serves as a vital courier mission linking the Royal Apothecary Society's research in Brill with their ongoing efforts in Silverpine Forest. Tasked by Apothecary Johaan, you carry valuable findings to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher to aid the development of the Dark Lady's New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society operates under the direct command of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, tasked with concocting a New Plague capable of wiping out both the living and the Scourge. Isolated laboratories across Forsaken territory cannot work in a vacuum; survival and progress demand constant communication. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan has gathered experimental results that must be circulated to other researchers in the field without delay.

Delivery to the Gnomes. Kravel Koalbeard now has what he needs, and wants the Delicate Car Parts carried to Fizzle Brassbolts in the Shimmering Flats, who has waited a long time for them. Kravel admits he removed a little piece from Fizzle's order, and suggests you leave it unmentioned. Kravel Koalbeard tells you the parts are for Fizzle Brassbolts, who has been waiting a long time. Kravel confesses he took one little piece out of Fizzle's order, but feels sure it will not be missed. He calls the piece small and worthless, advises you not to bring it up, and asks you to trust him.

Demisette Cloyce. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Demisette Cloyce teaches warlocks beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. She guides students in fel magic and sends those ready for more toward other summoners. Warlocks gather in the cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, while the city's authorities uphold order and the Holy Light. Demisette Cloyce lives in the catacombs below, teaching those willing to study forbidden arts. She warns that dark energies corrupt only those without the discipline to master them.

Demon Fall Canyon. Demon Fall Canyon is a scarred, fel-corrupted gorge situated in southern Ashenvale. It marks the legendary battleground where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall confronted the pit lord Mannoroth, ending the demonic blood curse that had enslaved the orcish race for a generation. Carved into the rugged southern borders of Ashenvale near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, this canyon bears the heavy scars of the Third War. It was here that Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked down the pit lord Mannoroth to break his hold over the Horde. During the fierce duel, Mannoroth incapacitated Thrall, but Grom seized the opening to drive his axe, Gorehowl, straight into the demon's chest. The resulting infernal explosion shattered the pit lord and slew Grom as well, permanently liberating the orcs from their lingering demonic servitude.

Demon Fall Ridge. Demon Fall Ridge is a blighted highland in south-eastern Ashenvale, overlooking the canyon where Mannoroth fell. Swarming with lesser demons and corrupting magic, the ridge centers around a desecrated night elf barrow den claimed by the Burning Legion. Rising directly west and above Demon Fall Canyon, Demon Fall Ridge is stained with lingering fel residue from the Third War. While the canyon below marks the site of the catastrophic clash between Grommash Hellscream and the pit lord Mannoroth, this high ground serves as a staging area for surviving demonic invaders. Lesser demons patrol the rocky cliffs, defiling the ancient woodland and threatening any travelers traversing the southern border of Ashenvale.

Demont's Place. Outlaws hold Demont's Place, a ruined farm west of Moonbrook in southwestern Westfall. The farm once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind, but economic collapse and the Defias Brotherhood drove its caretakers away. Its fields remain empty and its fences weathered. Demont's Place lies within sight of Moonbrook, among the family holdings that once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and outlaw brigands stripped the farm of its livelihood and drove out its caretakers. Like the neighboring fields, it has fallen into a rough hideout, where outlaws use its grounds as an extension of the Defias stronghold in Moonbrook.

Den of Flame. The Den of Flame is a fortified cavern in western Dustwallow Marsh, situated just west of the Stonemaul Ruins. Originally constructed by the Stonemaul ogres as their mound, it has since been overrun by the dragonkin of the black dragonflight serving Onyxia. Built by the Stonemaul ogres to serve as their main mound and sanctuary, the Den of Flame bears the unmistakable, rough-hewn stone architecture of ogre masonry. However, when the black dragonflight laid waste to the Stonemaul clan's settlement, the brood did not merely scatter the ogres—they seized the stronghold for themselves. Today, black dragonspawn patrol the burning perimeter and cavern entrance under the shadow of Onyxia's nearby lair.

Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies Teldrassil's unusual plants and seeks remedies for its corruption. He tends a small lakeside plot and asks young adventurers to gather samples, examine timberlings, and test enchanted soil. Denalan studies plants on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore. He works beneath a cloth awning, with field tools and rows of planter boxes close at hand. While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, he gives his days to herbalism. He chooses this plot over Darnassus's grand barrows, so he can examine the unusual flora that has grown since the new World Tree was planted.

Denalan's Earth. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf sends a late shipment of rare earth south to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth. The night elf researcher studies Teldrassil's young plants. Syral Bladeleaf stops travelers in Dolanaar with a special shipment of rare earth for Denalan. The soil came from Darnassus to support his botanical studies, but delays kept it from reaching Dolanaar until now. Syral seeks a courier to carry the parcel south along the forest trail to Denalan's campsite by Lake Al'Ameth.

Dendrite Starblaze. Dendrite Starblaze is a night elf druid residing in the sacred village of Nighthaven within Moonglade. Serving the Cenarion Circle, he acts as a vital mentor and guide for budding druids of both night elf and tauren descent. Through him, practitioners are summoned to the holy grove to master essential rites such as cleansing toxins and communing with nature's forms. Perched within Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze represents the nonpartisan, enduring spirit of the Cenarion Circle. When novice druids learn to attune their spirits to Teleport: Moonglade, Dendrite is among the first to welcome them upon arrival. He bridges the gap between ancient Kaldorei tradition and the emerging path of the tauren, treating all who heed the call of the wild as kin beneath the boughs of the sacred haven.

Deputy Feldon. Deputy Feldon is a member of the Redridge town guard stationed just south of the Great Lakeshire Bridge. Tasked with watching the primary road into Lakeshire, he keeps a nervous vigil against the aggressive gnoll packs creeping toward the town perimeter. Standing watch near the southern approach to the Lakeshire bridge, Deputy Feldon represents an overextended town guard fighting to keep basic trade and travel routes open. With the Blackrock orcs pressing from the north and gnoll packs overrunning the southern hills, guardsmen like Feldon are stretched to their limits. Unable to leave his post without compromising the town's perimeter, he relies on passing adventurers to cull the gnolls encroaching on the roadway before they can cut Lakeshire off entirely.

Deputy Rainer. Outside Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer holds Elwynn's western border. The Stormwind Army officer faces gnolls and bandits from Westfall, coordinating local defenses while reinforcements fail to arrive. At Westbrook Garrison, Elwynn Forest's westernmost post, the road crosses into Westfall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City leaves much of the army abroad or caught in bureaucracy, and border posts like this one lack troops. Deputy Rainer organizes the defense from outside the tower with the few forces at hand. Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves threaten the local roads, so he depends on passing travelers and mercenary adventurers to keep the forest trails secure.

Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, human priests seek a prayer for their own hour of need. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena teaches acolytes to call on the Holy Light when their lives are at risk. Priests in the Cathedral of Light learn to use their faith to shield companions, heal wounds, and strike at evil. Yet even the devout can be isolated, cornered, or brought close to death. In such moments, an acolyte may cry out to the Holy Light for help, with their own survival at stake.

Desperate Prayer. Promising priests from Elwynn Forest are summoned to Stormwind for further training in the Church of the Holy Light. After proving their devotion and discipline, they come before High Priestess Laurena at the Cathedral of Light. Priestess Josetta guides novice priests in Goldshire, while other local mentors serve the outlying settlements of Elwynn Forest. When a disciple proves capable in spirit and deeds, word reaches the senior priesthood in Stormwind. A summons to the Cathedral of Light marks the move to deeper responsibilities in the faith and formal training at the spiritual heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind.

Desperate Prayer. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight sends human priests home to Stormwind for further training. A fellow priest has crossed continents to summon them to the Cathedral of Light. In Dolanaar, Priestess Laurna Morninglight brings you word from home. A fellow priest has crossed continents to find you, and Laurna urges you to return without delay. She offers Elune’s blessing and good wishes for your faith as you leave Teldrassil.

Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, dwarven priests are called to deepen their service to the Light. High Priestess Laurena summons promising acolytes from Dun Morogh to the Cathedral of Light. There they take on wider duties among the Alliance. Dwarven priests trained in Dun Morogh can outgrow the lessons of local mentors like Maxan Anvol in Kharanos. When an acolyte shows promise, High Priestess Laurena sends a formal summons from the Cathedral of Light. Her attention means the young priest is ready for deeper study and greater duties in the faith.

Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, a summons carries a young priest from the Park to the Cathedral of Light. Nara Meideros sends you to High Priestess Laurena for further instruction. In Stormwind’s Park, Nara Meideros keeps faith with Elune. The city’s spiritual guides share ties across their different traditions. When the Cathedral seeks a promising student, Nara sends you across the canals with quiet encouragement. The message brings good tidings, not cause for alarm.

Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is a rite of passage for dwarven priests coming of age in Ironforge. Dispatched by High Priest Rohan, acolytes journey through the Deeprun Tram to Stormwind to continue their training under High Priestess Laurena. Reaching the grand Cathedral of Light marks an initiate's transition into deeper mysteries of healing and survival. Within the stone vaults of Ironforge's Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan oversees dwarven initiates dedicated to the Holy Light. When an acolyte demonstrates sufficient discipline and faith, Rohan directs them southwest to the human kingdom of Stormwind. Human and dwarven clerics maintain close spiritual bonds, and advanced theological instruction is centralized in the grand halls of Stormwind City.

Desperate Prayer. In Darnassus, young human and dwarven priests find guidance in another faith. Priestess Alathea teaches the ways of Elune, while followers of the Holy Light are directed to Stormwind. There, High Priestess Laurena welcomes the returning acolyte to the Cathedral of Light. Alliance priests follow different sacred paths. In Darnassus, the priesthood tends to Elune, channeling the moon goddess's radiance and wrath. Priestess Alathea honors Elune and respects the Holy Light, but cannot teach another race the deeper prayers bound to a different devotion. Human and dwarven acolytes who seek those prayers must look elsewhere.

Destiny Calls. Syurna sends you to learn what Sethir the Ancient knows of Teldrassil's corruption. The satyr waits near the Oracle Glade, beyond the reach of those who tried force or diplomacy. Teldrassil's growing sickness troubles the night elf leaders in Darnassus. Syurna, the rogue trainer, needs someone subtle; armed patrols have died trying to reach Sethir the Ancient. The satyr roosts on a remote bough near the Oracle Glade and has turned away force and diplomacy alike. To learn what he knows, you need to enter his lair and take his personal possessions.

Destruction in Deadmines. Deep beneath Moonbrook, Defias industry is poisoning the land. Alba Fairmoon suspects their metallurgical forge is the source of the blight and sends you to destroy it with explosives. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines shelter a fortified complex that powers the Defias Brotherhood. Its heavy forge smelts metal and builds machinery. Alba Fairmoon believes this forge is the likely origin of the contamination blighting the area. Destroying it is her aim.

Destruction in Deadmines. In Westfall, Alba Fairmoon sends an operative to destroy the Defias forge in the Deadmines. The explosives are already planted, and Alba waits in the hills behind Moonbrook for the detonator. The Deadmines hold the Defias Brotherhood's strength beneath Westfall. Alba Fairmoon directs you to sabotage the forge hidden in the mines. The explosives are already planted beside it, and you return to Alba in the hills behind Moonbrook to set them off from a safe distance. She hopes destroying the forge will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal.

Detonation at a Distance. Sprite Jumpsprocket needs a safer way to set off explosives, and Stormwind holds the answer. She sends you to Stormwind Intelligence for a remote detonator. Sprite Jumpsprocket wants to set off explosives from a safe distance. Goblins and gnomes are known for handling volatile chemicals recklessly, but some blasts demand care. A standard fuse can put the person lighting it in danger. Sprite knows a controlled explosion needs a special trigger, the kind common tinkerers do not keep on hand.

Detonation at a Distance. In Moonbrook, explosions beneath Westfall draw SI:7's attention. Jasper Fel, a Stormwind operative, sends a remote detonator kit to help handle the work from a safe distance. Jasper Fel and SI:7 watch events across Stormwind's lands, including Westfall's troubled border. When word reaches him of explosive work in Moonbrook, Fel already knows what is happening in the abandoned mining tunnels beneath the countryside.

Deviate Eradication. Deviate Eradication is a task assigned by the night elf druid Ebru above the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. While other disciples focus on waking their slumbering leader, Ebru asks adventurers to purge the caverns of mutated deviate beasts spawned by his twisted vision. Ridding the subterranean oasis of these horrors is an essential step in stemming the corruption threatening the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex brought his followers to the subterranean springs of the Barrens with an ambitious vision: tap into the Emerald Dream to regrow the parched plains into a lush, thriving woodland. Instead, Naralex became ensnared within the Dream, his slumber twisting into an agonizing nightmare. Rather than healing the land, the power surging through the caverns warped the native wildlife and plant life into monstrous, aggressive mutants known as deviate beasts.

Deviate Hide. Deviate Hides are the mutated skins stripped from the beasts dwelling within the Wailing Caverns. Warped by the corrupting dream of the druid Naralex, these otherworldly pelts are sought by druids looking to repurpose the nightmare's taint into durable leather goods. When the night elf druid Naralex entered his deep slumber beneath the Barrens, his dream turned into an Emerald Nightmare that warped the local cavern ecology. The beasts lurking in the depths transformed into unnatural deviate predators with tough, mutated hides. While inherently touched by evil, these pelts possess unusual, supple resilience that makes them uniquely suited for leathercrafting. Nalpak, perched high above the cavern mouth in the skull-shaped rock formation, collects these hides to study their properties and fashion them into sturdy utility packs.

Deviate Hides. Deviate Hides is a task given by Nalpak, a disciple of Naralex stationed above the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. While Naralex lies trapped in a twisted nightmare, Nalpak seeks to salvage something useful from the mutated beasts spawned beneath the Barrens. By gathering skins from these deviate predators, he hopes to put their strange, otherworldly properties to practical use. When the night elf druid Naralex attempted to tap the subterranean springs beneath the Barrens to restore lush life to the arid plains, his mind slipped into a terrifying nightmare. That dark reverie bled into reality, mutating the native wildlife of the Wailing Caverns into vicious deviate beasts. Raptors, crocolisks, vipers, and shambling horrors emerged warped and aggressive, altered by the emerald corruption leaking from their dreaming master.

text.enUS: Devils in Westfall. Dust devils roam Westfall, and Collin Mauren needs their remains for a spell. The Mage Quarter wizard is helping Gaxim Rustfizzle with an unusual experiment. Their work calls for a messaging scroll, and the dust holds what Mauren needs to enchant it. Collin Mauren is preparing a messaging scroll for Gaxim Rustfizzle. The wizard is helping the tinkerer with an unusual venture, but the spell needs more than ink and vellum. Dust devils roam Westfall with elemental magic swirling within them. Their remains provide the volatile medium Mauren needs to bind Gaxim's spell to parchment.

Devlin's Remains. Devlin's Remains are the collected skeletal bones of Devlin Agamand, the younger son of the wealthy family who owned the Agamand Mills. Stalking the roads near his ruined ancestral estate as a mindless Scourge thrall, he was struck down to deliver his bones to a vengeful survivor in Brill. In life, Devlin Agamand stood in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Where Thurman was gentle and tall, Devlin was remembered as physically frail and viciously sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect their lands and laborers. Devlin was among the first to fall, reanimated as a ravenous Scourge ghoul whose frantic, mad chattering haunted the roadside leading up to Agamand Mills.

Devourer of Souls. Devourer of Souls is an introductory step in a Forsaken warlock's journey to summon and bind a succubus. Directed by Carendin Halgar in the Undercity's Temple of the Damned, the practitioner must confer with his assistant, Godrick Farsan, to learn how to lure such a creature from the Twisting Nether. The ritual demands an irresistible stimulus: the hearts of pure and loving mortals. Carendin Halgar teaches that a succubus cannot simply be pulled across the threshold on command; it must be enticed. Driven by an insatiable hunger to ruin virtue and consume mortal essence, the demon requires a specific lure. The warlock's strategy relies on exploiting this singular desire by offering up the hearts of genuinely virtuous, loving men as bait. Halgar directs his acolytes to Godrick Farsan, who knows where such rare quarry can be harvested.

Devourer of Souls. Gan'rul Bloodeye sends an aspiring Horde warlock to begin the path to summoning and commanding a succubus. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the warlock seeks Cazul's counsel on luring and binding the demon. Horde warlocks who master lesser demons such as imps and voidwalkers may seek a succubus next. Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the dark arts beneath Orgrimmar and judges when a warlock is ready to call one from the Twisting Nether. A succubus can turn the frail against themselves, so binding one takes subtlety as well as strength.

Devourer of Souls. An Alliance warlock crosses the sea to seek Takar the Seer’s counsel on summoning a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder sends Stormwind initiates into the Barrens for the wisdom they need. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder guides promising warlocks toward summoning a succubus. The demon devours souls, destroys hearts, and dominates minds, so it cannot be called blindly into Azeroth. A warlock needs a potent lure: an object tied to pure love. That token draws the succubus from the Twisting Nether, where the warlock can defeat and bind it. Stormwind’s covens cannot teach them where to find such an object.

Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite of passage quest for Forsaken priests journeying far from Lordaeron. Guided by the Forsaken priest trainer Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff, the adept is directed back across the seas to Aelthalyste in the Undercity to unlock a signature manifestation of Shadow magic. While visiting Thunder Bluff, Forsaken priests who have honed their mastery over divine and shadowy disciplines are evaluated by Miles Welsh, a Forsaken priest posted among the tauren. Recognizing that an acolyte has grown sufficiently in power, Miles bids them return to the Ruins of Lordaeron rather than attempt to impart these higher mysteries himself in Kalimdor.

Devouring Plague. In Orgrimmar, Devouring Plague training begins with Ur'kyo sending Forsaken priests home. They have come to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear, but Aelthalyste waits in Undercity to teach them the shadow arts of their own people. Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power in Orgrimmar. Among the Horde, Darkspear trolls and Forsaken share a curious bond in matters of faith, while orcs and tauren show little inclination toward priestly worship. Ur'kyo knows Forsaken initiates must master the shadow arts tied to their own condition. In respect between their peoples, he sends wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to complete their training.

Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite of instruction offered to Forsaken priests who have proven their dedication to shadow magic. Granted by Priestess Aelthalyste in the Undercity, the teaching marks an acolyte's initiation into one of the most dreaded curses woven by the undead priesthood. In the murky cloisters of the War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste guides Forsaken practitioners through the grim arts of the Shadow. While living priests of other races appeal to the Holy Light or ancestral spirits for their power, the Forsaken have forged their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague represents the crystallization of their philosophy: inflicting suffering upon their foes while leeching the stolen vitality back into their own decaying bodies.

Devrak. At the Crossroads, Devrak keeps the Horde’s wind riders ready for the roads across Kalimdor. The orc flight master carries couriers and supplies between Durotar, Mulgore, frontier outposts, and the Horde’s capitals. At the Crossroads, Devrak tends the wind riders that link the Horde’s far-flung holdings. The outpost stands where Kalimdor’s major trade routes meet, exposed beneath the sun and vulnerable to quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. Quick flights matter here. Devrak pairs seasoned travelers and new messengers with trained wind riders that cross the savannah and reach Mulgore’s mountains or Durotar’s stone canyons.

Dextren Ward. Dextren Ward is an infamous criminal and grave robber locked away inside the Stormwind Stockade. Before his capture, he profited by exhuming bodies from Duskwood's Raven Hill Cemetery and delivering them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Now caught in the midst of the prison's bloody uprising, he remains marked for death by the town council of Darkshire. Before ending up in chains beneath the streets of Stormwind, Dextren Ward conducted a grim and lucrative business in the fog-choked woods of Duskwood. Raven Hill Cemetery was already a site of sorrow and growing horror, but Ward treated its burial grounds as a private quarry. Rather than hunting merely for trinkets and heirlooms left with the dead, Ward dealt in flesh, unearthing fresh graves to supply local dark practitioners.

Dig Rat Stew. Grub waits east of the Crossroads, hungry for a pot of dig rat stew. He sends travelers to Bael Modan in the southern Barrens to bring back dig rats for his recipe. Across the dry Barrens, hunters bring down zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors. Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads, craves something different: dig rats. He says he is hungry all day and offers to share his recipe with any traveler willing to catch the burrowing rodents.

Digging Through the Dirt. Digging Through the Dirt marks the grim culmination of the hunt for the Embalmer's missing heart in Duskwood. Deep in the ravenous quiet of Raven Hill Cemetery, a disturbed mound of earth conceals a buried horror that refuses to stay dead. Amid the countless weathered headstones of Raven Hill Cemetery sits a patch of recently turned, semi-loose soil marked with the name Eliza. While many graves in Duskwood lie desecrated by scavengers or feral ghouls, this earth was placed with deliberate intent. Digging past the topsoil reveals the splintered timber of a buried coffin, sealing away whatever remnant the Embalmer sought to hide away from the light of day.

Digging Through the Ooze. While paying her regular respects at Ironbeard's Tomb, Sida was startled by the foul oozes prowling the barrows and threw her bag to distract them. Unable to face the creeping sludge again, she asks brave adventurers in Menethil Harbor to track down the creature that swallowed her belongings. Sida, a traveler residing in Menethil Harbor, regularly ventures northeast into the Wetlands to pay homage at Ironbeard's Tomb. On her latest visit, she found the ancient barrow crawling with foul, dripping oozes. Panicking at the sight of the shapeless horrors, she hurled her satchel at one of them. The creature simply engulfed the bag whole, though the distraction gave Sida just enough time to flee back to the safety of the port town.

Dirania Silvershine. Dirania Silvershine is a night elf resident of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. Deeply loyal and observant, she watches over the tranquil grove and looks out for her companion Iverron when his reckless ventures land him in peril. Dirania stands among the tranquil boughs of Shadowglen, the secluded vale where young night elves begin their service to Kalimdor and the Alliance. While many in the barrow mounds and sanctuaries look to broad spiritual duties, Dirania stays mindful of those nearest to her, attentive to the quiet dangers that stir even in the heart of Teldrassil.

Dire Maul. Dire Maul is the ruined expanse of Eldre'Thalas, an ancient Highborne city hidden deep in the wilderness of Feralas. Once built to safeguard Queen Azshara's arcane secrets, its crumbling plazas and towering coliseums are now divided between occupying Gordok ogres, invading satyrs, and the withered remnants of its original elven caretakers. Twelve thousand years ago, Eldre'Thalas served as a wondrous bastion for Queen Azshara's favored sorcerers, the Shen'dralar. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, Prince Tortheldrin wove a magical barrier that shielded the city from ruin. Severed from their source of magic, the surviving Highborne trapped a colossal demon named Immol'thar beneath their sanctum, siphoning its fel essence to sustain their immortality and arcane powers for millennia.

Direforge Hill. Direforge Hill is a rugged highland in the northeastern Wetlands, southeast of Dun Modr and northeast of the Green Belt. The Dark Iron dwarf warlock Balgaras the Foul commands a hostile encampment on its slopes. Direforge Hill serves as a major Dark Iron campsite in the northeastern Wetlands. Balgaras the Foul, a Dark Iron dwarf warlock, commands the hostile dwarves occupying the hill southeast of Dun Modr.

Dirge Quikcleave. Inside Gadgetzan's inn, Dirge Quikcleave holds court as a goblin culinary master and vendor. His inventive dishes are renowned across Azeroth, and seasoned chefs come to him to master artisan cooking. In dusty Gadgetzan, Dirge Quikcleave serves drinks and meat to travelers parched by the Tanaris sands. Though his kitchen is in a frontier tavern, he claims to be Azeroth's greatest living culinary artist. Cooking trainers in cities send their most promising students to him when ordinary lessons are spent. Dirge's demanding recipes call for unusual ingredients, from giant clam meat and eggs for his Clamlette creations to exotic beasts from distant shores.

name.esES: Fabulosas chuletillas de quimerok de Dirge
name.frFR: Pyro-côtelettes de chimaerok à la Dirge
name.zhCN: 迪尔格的超美味奇美拉肉片

text.enUS: Dirge's Kickin' Chimaerok Chops. Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan has finished working out his recipe. He still needs twenty Goblin Rocket Fuel and twenty Deeprock Salt from you, and he wants them fast so the meat you brought him does not spoil. Dirge Quikcleave sees to the spices himself, and the meat you brought him makes up the remainder of the dish. All he lacks is rocket fuel and deeprock salt, twenty of each. With those in his hands, the chicken will be ready to go back to Narain Soothfancy. Dirge urges you not to dawdle, because he does not want the meat going bad.
Dirt-Caked Pendant. In the Barrens, a captive orc gives up the Dirt-Caked Pendant he carried. The keepsake reaches Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar, where it is used to draw a succubus.

Disarming Colloid. Disarming Colloid is a specialized chemical agent formulated to counter the volatility of Seaforium explosive powder. Provided by the dwarf Ashlan Stonesmirk in the Wetlands, it serves as the crucial stabilizing component in a neutralizing mixture meant to prevent a catastrophic demolition of the Stonewrought Dam. When Ashlan Stonesmirk analyzed the unusual blasting powder left by Dark Iron sappers at the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan, he recognized it immediately by its distinct scent and fine silver crystals: Seaforium. While harmless when completely dry, Seaforium becomes immensely destructive upon contact with moisture, making it an existential threat to the waterlogged Stonewrought Dam. To halt this reaction before a detonation occurs, Stonesmirk provided a disarming colloid. When combined with three specific local reagents—lurker venom, crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and a crocolisk tear—this colloid effectively neutralizes the explosive properties of the Seaforium compound.

Disarming Mixture. Disarming Mixture is a specialized chemical concoction prepared by Chief Engineer Hinderweir at the Stonewrought Dam. Created to neutralize volatile Seaforium explosives, it is used to prevent Dark Iron saboteurs from destroying the massive dwarven structure holding back the waters of Loch Modan. When Dark Iron saboteurs planted a heavy Seaforium charge beneath the foundation of the Stonewrought Dam, standard methods of defusal were far too risky. Lacking immediate Mountaineer support, Chief Engineer Hinderweir combined the Disarming Mixture from ingredients named by the explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk to rapidly neutralize the underwater explosive. When stirred directly into the planted powder keg, the solution neutralizes the reactive compounds, reducing a catastrophic explosion to a harmless, fizzling ruin.

Discipline. Discipline is a task issued by Executor Zygand in Tirisfal Glades. Unimpressed by the competence of the local Deathguard garrison, Zygand commissions outside adventurers to administer physical punishment to slackening undead sentries. The Deathguard form the military spine of the Forsaken across Lordaeron, but freedom from the Lich King's iron will brings its own complications: apathy, fatigue, and negligence. Taskmasters like Executor Zygand have little patience for slackening discipline, especially with threats from the Scarlet Crusade and Scourge prowling Tirisfal's borders. To keep the troops sharp, officers rely on blunt instruments and aggressive oversight to maintain military readiness.

Discover Rolf's Fate. In eastern Elwynn, two Stormwind guards are missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks lead toward a murloc village, where the search for Rolf continues. Guard Thomas sent patrols around eastern Elwynn Forest as threats grew, but Malakai and Rolf vanished near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints pressed into the mud lead east along the water's edge, straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

name.esES: Acabar con los ataques de los Crines de Acero
name.frFR: La défense du poste de Guet-Lointain

text.enUS: Disrupt the Attacks. Thork needs the Crossroads defended as Razormane quilboar cut its supply roads. Their ambushes have halted caravans from Durotar, and the outpost is running short on food and gear. You strike at the quilboar while scouts search for the one directing their warband. The Crossroads guards a key junction for Horde traffic through central Kalimdor. Freight wagons and caravans bring food, iron, and equipment west from Durotar, and the outpost depends on those supplies. Razormane ambushes along the northeast trails have stopped the deliveries. Stores are running low, and Thork cannot wait for peaceful talks.

Distracting Jarven. Down in the cellar of Thunderbrew Distillery, guard Jarven Thunderbrew finds himself surrounded by barrels he is forbidden to touch. Craving a taste of the family craft, he asks a passing adventurer for a mug of Thunder Ale to help sharpen his wits on duty. Jarven Thunderbrew is tasked with keeping watch over the deep stores of Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Despite being surrounded by the finest stout in Dun Morogh, he works under strict family orders not to dip into the stock while on guard. The temptation proves too much, prompting him to enlist passing travelers to fetch him a pint of potent Thunder Ale from the taps upstairs.

Divine Retribution. Kalaran Windblade asks you to hear his tale in Searing Gorge. His father is dead at the hands of what lurks in the cauldron, and the Stormwind magistrate would not listen. Kalaran seeks vengeance and wants an adventurer to act for him. Kalaran says the filth in the cauldron killed his father. He pleaded with the Stormwind magistrate for help, but the pleas fell on deaf ears. Stormwind, he says, would rather not admit this part of the world exists, let alone send soldiers to see justice done here.

Divined Scroll. The Divined Scroll is an enchanted parchment used by the night elves of Silverwind Refuge to unmask the source of Ashenvale's disturbed waters. By channeling the residual magic within intact water elemental bracers, the scroll reveals the identity of the rogue spellcaster summoning them. The tainted waters of Mystral Lake have long troubled the Sentinels guarding Ashenvale. To pinpoint who is manipulating the water elementals infesting the lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike provides travelers with an uncharged divining scroll. By gathering intact bracers directly from the slain elementals and using them as an arcane reagent, the latent bindings within the metal bleed into the parchment. The resulting Divined Scroll exposes the magical signature of the rogue wizard behind the infestation.

Divining Scroll. The Divining Scroll is an enchanted parchment provided by Sentinel Velene Starstrike at Silverwind Refuge. Its magic allows investigators to trace the magical signature of the unnatural water elementals infesting Ashenvale back to their creator. When corrupt water elementals began rising from the pristine pools of Ashenvale, the Sentinels knew the disturbance was not a natural emergence. Sentinel Velene Starstrike acquired this divination scroll to identify the person responsible. By channeling the scroll's magic through intact elemental bracers as a focusing reagent, the user extracts the summoner's signature, transforming the blank parchment into a Divined Scroll that names the guilty party.

Doan Karhan. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan studies the Burning Legion’s demonic artifacts. A human scholar and practitioner of the dark arts, he lives alone to pursue his research, especially into the enigmatic Orb of Soran'ruk. Doan Karhan keeps a solitary camp in the southern Barrens, far from the Alliance’s civilized bastions. He withdrew into the wilderness to study dangerous demonic relics without disturbance. He knows much about powerful fel vessels, possesses the Orb of Zargain, and is absorbed by the legendary Orb of Soran'ruk. Warlocks seeking knowledge of artifact crafting and dark rituals often come to him.

Doctor Gregory Victor. Doctor Gregory Victor is a Forsaken surgeon stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Renowned as the premier trauma physician within the Horde, he evaluates aspiring medics seeking to master advanced triage and battlefield first aid. His cold, clinical efficiency keeps frontline warriors stitched together amidst bitter regional conflicts. While many view Forsaken apothecaries with suspicion, Doctor Gregory Victor serves the Horde through practical battlefield surgery rather than blighted alchemy. Stationed deep within the contested Arathi Highlands at Hammerfall, he operates on soldiers battered by Syndicate brigands, Boulderfist ogres, and Alliance forces. His station doubles as the primary proving ground for Horde field medics, demanding ruthless efficiency and prioritizing critical patients under intense pressure.

Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen. Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen serves as the trauma surgeon and chief physician of Alliance Trauma in Theramore Isle. Stationed within Foothold Citadel, he trains the island's healers and evaluates medics who wish to master the highest tiers of field triage and bandage work. Located on the ground floor of Foothold Citadel in Theramore Isle, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen oversees the medical care of Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces and trains the outpost's frontline healers. Facing harsh conditions in Dustwallow Marsh, VanHowzen insists on rigorous field competence, personally putting experienced medics through an intense triage test to ensure they can prioritize critical wounds under severe pressure.

Dogran's Captivity. At Camp Taurajo, a warlock faces a vital trial in Horde training: rescue a captured orc warrior. With Ken'zigla's Draught, you must find battered Grunt Dogran in a quilboar camp and give him strength to escape. Grunt Logmar at Camp Taurajo will not risk Horde soldiers in a costly attack on the entrenched quilboar. Dogran's fate rests with you, an aspiring warlock armed only with Ken'zigla's Draught. Travel north through the brambles and hostile camps to find where the quilboar hold him captive.

Dogran's Pendant. Dogran's Pendant draws a succubus toward the warlocks of Orgrimmar. Dogran, a wounded orc, carries it while separated from his mate, Zankaja. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks turn the sorrow bound to it into a lure. Dogran's Pendant carries the sorrow of an orc separated from Zankaja. Captivity and crippling wounds have overshadowed their love. The warlocks of the Cleft of Shadow know that demons such as succubi prey on love, yearning, and vulnerability. They use the pendant's grief to draw a succubus across the Twisting Nether and into Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle.

Dolanaar. Dolanaar gathers travelers and guides beneath Teldrassil’s boughs. Southwest of Shadowglen, the town is the first place young night elves find after leaving their sheltered training grounds. Rangers, druids, and craftsmen help newcomers while strange afflictions spread through the World Tree. Dolanaar is a crossroads for travelers crossing Teldrassil. Beneath the canopy southwest of Shadowglen, its homes and platforms follow the traditional night elven way, woven into the woodland. Young night elves come here for their first broad training in trades, martial arts, and nature crafts. The road west leads toward Darnassus, the capital. From the surrounding boughs come reports of corrupted wildlife, aggressive furbolgs, and foul mosses, all brought before Dolanaar’s council.

Dolanaar Delivery. In Shadowglen, young travelers carry harvested herbs south to Dolanaar. Porthannius entrusts them with the bundle for Innkeeper Keldamyr. Fresh herbs from Aldrassil are bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius is occupied with matters among the druids of Shadowglen, so he entrusts the bundle to young travelers heading south along the road. They carry it to Innkeeper Keldamyr.

Dolanaar Delivery. Travelers leave Shadowglen with a parcel of herbs bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius, occupied with the druids, asks them to carry it south, marking their first venture beyond the sheltered glade. Porthannius asks travelers heading south from Shadowglen to carry a bundle of freshly harvested herbs along the forest path. He is occupied with pressing business alongside the druids tending the glade, and cannot leave to handle the errand himself. The bundle goes south as young adventurers prepare to leave the training grounds for the wider reaches of Teldrassil.

Doling Justice. With the sprite darters freed, Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal mean to take the fight to the Grimtotem clan. Jer'kai asks you to cut down Grimtotem Naturalists, Raiders and Shamans, then return to Jer'kai. This follows Freedom for All Creatures. After Freedom for All Creatures, Jer'kai Moonweaver tells you that Kindal and Jer'kai will now strike back at the Grimtotem. Together they can thin out some of the tauren without much risk to themselves, but they would welcome your help. You have seen the camp below, and there are more to the east. Use your own tactics against Grimtotem Naturalists, Raiders and Shamans, then meet back where Jer'kai waits.

Doling Justice. Out in the wilderness, Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal have little to give in thanks, so Jer'kai hands you a signet ring. It is yours to carry to High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where it will tell her that the two of them are well and lend weight to your story. This follows Doling Justice. Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal cannot offer much out in the wilds of Feralas, but they do not want you to feel unappreciated. Jer'kai hands over a signet ring and points you toward Darnassus, where High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind waits in the Temple of the Moon. The ring will show her that the pair are well, and it backs up the tale you will tell.

Donova Snowden. Donova Snowden is an intrepid dwarven researcher encamped alongside the thermal waters near Frostfire Hot Springs in Winterspring. Despite the bitter cold and hostile wildlife, she studies the strange thermal activity of the region and monitors the increasingly corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. While most travelers stick to the safety of Everlook, Donova Snowden has chosen to camp in the freezing wilderness near the Frostfire Hot Springs. She spends her days investigating the curious geothermic anomalies bubbling up through the permafrost, as well as the dark influences encroaching upon Winterspring's native wildlife. Practical and determined, she enlists passing adventurers of both the Alliance and the Horde to gather samples and help curb local threats.

Donyal Tovald. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s historical works. Under an initiative sponsored by young King Anduin Wrynn, he preserves and copies books for wider public use. Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s collection in Stormwind Keep. The library holds historical accounts, scrolls, and scholarly volumes, chiefly for the nobility and royal court. Young King Anduin Wrynn has sponsored an effort to make that knowledge more accessible to ordinary citizens. Tovald preserves and copies the texts, helping keep the Alliance’s lessons and triumphs recorded amid the kingdom’s political troubles.

Doom Weed. Doom Weed is a task given by Junior Apothecary Holland in Brill to gather noxious flora sprouting near Tirisfal's northern mass graves. Holland recruits passing adventurers after becoming frustrated with the clumsy harvesting efforts of the abomination Gordo. Junior Apothecary Holland conducts research on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society from the settlement of Brill. Seeking to advance his experiments, he requires quantities of doom weed, a vile plant that infests the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades. Finding Gordo incapable of discerning the proper reagents, Holland turns to sharper hands to salvage his harvest.

name.frFR: Le Refuge des saisons de Dor'danil

text.enUS: Dor'Danil Barrow Den. Dor'Danil Barrow Den is an ancient night elven sanctuary carved into the earth of central Ashenvale, south of Splintertree Post. Once a tranquil resting place for slumbering druids commune with the Emerald Dream, it has fallen into horror following Forsaken meddling that severed the dreamers' spirits from their bodies. Barrow dens across Kalimdor are revered sanctuaries where night elven druids historically slept for centuries, roaming the Emerald Dream while their mortal frames remained protected underground. When the Horde pushed into Ashenvale, Dor'Danil fell deep behind enemy lines. The orcs largely ignored the comatose elves, but the newly allied Forsaken saw an opportunity. Forsaken operatives infiltrated the depths and began gruesome experiments designed to sever the sleeping druids from their spirits, fracturing their minds and driving them hopelessly insane. The darkened hollows now crawl with sinister Forsaken assassins and the furious, torment-maddened spirits of druids who can no longer return to their bodies.

Doras. Above Orgrimmar, Doras directs the Horde's wind riders across Kalimdor. He oversees the capital's wyverns, sending couriers, scouts, and travelers on their way. Doras tends the wind riders on a wooden platform above the Valley of Strength. The Horde settled in Durotar, and these clever, leathery-winged beasts became its chief means of communication and travel across Kalimdor. Doras pairs resting mounts with riders and sees that important messages and reinforcements reach distant outposts. Their routes reach the Crossroads, Thunder Bluff, and settlements deep in Ashenvale or Dustwallow Marsh.

name.esES: Doras, maestro de jinetes del viento
name.frFR: Doras, le maître des coursiers du vent
name.zhCN: 双足飞龙管理员多拉斯

text.enUS: Doras the Wind Rider Master. Innkeeper Gryshka needs a courier to carry her thanks to Zargh at the Crossroads. She sends travelers to Doras the Wind Rider Master at Orgrimmar's skytower to arrange the flight back to the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka sends thanks to Zargh after a shipment of meat arrives safely from the Barrens hunting grounds. With no time to travel through Durotar herself, she trusts the established aerial courier network linking major Horde settlements to carry her letter back across the frontier.

Doren. Lieutenant Doren commands the Rebel Camp nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Once an officer under Colonel Kurzen, Doren led a mutiny after his superior and fellow expeditionaries descended into madness. Now, he directs a guerrilla resistance determined to uncover the source of the affliction and eliminate Kurzen. Lieutenant Doren initially deployed to Stranglethorn Vale under the banner of Stormwind and the command of Colonel Kurzen. The expedition was meant to establish a foothold in the wild southern jungle, but it quickly soured as Kurzen and his inner circle succumbed to an erratic, violent insanity. Refusing to abandon their sanity or their honor, Doren and a cadre of loyalists broke rank. They fled north and carved out the Rebel Camp along the road, choosing defection over servitude to a madman.

Dormitory. The Dormitory is a residential sector within the fallen technological capital of Gnomeregan. Once providing living quarters for countless gnome citizens, it now lies choked with radioactive fallout and crawls with savage, irradiated troggs. Situated just past the decontamination chambers of the Clean Zone, the Dormitory formerly housed the inventors, laborers, and families of Gnomeregan. When High Tinker Mekkatorque initiated the emergency radiation venting to combat the invading trogg horde, this densely populated sector became a trap. Today, its communal halls and living units are completely abandoned by gnomish life, occupied instead by mutated troggs that thrive in the radioactive miasma. Travelers descending toward the lower levels of the city must fight through this tragic reminder of the catastrophe to reach the lower Hall of Gears.

Dorn Plainstalker. Dorn Plainstalker is a solitary tauren elder residing in the Weathered Nook overlooking the canyons of Thousand Needles. He serves as an overseer of traditional rite of passage trials, challenging Horde adventurers to prove their character and fortitude. Through trials of faith, endurance, strength, and lore, he tests whether travelers are worthy servants of the Earth Mother and their people. Secluded in a shallow cave high atop the canyon ridges of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker lives apart from the bustle of Freewind Post. Reaching his mountain redoubt requires winding along the sheer northern cliffs overlooking the towering mesas below. From this quiet vantage point, Dorn maintains ancient customs and judges those who seek guidance in the harsh southern barrens.

name.esES: A lo largo de la costa

text.enUS: Down the Coast. Down the Coast is an Alliance task given by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle in Southshore. Deeply unhappy with his frontier transfer from Stormwind, the guard lieutenant prefers drinking ale to patrolling and hires adventurers to clear out the Torn Fin murlocs encroaching along the Western Strand. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle was reassigned from the polished stone streets of the Stormwind city guard to the remote, salty port of Southshore. Finding the town dreary and its fishy harbor odor unbearable, Orinelle spends his days nursing drinks at the local inn rather than patrolling the frontlines. When ordered by Marshal Redpath to protect Southshore from the surrounding dangers, Orinelle chooses to subcontract his duties to passing sellswords instead.

Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton says your deeds against the undead in Desolace are only a start, because the plague's real danger is in Lordaeron. He gives you a letter of commendation bearing his seal for Raleigh the Devout in Southshore. Anton speaks proudly of the Scarlet Crusade's bastions of cleansing in Lordaeron. The Crusade claims strongholds all the way between Hearthglen and Tirisfal Glades. Anton says your work against the undead in Desolace has proven you, yet the plague's real danger is in Lordaeron.

Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton of the Scarlet Crusade, at Nijel's Point, says his order is at war with the Scourge, an evil that corrupts the people and infects the land. He asks you to prove your allegiance by destroying thirty undead ravagers in the Valley of Bones. Brother Anton speaks bluntly. He says the Scourge must be halted before it swallows the land and pulls the world into darkness, and the Scarlet Crusade has pledged itself to that fight. If you are with them, he wants your courage and allegiance shown by destroying thirty undead ravagers. They are found south of Anton, in the Valley of Bones. Succeed, and the Crusade will welcome you.

Downstream. Downstream is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest tasked by Ormin Pelford at Eastvale Logging Camp. After Ormin's wagon accidentally overturns into the river, adventurers are asked to brave murlocs and wolves downstream to recover waterlogged timber supplies. While transporting a shipment of gear back from a local trading post, laborer Ormin Pelford suffered a mishap when his wagon tipped over along the waterway near Eastvale Logging Camp. The cargo tumbled into the current and was quickly swept downstream before he could secure it. Without these vital woodworking tools, the loggers face delays in their timber operations.

Draconic for Dummies. Narain Soothfancy remembers a book he stowed somewhere safe. To reach it you look for his crashed gyrocopter on Land's End Beach, then swim south from there to an island in the South Seas. This follows Translating the Ledger. Narain Soothfancy says the book is bound to come in handy, and that he hid it where nobody could hope to find it. He needed a gyrocopter to get there the first time and crashed it on the beach on the way back. That crash, he says, gave him his super-gnomish psychic powers. The wreck lies somewhere along Land's End Beach, and from there you swim south. Narain is sure you will recognise the place at a glance. The island where the book lies buried is out in the South Seas.

Draenethyst Crystals. Magtoor, at the Harborage, asks for six draenethyst crystals, sacred to Magtoor's people and stolen by the lost ones of the Fallow Sanctuary. Without them, Magtoor's people fear they too may lose their way. The lost ones of the Fallow Sanctuary look as Magtoor's people do, but the rigors of the journey to Azeroth drove them mad. Once brethren, they now dwell in the Sanctuary, to the east, and they seize or kill anyone who strays close. They have also stolen something sacred: draenethyst crystals.

Drag. In Orgrimmar, the Drag links the Valley of Strength, Valley of Honor and Valley of Wisdom. Crafters and traders line its shaded red-rock canyon, where the descent to the Cleft of Shadow also lies. The Drag runs between Orgrimmar’s red canyon walls, where crafters and traders fill the Horde capital’s streets. Unlike the Valley of Strength, with its military musters and commands, the Drag is where daily city life unfolds. High cliffs and hides shade the street, where tanning vats, alchemical cauldrons and tinkers’ gears fill the air with their sounds and smells. Craftsmen gather to practice their trades and teach aspiring adventurers. Their work ranges from leatherworking and tailoring to the goblin workshops of Nogg’s Machine Shop.

Dragonmaw Gates. The Dragonmaw Gates are a series of imposing fortifications along the mountain road leading up from the eastern Wetlands. Built to guard the steep ascent to the mountain fortress of Grim Batol, these heavy barricades bar entry into the cursed heights of the dwarven ruins. Carved into the rugged peaks bordering the eastern Wetlands, the Dragonmaw Gates seal the winding road that climbs into the mountains toward Grim Batol. Named after the Dragonmaw clan of orcs who held the dwarven mountain city during the Second War, these defensive barriers remain deeply fortified checkpoints. Anyone attempting to ascend toward the heights must contend with the lingering perils of the pass, where powerful drakes and grim reminders of the clan's dark history still cast a long shadow.

Dragonmaw Shinbones. Dragonmaw Shinbones is a Horde warrior quest directed by the armorer Velora Nitely in the Undercity. To craft the resilient Brutal Legguards, warriors are dispatched into the southern Wetlands to harvest exceptionally thick shinbones from the hostile Dragonmaw orcs. Forging armor fit for a seasoned frontline warrior demands unorthodox materials. When tasked with fashioning Brutal Legguards, the Forsaken armorer Velora Nitely specifies a structural brace constructed from thick, resilient bone. Rather than utilizing common beasts, she directs aspiring warriors toward the Dragonmaw orcs of the Wetlands, whose dense skeletal builds provide the necessary resilience to withstand heavy blows in combat.

text.enUS: Dragonmaw War Banner. Dragonmaw War Banners are rallying standards carried by the Dragonmaw orcs entrenched in the Wetlands. Stamped with the iconography of their clan, they serve as proof of battle for the dwarven defenders of Menethil Harbor seeking to quell the rising orcish threat. Following the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan was shattered after losing control of their enslaved red dragons. The enraged drakes turned on their captors, driving the survivors out of Grim Batol and into the eastern hills. In recent times, the remaining orcs have begun gathering strength once more under Chieftain Nek'rosh, raising their war banners over encampments northeast of Menethil Harbor. These crude, imposing standards represent both their lingering defiance and a direct menace to the marshland settlements.

Dragonmaw clan. The Dragonmaw clan is an infamous orcish faction notorious for subduing and riding red dragons during the Second War. Guided by dark artifacts and foul magic, they imprisoned the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza beneath the cursed halls of Grim Batol until her liberation shattered their dominion. Today, their scattered remnants lurk in the wetlands and mountains of Khaz Modan, remaining hostile to both the Alliance and Thrall's New Horde. The Dragonmaw clan hailed from Draenor and crossed the Dark Portal with the Old Horde. On Azeroth, they turned their talents to subjugating its winged terrors.

Dragonmurk. Dragonmurk is a sprawling, hazardous tract of southern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with black dragonspawn and hatchlings. Flanked by ancient ogre ruins and scorched caverns, it serves as the hostile outer perimeter for the brood of Onyxia. Spanning the southern interior of Dustwallow Marsh, the Dragonmurk marks the threshold where damp wetlands give way to the dominion of the black dragonflight. The waterways and thick mud here crawl with black wyrmkins, dragonspawn, and ravenous whelps. The surrounding landscape has suffered deeply from their presence; adjacent territories such as the ruined village of Stonemaul and the scorched cavern known as the Den of Flame have both fallen completely under the flight's territorial grip.

Dreadmaul Post. Dreadmaul Post is an entrenched ogre settlement situated in the scorched wastes of the Blasted Lands. Established by the Dreadmaul clan, this mound serves as a fortified redoubt near the Dark Portal where ogres have lingered since their arrival from Draenor. Travelers passing through the region must contend with these fierce brutes and the treacherous terrain surrounding their encampment. When the Horde surged through the Dark Portal in decades past, clans of ogres marched alongside them into Azeroth. The Dreadmaul clan chose to dig in near the gateway itself, raising crude stone mounds and earthworks across the red wastes of the Blasted Lands. Dreadmaul Post stands as one of their primary outposts, maintaining a firm grip over the badlands and clashing with wandering beasts and any travelers foolish enough to draw near their territory.

Dreadmaul Rock. Thal'trak Proudtusk's wife Sha'ni was sent over three weeks ago to look into strange rituals among the Firegut ogres, and nobody has heard from her platoon. Thal'trak cannot leave his post, so he asks you to go and learn what became of her. Sha'ni's orders took her to the Burning Steppes, to look into strange rituals among the Firegut ogres. That was more than three weeks ago. Goretooth says nothing has been heard from anyone in her platoon, and advises Thal'trak to put it behind him and keep to his duty. Thal'trak will not accept that, for it is his wife who is missing. He cannot leave his post, so he asks you to go there and search for her.

Dreadmaul Rock. Dreadmaul Rock is a towering crag and cave complex rising out of the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. It serves as the primary base of operations for the Firegut ogres, who make their home within its winding, subterranean mounds. Towering above the scorched plains of the Burning Steppes, Dreadmaul Rock is a massive stone formation carved out by a labyrinthine cave system. Though its name hints at a possible connection to the Dreadmaul ogres of the Blasted Lands, the rock is held firmly by the Firegut clan. These brutish ogres use the elevated paths, crags, and interior earthen mounds as a defended encampment, dominating the surrounding wasteland and menacing anyone attempting to traverse the northern slopes toward Blackrock Spire.

Dreadmist Den. In the northern Barrens, Burning Blade cultists keep their rites beneath Dreadmist Peak. Red haze fills the cavern they use as a shrine to demons. Dreadmist Den cuts into the jagged slopes of Dreadmist Peak, where Burning Blade cultists gather in a dark sanctuary. Thick crimson vapor hangs through its stone tunnels, dimming the cavern in red twilight. Away from the Horde's watch in the plains below, the cult performs demonic rites, guards its blasphemous relics, and plots to spread corruption across Kalimdor.

Dreadmist Peak. Red haze cloaks Dreadmist Peak, northwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens. The Burning Blade cult keeps a hidden refuge on its crags. Dreadmist Peak rises above the Barrens, its crags swallowed by a dense red haze that dims the sky. At the crest and in the hollows below, Burning Blade cultists shelter warlocks and toxicologists. They poison nearby water and scheme against the new powers claiming central Kalimdor.

Dreadmurk Shore. Dreadmurk Shore encompasses the foggy coastline and scattered islands of Dustwallow Marsh running north toward the Barrens. Dominated by aggressive Mirefin murlocs and sea beasts, these treacherous waters have recently become the hiding ground for shipwrecked Defias Brotherhood outlaws. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Dustwallow Marsh between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold, Dreadmurk Shore is a dismal expanse of muddy shoals, tide pools, and misty islands. The coast is overrun by the Mirefin tribe, a territorial clan of murlocs that aggressively attacks any travelers nearing their coastal villages. Sea turtles and aquatic predators prowl the shallows, making the shoreline dangerous to navigate even without factoring in the surrounding swamplands.

Dream Bough. Dream Bough is a colossal Great Tree nestled on an island in the center of Jademir Lake in northern Feralas. The ancient tree shelters a mysterious gateway connecting Azeroth directly to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons loyally watch over the sanctuary, keeping unwanted intruders away from its verdant boughs. Rising high above the canopy of northern Feralas, the Dream Bough stands as the largest tree in the region. Situated in the tranquil waters of Jademir Lake, the towering sentinel houses a natural portal carved into its trunk, providing a direct threshold into the untamed Emerald Dream.
