text.enUS: Dream Dust in the Swamp. Krazek of Booty Bay says that learning about Nazz is quite a favor. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to bring 10 specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, for Krazek's snuff pouch. Bring it back and Krazek will give you the information you seek. Krazek tells you that learning about Nazz is a considerable favor, and that you have already come a long way from the Shimmering Flats for it. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to gather something. The choice falls on ten specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, which Krazek would love for a snuff pouch. Once you return with it, the information is yours.

Dreamer's Rock. Dreamer's Rock is a secluded natural sanctuary tucked deep within the Wailing Caverns past the Screaming Gully. Here lies the sleeping night elf druid Naralex, whose noble effort to revive the Barrens has instead birthed a living nightmare. It serves as both a sacred barrow chamber and the epicenter of the corruption mutating the surrounding subterranean ecosystem. Located in the heart of the Wailing Caverns, Dreamer's Rock functions much like an improvised barrow den. Here, the night elf druid Naralex entered a deep trance to tap the underground springs and channel the Emerald Dream into the arid soil of the Barrens. Instead of bringing life, his connection was seized by dark forces. The nightmare twisting his thoughts now spills physically into this chamber, twisting the local wildlife, turning his followers into the venomous Druids of the Fang, and manifesting terrifying aberrations into the waking world.
Dried Seeds. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem gives travelers Dried Seeds to test the life-giving power beneath the Barrens' waters.

Driftwood. After The Lost Caravan, Watcher Biggs still has a wagon to mend before reaching Nethergarde. Biggs needs strong, dry wood, and sends you east to the coast to search for driftwood dried by the sun. Watcher Biggs says you are owed great thanks, and asks for your help once more. If Biggs is ever to reach Nethergarde, the wagon must be fixed, and that takes strong, dry wood. Wood from the swamp's trees is spongy and tangled, and will not do.

Drowned Reef. The Drowned Reef is a treacherous stretch of coastal waters off the southern cliffs of the Arathi Highlands. Beneath the waves lie ancient sunken ruins, claimed by hostile Daggerspine naga who appear able to control the bay's tides, endangering passing vessels. Just outside the hidden entrance to Faldir's Cove, the Drowned Reef forms a watery graveyard for navigators. Shattered ships, including the Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine, lie submerged beneath the waves. Daggerspine naga led by Prince Nazjak inhabit the reef and appear able to control the bay's tides, dooming crews seeking refuge in the cove.

Drowned Sacellum. The Drowned Sacellum is a submerged elven shrine lying just inside the entrance of Blackfathom Deeps. Submerged beneath brackish saltwater and draped in cavernous roots, its shattered masonry is now overrun by murlocs and makrura. Stepping through the threshold of Blackfathom Deeps immediately brings explorers into the Drowned Sacellum. Once a tranquil subterranean chapel dedicated to Elune, the sacellum has long collapsed into the sea-swept abyss beneath Ashenvale's coast. Saltwater pools swallow ancient marble flagstones overgrown with starfish, while massive tree roots dangle from the cavern ceiling above. Dark, flickering wisps provide the only dim light in the gloom, illuminating a ruined pathway of stones that adventurers must carefully navigate to reach the Pool of Ask'ar deeper within the temple complex.

Drowned Sorrows. Captain Steelgut sits mourning at Faldir's Cove after losing the beloved Maiden's Folly. Steelgut asks you to go after the Daggerspine naga who slaughtered the survivors of the wreck. Captain Steelgut sits by the fire at Faldir's Cove, wishing for a watery grave instead. The crew fought hard to save the beautiful Maiden's Folly, but the sea sank it, with water rushing in all at once. O'Breen reached shore safely, yet naga killed the survivors. Steelgut wants Daggerspine raiders and sorceresses dead.

Druid. Druids are guardians of the natural world who draw power directly from the wild spirits, the celestial bodies, and the Emerald Dream. Master shapeshifters, they adopt the forms of primal beasts to protect the land or mend grievous wounds. Practiced primarily by the night elves, newly revived among the tauren and kept alive by the Skyborne, druids place the preservation of nature above all mortal allegiance. Druidism is far more than a martial art; it is an ancient way of life rooted in deep communion with nature and the demigod Cenarius. Druids wield raw natural energies, commanding roots to entangle their foes, directing the celestial brilliance of the moon and stars, and invoking restorative flora to knit bone and flesh. Their duty is to preserve the cosmic balance and protect the unfettered wild from exploitation and corruption.

Druid of the Claw. Oben Rageclaw’s spirit waits in the barrows beneath Teldrassil, unable to rest. The Gnarlpine furbolgs have bound his body with a dark enchantment, and you can break that bond by destroying his soulless shell. Oben Rageclaw was resting in the barrows beneath Teldrassil when the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs laid a voodoo enchantment over his sleeping body. The magic tore his spirit from his mortal flesh and trapped it in the Emerald Dream. Now his spirit lingers nearby, unable to rest or reclaim his body.

Druids of the Fang. The Druids of the Fang are a sinister sect entrenched deep within the labyrinthine Wailing Caverns. Severing all ties to the Cenarion Circle, these rogue night elves have adopted serpent-like forms under the command of the self-proclaimed Lord Serpentis. While the true origin of their dark communion remains a mystery to outside observers, they relentlessly pursue their grand design: to seize the subterranean waters and remake the Barrens into their own twisted paradise. The Barrens was not always an arid wasteland, and Naralex sought to return it to the lush, verdant sanctuary it once was. Naralex led a dedicated order of young druids into the subterranean depths of the Wailing Caverns, tapping into the natural underground fissures and subterranean springs. By entering an induced slumber, Naralex hoped to channel the living energies of the Emerald Dream into the waterways, nursing the scorched savannah above back to vibrant life.

Drum Fel. Drum Fel is an orc commander stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Alongside his wife, Korin, he directs military efforts to secure the refuge against encroaching trolls, ogres, and human remnants. His strategic push is vital to carving out a lasting foothold for the Horde in Arathi. Situated within the fortified refuge of Hammerfall, Drum Fel oversees the defense and territorial expansion of the Horde in Arathi. Surrounded by rival factions, he coordinates military strikes against the Witherbark forest trolls and the Boulderfist ogre clan holding Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall. Drum recognizes that Hammerfall cannot merely survive through isolation; it must break its neighbors' strength to thrive. To that end, he regularly directs veteran champions into hostile territory to disrupt regional threats before they can mount an assault on the Horde encampment.

Drusilla La Salle. Outside Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle teaches warlocks in the graveyard. The human trainer works beyond the Holy Order’s reach, guiding new spellcasters in shadow and summoning. When forbidden knowledge leaves the abbey, she moves to claim it. Drusilla La Salle teaches novice warlocks among the headstones outside Northshire Abbey. Paladins and priests practice beneath the abbey’s stained glass, while warlocks keep to society’s edges because demonology and fel magic are taboo in Stormwind. Recruits receive tainted correspondence before Drusilla shows them how to wield shadow power without drawing the abbey authorities’ immediate anger.

Dry Hills. Witchwing harpies menace the Dry Hills, where greener slopes rise above the Barrens. The Dry Hills grow greener than the dry plains below, on the Barrens' northwestern edge beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. Travelers find little safety among the bluffs. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing harpies from their roosts along the crags. Their raiding parties swoop down on supply caravans along the northern Gold Road. Abandoned orcish fortifications and derelict siege engines lie rotting in the brush.

Dry Times. Dry Times is a task given by Barkeep Daniels of Lakeshire to resupply the town inn with liquor during an ongoing siege. With the Blackrock orc invasion severing trade routes, Daniels relies on adventurous couriers to fetch specialty alcohol from across Stormwind's territories. Lakeshire sits on the front line of an aggressive push by the Blackrock clan orcs descending from Stonewatch Keep. With regular supply lines choked and the roads unsafe, the town's local innkeeper, Barkeep Daniels, faces an imminent crisis of empty casks. To keep spirits high among frightened villagers and beleaguered town guards, he turns to outside travelers to bypass the road blockades and restock his shelves.

Drygulch Ravine. Dustwind harpies hold Drygulch Ravine, where they menace nearby supply caravans. The gorge lies among eastern Durotar's rocky bluffs, reached by a cave passage from Razorwind Canyon or a perilous drop from above. In the crags east of Orgrimmar, Drygulch Ravine forms a sheltered depression and a lawless pocket of Durotar. A cramped natural tunnel from Razorwind Canyon is its only ground-level route. Dustwind harpies roost along the steep cliffs, where they nest their broods and stockpile goods stolen from Horde supply trains on the regional trails.

Drywhisker Gorge. Drywhisker Gorge is a rugged cleft in the eastern mountains of the Arathi Highlands, situated northeast of the Horde outpost of Hammerfall. The gorge and its inner cavern are held by a hostile clan of kobolds, who fiercely guard rich mineral deposits and ancient elemental relics buried deep underground. Tucked away in the mountainous folds east of Hammerfall, Drywhisker Gorge serves as the primary redoubt of the Drywhisker clan of kobolds. While kobolds are often dismissed as simple mine pests, the Drywhiskers in Arathi are heavily entrenched. They guard their subterranean passages with fierce territorial tenacity, working veins of rare Lesser Bloodstone Ore and defending the deep recesses of the earth. Their proximity makes them a persistent nuisance to the nearby orcs of Hammerfall.

Duke Hydraxis. Duke Hydraxis is a noble water elemental commanding the Hydraxian Waterlords from a remote, wave-battered islet off the coast of Azshara. Pledged to Neptulon the Tidehunter, he rallies mortal adventurers to strike against his ancient elemental rivals, particularly Ragnaros the Firelord. Perched on a solitary rock northeast of the Ravencrest Monument in Azshara, Duke Hydraxis serves as the primary emissary of the Hydraxian Waterlords. While most elementals bound to Azeroth are hostile and chaotic, Hydraxis acts with measured purpose. As a devoted vassal of Neptulon the Tidehunter, he considers water the purest and most essential of the primal forces. He watches the rising turmoil across Azeroth with cold scrutiny, seeking champions capable of shifting the balance of elemental warfare.

Dun Algaz. Dun Algaz is the fortified mountain pass and network of tunnels connecting Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Historically contested during the Second War, this vital trade artery has recently fallen under siege by Dragonmaw orcs, cutting off easy transit between Ironforge's territories and Menethil Harbor. Dun Algaz predates the War of the Three Hammers, originally serving as the passage the Wildhammer clan used to migrate north after being driven out of Ironforge. Carved deep into the jagged peaks separating Loch Modan and the Wetlands, the pass consists of sweeping stone tunnels, bastions, and watchposts. Its strategic value cannot be overstated: whoever holds Dun Algaz commands the only overland highway linking the dwarven heartlands to the western sea at Menethil Harbor.

Dun Garok. Dun Garok is a fortified dwarven mountain bastion situated in the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the outpost's stalwart garrison defends regional Alliance interests and nearby operations like the Azurelode Mine against hostile encroachment. To the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, this entrenched dwarven stronghold stands as a constant military threat bordering their domain. Carved into the craggy southeastern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills, Dun Garok stands as a heavily defended redoubt of Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the dwarves here maintain a critical defensive perimeter, shielding human settlements in Hillsbrad and securing vital operations at the Azurelode Mine. Their sturdy stone architecture and deep entrenchments provide the Alliance with an anchor against nearby threats.

Dun Mandarr. Dun Mandarr is an abandoned dwarven camp situated before an icy cavern in south-eastern Winterspring. Established by the dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper, the site now sits in ruins after its occupants fled an onslaught of enraged local moonkin. Bearing the traditional dwarven prefix 'Dun', Dun Mandarr was established by the explorer Jaron Stoneshaper as a base of operations in the frozen reaches of southeastern Winterspring. Stoneshaper's curiosity proved his undoing when he uncovered a relic known as the Blue-Feathered Amulet. The artifact's disturbance provoked the fury of the native wildkin, who descended upon the encampment in an uncontrollable rage. Overwhelmed and driven out, the dwarves abandoned the camp entirely. Today, no friendly souls remain among the snowbanks; ferocious, territorial moonkin guard the cavern and prowl the broken shelters.

Dun Modr. Dun Modr is an ancient fortified dwarven town in northern Wetlands, guarding the southern approach to the Thandol Span. Once a critical fortress held and contested across multiple wars, it has recently fallen to a hostile force of Dark Iron dwarves. Situated at the northern edge of the Wetlands, Dun Modr commands the primary overland highway linking Khaz Modan with the northern human kingdoms. Because of this vital location, the stronghold has seen heavy bloodshed over the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde captured and entrenched themselves within the dwarven fortress, using it as a forward staging ground to launch raids and repel Alliance armies. Stromgarde warriors launched a brutal amphibious assault from Tol Barad to reclaim it, only for the Orcs to strike back in a bloody tug-of-war. Alliance forces led by Lord Anduin Lothar ultimately drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span, restoring dwarven custody over the bastion.

Dunemaul Compound. Dunemaul Compound serves as the central settlement and ogre mound for the Dunemaul clan in Tanaris. Tucked into the rocky ridges bordering the desert wastes, it houses the clan's brute enforcers and spellcasters. Carved into the rugged desert rock of western Tanaris, the Dunemaul Compound is the primary stronghold of the Dunemaul ogres. These hulking desert dwellers have adapted to the harsh arid climate, scratching out an existence through brute force and opportunism. The compound itself centers on an ogre mound and cave network. Though primitive, the clan fields a dangerous mix of warriors, enforcers, and twisted spellcasters practicing dark warlock and mage magics. For travelers journeying across the dunes, the settlement is a treacherous den of aggressive giants who violently reject uninvited guests.

Dungar Longdrink. At Stormwind's Trade District roost, Dungar Longdrink arranges swift gryphon transport for supplies bound to Westfall's embattled defenders. Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems have pushed Westfall close to breaking point. Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia are desperate for provisions. Lewis sent word to the capital, and armorer Osric Strang packed the requested equipment. Carrying military cargo on foot through bandit-ridden Elwynn and Westfall takes precious time. Stormwind's new aerial routes offer a vital link to the frontier.

Durnan Furcutter. Durnan Furcutter is a dwarven clothier and leather merchant operating out of Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Working inside Anvilmar, he equips freshly trained dwarven and gnomish adventurers with lightweight attire suited to withstand the biting mountain chills. Anvilmar serves as the first proving ground for young dwarves and exiled gnomes, and not every warrior steps forth clad in heavy iron. Durnan Furcutter caters to scouts, rogues, and spellcasters who need light, pliable layers to stay agile without succumbing to the bitter winds of Dun Morogh. Positioned right near the hearth of Anvilmar, he sells everyday tailoring and stitched leather, claiming his stock is the finest to be found in the entire valley.
