text.enUS: Durnan's Scalding Mornbrew. Durnan's Scalding Mornbrew is a freshly poured, piping-hot dwarven beverage intended for Durnan Furcutter in Coldridge Valley. Because the drink quickly loses its heat in the frigid mountain air, it must be rushed directly to Anvilmar before it goes cold. In the biting chill of Coldridge Valley, few comforts rival a mug of fresh mornbrew served piping hot. When a courier gets delayed delivering a round to Grelin Whitebeard, the fresh cup meant for Durnan Furcutter inside Anvilmar risks freezing over. Durnan specifically expects his brew scalding, leaving only a short window of a few minutes to carry the steaming mug up the snowy path into the mountain hall before it cools completely.

Durnholde Keep. Durnholde Keep is a shattered fortress situated east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once the nerve center of the Alliance's orc internment camps and the place where Warchief Thrall was raised as a captive gladiator, it now lies in ruin, occupied by outlaws of the Syndicate. Built by the Alliance, Durnholde served as the headquarters overseeing the southern internment camps following the Second War. Commanded by the ambitious and corrupt Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore, it functioned as both an administrative fortress and a gladiatorial arena. It was here that Blackmoore raised the orphaned infant Go'el, naming him Thrall and training him to fight for sport and profit. Aided by Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped captivity and later united the dispersed orc clans under the banner of the new Horde. Returning to Durnholde, Thrall laid siege to the fortress, slew Blackmoore, and called upon the earth spirits to shatter its walls.

Durotar Tiger Fur. Across the Echo Isles off Durotar's southeastern coast, tigers supply fur for the Darkspear, whose refugee population keeps growing. The trolls use the pelts for blankets, tents, and armor. In Sen'jin Village, the Darkspear must make scarce supplies last. They let the local tigers thrive until their growing needs call for a cull. Trolls cure the thick hides into goods their settlement needs, including protective armor and warm blankets for changing seasonal weather.

Duskbat Wing. A Duskbat Wing is a raw material harvested from the leather-winged bats flitting through the gloom around Deathknell. In the resource-starved Forsaken settlement, these leathery appendages are salvaged and repurposed by local tailors into sturdy makeshift armor for newly risen soldiers. When new undead claw their way from the soil of Deathknell, they emerge bearing little more than rags and brittle bones. Surrounded by the lingering Scourge mindless and hostile wildlife, the fledgling Forsaken must scrape together whatever protective gear they can find. Novice Elreth, assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis, collects Duskbat Wings alongside wolf paws to piece together and reinforce clothing and armor for freshly raised warriors before they are sent into the wilderness to fight.

Dusky Crab Cakes. Dusky Crab Cakes are a savory dish prepared by Chef Grual in Darkshire to satisfy the desperate hunger of Jitters. The local delicacy has a tangy flavor, and a famished Jitters considers it an exquisite meal.

Dusky Crab Cakes. Chef Grual of Darkshire's Scarlet Raven Tavern has a secret behind his famous Dusky Crab Cakes: they contain no crab at all. Tasked with aiding the famished and nervous Jitters, adventurers are sent to harvest spider legs from the deadly arachnids roaming northern Duskwood to prepare the town's beloved snack. Duskwood has long suffered from isolation, dark magic, and severed supply routes, forcing the locals of Darkshire to adapt their cuisine. Chef Grual, the resident cook at the Scarlet Raven Tavern, solved his meat shortages by inventing the Dusky Crab Cake. Despite the name suggesting seafood from distant shores, Grual readily admits that the dish's distinctively tangy flavor comes entirely from the gooey legs of local giant spiders.

Dust Devil Debris. Across Westfall, Dust Devils leave charged grit in their wake. Mages value this debris as a reagent for enchanting parchment and binding messaging spells into scrolls. Dust Devils sweep across Westfall’s plains as violent whirlwinds. When one is struck down, the living storm collapses into charged dust and grit called Dust Devil Debris. A faint trace of the elemental vortex remains in the residue. In Stormwind, arcane practitioners such as Collin Mauren prize it for specialized sorcery. Infused into enchanted ink and parchment, the grit helps a wizard bind an airy messaging spell to a scroll, carrying words across the kingdom.

Dust Plains. Gnoll packs hold the Dust Plains, Westfall’s dry southern frontier. The plains stretch toward the coast and eastern hills, where Klaven’s Tower overlooks the wastes. Across southern Westfall, the Dust Plains run from troubled farmland toward desolate wilderness. Feral gnolls have long claimed this arid ground, ambushing travelers and challenging anyone bound for the coast or nearby hills. Klaven’s Tower stands on the eastern boundary. The old mage tower is held by Klaven Mortwake, a Defias rogue, and offers no shelter from the gnolls prowling the surrounding wastes.

Dustbowl. The Dustbowl is a sprawling, arid expanse in the northwestern Badlands, lying between the Horde outpost of Kargath and the central Valley of Fangs. Swept by scouring desert winds, it is a harsh wilderness populated by scavengers, prowling beasts, and wandering elementals. It is also the site of Camp Wurg, making it a frequent crossing point for travelers braving the wasteland. Stretching across the northwest of the Badlands, the Dustbowl is characterized by dry gulches, cracked clay, and relentless winds that stir up choking plumes of grit. Despite the barren landscape, tough desert flora persists in the form of hardy cacti and scattered, gnarled trees. The open flatland presents constant danger to unguided wayfarers, who must contend with predatory coyotes, circling buzzards, and living rock elementals born of the rugged earth. Tucked within this scrubland lies Camp Wurg, providing a recognizable landmark amidst the otherwise desolate expanse.

Dustfire Valley. Dustfire Valley is a dry, windswept gulch nestled along the northern edge of the Searing Gorge. It serves as the scorched threshold leading directly to the fortified gate of Stonewrought Pass, which bars the mountain route into Loch Modan. Tucked away in northern Searing Gorge, Dustfire Valley is defined by choking ash, brittle rock, and barren canyon walls. Its most notable feature is the imposing, locked dwarven gateway sealing Stonewrought Pass. Because of these locked iron doors, direct travel north into the Valley of Kings and Loch Modan remains entirely barred to ordinary wanderers, leaving the valley an isolated cul-de-sac amidst the sulfurous wastes.

Dustwallow Bay. Dustwallow Bay is an inlet of the Great Sea tucked between the sodden coast of Dustwallow Marsh and the fortified port of Theramore Isle. Its brackish coastal shallows teem with marine life, treacherous shoals, and secluded coves just off the main maritime routes of eastern Kalimdor. Dustwallow Bay defines the coastal boundary where the stagnant, murky wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh meet the open waters of the Great Sea. Flanked to the east by Theramore Isle, the bay serves as an oceanic approach for vessels arriving at Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island haven. Despite heavy maritime traffic running to and from the docks, the surrounding coastline remains wild and hazardous, pocked with rocky outcrops, murloc encampments, and tucked-away inlets like Tidefury Cove.

Dustwind Cave. Burning Blade initiates train in Dustwind Cave, high above Razorwind Canyon northeast of Razor Hill. The cave is both a training ground and a covert refuge for the cult in Durotar. Dustwind Cave overlooks Razorwind Canyon, close to Razor Hill and a perilous threat to the town. The Burning Blade trains new recruits here beneath the notice of Horde authorities. Cultists teach initiates forbidden dark magic and demonology, preparing them to undermine the young orcish realm from within Durotar's borders.

Duthorian Rall. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall guides new holy warriors through their trials. The respected human knight of the Silver Hand is one of the Alliance's most influential paladins, overseeing their training and spiritual tests. He teaches charity, valor, and devotion as they prepare to defend Azeroth from the Scourge and threats within the kingdom. In the Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall upholds the traditions of the Knights of the Silver Hand. The kingdom is unsettled by internal strife, and King Varian Wrynn is missing. Duthorian carries the duty of teaching discipline to new initiates. Respected paladins in the field send promising recruits to him: Brother Wilhelm in Goldshire and Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, so they can begin their sacred trials.

Dwarf. Dwarves are a stout, resilient race carved from the living stone of ancient titan-forged earthen, now inhabiting the snow-capped mountain kingdoms of Khaz Modan and beyond. Known for their mastery of stonework, metallurgy, and devastating frontline combat, they stand as one of the Alliance's fiercest and most dependable pillars. Under the reign of King Magni Bronzebeard, their sprawling subterranean capital of Ironforge serves as the beating heart of dwarven society. Long ago, the subterranean titan-forged known as earthen awoke from an eons-long slumber within the vaults of Uldaman, transformed by the Curse of Flesh into beings of blood and bone. Taking the name dwarves, they reclaimed the high crags of Khaz Modan—named in honor of the titan Khaz'goroth—and carved the majestic subterranean stronghold of Ironforge beneath the peaks of Dun Morogh. Endowed with incredible natural fortitude, a sharp eye for stone and ore, and a penchant for roaring hearths and heady ale, dwarves approach craftsmanship and warfare with identical tenacity.

Dwarven Digging. Dwarven Digging is a quest in Mulgore given by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village. Concerned that dwarven excavations will enrage the native beasts and defile the sacred earth, Baine tasks young Horde defenders with sabotaging their efforts by confiscating and shattering their pickaxes. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have begun staking out a dig site in the rolling hills of Mulgore. The Explorer's League and its excavation crews seek titan relics and earthen secrets across Kalimdor, but their operations rarely respect indigenous lands or customs. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother to be revered, not stripped and hollowed for stones and metal.

Dwarven District. Dwarven craftsmen keep their furnaces and workshops working in Stormwind's northern quarter. The district brings a piece of Khaz Modan to the human capital, with the Deeprun Tram linking it to Ironforge. Dwarven artisans, smiths, and engineers make their home in Stormwind's northern quarter. Heavy stonework, smelting works, and craft shops recall Ironforge. At Potts' Plates, craftspeople from Khaz Modan find familiar company. On the district's eastern side, an open, arched tunnel leads to the Stormwind station of the Deeprun Tram, linking the human capital directly to Ironforge.

Dwarven Outfitters. Dwarven Outfitters is an introductory survival task in Coldridge Valley offered by Sten Stoutarm. In exchange for culling local wolves and gathering their tough meat for winter rations, fresh recruits are rewarded with sturdy gloves to ward off frostbite in Dun Morogh's biting cold. The high mountain pass of Coldridge Valley is brutally cold, and unprepared travelers quickly learn that standard kit is no match for the elements. Standing outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm offers a straightforward frontier bargain to new recruits: venture into the snowy drifts, hunt down the prowling wolves, and bring back cuts of tough meat to help supply the outpost. In return, he provides proper cold-weather gloves to ensure young adventurers keep all ten fingers.

Dwarven Tinder. Dwarven Tinder is a specially prepared flammable substance used by Alliance forces in the Wetlands. It was distributed to saboteurs tasked with incinerating the Dragonmaw clan's siege engines before they could be brought against Menethil Harbor. When Alliance scouts discovered that Chieftain Nek'rosh had constructed heavy catapults within the Dragonmaw encampment, Menethil Harbor faced an imminent crisis. Cut off from southern reinforcements by intense fighting in Dun Algaz, the defenders could not survive a prolonged siege. The solution was preemptive sabotage. Provided to volunteers advancing into orcish territory, Dwarven Tinder catches quickly from a struck spark, producing flames intense enough to consume reinforced wooden siege engines in minutes.

Eagan Peltskinner. Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner has work for recruits as timber wolves threaten the valley. The local furrier needs hunters to thin the packs and bring back pelts. Deputy Willem often sends recruits from the abbey to find Eagan Peltskinner, who works nearby on its grounds. Northshire Valley's orchards and fields lie beside wild woods where timber wolves prowl. Eagan wants newcomers to hunt the aggressive packs and gather pelts for his craft.

Ear of Balgaras. The Ear of Balgaras serves as grim proof of the death of Balgaras the Foul, a Dark Iron warlock who led the assault on Dun Modr. Recovered from the cowardly commander's corpse, it brings closure to the Ironforge mountaineers defending the northern Wetlands. Dun Modr fell into ruins when Dark Iron invaders sabotaged the Thandol Span and wiped out the local dwarven garrison. Their commander in the field was Balgaras the Foul, a scheming warlock who directed his troops from the shadows while shying away from personal combat. For Longbraid the Grim, the mountain king's officer stationed outside the ruined outpost, justice demanded tangible evidence of the ringleader's fall. Severing Balgaras's ear provides absolute verification that the warlock's reign of terror at the northern border has ended.

Earth Mother. The Earth Mother is the supreme, benevolent creator deity worshipped by the tauren, revered as the living embodiment and architect of Azeroth's land and elements. In tauren myth, she shaped the mountains, plains, and seasons and set the sun and moon in the sky as her watchful eyes. Her presence permeates everyday tauren culture, guiding their reverence for nature, duty to the elements, and hopes for the afterlife. Tauren creation myths tell that before day and night existed, the Earth Mother set about shaping Azeroth as a haven for her coming children. Scraping her nails across newly raised mountains sparked the world's first fires, while her hands carved rivers and ocean beds. Her laughter gave breath to the wind, and by lifting the primordial fogs into the sky, she brought the first rains, which coaxed grass, forests, and grain from the soil.

Earth Sapta. Earth Sapta is a replenishment ritual offered by Seer Ravenfeather in Camp Narache. Young shaman undertaking their initiation to commune with the spirits of the stone require this draught to open their inner sight. Should a novice lose or spill their prepared brew before finishing their rite, the seer prepares another to ensure their trial may continue. The path of the shaman begins with attuning the mortal senses to forces beyond physical sight. To perceive the elemental spirits of the land, an initiate must ingest a potent ritual brew known as a sapta. Infused with natural essences bound to the element of stone and soil, the Earth Sapta lifts the veil between the physical realm and the spiritual plane, allowing a novice to commune directly with the earth elementals of Mulgore.

Earth Sapta. In the Valley of Trials, an initiate who loses the Earth Sapta can ask Canaga Earthcaller for another. The replacement gives the young shaman a chance to commune with the spirits of the land, along with a warning to guard sacred draughts carefully. A misplaced Earth Sapta can interrupt an initiate's communion with the spirits of stone and soil. Prepared through specific rituals, the elemental brew thins the veil between the physical realm and the spirits. When an initiate loses or spills it while traveling through Durotar, Canaga Earthcaller prepares another in good faith, but warns the novice to guard sacred gifts with greater care.

Earthen Arise. Deep within Boulderslide Ravine, the shaman Mor'rogal discovers a slumbering Earthen named Goggeroc sealed inside a Resonite cask. Fearing the raw destructive power an ancient being of stone could unleash upon Kalimdor, he sends a champion to shatter the cask and strike Goggeroc down before the creature can recover its full strength. While investigating the vermin infestation in Boulderslide Ravine, scouts discovered a strange relic nestled among the kobolds: a Resonite cask radiating unearthly force. Mor'rogal, a tauren shaman stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, recognized the container for what it truly was—a prison and sanctuary housing Goggeroc, a dormant Earthen. These primordial creations of stone possess strength that outmatches mortal warriors, making the prospect of Goggeroc roaming free an existential threat to the region.

Eastern Strand. The Eastern Strand is a stretch of southern coastline in Hillsbrad Foothills, lying to the southeast toward the border of the Arathi Highlands. Once peaceful shores, the beaches and shallows have been overrun by hostile Daggerspine naga establishing a coastal beachhead. Running along the southeastern edge of Hillsbrad Foothills, the Eastern Strand complements the Western Strand across the bay. While the region is primarily known for human farming settlements and territorial clashes between Southshore and Tarren Mill, these sandy flats and tidelines are dominated entirely by the Daggerspine naga. Creeping out of the Great Sea, the serpent folk slither across the sandbars and dwell among the rocky outcrops, watching the mainland closely.

Eastmoon Ruins. The Eastmoon Ruins are an ancient troll archaeological site situated in eastern Tanaris, perched just west of the Gaping Chasm. Once built by the desert empires of old, the crumbling stone masonry is now occupied by Dunemaul ogres using the remnants as a desert encampment. Rising out of the blistering desert floor just west of the insect-infested Gaping Chasm, the Eastmoon Ruins preserve the crumbling architecture of ancient troll civilization. Decaying pillars, weathered stone plazas, and sun-bleached monuments hint at a time long before the sands swallowed this region. Rather than scholars or troll descendants tending the shrines, the site is firmly held by the Dunemaul ogres, who rely on the broken walls for shelter and vantage over nearby trade routes.

name.esES: Aserradero de la Vega del Este
name.frFR: Camp de bûcherons du Val d'est

text.enUS: Eastvale Logging Camp. At Eastvale Logging Camp, timber orders from Stormwind meet the dangers of Elwynn’s eastern woods. Wolves and bears drive lumberjacks from their work, while the camp keeps timber moving toward Stormwind and nearby settlements. Timber buyers across the Kingdom of Stormwind send orders to Eastvale Logging Camp, each with a strict deadline. Wolves and bears prowl the woods around the work sites, driving lumberjacks away and leaving cut timber behind. Supervisor Raelen directs the camp’s work, and travelers help drive off the beasts and recover the abandoned wood before deliveries fall behind schedule.

name.esES: Puerta de la Muralla del Este

text.enUS: Eastwall Gate. Eastwall Gate is a fortified side entrance set into the perimeter wall of the fallen city of Stratholme. Located in the northern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, it offers a direct secondary access point into Stratholme's interior ruins, bypassing the chaos of the city's main gates. While the grand main entrance of Stratholme opens directly onto King's Square, the Eastwall Gate pierces the city's eastern fortifications. Barred securely against intruders, this gateway leads straight into Elders' Square, close by the steps of Alonsus Chapel. For those venturing into the burning heart of the Scourge stronghold, bypassing the front barricades can mean the difference between a swift strike into the city's depths and a meatgrinder assault through the forward undead lines.

name.esES: Torre de la Muralla del Este

text.enUS: Eastwall Tower. Eastwall Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the Eastern Plaguelands near the eastern road. Sacked during the Third War when the Scourge swept across the kingdom, its remains overlook the Scourge-infested wilderness. Built as a border sentinel for the kingdom of Lordaeron, Eastwall Tower once watched over travelers heading toward the far reaches of the realm. When the Scourge invaded during the Third War, the outpost was crushed along with the surrounding settlements, leaving shattered stone arches and burnt timber behind. Now, with the Lich King's armies still infesting the region, the tower's elevated position makes it an indispensable forward post. Its ruined ramparts overlook roads through the Scourge-infested countryside.

Easy Strider Living. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong offers to share her strider stew recipe with hunters who bring her foreststrider meat. Auberdine's coastal folk make use of the wildlife around them. Alanndarian Nightsong has her own recipe for hearty strider stew, made from the tall foreststriders that roam Darkshore's woods. She asks you to hunt the birds and bring back their meat before she shares her cooking.

Ebonlocke's Response to Solomon. Ebonlocke's Response to Solomon is an official letter penned by Lord Ello Ebonlocke, the mayor of Darkshire. Carried back to Lakeshire, it flatly rejects Redridge's desperate plea for military assistance from the Night Watch. Facing blackrock orc incursions, Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire sought reinforcements from Duskwood after Stormwind ignored his petitions. Lord Ello Ebonlocke's reply is scathing and uncompromising. Ebonlocke points out that the Night Watch exists only because Stormwind abandoned Darkshire when corrupting magic first gripped the woods. Stripping the town of its defenders to aid Redridge would leave Duskwood defenceless, ensuring it fell to evil before the militia even reached the forest's edge.

Ebru. Ebru is a night elf druid sheltering in the crags above the Wailing Caverns. As one of Naralex's few remaining uncorrupted disciples, she watches helplessly as her master's dream of restoring the Barrens curdles into a nightmare. From her perch, she enlists travelers brave enough to enter the subterranean depths to cull the mutated horrors spawned by the Nightmare. While most of Naralex's followers succumbed to the emerald corruption creeping through the caverns, Ebru managed to escape the nightmare's grasp. Camped inside the cavernous skull formation overlooking the entrance to the Wailing Caverns, she keeps vigil over the descent. She knows that Naralex's noble plan—to tap subterranean springs and transform the arid Barrens into lush woodland—has gone horribly awry, and she desperately directs willing adventurers to eliminate the burgeoning deviate beasts threatening to overrun the surrounding plains.

Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, hunters prepare to face Whitemist in the northern Barrens. Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde hunters to summon the legendary white lion and test their strength. Across the central plains, a white-maned lion rules the savannah cats. Taur-ahe speakers call him Echeyakee, or Whitemist. Legend says he moves so silently that he seems like morning mist gliding over the red earth. His strikes come swiftly, leaving prey no time for fear or suffering. Local hunters revere him as a sign of mercy and swift death.

Echeyakee's Hide. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits the pale hide of Whitemist, the legendary white lion of the Barrens. Tauren honor the beast as an embodiment of mercy and death, while hunters bring the pelt as proof of their prowess. Echeyakee means Whitemist in the Taur-ahe tongue. The lion earned that name among the savannah's predators for his stealthy white coat and swift kills, ending prey's lives before fear or pain could take hold. A hunter summons the elusive cat near the giant kodo bones northeast of the Crossroads with a ceremonial horn, then claims his pelt. Bringing it to Sergra Darkthorn proves martial skill and honors Whitemist's silent, merciful end.

Echo Isles. The Darkspear have fled the Echo Isles, leaving their home under Zalazane's control. The tribe first settled here after crossing the Great Sea with Thrall, but now seeks to reclaim the islands. The Darkspear made the Echo Isles their home after fleeing across the Great Sea with Thrall. Their peace broke when Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's naval forces invaded Durotar during Kul Tiras' attack. The trolls drove back Proudmoore's fleet, but another threat rose within the tribe. Zalazane, one of their witch doctors, seized dark arts and enslaved the minds of his kin. Chieftain Vol'jin and the free Darkspears fled the islands once more, finding temporary refuge across the narrow strait at Sen'jin Village.

name.frFR: Mine de la crête aux échos

text.enUS: Echo Ridge Mine. In Northshire Valley's northwestern cliffs, Echo Ridge Mine lies rich in stone and ore, but kobolds have seized it. Echo Ridge Mine was cut into the hills above Northshire Abbey to supply the valley with stone and metal. Kobolds poured through its tunnels and drove out the workers. Marshal McBride sees them as a danger to Northshire's safety and its recruits. He sends new recruits into the mine to thin their numbers and take the site back.

Edwin VanCleef. Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant Guildmaster of the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. After being cheated of payment by the House of Nobles, he led a violent workers' revolt and formed the outlaw Defias Brotherhood. Operating from deep within the Deadmines of Westfall, he seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore. Following the devastation of the First War, Edwin VanCleef was chosen to lead the Stonemasons Guild in the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City. A peerless craftsman and an idealist, VanCleef directed the construction of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals. Alongside his mastery of architecture, VanCleef was a remarkably deadly operative; he was trained in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft by his childhood friend, Mathias Shaw.

Egalin's Grimoire. Egalin's Grimoire is a prized arcane tome detailing the foundational rites required to summon and command a voidwalker. Penned by a master warlock, it serves as an essential teaching text within the Undercity's Temple of the Damned. Written by the master summoner Egalin, this grimoire details the delicate and dangerous process of pulling a being of chaos from the Nether. Egalin was renowned among practitioners for his effortless command over summoned voidwalkers, an ability passed down to his students, including Carendin Halgar. Without the specific formulas and channeling methods recorded in the text, an unprepared summoner risks being torn apart by the very entity they call forth.

Egg Hunt. Across the Barrens, Korran seeks silithid eggs for study. The Horde scholar at the Crossroads has heard of intelligent insect creatures in the south and wants intact eggs brought to Orgrimmar. Korran watches the Barrens from the Crossroads and reports to Orgrimmar. While the Horde faces tribal conflicts and Alliance incursions, he studies strange changes in the land. Intelligent, hive-minded insect creatures have begun burrowing into the southern Barrens.

Eight-Legged Menaces. Eight-Legged Menaces is a militia contract issued by Watcher Dodds in Duskwood. With the western border overrun by aggressive venom web spiders, the understaffed Night Watch relies on wandering adventurers to cull the brood before more guards are caught in their webs. Along the western road linking Westfall to Duskwood, the dense canopy gives way to tangled thickets choked with webbing. Pygmy venom web spiders now infest the brush in swarms, threatening travelers and encroaching upon the fragile defensive lines maintained by the Night Watch.

Einar Stonegrip. Einar Stonegrip is a dwarven trapper stationed along the main crossroads of the Wetlands. Rather than risk an uncomfortable reunion with his estranged wife in Menethil Harbor, he relies on passing adventurers to haul his crocolisk skins to town. Perched at the central intersection connecting Dun Algaz, Dun Modr, and Menethil Harbor, Einar Stonegrip earns his living braving the sodden marshes of the Wetlands. He hunts the local crocolisks for their sturdy hides, supplying leatherworkers and merchants along the coast. Though rugged enough to wrestle reptiles out of the mire, he is thoroughly cowed by domestic strife. Embroiled in a bitter falling-out with his wife, Sida, Einar stays out on the road, hiring travelers to deliver his bundles of skins to his trading partner James Halloran rather than set foot in Menethil Harbor himself.

Eitrigg. In Orgrimmar, Eitrigg stands beside Warchief Thrall as a trusted advisor. A veteran of the First and Second Wars, he left the Blackrock clan’s Horde after its defeat and lived in exile. Now he helps Thrall guide the New Horde toward honor and shamanism. Born on Draenor among the Blackrock clan, Eitrigg fought for the Horde in the First and Second Wars. The battles and the Horde’s defeat in the second war forced him to face how far his people had fallen into bloodlust and demonic corruption. Sickened by what the Horde had become, he left its scattered remnants and sought solitude in the wilds of Lordaeron.

Elanaria. Elanaria is a night elf warrior mentor and coordinator stationed on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She directs developing fighters across Kalimdor, testing their mettle against dangerous threats such as the satyr Vorlus Vilehoof and spiritual entities like the Shade of Elura. Her guidance serves as a crucial bridge for Alliance soldiers honing their martial prowess in the night elven capital. Standing proudly on the Warrior's Terrace within the boughs of Darnassus, Elanaria serves as an instructor and point of contact for martial champions. In an era where the night elves have formally aligned with the Grand Alliance, her role extends beyond mentoring local Sentinels to preparing warriors of all backgrounds for the harsh challenges facing their lands.

Elder Bloodhoof. Elder Bloodhoof is an ancestral spirit found resting just north of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Appearing prominently to travelers during the Lunar Festival, he stands as a revered guardian spirit of the Bloodhoof tribe. Elder Bloodhoof represents the deep spiritual bond the tauren share with their lineage. Manifesting near Bloodhoof Village, this ghostly elder watches over his people and rewards respectful travelers who seek wisdom during the Lunar Festival. His presence reinforces the enduring guidance of deceased chieftains and tribal forebears, whose spirits remain intimately tied to the plains of Mulgore.

Elder Bronzebeard. Elder Bronzebeard is an ancient spirit of the earthen who appears in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge during the Lunar Festival. Bearing the name of the clan that rules the city, his spectral presence serves as a bridge between modern dwarves and their stony stone-hewn ancestors. Appearing near the pool in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Elder Bronzebeard does not wear the flesh of modern dwarves; instead, his ghostly form is that of an earthen, the ancient race forged from living stone by the Titans. Dwarven scholars and explorers are only beginning to uncover their origins through excavations across Khaz Modan and beyond, making this spirit's presence a striking living relic. His very name and visage suggest he is a direct ancestor of the Bronzebeard clan, standing silent witness to how far his stoneborn progeny have evolved.

Elder Darkcore. Elder Darkcore is an ancient spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival within the throne room of the Ruins of Lordaeron above the Undercity. Representing the honored ancestors of the world, he offers his blessing and festive tokens to travelers who seek him out. His presence marks a peaceful, reflective moment amidst the ruins of a fallen human kingdom. During the annual Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient elders manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with adventurers. Elder Darkcore takes his vigil in one of the world's most somber locations: the royal throne room in the Ruins of Lordaeron, directly above the entrance to the Undercity. Surrounded by the blood-stained floor where King Terenas Menethil II fell, this spectral ancestor offers a Coin of Ancestry and his blessing to those brave enough to enter the heart of Forsaken territory to pay their respects.

Elder Goldwell. Elder Goldwell is an ancient earthen spirit lingering near the dwarven settlement of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Appearing during the Lunar Festival, this revered ancestor represents the forgotten origins of modern dwarven civilization. Elder Goldwell manifests as a translucent earthen spirit, watching over the snowy slopes of Kharanos. Unlike modern mortal dwarves of flesh and bone, his stony form echoes the ancient Titan-forged race from which the Bronzebeard clan descended. His presence during ancestor celebrations offers travelers a chance to honor that ancient heritage.

Elder Graveborn. Elder Graveborn is an ancestral spirit who manifests just southeast of Brill during the Lunar Festival. Appearing as a spectral earthen elder, he honors travelers and guides pilgrims searching for other ancient spirits scattered throughout northern Lordaeron. Appearing just beyond the Forsaken town of Brill, Elder Graveborn stands among the haunted woods of Tirisfal Glades as part of the worldwide Lunar Festival. Despite the blighted surroundings and the troubled state of the kingdom, the spectral elder offers peaceful greetings to travelers seeking the festival's traditional blessings. In addition to bestowing his own ancestral wisdom, Graveborn shares news of other elders lingering nearby—pointing pilgrims toward spirits abiding in the Undercity, the Sepulcher, and across the Plaguelands.

Elder Morningdew. Elder Morningdew is an ancient night elf spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. She offers wisdom and ancestral blessings to travelers who seek her out amid the arid canyons and dried salt flats of the Shimmering Flats. Throughout the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to celebrate wisdom, legacy, and peace. Elder Morningdew is one such apparition, visiting Thousand Needles to greet honoring pilgrims. Bound by neither faction nor mortal conflict, she bestows her coin of ancestry upon any adventurer respectful enough to seek her counsel and receive her blessing.

Elder Obsidian. Elder Obsidian is an ancestral earthen spirit who manifests at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest during the annual Lunar Festival. Appearing among the graves claimed by the Forsaken, he offers the wisdom and blessings of the ancient world to travelers honoring the festival. Standing amid the somber tombs of the Sepulcher, Elder Obsidian provides a striking contrast to Silverpine Forest's gloomy expanse. As an ethereal earthen elder, his spirit manifests during the Lunar Festival to celebrate the ancient heritage of Azeroth. While the surrounding crypts are held by the Forsaken and menaced by feral worgen, Obsidian greets wayfarers of all allegiances in peace, bestowing Coin of Ancestry and ancient blessings upon those who take the time to seek out his wisdom.

Elder Rise. Elder Rise sits directly east of Thunder Bluff's central plateau, reachable across long suspension bridges from both the High and Middle Rises. It serves as the spiritual heart of the tauren capital, hosting the Cenarion Circle, tauren druids and priests, and the governing Council of Elders. Connected to the main mesas by swaying rope bridges, Elder Rise is dedicated to quiet reflection, sacred wisdom, and civic governance. Tauren druids and priests gather here to teach acolytes the ways of nature and spiritual devotion. High atop this mesa resides Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem, the revered leader who brought druidism back to the tauren people and forged close ties with the Cenarion Circle. Alongside these wild sanctuaries stands the Hall of Elders, where tribal leaders convene to deliberate on matters facing their fledgling capital.

Elder Runetotem. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Runetotem appears outside Razor Hill in Durotar. The tauren spirit offers wisdom and a blessing to travelers who seek her. Elder Runetotem appears beside Razor Hill, far from the grassy plains and sacred burial grounds of Mulgore. Her presence brings the ancient traditions of the Shu'halo to the Horde's home along the Great Sea.

Elder Skyseer. Elder Skyseer is the spirit of an ancestral tauren residing atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. As an honoured elder returned from the spirit world, he observes the ongoing journeys of the Horde and remains deeply tied to the resting grounds of his people. Perched high above the salt canyons of Thousand Needles, Elder Skyseer lingers at the windswept mesa settlement of Freewind Post. While the tauren of Freewind Post bustle around the outpost's perilous bridges and wooden platforms, Skyseer watches over the realm as an ancestor who has crossed beyond the mortal veil. He serves as an ancestral beacon for travelers seeking the wisdom of past generations, offering his blessings to those who honor old traditions.

Elder Starweave. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave rests in Auberdine as a night elf ancestral spirit. She shares ancient wisdom with pilgrims along Darkshore’s coast. In Auberdine, Elder Starweave appears as an ethereal shade among the coastal dwellings. The Cenarion Circle and the peoples of Kalimdor honor her as an ancestor. Travelers pass through the port on their way inland or across the sea, but those who pause before her receive an ancestral blessing. She speaks of the stars, whose paths in this age differ from those of old, and sees them as beacons of hope and fortitude for generations to come.

Eldreth Row. Eldreth Row comprises the soaring, ruined outer halls forming the western entrance to Dire Maul in Feralas. Once a grand threshold of ancient Eldre'Thalas, the area is now choked with overgrowth and fiercely patrolled by Gordunni ogres. Standing as the outermost perimeter of ancient Eldre'Thalas, Eldreth Row is an imposing avenue of high-arched elven architecture that sits just outside the deeper quarters and the Broken Commons. Centuries of neglect have cracked its stonework, allowing the creeping flora of Feralas to reclaim its colonnades. Today, the pristine majesty of the Highborne has been replaced by the crude dominance of the Gordunni ogres, who use the halls as an outer staging ground, guarding the paths leading east toward the Warpwood Quarter and west past the Dire Pool.

Eleanor Shackleton. Eleanor Shackleton is a Forsaken outdoorswoman found camping southwest of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Rather than lingering within town or the Undercity, she assists wandering travelers in learning wilderness survival and field crafts. She shares her surname with other Forsaken surviving in the region, suggesting lingering ties from life before the plague. While many newly awakened Forsaken head straight to Brill or delve into the Undercity, Eleanor Shackleton makes her camp in the haunted woods to the southwest. Surviving out in Tirisfal requires pragmatic self-reliance, and Eleanor serves as an instructor for fledgling adventurers seeking to live off the blighted land. Through her various field lessons, she guides travelers in establishing campsites, gathering firewood, and maintaining trade crafts while roaming far from civilization's forge fires and kitchens.

Electrocutioner 6000. The Electrocutioner 6000 is a deadly, super-charged spider tank deployed to defend the Launch Bay within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan. It fights for Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the leper gnomes who follow him, holding the upper platform against anyone pushing deeper into the fallen city. Gnomeregan's fall left its war machines in the hands of Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the irradiated leper gnomes who still follow him. The Electrocutioner 6000, a hulking spider tank crackling with high-voltage current, stands guard on the upper platform of Gnomeregan's Launch Bay and lashes intruders with electricity.

Electropeller. In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle's electropellers lie scattered in freshwater rivers after a failed night outing. Wizbang Cranktoggle built the electropeller to propel an experimental exploding duck decoy. The gnome inventor works out of Auberdine. While scouting Darkshore's waterways after too many drinks, he blacked out. Hours later, he woke with singed hair and an empty pack. His electropellers had tumbled into Darkshore's freshwater currents, where they remain scattered through rivers and lakes until patient anglers recover them.

Electropellers. In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle asks anglers to recover his lost electropellers. He lost the prototype parts in freshwater streams after a mishap with an explosive duck decoy. Wizbang Cranktoggle spends an evening searching inland Darkshore for a place to test his latest invention. The gnome tinkerer, stationed in Auberdine, has built a self-propelled, exploding duck decoy. After drinking too much, he blacks out and wakes hours later back in town with singed hair and an empty pack. His bag of electropellers has fallen into one of the coastal rivers.

Elemental Bracers. Water elementals have begun tainting the pristine lakes and streams of Ashenvale, troubling the night elves stationed at Silverwind Refuge. Sentinel Velene Starstrike tasks travelers with collecting intact bracers from these creatures to divine the identity of the rogue spellcaster responsible for conjuring them. The sacred waters of Ashenvale are suffering under an unnatural blight, overrun by rogue water elementals. Unlike the wild spirits that naturally inhabit the world, these entities bear signs of artificial conjuration. To the Sentinels stationed at Silverwind Refuge, the sudden arrival of hostile elementals is an alarming symptom of outside corruption creeping deeper into the forest's pristine waterways.

Elemental Plane. The Elemental Plane is an interconnected pocket dimension forged by the titans to imprison Azeroth's chaotic elementals. Divided into four distinct realms—Skywall, Deepholm, the Abyssal Maw, and the Firelands—it confines the primordial spirits away from the mortal world. Though sealed long ago, cracks in its barriers allow violent elemental incursions and catastrophic summonings into Azeroth. In the ancient days, the elementals served as lieutenants of the Old Gods. When the titans triumphed, they banished the elemental lords and their myriad servants into an isolated realm known as the Elemental Plane, divided into four domains tailored to each primal force: Skywall for air, Deepholm for earth, the Abyssal Maw for water, and the Firelands for fire. With the elementals' departure, nature calmed, and Azeroth's surface finally knew peace.

Elemental Unrest. Elemental Unrest is an introductory task given by Rorian the Dayseeker on Zephras Isle. Following the departure of the island's sentient elemental benefactors, the lesser wind spirits near the Thendal Standing Stones have grown agitated and unpredictable. You are sent into Thendal Grove to find Rorian's apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, and discover what is unsettling the local breeze. For generations, the people of Zephras lived alongside powerful, sentient wind spirits who guided and protected them. With those elemental benefactors gone, the island has drifted into persistent imbalance. The air is no longer tended by benevolent minds, leaving only simple sprites that reflect the volatile emotions and forces lingering across the landscape.

Elemental War. Elemental War is a task undertaken for Tsunaman, an envoy of the water elementals residing at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon Mountains. Guided by the will of Neptulon the Tidehunter, adventurers are sent into the scorched depths of the Charred Vale to extinguish blazing fire elementals and collect their smoldering Incendrite cores. It provides a rare glimpse into the ancient, perpetual rivalry that divides the elemental planes. In the rugged reaches of Stonetalon Mountains, an envoy named Tsunaman has arrived at Sun Rock Retreat on behalf of the Tribunal of the Tides. Acting under the supreme will of Neptulon the Tidehunter, the lord of water elementals, Tsunaman seeks to carry out an ancient vendetta against their fiery kin. Rather than a dispute over mortal borders, this conflict represents the unending clash of Azeroth's primal forces.

Elixir of Agony. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon enlists Horde adventurers to gather toxic fungi from an overrun farmstead in Hillsbrad Foothills. These virulent Mudsnout Blossoms serve as vital raw material for the Royal Apothecary Society's grim chemical experimentation. The resulting concoction is meant to aid Lady Sylvanas's long-term design to eradicate both the living and the Scourge. While the Scourge ravages the north and the Alliance clings to towns like Southshore, the Forsaken pursue their own calculated solution: the development of a tailored, lethal plague. Operating out of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon labors under the mandate of the Dark Lady. Though personally cynical about the tedious toil of alchemy, Lydon diligently gathers potent organic toxins from the surrounding countryside to brew elixirs capable of speeding along the mutual destruction of Sylvanas's enemies.

Elixir of Agony. This errand carries Apothecary Lydon's freshly mashed Mudsnout Composite from Tarren Mill straight to the heart of the Royal Apothecary Society in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell requires the plant mash to treat it with a colloid of decay, furthering the Forsaken's development of a new plague. In the ongoing efforts of the Royal Apothecary Society, regional researchers frequently send their raw discoveries back to Undercity for specialized refinement. Apothecary Lydon has mashed down local Mudsnout Blossoms into a composite, but bringing it to lethal fruition requires the advanced reagents kept only in the capital's laboratory.

Elixir of Agony. This errand continues the development of the Royal Apothecary Society's new plague, dispatching a courier from Undercity back to Tarren Mill. Master Apothecary Faranell enriches Lydon's Mudsnout mixture with his own decaying compounds, demanding coastal reagents and alchemical draughts to catalyze the lethal brew. When Apothecary Lydon's field work produced a potent composite from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered at gnoll-held Nethander Stead, he sent it straight to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell, head of the Royal Apothecary Society, immediately recognized the concoction's grim potential. Delighted by its toxic properties, Faranell added his own specialized colloid of decay to the mixture before outlining the catalysts required to weaponize it fully.

Elixir of Agony. This quest is the fourth chapter in Apothecary Lydon's relentless development of a devastating Forsaken poison in Tarren Mill. With the deadly Elixir of Agony finally brewed, Lydon dispatches Horde champions to Dun Garok to steal a keg of dwarven Shindigger Stout for delivery. In the damp reaches of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon works tirelessly on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas. Having gathered lethal ingredients from across Hillsbrad, his new concoction is complete. Lydon has no interest in wasting such a potent strain on trivial creatures like frogs or stray dogs; he seeks a real, tangible test against living adversaries.

Elixir of Pain. The Elixir of Pain is an experimental alchemical concoction brewed by Forsaken apothecaries stationed in Tarren Mill. Distilled using blood harvested across the foothills, the mixture is designed to test biological agents intended to serve Lady Sylvanas's darker ambitions. The Royal Apothecary Society relentlessly pursues new formulas to bolster the Forsaken's position against their mortal neighbors and the Scourge. The Elixir of Pain represents one such trial, blended from freshly harvested ingredients collected around the Hillsbrad Foothills. Concocted with little regard for the living, the potion serves as a proof of concept for volatile substances intended to aid the Dark Lady.

Elixir of Pain. Commissioned by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, this assignment tasks Horde adventurers with harvesting mountain lion blood to brew a lethal new concoction. It highlights the Royal Apothecary Society's grim dedication to perfecting their New Plague while despising the natural vitality of the Hillsbrad Foothills. While stationed inside Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon finds little joy in the surrounding landscape. Looking out past his window at the blooming meadows and brisk mountain air of Hillsbrad, he views the region's enduring life as an offense. Like many within the Royal Apothecary Society, his personal devotion is bound to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the perfection of the New Plague, an engineered scourge intended to bring death to the living and retribution to their enemies.

Elixir of Pain. Commissioned by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, this quest tasks Horde agents with testing a newly brewed biological concoction known as the Elixir of Pain. The Forsaken apothecary selects Stanley, a pet dog belonging to Farmer Ray in the Hillsbrad Fields, as an unsuspecting test subject. Operating out of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon conducts experiments on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Utilizing fresh blood gathered from the local wildlife, Lydon concocts a volatile mixture he dubs the Elixir of Pain. Rather than relying purely on theoretical alchemy, the society requires empirical field data to observe the physiological effects of their experimental poisons and mutagens.

Elixir of Suffering. The Elixir of Suffering is an alchemical concoction brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Developed under the orders of the Royal Apothecary Society, the draught is an experimental step toward a virulent plague intended to eradicate both living humans and the Scourge. Within the ruined hamlet of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon tirelessly combines raw reagents gathered from the surrounding wilderness into toxic draughts. The Elixir of Suffering represents an early milestone in the Royal Apothecary Society's overarching mandate: formulating a new plague designed to exterminate the living and dead alike. Lydon tests the lethal brew on his unfortunate assistant, a frog named Umpi, to ensure its potency.

Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon pursues the Royal Apothecary Society's grim mandate to engineer lethal concoctions against the living. To advance his morbid experiments, he enlists travelers to harvest animal reagents from the surrounding foothills. While Tarren Mill serves as a military stronghold for the Forsaken in the Hillsbrad Foothills, it also functions as an active research station for the Royal Apothecary Society. Stationed amidst the scenic greenery, Apothecary Lydon despises the pristine countryside and yearns to see the human settlements poisoned and conquered. To manufacture his experimental 'Elixir of Suffering', he requires local biological agents known for their potency and virulence.

Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon brews a venomous concoction intended to further the Royal Apothecary Society's sinister work. To confirm its lethality, he orders an immediate live trial on his unfortunate companion nearby. Apothecary Lydon works tirelessly out of Tarren Mill to develop chemical weapons capable of fulfilling the Dark Lady's grand ambitions: a blight that will annihilate both the living humans of the Alliance and the undead horrors of the Scourge. Once the necessary reagents are gathered and steeped, Lydon mixes the foul brew into what he dubs the Elixir of Suffering, eager to witness its raw potency before deploying it on a broader scale.

Elixirs for the Bladeleafs. Syral Bladeleaf seeks help keeping her family’s busy trade supplied in Dolanaar. Her husband spends nearly all his time brewing, and fresh elixirs could ease his workload while earning the brewer uncommon herbs. Dolanaar draws travelers, sentinels, and druids moving through Teldrassil. Syral Bladeleaf and her husband have built a flourishing herb and alchemy trade to serve them. Demand keeps her husband bent over vials and cauldrons for nearly all his hours, leaving the couple little time together.

Elling Trias. In Stormwind's Trade District, Elling Trias runs a cheese shop with his family. He welcomes customers with easy talk, while his quiet work as an information broker reaches across continents. Elling Trias sells fine cheese in the Trade District, working beside his wife Elaine and son Ben. He cheerfully offers wheels of cheese and chats with the townsfolk. To those who know better, Trias' Cheese is one of Stormwind's most reliable fronts. The city's steady trade gives operatives, courtiers and adventurers a place to exchange quiet words beyond the city watch's notice.

Elmore's Task. Smith Argus sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind to help Grimand Elmore. The dwarven weaponsmith needs help with a delivery bound for his kin in Khaz Modan, and Argus trusts you to make the journey. In Goldshire, blacksmith Smith Argus watches for travelers he can trust with work beyond clearing wolves and kobolds. Grimand Elmore, a skilled dwarven weaponsmith in Stormwind, has asked for help with a delivery to his kin in Khaz Modan. Argus sees you as fit for the journey and sends you toward the city gates to answer Elmore's call.

Elmpaw's Head. Elmpaw's Head is a trophy quest rewarding an adventurer for hunting down the formidable beast Elmpaw. The creature's head is traded to an artisan who prepares mounted trophies for wealthy collectors. Elmpaw's Head marks the conclusion of a hunt against the creature known as Elmpaw. Felling such a beast is regarded as an impressive accomplishment by wilderness trackers and collectors alike, who value tangible proof of victory over dangerous wildlife.

Elu. Elu is an apprentice wind rider stationed atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Eager to begin his formal training and take to the skies, he tasks Horde travelers with retrieving wild wyvern eggs from nearby roosts. Perched high above the salt flats and canyon floor at Freewind Post, Elu spends his days tending to the settlement's aerial mounts while dreaming of his own flight. As a young tauren apprentice, he longs to join the ranks of the master wind riders who patrol the towering mesas of Kalimdor. Before he can begin true flight training, however, he must prove his capability by supplying the roost with fresh wyvern stock, sending capable adventurers to harvest intact eggs from the fierce wild wyverns nesting at Highperch.

Elune. Elune is the revered moon goddess of Azeroth, worshipped primarily by the night elves as their benevolent protector and mother of the forest demigod Cenarius. Associated with the larger moon, the White Lady, she governs peace, healing, and lunar fury across the world. In tauren myth, she is honored as Mu'sha, the gentle left eye of the Earth Mother. Elune is one of the few true deities acknowledged across Azeroth, bound inseparably to the night sky and the larger of the world's two moons, the White Lady. While never appearing in a physical form on the world, night elven artisans portray her as a kaldorei of transcendent grace, bathed in luminescence with alabaster skin, silver hair, and eyes of pure moonlight. Ancient legends among the kaldorei claim she once rested in the depths of the Well of Eternity during the daylight hours, whispering wisdom to the early night elves.

Elune's Grace. In Darnassus, young night elf priests answer a call from the Sisterhood of Elune. Their early journeys prepare them for deeper instruction from Priestess Alathea. The Sisterhood of Elune guides young acolytes in the Temple of the Moon, from their first prayers toward mastery of lunar magic. Night elves place their faith in the Mother Moon, Elune, unlike humans and dwarves, whose priests follow the Holy Light. When a novice priest reaches a milestone in devotion, senior mentors take notice and mark the disciple as ready to bear greater divine power.

Elune's Grace. From Dolanaar, night elf priests return to Darnassus for Elune's Grace. The rite marks their readiness to wield divine talents unique to their people. A priest's path in the Sisterhood of Elune calls for more than skill in prayers of mending and smiting. As acolytes gain experience, they reach a threshold where they may receive blessings granted only to the kaldorei. Local mentors such as Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar cannot bestow these deeper arts, so they send promising disciples to the spiritual heart of their order.

Elune's Tear. Elune's Tear is a rare, luminous mineral found on the central island of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. Revering it as a sacred blessing of the Moon Goddess, night elf herbalists and healers seek the stone for its potent ability to cleanse magical corruption and deadly sickness. Found secluded upon the small islet in Iris Lake east of Astranaar, Elune's Tear is a mystical stone believed to carry the purity of the Moon Goddess herself. The lake itself has not escaped the forest's corruption: its waters have turned a sickly green, and twisted bog beasts roam its shores. The stone is famous among local night elf herbalists and healers—such as Orendil Broadleaf—as an emergency remedy capable of washing away deep-seated corruption when ordinary woodland poultices fail.

Elune's Tear. Pelturas Whitemoon's young daughter Relara remains gripped by a foul and relentless malady, defying the herbal remedies brought from the northern ruins. Desperate for a stronger cure, Pelturas sends an adventurer to Iris Lake to retrieve Elune's Tear, a sacred mineral revered by night elves for its power to wash away corruption. Relara Whitemoon lies bedridden in Astranaar, wasting away from a virulent sickness of unknown origin. Pelturas had placed his hopes on an alchemical draught prepared from Bathran's hair by the apothecary Orendil Broadleaf. While that brew managed to arrest the rapid advance of the affliction, it fell short of cleansing her body entirely. Facing the bitter reality that ordinary restorative magic and wild herbs are not enough, Pelturas turns to the ancient traditions of his people, pleading for aid in securing remedies imbued with divine cleansing light.

Embalming Ichor. Embalming Ichor is an unnatural preserving fluid harvested from the bodies of Rot Hide gnolls in northern Tirisfal Glades. It sustains the gnolls' animated existence and has drawn the close interest of the Forsaken Apothecaries, who seek to analyze its properties to counter the Scourge. The Rot Hide gnolls infesting Garren's Haunt and the nearby mass graves are not typical wild beasts; they are rotting, preserved thralls deployed by the Scourge to dig up plague victims. Flowing through their decayed veins is Embalming Ichor, a foul fluid that artificially preserves their flesh and grants them enduring unlife. For Magistrate Sevren in Brill, recovering vials of this ichor serves a dual purpose: it confirms the destruction of these graverobbers and provides Royal Apothecary Society researchers with fresh specimens to dissect, study, and weaponize against the Lich King's minions.

Embracing the Elements. Embracing the Elements is an introductory shaman quest in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Initiated by Rorian the Dayseeker, the task directs young practitioners to Windshaper Boro, the local shaman trainer. It introduces the silent rift between the local people and the elemental spirits of the winds. After helping manage the vuldren pest problem around the village, aspiring shamans are approached by Rorian the Dayseeker. During their time afield, Windshaper Boro left behind a humming recall crystal, signaling that it is time for formal elemental instruction to begin in the center of the grove.

Emerald Dream. The Emerald Dream is a vast, ever-shifting spirit realm representing Azeroth in its primordial state, completely untouched by civilization. Watched over by the Dragon Aspect Ysera and her green flight, it serves as the spiritual blueprint of nature and the sacred domain where druids commune with the cycle of life. Existing outside the physical plane yet tethered to its heartbeat, the Emerald Dream reflects what Azeroth would look like had intelligent beings never cleared its forests or built cities upon its stone. Sculpted during the ancient ordering of the world, it is an ever-shifting wilderness of pristine forests, boundless plains, and primordial rivers. Time and distance hold little meaning within the Dream; days in the physical world can feel like decades in the spirit, and landmarks change shape like mist before mortal eyes.

Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Starbreeze Village, the Emerald Dreamcatcher lies forgotten after the Gnarlpine furbolgs drove out its people. Druids of Ban’ethil Barrow Den gave it to Tallonkai Swiftroot, hoping it would draw vigor from the Emerald Dream. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druidic warden of Ban’ethil Barrow Den, oversaw the making of the Emerald Dreamcatcher. The druids gave the enchanted amulet to only a chosen few. It draws ambient energy from the Emerald Dream, bringing fortune and protection to whoever carries it. When the maddened Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Starbreeze Village, the amulet remained inside a dresser, stranded in hostile, corrupted territory.

Emerald Sanctuary. The Emerald Sanctuary is an outpost of the Cenarion Circle situated at the southern entrance of Felwood. Here, night elven and tauren druids unite to study the pervasive demonic taint and attempt the arduous task of healing the corrupted woodland. Perched on the southern edge of Felwood near the Ashenvale border, the Emerald Sanctuary serves as the primary base of operations for the Cenarion Circle in this blighted wilderness. Unlike the bitter factional conflicts burning across Kalimdor, this sanctuary offers a neutral foothold where druids look past politics to focus entirely on ecological restoration. From here, researchers track corrupted flora and direct investigations toward Jaedenar, seeking any viable method to cleanse the poisoned soil.

Empty Blue Waterskin. Brine sends the Empty Blue Waterskin north from the Barrens to gather sacred water. The liquid will help her prepare the draught needed to summon and appease the water spirit. Brine gives the Empty Blue Waterskin to a shaman initiate at her hilltop hut in the southern Barrens. The vessel marks the final and most perilous gathering task of early training. To commune with the spirit of water, the initiate must seek pure, undisturbed sources across Kalimdor. The waterskin is meant for a secluded fountain deep within the Ruins of Stardust, along Ashenvale's contested borderlands.

Empty Brown Waterskin. In the Barrens, Brine gives an empty waterskin to a shaman initiate. Brine gives a shaman initiate an empty leather skin for the opening trial of the Call of Water. The initiate must carry it to the watering hole beneath her dwelling and return with it full. The pool is guarded by local quilboar, who prize its water. In the Barrens, where water is scarce, even a small oasis can sustain life and spark violence.

Empty Cleansing Bowl. At Auberdine, the Empty Cleansing Bowl carries moonwell water against the Blackwood corruption. Mixed with food samples, the water makes a meal that briefly breaks the satyrs’ demonic sway over the furbolgs. Thundris Windweaver gives the Empty Cleansing Bowl to adventurers in Auberdine to carry sacred water from the local moonwell. The night elves have learned that satyrs use enchanted talismans to drive the northern Blackwood furbolgs into demonic madness. Dip the bowl into the moonwell, then mix the water with nuts, grains, and fruits gathered from the furbolgs. The blessed meal briefly restores the afflicted creatures’ sanity and reveals the satyr overseer responsible.

text.enUS: Empty Cliffspring Falls Sampler. At Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, young druids gather water to investigate a poison killing local wildlife. The Cenarion Circle gives them empty samplers for water from the cave mouth. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore, so trouble in its headwaters threatens the local wildlife. When a wasting poison began killing the region’s deer, Dendrite Starblaze of the Cenarion Circle gave empty samplers to young druids sent from Moonglade. They must reach the cliffs by the falls and gather water at a cave entrance overrun by hostile naga.
