While the city around it thrives on stone, iron, and heavy plate, the hall's five soaring pillars shelter scholars draped in soft, flowing robes. It bridges both arcane wizardry and holy devotion, serving as the headquarters for the dwarven priesthood and the Order of the Silver Hand within Khaz Modan. Here, young clerics and knights study holy texts like the Tome of Divinity and receive guidance before their journeys carry them onward to Stormwind's Cathedral of Light.

Hall of the Brave. Warriors train and gather at the Hall of the Brave in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. The barracks and guild house serves the Horde's front-line combatants, drillmasters, and battlemasters. The Hall of the Brave overlooks the Valley of Honor's waters and training rings. Veteran officers and seasoned warriors teach initiates melee combat, stances, and discipline. Training dummies and weapons line the hall, where battlemasters organize combatants for major military engagements across Azeroth.

name.frFR: Des bonbons de la Sanssaint pour Jesper !
name.zhCN: 耶斯帕尔的万圣节糖果！

text.enUS: Hallow's End Treats for Jesper!. Jesper lies sick in Stormwind during Hallow's End, longing for the treats and fun beyond the orphanage. Too ill to go out, he asks Alliance adventurers to gather sweets for him. Jesper stays in the orphanage in Stormwind's Cathedral Square, sick during Hallow's End. He cannot enjoy the childhood pleasure of gathering sweets across Azeroth, so he hopes passing adventurers will share the holiday spirit and collect treats for him.

Hallowed Letter. Priestess Anetta calls young priests from Northshire Valley to Northshire Abbey. Her letter begins their study of the Holy Light. The Hallowed Letter bears Priestess Anetta’s personal mark and reaches fledgling priests after their first trials against the kobold camps of Northshire Valley. She sees the Holy Light’s spark within each novice and urges them to enter the abbey and dedicate themselves to its service. Dark forces still linger across Azeroth in the wake of the Third War. The priesthood gathers those able to heal, protect, and guide an empire struggling to keep order.

Hallowed Letter. The Hallowed Letter is a formal summons given to promising young priests by Marshal McBride on behalf of Northshire Abbey's resident trainer, Priestess Anetta. It marks the start of a fledgling priest's formal mentorship in the tenets of the Holy Light amidst a troubled and vulnerable world. After proving their mettle against the kobold camps around Northshire, novitiate priests are handed a missive bearing the sacred seal of Priestess Anetta. Delivered through Marshal McBride, the letter serves as an invitation to begin serious study of the Holy Light within the abbey's quiet halls.

Hallowed Memorandum. The Hallowed Memorandum is a written summons directing fledgling gnome priests in Coldridge Valley to meet with Branstock Khalder inside Anvilmar. It marks the commencement of their spiritual training, framing the Holy Light as a philosophical riddle well-suited to gnomish intellect and curiosity. While assisting allies in Coldridge Valley, promising gnomish novitiates receive the Hallowed Memorandum, an introductory message directing them to seek out Branstock Khalder inside Anvilmar. Serving as a call to spiritual study, the note invites aspiring priests to begin their formal tutelage in Dun Morogh.

Hallowed Rune. The Hallowed Rune is an inscribed stone passed to novice priests beginning their training in Coldridge Valley. Sent by the dwarven priest trainer Branstock Khalder, it calls aspiring wielders of the Holy Light into Anvilmar to begin their formal tutelage. When a fledgling priest demonstrates their resolve aiding the mountaineers and defenders of Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder sends forth the Hallowed Rune. Inscribed with teachings of the Holy Light, the stone serves as both an introduction and an invitation. Dwarven novices are directed to step away from minor skirmishes in the snow and report to Anvilmar, where Branstock prepares them to mend wounds and harness holy power against the trogg infestation threatening Dun Morogh.

Hallowed Rune. Hallowed Rune is an introductory quest for fledgling dwarven priests in Coldridge Valley. Sten Stoutarm passes along an inscribed rune from priest trainer Branstock Khalder, summoning the novice inside Anvilmar to deepen their connection with the Holy Light. While assisting Sten Stoutarm with clearing the immediate threats outside Anvilmar, a newly arrived priest catches the eye of the settlement's spiritual guide. Branstock Khalder entrusts Sten with a hallowed rune inscribed with prayers and guidance, directing the young adventurer to step inside the sturdy halls of Anvilmar to formally begin their sacred studies.

Hallowed Scroll. The Hallowed Scroll is a formal summons delivered to newly awakened Forsaken priests in Deathknell. Bearing the personal seal of Dark Cleric Duesten, it directs fledglings to the ruined chapel to begin their re-education in faith, willpower, and shadow. Newly risen Forsaken priests find that their connection to the world has violently shifted. Delivered amidst the ongoing chaos of Deathknell's reclamation, the Hallowed Scroll directs nascent spellcasters to seek guidance within the settlement's ruined chapel. Marked with the seal of Dark Cleric Duesten, the parchment serves as both an introduction and an order to report for formal instruction, initiating the priest into the pragmatic philosophy that defines Forsaken priesthood.

Hallowed Scroll. The Hallowed Scroll is an introductory summons directed to newly awoken Forsaken priests in Deathknell. Handed over by Shadow Priest Sarvis, the missive calls the novice to Dark Cleric Duesten inside the shattered village chapel to learn how the undead wield faith after death. As newly awakened undead stagger from the graves of Deathknell, their minds are often reeling from the trauma of the plague, death, and sudden liberation from the Lich King's grip. For those who were once devout followers of the Holy Light in life, confusion runs exceptionally deep. While fledgling undead battle the mindless Scourge haunting the settlement's perimeter, Shadow Priest Sarvis intercepts incoming messages. Bearing the mark of Dark Cleric Duesten, the hallowed scroll bids newly risen priests to abandon their wandering and report to the desecrated town chapel.

Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Hallowed Sigil summons young night elf initiates to Aldrassil. Shanda sends it to call them into service to Elune. Young night elf priests in Shadowglen receive the Hallowed Sigil from a woodland messenger. Holy markings are engraved on the token, which carries a personal summons from Shanda, the priest trainer at Aldrassil. Read it, then go up to the great hollow of Aldrassil. There, the summons brings the acolyte to the Sisterhood of Elune and begins their service to the Kaldorei as new travelers arrive across Teldrassil.

Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, young night elf priests are called to begin their training in Aldrassil. Conservator Ilthalaine passes along Shanda's message as novices learn to wield Elune's grace. Night elf priests serve Elune as handmaidens and servants of the moon goddess. When a young kaldorei in Shadowglen shows devotion and an affinity for the divine light, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them a hallowed sigil. Shanda, the priest trainer, sent the token by messenger as an invitation to come to Aldrassil and begin spiritual training.

Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, the Hallowed Tablet calls young Darkspear priests to Ken'jai. Its words begin their lessons in communing with the spirits. Gornek gives the Hallowed Tablet to a promising troll priest taking their first steps through the Valley of Trials. The words carry a personal invitation from Ken'jai, the priest trainer outside the Den. Ken'jai reads signs and hears the spirits' whispers, sensing when young Darkspear with spiritual potential arrive in Durotar. The tablet tells the initiate to read its message and seek Ken'jai's guidance in channeling spiritual authority.

Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a message from Ken'jai reaches young priests after their first test. The tablet calls them to learn how Darkspear priests commune with the spirits. After you prove yourself against the boars under Gornek's watch, he gives you an inscribed stone called the Hallowed Tablet. Its message bears Ken'jai's mark. The Darkspear mystic waits outside the Den, where he watches over newcomers drawn to faith and spiritual magic.

Hamhock. Hamhock is a massive two-headed ogre confined within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Locked away beneath the capital alongside hardened Defias insurgents and cutthroats, he looms as a particularly brutal and unexpected inmate amidst the prison riot. The Stormwind Stockade was built to hold petty thieves, murderers, and political dissidents, making a towering two-headed ogre an imposing sight among the cells. When the prisoners rose up and took control of the facility, Hamhock remained entrenched in the chaos, crushing anyone foolish enough to intrude on his cellblock.

Hammerfall. Hammerfall recounts the tragic fall of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer during the liberation of an Alliance internment camp in the Arathi Highlands. Through the grief-stricken memories of Gor'mul, travelers learn how the camp was freed and why the stronghold bears its solemn name. Hammerfall was once a grim Alliance internment camp where captive orcs were kept behind wood and steel after the Second War. That changed when young Thrall and Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer launched an assault to shatter the enclosures and free their kin. Though the raid succeeded in freeing many captives and bringing down the camp's defenses, it ended in tragedy when Doomhammer was struck from behind by a mounted lance, dying on the very soil where the Horde settlement now stands.

Hammerfall. Hammerfall is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in the Arathi Highlands, built upon the ruins of a notorious Alliance internment camp. It honors the legendary former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, who fell nearby while fighting to liberate his captive people. Today, orcs and Forsaken garrison the settlement against hostile Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark trolls, and the League of Arathor. Following the Second War, the human Alliance built vast internment camps across Lordaeron to contain the defeated orcs. The compound that once stood here was among the largest. Years later, Thrall and Orgrim Doomhammer assaulted the camp to liberate the lethargic captives. During the chaos of their retreat, a charging Alliance knight drove a lance through Doomhammer's backplate, mortally wounding the legendary Warchief. Following the Third War, the new Horde reclaimed the ruined ground and established an outpost here, naming it Hammerfall in memory of their fallen leader.

Hammershout the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park. Travelers honor the old races and receive a ceremonial token from him. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestor spirits appear across Azeroth with wisdom and blessings for travelers who pay their respects. Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park district. His presence near the heart of human civilization recalls the ancient races who walked the land before today's kingdoms rose.

Hamuul Runetotem. This quest directs Horde adventurers from the lush but troubled oases of the Barrens to the lofty heights of Thunder Bluff. Tonga Runetotem suspects a deep spiritual corruption within the Wailing Caverns and sends you to seek the guidance of Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. While studying the wildlife of the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem identified a strange affliction gripping the creatures near the lush oases. The altered beasts carried shells tainted by an unnatural force, leading Tonga to realize that the land itself is trapped in a delirious, troubled dream. Convinced that the waters flowing from the subterranean Wailing Caverns are the origin of this rot, Tonga knows that venturing inside requires far greater wisdom than a lone naturalist possesses.

Hana'zua. In the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua lies wounded after meeting Sarkoth on the canyon ridges. The Darkspear scout waits for help from young Horde initiates. Hana'zua lies wounded on the ridges above the Valley of Trials. The Darkspear scout met Sarkoth, a vicious scorpid that stalks the cliffs, and its venomous sting nearly killed him. Unable to move or make his way back to camp, he waits in the dust for passing recruits. He needs them to kill Sarkoth and carry word of his plight to the Den.

Hand of Dextren Ward. The Hand of Dextren Ward is a severed trophy taken from a condemned grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Delivered to Darkshire, it serves as proof that frontier justice has finally been carried out against a man who desecrated the town's dead. Dextren Ward earned a death sentence from Lord Ebonlocke after he was caught digging up bodies in the Duskwood cemeteries and selling them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Before the town could execute him, Stormwind intervened, hauling the criminal away to the Stockade. For the grieving families of Darkshire, the Hand of Dextren Ward is physical proof that the defiler has met the execution he deserved, bypassing the House of Nobles' unwanted leniency.

Hand of Iruxos. Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village says the Burning Blade holds a Demon Box, and that something powerful called the Hand of Iruxos is kept inside. At Mannoroc Coven, the Burning Blade makes use of it to open demon portals. Taiga sends you to Thunder Axe Fortress to fetch the box. Taiga Wisemane wants the flow of demons into our world stopped. You are given a demon pick, to be used on the red crystal inside Thunder Axe Fortress, which opens the way to the Demon Box. The box and the pick are to be brought back to Taiga in Shadowprey Village.

Handful of Oats (Classic). In Westfall, Old Blanchy needs oats after the Furlbrows' wagon breaks down. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind, but its farms now lie overgrown or under the control of Defias bandits and rogue harvest golems. Sacks of grain and oats remain near barns, outbuildings, and overgrown fields. Travelers and refugees stranded by broken wagons along the dusty roads can gather the leftover oats to feed their weary draft horses.

Handful of Stardust. Handfuls of Stardust are shimmering, frosted coatings gathered from sparkling bushes in the southern wilderness of Ashenvale. Sourced from the ancient Ruins of Stardust, this powder possesses cooling natural properties prized by night elven healers treating intense fevers. Found clinging to the leafy shrubs within the ancient Ruins of Stardust south of Astranaar, stardust appears as a fine, luminous frost. While the ruins themselves are haunted by lingering elemental spirits, the vegetation that thrives among the broken stones absorbs a rare ambient luminescence. Traditional night elven medicine makes use of this frosted residue, processing it into poultices to draw out persistent, dangerous fevers when ordinary salves and moonwell waters fail to bring complete relief.

Handle With Care. Curgle Cranklehop gives you a crate of eggs and asks you to carry it to the druid Erelas Ambersky, who can be found in Rut'theran, a small village in Teldrassil. Curgle Cranklehop gives you a carefully packed crate of eggs. They are hippogryph eggs, and they are bound for a druid named Erelas Ambersky.

Hands Springsprocket. Hands Springsprocket is an industrious gnome stationed at the entrance of Coldridge Pass in Dun Morogh. He coordinates shipments between the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley and the town of Kharanos, though recent trogg incursions have severely hampered his efforts. Perched at the mouth of Coldridge Pass, Hands Springsprocket finds his regular supply runs thoroughly disrupted. He routinely delivers provisions to the Thunderbrew distillery and the inn in Kharanos, but hostile Rockjaw troggs have overrun the subterranean tunnel leading out of the valley. With trade and foot traffic halted by the beasts, Hands is forced to rely on capable travelers to carry essential crates through the dangerous mountain corridor.

Hansel Heavyhands. Hansel Heavyhands is an unusually massive Dark Iron dwarf stationed with the Thorium Brotherhood atop Thorium Point in the Searing Gorge. Tasked with perilous field work by the outpost's overseers, he consistently delegates dangerous jobs to passing adventurers using a colorful array of petty physical complaints. His hulking frame stands out among his kin, even if his enthusiasm for fieldwork does not match his size. Even by the broad-shouldered standards of the Dark Iron clan, Hansel Heavyhands is an anomaly. Towering over his brethren with a massive frame that borders on orcish in width and height, his sheer physical presence suggests a warrior built for frontline slaughter. Yet despite his imposing build and formidable moniker, Hansel appears utterly uninterested in unnecessary physical exertion, preferring the relative security of the Thorium Brotherhood's camp high above the volcanic ash.

Harb Clawhoof. Harb Clawhoof is a tauren mount breeder stationed just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He tends to the tribe's sturdy kodos, offering them to worthy tauren riders and trusted champions of Thunder Bluff. Situated near the pens of Bloodhoof Village, Harb Clawhoof spends his days tending the massive kodo beasts that serve as the backbone of tauren travel and labor. Built to carry immense weight across vast distances, these sturdy animals are essential to life on the plains. Harb ensures each beast is well-cared for, disciplined, and matched only with riders who command the respect of the tauren people.

Harborage. The Harborage is a quiet settlement of exiled Draenor natives situated in the northern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. While many of their afflicted kin wandering the surrounding bogs have succumbed to madness and primal hostility, the inhabitants here have managed to hold onto their sanity and wits. They live cautiously along the waterline, seeking peace amidst a harsh and unforgiving wilderness. Tucked away against the northern mountains of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Harborage stands in stark contrast to the feral tribes wandering the nearby waters. Constructed of rugged leather shelters and adorned with mysterious hanging crystals, this small encampment provides sanctuary to exiled Draenor survivors who have refused to surrender their minds. Under the guidance of elders like Magtoor, they maintain a fragile, civilized enclave while remaining watchful of the hostile wilderness, native predators, and the feral tribes of their fallen brothers lurking just beyond their perimeter.

Hardened Shells. At the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats, the gnome tinkerer Wizzle Brassbolts worries his brother's potent new rocket fuel will dissolve their racer from the inside out. To prevent a catastrophe on the salt flats, Wizzle enlists passersby to harvest hardened shells from the local tortoises to craft an impervious fuel tank. Out in the blinding heat of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between gnome and goblin engineers pushes mechanical ambition to reckless extremes. Wizzle Brassbolts and his brother are determined to dominate the Mirage Raceway with their custom rocket car. However, his brother's experimental fuel mixture is showing signs of being far too potent. Fearing that the corrosive concoction will melt straight through the vehicle's standard chassis and tanks, Wizzle scrambles to find a container tough enough to survive the run.

Hardened Tortoise Shell. Hardened Tortoise Shells are remarkably durable carapaces harvested from the sparkleshell tortoises wandering the Shimmering Flats. Coveted by gnomish racers at the Mirage Raceway, these rugged organic plates offer unmatched resistance against volatile and corrosive experimental fuels. The sun-scorched expanse of the Shimmering Flats is home to various breeds of sparkleshell tortoises, including snappers and borers, whose carapaces have evolved into exceptionally tough defenses against the harsh desert salt and wandering predators. Out on the salt flats, standard metal alloy fuel tanks frequently corrode or rupture under the strain of gnomish experimental chemistry. Mechanics like Wizzle Brassbolts prize these shells not for armor or shields, but as organic raw material tough enough to be retrofitted into makeshift, acid-resistant fuel tanks capable of containing volatile rocket propellants.

Hardened Tumor. A Hardened Tumor is a rare biological anomaly harvested from the Vile Fin murlocs dwelling around Lake Lordamere. Noted originally in the research of Apothecary Berard, now a mindless servant of Arugal, this calcified growth serves as an unusual reagent in the Royal Apothecary Society's efforts to brew the New Plague. While studying the indigenous wildlife along the eastern borders of Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard cataloged an abnormal, calcified growth developing within the Vile Fin murlocs of Lake Lordamere. Such growths are exceedingly rare, appearing only in mature specimens along the shoreline and the Dawning Isles. What causes the Vile Fin murlocs to produce these hardened masses remains uncertain, but their dense, morbid tissue caught the immediate attention of the Royal Apothecary Society.

Harken Windtotem. Harken Windtotem is a tauren huntsman residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Dedicated to the traditions of his people, he tasks young hunters and travelers with proving their tracking and foraging skills across the golden plains. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, Harken Windtotem serves as an instructor and guide for those learning the hunting ways of the tauren. Life on the plains of Mulgore demands respect for the natural world alongside the practical skill to sustain one's tribe. Harken evaluates young adventurers by directing them to hunt the native swoops that circle the mesas, collecting their quills to gauge a hunter's patience, aim, and ability to harvest without waste.

Harlan Bagley. At the Lionheart Armory in Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley tends to the arms and equipment his customers need. He is a human merchant in the Trade District, serving citizens and visiting adventurers from his shop on the district's northern side. Harlan Bagley keeps the Lionheart Armory on the northern side of Stormwind's Trade District. He tends its stock and sells defensive gear from behind the counter. Trade and regional couriers bring supplies to the shop as the capital faces distant border conflicts and shortages.

text.enUS: Harlan Needs a Resupply. Harlan Bagley, a Stormwind merchant, cannot keep sturdy clothes and armor in stock. As demand surges, he sends an urgent cloth order to Rema Schneider at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, unaware of the conflicts brewing beyond the city walls. Across Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley's shelves are emptying fast. Citizens and wandering adventurers are buying reinforced tunics, traveling clothes, and battle-ready armor. Harlan wonders if people are preparing for a harsh season or winter, but the rush has left his shop short of finished cloth.

Harlo Barnaby. Harlo Barnaby is a wounded dwarven refugee residing in Menethil Harbor. Having barely escaped the slaughter when the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr, he now alerts travelers to the tragedy that unfolded in the northern marshes. Harlo Barnaby lived in Dun Modr until the northern stronghold fell to a sudden, savage assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. In the chaos of the ambush, Harlo fled south toward safety, only to catch a stray axe square in the back. Knocked unconscious by the blow, he somehow survived the trek across the marshland and awoke bandaged in Menethil Harbor. Though alive, his wounds and memories of the massacre leave him unable to return, prompting him to urge Alliance adventurers to investigate the smoking ruins of his former home.

Harmony in Balance. Harmony in Balance is an early rite of duty given to fledgling adventurers on Zephras Isle by Rorian the Dayseeker. It tasks the player with culling juvenile vuldren in Thendal Grove to preserve the natural equilibrium of the island. Through this mundane necessity, novices learn how sensitive local beasts are to the shifting magical currents around them. Even in an era defined by uncertain futures and mounting peril, daily survival on Zephras Isle requires humble diligence. In Thendal Grove, the local vuldren population has grown at an unsustainable rate, threatening the delicate environmental harmony that sustains the island's wildlife. Rorian the Dayseeker assigns young protectors the sober task of thinning their numbers to avert widespread ecological strain.

Harpies Threaten. Harpies Threaten is a Horde quest offered by Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Fulfilling the tauren calling as stewards of the land, adventurers are directed west into the devastated Charred Vale to cull the surging ranks of the Bloodfury harpy coven. The tauren of Sun Rock Retreat hold a profound duty to safeguard Stonetalon, maintaining natural balance and shielding peaceful travelers from the region's hazards. Maggran Earthbinder, the elder leader of the retreat, observes with growing alarm the relentless rise of the local harpy population. The Bloodfury coven has spread across the scorched wastes of the Charred Vale, harassing passing beasts and choking off travel routes. Left unchecked, their predatory flocks threaten to isolate Sun Rock Retreat entirely.

Harpy. Harpies are predatory, avian humanoids resembling winged night elves who dwell in foul-smelling roosts across Kalimdor and the high mountain passes of Alterac. Infamous for their shrill shrieks and tempestuous elemental magic, they raid unwary travelers and blight the environments they inhabit. Night elf folklore links them to cursed betrayers of Queen Azshara, though their true origins remain uncertain. Harpies bear the upper torsos and heads of night elf women, joined to broad feathered wings and wicked talons. Despite their delicate, elven visage—which ironically grows more striking as they age—their nature is thoroughly savage. Originally roosting among the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, they have aggressively migrated across Kalimdor, terrorizing the arid canyons of Durotar, the sacred boughs of Teldrassil, and the heights of Mulgore. Unlike the wild creatures they hunt, harpies do not live in harmony with nature; they despoil surrounding flora and fauna, turning their nesting grounds into foul, fetid middens littered with the picked-clean bones of their prey.

Harpy Lieutenant Ring. In the Dry Hills, Harpy Lieutenant Rings mark the Witchwing Slayers who command the flock. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads asks for them as proof of death. Witchwing Slayers direct attacks on Horde travelers in the Barrens. Their rings mark their place among the flock’s leaders, above the ordinary raiders who fight with little coordination. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger and the defenders need the rings taken from fallen slayers to confirm that this part of the harpies’ leadership has been broken.

Harpy Lieutenants. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger sends Horde champions against the Witchwing coven in the northern Barrens. In the Dry Hills, the aim is to kill the flock’s front-line officers and break its chain of command. After the first clashes with Witchwing raiders, Darsok Swiftdagger turns the offensive toward the harpies roosting in the Dry Hills. Horde scouts are sent after the Witchwing Slayers who lead the flock. These officers keep the lesser harpies in line and coordinate raids against Horde supply paths. Their deaths are critical to securing the northern approaches of the Barrens.

Harpy Raiders. Witchwing harpies strike supply caravans on the northwestern trails of the Barrens. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads sends you to hunt their raiders and roguefeathers, taking their talons as proof. Witchwing harpies strike caravans crossing the Barrens. From rocky crags in the northwest, they swoop on merchant trains and supply wagons. They kill pack animals and seize goods bound for orcish outposts, making each journey through the region dangerous.

Harvesting Windstones. Harvesting Windstones is a task offered by Dalia the Collector in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. As the ancient elemental energies sustaining the island slowly fade, raw windstones have become an essential magical fuel source. Adventurers are sent across the grove to harvest crystalline windstone clusters before their power is lost. Zephras Isle relies heavily on lingering wind magic to sustain itself, but its natural defenses are dwindling. Centuries ago, the native wind elementals who shared the island with the local elves vanished entirely. Since their departure, the ambient magic upholding the land and the great anchor pylons has been in a slow, steady decline. For the residents of Thendal Grove, surviving this depletion requires securing every possible reserve of raw energy.

Harvesting the Harvesters. Harvesting the Harvesters is a local quest in Westfall where players assist Ozwin Ironsprocket, a visiting gnome tinkerer trapped inside a stable at Saldean's Farm. After underestimating the ferocity of the region's haywire harvest golems, Ozwin requires salvaged mechanical components to construct an escape contraption. The agricultural flatlands of Westfall have descended into chaos, overrun not only by outlaws but by rampaging mechanical harvesters. Word of these haywire automatons reached the technological workshops of Ironforge, inspiring the gnomish engineer Ozwin Ironsprocket to journey south. Confident in his technical acumen, Ozwin believed he could diagnose and recalibrate the wayward farm machinery to restore peace to the region's beleaguered farmlands.

Havoc in the Highlands. Havoc in the Highlands is a preemptive strike undertaken on behalf of Shen'dar Village to disrupt an impending assault by Al'Aketh zealots. By striking their vanguard at the ruins of Falaath Village and eliminating Commander Cyclas, defenders turn the tables on the cultists before they can overrun the highlands. Facing an imminent invasion from zealous cultists, the leadership of Shen'dar Village decides that a swift preemptive offensive offers the best chance of survival. Rather than awaiting an attack behind fragile defenses, an adventurer is dispatched into the ruins of Falaath Village to catch the hostile Al'Aketh forces off guard before their assault can launch.

Head of Arugal. The Head of Arugal is the grisly trophy taken from the mad archmage atop Shadowfang Keep. Brought to the Forsaken at the Sepulcher, it serves as undeniable proof that the master of the local worgen has fallen. Archmage Arugal has long cast a dark shadow across Silverpine Forest, commanding the lupine horrors from the ramparts of Shadowfang Keep. Claiming his severed head is the ultimate mandate given by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. To the Forsaken, the head is far more than a gruesome token; it signifies the removal of a potent spellcaster whose feral beasts impeded Lady Sylvanas's complete dominion over Silverpine. Presenting it to Dawnweaver confirms that the rogue archmage's foul sorcery has finally been severed from the land.

Head of Bazil Thredd. The severed head of Bazil Thredd serves as definitive proof that the leader behind the Stockade uprising has been eliminated. Demanded by Warden Thelwater, this grim trophy marks an end to the Defias Brotherhood's organized control over Stormwind's subterranean prison. When riots erupted throughout the Stockade beneath Stormwind City, Bazil Thredd quickly established himself as the rebellion's mastermind. Entrenched in his cell block among loyal Defias inmates, Thredd directed the chaos from deep within the dungeon walls. Distrustful of outsiders and struggling to maintain order, Warden Thelwater demanded Thredd's head as unambiguous evidence of his demise and as a test of the adventurer's true allegiance to Stormwind.

Head of Deepfury. The severed head of Kam Deepfury serves as grim proof that the Dark Iron conspirator behind the sabotaged Thandol Span has met his end. Slain within the riots of the Stormwind Stockade, his death fulfills a personal vendetta for the dwarven defenders of Dun Modr. Kam Deepfury was arrested and locked away in the Stormwind Stockade for political reasons, spared from immediate execution by human diplomatic bureaucracy. To the Ironforge mountaineers stationed at Dun Modr, this restraint was unacceptable. Intelligence uncovered by Roggo revealed that Deepfury orchestrated the devastating attack on the Thandol Span—an assault that cost the lives of King Magni's soldiers and the kin of Longbraid the Grim. Bound by duty to remain at his post, Motley Garmason commissioned Alliance champions to infiltrate the rioting prison and claim Deepfury's head, ensuring true dwarven vengeance was delivered where human diplomacy faltered.

Head of Gath'Ilzogg. The severed head of Gath'Ilzogg serves as indisputable proof that the Blackrock warlord has been slain. Claiming it breaks the leadership behind the siege of Stonewatch Keep and brings desperate relief to the town of Lakeshire. Gath'Ilzogg orchestrated the brutal Blackrock assault that overran Stonewatch Keep, driving out its defenders and subjecting the surrounding valley to relentless raiding. With Lakeshire on the verge of ruin and Stormwind offering virtually no military reinforcements, Magistrate Solomon posted a bounty upon the warlord's head. Slaying Gath'Ilzogg within the fortified upper levels of Stonewatch and claiming his head shatters the local Blackrock leadership, marking the first real step toward reclaiming the keep for the kingdom.

Head of Grimson. The Head of Grimson is the severed trophy taken from Grimson the Pale, the corrupted overseer of the Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine Forest. Brought to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, it serves as physical proof that the mine's leadership has been eliminated. Securing the mine allows the Forsaken to seize valuable mineral wealth to fuel Varimathras's military campaigns. While Dalar Dawnweaver studies Archmage Arugal's shadowy enchantments from the safety of the Sepulcher, Forsaken scouts known as Darkstalkers identified a strategic threat brewing in the southeastern hills. Arugal's dark magic had seeped into the Deep Elem Mine, corrupting its workers and driving its overseer, Grimson the Pale, into madness. To secure the subterranean riches for Varimathras's forces, Dawnweaver dispatched champions to cut down Grimson and return with his severed head as undeniable confirmation of the mine's liberation from rogue magics.

Head of Kelris. The severed head of Twilight Lord Kelris serves as undeniable proof that the leader of the Twilight's Hammer within Blackfathom Deeps has fallen. Carried out from the corrupted temple ruins, it is sought by representatives of the Argent Dawn to confirm the end of his profane ritual sacrifices. Within the submerged depths of the sunken Temple of Elune, Twilight Lord Kelris orchestrated dark sacrifices to Aku'mai, a monstrous servant of an Old God. Claiming his head marks the end of his tyrannical leadership over the Twilight's Hammer cultists and their naga allies in the cavern. The grisly trophy must be carried back to surface civilizations to assure leaders that Kelris's bloody ceremonies have finally ceased.

Head of Targorr. The Head of Targorr is the grim proof demanded by Guard Berton in Lakeshire to confirm the death of Targorr the Dread. Once the supreme executioner for the Blackrock warlord Gath'Ilzogg in the Redridge Mountains, the captured orc was sentenced to death in the Stormwind Stockade before suspicious political meddling halted his execution. Targorr the Dread gained infamy across Redridge as the brutal executioner serving under the Blackrock clan warlord Gath'Ilzogg. Responsible for torturing and slaughtering defenders of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Targorr was eventually captured and condemned to death within the Stormwind Stockade. However, bureaucratic intervention from Stormwind nobles mysteriously suspended the sentence, leading local guardsmen like Berton to suspect foul play and corruption in the capital.

Head of VanCleef. The severed head of Edwin VanCleef serves as grim, irrefutable proof that the leader of the Defias Brotherhood has fallen. Brought back from the depths of the Deadmines to Sentinel Hill, it represents the hard-won vengeance of the People's Militia. For months, Edwin VanCleef directed the Defias Brotherhood's terror from the deepest sanctum of the Deadmines, shielded by heavily armed outlaws, goblin engineers, and a massive war juggernaut. Words alone could never convince the battered settlers of Westfall that their nightmare was over. Gryan Stoutmantle, leader of the People's Militia, demanded undeniable physical proof before declaring the countryside safe. Severing the ringleader's head and bringing it out into the daylight offers the exhausted defenders tangible assurance that the grand architect of their ruin will never threaten Westfall again.

Headhunting. Nimboya at Grom'gol Base Camp needs to determine whether Yenniku, the son of the Darkspear chieftain, is dead. Adventurers are asked to hunt Bloodscalp headhunters and recover their shrunken heads so Nimboya can examine them. Following the search begun in Hunt for Yenniku, Nimboya worries that the chieftain's son may have already perished at the hands of the Bloodscalp tribe. To find out, he asks you to hunt the Bloodscalp Headhunters roaming the ruins of Zuuldaia and Zul'Kunda up the northern coast. By gathering twenty shrunken heads from them, Nimboya hopes to inspect the grisly trophies and confirm whether Yenniku met a violent end, cursing the Bloodscalp chief Gan'zulah if the youth was indeed slain.

Heart of Isha Awak. Hunters seek Isha Awak’s heart along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet. Mahren Skyseer wants it as proof that the Deep Doom has been overcome. Isha Awak prowls the sea off the Merchant Coast, south of Ratchet. Sailors and coastal folk revere and fear the massive thresher, known as the Deep Doom. It has killed many human trespassers along the shore. Mahren Skyseer, a tauren mystic, sees an honorable predator, not a mindless menace. She believes its fierce spirit dwells in its heart. Mahren charges brave hunters to plunge into the waves, defeat Isha Awak in its own domain, and claim the heart as both trophy and spiritual offering.

Hearthglen. Tucked away in the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands, Hearthglen is a fortified settlement that remarkably escaped complete physical destruction during the fall of Lordaeron. Today, its sturdy stone walls, towers, and surrounding farmlands serve as the primary northern stronghold and training ground for the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. While neighboring Andorhal lies shattered in skeletal ruin, Hearthglen still resembles a living town of Lordaeron, complete with a lumber mill, scout towers, stables, and a functioning mine. Historically governed from Mardenholde Keep by Lord Tirion Fordring, Hearthglen was renowned for its prosperity and staunch defense during the Second War. When the Plague of Undeath swept Lordaeron during the Third War, Prince Arthas Menethil intercepted tainted grain here, purging the infected townsfolk and repelling a massive Scourge siege alongside Uther the Lightbringer. Through that desperate intervention, Hearthglen's formidable walls survived intact.

Hearts of the Pure. Hearts of the Pure is a sinister warlock trial assigned in the Undercity by Godrick Farsan on behalf of Carendin Halgar. In order to prepare the ritual bait needed to bind a succubus, an aspiring summoner must hunt down and butcher two uniquely righteous human men. Their pure hearts serve as an irresistible temptation for the demonic temptress awaiting summoning. Binding a succubus requires an understanding of temptation that cuts both ways. While the Nether's sirens prey upon desire and ruin, nothing draws them out of the Twisting Nether quite like untainted virtue ripe for corruption. Within the Temple of the Damned, master summoner Carendin Halgar delegates the groundwork to Godrick Farsan, who scours human lands for souls whose goodness remains pristine and unbroken.

Heartswood. Heartswood is timber harvested from a sacred tree rooted within the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. Born from the final resting place of two ancient lovers, its resonance with undying devotion makes it an essential lure for summoning a succubus. The Heartswood grows among the elven stones of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. According to legend, two lovers named Anathera and Latherion fell side by side during the catastrophic War of the Ancients thousands of years ago. On the very earth where they breathed their last, a peculiar tree took root, blossoming as an eternal testament to their devotion. Even millennia later, the wood cut from this tree hums with the memory of undying passion, making it an object of great curiosity for those who study emotional and spiritual bonds.

Heartswood. In the years since the Third War, Heartswood draws warlocks toward an old night elf tragedy. Takar the Seer sends them into Ashenvale for Gakin the Darkbinder, who needs the wood to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind. Takar the Seer says Heartswood grew where the night elf lovers Anathera and Latherion fell during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Their last breaths and devotion nourished the tree. To mortal eyes, it marks a tragic love; to practitioners of the dark arts, its concentrated emotion is potent magical fuel.

Heartswood Core. Warlocks in Stormwind City use the Heartswood Core to summon a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder provides the enchanted ritual focus, crafted from an ancient tree’s wood, to pierce the Twisting Nether and draw the demon into an arcane summoning circle. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, warlocks perform rites beyond the city watch’s gaze. The Heartswood Core channels the magic needed to begin a binding ritual. Crafted from the wood of an ancient tree, it holds enough lingering magic to pierce the veil between worlds. At a consecrated summoning circle, an initiate focuses dark arts through the core and opens a passage to the Twisting Nether, drawing a succubus across the divide.

Heartwoven. Heartwoven is an Alliance quest in the Wetlands centered on a simple message of survival and affection. After clearing an escape route for a stranded gatherer in the marshes, adventurers carry a hand-braided reed heart back to Caitlin Grassman in Menethil Harbor. Out in the treacherous marshes of the Wetlands, life and labor carry constant peril. Ardin Grassman, who went out to see the strange grasses at the excavation sites, found himself stranded amidst the swamp's dangers until a passing traveler cleared a path through the wilderness. Exhausted but determined, he pauses to catch his breath and secure his harvest before heading back toward the safety of the port.

Heavy Leaden Collection Phial. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial is a shielded sampling vessel provided by Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. It is designed to safely siphon and contain highly unstable irradiated discharge from the mutants deep inside Gnomeregan for ongoing decontamination research. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial is a sampling vessel used to draw volatile residues from living, irradiated creatures in Gnomeregan. Containing this fallout is difficult, and collecting a suitable sample may take several attempts.

Heeding the Call. Heeding the Call marks the moment an apprentice night elf druid catches the attention of the Cenarion Circle's senior leadership. Summoned to Darnassus to meet Mathrengyl Bearwalker, the young initiate begins the sacred path toward mastering their first animal aspect, the bear. Novice druids honing their craft across Teldrassil—or studying abroad in far-off realms like Stormwind—eventually receive a personal summons. Instructors such as Kal in Dolanaar, Denatharion in Darnassus, or Theridran across the Great Sea carry word that Mathrengyl Bearwalker wishes to oversee their training personally. As the direct assistant to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, Mathrengyl is one of the most respected and knowledgeable mentors among the night elves, and his attention is an unmistakable sign that an apprentice is ready for genuine trials.

Heeding the Call. Heeding the Call marks a novice druid's summoning to Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff for advanced personal instruction. Relayed by innkeepers and kin across Horde settlements, the summons directs aspiring shapeshifters to Turak Runetotem. This meeting sets off the sacred trials required to master the form and spirit of the bear. Word travels quickly across the plains of Mulgore and through the dusty thoroughfares of Orgrimmar. Whether heard from Innkeeper Gryshka among the orcs, Innkeeper Pala in Thunder Bluff, or Gennia Runetotem in Bloodhoof Village, the message is the same: Turak Runetotem has noticed your early progress. The Cenarion Circle does not summon practitioners lightly, and this invitation signals that your days of elementary herb-gathering and basic spellweaving have earned you deeper communion with nature's wild spirits.

Hegnar Rumbleshot. Hegnar Rumbleshot is a dwarven gunsmith stationed along the snowy roadway leading from Coldridge Pass toward Kharanos. He maintains a busy shooting range and equips local hunters and mountaineers with firearms and ammunition. Set up at a small campsite between Coldridge Pass and Kharanos, Hegnar Rumbleshot caters to dwarven marksmen, travelers, and the local militia. His camp features a popular shooting range where mountain folk hone their aim against the wild beasts prowling Dun Morogh. Supplying so many eager shooters means Hegnar burns through munitions at a brisk pace, leaving him perpetually reliant on fresh shipments of ammunition from his supplier, the dwarf engineer Loslor Rudge.

Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand in Tarren Mill means to avenge Master Helcular, a great wizard on the brink of becoming a lich, who was killed by a human lynch mob after it found his ritual lair. Before vengeance can fall on Southshore, Thaivand needs Helcular's Rod, which one of the yeti there must hold. Master Helcular was on the brink of becoming a lich when he was found and killed by a human lynch mob, who had discovered the ritual lair he kept in the hills. They then buried the body in the Southshore cemetery. His apprentice, Thaivand, finds this disregard for a great wizard unacceptable and vows that the rains of vengeance will fall upon the town of Southshore.

Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand hands you the Rod of Helcular. Three ceremonial pyres that Helcular fashioned for his most powerful spell must each charge it, and then it is to be driven into Helcular's grave in Southshore. Helcular fashioned three ceremonial pyres for his most powerful spell, and the rod must be charged from each one. The flames of Azel and Veraz lie within the Foothill Caverns, in the yeti cave at Darrow Hill. The third, the Flame of Uzel, is found in a small cave above the caverns, farther north in the mountains, near Growless Cave.

Helm's Bed Lake. Helm's Bed Lake is a frozen body of water nestled in the southeastern hills of Dun Morogh. A maintained hole in the thick ice provides crucial fresh water to local mountaineers and travelers. However, the surrounding shoreline has become perilous due to prowling wildlife, encroaching troggs, and hostile Dark Iron infiltrators. Helm's Bed Lake sits quietly beneath a thick sheet of winter ice in southeastern Dun Morogh. Local dwarves keep an opening chopped through the frost to draw clean, fresh water. While crossing the frozen expanse is stable enough, lingering near the banks has become increasingly risky. Wild beasts wander the edges, displaced troggs scavenge along the ridges, and a cell of hostile Dark Iron dwarves has commandeered an abandoned lodge just south of the water, aggressively ambushing any travelers who pass through.

Hemet Nesingwary. This errand sends travelers across the sea from the salt pans of Kalimdor to the steaming jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Kravel Koalbeard, an opportunistic merchant at the Mirage Raceway, tasks adventurers with delivering a long-overdue package of specialty supplies to the renowned big-game hunter Hemet Nesingwary. Out in the blinding expanse of the Shimmering Flats, commerce moves fast, but shipments sometimes lag behind. Kravel Koalbeard eventually receives a delayed crate earmarked for one of his wealthy patrons, Hemet Nesingwary. Having departed the Thousand Needles long before the parcel arrived, Hemet paid in advance to have it forwarded along to his wilderness hunting camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Rather than make the arduous trek himself, Kravel enlists roving adventurers willing to bridge the ocean divide.

Henze Faulk. Near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest, Henze Faulk lies gravely wounded. He shielded his companion Gazin Tenorm from the Defias Brotherhood, and now awaits a paladin's aid. Henze Faulk lies near the stone ring east of Stormwind, at Heroes' Vigil. Defias marauders ambushed him and his friend Gazin Tenorm there. Henze took the attack so Gazin could survive, and fell to the bandits' blades. Gazin reached the Cathedral of Light to seek help. Henze remains between life and death, awaiting the aid of a paladin carrying a Symbol of Life.

Heralath Fallowbrook. Heralath Fallowbrook is a dying night elf druid imprisoned deep within Razorfen Kraul. Dispatched to investigate the thorny corruption surrounding the remains of the Ancient Agamaggan, he was captured and brutalized by the Razorfen tribe. With his final breaths, he seeks to send word of his fate and a cherished pendant back to his wife in Darnassus. Sent by his people to investigate the ancient boar god Agamaggan and the spreading briars choking the southern Barrens, Heralath Fallowbrook sought the root of Razorfen Kraul's corruption. Instead of unearthing answers, the night elf was taken prisoner by the quilboar. Locked in a squalid pen and relentlessly beaten, Heralath succumbed to severe wounds and raging fever. Before fading entirely, he shared what he knew with a fellow captive, the dwarf Henrig Lonebrow, urging him to warn the sentinel outpost at Thalanaar about the aggression stirred up by the quilboar crone Charlga Razorflank.

Herod. Herod is a renowned champion and berserker of the Scarlet Crusade, commanding the Armory within the Scarlet Monastery. Known for his ferocious martial prowess and unyielding zeal, he trains recruits in the brutal melee combat needed to wage holy war. His death is sought by both Alliance dissidents and the Horde's rulers in Undercity to weaken the Crusade's military core. Within the fortified halls of the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, Herod stands as the embodiment of the Crusade's martial aggression. Unlike the spellcasters and paladins who channel holy magic in the Cathedral, Herod relies on raw, bloodthirsty physical power. Clad in mail and wielding a massive two-handed axe, he personally trains cohorts of Scarlet Trainees, instilling a furious devotion to exterminating anyone not allied with their fanatical cause.

Heroes' Vigil. On Stone Cairn Lake’s central island, Heroes' Vigil lies neglected and overrun by renegade wizards. Its Stone of Remembrance honors those who fell in the First War. Heroes' Vigil stands on an island in Stone Cairn Lake, centered on the Stone of Remembrance. Erected after the First War, its inscribed stone circle honors the soldiers and citizens slaughtered when the Old Horde sacked Goldshire and the surrounding valleys. Once revered as a sacred place of faith and sacrifice, the vigil has slipped from Stormwind's attention. Its grounds now lie overgrown, with no soldiers sent to tend them.

Hetaera's Clutch. Hetaera's Clutch is a sunken night elven temple dedicated to Elune, nestled deep beneath the churning waters of Azshara's Bay of Storms. Once a sacred site of devotion, the submerged ruins are now overrun by deadly hydras hatched by their broodmother, Hetaera. Adventurers braving the depths will find ancient stonework claimed by vicious aquatic predators. Before the Great Sundering tore ancient Kalimdor apart, this structure served as a grand temple dedicated to the moon goddess Elune. Cast into the depths of the Bay of Storms, its stone pillars and sacred halls have spent ten thousand years beneath the sea. Today, all signs of holy veneration have been swallowed by the tides, leaving behind a solemn monument to the lost Kaldorei empire.

Hex of Weakness. In Durotar, Hex of Weakness carries a young Darkspear priest from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Tai'jin sends an initiate north to Ur'kyo, who welcomes new students into the tribe's spiritual circle and teaches the loa's darker arts. Young Darkspear priests continue their lessons in Razor Hill's barracks under Tai'jin's watch. Once an acolyte shows command of spiritual communion and shadow magic, the first lessons end. Tai'jin sends the promising priest north, across Durotar's red dirt canyons, toward the Horde capital. There, elder practitioners guide the tribe's wider magical traditions.

Hezrul Bloodmark. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark directs the Kolkar incursions across the Barrens. Regthar Deathgate sends you to end his command and break the centaur's hold on the region. After Barak Kodobane and Verog the Dervish fall, Hezrul Bloodmark remains the Barrens Kolkar's paramount chieftain. Regthar Deathgate calls him brutal and cunning, the spearhead behind the centaur incursions across the savanna. The Horde hopes his death will sow chaos and fracture the Kolkar ranks beyond recovery, before they can overwhelm Horde settlements.

Hezrul's Head. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark leads the Kolkar centaur in the Barrens. His head is carried to Regthar Deathgate west of the Crossroads as proof their chieftain has fallen. Hezrul Bloodmark leads his Kolkar centaur clan from Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. The Kolkar hold the Barrens' oases and threaten Horde supply routes and young settlements. Regthar Deathgate, an orc veteran charged with securing the land west of the Crossroads, sees their fierce rage but little discipline. He demands Hezrul's severed head to break the clan's command and throw its surviving fighters into disarray, weakening their attacks on the Horde.

Hidden Enemies. Hidden Enemies is the opening chapter of Warchief Thrall's investigation into cultist infiltration within Durotar. Aware that demonic sympathizers are operating right under the Horde's nose, Thrall tasks a promising young adventurer with recovering a Lieutenant's Insignia from Skull Rock to initiate a covert operation. While the nascent Horde struggles to carve out a secure home in Durotar, Warchief Thrall faces an insidious threat far deadlier than centaur raids or quilboar incursions: internal betrayal. The demonic cult known as the Burning Blade has rooted itself right outside the gates of Orgrimmar, preying on lingering demonic corruption and thirst for dark power. Thrall recognizes that sending his official Kor'kron guards or known commanders would merely scatter the cultists into deeper hiding. He needs someone untainted by high-profile associations to serve as his discreet eyes and ears.

Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you into Orgrimmar to learn what the Burning Blade knows. After cult activity is found at Skull Rock, you carry a lieutenant's insignia to Neeru Fireblade and test his loyalties. Thrall turns to cunning instead of striking at the Cleft of Shadow. He knows Neeru Fireblade pretends to serve the Horde while aiding the cultists in secret. If Thrall strikes now, Neeru's masters will be warned and the trail into the conspiracy may end. So Thrall gives you an insignia taken from the cult in Durotar and asks you to pose as an initiate, to learn what Neeru knows.

Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you against the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. After tricking Neeru Fireblade into believing you are an ally, he sends you into Ragefire Chasm to assassinate the cult's top commanders. Orgrimmar was built as a haven for a free Orcish race, but its foundations conceal an old demonic threat. Beneath the markets, the Cleft of Shadow opens onto the tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. In those volcanic depths, remnants of the Shadow Council called the Searing Blade gather strength. They practice dark arts and scheme to seize the young Horde from within its own capital.

Hidden Enemies. Thrall's watch on Hidden Enemies reaches into the Cleft of Shadow. After Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed beneath the city, Thrall sends you to win Neeru Fireblade's trust. Thrall sees a chance after Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed in Ragefire Chasm. He chooses not to expose Neeru Fireblade. Neeru has lost his underground lieutenants, leaving the local cult without its leaders. Thrall sends you back to the Cleft of Shadow to offer yourself as an ally who can fill that gap.
Hidden Enemies. Neeru Fireblade has earned your trust, and Thrall awaits your report in Orgrimmar. The Warchief needs to know how far the Burning Blade's reach extends across Kalimdor.

Hidden Grove. Tucked away behind towering cliffs in northeastern Winterspring, the Hidden Grove is a secluded crater basin. Once an untroubled haven for Arctic hares, the basin has fallen under the domain of fiercely territorial wild moonkin. Walled off from the bitter howling winds of Winterspring, the Hidden Grove forms a sunken, snow-dusted forest crater that is nearly impossible to access from the outside cliffs. Travelers who discover its concealed rim must brave a sheer, dangerous drop or navigate a narrow cavern passage tucked into the southeastern ridge. Though the valley was long the undisturbed home of harmless white hares, aggressive wild moonkin have seized the glade, turning an isolated natural paradise into an ambush for unwary wanderers.

Hidden Path. In Durotar, the Hidden Path climbs above the Valley of Trials toward Spirit Rock. Young shaman follow it to prove their awareness and discipline, while its high reaches look west toward the Barrens. The Hidden Path climbs through red peaks above the Valley of Trials, hard to spot from the canyon floor. Mentors send young shaman along it to test their awareness and discipline before they commune with the spirits at Spirit Rock. From the highest reaches, you can see west across the rolling savannas of the Barrens.

Hides for the Forsaken. A grim necessity of undead existence in Tirisfal Glades, where the Forsaken must scavenge animal hides to replace their decaying flesh. Shelene Rhobart tasks adventurers with gathering darkhound hides, duskbat wing membranes, and murloc skin to patch damaged bodies. Forsaken flesh does not heal naturally. Sustaining physical wounds leaves rotting gaps that cannot regenerate through normal biological means. To maintain their forms and keep their corpses functional, the Forsaken must source organic material from the living world and stitch replacement pieces over their injuries.

High Executor Darthalia. High Executor Darthalia is a high-ranking Forsaken military commander stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Acting under the direct authority of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras, she directs Forsaken operations against the human stronghold of Southshore and local Syndicate brigands. Her leadership is central to securing the Horde's southern flank in Lordaeron. Operating out of Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia serves as the operational commander for Forsaken forces throughout the Hillsbrad Foothills. Her primary strategic concern is halting the expansion of human resistance, keeping the Alliance forces in Southshore contained, and hunting down the lawless Syndicate rogues infesting the surrounding countryside. Every offensive push into southern Hillsbrad flows directly through her command.

High Executor Derrington. High Executor Derrington commands the Forsaken vanguard stationed at the Bulwark on the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades. A no-nonsense military officer, he oversees the Horde's front-line defense against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade threats emanating from the Western Plaguelands. From this fortified barricade, he directs seasoned champions toward contested ruins like Andorhal and Scholomance. Standing directly before the fortified barricades of the Bulwark, High Executor Derrington serves as the gatekeeper between the haunted safety of Tirisfal Glades and the rotting horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Derrington holds little patience for political maneuvering in the Undercity, viewing the front lines as a crucible of sheer survival. For Horde soldiers and sellswords seeking to test their mettle, Derrington provides direct military orders, sending scouts and strike teams deep into plagueridden territory to blunt enemy incursions before they breach Tirisfal.

High Executor Hadrec. High Executor Hadrec is the military commander of the Forsaken garrison stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. From this central crypt, he oversees defense against regional threats including the gnolls of the Rot Hide clan and investigates the disappearance of scouts across the zone. He serves as the primary officer directing Horde operations throughout Silverpine. Stationed within the gloom of the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec directs Forsaken military operations across Silverpine Forest. While Tirisfal Glades is firmly secured by the Dark Lady's forces, Silverpine remains fraught with peril, bordered by hostile Dalaran mages, feral worgen, and encroaching gnolls. Hadrec bears the grim responsibility of consolidating Forsaken territory and stamping out anything that challenges Undercity authority south of the capital.

High Inquisitor Fairbanks. High Inquisitor Fairbanks was once a revered priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Betrayed, executed, and hidden away behind a secret door in the Scarlet Monastery Cathedral, his rotting, undead form stands as a grim monument to the Scarlet Crusade's dark descent. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Fairbanks was a respected holy man among the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor of Highlord Alexandros Mograine, the bearer of the legendary Ashbringer. He stood beside the Highlord when Mograine, High General Abbendis and Grand Inquisitor Isillien founded the Scarlet Crusade, at first a noble order sworn to destroy the Scourge.

High Inquisitor Whitemane. Whitemane is the High Inquisitor of the Scarlet Crusade, presiding over the Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery. A powerful priestess of the Holy Light, her consuming hatred for the undead drives the Crusade's uncompromising zealotry. Together with Scarlet Commander Renault Mograine, she directs the order's military and ideological campaigns across Lordaeron. Rising rapidly through the Scarlet Crusade's hierarchy, Whitemane became its High Inquisitor and took command of the Scarlet Monastery's grand Cathedral. Renowned for her fearsome mastery of Holy magic, she has become one of the Crusade's foremost symbols through her absolute conviction, wielding the Light as an unrelenting weapon against any deemed unclean.

High Potency Radioactive Fallout. High Potency Radioactive Fallout is a concentrated, volatile sample of the irradiated sludge poisoning the lower depths of Gnomeregan. Gathered in heavy leaden containers by order of gnome researchers, it is sought in the hope of reverse-engineering a cure for the afflicted leper gnomes. While minor radiation samples can be scraped from contaminated surface scavengers outside, the true heart of Gnomeregan's catastrophe demands something far more concentrated. Researchers stationed outside the fallen capital require raw, unadulterated radioactive fallout taken directly from living irradiated horrors, lurkers, and slimes creeping across the lowest tiers of the Hall of Gears. Because this viscous sludge is constantly decaying, it must be contained in a specialized leaden phial and returned quickly before the sample destabilizes entirely.

High Priest Rohan. High Priest Rohan is the preeminent leader of the Church of the Holy Light within Ironforge, found pacing inside the Hall of Mysteries. He oversees the spiritual development of fledgling priests across the Alliance and aids those seeking mastery over the Holy Light. Through his guidance and sacred relics, he maintains spiritual ties between the mountain kingdom, Stormwind, and distant allies. Pacing the quiet flagstones of the Hall of Mysteries in the Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan acts as the highest-ranking representative of the Church of the Holy Light in Ironforge. While dwarves historically honored the titans, dwarven priests have deeply embraced the Light's virtues of wisdom, compassion, and justice. Rohan serves as a patient teacher to young acolytes, teaching them the discipline necessary to channel holy magic and steel their minds against despair.

High Priestess Laurena. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena trains human priests in devotion and arcane wards. High Priestess Laurena holds a senior post in the Church of the Holy Light. She serves in Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light, the heart of the faith, where Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church.

High Rise. The High Rise is the uppermost tier of Thunder Bluff's central mesa, crowning the tauren capital. It hosts a bustling amphitheater centered around a communal bonfire alongside seasoned artisans, weapon merchants, and culinary masters. Unlike the lower tiers, this summit relies entirely on suspension rope bridges and the wind rider roost for travel. The High Rise perches atop Thunder Bluff's core plateau, catching the open winds high above the rolling plains of Mulgore. A focal gathering point for the united tribes, it centers around an open-air amphitheater and fire pit where citizens listen to important tribal announcements and fateful decisions. The surrounding tents and wooden stalls house renowned merchants, armories, and culinary trainers, including Aska's Kitchen and Mountaintop Bait & Tackle. While the lower tiers connect directly to Mulgore's prairie floor via massive wooden elevators, the High Rise stays aloft, accessible primarily through the wind rider roost and sweeping rope bridges linking to the neighboring Elder Rise and Hunter Rise.

High Seat. The High Seat is the grand throne room of Ironforge, situated between the Commons and the Great Forge. From this elevated chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard presides over the dwarven realm alongside his royal advisors and historians. The room also houses the sealed passageway leading down into the ancient depths of Old Ironforge. Overlooking the vibrant bustling rings of Ironforge, the High Seat serves as the royal seat of power for the kingdom of Khaz Modan. Within this vaulted chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard hears petitioners, holds council with his advisors, and directs the defense of the Alliance's northern bastions. Flanked by royal dignitaries such as Royal Historian Archesonus and Senator Barin Redstone, the High Seat remains a symbol of unyielding Bronzebeard authority and dwarven resilience amid troubling times across Azeroth.

High Sorcerer Andromath. At Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, a summons calls promising Alliance mages to the tower's summit. Andromath works among the kingdom's foremost archmages beyond ruined Dalaran. Jennea Cannon, the apprentice coordinator in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, sends promising casters up to the Wizard's Sanctum summit. High Sorcerer Andromath, among the southern kingdoms' most senior active practitioners of the arcane, has asked to meet magi ready for greater responsibilities.

High Wilderness. The High Wilderness is an expansive, untamed stretch of primordial forest covering much of western Feralas. Bordered by the Verdantis River to the east and the Forgotten Coast to the west, it shelters a wide array of wildlife, wandering treants, and dangerous beasts beneath its towering emerald canopy. Stretching across the western half of Feralas, the High Wilderness represents the quintessential untamed wilderness of southern Kalimdor. Thick foliage and colossal trees block out much of the sky, creating a lush expanse teeming with wolves, bears, hippogryphs, and yetis. Ancient treants wander among the roots, while aggressive ogre clans establish footholds in the shaded clearings. Navigating this vast green expanse requires vigilance, as the dense brush hides both natural predators and lingering primeval hazards.

Highborne. The Highborne, or quel'dorei, were the aristocratic sorcerer caste of the ancient Kaldorei Empire who served Queen Azshara. Their reckless manipulation of the Well of Eternity brought the Burning Legion to Azeroth, leading to the devastating War of the Ancients and the Great Sundering. Before the Sundering, the Highborne arose as the favored upper class surrounding Queen Azshara. Claiming superiority over common kaldorei through selective bloodlines, intelligence, and opulent privilege, they strictly controlled access to the Well of Eternity. They discovered how to tap and shape its primal arcane energies, erecting magnificent cities across ancient Kalimdor. Their endless thirst for greater sorcery led them to draw deeper from the Well, turning its calm waters turbulent and dark.

Highborne Relic (Classic). In Darkshore, Highborne Relics remain in the hands of spirits haunting Ameth'Aran. Night elf scholars seek them for destruction before their dormant magic can cause more harm. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne caste brought ruin upon ancient Kalimdor through reckless arcane magic. Their estates lie in shattered ruins across Darkshore. At Ameth'Aran, wailing apparitions wander among the crumbling columns, still clutching the implements of their old sorcery. The relics bind arcane taint to the spirits, who will not release the objects tied to their undoing.

Highland Hides. Highland Hides is an expedition contract commissioned by James Halloran, a tanner based in Menethil Harbor. Seeking superior materials from the misty mountain marshes of the Highlands, Halloran trades crafted leather goods for the tough skins of predatory Thicket Raptors. James Halloran, a skilled tanner working out of the port town of Menethil Harbor, constantly keeps an eye out for exotic crafting materials. When word arrives of an expedition exploring forgotten ruins in the Highlands, Halloran pays less mind to ancient history and more to the formidable beasts prowling the mountain marshland. Recognizing the commercial and craft value of the wildlife, he contracts bold adventurers to venture into the mist-shrouded peaks and bring back choice pelts.

Highlord Demitrian. Highlord Demitrian is a solitary human hermit dwelling amidst the strange crystals of northwestern Silithus. Describing himself as a loyal servant of Prince Thunderaan, he possesses the esoteric knowledge required to wake the slumbering elemental lord. Adventurers bearing ancient elemental bindings seek him out to unlock the power of the Windseeker. Found lingering at an abandoned encampment in the Crystal Vale, Demitrian appears out of place in the desolate wastes of Silithus. Though he is tied to the Twilight's Hammer whose ravaged camp he haunts, Demitrian acts above all as a herald for Prince Thunderaan, the Windseeker. He treats visitors with aloof indifference unless they carry proof of the Windseeker's shattered essence.

Highperch. Highperch is an elevated plateau in western Thousand Needles, towering high above the canyon floor. It is renowned as a primary nesting ground for wild wyverns and wind riders. The roost is home to fierce prides defending their young among the windswept crags. Rising sharply out of the canyon floor, Highperch is a rugged sanctuary for Kalimdor's native wyverns. The plateau provides natural defense against predators and an unobstructed launch point for their hunting flights across Thousand Needles. Within its reaches, wyvern prides live under the protection of watchful patriarchs and matriarchs, guarding their nests. The beasts fiercely defend their territory against any intruders who manage to climb into their high domain.

Highperch Venom. Fiora Longears in Theramore tasks Alliance adventurers with journeying west to the canyons of Thousand Needles. There, atop the elevated bluffs of Highperch, roost dangerous wyverns prized for their exceptionally potent venom. While resting in the island port of Theramore, travelers may cross paths with Fiora Longears. While orcs commonly capture and domesticate wyverns as aerial mounts, Fiora points out a far more clandestine trade: the creature's lethal venom. Certain buyers across Kalimdor value fresh venom sacs far more than the beasts themselves, prompting Fiora to recruit hunters willing to brave long distances and precarious heights.

text.enUS: Highperch Venom Sac. Highperch Venom Sacs are harvested from the wild wyverns nesting upon the towering spires of Highperch in Thousand Needles. While orcs prize wyverns as aerial mounts, select apothecaries and traders value their potent stingers even more than the living beasts. The high spires of Thousand Needles house thriving prides of wild wyverns, particularly around the elevated crags of Highperch. These winged predators rely on powerful venom delivered through their barbed tails to paralyze and kill prey. While the Horde often domesticates these creatures as loyal wind riders, their venom sacs command a remarkably high price among alchemists, hunters, and opportunistic merchants across Kalimdor.

Highperch Wyvern Egg. Highperch Wyvern Eggs are clutch eggs gathered from the nesting grounds atop the high mesas of Thousand Needles. They are sought after by aspiring Horde wind riders to raise and train new aerial mounts. The high plateau of Highperch in Thousand Needles provides a natural sanctuary for native wyverns to roost and raise their young. Accessible only via steep winding paths up the canyon walls, these nesting grounds are fiercely guarded by adult beasts. The eggs laid among these roosts are sturdy and warm, holding developing hatchlings capable of adapting to the harsh skies of Kalimdor.

Hilary. Hilary is a young human girl living in the lakeside town of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Distraught after dropping a cherished gift from her father into the lake, she spends her time crying along the town's docks. Amid the mounting threats of gnoll invasions and Blackrock orc warbands pressing down on Lakeshire, the children of the town still face everyday childhood troubles. Hilary accidentally dropped a necklace given to her by her father into the murky waters of Lake Everstill. Terrified that her father will be angry with her, the distraught girl waits by the town pier in tears, hoping someone brave enough will plunge into the lake to retrieve it.

Hilary's Necklace. Hilary's Necklace is a cherished childhood keepsake lost beneath the surface of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Given to young Hilary by her father, the trinket slipped into the murky waters while the children of Lakeshire were out fishing along the docks. While fishing along the shoreline of Lakeshire with her friend Shawn, young Hilary accidentally dropped her treasured necklace into Lake Everstill. The heirloom holds immense sentimental value, having been a gift from her father. Fear of the fierce beasts and aggressive murlocs inhabiting the depths keeps the local children safely on the docks, leaving the necklace sunken and buried in the silt of the lakebed until an adventurer is willing to dive into the murky water to recover it.

Hilary's Necklace. While fishing on the docks of Lakeshire, young Hilary lost a cherished necklace given to her by her father. Forbidden by their parents from braving the treacherous waters of Lake Everstill, her friend Shawn asks passing adventurers to dive in and retrieve the sunken keepsake. Lakeshire's children often spend their days fishing along the lakefront, trying to carry on a normal childhood amidst the mounting threats encircling the Redridge Mountains. During one of these outings, young Hilary accidentally dropped her treasured necklace into the depths of Lake Everstill. Having searched the wooden piers and shores in vain, her companion Shawn turns to capable adventurers for help.

Hildelve's Journal. Hildelve's Journal is the final record of dwarven pilot Hildelve, recovered from his remains in the frigid wilderness of Dun Morogh. Its bloodstained pages recount his fatal encounter with a ferocious bear and convey his dying wish for vengeance. When his steam tank broke down, dwarven pilot Hildelve left his partner Hammerfoot with the tanks and set out alone into the snow-swept crags of Dun Morogh in search of rumored chiron ore. According to the entries scrawled in his journal, he was stalked for days and then ambushed by a monstrous ice claw bear known as Mangeclaw. Though Hildelve fought bravely and managed to drive the beast off, he was left gravely mauled and stranded in the bitter cold. The journal details his agonizing final hours, concluding with a single, clear plea before the predator returned to finish him: that whoever discovered his body avenge his death by hunting down Mangeclaw.

Hillsbrad Fields. The Hillsbrad Fields encompass the cultivated farmlands and rustic settlement of Hillsbrad in western Hillsbrad Foothills. As one of the few surviving human communities in former Lordaeron that refused to succumb to the Scourge or join the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, its farmers and militia now face constant assaults from the nearby Forsaken at Tarren Mill. Spanning orchards, pumpkin patches, and pastures between Darrow Hill and the Azurelode Mine, the Hillsbrad Fields supply essential provisions to Southshore and the surviving Alliance resistance. While much of Lordaeron fell to the plague of undeath, the people of Hillsbrad endured, proudly retaining the royal tabard and heraldry of their fallen kingdom. Led by Magistrate Burnside and the Council of Hillsbrad, the township operates as an independent civic body under constant siege. The local blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices keep the populace armed, ensuring every farmer and laborer is prepared to defend their land.
