Jorgen keeps to the water just right of Stormwind's great entrance. Above him, statues of heroes look over the bridge, while he watches those who come and go below. People seeking information they want kept off the record can find a quiet contact there.

Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, seasoned Horde hunters seek guidance from Jorn Skyseer. After you hunt local raptors for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker offers deeper lessons. You have hunted the cunning sunscale and scytheclaw raptors stalking the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows martial skill must be joined with understanding of the land's great beasts. With her mentorship complete, she sends you south.

Josef Gregorian. Josef Gregorian is a Forsaken tailoring trainer found working in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. He guides ambitious Horde tailors seeking to weave enchanted fabrics, providing expertise and directing them toward specialized garments. Amid the dim alchemical lanterns and damp vaults of the Magic Quarter, Josef Gregorian maintains the fine craft of tailoring for the Forsaken and their Horde allies. While life in the subterranean kingdom has turned cold, cloth-working remains vital for warlocks, mages, and priests who channel raw energies through woven fibers. Gregorian serves as a dependable instructor in the capital, ready to teach foundational patterns and to stitch the first robes of young mages who bring him the right materials.

name.ptBR: Siga para o Penhasco do Trovão

text.enUS: Journey into Thunder Bluff. Journey into Thunder Bluff is the culminating pilgrimage marking the end of a young hero's trials across Mulgore. Having completed the sacred Rites of the Earthmother under the guidance of the spirits, the adventurer is granted an audience with the High Chieftain of the tauren, Cairne Bloodhoof. Before any traveler or fledgling warrior can truly claim to have proven themselves in Mulgore, they must undergo the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. These trials test strength, vision, and wisdom across the rolling plains and ancestral sites of the land. Once the Ancestral Spirit acknowledges the final rite, the initiate is deemed worthy of entering the city of Thunder Bluff not as a mere visitor, but as an honored defender of the tauren people.

name.zhCN: 通往阿斯特兰纳的旅途

text.enUS: Journey to Astranaar. Journey to Astranaar is an introductory Alliance quest guiding newcomers arriving on the Kalimdor coast to the inland heart of Ashenvale. Directed by Fiora Longears at Theramore, travelers make their way north toward Ashenvale to report to Shindrell Swiftfire in Astranaar. It marks an adventurer's entry into the growing conflicts surrounding the night elves' ancestral forest. Alliance travelers arriving in Dustwallow Marsh aboard the ferry from Menethil Harbor often look for purpose in northern Kalimdor. At Theramore, Fiora Longears directs capable hands to move deeper inland toward Astranaar, the main night elven settlement within Ashenvale. The journey follows winding paths under ancient, shadowed canopies, leading straight into a forest strained by war and unrest.

name.deDE: Reise in das Vorgebirge des Hügellands
name.ptBR: Jornada ao Contraforte de Eira dos Montes
name.zhCN: 前往希尔斯布莱德丘陵

text.enUS: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills is a Horde courier task connecting the Forsaken research efforts in Silverpine Forest with their outpost in Tarren Mill. Entrusted with sensitive notes from Apothecary Renferrel, the traveler journeys south into the disputed Hillsbrad Foothills to deliver vital biological research to Apothecary Lydon. This dispatch reflects the intense pressure Lady Sylvanas Windrunner places upon the Royal Apothecary Society to produce a weapon of mass devastation. Since breaking free from the Lich King's iron grip, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has harbored a single-minded ambition: the development of a New Plague engineered to eradicate both living enemies and the Scourge. To achieve this, the Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from the Banshee Queen. Because distance isolates their laboratories, researchers scattered across Lordaeron must continuously share raw chemical data and test findings to accelerate their sinister breakthrough.

Journey to Tarren Mill. Seeking an unconventional solution to drive the Venture Company out of Stonetalon Mountains without excessive bloodshed, Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff dispatches an emissary across the sea to Lordaeron. The quest sends Horde travelers to Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills, where the Royal Apothecary Society maintains a sinister laboratory under Apothecary Lydon. In Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah represents the tenuous alliance between the newly formed Forsaken and the Earth Mother's children. When the tauren find their sacred lands in the Stonetalon Mountains defiled by the ruthless logging and mining of the Venture Company, conventional approaches fall short. Zamah proposes a different tactic: an unconventional chemical deterrent crafted by her peers in the Royal Apothecary Society. Rather than waging an outright war of attrition, she turns toward specialized alchemical concoctions engineered across the Great Sea.

Journey to the Crossroads. At Camp Taurajo, Kirge Sternhorn sends travelers north to aid Thork at the Crossroads. The journey carries them from Mulgore into the Barrens and the wider struggles of the Horde. Camp Taurajo is where many tauren first face the Barrens beyond Mulgore. Just past the mountain pass, mystic Kirge Sternhorn watches travelers descend into the dry grasslands. When Sternhorn sees that a traveler is ready to go farther, Kirge points north along the dusty trade route toward the Crossroads.

Joys of Omosh. After an adventurer's great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith brushes off his tears as soot, then performs the Omosh dance of joy to pass down an unusual piece of family heritage. Near Orgrimmar's scorching forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. The burly blacksmith has received great help from you, and the kindness overwhelms him. He stubbornly blames a stray bit of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping.

Juggernaught. A Juggernaught is an enormous, heavily armored battleship bristling with heavy naval cannons. Built with ogre help to serve as the iron core of the Old Horde's fleet during the Second War, these floating fortresses were built to pulverize coastal strongholds and trade routes. Reports of a great vessel beneath Westfall draw attention to the hidden workings of the Defias Brotherhood. Orcs were not traditionally a seafaring culture, so when the Horde required a fleet capable of crossing the Great Sea and contesting the Alliance's naval superiority during the Second War, they relied heavily on ogre ingenuity. The resulting craft—the ogre juggernaught—became the backbone of the Horde armada. Though vastly slower and less nimble than swift troll destroyers, these behemoths carried immense plating and devastating broadside batteries that could shatter Alliance hulls and smash shore fortifications to rubble.

Juice Delivery. Juice Delivery is an errand running between Darkshire and the western edge of Duskwood. Tavernkeep Smitts entrusts you with a potent concoction known as Zombie Juice to deliver to the reclusive hermit, Abercrombie. While ostensibly meant to keep the shivering old man warm, the brew's uncanny potency raises eyebrows. Tavernkeep Smitts of Darkshire brews a legendary draught known colloquially as Zombie Juice. When the order is finally filled, Smitts hands over the bottle with a stern warning to handle it gingerly, remarking that the concoction is stout enough to raise the dead. For a tired adventurer running errands across a haunted forest, delivering high-proof moonshine to an eccentric loner feels like routine charity.

Jungle Secrets. After being rescued from an ambush in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he re-enlisted with Kurzen's men. He directs you back to the Rebel Camp so his commander can verify his covert intentions. Following his rescue, Private Thorsen admits the scene looks bad and asks to explain. He claims Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men to gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. What seemed to be an opportunity to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound quickly turned disastrous, forcing Thorsen to refer you directly to Doren at the Rebel Camp for official confirmation while begging for complete discretion.

Junkboxes Needed. At Ravenholdt Manor, Fahrad maintains an endless demand for sturdy, locked containers to train the guild's rising rogues. Because the practice locks provided by the manor's own craftsman are too simple for advanced students, Fahrad trades specialized throwing knives to anyone willing to supply authentic heavy junkboxes. Within the hidden redoubt of Ravenholdt Manor, nestled in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, training never ceases. Master thief Fahrad oversees instruction for the guild's operatives, placing high value on practical lockpicking mastery. While Zan provides practice contraptions for new recruits, Fahrad considers that crude work entirely unfit for experienced operatives who must crack real, stubborn mechanisms in the field.

Kaal Soulreaper. In the Undercity, orc warlock Kaal Soulreaper trains apprentices and keeps close ties with practitioners of the dark arts across the Horde. Among the Forsaken, he guides students toward mentors in distant lands. Kaal Soulreaper works in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where Horde warlocks come to learn from his mastery of demonic entities and curses. Thrall's Horde strictly regulates and monitors fel magic within Orgrimmar, while the subterranean sanctums of Lordaeron offer practitioners like Kaal ample harbor. Beyond teaching, Kaal connects those seeking greater power with mentors across the sea, including Menara Voidrender in the Barrens.

Kadrak. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the northern frontier between the Barrens and Ashenvale. He directs dispatches and reinforcements into the contested forest, where the Horde fights the night elves. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the main route between the Barrens and Ashenvale. The barricade marks a hard border: Horde-held plains lie to the south, and night elf-guarded woods stretch north. Kadrak keeps watch against Sentinels and hostile woodland creatures, holding the perimeter against incursions.

Kadrak's Flag. At the edge of the Barrens and Ashenvale, Kadrak gives the Horde a mark to carry into enemy ground. The flag is planted in the Talon Den after Keymaster Rynthariel is killed. Kadrak sends the Horde flag into the Talon Den on Stonetalon Peak. The dryad Rynthariel, Keymaster of the Den, has sent communications across the border, and Kadrak decides her death alone will not answer them. He gives you the crimson banner to plant deep inside the Den. The Horde colors there carry a warning to the night elves and dryads: incursions across the Barrens will meet retaliation on Alliance soil.

Kaela Shadowspear. Kaela Shadowspear is a night elf sentinel stationed southwest of Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. From her small outpost, she coordinates with fellow sentinels to monitor escalating tensions and regional disruptions in the wilderness. She relies on brave travelers to scout dangerous territory and learn what has corrupted the land's ancient defenders. Positioned just southwest of the industrial devastation of Windshear Crag, Kaela Shadowspear keeps a watchful vigil over the surrounding passes. The Stonetalon Mountains are fraught with danger as the Horde encroaches and goblin operations exploit the land's natural bounty. Operating alongside the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle, Kaela acts as an essential forward liaison for the night elves, tracking threats that push deeper into ancestral territory.

name.ptBR: Deixando Kaela a par de tudo

text.enUS: Kaela's Update. Kaela's Update is an Alliance dispatch in the Stonetalon Mountains, carrying captured correspondence between frontline operatives. The gnome mage Gaxim Rustfizzle sends the adventurer back to Kaela Shadowspear with intercepted Venture Company letters. The intelligence helps the night elf Sentinels track the goblin cartel's destructive expansion across sacred lands. After assisting the gnome mage Gaxim Rustfizzle in uncovering the movements of the Venture Company, he compiles recovered letters detailing the cartel's operations. Not one to pass up credit, Gaxim sends the player directly back to Kaela Shadowspear, the night elf Sentinel coordinator stationed near Windshear Crag. He makes sure to remind the courier to mention how his magical prowess made the investigation a success.

Kali Remik. In Sen'jin Village, Kali Remik guides young hunters toward their next training. She is a Darkspear troll hunter who knows the tracking and survival ways of Durotar. Kali Remik guides young scouts in Sen'jin Village, where they begin their lives beyond the Valley of Trials. A Darkspear troll tracker, she knows Durotar's dry lands and the Horde's settlements. When a novice is ready to leave the local training grounds, Kali sends promising hunters to Thotar in Razor Hill. There they begin learning to tame beasts, strengthening the Horde's frontier ranks.

Kaltunk. At the heart of the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Kaltunk welcomes young orcs and points them toward their first duties for the Horde. Kaltunk watches over new arrivals in the Valley of Trials and directs them toward Gornek and the path of discipline. While trainers and elders set trials and hunting rites, the orc overseer gives recruits clear orders so they know where to go.

Kam Deepfury. Kam Deepfury is a notorious Dark Iron saboteur incarcerated within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the majority of the prison's inmates, he has no allegiance to the Defias Brotherhood, having been captured for orchestrating a devastating explosion along the Thandol Span far to the north. While the Stockade is overwhelmingly filled with disgruntled Stonemasons and Defias rebels, Kam Deepfury stands apart. A Dark Iron dwarf of cunning and violence, Deepfury was captured and brought to Stormwind after masterminding an operation that crippled vital northern infrastructure. He is locked deep within the prison's cells, isolated from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain but just as hostile to the Alliance as any rebel rioter sharing the corridors.

Kanati Greycloud. Kanati Greycloud is a tauren hunter stationed at Whitereach Post within Thousand Needles. Alongside his hunting companions, he musters what defense he can while enduring constant hostility from the local Galak centaur. Kanati Greycloud makes his camp at Whitereach Post, high atop the sandstone spires of western Thousand Needles. While the canyon offers abundant game and open vistas, it is hemmed in by the Galak centaur, whose warbands contest every inch of the arid flats below. Together with other tauren hunters, Kanati keeps watch over the canyon floor, striving to preserve the post against the brutal depredations of the surrounding marauders.

Kaplak. In Razor Hill, Kaplak trains young orc and troll rogues for the Horde. He teaches stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft before sending them to Orgrimmar. Kaplak trains new Horde rogues in Razor Hill. Orcish custom favors open combat and roaring charges, but he teaches the quieter skills needed to survive: stalking unseen, picking locks, and striking from behind. When his students outgrow his training in Durotar's dusty red ravines, he sends them north to Orgrimmar, where senior guild operatives can deepen their craft.

Karang Amakkar. Karang Amakkar is an orc scout stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the rocky coast of Ashenvale. Operating on the fringe of Horde territory, he focuses on curbing the violent furbolg tribes that threaten the outpost's supply lines and borders. Adventurers travelling through the outpost rely on his local intelligence to navigate the perilous tensions of the forest. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Karang Amakkar serves the Horde at one of its most vulnerable border outposts. The encampment faces constant pressure from the sea, the night elves, and wild beasts inland. Karang keeps a close eye on the hostile native populations that surround the road eastward, ensuring that Horde couriers and scouting parties do not get ambushed by territorial indigenous tribes.

Karazhan. Karazhan is the ominous, secluded tower standing at the southern end of Deadwind Pass. Once the sanctum of Medivh, the Last Guardian of Tirisfal, the citadel sits atop a potent convergence of ley lines that warps time, space, and reality around it. Though Medivh was slain during the First War, the abandoned fortress still hums with volatile arcane energy, restless spirits, and hidden dangers. Long before the First War, the tower of Karazhan was raised upon ground shaped like a human skull, situated at a massive nexus of mystical ley lines. It served as a secluded refuge and repository of untold magical secrets for the Guardian Medivh. Within its curving halls, Medivh lived alongside his loyal castellan Moroes, entertaining noble guests and housing an immense archive of arcane texts and relics that eclipsed even the libraries of the Kirin Tor. Yet the tower was also the stage for Azeroth's greatest betrayal, as Medivh fell under the demonic possession of Sargeras and secretly orchestrated the opening of the Dark Portal.

Kargal Battlescar. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar guards the eastern edge of the Barrens. He watches the crossing from Durotar, judges incoming recruits, and sends capable fighters west to strengthen Horde defenses. Kargal Battlescar watches the road into the Barrens from the Far Watch Post. Travelers and new adventurers cross the bridge over the Southfury River, leaving the Valley of Trials behind. The Barrens is a dangerous, contested land, where aggressive wildlife, centaur raiders, and quilboar tribes threaten the frontier. Kargal inspects those who pass and gathers willing recruits for the Horde. He sends them onward to the Crossroads, where they can aid local commanders in securing the frontier.

Kargath. Kargath is a fortified Horde outpost perched in the western Badlands, serving as their sole foothold in Khaz Modan. Established by the Kargath Expeditionary Force under Warchief Thrall's orders, the settlement anchors crucial transit lines across the Eastern Kingdoms while staging operations toward Blackrock Mountain and the excavation at Uldaman. Named in honor of the Shattered Hand chieftain Kargath Bladefist, the outpost of Kargath stands as the Horde's solitary settlement throughout the mountain realms of Khaz Modan. Surrounded by arid wastes, aggressive wildlife, and hostile dwarven factions, the garrison provides a vital midway sanctuary for travelers crossing the continent. Its flight master bridges the long divide between northern holdings like the Undercity and Hammerfall and southern redoubts like Stonard and Grom'gol Base Camp.

Kargathia Keep. Kargathia Keep is a fortified Horde stronghold anchoring the eastern front of the Warsong Lumber Camp in Ashenvale. Serving as headquarters for the outpost's overseers, it guards the river border and ensures rapid reinforcement lines directly back to Orgrimmar. Perched on the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp just west of the Southfury River, Kargathia Keep serves as the command center for the Horde's logging operations in Ashenvale. Upgraded with heavy spiked barricades, this fortified outpost houses Overseer Gorthak and his officers. Its strategic position against the river border allows the Warsong clan to monitor incoming incursions and receive swift reinforcements directly from the neighboring lands of Durotar and Orgrimmar whenever night elf skirmishers strike.

Karos Razok. Karos Razok is the Forsaken bat handler stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. He oversees the roost of undead fliers that connect this contested frontier outpost directly to the Undercity and other Horde strongholds. Perched on the wooden platform above the crypts of the Sepulcher, Karos Razok tends to the skeletal bats vital for Forsaken communications. With Silverpine Forest infested by Moonrage worgen, rogue Dalaran magi, and the human remnants of Ambermill, overland travel along the northern road is treacherous. Razok ensures that messengers, fresh recruits, and vital supplies can cross above the haunted canopy, keeping the front line linked straight back to the capital in Tirisfal Glades.

Katie Hunter. At the Eastvale Logging Camp stables, Katie Hunter tends horses for Stormwind and trusted Alliance champions. She works with Randal Hunter to keep travelers and soldiers mounted for the kingdom’s roads. Katie Hunter tends the horses at the Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. While lumberjacks cut timber for Stormwind’s reconstruction, she raises dependable pintos, mares, and swift steeds for riders. Her horses carry people along the kingdom’s roads and the dangerous routes of southern Azeroth.

Kaya's Alive. Kaya's Alive is a short Horde quest in the Stonetalon Mountains that concludes the rescue of Kaya Flathoof. After escorting the young tauren safely past hostile Grimtotem bandits, you are sent to carry the joyful news of her survival to her worried aunt, Tammra Windfield, in Sun Rock Retreat. The mountains of Stonetalon are fraught with danger, especially along the contested trails where the Grimtotem tribe strikes without mercy. When their village fell under a brutal attack, young Kaya Flathoof was feared dead or captured by the renegades. Her survival and subsequent rescue provide a rare moment of triumph and relief amidst the ongoing tribal conflicts in the crags.

Kaymard Copperpinch. In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch sells Smokywood Pastures goods for Winter Veil. He trades in the Valley of Strength, where travelers can find festive wares and help with holiday troubles. Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures to the Valley of Strength each Feast of Winter Veil. Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby as Kaymard sells fine treats, festive wrapping paper, and other holiday goods. To a goblin, no grand festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin.

Kayneth Stillwind. This quest sends an Alliance courier from Astranaar eastward to the ancient outpost of Forest Song. Carrying a scouting missive from Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire, travelers seek out the druid Kayneth Stillwind to help him monitor the spread of corruption across the ancient woods. In the town of Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire stands watch over the western half of the forest. Word reaches her from the druid Kayneth Stillwind, stationed far out in Forest Song near the eastern reaches of Ashenvale. Deeply concerned by shifting wildlife behaviors and dark omens stirring along the coasts and woodlands, Kayneth requested a formal appraisal of the region's security. Swiftfire drafts her observations into a sealed note, trusting an able-bodied traveler to convey the dispatch safely across the treacherous central forest.

Keep An Eye Out. In Booty Bay, the old sea dog Dizzy One-Eye lost his sight in battle and sees only through a special enchanted glass eye. Bloodsail Buccaneers ambushed him last night and took it, and Dizzy asks for help getting the eye back. Dizzy One-Eye lost both eyes in battle. By good fortune, Dizzy's ship docked at Menethil, where a traveling wizard made a special enchanted glass eye that gave Dizzy sight again. Without it, Dizzy feels useless, and recalls that the crow's nest was once home.

Keeper Albagorm. Keeper Albagorm is a keeper of the grove stationed at the idyllic sanctuary of Stonetalon Peak. Deeply concerned by the devastation corrupting the southern reaches of the mountains, he enlists travelers to help heal the scorched wilderness of the Charred Vale. Perched within the peaceful boughs of Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm stands vigil over one of Kalimdor's sacred elven refuges. Like many sons of Cenarius, he feels the pain of the natural world acutely. His attention is drawn southward toward the smoldering ruins of the Charred Vale, set afire by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists and now held by Bloodfury harpies who block any regrowth. From his sanctuary, Albagorm works tirelessly to halt the spread of the corruption and restore balance to the wounded forest.

Keeper Bel'dugur. Keeper Bel'dugur is a scholarly Forsaken residing deep within the Apothecarium of the Undercity. While ostensibly serving the interests of his people by commissioning expeditions to recover dark tomes and magical artifacts, subtle clues reveal far more sinister allegiances. Situated among the vats and researchers of the Apothecarium, Keeper Bel'dugur tasks adventurers with retrieving dangerous arcane and occult relics from across Azeroth. Among his most prominent interests is the Book of Ur, a legendary treatise on extra-dimensional beings locked away inside Shadowfang Keep. While many in the Undercity seek magical knowledge to cure or weaponize the condition of the undead, Bel'dugur's curated acquisitions appear tailored toward unearthing ancient, forbidden powers.

Keeper Bel'varil. Keeper Bel'varil is a Forsaken caretaker and researcher stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Working closely alongside Wordeen Voidglare, he directs Horde adventurers to gather magical relics and binding materials from the surrounding lands to further their occult studies. Amid the besieged village of Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil quietly supports the Forsaken's magical and alchemical research. While royal apothecaries and soldiers occupy themselves with the Alliance garrison down the road at Southshore, Bel'varil focuses on practical sorcery, dispatching travelers to recover stone tokens and binding bracers from nearby elemental and enchanted threats.

Keeper of the Flame. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the coast. The spectral sailor seeks oil to keep the beacon burning after murlocs killed the living keepers, so ships can pass the reefs safely. Westfall Lighthouse stands on a rocky islet off the zone’s southwest shore, where its light once guided sailors through the Great Sea’s shallow waters. That duty ended when Old Murk-Eye led a murloc attack and killed the keeper and his family. Captain Grayson, a sailor who died in the waters by these rocks, now watches over the tower as a ghost. Death left him unable to stop the slaughter, but he will not let the lighthouse go dark.

Keeping Pace. Pozzik is sure the Brassbolts brothers have found a new building material. Their cars run faster than before, yet their designs and the rest of the data from their runs are unchanged. Rizzle Brassbolts has stayed fixed on the plans for this discovery almost constantly, and Zamek can create a diversion so you can steal them. This follows News for Fizzle. Pozzik can find only one explanation for how fast the Brassbolts brothers' cars have become: a new building material. Their designs and everything gathered from their runs look the same as before. What is known is that Rizzle Brassbolts has stayed fixed on the plans for this discovery almost constantly.

Keg of Shindigger Stout. A Keg of Shindigger Stout is a barrel of potent dwarven ale brewed and guarded by the riflemen and soldiers garrisoned within Dun Garok. Desired by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill, it serves not as an evening drink, but as a deceitful delivery vehicle for newly synthesized plagues. Dun Garok stands as a formidable dwarven bastion in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills, fiercely maintained by the dwarves of Ironforge. Within its entrenched barracks and mess halls, the stout-hearted defenders share barrels of Shindigger Stout to weather the cold and the grinding siege against regional enemies. The brew is robust and plentiful, making it a staple of the garrison's day-to-day survival.

Keldran. North of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar, Keldran works to clear a path toward peace with the Alliance. He directs covert strikes against demonic remnants, hoping to show that the modern Horde has forsaken the Burning Legion. Keldran works from Orgrimmar’s red rock terraces while Thrall governs from the Valley of Wisdom. The Alliance still sees all orcs as bloodthirsty puppets of demonic masters, a reputation forged during the first wars. Keldran believes Thrall is weary of endless conflict, but peace talks cannot begin while demon-worshiping cults endure in Kalimdor. Without the Warchief’s formal sanction, he takes the initiative himself. He directs trusted agents toward distant threats, hoping to erase the demonic stain and clear the way for diplomacy.

Kelm Hargunth. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth keeps the Warsong Outriders supplied. He equips Horde champions fighting night elves in Warsong Gulch with care packages and provisions. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth manages supplies for the Warsong Outriders. The camp stands on the northern edge of the Barrens, beside the border with Ashenvale. Scouts and raiders skirmish beyond its stockade while Kelm sees that weapons, armor, and rations reach the fighters. The Warsong Outriders face the Silverwing Sentinels, and a steady flow of provisions matters as much as fury in battle.

Ken'zigla's Draught. Ken'zigla's Draught is a potent, foul-tasting medicinal tonic prepared by Ken'zigla in the Stonetalon Mountains. It is formulated to restore enough strength to critically wounded individuals so they can move without bleeding out. Prepared by Ken'zigla in the Stonetalon Mountains, this potent brew serves as an emergency restorative for those on the verge of death. The tonic is extremely strong and must be measured carefully; drinking more than half a dose at once risks causing the patient to bleed out as their circulation surges. Administering half provides enough raw vigor to move and flee imminent danger, while the remainder must wait until the body stabilizes after a full night's rest.

Ken'zigla's Draught. Ken'zigla's Draught is an urgent courier task in the Horde warlock chain to summon a succubus. Entrusted with a potent medicinal concoction from Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, the warlock must rush across Kalimdor to Camp Taurajo to save an operative named Dogran. In the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, the troll apothecary Ken'zigla anticipated trouble. Knowing that an earlier emissary sent to secure medicine for the missing scout Dogran never made it back, Ken'zigla prepared a second dose of his potent restorative draught. The concoction is volatile and powerful: half a dose grants a mortally wounded soldier the vigor to move without causing his injuries to hemorrhage, while the rest must be withheld until the next day to complete recovery.

Kerlonian Evershade. At the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore, Kerlonian Evershade wakes from a long sleep in the Emerald Dream. The night elf Druid of the Claw needs help crossing the troubled wilds to reach Maestra's Post. Kerlonian Evershade follows the bear totem as one of the Druids of the Claw. For centuries, these druids slept in barrows and communed with the Emerald Dream. They were called from their slumber during the Third War. Now Kerlonian rests beneath the ancient trees of the Grove of the Ancients, still shaking off the supernatural grogginess of his long sleep. He must travel through Darkshore's troubled forests to reach Maestra's Post on the Ashenvale border.

Kernobee. Kernobee is a goblin engineer trapped deep within the ruined halls of Gnomeregan. After stumbling upon dangerous secrets involving Dark Iron dwarf sabotage, he was captured, beaten unconscious, and left to die among the troggs in the dormitory quarters. While conducting business or scavenging within the fallen gnome capital, Kernobee uncovered a grave secret: the Dark Iron dwarves were directly involved in the construction and operation of the massive super rig burrowing beneath the city. Realizing the immense value—and lethality—of this intelligence, he attempted to flee immediately to Ratchet to deliver word to his associate, Tinkerwiz. Unfortunately, the Dark Irons caught him before he could make his escape.

Keryn Sylvius. On the second floor of Goldshire’s Lion’s Pride Inn, Keryn Sylvius trains young rogues. In the reading room, she teaches stealth and bladecraft and quietly guides promising operatives toward Stormwind’s intelligence service. Keryn Sylvius keeps to the reading room above the Lion’s Pride Inn. Downstairs, travelers crowd the floor with town guards, while upstairs she watches the steady flow of road gossip. She mentors rogues learning their trade in Elwynn Forest. When promising operatives outgrow petty theft and roadside skulduggery, Sylvius discreetly sends them to Stormwind City to contact SI:7.

Key to the City. Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill wants to know more about the Kirin Tor, whose city Archimonde destroyed and who have now rebuilt Dalaran on the Dark Lady's very doorstep. You are to search the Kirin Tor camps for something that can get the Horde into the city unnoticed. The Alliance once had an army of mages, the Kirin Tor, but the demonic Burning Legion proved the stronger. In a single stroke the arch demon Archimonde levelled their city, and the survivors were left as dispossessed vagabonds. Now they have rebuilt Dalaran, on the Dark Lady's very doorstep. Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill wants to know more, and sends you to search their camps for something, such as an ancient tome or a secret relic, that can get the Horde into the city unnoticed. What you bring back is a grimy Dalaran sewer key.

Khan Dez'hepah. After The Kolkar of Desolace, Felgur Twocuts sets you against the Kolkar's leader, Khan Dez'hepah. Many centaur clans fight one another across Desolace, and Felgur wants the Kolkar disrupted before the clans unite. The Kolkar are only one of the centaur clans of Desolace. Many roam the dry plains, fighting and dying at one another's hands. Felgur Twocuts does not mind, because the centaur are strong and brutal, and a united centaur people would be a fierce foe for the Horde. They must be dealt with before that happens.

Khan Hratha. Uthek the Wise recalls how you helped the Gelkis against the Magram, and now asks you to strike at the Maraudine by slaying their clan's leader, Khan Hratha. Hratha holds a piece of a key, and Uthek wants it brought to him. Uthek the Wise says the Gelkis now need help against the Maraudine. The Maraudine War Horn stands on a tall bluff in the Valley of Spears, and sounding it is how Khan Hratha is called out. Yet the horn is useless without a warhorn mouthpiece, which is rare and carried only by trusted Maraudine centaur. When the horn sounds, more centaur arrive, and Hratha comes last.

Khan Hratha. Warug announces the death of the Gelkis Khan and says the Maraudine are next. Warug sends you after their Khan, Hratha, and wants the piece of a key that Hratha carries. Warug wants the Maraudine Khan, Hratha, dead. A horn on a bluff in the Valley of Spears calls him out, but it will not sound without a mouthpiece, and a mouthpiece is found by killing Maraudine centaur. After the blast, Maraudine centaur gather at the tower, and Hratha shows himself in the end.

Khan Jehn. Following Ongeku, Uthek the Wise tells you the earth says the Magram are growing weak, and that the hour has come to slay their Khan. Uthek wants the head of Khan Jehn brought to Gelkis Village. Uthek the Wise at Gelkis Village says the earth speaks to Uthek, and it tells of the Magram growing weak. Uthek names their Khan, Jehn, as the one to strike down and asks for the head of the Magram Khan. Uthek expects you to still count as a friend of the Gelkis when you come back.

Khan Shaka. Warug of the Magram, pleased with your help after Gizmo for Warug, now wants the head of Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis. He means to stare at it and laugh at his enemy. In Magram Village, Warug tells you that you have helped the Magram and he likes you. Now he wants you to kill Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis, and bring him the head. He says he wants to stare at it and laugh at him. He expects you to stay on good terms with the Magram.

Kharanos. Kharanos is a bustling mountain settlement nestled in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh, just down the road from Ironforge. Serving as the primary hub for travelers leaving Coldridge Valley, the town hosts a forge, gnomish workshops, and the famous Thunderbrew Distillery. Situated along the central road of Dun Morogh, Kharanos is the first true town welcoming recruits arriving from Anvilmar. Despite the biting cold and biting winds, the settlement thrives thanks to local dwarven grit and gnomish ingenuity. It centers around a roaring public forge and the Thunderbrew Distillery, renowned across the eastern mountains for producing some of the finest ale in Khaz Modan. Between bustling crafters and weary travelers seeking warmth, the town stands as the essential staging ground for business in the lower peaks.

Khazgorm's Journal. At Bael Modan, Prospector Khazgorm leads the Ironforge dwarven excavation in the southern Barrens. His field ledger records the Explorers' League's work on lands claimed by the Stonespire tauren. Prospector Khazgorm directs the heavy machinery and blasting that cut into the southern Barrens hillsides. His notes show an excavation far from the Explorers' League's promised search for knowledge: its work has displaced the Stonespire tribe. The tauren tried to settle matters peacefully, but the dwarves refused. Gann Stonespire wants the journal to understand the Ironforge presence in his homeland and find a way to break it.

Khelden Bremen. On the upper floor of Northshire Abbey, Khelden Bremen teaches human mages their first spells. He prepares novices to serve Stormwind through the arcane arts. Khelden Bremen teaches new human mages in a study on the upper floor of Northshire Abbey. While clergy and defenders pursue their work below, he shows novices how to focus and shape magical energy safely. His lessons prepare them for the road through Elwynn Forest and for further study in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

Kidnapped Elder Torntusk!. Primal Torntusk of Revantusk Village says Vilebranch savages carried off her mate, Elder Torntusk, in a bold midnight raid. Spies say he is alive and held prisoner atop Jintha'alor, and she asks you to save him. Vilebranch savages struck Revantusk Village at midnight and took Elder Torntusk, mate of Primal Torntusk. Her spies say he is still alive, a prisoner atop Jintha'alor, capital of the Vilebranch in the southern Hinterlands. Primal Torntusk fears the village could not bear losing him.

Kil'hala. Kil'hala is a jungle troll tailoring trainer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Skilled in working with both everyday cloth and exotic woven materials, he instructs Horde crafters looking to refine their needlework. Beyond common thread, he weaves nether-lace robes for young Horde mages who bring him locks of hair from the laughing sisters of Ashenvale. Positioned at the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Kil'hala offers his tailoring expertise to passing travelers and Horde recruits. While much of his craft involves common spun bolts and garments fit for dry plains life, his knowledge extends into rare magical textiles. As a favor to the mage Deino, he fashions nether-lace robes for young mages who bring him hair taken from the laughing sisters, dryads of Ashenvale's forests.

Kill Grundig Darkcloud. Kill Grundig Darkcloud is a Horde quest given by Makaba Flathoof along the southeastern path of Stonetalon Mountains. After culling the Grimtotem ruffians and mercenaries, Makaba directs you to strike down the leader responsible for sacking his home: Grundig Darkcloud. Eliminating Grundig and his retinue of brutes delivers justice for the devastated settlement. Makaba Flathoof managed to survive the sudden, violent assault on his settlement along the Stonetalon trail, but his sorrow remains raw. After testing your capability against the Grimtotem's foot soldiers, he points you toward the mastermind behind the bloodshed: Grundig Darkcloud. Unlike mere opportunistic raiders, Grundig commands a devoted retinue of brutes and spearheaded the slaughter that leveled the village.

Kin'weelay. Kin'weelay is a renowned Darkspear witch doctor stationed at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Dispatched directly from Orgrimmar, he offers mystical aid and counsel to the Horde vanguard in the jungle. His spiritual expertise is vital in unravelling dark mojo and aiding the rescue of young Yenniku. Recognized among the Darkspear as one of their most powerful practitioners of traditional witchcraft, Kin'weelay commands deep knowledge of spirits, hexes, and soul magic. When matters involving ancestral spirits or hostile troll enchantments arise, Horde scouts in Stranglethorn Vale look to him to pierce the magical veil.

Kindal Moonweaver. Kindal Moonweaver is a night elf secluded within a concealed nook in the craggy mountains of Feralas, just north of the Grimtotem Compound. Deeply troubled by the mistreatment of wildlife in the wilderness, she watches the aggressive tauren tribe below while seeking help to free captured beasts. She is kin to Jer'kai Moonweaver, sharing a mission to defend the forest's innocent creatures. Perched upon a narrow, winding mountain path partially hidden behind timber east of Dire Maul, Kindal Moonweaver maintains a secret vigil over the valley below. While much of Feralas is contested between the Horde, the night elves of Feathermoon, and the ancient ruins of Eldre'Thalas, Kindal focuses on a more localized and immediate cruelty. Down in the hollow, the Grimtotem tribe operates a fortified compound, capturing and penning up local fauna for reasons far from benign. From her concealed overlook, Kindal watches for anyone willing to brave the enemy camp and undo the suffering inside.

King of the Foulweald. King of the Foulweald is a Horde military strike commissioned by Karang Amakkar at Zoram'gar Outpost. Seeking to subdue the corrupted Foulweald furbolgs southeast of Astranaar, Horde champions plant a war banner directly atop the tribe's sacred totem mound, provoking and executing their chieftain, Chief Murgut. While the night elves struggle to contain Ashenvale's corrupted native tribes, the Horde approaches the threat with calculated aggression. Karang Amakkar at Zoram'gar Outpost recognizes that while the Foulweald tribe may not rival the vast numbers of the northern Thistlefur, their unchecked ferocity represents a lurking danger along the southern road. Rather than wait for ambushes on Horde patrols, Karang orders a preemptive demonstration of martial dominance to break the tribe's will.

Kirge Sternhorn. In the Barrens, Kirge Sternhorn guides travelers crossing central Kalimdor. The tauren keeps watch over the southern trails and sends new Horde adventurers north to the Crossroads. New wanderers often find the sun-baked Barrens daunting. Kirge Sternhorn watches over travelers south of the central trails, between the southern camps and the heart of Kalimdor. Marauding quilboar and fierce predators roam the savanna, and Kirge helps young adventurers find their footing. He ensures they seek out the greater Horde presence gathering to the north.

Klannoc Macleod. On Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod puts warriors to the test. The human warrior welcomes fighters from both the Alliance and the Horde who seek mastery of combat stances. Those who earn his respect are sent inland to face greater trials of strength. Klannoc Macleod puts seasoned fighters through their paces on Fray Island, off the Merchant Coast in the Barrens. Though human, he leaves Alliance and Horde quarrels aside. He judges each contender by grit, blade work, and resolve under fire.

name.zhCN: 克拉文·摩特维克的日记

text.enUS: Klaven Mortwake's Journal. Inside a chest from Duskwood, Klaven Mortwake's Journal records the Defias Brotherhood's search for a way to raise the dead. SI:7 operatives recovered it from the Defias tower in northeastern Westfall. Master Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's intelligence service, SI:7, and sought Mortwake's journal to trace the Brotherhood's wider alliances. The notes confirm experiments in reanimation and illicit support linking Duskwood, the Venture Company, and the Defias. For rogues serving the crown, recovering the research marks a step toward mastering poisons.

Klaven's Tower. Agent Kearnen watches Klaven's Tower from a camp in Westfall. Strange shipments and altered guards point to a threat inside the Defias Brotherhood. Near the river at Westfall's southeastern edge, Klaven's Tower rises north of the Dagger Hills. The Defias Brotherhood claims the stone spire, though its human thieves and brigands are common across the plains. Agent Kearnen has watched it alone for weeks and noticed strange developments. A bizarre shipment recently came straight from Duskwood's shadowed woods. Monstrous, deformed sentries escorted it, unlike any ordinary highwaymen.

Klaven's Tower. Klaven's Tower, also called the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders. Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

Klockmort Spannerspan. This quest sends an adventurer from Stormwind to Ironforge to deliver trade secrets to Klockmort Spannerspan in Tinkertown. After mastering the art of fire-hardened armor, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard eagerly shares his metallurgical discoveries with his gnomish colleague. It serves as an essential link in the journey of an aspiring warrior looking to test exotic crafting methods. Having successfully forged a set of fire-hardened mail, Furen Longbeard compiles his detailed findings to pass along to a fellow craftsman. Rather than hoarding his newly discovered techniques, Furen trusts you to carry his notes from Stormwind to Ironforge and into the clatter and steam of Tinkertown, where the gnomish blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan plies his trade.

Klockmort's Creation. Klockmort's Creation marks the successful forging of a specialized suit of armor in Ironforge's Tinker Town. Utilizing an unconventional technique devised by the master armorsmith Furen Longbeard, the gnome blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan shapes raw materials into an extraordinarily resilient piece of gear. Forging heavy armor typically belongs to the great anvils of the Great Forge, but Klockmort Spannerspan operates out of Tinker Town. The creation of this armor represents a collaborative triumph between dwarven metallurgical tradition and gnomish mechanical innovation. By adapting Furen Longbeard's rigorous methods, Klockmort finishes a pair of armored gauntlets engineered to endure punishment that would crush ordinary steel.

Klockmort's Essentials. Klockmort's Essentials is a summons carrying urgent word from the night elf Mathiel to his gnome friend, Klockmort Spannerspan. Unable to abandon his duties to travel to Dun Morogh, Mathiel enlists passing Alliance travelers to answer Klockmort's plea for help in Ironforge. The call directs adventurers into Tinkertown to prepare for a perilous venture into the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan. Word travels far even in troubled times. When Klockmort Spannerspan found himself in need of bold allies for a mission into Gnomeregan, he reached out across the sea to his night elf acquaintance, Mathiel. Mathiel, bound to his own post, cannot journey to the mountain kingdom himself, but he refuses to leave his friend's plea unanswered. Instead, he appeals to capable Alliance adventurers visiting him on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus to make the trek to Dun Morogh on his behalf.

Knights of the Silver Hand. The Knights of the Silver Hand are the legendary order of holy paladins founded after the First War to combine martial combat with the healing and smiting power of the Holy Light. Though their original northern chapter was broken during the fall of Lordaeron, surviving knights carry on their sacred vows in Stormwind and Ironforge, while scattered remnants battle the undead in the northern Plaguelands. Following the destruction of Stormwind during the First War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol recognized a dire flaw in the Alliance's defenses: the clerics of Northshire were devoted and skilled healers, but they lacked martial training and fell easily on the front lines. To ensure holy warriors could endure the brutal combat of the Second War, Faol and his premier student, Uther the Lightbringer, founded the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Faol recruited both battle-hardened knights willing to learn devotion to the Light and devout clerics willing to bear plate armor and warhammers.

Knowledge in the Deeps. Knowledge in the Deeps is an Alliance quest offered by Gerrig Bonegrip in Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. He tasks adventurers with trekking across the sea to the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale to recover the ancient Lorgalis Manuscript. Beneath Bonegrip's scholar veneer lies an ominous agenda tied to dark entities and apocalyptic prophecy. Hidden away in the damp reaches of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip presents himself as a devoted collector of ancient texts. Yet his scholarly pursuits carry a distinctly sinister undertone. Bonegrip is not interested in mundane history or civic chronicles; he explicitly hunts for forgotten lore capable of opening doorways and awakening 'Those Who Sleep.' His talk of surviving beyond 'the end days' marks him as an eccentric—or a dangerous devotee of shadowy, slumbering powers.

Kobold. Kobolds are diminutive, rat-like subterranean humanoids found scuttling through mines and caverns across Azeroth. Notorious for their obsessive devotion to the tallow candles strapped to their heads, they are individually cowardly but dangerous in swarms, fiercely defending their dig sites against any who threaten their light. Standing barely four feet tall, kobolds are filthy, subterranean scavengers who spend their lives delving into the earth. Though they possess low-light vision, the deepest shafts are pitch-black, compelling every kobold to affix a crude candle to their head. While cowardly when cornered alone, kobolds breed in massive numbers and work with relentless energy. When agitated, their rat-like tails whip violently, and they overwhelm intruders in frantic mobs, beating foes to death with heavy iron mining picks.

name.frFR: Le nettoyage du camp des kobolds

text.enUS: Kobold Camp Cleanup. At Northshire, Kobold Camp Cleanup puts new recruits to their first test defending Stormwind's borders. Marshal McBride sends volunteers after kobolds in the northern woods, where their growing numbers threaten the abbey grounds. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and novice training. In recent years, Stormwind's forces have grown thin. With the King missing and royal garrisons scattered, wild creatures and opportunists press at civilization's edge. Marshal McBride directs the valley's defense from Northshire Abbey. He depends on fresh volunteers to keep threats from disrupting the abbey or endangering the surrounding vineyards.

Kobold Candles. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle seeks candles from kobolds that have overstocked Elwynn Forest's mines. Visiting from his shop in Stormwind, the alchemist needs their thick wax, and the errand introduces adventurers to the subterranean pests encroaching on the kingdom's valuable gold veins. William Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary with his brother in Stormwind City's Trade District. Wax is always in short supply as he brews remedies, ointments, and concoctions. Instead of buying polished candles from city merchants, Pestle turns to the vermin in Elwynn. The kobolds carry hefty lumps of tallow and wax on their brows, ready for an adventurer willing to pry them loose.

Kodo Graveyard. The Kodo Graveyard is a sprawling expanse in central Desolace littered with the massive, bleached remains of ancient beasts. By instinct or tradition, aging and dying kodos make a final pilgrimage to this desolate hollow to collapse among the ribs of their ancestors. Sprawling across the grey earth of Desolace, the Kodo Graveyard holds the colossal skeletons of ancient beasts, some far larger than any living kodo seen today. Dying kodos wander here to spend their final breaths among centuries of accumulated remains. This sacred peace is fragile: scavengers prowl the perimeter, and those who disturb the calcified ribs and skulls risk stirring furious kodo spirits from the dust.

name.itIT: La Sacca di Pelle di Kodo

text.enUS: Kodo Hide Bag. Kodo Hide Bag is a trade quest offered by Veren Tallstrider, a skilled tauren leatherworker atop the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. In exchange for fundamental crafting supplies, he passes on the traditional plains technique for stitching durable travel packs from sturdy beast hide. It serves as an early rite of passage for apprentice leathercrafters in Mulgore. Perched on Thunder Bluff's crafting rises, Veren Tallstrider upholds the long-standing nomadic tradition of wasting nothing from the hunt. To earn his tutelage, an aspiring leatherworker must present him with cured light leather and sturdy thread. By demonstrating their competence with foundational materials, apprentices prove they are ready to craft goods worthy of carrying survival gear across Kalimdor's rugged expanses.

Kodo Horn. In the Barrens, Kodo Horns are gathered from the roaming kodos. Tonga Runetotem uses them in herbal remedies for poisoned wildlife. Across the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem uses intact kodo horns in his herbal remedies. He works from the Crossroads, where the horns help strengthen his salves. Chips and fragments lack the strength he needs, so he gathers whole horns from mature kodos wandering the plains.

Kodo Liver. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn needs Kodo Liver for a strange ale. He learned to brew trogg ale from the wandering brewmaster Chen Stormstout. Kodos roam the Barrens, where tauren and predators hunt them for their hides and meat. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn uses a fresh Kodo Liver with thunderhawk saliva glands and lightning glands to make trogg ale. Chen Stormstout taught Drohn the recipe, and Drohn says the blend packs a potent kick for adventurous travelers. The ingredients come from the wilds of central Kalimdor.

Kodo Rock. Kodo Rock is a natural stone monument located in the plains of Red Cloud Mesa, between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. Standing quietly amid the grasses of Mulgore, it serves as an early pilgrimage site for young tauren shamans learning to commune with the spirits of the earth. Because of its modest silhouette against the rolling landscape, travelers must keep a keen eye out to spot it. Situated roughly halfway along the path connecting Camp Narache to the hostile quilboar territory of Brambleblade Ravine, Kodo Rock is marked by a patch of worn earth at its base. While it lacks the sheer grandeur of the towering bluffs surrounding Red Cloud Mesa, its distinct profile resembles the revered kodo beasts that wander the grasslands. For wandering tribesfolk, it acts as a quiet natural beacon in the windswept plains of Mulgore.

Kodo Roundup. At Scrabblescrew's Camp in Desolace, Smeed Scrabblescrew is expecting a caravan and wants five tamed kodos ready for it. You carry Smeed's kodo kombobulator out among the ancient, aged and dying kodos, and lead the ones it tames back to the camp. Bibbly believes no other goblin in Desolace knows how to turn a profit. Smeed Scrabblescrew disagrees: the one caravan willing to brave this land depends on Smeed, and Smeed has formed a partnership with Cork and Rigger. The caravan is due at the camp shortly.

Kodobane's Head. Near the Forgotten Pools, Barak Kodobane's severed head proves the cunning chieftain's death. The orc warlord Regthar Deathgate receives it as proof that the centaur threat there has been broken. Kolkar bands in the Barrens have long been divided, but ambitious warlords now threaten to gather them into an army. Barak Kodobane made his camp by the lush waters of the Forgotten Pools, where the oasis offers vital resources and nearby paths lie open to raids. Regthar Deathgate, stationed in a bunker west of the Crossroads, demands Kodobane's severed head as proof that this commander can no longer rally his kin against the Horde.

Kolkar Crag. Kolkar centaur watch the southern Durotar flats from Kolkar Crag, a gorge they have claimed for their raids. Warlord Kolkanis leads them against nearby Horde settlements. Kolkar centaur hold a fortified gorge in southern Durotar. They guard its natural choke points and watch the surrounding flats for openings in orc and Darkspear holdings. Scouts and marauders range from the crag, probing those defenses. For young warriors training in the Valley of Trials and patrols along the southern coast, this is the nearest organized centaur threat.

Kolkar Leaders. Kolkar Leaders begins a campaign led by the orc Regthar Deathgate to crush rising centaur warlords in the Barrens. The nomadic Kolkar have plagued the tauren for generations, but newly emerged chieftains are organizing their disorganized bands into a genuine military threat. Regthar tasks champions of the Horde with cutting down Barak Kodobane at the Forgotten Pools before his influence can spread. For countless years, the horse-bodied centaur have terrorized Kalimdor, driving the nomadic tauren nearly to extinction before Thrall's Horde arrived to turn the tide. In the Barrens, the dominant Kolkar tribe generally roams in scattered, fractured marauding parties. Recently, however, aggressive chieftains have begun uniting the disparate bands, turning simple raiding parties into a cohesive military threat capable of contesting the Horde's fortified outposts.

Kolkar clan. The Kolkar are an aggressive clan of centaur native to central Kalimdor, claiming descent from the legendary first Khan, Kolk. They maintain strongholds in Desolace and across the Barrens, frequently raiding Horde settlements and fighting anyone who crosses their path. The Kolkar take their name from Khan Kolk, the legendary first centaur khan born from the union of Zaetar and Theradras. Driven by a deep hatred for other races and their fellow centaur clans alike, the Kolkar distinguish themselves by their red markings and an absolute refusal to form alliances. Historically based out of their ancient village in eastern Desolace, the restless spirit of Khan Kolk still wanders the subterranean depths of their ancestral lands.

Kor'ghan. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan watches over remedies and toxins. The Darkspear troll stands outside Rekkul's Poisons and seeks help preparing antidotes for Durotar’s venomous predators. Kor'ghan keeps watch over remedies and toxins outside Rekkul's Poisons in Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow. From the capital, he sends travelers into Durotar’s red canyons to gather venomous components from scorpids. He needs them to prepare antidotes for the dangers of the wilderness.

Kormek's Hut. Kormek's Hut is a remote, ramshackle dwelling sitting amid the barren flats of north-central Desolace. Despite its desolate surroundings and mysterious namesake, it currently shelters an eccentric pair: an oddly peaceful cultist and a goblin obsessed with harvesting kodo bones. Perched out in the arid wastes of north-central Desolace, this small hovel is named after a figure whose whereabouts and identity remain completely unknown. Instead of Kormek, travelers stumbling upon the hut encounter an unusual pairing living out in the middle of nowhere: Willow and Bibbly F'utzbuckle. Inside the hut sits Willow, a member of the otherwise hostile and nihilistic Twilight's Hammer who curiously treats outsiders with calm hospitality. Outside, a pen littered with sun-bleached kodo bones serves as the personal dance floor and staging ground for Bibbly, an excitable goblin captivated by the commercial potential of bone scavenging.

Korran. At the Crossroads, Korran watches the Barrens for threats to the Horde. The Darkspear troll serves Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar and studies the silithid emerging across the scrublands. At the Crossroads, Korran watches for threats beyond the quilboar and centaur clans. Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar stationed the troll scout there to observe changes in the land. Korran coordinates the gathering of intelligence for the Horde's leadership.

Kravel Koalbeard. Kravel Koalbeard is a scheming dwarven entrepreneur and con artist stationed out at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Rather than cheering purely for the love of the sport, he views the fierce gnome and goblin racing rivalry as a golden opportunity to fill his pockets. From scavenging stray machine parts to fixing race results through blackmail and booze, Kravel is always hunting for his next profitable scheme. While most spectators and crew members at the Mirage Raceway are consumed by mechanical rivalries and the roar of rocket engines, Kravel Koalbeard has his eyes squarely on everyone's coin purses. He is an opportunist who operates in the dusty cracks of the raceway encampment, quick to offer contracts and favors that rarely have clean motives. Kravel sees the high-stakes friction between gnome and goblin engineers not as an inspiring competition, but as a fertile ground for extortion, sabotage, and theft.

Kravel's Crate. Kravel's Crate is a heavy package dispatched by Kravel Koalbeard from the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Destined for the Nesingwary expedition in Stranglethorn Vale, it contains specialized hunting ammunition designed to bring down the jungle's deadliest game. Handed out by the shrewd entrepreneur Kravel Koalbeard at the Mirage Raceway, Kravel's Crate represents an unfinished business transaction across continents. Ordered weeks prior by a wealthy dwarven patron, the shipment was delayed long enough for its buyer to depart Kalimdor entirely. Rather than lose out on the favor of a wealthy customer who already paid for forwarding, Kravel entrusts passing adventurers to haul the crate all the way to northern Stranglethorn Vale.

Krazek's Cookery. Corporal Kaleb's mechanical cooking pot, bought off a goblin trader in Booty Bay, was a marvel until it broke. Kaleb asks you to take it back to the goblin Krazek for mending. Corporal Kaleb does most of the cooking for the camp. It used to be heavy work until Kaleb bought a mechanical pot off a goblin trader in Booty Bay, and the pot spared Kaleb hour after hour. Then it broke. Krazek's Crock Pot must go back to the goblin Krazek to be fixed, and Kaleb hopes you will carry it there.

Kreenig Snarlsnout's Tusk. At the Crossroads, Thork seeks proof that Kreenig Snarlsnout has fallen. His tusk marks the end of the Razormane leader's attacks on Horde caravans in the northern Barrens. Horde caravans traveling west from Durotar face constant attacks in the Barrens. Those raids grew bolder under Kreenig Snarlsnout, a fierce Razormane leader. Thork, commander of the Crossroads watch, ordered Kreenig killed to disrupt the quilboars' coordination. His tusk offers proof that the leader is dead and insults the Razormane, weakening their resolve and leaving their fighters without central direction.

Kreldig Ungor. Kreldig Ungor is an enterprising dwarven operative representing Reclaimers Inc., stationed high among the crags of Nijel's Point in Desolace. Tasked with managing field operations in the barren wasteland, he hires Alliance adventurers to recover lost cargo and secure valuable local reagents. His salvage and recovery contracts make him a central contact for travelers navigating the hostile region. Nijel's Point offers the Alliance a rare sanctuary amid the blighted canyons of Desolace, making it an ideal staging ground for commercial opportunists like Kreldig Ungor. Representing Reclaimers Inc., Kreldig has ventured far from the safety of Khaz Modan into a desolate wilderness contested by centaur clans, demons, and the Horde. Where others see ruin and ash, Kreldig sees untapped profit and lost assets ripe for recovery.

Krolg. Krolg is an uncorrupted furbolg living in an isolated hut south of Mystral Lake in Ashenvale. Formerly a member of the Foulweald tribe, he was cast out by his kin, who fell to demonic madness, and will only speak with those who appear to him in furbolg form. While most of the Foulweald furbolgs in Ashenvale have succumbed to the demonic taint left behind by the Burning Legion, Krolg remains lucid and untouched by madness. Residing in a secluded shelter south of Mystral Lake, he keeps a cautious vigil over the forest. Having witnessed the tragic descent of his brethren into senseless violence, he refuses to interact with outsiders at face value, speaking only with beings that appear as kin.

Krom Stoutarm. Krom Stoutarm is a dwarven scholar and warlock found deep within the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Unlike most of his kin who delve solely into ancient stone and titan relics, Krom studies darker, arcane texts and demonic rituals. He acts as an indispensable contact for Alliance warlocks seeking esoteric knowledge across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. The Hall of Explorers is typically known for dwarven archaeologists obsessed with picks, shovels, and titan artifacts. Krom Stoutarm cuts an unusual figure among them. Lurking in the Library surrounded by massive tomes, he pursues occult lore and the binding rites of demonic summoners. His presence in Ironforge demonstrates that while warlock arts are widely distrusted, scholar-practitioners who study the forbidden arts still operate within the mountain city's halls.

Krusk. Krusk is an orc scout stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Dispatched directly under Warchief Thrall's orders to investigate the Syndicate and recover relics from the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he now coordinates reconnaissance and rescue efforts after his initial infiltration was ambushed. When Warchief Thrall turned his attention back to the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he dispatched Krusk and a small strike team to scout Syndicate activity and retrieve relics tied to the fortress's grim past. However, the human outlaws proved more entrenched and coordinated than anticipated. An ambush inside Durnholde's crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scout squad. Krusk managed to fight his way out, but his comrades were taken captive: Drull and Tog'thar were locked away within the ruins, while the expedition's leader, Gol'dir, was moved to another Syndicate hold. Regrouping at Tarren Mill, Krusk now directs Horde adventurers to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and liberate his trapped comrades.

Kul Tiras. Kul Tiras is an insular maritime human kingdom situated on an island archipelago in the Great Sea, west of Dun Morogh and Baradin Bay. Renowned for possessing the mightiest navy in Azeroth, it served as a cornerstone of the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. Following the fracturing of the old Alliance and tragic losses in Kalimdor, the island realm has largely receded into isolated waters. Kul Tiras blossomed into an unmatched seafaring power, sustained by an industrious merchant marine, rich fishing grounds, and a naval armada without peer in human history.

Kuray'bin. Kuray'bin is a Darkspear jungle troll scout stationed at a guard post outside Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He watches the surrounding forest trails for night elf scouts sneaking close to the Horde encampment. Positioned just outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin keeps watch against Alliance infiltration in the deep woods of Ashenvale. The Silverwing Sentinels constantly patrol the surrounding canopy, sending agile outrunners across the border to gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Knowing that unmonitored scouts quickly become ambushing forces, Kuray'bin directs capable Horde fighters to hunt down the outrunners before they can report back to Silverwing Outpost.

Kurzen's Compound. Kurzen's Compound is a heavily fortified human settlement tucked into the hills of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Established by an expedition dispatched from Stormwind under Colonel Kurzen, the outpost has devolved into a rogue camp of cutthroats and wild beasts following their commander's descent into madness. What began as an official expedition into the untamed jungles of Stranglethorn turned into a nightmare when Colonel Kurzen lost his mind. Rather than fulfilling Stormwind's mission, the garrison broke away from the kingdom's authority, cutting ties with the crown and descending into tyranny. Today, the compound operates like a mercenary stronghold, complete with a functional lumber mill, stables for training captured Stranglethorn panthers and tigers as weapons of war, and an extensive cave complex known as the Stockpile where the rogue soldiers stash their plundered supplies.

Kurzen's Mystery. Brother Nimetz at the Rebel Camp wants to know what turned Colonel Kurzen to depravity. Suspecting that troll magic holds him, Nimetz sends you to the troll ruins of Stranglethorn to copy the legends written on four tablets. Colonel Kurzen was once a great and noble man, and Brother Nimetz means to learn what caused his fall into depravity. Nimetz suspects troll magic has a hold on the colonel. To test that, the old troll legends must be read, and they are carved on four tablets hidden among the troll ruins of Stranglethorn. You are asked to copy the markings from each tablet and carry the copies back.

Kuz's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Kuz's Skull marks the end of a feared Razormane raider. Kuz came from Razorfen Kraul and helped lead attacks on Horde outposts before a captive former kin sought vengeance. Kuz, Nak, and their chieftain Lok Orcbane led Razormane attacks across the southern Barrens. Sent from Razorfen Kraul, the three raiders struck travelers and settlements such as the Crossroads. Their betrayal of Mangletooth, a fellow quilboar, turned one of their own against them. They left Mangletooth to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo. From that cage, he revealed Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to kill the raider and take her head.

Kyle's Gone Missing!. Kyle's Gone Missing! is a local quest in Bloodhoof Village where Ahab Wheathoof asks passing adventurers to find his wayward dog, Kyle the Frenzied. Feeding the hungry pup a cut of tender strider meat soothes his temper and ensures his safe return home. In Bloodhoof Village, elder Ahab Wheathoof worries over his wayward pet, Kyle the Frenzied. While the title might sound alarming to outsiders, Kyle is Ahab's prized puppy who has slipped away onto the grassy plains of Mulgore. Ahab asks travelers passing through the settlement to track down his unruly companion and offer him a hearty meal to calm his wild spirits.

Kzan Thornslash. In the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to new Horde recruits. He is an orc merchant in Durotar. Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to young orcs and Darkspear trolls in the Valley of Trials. They are taking their first steps as Horde warriors. He offers basic hand axes, shortswords, clubs, and staves for recruits facing local wildlife and hazards.

Laced Pumpkin. A Laced Pumpkin is an ordinary gourd treated with a lethal concoction developed by Apothecary Johaan in Brill. Handed to a starving, imprisoned Scarlet Crusader under the guise of sustenance, it serves as a live field test for the Forsaken's growing arsenal of alchemical weapons. To the untrained eye, the laced pumpkin appears to be ordinary produce salvaged from the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades. Under the supervision of Apothecary Johaan in Brill, however, the vegetable is treated with experimental toxins designed to realize the full potential of undeath. The Royal Apothecary Society constantly seeks new weapons to repel both the Scourge in the north and living human forces advancing from the south, turning even simple harvest goods into vectors for infection and chemical death.

Lack of Surplus. Dar is gathering supplies for the outpost by the beach in the east, where Tok'Kar has little time to spare between guard shifts and cooking for the soldiers. Dar asks you to bring Tok'Kar a shipment of sawtooth meat. Dar is collecting supplies for the outpost by the beach in the east. Tok'Kar does what is possible there, but guard shifts and cooking for the soldiers leave little time in the day. The soldiers enjoy cooking sawtooth meat when they can get it, and Dar has had no time to send them another shipment.

Lack of Surplus. Tok'Kar and the soldiers on the coast are stationed to guard Stonard against murlocs, or to send warning when the force is too large. Tok'Kar wants six sawtooth snapper claws and offers one of the outpost's weapons in thanks. With murlocs a threat along the coast, Tok'Kar and the soldiers are posted here to protect Stonard, or to warn it if the force is too large. That leaves little time for rest, and Tok'Kar could use more help. The claws of sawtooth snappers make fine weapons when properly prepared. Tok'Kar asks for six, and offers one of the outpost's weapons in return, grateful for the meat and the company.

Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once one of the night elf druids who followed Naralex in his ambitious effort to heal the Barrens, she was lost when her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare. Her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a drive to remake the land to match that twisted dream. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was one of Naralex's druids. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she followed him into the caverns. Her loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering her sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession.

Lady Sarevess. Lady Sarevess is a twisted naga sorceress dwelling within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, where she dabbles in dark sorceries. Within the Pool of Ask'ar, Lady Sarevess conducts her rituals in a flooded grotto of the ruined temple. A very twisted spellcaster, she dabbles in dark magic while the Twilight's Hammer cultists who also haunt the sunken temple pursue their own worship deeper in the cavern.

Laird. At Auberdine's inn, Laird sells fish and cooking supplies to travelers along Darkshore's coast. Laird sells fish and supplies inside Auberdine's inn. Sailors, locals, and travelers come to him while Darkshore's waters churn with dangers greater than those along Teldrassil's sheltered shores. For anglers willing to cast from the misty beaches, the local catch can bring a handsome profit.

Laird's Response. Along Teldrassil's shores, Laird's Response carries a puzzle for Nessa Shadowsong. The fish there are larger and more plentiful than those along mainland Darkshore. Laird compares catches from across the Veiled Sea. Fish from Teldrassil's coast are larger and more plentiful than those from Darkshore's mainland beaches. In his reply to Nessa Shadowsong, Laird of Auberdine offers a theory: the newly planted World Tree's unusual presence and vitality may be changing the surrounding sea life. Travelers carry his letter across the water to Rut'theran Village, where the fisherfolk greet the news with wonder and quiet curiosity.

Lake Al'Ameth. South of Dolanaar, Lake Al'Ameth's shores have turned perilous as the local plant life grows violent. Once a quiet haven with little more than a wooden jetty, the lake is one of Teldrassil's largest freshwater bodies. At Lake Al'Ameth, swarms of timberlings and timberling sprouts prowl the water's edge. The lake lies just south of Dolanaar, where its calm waters and sparse settlement offer little sign of the danger ashore. An unnatural sickness spreading through Teldrassil has driven the plant life into a frenzy. Druids and researchers from Dolanaar send travelers to gather seeds and kill the aggressive creatures before the corruption spreads deeper into the forest.

Lake Creeper Moss. Lake Creeper Moss is an organic compound harvested from the aquatic creepers dwelling among the Dawning Isles in Lake Lordamere. It serves as a vital reagent sought by the Royal Apothecary Society for their efforts to engineer a lethal new plague. Grown along the hides of the vicious freshwater beasts that prowl the southern Dawning Isles of Lake Lordamere, Lake Creeper Moss carries unique properties shaped by Lordaeron's blighted waters. Apothecary Berard, before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, documented it in his journal, noting that the moss resembled trace materials on the fossils of creatures killed by an ancient plague in the lake. When recovered by Forsaken agents, samples are dispatched directly to the Apothecarium in the Undercity to fuel Master Apothecary Faranell's dark research.

Lake Elune'ara. Lake Elune'ara is the shimmering, sacred body of water that occupies the heart of Moonglade. Revering the Moon Goddess Elune, the lake serves as a place of spiritual reflection for the Cenarion Circle, though deep within its murky floor lies the dormant, corrupted demigod Omen. Framed by the moonlit groves of Moonglade, Lake Elune'ara provides serene waters said to be blessed by the White Lady herself. The lake lies at the spiritual center of the druidic haven, bordered by Nighthaven to the north and the shrine grounds of the Cenarion Circle. Initiates have long plumbed its tranquil depths to retrieve long-lost relics, attuning themselves to the currents of nature as they seek harmony with the land.

Lake Everstill. Lake Everstill is the expansive azure body of water dominating the heart of the Redridge Mountains, flanking the town of Lakeshire. Once celebrated for tranquil fishing and clean mountain runoff, its shores and waters have lately turned treacherous due to aggressive murloc tribes and predatory lake beasts. Spanning the central basin of Redridge, Lake Everstill provides the scenic backdrop and vital waterway for the township of Lakeshire. Its crystal-clear waters drain eastward toward the looming heights of Stonewatch. Spanned by the town's central bridge, the lake has long sustained local trade and quiet anglers, though anyone walking the shoreline today will find its peaceful reputation thoroughly shattered by encroaching wilderness threats.

Lake Falathim. Lake Falathim is a tranquil body of water nestled in the forested hills of western Ashenvale, southwest of Maestra's Post.
