text.enUS: Never Ask Me About My Business. Narain Soothfancy has a plan he refuses to explain, and it calls for a chicken of five hundred pounds. You head for Gadgetzan to speak with Dirge Quikcleave, who can get you started on finding a fitting bird. Narain Soothfancy wants no more questions about his business, which deals in things you could never hope to grasp. The planning is his and the fetching is yours. As he said before, the plan needs a chicken of five hundred pounds, and Dirge Quikcleave in the Gadgetzan inn can point you toward one.

New Horde. The New Horde is the modern coalition forged under Warchief Thrall, departing from the bloodthirsty, demon-corrupted Old Horde of the First and Second Wars. Founded upon shamanic tradition, honor, and mutual survival, it unites the liberated orcs, the Darkspear trolls, the tauren tribes of Kalimdor, and a tenuous pact with the Forsaken in Lordaeron. The original Horde was a weapon crafted by the Burning Legion and the Shadow Council, fueling the orcs with demonic bloodlust and driving them across the Dark Portal. After the Second War ended in devastation, surviving orcs were rounded up into Alliance internment camps, sinking into a soul-draining lethargy. Through the efforts of Orgrim Doomhammer, Grommash Hellscream, and the young shaman Thrall, the orcs cast off their demonic shackles, rediscovered their ancestral shamanism, and fought their way to freedom.

New Life. New Life is a restorative Horde quest offered by Tammra Windfield in Sun Rock Retreat. Following the collection of enchanted seeds, the player journeys west into the ashen ruins of the Charred Vale to sow them into fertile earth. This ritual effort aims to spark the land's recovery amidst hostile elementals and harpies. The Charred Vale stands as a tragic testament to recent devastation, choked by soot, furious fire elementals, and scavenging harpies. Tammra Windfield refuses to let the region surrender to ruin. Relying on the ancient resilience of the Earth Mother, she dispatches travelers into the heart of the blackened valley to seek out Gaea Dirt Mounds—patches of fertile topsoil that survived the inferno.

News for Fizzle. Martek the Exiled in the Badlands has news about indurium for Fizzle Brassbolts. You carry Martek's message back to the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Martek reports that indurium stands up to heat remarkably well, and believes it suits Fizzle's pistons. Flakes will not do, though: Fizzle needs real indurium ore, dug out of the depths of Uldaman at the northern edge of the Badlands, which Martek names as the true source of indurium. Martek asks you to pass on regards and repeat all of this to Fizzle Brassbolts.

News of Dogran. A missing grunt named Dogran leaves Zankaja waiting in Orgrimmar. His mate has heard nothing for days, so she sends you to question his superior, Gazrog, at the Crossroads. For a warlock, the search also serves a ritual to bind a succubus. Zankaja waits on the bluffs of Orgrimmar, fearing for her mate Dogran. He was sent to the Crossroads on an honorable promotion, but his return is overdue and she has heard nothing for days. She asks you to seek news from his commander, Gazrog. She does not know that dark arts are at work behind the search.

News of Dogran. This quest sends Horde adventurers deep into the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains to contact the Darkspear troll Ken'zigla at Malaka'jin. An injured grunt from Camp Taurajo named Dogran lies wounded, and the first runner sent to fetch a lifesaving herbal draught never returned. Dogran, a Horde grunt stationed at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens, was grievously wounded during a skirmish against entrenched quilboar. The grunts with him made it back and tried to rescue him, but his wounds had festered so badly that they were afraid to move him without patching him up first. Desperate for a potent remedy, Taurajo sent word north to the Crossroads, hoping to procure a traditional healing draught prepared by the jungle trolls of Malaka'jin.

Nibbled-On Book. The Nibbled-On Book is a volume from Northshire Abbey's library recovered from kobold scavengers in Northshire Valley. Bearing the tooth marks of a confused or ravenous creature, it must be returned to Brother Paxton to preserve the abbey's modest collection. Among the subterranean pests troubling Northshire Valley, kobolds are notorious scavengers known for dragging off anything left unguarded. When an adventurer recovers a chewed tome dropped by a slain kobold, it becomes evident that the creature was not merely hoarding shiny trinkets, but actively trying to gnaw through the cover and parchment. The text clearly originates from the library shelves of nearby Northshire Abbey, bearing marks from the pests' voracious appetites.

Night Run. Night Run is a small, secluded satyr outpost perched atop a cliff-ringed bluff in east-central Ashenvale. Inhabited by the demonic Felmusk satyr, it serves as a corrupted encampment harboring dark soul magic within ancient elven ruins. Night Run is the smallest and most isolated of Ashenvale's three major satyr strongholds, alongside Xavian and Satyrnaar. Sheltered among crumbling elven stonework and broken pillars, the settlement juts outward on a high ridge bounded by steep, impassable cliffs. Reaching it requires a circuitous trek along the Falfarren River near the waters of Xavian or navigating a precarious northern ledge above Raynewood Retreat. Despite its modest size, the enclave poses a severe danger: the Felmusk satyr who dwell here work in concert with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, anchoring twisted soulgems to pool demonic essence within the forest.

Night Watch. The Night Watch is the beleaguered town militia responsible for defending Darkshire and the shadowy roads of Duskwood. Abandoned by the House of Nobles in Stormwind, these local volunteers stand alone against roaming undead, feral worgen, and lurking necromancy. Led by Commander Althea Ebonlocke, they rely heavily on visiting adventurers to keep darkness from overtaking their home. When foul magic overtook the once-vibrant Grand Hamlet and turned the forest into Duskwood, the kingdom of Stormwind turned its back. Following King Varian Wrynn's disappearance, the royal garrison was pulled back to the capital. Stripped of official royal troops and supplies, the townsfolk formed their own volunteer militia—the Night Watch—swearing to hold the borders of Darkshire against the creeping horrors of the woods.

Night Web's Hollow. Night Web's Hollow is an early assignment from Executor Arren to clear out the spiders infesting a nearby gold mine northwest of Deathknell. Facing critical shortages of raw materials, the fledgling Forsaken need the mine's wealth to sustain their settlement and war effort. Newly risen recruits are sent into the tangled cavern to cull the arachnid infestation piece by piece. Survival for the newly risen Forsaken involves more than just defending against the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders. Building a fledgling society requires raw resources, and precious metals like gold were scarce in northern Lordaeron even at the height of the Alliance's strength. Executor Arren, overseeing operations in Deathknell, recognizes that the Forsaken cannot hope to arm, equip, and establish themselves without secured wealth.

Night Web's Hollow. Night Web's Hollow is a sunken vale and abandoned gold mine located just northwest of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Heavily overrun with arachnids, it serves as a testing ground for freshly awakened Forsaken sent to cull the vermin and prove their combat readiness. Tucked away in the northern hills of Deathknell, Night Web's Hollow was once an ordinary human gold mine before the plague swept through Lordaeron. In the aftermath of the kingdom's fall, the shafts were entirely abandoned to nature. Today, thick strands of webbing shroud the rock walls and suffocating shadows conceal a thriving colony of aggressive night web spiders. Freshly raised Forsaken are routinely dispatched into the hollow and its subterranean tunnels to cull the young and adult spiders so the Forsaken can regain access to the mine's gold.

Night elf. The night elves, or kaldorei, are an ancient and reclusive race native to the forests of northern Kalimdor. Once the masters of a sprawling magical empire, they abandoned arcane magic following the catastrophic War of the Ancients and turned to the worship of Elune and the path of druidism. In the wake of the Third War, having sacrificed their immortality to stop the Burning Legion, they joined the Alliance to defend their ancestral lands from Horde encroachment. Millennia ago, an inquisitive nocturnal tribe gathered around the shores of the Well of Eternity, a vast font of raw arcane energy. Over generations, the Well's cosmic magic transformed them into tall, violet-skinned, long-lived beings who called themselves the kaldorei—'children of the stars.' Guiding their early society were the moon goddess Elune and the forest demigod Cenarius, who nurtured their deep connection to the living wilds of Kalimdor.

Nighthaven. Nighthaven is a secluded settlement resting on the northern shores of Lake Elune'ara in Moonglade. Serving as the heart of the Cenarion Circle, it is a haven where night elf and tauren druids study together in peace beyond the factional wars of Azeroth. Built with traditional night elf architecture along the calm shores of Lake Elune'ara, Nighthaven is a tranquil retreat largely secluded from the outside world. Here, moonwells cast a gentle glow over groves and halls dedicated to preserving the natural balance. As the primary enclave of the Cenarion Circle, it provides trainers, herbalists, and specialized suppliers for druidic initiates. The settlement maintains a strict neutrality, welcoming practitioners regardless of whether their home loyalties lie with the Alliance or the Horde.

Nightmare Shard. The Nightmare Shard is a crystalline relic handed to couriers by Falla Sagewind after she examines a tainted glowing shard recovered from the Wailing Caverns. Containing the pure, disturbed essence of the Emerald Dream, it carries a troubling vision that prompts immediate warning and secrecy among senior druids in Darnassus and Thunder Bluff. When Falla Sagewind inspects the mysterious glowing shard unearthed deep within the Wailing Caverns, she realizes its energy is far darker than anticipated. Rather than mirroring the serene vitality of the Emerald Dream, the fragment reflects a twisting, unnatural affliction—a waking nightmare. Fearful of what its presence implies, she binds this tainted essence into the Nightmare Shard and commands that it be ferried straight to elder leaders of the Cenarion Circle without delay.

Nightmare Vale. Nightmare Vale is a shadowed hollow nestled in southwestern Tirisfal Glades, just west of the Crusader's Outpost. Once a lush forest haven, its trees have withered under the blight, and vicious predators now roam among the twisted trunks. Before the Third War, this valley was a verdant part of the Tirisfal countryside, filled with songbirds and standard woodland game. In the wake of the Scourge's plague, the vegetation has blackened and rotted away. Ravenous darkhounds and massive vampire bats have devoured the native wildlife, turning the hollow into a grim haven for scavengers and beasts of prey.

name.esES: Colmillo de sable de la noche

text.enUS: Nightsaber Fang. In Teldrassil, hunters take fangs from the nightsabers prowling the forest. Woodland residents also seek these teeth as reagents. Nightsabers hunt beneath Teldrassil’s canopy, among the deadliest natural predators of northern Kalimdor. Night elves revere them for their agility, ferocity, and deep spiritual bond with Elune. A hunter who kills one can take its sharp fangs as proof of skill. Some figures in the forest seek those fangs for darker rites.

Nightsong Woods. Nightsong Woods forms the embattled eastern expanse of Ashenvale, reaching from Raynewood Retreat toward the borders of Azshara. It serves as the primary battleground between the night elves defending their sacred forest and the Warsong clan harvesting lumber for the Horde. Across its shadowed glades, ancient groves clash with fortified encampments amidst persistent demonic corruption. Stretching eastward across Ashenvale to Azshara, Nightsong Woods is defined by escalating violence. The Falfarren River bisects the western reaches, creating a volatile boundary between Alliance settlements and Horde encroachments. Further east, the forest fractures into heavily disputed territories where Splintertree Post coordinates Horde campaigns against the Silverwing Sentinels. Orcish axes continuously clear southern groves to fuel the Horde's expansion, leaving clear-cut swaths that infuriate the Kaldorei. Adding to the peril, satyr strongholds like Satyrnaar and Xavian, alongside demonic remnants in Demon Fall Canyon and Felfire Hill, taint the eastern canopies.

Nijel's Point. Nijel's Point is a fortified Alliance and Cenarion Circle redoubt perched high on the northern bluffs of Desolace. Tucked safely away from the blighted valleys below, it serves as the sole safe haven for Alliance travelers, researchers, and soldiers navigating the harsh wasteland. Carved into the sheer cliffs bordering the Stonetalon Mountains, Nijel's Point stands well above the gray dust and marauding centaur packs of Desolace. The settlement is held by a detachment of the Stormwind Army under Captain Pentigast, charged with monitoring the violent clan wars that threaten Alliance interests across southern Kalimdor. Its high elevation and narrow access trails make it readily defensible, providing a secure staging ground for couriers, scouts, and griffin riders travelling between Stonetalon Peak, Theramore, and Feathermoon Stronghold.

Nikova Raskol. In Old Town, Nikova Raskol grieves for her murdered grandson. The elderly Stormwind townswoman seeks justice against the Defias Brotherhood rioters held in the Stockade. Nikova Raskol wanders Old Town, carrying the grief of a recent loss. Her beloved grandson, Mac, was slain by Defias Brotherhood brigands. While the kingdom faces treason on a grand scale, Nikova bears the private cost of the Brotherhood's lawless rampage.

Nip 'Em in the Bud. Nip 'Em in the Bud is a mission directed by Earthseer Farsen to eliminate Dark Iron spies infiltrating Dun Morogh. The clandestine operatives have been spotted lurking near Ironband's Compound, threatening the security of the Bronzebeard homeland. Dun Morogh has long been a fortified sanctuary for the Ironforge dwarves, but the ancient enmity between the dwarven clans never truly sleeps. Dark Iron infiltrators have slipped through the high passes and snowy crags, skulking suspiciously close to vital excavations and settlements. Earthseer Farsen recognizes that even a few hidden observers can presage a devastating strike, calling on stalwart defenders of the Alliance to root them out before their schemes take hold.

Nissa Firestone. Nissa Firestone is a dwarven physician stationed above the bustle of the Great Forge in Ironforge. She serves as an instructor in field medicine, teaching travelers and soldiers how to dress wounds and bind trauma. Amid the clanging metal and blistering heat of the Great Forge, Nissa Firestone practices medicine from the upper floor of the Ironforge Physician shop. While dwarven warriors are famed for their endurance, even stone-hard skin splits against blade and claw. Nissa ensures that those heading out into the snows of Dun Morogh or beyond know how to keep themselves and their allies alive with basic bandaging and field dressings.

Nissa's Remains. Nissa's Remains are the recovered earthly remnants of Nissa Agamand, a noblewoman of the once-wealthy Agamand dynasty in northern Tirisfal Glades. Slain and raised as mindless servants of the Scourge during the Third War, she and her family are now hunted down by former laborers seeking vengeance. Before the Third War, the Agamand family stood as the wealthiest and most influential dynasty in Tirisfal Glades, operating prosperous mills across the northern hills. When the Plague of Undeath crept across Lordaeron, the family patriarchs stubbornly refused to evacuate. Instead, they fortified their estates and convinced their retainers and laborers to stand their ground. That arrogance cost everyone their lives. The Agamands fell to the Scourge, rising not with their proud independence intact, but as shambling, mindless thralls bound to the Lich King's will.

Nitroglycerin. At Bael Modan, Nitroglycerin helps the dwarves drive their excavation through tauren lands. Their soldiers and officers carry the volatile chemical, which can also be used against the fortress. Bael Modan's dwarves dig into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tauren with heavy drillers and volatile chemicals. At the excavation site and its fortified keep, they keep nitroglycerin close to blast deep holes and break apart hills. Soldiers and officers, including Lord Cyrik Blackforge, carry vials of the fluid as the digging continues.

Noble Deaths. Magistrate Henry Maleb fears that the Syndicate's leaders are bent on Southshore's ruin and wants them struck down before their plans come to pass. You are to head north into the Alterac Mountains, to Strahnbrad's ruins, which the Syndicate is thought to use as a headquarters. After Foreboding Plans, Magistrate Henry Maleb in Southshore wants the Syndicate's leadership dealt with before its plans are realized. The Syndicate's cutthroats answer to former Alterac nobles, who may be hiding as ordinary agents. A noble can be known by the signet ring worn. Maleb asks for seven Alterac signet rings to be brought back to him in Southshore, and he thinks the Syndicate has made a headquarters of Strahnbrad's ruins, up north in the Alterac Mountains.

Noboru the Cudgel. For months, Noboru has tormented the Draenei at the Harborage. Noboru's cudgel stands as a mark of the cruelty the lost ones have dealt them, and you are asked to bring it to the leader of the Harborage. Noboru has tormented the Harborage's Draenei for months. The cudgel has come to stand for the cruelty the lost ones have dealt them. With it in hand, you carry it to the leader of the Harborage.

Nogg. Nogg is a goblin engineer operating out of a workshop in the Valley of Honor in Orgrimmar. He offers tinkering expertise and specialized craftsmanship to the Horde, notably analyzing strange mechanical salvage recovered from deep within Gnomeregan. Tucked away in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Nogg runs an independent engineering workshop catering to adventurers and craftsmen alike. While the surrounding city relies heavily on traditional orcish steel and brute strength, Nogg provides the specialized mechanical finesse that only a goblin can offer. He maintains a keen interest in foreign contraptions and tech, happily examining curious trinkets and mechanical oddities dragged back from Alliance lands or subterranean ruins.

Nogg's Ring Redo. In Orgrimmar, Nogg works to improve a ring recovered from Gnomeregan. He asks for rare materials and information about Dark Iron dwarves, eager to prove goblin craft superior to gnomish design. You bring a cleaned gold ring from Gnomeregan to Nogg's workshop in the Valley of Honor. The goblin engineer takes one look at its modest gnomish craft and offers a bargain. Bring raw materials and a modest fee, and he will add an intricate lattice of silver and moss agate to the band, meant to amplify the magic within it.

Noggenfogger Elixir. Marin Noggenfogger in Gadgetzan takes the Violet Powder to mix into the dew, and asks you to come back to him in a moment, once his fabulous elixir is perfected. Marin, who has the dew and now the powder, sets about mixing the one into the other. You are to wait a short while and then speak to Marin again, when the Noggenfogger Elixir should be ready.

Nondescript Letter. The Nondescript Letter is a sealed, unmarked missive entrusted to newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell. Handed over by Calvin Montague under the guise of an errand, it directs the bearer down the road to Innkeeper Renee at the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Newly arisen Forsaken looking to venture beyond Deathknell are approached by Calvin Montague, a shifty rogue lingering near the village perimeter. Claiming to be weary from fighting mindless zombies and arachnids, Calvin asks travelers to carry a plain, unmarked envelope along the eastward road to Brill. Addressed casually to an innkeeper named Renee, the letter serves as an excuse to push travelers out of the valley and toward the Gallows' End Tavern, though Calvin's promises of rich compensation ring hollow from the start.

Nordrassil. Nordrassil, the 'Crown of the Heavens,' is the original World Tree planted atop Mount Hyjal to shield the second Well of Eternity. Blessed by the Great Dragon Aspects, it granted the night elves ageless immortality and a deep connection to the Emerald Dream for ten thousand years. Its sacrifice during the climax of the Third War broke Archimonde's assault, leaving the tree wounded and the night elves mortal. Ten thousand years ago, in the ashes of the Great Sundering, Illidan Stormrage cast vials of the original Well of Eternity into a mountaintop lake atop Mount Hyjal, birthing a new font of arcane power. To prevent this raw magic from corrupting the world or drawing the Burning Legion anew, the Dragon Aspect Alexstrasza planted an acorn from the Mother Tree, G'Hanir, directly over the waters. From it grew Nordrassil. The roots spread deep beneath Azeroth, sealing the Well's volatile energies and distributing gentle, life-giving vigor across the continents.

Nori Pridedrift. Nori Pridedrift is an enterprising dwarf peddling his piping-hot Scalding Mornbrew throughout snowy Coldridge Valley. He makes his living braving the cold to supply shivering mountaineers with their morning pick-me-up, often enlisting swift recruits to run deliveries while the drink remains steaming. Life in Coldridge Valley is harsh and bitterly cold, and nothing cuts through the chill quite like a draught of Scalding Mornbrew. Nori Pridedrift has carved out a living by brewing and distributing this hot, coffee-like morning drink across the frozen drifts. Because the brew must be consumed while still scalding to be fully appreciated, delivery is a race against the elements. Nori frequently recruits brisk couriers to sprint fresh draughts out to freezing sentries before the mountain air robs the brew of its heat. Just as important as the brew itself are his limited supplies of sturdy mugs, which he expects his runners to return promptly.

Nori's Mug. Nori's Mug is the personal drinking vessel of Nori Pridedrift, used to deliver scalding mornbrew across the frigid drifts of Dun Morogh. After delivering a warm drink to stave off the biting alpine chill, travelers are tasked with returning the empty cup to its thrifty owner. In the freezing mountain passes of Dun Morogh, a piping hot tankard of mornbrew is one of the few comforts capable of cutting through the bitter cold. Nori Pridedrift entrusts his mug to travelers delivering a fresh, steaming pour to Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar. Once drained, the sturdy vessel must make the trek back. As Nori notes, mugs do not grow on trees, and keeping track of hard-wearing dwarven dishware is essential business when hospitality meets snowy wilderness.

North Coast. The North Coast is a bleak, fog-shrouded stretch of shoreline marking the northern edge of Tirisfal Glades along the Great Sea. Tainted by the fall of Lordaeron, the cold beaches are littered with rotting marine life and aggressively defended by tribes of hostile murlocs. Before the Third War, these northern waters and stony beaches were part of the peaceful northern boundary of Lordaeron. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the continent, its corrupting blight seeped down the bluffs and poisoned the coast. The waters turned chill and murky, washing up the carcasses of giant sea creatures that now rot upon the sand amid the perennial coastal fog.

text.enUS: North Gate Outpost. North Gate Outpost is a fortified dwarven camp situated high in the North Gate Pass of Dun Morogh. Manning the rugged route between Ironforge's snowy heartland and Loch Modan, its mountaineers guard travelers against the hostile wildlife that infests the crags. Positioned in the middle of North Gate Pass, this small settlement serves as the northeastern threshold of Dun Morogh. Dwarven mountaineers stationed here keep the main roadway cleared of prowling beasts and monitor traffic heading through the mountain tunnels into Loch Modan. The harsh climate and steep ravines make patrol duty treacherous, and the garrison frequently calls upon travelers to scout the surrounding ridges for missing patrols and dangerous predators.

North Gate Pass. North Gate Pass is a vital mountain thoroughfare connecting the snowy crags of Dun Morogh with the rolling basin of Loch Modan. It forms the northern corridor through the Khaz Modan peaks, watched over by a fortified dwarven outpost. Travelers heading toward the northern lowlands of the Wetlands frequently traverse this high road. Carved into the sheer stone of Khaz Modan, North Gate Pass serves as the northern arterial link between the high, frozen valleys of Dun Morogh and the temperate waters of Loch Modan. Descending through steep mountain tunnels, travelers emerging from the west are greeted by the broad expanse of the loch valley. Because it sits within easy striking distance of the paths heading down into the Wetlands, the pass carries heavy traffic of dwarven messengers, merchants, and roaming adventurers. Its strategic value is anchored by the North Gate Outpost, where mountaineers keep vigilant watch against troggs and mountain predators.

North Tide's Hollow. North Tide's Hollow is a rugged wilderness pocket in Silverpine Forest located just north of the Sepulcher. Haunted by feral Moonrage worgen loyal to the rogue Archmage Arugal, the clearing serves as a base of operations for the beasts stalking the coastal woods. Tucked away in the dense timber north of the Forsaken settlement of the Sepulcher, North Tide's Hollow is dominated by the savage Moonrage pack. These feral worgen, brought into Lordaeron through the reckless sorcery of Archmage Arugal, have established crude encampments throughout the hollow. Built with only the barest necessities required by the hardy beasts, these rough shelters provide a forward staging ground dangerously close to Forsaken travel routes.

North Tide's Run. North Tide's Run is the windswept northwestern shoreline of Silverpine Forest, skirting the edge of the Great Sea. Marked by a half-sunken shipwreck, this stretch of sand is known as a secluded trial ground for traveling druids seeking harmony with the waters. Stretching along the northwest edge of Silverpine Forest, North Tide's Run consists of cold sand, pounding surf, and a strip of the Great Sea. Its most unmistakable landmark is a partially submerged shipwreck tilted precariously in the shallows near the beach.

Northdale. Northdale is a ruined settlement nestled north of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands, near the border of Quel'Thalas. Once a thriving northern township, it now lies broken and overrun by banshees, shadowy watchers, and corrupted elementals. It is most famous as the bitter crossroads where Taelan Fordring abandoned the Order of the Silver Hand to embrace the fanaticism of the Scarlet Crusade. Situated along the hills north of Light's Hope Chapel, Northdale was once a peaceful community along the northern highway leading toward Quel'Thalas. The Third War left it in shattered ruins, its hearths cold and its population slain or driven out. Today, wailing banshees drift through the crumbling masonry, while invisible Eyeless Watchers lurk in the dark to survey the cursed roads. Even the nearby lake has succumbed to the plague, its waters bubbling with twisted, corrupted water elementals.

Northfold Manor. Captain Nials, at Refuge Pointe, asks for help against the Syndicate holding Northfold Manor. Their hold on the land between the defenders of Stromgarde and Southshore makes it hard for supplies to arrive. Stromgarde has been carved up between the ogres, the Syndicate and the Alliance, and every faction fights the others to a bloody stalemate. The Alliance's forces dwindle while their enemies grow. The defenders need help from Southshore, but supplies are slow to arrive.

Northfold Manor. Northfold Manor is a dilapidated agricultural estate situated on the northwestern fringes of the Arathi Highlands. Once a prosperous human homestead before the collapse of Stromgarde, the grounds are now occupied by criminal operatives of the Syndicate engaging in unsettling, dark practices. Perched on the rolling highlands near the Thoradin's Wall passage, Northfold Manor once supported the kingdom of Stromgarde. In the chaos following the realm's fracturing, displaced Alteraci nobility and outlaws of the Syndicate claimed the manor house, barn, and fields as an operational base. Instead of tending crops, Syndicate mercenaries, highwaymen, and pathstalkers use the farmstead to stage ambushes along the roads and coordinate their presence across Arathi.

Northpass Tower. Northpass Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the northern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands along the road to Quel'Thalas. Shattered during the Third War, it still overlooks the northern road toward the elven lands. Built by the Kingdom of Lordaeron to guard the vital thoroughfare leading north into Quel'Thalas, Northpass Tower was reduced to a broken shell during the Scourge invasion. Despite its shattered stonework, the tower's elevated position retains immense tactical value, overlooking the blight-choked frontier between Stratholme's blighted outskirts and the distant elven lands.

name.frFR: Camp de bûcherons de la Crête du nord

text.enUS: Northridge Lumber Camp. Northridge Lumber Camp is an active lumber mill nestled in the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands near Hearthglen. Currently held and fortified by the Scarlet Crusade, it provides timber vital to sustaining their nearby strongholds. Both the Alliance and the Horde view the facility as a prime target to cripple the zealots' regional infrastructure. Situated just down the road from Hearthglen, the Northridge Lumber Camp serves as a vital logistics node for the Scarlet Crusade. Despite the lingering plague choking the surrounding forests, the camp fells and processes regional timber to construct fortifications, repair watchtowers, and furnish the crusade's war effort in Lordaeron. Heavily garrisoned by fanatical laborers and guards, the mill is fiercely protected against both the Scourge and outside trespassers.

Northshire Valley. Northshire Valley shelters Stormwind's newest defenders in northern Elwynn Forest. Natural barriers guard the peaceful valley, where ancient Northshire Abbey, fertile vineyards, and the rich Echo Ridge Mine sustain a pocket of the kingdom. Bandits, kobolds, and displaced predators now trouble its quiet pastures. Northshire Valley lies behind mountain ridges, with one road south through a fortified gatehouse toward Goldshire and the rest of Elwynn Forest. A clear river crosses the pastures and flows into Crystal Lake. At the valley's heart, ancient Northshire Abbey teaches the Holy Light and trains recruits under the Knights of the Silver Hand and seasoned veterans. Beyond its walls, the fertile Northshire Vineyards and Echo Ridge Mine make this a self-sustaining pocket of Stormwind territory, far from the wars beyond its ridges.

Northshire Vineyards. At Northshire Vineyards, Defias brigands have seized the fields east of Northshire Abbey. The grapes once supplied wine to the clerics, but now the thieves plunder the harvest and threaten local farmers. Northshire Vineyards lie east across the stream from Northshire Abbey, where workers such as Milly Osworth once tended the fields. Defias Brotherhood brigands now hold the acreage, led by Garrick Padfoot. The thieves plunder the harvest and strip local farmers of their livelihood. Their occupation gives new Brotherhood recruits a foothold close to the abbey.

Not Dead Yet. 'Not Dead Yet' is an urgent plea from Eralya, a mortally wounded night elf discovered after a disastrous mission toward the Oracle Tree. Overwhelmed by vicious harpies, she begs travelers to deliver word of her patrol's fate to Byancie in Dolanaar. It highlights the deadly threats encroaching upon the woodland paths of Teldrassil. A desperate plea in the wilderness of Teldrassil, 'Not Dead Yet' centers on Eralya, a wounded night elf messenger found bleeding and clinging to life. Sent on a crucial mission toward the sacred Oracle Tree alongside her sisters, the patrol was violently ambushed and cut down by encroaching harpies. With no help coming and her own strength fading rapidly, Eralya entrusts passing travelers with carrying urgent news back to safety.

Notched Rib. A Notched Rib is a bone trophy harvested from the ranks of mindless undead wandering Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill collects these scarred remains as proof of efforts to break the Scourge's foothold at the Agamand Mills. The Scourge forces massing across the northern fields of Tirisfal Glades consist of reanimated skeletons clad in ruined armor. Among their ranks, Cracked Skull Soldiers and Rattlecage Soldiers throw themselves against any living or free-willed being they encounter. Slicing through their brittle frames leaves their bone structure pitted and scored. To ensure that Forsaken scouts and volunteers actually cull these mindless intruders rather than merely observing them, the Deathguards demand tangible evidence. A notched, battle-marked rib serves as unmistakable proof that another of the Lich King's thralls has been shattered.

Note to William. "Note to William" is an errand undertaken for Gramma Stonefield in southern Elwynn Forest to help two secret lovers from feuding families. By delivering Mildred's message to the apothecary William Pestle in Goldshire, adventurers seek an alchemical solution to unite young Maybell and Tommy Joe. The Stonefield and Maclure families have lived as neighbors in southern Elwynn Forest for years, yet their bitter feuding has made normal relations impossible. Caught squarely in the middle are young Tommy Joe Stonefield and Maybell Maclure, whose romance must be conducted in utter secrecy. While their parents harbor relentless resentment, Gramma Mildred Stonefield takes pity on the young lovers and seeks an unconventional remedy to unite them.

Note to the Mayor. Note to the Mayor is an Alliance errand in Duskwood that links the eccentric hermit Abercrombie to the leadership of Darkshire. After aiding the reclusive old man, adventurers are asked to hand-deliver a personal message to Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke. However, the missive immediately stirs suspicion rather than warmth. After helping Abercrombie recover his stolen chest from the ogres of the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, the hermit sends you back down the mist-shrouded roads toward town. Cackling with delight, Abercrombie claims that he and Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke are old friends. He insists that upon discovering what the adventurer has accomplished, the mayor will be just as thrilled as he is.

Novice Elreth. Novice Elreth is an undead member of the Forsaken stationed inside the chapel at Deathknell. As newly risen undead awaken into their second life, she directs them to confront the mindless Scourge haunting the nearby graves and tend to the tragic aftermath of the plague. Inside the desecrated chapel at Deathknell, Novice Elreth assists the emerging undead as they struggle to understand their horrific awakening. Rather than succumbing to despair or the mindless hunger of the Scourge, the Forsaken must organize quickly to secure their territory. Elreth provides newly freed souls with early tasks, directing them to gather paws and wings from the wolves and bats to the south and deal with the lingering remnants of Lordaeron's tragic downfall, including the sorrow of her friend Marla Fipps, slain by her own husband Samuel after he joined the mindless Scourge.

Noxious Glade. Tucked away in the hills just north of Light's Hope Chapel, the Noxious Glade is a secluded basin steeped in concentrated plague. Choked with toxic green air and darkened soil, it functions as a nearby redoubt for Scourge operations right under the Argent Dawn's nose. While the Argent Dawn maintains its vigil at Light's Hope Chapel, an encampment of the Scourge lurks directly in the hills above them to the north. The Noxious Glade suffers from an infection far more severe than much of the surrounding terrain: the air hangs thick with a sickly green mist, and the soil has rotted into deep bruised purples. Within the hollow, the undead have erected ziggurats, a slaughterhouse for cobbling together abominations, and a plague cauldron that continuously spews pestilence into the atmosphere.

Noxious Lair. The Noxious Lair is a sunken silithid hive situated in the southwestern deserts of Tanaris, bordering Un'Goro Crater. Once a verdant basin with flowing water, the territory has been infested and drained of its vital resources by the burrowing Centipaar swarm. Now, it stands as an acidic breeding ground filled with swarming insectoids and rich mineral veins. Resting against the western ridges overlooking Un'Goro Crater, the Noxious Lair occupies a depression in the sand that once held a lake or shallow river. When the Centipaar silithid invaded, they consumed the desert's remaining underground moisture and transformed the basin into an encroaching colony. Vast pincers and twitching limbs rise directly from the sand dunes, surrounding subterranean tunnels slick with corrosive insect secretions and clusters of incubating eggs.

Noxious Lair Investigation. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser wants to know who the enemy is. Bugs have been draining the pools of water that lay where the Noxious Lair now stands, and little else is known about them. You are asked to take five insect parts from the Centipaar in the lair and bring them to Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan. After the Gadgetzan Water Survey, Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser turns to the reports about the bugs. Little is known except that they are draining the pools that once lay where the Noxious Lair now is. Fizzledowser wants to learn who the enemy is first, and asks you to go into the lair, take five parts from the Centipaar found there, and carry them back to Gadgetzan, to the alchemist Pestlezugg, to be examined.

Nugget Slug. Nugget slugs are specialized 17.5-gauge mechanical fasteners used in industrial engineering. Stockpiled in tool buckets by the Venture Company at the Sludge Fen, they are coveted by tinkerers attempting to repair volatile machinery. Nugget slugs are heavy-duty metallic fasteners manufactured for demanding industrial assemblies. Specifically sized at 17.5 gauge, these components are an essential part of the heavy equipment deployed across Venture Company extraction sites. While useless as ordinary trade goods, they are indispensable to tinkerers dealing with customized goblin hardware.

Nugget Slugs. At the Sludge Fen, Wenikee Boltbucket needs parts for a recovered samophlange. The eccentric tinkerer sends you to the nearby Venture Company drilling crews for spare hardware. Wenikee Boltbucket has a recovered samophlange and wants to learn how the intricate machine works. Its goblin mechanisms need exact parts, so she sends you to the Venture Company crews at the Sludge Fen. Their heavy tool buckets hold the seventeen-point-five gauge nugget slugs she needs.

Oakenscowl. Along Lake Al'Ameth, blight spreads from a corrupted timberling called Oakenscowl. Denalan asks you to end the threat. The maddened creature dwells in a cave on the lake's southern bank. Timberlings tend the boughs of Teldrassil, and Oakenscowl once led them. Now corruption runs through the world tree, reaching humble wildlife and ancient protectors alike. A massive growth swells across Oakenscowl's bark, driving the timberling mad. Where it once guarded the forest, blight now takes hold.

Oben Rageclaw. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Oben Rageclaw's spirit wanders, unable to wake or pass on. His sleeping body remains under the Gnarlpine furbolgs' control. Oben Rageclaw entered Ban'ethil Barrow Den to commune with nature and wander the Emerald Dream, as many Druids of the Claw do. When the Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to corruption and overran the barrows, Oben lay defenseless in his trance. A corrupted Gnarlpine shaman used dark rituals to take control of his comatose body. His spirit was left behind as an anguished ghost, unable to wake or pass on.

Oggleflint. Beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint leads the trogg tribe in Ragefire Chasm. His pack climbs from lava-filled tunnels toward the surface, where he commands them near the cavern entrance and threatens the Horde capital above. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint and his troggs climbed from fiery tunnels into Ragefire Chasm. They carved a primitive domain among the molten rock and defend it with brutal force. Troggs have little advanced civilization, and Oggleflint rules his pack through sheer strength.

Ogre Thieves. Abercrombie, the peculiar hermit dwelling in western Duskwood, asks travelers to venture into the ogre stronghold of Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. He claims that ogres ambushed him while he was foraging and made off with a crate filled with his irreplaceable herbs and tools. Isolated out along the damp roads of western Duskwood, the aged hermit Abercrombie claims he was attacked while gathering supplies in the wilderness. According to him, brutes from the southern ogre mound drove him off, forcing him to abandon a sturdy wooden crate packed with precious herbs and delicate instruments.

Ogre's Monocle. The Ogre's Monocle is an oversized eyeglass worn by Zzarc'Vul, an ogre dwelling in southern Duskwood's Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. Its immense glass lens provides the exact dimensions needed by Viktori Prism'Antras in Darkshire to assemble an elaborate stargazing telescope. While ogres are rarely renowned for refined scholarship, Zzarc'Vul somehow came into possession of an enormous monocle tailored to his massive stature. When the Darkshire resident Viktori Prism'Antras set out to build a stargazing instrument using blueprints drafted by the gnome engineer Cog, he found standard lenses far too small. Zzarc'Vul's eyewear proved to be the only piece of polished glass in the region with the curvature and size necessary to focus light through the completed device.

Ogtinc. Ogtinc is an independent furbolg hunter perched on a high ridge overlooking the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Having parted ways with his tribe to serve the balance of nature, he acts as a trusted ally and mentor for the Cenarion Circle. Skilled hunters seeking to test their craft against the fiercest beasts of Kalimdor often seek out his guidance. While most furbolg in Kalimdor remain fiercely bound to their tribes—or have succumbed to corruption following the Third War—Ogtinc chose a distinct path. Departing from his kin, he dedicated his bow and survival lore to aiding the Cenarion Circle. He makes his camp high on a bluff southeast of Timbermaw Hold, vigilantly watching over the ancient, shattered lands of Azshara.

Ogunaro Wolfrunner. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Honor, Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends the Horde’s foremost wolf kennel beside the Hunter’s Hall. He breeds and trains fierce wolves for orc champions and their trusted allies. Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends Orgrimmar’s battle wolves beside the Hunter’s Hall in the Valley of Honor. Orcs and wolves have shared a bond for generations, across Draenor’s plains and Durotar’s wilderness. It rests on mutual respect, not simple domestication. Ogunaro entrusts only the hardiest beasts, from dire wolves to agile timber prowlers, to warriors who have proven their strength and worth to the warchief.

Oh Brother. . .. "Oh Brother. . ." is an Alliance mission given by Wilder Thistlenettle in Stormwind City. Distraught over a cave-in during an expedition into the depths beneath Moonbrook, Wilder asks adventurers to search the labyrinthine mines for his missing sibling, Foreman Thistlenettle, or recover his Explorers' League Badge. Wilder Thistlenettle and his brother entered the cavernous subterranean tunnels beneath Moonbrook as members of a mining company. However, things turned catastrophic when hostile thieves swarmed the area and a violent cave-in sealed off the lower tunnels. Wilder managed to escape to Stormwind, but his brother and the rest of the crew were left trapped behind the rubble.

Okra. In Westfall, Okra grows in the plots at Saldean's Farm. Homesteaders prize the crop, and it thickens the stews that feed them. Saldean's Farm still yields vegetables while much of Westfall lies fallow under threat from Defias outlaws and rogue harvest golem attacks. Okra grows in the tilled plots around the farm. The crop persists through the harsh conditions, nourishing local homesteaders when trade and supplies from Stormwind run dry.

Old God. The Old Gods are colossal, malevolent horrors of flesh and madness who ruled Azeroth in its primordial dawn. Though vanquished and bound deep beneath the crust by the Titans, their ancient whispers still corrode mortal minds, twist nature, and drive doomsday cults to unearth their prisons. Long before mortal records began, Azeroth was dominated by the Old Gods, colossal entities of chaotic flesh such as C'Thun. They embedded themselves into the planet's crust, commanding elemental armies and insectoid swarms. When the Titans arrived, their armies fought an apocalyptic war against them. Rather than destroying them, the Titans bound the Old Gods in vast, subterranean prisons to keep them dormant forever.

Old Horde. The Old Horde was the blood-crazed coalition of orcish clans manipulated by demonic power into conquering Draenor and invading Azeroth. Led first by Blackhand and later by Orgrim Doomhammer, its path of destruction shaped the First and Second Wars until its decisive defeat by the Alliance of Lordaeron. Today, Thrall's New Horde seeks to overcome that dark legacy, while isolated remnants like the Dark Horde still cling to its bloody past. Before it crossed into Azeroth, the Horde was forged on Draenor through demonic manipulation. The demon lord Kil'jaeden used the warlock Gul'dan and the elder shaman Ner'zhul to corrupt the proud, spiritual orc clans. As elemental spirits abandoned the warring orcs, shamanistic traditions were cast aside for warlock magic. Sealed by the consumption of the blood of Mannoroth, the clans surrendered to bloodlust, slaughtering the draenei and draining their homeland of life.

Old Ironforge. Old Ironforge, also called the Assembly of Thanes, is an ancient subterranean chamber lying directly beneath the High Seat of Ironforge. Carved deep into the mountain's roots above glowing magma veins, it represents the ancestral heart of the dwarven capital. In the present day, its heavy access gates in the royal throne room remain sealed and vigilantly guarded. Beneath King Magni Bronzebeard's throne in the High Seat rests the cavernous hall known as Old Ironforge or the Assembly of Thanes. Deep inside these fiery subterranean foundations, winding stone bridges cross pools of subterranean lava. Long before the bustling halls of the Great Forge and the Commons echoed with modern dwarven commerce, early thanes gathered in these cavernous depths to deliberate and govern the mountain kingdom.

name.deDE: Eindringlinge in der Altstadt von Eisenschmiede

text.enUS: Old Ironforge Incursion. Old Ironforge Incursion is the culminating mission in the investigation of Dark Iron infiltrators lurking deep beneath Ironforge. Directed by Earthseer Farsen, champions delve into the ancient Hall of Thanes beneath Old Ironforge to eliminate the enemy commander, Durgen Dirgehammer, and report the threat directly to King Magni Bronzebeard. Following the discovery of an underground map revealing Dark Iron movements, Earthseer Farsen identifies the mastermind behind the subterranean intrusion. Deep within the ancient stone halls of Old Ironforge lies the entrance to the Hall of Thanes. While the upper city busies itself with surface matters, insidious forces have slipped into these dormant caverns right under the kingdom's feet.

Old Murk-Eye. Near the Westfall Lighthouse, Old Murk-Eye prowls the southern coast. His kind revere him, and sailors fear the lethal menace he poses to anyone who wanders near the lighthouse. Old Murk-Eye prowls the surf around the Westfall Lighthouse, where he is far tougher and more aggressive than the murlocs common along Westfall’s shores. His attacks have brought enough grief to local mariners that the spectral Captain Grayson seeks his death. Grayson offers a bounty for Old Murk-Eye’s pristine scales, hoping to break his hold on the shallows.

Old Port Authority. The Old Port Authority is a bustling, multi-vendor warehouse nestled along the boardwalks of Booty Bay. Beneath its roof, travelers browse everything from exotic pets and firearms to hearty rations and finely crafted weapons. Perched inside the pirate haven of Booty Bay, the Old Port Authority serves as an indoor marketplace divided into distinct stalls, and its interior buzzes with brisk commerce. Merchants hawk general adventuring supplies, firearms, bows, food, and weapons to scoundrels and privateers alike. It also houses exotic imports, offering colorful birds and nautical oddities straight off the docks to anyone with coin.

Old Serra'kis. Old Serra'kis is an ancient, massive threshadon dwelling in the submerged subterranean waters of Blackfathom Deeps. Hidden in a flooded cave beneath the ruins, the enormous beast is lethal to any who seek it out. The Twilight's Hammer has made its home in the sunken Moonshrine Ruins, but the dark waters beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum hide older, wilder things. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, lurks in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded cave beneath the ruins where few would think to look.

Old Town. In Old Town, soldiers train beside weathered tenements and crowded alleys. The quarter largely survived the First War and remains home to Stormwind’s military Command Center and the covert headquarters of SI:7. Old Town keeps much of the shape of Stormwind before the First War. While the Stonemasons rebuilt the rest of the city from the ground up, this quarter escaped total ruin. It never gained the pristine marble facades and grand canals found in the Trade District and Cathedral Square. Working folk, laborers, and the city’s poorest residents live among its crowded tenements. Its cobbled streets are narrower, dirtier, and more chaotic than those elsewhere in the capital, preserving the feel of the old kingdom.

Olsen's Farthing. Olsen's Farthing was once a flourishing farmstead situated along the primary trade road running through Silverpine Forest. In the wake of the Third War, the fields fell into ruin and became overrun by reanimated thralls bound to the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, Olsen's Farthing was a busy agricultural homestead with direct access to Silverpine's main overland trading route. Today, its tilled fields are choked with weeds, its structures lie broken, and any memory of honest farming has been erased by Scourge necromancy. Undead thralls, bound as slaves and raiders under the command of Thule Ravenclaw, wander the barren grounds to slaughter any travelers who stray too close.

text.enUS: On Guard in Stonetalon. On Guard in Stonetalon is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers south from Ashenvale into the rugged Stonetalon Mountains. Sentinel Thenysil dispatches travelers to check on her scout friend, Kaela Shadowspear, who was sent into the crags alongside a gnome mage to monitor industrial incursions by the Venture Company. Stationed in Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil keeps a close watch on threats pressing toward the ancient forest. Deeply concerned for her friend Kaela Shadowspear, Thenysil asks passing Alliance champions to track her down. Kaela was dispatched into the Stonetalon Mountains by Sentinel Wolfrunner to survey rising turmoil in the heights, but communication has fallen silent, leaving Thenysil anxious for her safety.

name.ptBR: Em guarda nas Torres de Pedra

text.enUS: On Guard in Stonetalon. On Guard in Stonetalon directs Alliance travelers from Kaela Shadowspear to Gaxim Rustfizzle at their camp near Windshear Crag. Facing rampant despoilment by the Venture Company, an otherwise unlikely pair—a cautious night elf sentinel and an eccentric gnome tinkerer—join forces to safeguard the mountain pass. Night elves and gnomes rarely share common ground, especially when it comes to technology and the natural world. In the crags of Stonetalon Mountains, however, necessity bridges the cultural gulf. With the rapacious Venture Company carving out the wilderness and felling ancient trees, the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear has recognized that pure martial prowess alone cannot overcome industrialized pillaging. Welcoming gnome ingenuity into sacred Kaldorei territory demonstrates just how precarious the situation has become.

One Shot. One Kill.. On the road to Auberdine, Sentinel Aynasha needs help to survive an ambush and deliver her message. Marosh the Devious and his furbolg trackers have poisoned her, leaving her unable to travel while she mixes an antidote. Sentinel Aynasha was carrying important communications toward Auberdine when hostile furbolgs intercepted her on a northern Kalimdor trail. Marosh the Devious led the pack. Their venom left the scout unsteady and unable to continue on foot.

Oneiros. Oneiros is a sprawling expanse of ancient night elven ruins located south of Jademir Lake in northern Feralas. Tied intimately to the nearby portals leading toward the realm of Ysera, its moss-covered stones are guarded by elite green dragonkin. Stretching across the dense forest floor of northern Feralas, the crumbling stone arches and column fragments of Oneiros hint at an ancient Kaldorei settlement abandoned millennia ago. In the present day, nature has reclaimed the structures, entwining them with massive roots and verdant overgrowth. Elite guardians of the Green Dragonflight relentlessly patrol the shaded paths and broken plazas, warding mortals away from ancient secrets.

Ongeku. Uthek the Wise of the Gelkis says you still have more to prove, and that for now the Gelkis will take on the Magram without your help. The earth has whispered to Uthek of draenethyst, and you are sent far away to the Swamp of Sorrows for a shard held by the lost one Ongeku. After Stealing Supplies, Uthek the Wise tells you that your next undertaking lies a long way off. Those who listen hear many secrets in the earth, and one Uthek has heard is of a red crystal called draenethyst, newly arrived in this land and brought from a place of flying mountains and ruling demons. A shard of it, Uthek says, will make the magic strong. The lost one Ongeku holds a shard in the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. When you return, Uthek will look for proof that the Gelkis can still call you friend.

Onu. Barithras Moonshade sends you south from Auberdine to speak with Onu. Your findings in Cliffspring Falls have drawn the attention of one of Darkshore's oldest guardians. Barithras Moonshade sees more than strange fungi in the samples you brought back to Auberdine. The caves beneath Cliffspring Falls are tainted, and word of them reaches Onu, an Ancient of Lore in the Grove of the Ancients south of town. The corruption in Darkshore's waterways may reach beyond anything a naturalist can explain. Onu wants counsel, and even an Ancient's patient nature cannot hide the weight of that summons.

Onu is meditating. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Onu enters a deep trance over a growing threat. The ancient of lore weighs the alliance and motives of the Twilight's Hammer cult and the naga. If you lose your scrying phial, you can speak to him for another. In the Grove of the Ancients, Onu is an Ancient of Lore and a living repository of Kalimdor's history. Ominous reports of dark excavations at the Master's Glaive draw his immense consciousness inward. He ponders what brings the fanatical Twilight's Hammer cultists and the naga to the petrified remains of an ancient behemoth. For adventurers carrying out his reconnaissance, Onu remains within reach and can replace a scrying phial misplaced in the wild.

Onyxia. Onyxia is the broodmother of the black dragonflight and the devious daughter of Deathwing. From her lair in Dustwallow Marsh, she schemes to restore the black dragonflight's dominion over the mortal kingdoms.

Onyxia's Lair. Onyxia's Lair is a subterranean cavern located deep within the Wyrmbog of Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the nesting sanctuary and stronghold for Onyxia, broodmother of the black dragonflight. Inside its sweltering, magma-filled chambers, the great dragon watches over clutches of black dragon eggs. Carved into the treacherous mud and petrified wood of the Wyrmbog, the cavern entrance resembles the yawning maw of a dragon. Within, the cool rot of the marsh gives way to intense volcanic heat. Magma seeps from cracks in the obsidian stone, while subterranean tremors routinely shake the ceilings. The central chamber opens into a vast incubator where hundreds of black dragon eggs lie nested amid ash and embers, overseen by flightkin, dragonspawn guards, and Onyxia herself.

Operation Recombobulation. Operation Recombobulation is a bold engineering effort orchestrated by Razzle Sprysprocket in Kharanos. In response to the tragedy of Gnomeregan, Razzle and Ozzie Togglevolt seek to reverse the horrific transformation of their afflicted kin into leper gnomes using an experimental contraption known as the Recombobulator. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan to purge the trogg menace, it failed to destroy the invaders and instead warped the majority of the gnomish population into deranged, sickly leper gnomes. Refusing to accept this tragic mutation as permanent, inventor Razzle Sprysprocket has partnered with Ozzie Togglevolt to develop a technological cure: the Recombobulator. Their audacious goal is nothing less than restoring their mutated brethren back to health and sanity.

Oracle Glade. Bloodfeather harpies harry Oracle Glade in northwestern Teldrassil. The sacred woodland holds the ancient Oracle Tree and Teldrassil’s first and most potent moonwell. Between Darnassus and Wellspring Lake, the Oracle Glade shelters a place of communion with nature. At its heart stands the ancient Oracle Tree, magically nurtured, its great boughs shaped like an eagle perched atop a bear. Nearby lies the first and most potent of Teldrassil’s sacred moonwells, bright with Elune’s grace. The Circle of the Ancients and the Oracle Tree watch over the island boughs. The tree sheds bark marked with messages for Archdruid Fandral Staghelm about the World Tree’s health.

Oran's Gratitude. After Rin'ji's Secret, the chain that began with Rin'ji is Trapped! comes to its close with Oran Snakewrithe, to whom you bring a tablet. Rin'ji is Trapped! began this chain, and Rin'ji's Secret was the step just before this one. Oran Snakewrithe is the one who receives the tablet you carry.

Orc. Originally a shamanistic clan people hailing from the alien world of Draenor, the orcs were deceived and corrupted into a bloodthirsty conquering force by the demonic Burning Legion. After invading Azeroth and suffering eventual defeat and internment, they were rallied by Warchief Thrall to reclaim their spiritual heritage. In this new era, the orcs lead the Horde from their newly carved nation of Durotar, striving for honor while grappling with the lingering shadow of their demonic past. Before their fall, orcs lived as nomadic hunter-gatherers and spiritual clans across the rugged landscapes of Draenor. Their culture was grounded in ancestral reverence and deep communion with elemental spirits, guided primarily by revered shamans. Among the disparate clans were the Frostwolves, Warsongs, and Shadowmoon. Though physically formidable and deeply proud, traditional orcish society was defined by survival, honor, and harmony with the natural elements rather than mindless conquest.

Ordanus. Braelyn Firehand at Sunrock Retreat uses her arcane sight to track down Keeper Ordanus, an elder son of Cenarius who fled Stonetalon Peak. Believing his people desecrated ancient Highborne ruins, she sends Horde champions across the border into Ashenvale to take his head. Braelyn Firehand arrived in Stonetalon Mountains on orders from her master to reclaim the sacred ruins of Azshara's ancient temples. She found the night elves already occupying the peak, treating the relics of her Highborne forebears as wilderness to be contained. Her chief target, Keeper Ordanus, fled before she could corner him, slipping across the border into Ashenvale. Using her arcane vision, Braelyn scried his hiding place high in a wooden refuge at Raynewood Retreat and enlisted the Horde to finish the hunt.

Ordanus' Head. Ordanus' Head is the grisly trophy taken from Keeper Ordanus at Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale. Claimed on behalf of the blood elf magi Braelyn Firehand, it serves as undeniable proof that one of Cenarius's eldest sons has fallen to arcane vengeance. Keeper Ordanus was an ancient keeper of the grove, one of the elder scions of the forest god Cenarius. When Braelyn Firehand climbed the heights of Stonetalon Mountains on orders from her master, she sought to end the druids' stifling of magic at the peak and exact vengeance on Ordanus. However, the keeper was spirited away to the heart of Ashenvale before she could strike. Using arcane scrying to peer through the forest canopy, Firehand located his sanctuary in the boughs of Raynewood Retreat, demanding his severed head as proof that the wild demigod's arrogance had finally been answered.

Orendil Broadleaf. Orendil Broadleaf is a skilled night elf herbalist and healer stationed at Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale. Known for his deep knowledge of forest flora, he concocts vital remedies to save young lives across the troubled woodlands. Positioned at Maestra's Post along the western threshold of Ashenvale, Orendil Broadleaf tends to the sick as a skilled healer. Recognized for his masterful knowledge of local herbs and restorative craft, Orendil relies on passing travelers to gather rare natural reagents. Even as tension and conflict encroach upon the forest, his tireless focus remains on safeguarding his kin and soothing their ailments.

Orendil's Cure. Orendil's Cure is a medicinal draught concocted by the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf in northern Ashenvale. Created using the rare herb Bathran's Hair, it is meant to treat the mysterious, deathly sickness afflicting Relara Whitemoon in Astranaar. When young Relara Whitemoon fell deathly ill in Astranaar, conventional remedies proved useless against her ailment. Her desperate father, Pelturas Whitemoon, turned to Orendil Broadleaf, a hermit and master of natural medicine dwelling along the northern reaches of Ashenvale. Utilizing bundles of the rare plant Bathran's Hair harvested from the haunted ruins of Bathran's Haunt, Orendil brewed this tailored concoction. The arrival of the vial gives Pelturas hope where before he had little, though the cure only slows the disease, and Pelturas must turn to the further remedies Orendil suggested.

Orendil's Cure. Orendil's Cure is an urgent delivery errand tasked to Alliance travelers by the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf. After concocting a remedy from rare flora, Orendil sends the courier racing down the woodland roads to Astranaar to save a dying night elf child. In the central settlement of Astranaar, Pelturas Whitemoon watches over his daughter, Relara, as she wastes away from a severe and mysterious sickness. Facing the limits of local knowledge, Pelturas sought aid across the wild forest of Ashenvale, turning to the wisdom of distant herbalists before hope slipped entirely through his fingers.

Orenthil Whisperwind. Beneath Teldrassil’s boughs, Orenthil Whisperwind lives among the night elves of Shadowglen. Orenthil Whisperwind lives among the night elves beneath Teldrassil’s canopy in Shadowglen. Little is known of his personal history.

Orgnil Soulscar. At Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar watches for threats within Durotar. He gathers intelligence and coordinates defenses against dangers to the young orc nation, especially the Burning Blade cult in the canyons. At Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar tracks hidden threats across Durotar. While grunt patrols watch for Alliance forces and centaur raiders, he looks for danger among the orcs themselves. Scouts bring him reports from across the region, and he searches them for signs of corrupt rituals and secret gatherings.

Orgrim Doomhammer. Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor. Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces.

Orgrimmar. In northern Durotar, Orgrimmar rises as the New Horde’s warrior capital. Warchief Thrall founded the city in memory of Orgrim Doomhammer, and its red canyons shelter the orcs’ renewal and survival on Kalimdor. After the Third War and the victory at Mount Hyjal, Warchief Thrall brought his surviving people south to make a homeland in Durotar. Orgrimmar was built among steep mountain crags, with spiked timber walls, stone watchtowers, and caverns cut deep into the mountains. Darkspear trolls, tauren stonemasons, and goblin engineers helped raise the fortress. Its defenses turned the wilderness into a stronghold built to withstand a siege.

text.enUS: Orm Stonehoof and the Brutal Helm. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thunder Bluff to consult with Orm Stonehoof, an artisan smith. Recommended by Thun'grim Firegaze, Orm possesses the specialized craft required to forge the Brutal Helm. After proving their mettle and assembling pieces of the Brutal Armor in the Barrens, warriors are directed higher into the mesa city of Thunder Bluff. Thun'grim Firegaze, an accomplished armorsmith himself, recognizes his limits and refers his champions to Orm Stonehoof. Orm's craft is renowned throughout Kalimdor, specifically his ability to mold resilient battlefield helms from rare, savage trophies.

Ormak Grimshot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Ormak Grimshot trains hunters for life in the wild. Beside his wolf, Grimfang, he teaches Horde hunters to track, shoot, and tame beasts. Ormak Grimshot trains Horde trackers and marksmen in the Hunter's Hall. With his wolf, Grimfang, at his side, he teaches the skills needed to survive Kalimdor's wilderness. Orc and troll hunters who have completed their trials in Durotar learn from him how to tame and command wild beasts, and to form a lasting bond with an animal companion.

Ormer Ironbraid. Ormer Ironbraid is a dwarven archaeologist stationed at Whelgar's Excavation Site in the southern Wetlands. His team's historical research has been violently interrupted by ravenous raptors that overran the dig. Ormer seeks adventurous allies to clear out the beasts and avenge the miners driven from the site. Ormer Ironbraid arrived in the Wetlands as part of the dwarven effort to uncover Titan relics and ancient history at Whelgar's Excavation Site. Unfortunately, uncovering ancient stones also unearthed—or at least provoked—packs of fierce Wetlands raptors. Rather than cataloging ancient earthenware and tablets, Ormer spends his days watching the beasts prowl among the ruins, nursing a fierce hatred for the creatures that disrupted their work.

Ormer's Revenge. Ormer's Revenge begins the retributive campaign of Ormer Ironbraid, an explorer stranded high above the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. After unearthing ancient fossilized bones, the dwarven dig team inadvertently drew packs of ravenous mottled raptors that slaughtered their companions and trapped the survivors on a rocky bluff. The Whelgar Excavation Site was meant to be a triumph for dwarven archaeology, exposing massive prehistoric remains buried beneath the Wetlands muck. Instead, unearthing the colossal bones caught the attention of the marsh's native raptors. Drawn by the disturbance, packs of mottled predators swarmed the dig site, catching the excavators off guard and tearing through their ranks.

Ormer's Revenge. Ormer's Revenge is an Alliance task given by Ormer Ironbraid at the ruined Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. With the initial scout raptors culled, Ormer demands the slaughter of the heavier Mottled Scytheclaws and Razormaws that drove his expedition from the pits. Ormer Ironbraid's grudge against the raptors running rampant over the Whelgar Excavation Site is deeply personal. After thinning out the smaller juveniles that overran the upper camp, he turns your blades against the adult predators prowling the lower dig site. The Mottled Scytheclaws and Razormaws represent the core threat to any hope of reclaiming the archaeological effort, tearing through dwarven prospectors and leaving the trenches littered with shattered crates and abandoned picks.

Ormer's Revenge. Ormer's Revenge is the culmination of Ormer Ironbraid's campaign to avenge the dwarven excavators slaughtered at the Whelgar Excavation Site. Convinced that a cunning beast named Sarltooth spearheaded the savage raptor assault, Ormer sends an adventurer to slay the pack leader and claim his talon as proof. Following the slaughter of the Explorer's League diggers at the Whelgar Excavation Site, Ormer Ironbraid watched the teeming raptors from his ridge and observed a beast that dwarfed the rest. Known as Sarltooth, this particularly large and vicious raptor perched above the dig works, directing or leading the pack that drove the dwarves out. To Ormer, the beast was not merely wildlife, but the instigator of an attack on King Magni Bronzebeard's subjects.

Ornery Ornery Galestriders. Ornery Ornery Galestriders concerns an orchard farmer in the Gustberry Lowlands struggling with a meager seasonal harvest. The local lowlands galestriders—larger and more vicious than their highland kin—have been raiding the orchard for stormapples and threatening the farm's livelihood. Culling the aggressive birds secures the remaining fruit while providing much-needed fresh tenderloins for dinner. In the Gustberry Lowlands, local farmers face tough times following an already meager seasonal harvest. To make matters worse, wild galestriders have invaded the orchards, stripping branches of ripe stormapples and jeopardizing what little fruit remains. Keeping the farm viable means driving off or thinning out the boldest birds before the entire crop is lost.

Orokk Omosh. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh keeps his family's smithing craft alive. The aging orc has no children to inherit it, so he seeks worthy Horde apprentices to learn the Omosh armorcraft secrets. In the Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh is the last smith of the Omosh line. He has no children to inherit his craft, and he will not let his family's techniques die with him. Capable Horde blacksmiths can undertake his demanding trials of metalwork. Those who prove their dedication earn the revered secrets of Omosh armorcraft.

Orphan Matron Battlewail. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for children left without families by war. With Tosamina, she gives them shelter and raises young orcs. Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for children who have lost their kin to violence. In Orgrimmar, where war's toll reaches even the young capital, she and Tosamina shelter and nurture the next generation of the Horde. The orphanage in the Valley of Honor opens its doors to passing adventurers. During Children's Week, travelers are called upon to mentor the children.

Orphan Matron Nightingale. In Cathedral Square, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for Stormwind’s orphaned children. She and Matron Shellene give them shelter and guidance, and invite Alliance adventurers to spend Children's Week with them. Outside the orphanage, south-east of the Cathedral of Light, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for Stormwind’s most vulnerable children. Recent wars, gnoll attacks, and the rise of the Defias Brotherhood have left many without homes or parents. Nightingale and Matron Shellene give them shelter, basic care, and guidance under the Church of the Holy Light’s watch.

Ortell's Hideout. Ortell's Hideout is a modest, secluded cave nestled against the mountains in southeastern Silithus. It serves as the refuge of Hermit Ortell, one of the few solitary souls hardy or foolish enough to dwell alone in this barren wasteland. Tucked away in the jagged cliffs of southeastern Silithus, Ortell's Hideout offers sparse sanctuary from the raging sandstorms and prowling silithid swarms that dominate the wastes. The cave is occupied solely by Hermit Ortell, an eccentric recluse who ekes out an existence far from civilization and the fortified garrisons of the Cenarion Hold. Travelers who brave the dangerous journey to this remote corner often seek his peculiar knowledge of the desert and its hazards.

Oslow's Toolbox. Oslow's Toolbox contains the vital construction tools needed by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire. En route from Goldshire, the supplies were ferried across Lake Everstill only to be sunk by an orcish catapult bombardment. Maintaining the defenses and infrastructure of Lakeshire is a grueling challenge, particularly with the Blackrock orcs besieging the Redridge Mountains. Foreman Oslow ordered a vital set of construction tools brought in from Goldshire. Because the main bridge leading into Lakeshire had been destroyed by enemy action, the shipment had to be loaded into a rowboat to cross Lake Everstill. The crossing was abruptly cut short when Blackrock forces struck the vessel with a catapult blast, plunging the boat and Oslow's heavy chest straight down into the murloc-infested depths.

Osric Strang. In Stormwind's Old Town, veteran armor merchant Osric Strang supplies weary travelers and Alliance defenders with sturdy gear. His shop, Limited Immunity, specializes in heavy mail and plate armor, along with shields. Osric Strang runs Limited Immunity, where fighters find heavy armor and shields. He also helps arriving couriers who need a point of contact in the capital, including those coming from nearby settlements such as Sentinel Hill in Westfall.

Osric's Crate. At Sentinel Hill, Osric's Crate brings armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia. The defenders face the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls without the Stormwind army. Westfall faces the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls, while the Stormwind army remains absent. At Sentinel Hill, the People's Militia must make do without the crown's formal support. Osric's Crate holds freshly made armor from the capital, sent to Quartermaster Lewis to distribute among the volunteer fighters.

name.ptBR: Camarão que dorme a onda leva

text.enUS: Other Fish to Fry. Drulzegar Skraghook, a fisherman at Shadowprey Village in Desolace, lost the entire crew to the naga while fishing near Ranazjar Isle. Guilt weighs on Drulzegar, who asks you to go after the Slitherblade. Drulzegar Skraghook and the crew fished by Ranazjar Isle, which lies north of a wreck on the coast, and had done so many times. One morning the naga attacked and killed everyone except Drulzegar. Since then revenge is all Drulzegar thinks about, and the guilt is too much to bear.

Overlord Mok'Morokk. Overlord Mok'Morokk is the brute chieftain of the Stonemaul ogres, presiding over Brackenwall Village in Dustwallow Marsh. Originally appointed by Rexxar for his strength, he has become a tyrannical and cowardly ruler who refuses to defend his clan against the black dragonflight. When Rexxar bested the previous chieftain Kor'gall and led the Stonemaul clan in defense of Durotar, he left Mok'Morokk in command, seeing promise in his sheer martial strength. That faith proved misplaced. Mok'Morokk quickly succumbed to the corrupting influence of absolute authority, ruling through intimidation and self-indulgence rather than stewardship. Instead of caring for his kin, he demands unearned tribute, lounges in Brackenwall Village, and bullies anyone who questions his command.

name.esES: Las pertenencias del señor supremo Mok'Morokk

text.enUS: Overlord Mok'Morokk's Concern. Overlord Mok'Morokk of the Stonemaul clan is in Brackenwall Village and wants his grog, snuff and strongbox back. He left them behind in a hurry at the clan's old home, and he sends you south to find them. Mok'Morokk says Rexxar made him the mighty leader of the Stonemaul clan, and that he keeps his people safe. By his account, big dragons came to the old home and brought fire, so he found the clan a new home here in Dustwallow.

Overlord Ramtusk. Overlord Ramtusk is a massive quilboar warlord who leads the warriors deep within Razorfen Kraul. Crying out for victory and for Agamaggan, he fights at the head of his elite guards, and striking him down shatters the martial backbone of the Kraul's defenders. Overlord Ramtusk holds command deep within the thorny maze of Razorfen Kraul, the quilboar stronghold in the southern Barrens. He goes into battle with a war cry to the boar demigod Agamaggan, and he rules the Kraul's fighters with unyielding authority.

Owatanka. Across the southern Barrens, Owatanka roams as a swift thunder lizard known to the tauren as Bluebolt. Slaying the beast yields a crackling tailspike, carried to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo in honor of the elders’ tradition of learning from Kalimdor’s primordial beasts. Owatanka prowls the southern Barrens, where tauren hunters speak of him with reverence. Unlike his massive, plodding kin, he moves with blinding speed. The tauren call him Bluebolt, for the storm changed him.

name.frFR: Fourré de l'Aile de la chouette

text.enUS: Owl Wing Thicket. Owl Wing Thicket is a rugged cluster of caves and stone roosts in southern Winterspring. It is heavily populated by berserk, moontouched, and crazed owlbeasts that prowl the snowy crags. Deep within, ancient night elf altars preserve sacred knowledge about the origin of these creatures and their connection to the moon goddess Elune. Carved into the snowy highlands south of Everlook, Owl Wing Thicket serves as one of the densest nesting grounds for Winterspring's wild owlbeasts. Long ago, night elf caretakers revered these creatures as sacred guardians blessed by Elune.
