Ancient shrines and moonstone altars are still tucked among the cavern overhangs, watched over by the lingering spirits of the Guardians of Elune. Today, however, many of the beasts have succumbed to madness, lashing out at travelers who trespass upon their holy hollows.

Ozzie Togglevolt. Ozzie Togglevolt is a gnome engineer and survivor of Gnomeregan's fall, currently operating out of the snowy village of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Haunted by the tragedy that struck his people, he works alongside his partner Razzle Sprysprocket to research a remedy for the irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt was inside the subterranean wonders of Gnomeregan when catastrophe struck. When the toxic fallout was vented throughout the corridors to stem the trogg invasion, Ozzie stood right beside his fellow gnome, Gnoarn. A sudden radioactive discharge struck Gnoarn directly, altering him forever before Ozzie's eyes. Though Ozzie made it to the surface alive and reached the haven of Dun Morogh, the horrifying memory of that disaster never left him.

Pacify The Centaur. Pacify the Centaur is a retaliatory hunting mission issued by Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post. Charged with clearing the threat gathering beneath the canyon spires, Horde adventurers strike deep into the Galak centaur encampments of Splithoof Crag. Perched upon its precarious desert mesa, Freewind Post grants the tauren a commanding vantage over the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. However, that high ground offers little peace when hostile enemies mass directly beneath the ropes and elevators. The Galak centaur have established a sprawling war camp nestled directly north along the canyon wall at Splithoof Crag, directly menacing supply lines and tauren movement through the needles.

Package for Thurman. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider needs her son Thurman’s tailoring supplies at Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. He left home without his shears and needles, and Rema asks you to carry them to his workshop. Rema Schneider worries that Thurman will fall behind in his tailoring work without his shears and needles. He left home in a rush, and his mother asks you to carry the tools across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

name.esES: Paquete de contenedores de moco vacíos
name.frFR: Caisse de pots de Limon vides
name.ptBR: Pacote de Recipientes Vazios de Gosma

text.enUS: Package of Empty Ooze Containers. This package is a kit of specialized, empty specimen jars supplied by the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge. Intended for dangerous field sampling in the blighted forests of Felwood, it contains jars designed to safely hold tainted and cursed ooze extracts without dissolving. Containing a dozen empty jars—split between containers meant for cursed and tainted oozes—this kit was assembled by Laris Geardawdle for intrepid travelers heading out to Felwood. Because raw ooze specimens are notoriously caustic and prone to digesting ordinary luggage, sturdy, sealed glass is essential for transporting the acidic residues across continents back to the tinker's workbench in Ironforge.

Painted Gnoll Armband. At Westbrook Garrison, Painted Gnoll Armbands prove that Riverpaw gnolls have been slain. The marked bands come from packs pressing against Elwynn Forest's western border. Riverpaw warriors and scavengers wear rough armbands painted with crude tribal patterns. The bands come from gnolls along Elwynn Forest's wilderness borders. For Stormwind's defenders, the packs pose a growing threat near Stone Cairn Lake and in the woods south of Westbrook Garrison.

Paladin. Paladins are holy warriors who blend martial prowess with the power of the Holy Light. Clad in heavy plate, they protect the innocent, heal the wounded and strike down wicked foes. Humans and dwarves carry the Silver Hand's legacy for the Alliance, and among the Horde, Forsaken who served the Light in life still answer its call, though it burns them. The paladins were originally established during the Second War by Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Having witnessed the devastation wrought upon the pious Clerics of Northshire during the First War, Faol recognized that healers alone could not survive the brutality of orcish warfare. He gathered virtuous knights of Lordaeron and trained surviving clerics in the ways of martial combat and divine magic. Baptized as the Knights of the Silver Hand and led by Uther the Lightbringer, these champions provided both physical defense and spiritual renewal to the kingdoms of humanity.

Palemane Rock. Palemane Rock is a cavern and campsite nestled into the western mountains of Mulgore. It serves as a primary stronghold for the aggressive Palemane gnoll tribe, posing a continual nuisance and threat to the nearby tauren of Bloodhoof Village. Situated along the western rim of the grassy plains of Mulgore, Palemane Rock consists of a sprawling open-air encampment fronting a deep, shadowed cavern carved into the mountainside. The Palemane gnolls have claimed both the cave interior and the immediate foothills outside as their territory. Hostile and territorial, these gnolls aggressively defend their den, attacking hunters, travelers, and scouts who wander too close to their rocky haven.

name.esES: Llave de la jaula de pantera
name.frFR: Clé de la cage de la panthère

text.enUS: Panther Cage Key. The Panther Cage Key is a small metal key held by Wizlo Bearingshiner at Whitereach Post. It unlocks a reinforced cage holding an enraged, captive predator within the wreckage of an ambushed caravan in Thousand Needles. When a traveling caravan was attacked and ransacked by centaur raiders north of Whitereach Post, the goblin tinker Wizlo Bearingshiner barely escaped with his life. Amid the ruins of wagons and plundered cargo, the marauders left one thing entirely untouched: a sturdy cage housing a ferocious, rare panther. Around the predator's neck hung Wizlo's prized invention, a hypercapacitor gizmo. Unwilling to approach the snarling beast, the centaur gave the cage a wide berth, leaving Wizlo's key as the only way to open the door and retrieve the device.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse à la panthère

text.enUS: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition offers a trial to those seeking to prove their prowess as big-game stalkers in Stranglethorn Vale. To join Hemet's hunting company, adventurers must first demonstrate their basic tracking ability by taking down ten young panthers. Within the wild expanse of northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary has assembled a seasoned band of big-game huntsmen. Sir S. J. Erlgadin tells anyone who wants a part of the hunt that they must first prove themselves an able panther hunter.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse à la panthère

text.enUS: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin demands that you prove yourself worthy of the big game hunters at Nesingwary's Expedition. Following your initial cull of younger beasts, he challenges you to track down and slay ten fully grown panthers in the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale. After dispatching the young panthers around the jungle, Sir S. J. Erlgadin asks you to raise your sights. To show that you deserve to keep company with seasoned big game hunters, you are sent out to hunt ten mature panthers, which are far tougher and more dangerous than their younger kin.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse à la panthère

text.enUS: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition challenges big game hunters to track and bring down the deadliest panthers in Stranglethorn Vale. Following your earlier trials, you must now seek out and slay ten Shadowmaw Panthers. Sir S. J. Erlgadin considers Shadowmaw Panthers to be the most dangerous cats prowling the jungles of Stranglethorn. Proving your mettle as a true stalker requires crawling through the dense underbrush to track down ten of these elusive beasts, whose ferocity makes them far harder to kill than to find.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse à la panthère
name.itIT: La maestria nella caccia alla pantera

text.enUS: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin has set the final trial of his panther hunt before you in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Having proven your skill against the region's panthers, you are challenged to seek out Bhag'thera, an elusive predator that has so far eluded the expedition's party. Bringing back the beast's fang will establish your standing as a true master of the hunt. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Sir S. J. Erlgadin considers your trials nearly complete. One final quarry remains to prove your worth against the jungle's predators: a panther named Bhag'thera. The beast has so far eluded the expedition's own party as it prowls the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale. Erlgadin calls on you to track down this great stalker and claim the Fang of Bhag'thera as proof of your skill.

Pao'ka Swiftmountain. Pao'ka Swiftmountain is a young tauren naturalist stranded among the wild wyverns of Highperch in Thousand Needles. Having traveled south under the guidance of Motega Firemane, his youthful curiosity got the better of him when he ventured too close to a nesting site and ended up cornered in the cliffs. Pao'ka came to the canyon country of Thousand Needles alongside Motega Firemane, eager to catalog and study the dangerous beasts of the canyons. His father had been reluctant to let his son go on such a perilous journey, and Pao'ka's recent misadventure proves those concerns were warranted. Fascinated by the magnificent wyverns inhabiting Highperch, the young scholar crept up the mountain trail behind a solitary tauren totem. Unsurprisingly, the territorial beasts took offense to his intrusion, driving him deep into the crags where he found himself trapped and terrified, unable to slip past the swooping predators to return to Whitereach Post.

Park. In Stormwind's western edge, Park offers visiting night elves a haven amid the stone city. It lies between Cathedral Square and the Mage Quarter, with greenery and quiet for rest. Druid trainers here are the only ones in the Eastern Kingdoms. Stormwind's Park brings a quiet stretch of wilderness into the stone capital. Once a place for the city's people to seek recreation, it became an enclave for night elf emissaries and travelers from across the Great Sea. Shaded canopies shelter the district, and a central Moonwell stands amid its grounds. The grove offers a glimpse of Kalimdor's sacred glades in the heart of the human kingdom.

Parker's Lunch. Parker's Lunch is a freshly prepared meal packed by Darcy in Lakeshire. Intended for Guard Parker on patrol, it offers a simple glimpse into the daily bonds and modest comforts of Redridge's defenders. While Redridge Mountains reels under attacks from gnolls and Blackrock orcs, the small gestures of daily life persist. Darcy, a waitress at the inn in Lakeshire, packs this wholesome meal for Guard Parker, who patrols the exposed road leading south toward Duskwood. Redridge's garrison is stretched thin and isolated from Stormwind's aid, leaving individual guards to maintain long, lonely watches. Delivering this bundle not only keeps a sentry fed, but also sparks an enduring, bashful courtship between the two townspeople.

Parqual Fintallas. Parqual Fintallas is a Forsaken scholar and former human historian of Lordaeron, currently residing in the Undercity's Apothecarium. Despite the grim surroundings of his undead existence, he retains a polite demeanor and an enduring passion for ancient lore, often assisting travelers sent to consult his deep historical expertise. In life, Parqual was a respected human scholar of Lordaeron who knew all there was to know of the kingdom, immersing himself in historical texts. When the plague of undeath struck, Parqual was among the many citizens slain and raised, only to eventually break free under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. While the Forsaken largely embrace cold pragmatism and turn away from their former lives, Parqual retains his scholarly passion and pleasant manners, still seeking enlightenment, though of a different nature than in life.

Partially Filled Vessel. Tenaron Stormgrip gives young night elf initiates the Partially Filled Vessel in Aldrassil. It carries blessed moonwell water from Shadowglen toward Dolanaar. Young kaldorei initiates gather blessed water from Shadowglen’s secluded moonwell. In Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip pours a sample into the vessel for its journey across Teldrassil. More water from the tree’s moonwells must be gathered to tend to the island’s health.

Parts for Kravel. Having brought Kravel Koalbeard's parts order to Wharfmaster Dizzywig, you now carry Kravel's package back to him at the Mirage Raceway on the Shimmering Flats. Dizzywig sends a message along with it: if Kravel wants more special orders, he will have to pay his tab. Wharfmaster Dizzywig gives you a package meant for Kravel Koalbeard, who waits at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats of Thousand Needles. Dizzywig asks you to pass on a warning with it: if Kravel hopes for more special orders, he must first pay what he owes.

Parts of the Swarm. Turning a cracked silithid carapace over in Thousand Needles, you find its plating interwoven so tightly that it is remarkably strong, and the creature seems powerful and highly developed. Korran at the Crossroads would probably like to study more of them. Closer inspection shows the chitin woven so tightly that it is unlike anything you have seen. The rest of the body tells the same tale of great strength and advanced development. It occurs to you that Korran, at the Crossroads, would relish examining more of these creatures to learn their nature and their origins. The specimens wanted are one silithid heart, five silithid talons and three intact silithid carapaces.

Parts of the Swarm. Korran has a message for Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar. You are to carry word back that Moktar is serving well out in Thousand Needles, and that Korran's studies are moving along. After the cracked carapaces taken from the silithid at the Rustmaul Digsite, Korran sends you back to Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar. Tell Belgrom that Moktar is doing his bidding well out in Thousand Needles. Tell him too that Korran's studies are progressing and that he hopes to learn more soon.

name.ptBR: Um barco para a Angra do Butim

text.enUS: Passage to Booty Bay. This errand traces the missing Sentinel Velinde Starsong across the Great Sea to the lawless haven of Booty Bay. Following shipping logs uncovered by Wharfmaster Dizzywig, Alliance travelers must journey from Ratchet to the Eastern Kingdoms in search of a goblin caravan driver named Ruzzgot. The search for the night elf Sentinel Velinde Starsong leads away from the familiar boughs of Ashenvale and onto the ocean trade lanes. In the bustling goblin port of Ratchet, Wharfmaster Dizzywig eventually unearths old shipping manifests confirming that Velinde booked passage aboard a vessel named the Black Osprey, bound directly for the pirate haven of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale.

name.deDE: Kunde über die Bedrohung breitet sich aus

text.enUS: Passing Word of a Threat. Historian Karnik gives you a sealed note for Advisor Belgrum. You are to tell Belgrum what you have witnessed and ask how Belgrum wants to proceed, while Karnik turns to Hammertoe's spirit about the Shadowforge in the Badlands. Karnik wants you to find Advisor Belgrum quickly, tell what you have seen, and ask how Belgrum wants to proceed. The note explains more. Meanwhile Karnik will speak with Hammertoe's spirit, hoping Hammertoe knows something that could put an end to the Shadowforge's doings in the Badlands, and can only pray that it does.

name.deDE: Kunde über die Bedrohung breitet sich aus

text.enUS: Passing Word of a Threat. Advisor Belgrum has read Historian Karnik's note and sends you back to Karnik with a message spoken on the king's authority: act on what is known, swiftly and decisively, and halt the Shadowforge's doings in the Badlands. Belgrum reads to the end of the note with widening eyes and calls the tidings evil. You are to return to Karnik and relay, on the king's authority, that the information must be acted on quickly and decisively. The Shadowforge's activities in the Badlands have to stop.

name.esES: Esfuerzos del pasado en la Garganta Grito de Guerra
name.frFR: Efforts passés dans le goulet des Chanteguerres
name.ptBR: Esforços anteriores na Ravina Brado Guerreiro

text.enUS: Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch. In Warsong Gulch, soldiers fight for Ashenvale while commanders honor their sacrifices. Capital officers accept the Ribbon of Sacrifice as a sign of steadfast service, even when battles bring no clear victory. The Silverwing Sentinels and Warsong Outriders fight brutal skirmishes along Ashenvale’s southern border. Many battles end without a clear victory. Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and other capitals honor those who hold their ground despite the odds. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks fighters who gave themselves to the struggle.

Path of Defense. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek prepares young Horde warriors to defend those who cannot defend themselves. He sends them to Thunder Ridge to prove their endurance against its electric beasts. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek teaches young warriors that defense is part of the Horde's duty. The post lies on the border between the Barrens and Durotar. Uzzek says a warrior's highest calling is to stand between danger and those unable to defend themselves, taking the blows so the Horde can endure.

Patience. Patience is a task assigned by Executor Zygand in Tirisfal Glades, demanding strict military accountability for the Dark Lady. With routine field reports overdue, Zygand dispatches an adventurer to collect updates from nearby Deathguards and an unusual sentry. The assignment highlights the rigorous, uncompromising discipline enforced across Forsaken holdings. Executor Zygand holds command over local security in Tirisfal Glades and tolerates no lapses in vigilance. To Zygand, serving Lady Sylvanas requires nothing less than absolute efficiency. When regular field dispatches fail to arrive at his post on schedule, he sees it as an unacceptable breach of duty rather than a minor delay. Rather than abandon his post to investigate, he sends incoming Forsaken agents to rein in delinquent subordinates and ensure that the borders remain secure.

Patrol Schedules. Following the discovery of an incriminating message signed only by an initial, Lieutenant Doren seeks to identify the traitor within the Rebel Camp. By cross-referencing duty rosters, duty records can reveal who shared patrol routes with Private Thorsen during the previous week. The recovered note bears only the initial M, which provides little on its own to expose the conspirator aiding the Kurzen forces. However, the author mentions sharing regular duty paths alongside Private Thorsen throughout the previous week. Lieutenant Doren directs you across the Rebel Camp to speak with Corporal Sethman, the soldier responsible for maintaining duty logs, to identify who walked alongside Thorsen.

name.esES: En patrulla por los Páramos de Poniente
name.frFR: Une patrouille dans la marche de l'Ouest

text.enUS: Patrolling Westfall. Gnoll packs roam Westfall's grasslands, threatening the people who still live there. Captain Danuvin calls on volunteers from Sentinel Hill to hunt them, fearing they work with the thieves in the Deadmines. Sentinel Hill is Westfall's main defense, held by local volunteers rather than royal troops. With Stormwind sending no soldiers to protect the outer farmlands, the people formed the People's Militia. Captain Danuvin, once a farmer in Westfall, leads them and refuses to abandon his homeland. The militia depends on travelers who pass through to help hold its perimeter against the dangers gathering across the plains.

name.esES: El señuelo atrapa a la reina

text.enUS: Pawn Captures Queen. After Bungle in the Jungle, Alchemist Pestlezugg hands you the lure and sends you into the silithid hive in Un'Goro Crater. The lure is meant to rouse the Gorishi Hive Queen, whose brain Pestlezugg wants brought back to Gadgetzan for study. Pestlezugg gives you the lure. The hive network is thought to hold a crystal that the silithid use as a hive-wide attunement device, and the hatcheries are the best place to look. Apply the lure to that crystal and the queen should come out, though several guards will probably be with her.

Pearl Diving. Rigglefuzz, a goblin, finds the Badlands full of vicious predators and bold scavengers, and survives by being tricky: flash bombs scare off the wildlife. The supply of crushed blue pearl powder is running low, so you are sent to the Vile Reef in Stranglethorn for more. The Badlands are harsh, and Rigglefuzz admits to being scared as a short little goblin among predators and scavengers. Rigglefuzz knows the recipe for flash bombs and uses them to frighten wildlife away. One ingredient is running low: crushed blue pearl powder.

Pelturas Whitemoon. Pelturas Whitemoon is a night elf father dwelling in Astranaar whose young daughter, Relara, has been struck by a terrible, corrupting illness. Desperate to save her, he works closely with local herbalist Orendil Broadleaf and traveling Alliance champions to gather sacred remedies from the surrounding wilds. His quest to heal Relara takes adventurers into some of Ashenvale's oldest sacred groves and ruins. Residing in the serene boughs of Astranaar, Pelturas Whitemoon lives the quiet life typical of forest-dwelling Kaldorei, often venturing out with his young daughter Relara to collect shimmering moonstones around Fallen Sky Lake. However, when Relara falls critically ill with a mysterious affliction, his quiet world collapses into frantic desperation. Astranaar is besieged on many fronts, but for Pelturas, nothing in the great forest matters more than saving his child.

Pendant of Shadow. The Pendant of Shadow is a dark talisman worn by the renegade warlock Morganth atop the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Brought to the mage Theocritus at the Tower of Azora, it serves as undeniable proof that the rogue spellcaster has been eliminated before his sinister ambitions could bear fruit.

Pendant of the Sea Lion. The Pendant of the Sea Lion is a sacred druidic talisman representing the union of aquatic agility and endurance. Assembled at the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, it serves as proof that an initiate is ready to master their aquatic form. To claim the aquatic aspect of the sea lion, a druid must prove mastery over the water's greatest hazards. The pendant is created by recovering two distinct halves: one embodying the agility needed to slip past aquatic predators, and the other granting the endurance required to withstand prolonged submersion. Brought before the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, the two pieces are joined into a single whole.

People's Militia. In Westfall, the People's Militia holds its ground against the Defias Brotherhood. Gryan Stoutmantle founded the volunteer force at Sentinel Hill after Stormwind withdrew its troops. With local farmers and visiting adventurers, they defend the region against banditry. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind, but the kingdom withdrew its troops and left the people defenseless. The Defias Brotherhood spread across the plains, seizing family homesteads, taking over iron mines, and extorting local farmers. With no royal reinforcements in sight, veteran warrior Gryan Stoutmantle rallied citizens and retired soldiers to form the People's Militia.

Perenolde Tiara. In the ruins of Alterac, an emerald-studded heirloom of the Perenolde family has turned up again. Dwarven craftsmen of Ironforge made it, and collectors in Stormwind now seek it. The Perenolde family ruled Alterac before the kingdom fell during the Second War. Their treasures included a delicate tiara, made by master jewelers in Ironforge and set with brilliant emeralds. After King Aiden Perenolde’s treachery brought Alterac to ruin, the tiara vanished amid the devastation of the high crags.

Perfect Yeti Hide. You have found a yeti hide that may well be perfect: remarkably thick and tough, beyond what the yetis of Rage Scar yield. At Camp Mojache, Jangdor Swiftstrider is looking for yeti hides. The hide is plainly thicker and sturdier than the ones from the yetis of Rage Scar. At Camp Mojache in Feralas, Jangdor Swiftstrider wants to buy yeti hides, so this one is worth bringing there.

Pestilent Scar. The Pestilent Scar is a deep, blighted gorge carved into the blighted terrain of the Eastern Plaguelands. Unlike the jagged rents torn open by catastrophic Scourge blight, this chasm appears to be a natural canyon or dried lakebed that was subsequently corrupted and overrun by ravenous oozes. Winding through the eastern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, the Pestilent Scar forms a gloomy rift in the corrupted landscape. While nearby rifts like the Infectis Scar were ripped into the earth by sudden catastrophic eruptions of the Plague of Undeath, scholars note that the Pestilent Scar seems to have originated as a natural geological formation. It was likely a deep river canyon or natural lake that dried up when the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, leaving a barren trench that gradually pooled with noxious runoff and foul slime.

Petitioner's Chamber. Petitioners wait for the crown in a chamber just inside Stormwind Keep. Nobles, church dignitaries, and visiting subjects spend the time mingling, drinking, or awaiting an audience. The Petitioner's Chamber lies just to the right as you enter Stormwind Keep. Count Remington Ridgewell and Bishop DeLavey wait there for audiences with boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Between formal visits, the chamber gives nobles and clergy room to mingle, trade gossip, and quietly press their concerns. Who holds influence in the realm can often be seen in who speaks with whom.

Phial of Scrying. In Darkshore, scouts use the Phial of Scrying to reach Onu from afar. The ancient of lore provides the enchanted vessel, which calls forth a bowl for scrying across corrupted woodlands. The Phial of Scrying carries mystical waters that form a temporary bowl on the ground. Scouts investigating deep within Darkshore use it for long-distance divination. From perilous places such as the Master's Glaive, they can speak directly with Onu instead of returning to his grove.

Philmor's Favor. Philmor's Favor is a delivery task in Stormwind prompted by an ongoing shortage of local dockhands. Couriers are asked to transport a delicate Gatehouse shipment to a secluded stockroom entrance situated on the second floor of Trias' Cheese shop in the Trade District. A persistent shortage of dockhands across Stormwind has strained the city's routine freight operations. To keep local cargo schedules from falling behind, handlers look for reliable travelers willing to haul sensitive crates directly into the commercial quarter.

Pie for Billy. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has left Billy Maclure bargaining for a pork belly pie. The Stonefield and Maclure families have feuded for generations, and Billy will say who has the necklace only after he gets his pie. Billy Maclure gives no apology when asked about Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace. He will not return it or say who has it until he gets a freshly baked pork belly pie. He knows Bernice is the finest cook in the valley, and he means to enjoy the bargain.

name.frFR: Morceau de la bannière de Krom'zar

text.enUS: Piece of Krom'zar's Banner. At Regthar Deathgate's bunker west of the Crossroads, a torn banner marks the broken assault. Warlord Krom'zar led the Kolkar retaliatory force from Desolace. Warlord Krom'zar led a warband east from Desolace to strike back. Kolkar chieftains across the Barrens had fallen, and the furious centaurs attacked the defensive bunkers west of the Crossroads. A strip cut from Krom'zar's fallen standard gives Regthar Deathgate proof that the assault was crushed and the southern trade routes were preserved for the Horde.

Piercing the Veil. Piercing the Veil is an introductory warlock trial given by Venya Marthand in Deathknell. It tests a freshly risen warlock's resolve by directing them to collect skulls from nearby mindless skeletons. Completing the task earns the novice the knowledge required to summon and bind an imp minion. Newly awakened Forsaken warlocks begin their journey in Deathknell under the instruction of Venya Marthand. She teaches that true strength lies not in raw brute force, but in knowledge and the precise mastery of chaotic powers. To prove they possess the focus and capability required to pierce the veil between worlds and subjugate nether beings, novices are dispatched to harvest the skulls of restless Rattlecage Skeletons roaming near Deathknell's abandoned smithy.

Pig and Whistle Tavern. In Stormwind City's Old Town, the Pig and Whistle Tavern welcomes travelers and local laborers. Veterans gather there to remember the kingdom's past conflicts. In Old Town's winding alleys, the Pig and Whistle Tavern offers warmth, ale, and lodging. Common citizens, working folk, and travelers fresh from the road gather there. Merchants such as recipe vendor Kendor Kabonka share the room with grizzled veterans, who trade memories of the First and Second Wars over their tankards.

Pilfered Windstones. Pilfered Windstones is a local quest on Zephras where players recover vital stolen resources from the Highlands Bandits. Stored in reserve for emergencies, these windstones are crucial for daily survival, but local peacekeepers are too stretched by cultist threats to clear out the thieves themselves. On the island of Zephras, windstones are not merely curious artifacts—they are vital resources necessary for day-to-day living. Settlements maintain an emergency cache to ensure survival during crises. However, village stores began suffering steady shortages, which were only unraveled when captured bandits from the northern Shen'dar Highlands were discovered carrying the stones. These sneakthieves had apparently been slipping into local stockpiles for months, exploiting thin security to snatch whatever supplies they could carry.

Pilot Bellowfiz. Pilot Bellowfiz, affectionately known as 'Fizzer,' is a dwarven driver stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. As a member of the Ironforge Siege Brigade, he is responsible for maintaining and fielding heavy dwarven war machines, specifically his own siege engine, Jetsteam. Stationed just outside the bustling halls of Ironforge at Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz represents the mechanical backbone of the dwarven military. Piloting the powerful siege engine known as Jetsteam, Bellowfiz spends his days tuning components, procuring essential parts, and keeping his machine battle-ready. Alongside his comrade Pilot Stonegear, Bellowfiz is constantly discussing vehicular designs, armor plating, and engine output, ensuring that the mountain kingdom's mechanized firepower remains unmatched across Khaz Modan.

Pilot Hammerfoot. Pilot Hammerfoot is a dwarven siege engine pilot of the Ironforge Siege Brigade, stationed near the mountain passes connecting Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Worried for a fellow pilot lost in the hills, he seeks willing adventurers to search for his friend. His presence highlights the dangers faced by dwarves along the high alpine ridges. Ironforge's siege engines are the pride of its Siege Brigade, but driving them across harsh mountainous terrain carries extreme risk. Stationed at the North Gate Outpost overlooking the border between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan, Pilot Hammerfoot guards the pilots' engines and watches the mountain passes. When a pilot goes missing, finding him quickly becomes a priority, especially with savage beasts prowling the nearby hills.

Pilot Longbeard. Pilot Longbeard is a dwarven siege engine pilot of the Ironforge Siege Brigade, stationed in the Hall of Arms within Ironforge's Military Ward. Though posted in the mountain city, he maintains close ties with gnomish tinkerers and fellow racing enthusiasts operating far away in the Shimmering Flats. Found amongst the martial displays and weaponsmiths of Ironforge's Military Ward, Pilot Longbeard represents the proud siege engine corps of Khaz Modan. While his duties keep him within the fortress city, Longbeard keeps an eager ear out for innovations and news from fellow mechanics across the continent, including the Brassbolts brothers tinkering out on the salt flats of Kalimdor.

Pilot Stonegear. Pilot Stonegear, nicknamed 'Stone', is a dwarf mechanic and driver in the Ironforge Siege Brigade stationed at Steelgrill's Depot. He operates the formidable siege engine known as Trollplow and works tirelessly to enhance its performance and armor. Adventurers traveling through Dun Morogh often help him secure rare materials to keep his war machine battle-ready. Stationed among the rumbling boilers and clanking tracks of Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear serves Ironforge as a proud driver in the Siege Brigade. His pride and joy is Trollplow, a heavy siege tank built to smash through enemy lines. Stonegear takes his machine seriously—knowing that in the heat of battle, a driver's life depends entirely on the resilience of gears, plates, and steam pressure. He constantly seeks to fine-tune both Trollplow's combat efficiency and the everyday livability of its cramped cockpit.

Pirate. Pirates and buccaneers are lawless seafaring plunderers operating across the Great Sea and coastal waters of Azeroth. Preying on Alliance, Horde, and neutral merchant vessels alike, they band together under loose flags to seize wealth, capture cargo, and control coastal coves. Their violent presence drives constant naval skirmishes from the waters of Kalimdor to the shores of the Eastern Kingdoms. Pirates—often called buccaneers, corsairs, or freebooters—are maritime raiders of nearly every race who make their living seizing ships and raiding coastal settlements. Their operations stretch far beyond simple robbery; crews regularly engage in smuggling, kidnappings, and mercenary contracts for whoever has coin. With the chaos left behind by the Third War and the collapse of northern kingdoms, naval enforcement has fractured, giving pirate factions the freedom to carve out fortified footholds on neglected islands and coastal coves.

Pixel. Pixel is an enterprising goblin courier operating out of Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Making her living delivering heavy goods across dangerous territories, she handles shipments like Warsong saw blades for the local Horde forces—though she never lets any cargo go without proper compensation. While Splintertree Post serves as a fortified bastion for the Horde amidst the hostile canopies of Ashenvale, Pixel remains firmly focused on profit. As an independent courier willing to haul freight into active war zones, she provides essential logistics for the Warsong Clan's logging efforts. However, true to goblin custom, contracts and coin dictate her cooperation. She holds fast to her deliveries until the client produces payment; for the saw blades, she wants a deadly blunderbuss to protect herself on the road. Always alert to an opportunity, she also pays passing adventurers for satyr horns, which are in high demand in Ratchet.

Piznik. Piznik is a disgruntled goblin surveyor hiding deep within Windshear Mine in the Stonetalon Mountains. Once a high-ranking overseer in the local Venture Company operations, he was sidelined by the ruthless Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. Now nursing a grudge, Piznik secretly gathers intel to undermine his former workplace. Before Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle seized supreme authority over Windshear Crag, Piznik held the enviable title of second-in-command across the entire operation. However, corporate restructuring in the Venture Company is unforgiving. Once Gerenzo took full control, Piznik found himself pushed aside and relegated to the murky depths of Windshear Mine. Rather than accepting his demotion quietly, Piznik bides his time underground, keeping a watchful eye on mine movements and quietly plotting revenge against the boss who demoted him.

Plague of Undeath. The Plague of Undeath is a supernatural contagion concocted by the Lich King under the direction of the Burning Legion to scourge northern Eastern Kingdoms. Transmitted through infected grain, airborne cauldrons, and tainted waterways, the sickness rapidly kills living mortals and raises them as mind-bound thralls of the Scourge. The plague was devised by the fallen shaman Ner'zhul after he was transformed into the Lich King by Kil'jaeden. From his icy seat atop the Frozen Throne in Northrend, Ner'zhul perfected the sickness as an unholy vanguard for the Burning Legion's invasion. Testing his power on isolated human villages across Northrend, he discovered that he could snuff out life and psychically command the corpses that arose shortly after. Ner'zhul's telepathic summon reached across the Great Sea to the Kirin Tor mage Kel'Thuzad, who abandoned Dalaran to serve the entity. Kel'Thuzad organized the secretive Cult of the Damned, whose mortal infiltrators laid the groundwork to poison Lordaeron from within.

Plagued Lands. Corruption is spreading through Darkshore, where Tharnariun Treetender hopes to save the afflicted wildlife. He asks travelers to calm a rabid thistle bear with an enchanted relic and bring it back alive. A creeping sickness twists Darkshore’s beasts into maddened, aggressive versions of themselves. Thistle bears suffer most, their rabid frenzy threatening travelers and the coast’s fragile balance. Night elf sentinels often answer with steel, while druids seek to understand the sickness and heal its cause.

Plaguemist Ravine. Plaguemist Ravine is a narrow mountain passage connecting the verdant wilderness of the Hinterlands to the haunted shores of Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. Named for the sickly fog that rolls down from the north, it provides a quiet and desolate route across the mountain range. Tucked away in the mountains northwest of Quel'Danil Lodge, Plaguemist Ravine acts as a geographic threshold between two radically different realms. To the south lies the lush, untamed highland forest of the Hinterlands, while to the north the pass opens directly upon Caer Darrow and the blighted expanse of the Western Plaguelands. The ravine earned its name from the foul, unnatural vapors that creep southward out of the Plaguelands, creating a jarring contrast with the crisp mountain air of the neighboring wilderness.

Plaguewood. Once a peaceful woodland known as Greenwood, the Plaguewood is now a blighted, fungus-choked expanse stretching south of Stratholme. Crawling with Scourge infrastructure and patrolling Scarlet Crusaders, it stands as one of the most corrupt corners of the Eastern Plaguelands. Before the Third War, this region was Greenwood, a vibrant forest that mirrored the lush woods of Elwynn. A modest village sat near its entrance, and its roads were traveled by farmers and soldiers alike. All of that collapsed when tainted grain arrived from Andorhal. Today, spongy, corrupted soil has taken the place of rich earth, and titanic mushrooms dwarf the dead trees, constantly spewing noxious brown vapors across the woodland floor.

name.esES: Torre del Bosque de la Peste

text.enUS: Plaguewood Tower. Plaguewood Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the northern reaches of the Plaguewood near Terrordale. Shattered during the Scourge invasion, it now stands as a broken ruin amid the blighted forest. Standing on the edge of the blight-choked Plaguewood and the blighted town of Terrordale, Plaguewood Tower once served the Kingdom of Lordaeron as a vital northern watchpost. When the Scourge swept across the land, the fortification was battered into crumbling masonry and left in ruins amid corrupted fungal canopies. Today the fractured stones still overlook the northern trails, a silent reminder of the watch Lordaeron once kept over this land.

Plainstrider Beak. Across the Barrens, hunters bring Plainstrider Beaks back to the Crossroads. Huntmasters use them as proof that birds threatening local provisions have been culled. Plainstriders forage around the Crossroads and threaten its supplies. Greater, fleeting, and ornery plainstriders roam the surrounding savannah. Sergra Darkthorn asks arriving hunters to bring back their beaks as proof that the flocks have been culled away from supply lines and storehouses.

Plainstrider Feather. Plucked from the swift birds roaming the plains of Mulgore, Plainstrider Feathers are essential materials gathered by young hunters on Red Cloud Mesa. The tauren of Camp Narache use them primarily for crafting clothing and tribal adornments, while honoring the creatures that provide for the village. On Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren learn early that survival relies on keen tracking and hunting. Plainstriders run wild across the grassy plateau, offering both sustenance and practical materials. Plucking their sturdy feathers allows the camp to craft traditional garments and gear. Presenting these feathers alongside fresh meat to Grull Hawkwind demonstrates respect for the tribe's needs and serves as the very first test toward being recognized by Chief Hawkwind and welcomed in Thunder Bluff.

Plainstrider Kidney. Across the Barrens, hunters harvest Plainstrider Kidney for Kalimdor's unusual brewing traditions. The organ is unappetizing to most travelers, yet essential to an exotic brew. The vast, arid plains of the Barrens are home to tall, flightless plainstriders. Hunters often take their feathers and meat for tools and simple rations, while Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks their internal organs for another purpose. Drohn says plainstrider kidneys are needed to recreate Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. He claims the kidneys give the brew a unique kick, in a tradition passed down through an unconventional line of brewmasters.

Plainstrider Meat. Plainstrider Meat is freshly harvested game taken from the flightless birds that wander the plains of Mulgore. For the young tauren coming of age on Red Cloud Mesa, gathering this sustenance serves as both vital winter provisions and a core rite of passage. Tauren life is inextricably bound to the land, balancing respect for nature with the practical necessity of survival. On Red Cloud Mesa, the settlement of Camp Narache depends heavily on game hunted from the surrounding grasslands. Plainstrider meat provides essential food reserves for the village when stocks run lean, while the birds' plumage offers material for clothing and ceremonial adornments.

name.esES: La amenaza de los zancudos de llanura
name.frFR: La menace des trotteurs des plaines

text.enUS: Plainstrider Menace. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends new Horde adventurers after plainstriders east of the outpost. The birds threaten its food supplies, and the hunt gives newcomers a first measure of the Barrens. The Crossroads coordinates supplies across Kalimdor, but plainstriders east of the outpost have begun picking at its food crates. Sergra Darkthorn, an orc shaman, sends newly arrived Horde adventurers to hunt the birds before they damage the stores. Their attacks threaten provisions the settlement depends on.

Plainstrider Scale. A tough scale harvested from the tallstriders roaming the sweeping plains of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller to counter a virulent infection. While plainstriders are best known for their soft feathers and lean meat, their powerful legs are covered in tough, protective scales. These scales are resilient against the harsh scrubland terrain and predator claws. Finding one intact and suitable for medicine requires patience, as only select plainstriders across Mulgore yield scales firm enough to be ground and prepared for folk remedies.

Plainstrider Talon. A Plainstrider Talon is a sharp claw harvested from the large, flightless plainstriders native to Mulgore. Tauren shamans use these talons alongside other natural reagents to craft sacred cleansing totems when the land's water sources are corrupted. The large, flightless plainstriders roam the open grasses of Mulgore, relying on powerful legs and sharp claws to defend against predators and forage through the tough prairie earth. To the tauren of Bloodhoof Village, every part of a hunted beast carries spiritual resonance. When goblin ventures tainted sacred sources like the Winterhoof Water Well, shaman Mull Thunderhorn sought plainstrider talons alongside prairie wolf paws. In tauren ritual crafting, gathering reagents from native predators and foragers allows the spiritual essence of the land to be channeled into totems capable of purging unnatural poisons.

Planting the Heart. At Lake Al'Ameth, you help Denalan tend a wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling. After clearing away its moss, he asks you to place it in his planter and see whether it can be healed. Denalan has scraped the foul moss from the wooden heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling. Yet an unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. Trusting his years of botany and soil tending, the herbalist asks you to bury the heart directly in his personal planter. He hopes the rich nutrients he blended can draw its remaining natural vitality back toward health.

Plea To The Alliance. Plea to the Alliance carries a desperate request for reinforcements from the surviving dwarven defenders of Dun Modr across the Thandol Span into Arathi. Faced with the slaughter of their garrison by Dark Iron infiltrators, the dwarves seek aid from the human forces stationed at Refuge Pointe, only to find the Alliance stretched beyond its limits. Following the devastation of Dun Modr and the sabotage of the Thandol Span by Dark Iron dwarves, the dwarven survivors hold a precarious foothold at the northern rim of the Wetlands. With Ironforge's main reserves yet to arrive, Rhag Garmason and Longbraid the Grim look north toward the Arathi Highlands. Learning of an Alliance encampment established at Refuge Pointe, Garmason dispatches an emissary across the shattered bridge to appeal to Captain Nials for urgent military aid.

Plundering the Plunderers. Wrenix the Wretched sends new Shattered Hand rogues against the Southsea Freebooters near Ratchet. Aboard the Tide Razor, they face pirates, locked strongboxes, and a dangerous guardian before claiming the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin contact in Ratchet, tests aspiring Shattered Hand operatives. He sends rogues south along the Barrens coast to a cove where the Tide Razor lies at anchor, crewed by Southsea Freebooters. They must board without being seen, enter the pirates’ den where cutpurses train, pick the strongboxes in the hold, and bring back the plunder.

Podrig's Order. Podrig's Order is a written military requisition penned by Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher. It requests a fresh shipment of weapons from Undercity merchant Gordon Wendham to keep Silverpine's Forsaken garrison properly armed. Silverpine Forest is a precarious frontier for the Forsaken, caught between encroaching Scourge, feral beasts, and other lurking threats. After an equipment inventory conducted by Deathguard Podrig on the orders of Executor Hadrec, the Sepulcher's stores were found mostly adequate but desperately low on replacement weapons. This official dispatch details the needed blades and arms to sustain the Deathguards holding the outpost.

Poison Water. Poison Water begins the tauren effort to purge pollution from Mulgore's sacred wells. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, young Horde defenders gather natural components from the plains to craft a restorative ritual totem. The grassy plains of Mulgore are sacred ground to the tauren, but insidious forces have begun threatening their vital lifeblood. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder stationed in Bloodhoof Village, discovers that goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted the precious water wells that sustain the tribes and the local wildlife. The pollution strikes directly at the spiritual heart of the nomadic people who recently settled here.

Pool of Ask'ar. The Pool of Ask'ar is a sprawling, submerged cavern lake located deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Teeming with aquatic beasts and foul naga invaders, its waters conceal ancient night elven architecture alongside hidden passageways that wind deeper into the corrupted sanctuary. Situated just beyond the Drowned Sacellum, the Pool of Ask'ar fills a massive subterranean vault with murky, cold water. The natural caverns and ancient stonework have become a nesting ground for oversized snapping turtles and deep-sea crabs, overseen by the enormous ancient chelonian known as Ghamoo-ra. The naga who have taken over the temple utilize this submerged threshold as a defensive staging ground, guarding the waterlogged approaches that lead deeper into the complex toward Lady Sarevess and the Moonshrine Ruins.

Pool of Tears. In Stonard, Fel'zerul asks you to search around the Pool of Tears for Atal'ai artifacts. The Warchief sent Fel'zerul's people to look into strange events at the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, and they arrived to find it sunk. The Atal'ai trolls are dark casters, a tribe notorious for forbidden magic. When Fel'zerul's party reached the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, they were astonished to find it sunk. Green dragons now watch over the place and call themselves protectors of Azeroth.

Pool of Tears. The Pool of Tears is a large, murky lake dominating the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Deep beneath its surface lies the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar, brought low by the Green Dragonflight to contain the horrors within. Today, vicious frenzies patrol the turbid waters, and ancient troll ruins litter its drowned banks. Long ago, fanatical Atal'ai trolls raised a monumental ziggurat to their bloodthirsty god, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Horrified by the blasphemies taking place within, the Dragon Aspect Ysera shattered the ground beneath the structure, submerging the massive temple into the depths of the marsh. The existing lake flooded over the temple ruins. While the dragons sought to bury the evil forever, the ziggurat still stands beneath the silt and waves, and green drakes remain vigilant in the area to keep its corruption sealed.

Pools of Arlithrien. South of Darnassus, the Pools of Arlithrien have grown dangerous and neglected. Their moonwell once drew night elves to a quiet sanctuary, but beasts and nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs now threaten the springs. The Pools of Arlithrien lie beneath Teldrassil’s shaded boughs, south of Darnassus. A stone moonwell rests at their heart, holding waters touched by Elune’s grace. Though the sanctuary lies near the night elven capital, danger has driven the night elves to leave it untended. Agitated beasts roam the shallows, and the Gnarlpine furbolgs nearby remain hostile. What was meant to be a peaceful retreat now reflects the growing troubles across the island.

Pools of Vision. The Pools of Vision are a subterranean cavern nestled beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. Marked by still waters and dim caverns, this secluded subterranean space serves as the primary enclave for the Forsaken within the tauren capital. While the sunlit peaks of Thunder Bluff belong to the wind, earth, and sky, the Pools of Vision plunge directly beneath Spirit Rise into shadowy seclusion. Accessible from a discreet cave path off the bridge leading to the rise, this subterranean grotto offers subterranean respite quite unlike the open-air lodges above. Here, misty waters pool in the dark, creating an isolated atmosphere where Horde spellcasters gather far from the bustling central mesas.

Poor Old Blanchy. Verna Furlbrow waits beside the road in Westfall with her stranded family and starving mare. Their wagon broke during an attempt to escape, leaving Old Blanchy exhausted. Verna asks you to gather oats from nearby abandoned farmsteads and feed the old horse. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow are stranded beside Westfall's main road. Bandits and rogue mechanical harvest golems have driven families like theirs from their homes. As the Furlbrows tried to haul their belongings to safety, their wagon broke down, leaving them marooned in open country.

Pork Belly Pie. In Elwynn Forest, Billy Maclure wants a pie from the Stonefield farm before he speaks about a missing necklace. Auntie Bernice Stonefield bakes it despite the feud between their families. The Stonefield and Maclure families have quarreled over land and pride for years in Elwynn Forest. Young Billy Maclure has a weakness for Auntie Bernice's pork belly pie. When a valuable Stonefield family necklace goes missing, Billy refuses to share what he knows until an adventurer brings him a warm slice. Bernice bakes the pie reluctantly, wishing the greedy boy would choke on it.

Portals of the Legion. After Hand of Iruxos, Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village shows you the Hand and asks you to banish six demon portals at Mannoroc Coven, warning you to be wary of the portal guardians. Taiga Wisemane holds up the Hand of Iruxos, a grisly thing to look at, and says you must carry it if the demon portals around Mannoroc Coven are ever to be closed. The demon threat is increasing, and shutting the portals will check the number of demons crossing into this world. She wants all six portals banished, and she warns you to be wary of their guardians.

Powder to Ironband. Powder to Ironband is an Alliance delivery quest connecting the Explorer's League headquarters in Ironforge to Loch Modan. Having secured official approval from Prospector Stormpike, adventurers are sent to Thelsamar to oversee a crucial shipment of blasting powder bound for Ironband's Excavation. Archaeological excavation in the mountains of Khaz Modan requires heavy ordnance. When Prospector Ironband's expedition in southern Loch Modan ran short of blasting supplies, word was dispatched to the League's leadership in Ironforge. Prospector Stormpike quickly authorized the requisition, directing the runner to coordinate with Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar, the primary logistical hub for the valley.

Powdered Azurite. In Hillsbrad Foothills, Powdered Azurite is taken from the Azurelode Mine. Thun'grim Firegaze needs it to forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors. Powdered Azurite comes from the mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. Human workers dig the blue stone from Azurelode Mine, then grind and pack it for trade and metalworking. A skilled smith mixes the dust with dense metals to make armor more durable and resilient.

Power Overwhelming. Power Overwhelming is a quest issued by High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind City to assist the secluded Kirin Tor. Players are dispatched to the ruined city of Dalaran to quell a dangerous outbreak of wayward arcane energy manifested as a Mana Elemental. Following the devastating destruction of Dalaran at the hands of the arch-demon Archimonde during the Third War, the Kirin Tor retreated inward. Once welcoming scholars and sorcerers from across the world, the surviving magi have grown secretive, reclusive, and deeply distrustful of outsiders as they work tirelessly behind closed borders to rebuild their ruined city.

Power over Poison. In Darnassus, a young druid returns to complete Power over Poison. The Cenarion Circle's trial began in Darkshore, where the initiate learned to brew a remedy by hand. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong asks young druids to gather Earthroot and Lunar Fungus by hand. They brew a salve to heal stricken wildlife. Before granting the magic to purge toxins, the Cenarion Circle wants initiates to know the hardship of treating poison without spiritual aid. The work teaches them what common folk face when venom strikes, and why a druid must meet their suffering with care.

Power over Poison. Power over Poison is the concluding rite in a young Horde druid's trial to master restorative nature magic. Having cured afflicted gazelles around the Crossroads using only herbal mixtures, the initiate returns to Turak Runetotem on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise to receive the true gift of Cure Poison. Before granting a fledgling druid the innate magical power to cleanse venoms, the Cenarion Circle demands they understand the physical reality of affliction. Dendrite Starblaze sent the novice to the Crossroads, where Tonga Runetotem had them gather earthly reagents for a curative salve made by hand. Only by treating the poisoned plains gazelles of the Barrens without spiritual aid does the student witness the agonizing struggle ordinary creatures face against natural and unnatural toxins.

Powers of the Void. A stolen tome draws Drusilla La Salle's attention in Northshire. Powers of the Void was kept in a restricted wing of Northshire Abbey's library until a novice took it while defecting to the Defias Brotherhood. Drusilla seeks its recovery for her own study of dark magic. Powers of the Void was kept behind guarded shelves in Northshire Abbey's library. The abbey archives hold holy scripture and clerical records, along with scholarly works on shadow and nether energies. The tome was presumably penned by the archmage Khadgar. Because its subject was dangerous, abbey authorities kept the book under guard and away from casual visitors. That barred Northshire's warlock mentor, Drusilla La Salle, from browsing it without drawing the priesthood's suspicion.

Pozzik. Pozzik is an esteemed goblin tinkerer and racer stationed at the Mirage Raceway on the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Once one of the most respected engineers in Undermine, he now dedicates his technical genius to constructing experimental rocket cars and settling the ultimate debate of engineering supremacy against his gnome counterpart. Before retiring to the harsh salt flats of Thousand Needles, Pozzik built a legendary reputation among the goblins. As one of the most respected tinkerers out of Undermine, his technical expertise spans complex internal combustion, propulsion, and hazardous chassis construction. Rather than settling into comfortable obscurity, however, Pozzik took his mechanical mastery into the desert to push high-speed machinery far past its breaking point.

Practical Prey. Vel'rin Fang needs hunters to bring tiger hides from the Echo Isles to Sen'jin Village. The Darkspear need the supplies as their numbers grow and their stores run low. The Darkspear in Sen'jin Village have to make every resource last along Durotar's harsh coast. Tiger pelts can be made into tents, blankets and armor. As refugees arrive and scouts return, the village's stores have thinned, and leatherworker Vel'rin Fang has sent hunters out for more hides.

Prairie Alpha Tooth. A Prairie Alpha Tooth is taken from the fierce pack leaders roaming the plains around Thunder Bluff. In tauren tradition, these teeth serve as a potent offering to cleanse and honor the land's precious water sources. The water wells of Mulgore are vital lifelines for the tauren, and maintaining their spiritual purity demands rites of respect and sacrifice. To cleanse the Wildmane Well, Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village requires teeth gathered from the prairie wolf alphas that stalk the shadow of Thunder Bluff. As apex predators of the rolling grassy plains, these alphas represent the raw strength of the wild. Offering their teeth honors the balance between hunter, prey, and the spirits of the earth.

Prairie Wolf Heart. A Prairie Wolf Heart is a vital organ harvested from the wolves roaming the grasslands of Mulgore. It serves as an essential ingredient in an urgent folk remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village to counteract venomous infection. The wolves of the plains are fierce predators, hardy and persistent across the sweeping grasses of Mulgore. Their hearts are sought out by Maur Raincaller, a tauren residing in Bloodhoof Village who fell victim to the legendary plainstrider known as Mazzranache. Struck by the creature's virulent, fever-inducing venom, Maur relies on traditional plains medicine to halt the spreading poison. Alongside other potent reagents like cougar bone and bird gizzard, the vital essence of a freshly slain prairie wolf provides the cleansing properties needed to concoct a cure before delirium proves fatal.

Prairie Wolf Paw. Prairie Wolf Paws are harvested from the predators roaming the plains of Mulgore. Shamanic practitioners, such as Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, use them as organic components to bind the natural power of the land into cleansing totems. Prairie wolves stalk the rolling grasses across Mulgore, hunting in packs alongside prairie stalkers and their pack alphas. While dangerous to young hunters and local livestock, the creatures are deeply intertwined with the spiritual balance of the plains. Tauren shamans view the wolf's paws not merely as trophies, but as vital conduits of the earth's innate vitality.

Prayer to Elune. A spirit held in a cage in Searing Gorge, Zamael Lunthistle, asks if you will help him. He has not had visitors in many years, and first wants you to hear his tale. Zamael Lunthistle greets you with a praise to Elune and says that many years have passed since anyone visited him. He asks if you will help, and begins with a request that you hear his tale.

Prayer to Elune. Zamael Lunthistle asks you to find his prayer to Elune, set down on a tablet of gold. One of the idol-worshipping scoundrels must carry it, and Zamael wants it taken to Astarii Starseeker in Darnassus. Zamael's faith has been rekindled, but he says that matters little after the countless malevolent actions he has taken against the world and its inhabitants. He does not expect absolution. All he asks is that the prayer be heard, so he sends you to recover the golden tablet from the idol worshippers and carry it to Astarii Starseeker in Darnassus.

Prehistoric Prism. Prehistoric Prism is an exploratory quest directing adventurers to transport a multifaceted titan relic from the Wetlands to Ironforge. Entrusted by Prospector Whelgar, the relic is donated to High Explorer Magellas in the Hall of Explorers to further the League's study of the ancient keepers. While surveying the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar identifies a remarkable artifact adorned with intricate keeper inscriptions across its facets. Recognizing that a find of such historical weight belongs in scholarly hands, the dwarven prospector urges that it immediately be transported to the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Whelgar hopes the discovery will be entered into the official catalogue, ensuring the adventurer receives proper credit alongside his authentication.

Preserving Knowledge. Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore sends you into the Ruins of Alterac, where ogres have settled among the precious books left behind. Tomes the ogres looted must be recovered, and one above all: a worn leather book holding The Arm of Gri'lek, a work of ancient troll lore. Ogres have made their home in the ruins of Alterac, and Dibbs dreads what they might be doing to the books still there. You are to go in, hunt for the tomes the ogres have looted, and recover whatever you can. Dibbs would search the ruins too, but fears old bones would not survive the climb into the mountains.

Pridewing Venom Sac. Pridewing Venom Sacs are harvested from the lethal wyverns nesting around Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. The night elves of Astranaar seek to stockpile and destroy these sacs after intelligence suggests Horde operatives harvest the potent poison for covert assassinations. The pridewings of Stonetalon are dangerous, airborne predators native to the peaks south of Ashenvale, particularly around Mirkfallon Lake. While wild wyverns are naturally venomous, Alliance intelligence out of Theramore suggests that Horde assassins have begun milking them for poison to coat blades used in covert raids against night elf settlements. To safeguard their kin and disrupt enemy supplies, the Sentinels in Astranaar hire scouts to hunt down the beasts and collect the venom glands before the Horde can secure them.

Pridewings of Stonetalon. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim: Concerned about covert Horde attacks, the Sentinels in Astranaar seek to intercept a deadly weapon before it can strike their people. Intelligence from Theramore reveals that orc assassins harvest toxic venom from the wyverns of Stonetalon Mountains for clandestine raids. To protect their fragile border, Alliance scouts are dispatched south to harvest the venom sacs first and starve the enemy of their lethal poison. Though open war has not been declared between the Alliance and the Horde across northern Kalimdor, the peace between them is razor-thin. Skirmishes break out under thick forest canopies, and quiet, deniable strikes have replaced full-scale armies. Sentinel commanders in Astranaar maintain constant vigilance against covert enemy movements, knowing that complacency could cost them their sanctuary.

Priest. Priests are spiritual guides and conduits of immense unseen power who shape belief, mend flesh, and guard souls. Channeling the radiant energies of faith or plumbing the terrifying depths of the Void, they serve as the vital heart of any war party. Across Azeroth, their traditions range from the Church of the Holy Light to the Moon Goddess's Sisterhood and shadowy Forsaken cults. Priests guide the spiritual destiny of their communities. While physical combatants test their mettle with steel, priests draw power directly from conviction. Through divine connection, they soothe grievous wounds, raise fallen companions from death's threshold, and weave mystic barriers to repel incoming harm. Their presence on the field often marks the difference between survival and annihilation.

Priestess A'moora. Priestess A'moora is a devout night elf servant of the Moon Goddess residing within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Working closely under the guidance of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind's priesthood, she attends to rituals of spiritual purification and communion with Elune. Travelers exploring Teldrassil are often directed to her when matters involve sacred offerings and the mystical wildlife of the boughs. Within the serene marble halls of the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora spends her days in contemplation and service. As an ordained priestess of Elune, she assists in tending the spiritual needs of Darnassus and preserving the delicate rituals passed down through millennia. While much of the Sisterhood oversees military defenses or diplomacy, A'moora focuses on traditional devotions and sacred matters concerning the natural spirits of Teldrassil.

Priestess Alathea. Within Darnassus, Priestess Alathea guides night elf priests in the Temple of the Moon. Devoted to Elune, she teaches sacred rites and helps acolytes prepare for healing, protection, and celestial magic. Priestess Alathea teaches and guides the Sisterhood of Elune within Darnassus's Temple of the Moon. After leaving Shadowglen, night elf initiates come to the temple to deepen their bond with the Goddess. Alathea shares sacred knowledge with those who devote themselves to healing, protection, and divine light.

Priestess Anetta. Inside Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta teaches new priests their first rites of the Holy Light. She is a human cleric and a member of the Brotherhood of Northshire. On the ground floor of Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta keeps to the quiet library wing. Defias bandits and kobolds trouble the valley, and she reminds those who pass that the Light may be the one thing that saves them someday.

Priestess Josetta. In Goldshire, Priestess Josetta guides young priests beyond their first trials in Northshire. She teaches faith, devotion, and the work of serving others. Priestess Josetta tends to the people of Elwynn Forest from an upstairs room in the Lion's Pride Inn. Travelers, guards, and local workers come within her reach there. She offers spiritual care among ordinary folk, showing that service to the Holy Light can be given wherever people need comfort.

Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield wants Princess Must Die! before Princess ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning sow from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, and Ma wants the family to gather their crops in peace. Princess has put the Stonefield harvest at risk. The prize-winning sow belongs to the Brackwells, but she has grown enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots and devouring their vegetables. Ma Stonefield has had enough of the sow eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants Princess put down before the pig ruins the season’s yield.

Prismatic Punch Card. The Prismatic Punch Card is the highest security clearance data card found within the fallen city of Gnomeregan. Upgraded sequentially through a series of Matrix Punchograph terminals, it holds data desperately sought by gnome refugees in Ironforge. When the gnomes fled the trogg invasion and toxic irradiation of Gnomeregan, massive troves of research and civic records were abandoned in the depths. To safeguard high-level systems, the gnomes utilized an escalating security protocol. Accessing the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminal in the lower Engineering Labs requires working through a progression of punch cards: starting from a basic White Punch Card and advancing through Yellow, Blue, and Red clearances at dedicated terminals before stamping the final Prismatic Punch Card. Its encoded clearance level is whimsically noted as pending the invention of an entirely new number.

Prison Break In. Magus Wordeen Voidglare is in Tarren Mill on research but now faces a crisis. A few months ago four Forsaken fled the Undercity after stealing artifacts from a secure vault, and Sylvanas wants them back. Voidglare came to Tarren Mill to research and now must resolve a crisis. Four Forsaken turned their backs on their brethren and, worse, stole from the Dark Lady. They broke into a secure vault and took four artifacts the apothecaries required for certain studies. Sylvanas wants them returned.

Pristine Pesterhide Pelts. Pristine Pesterhide Pelts is a task undertaken on behalf of Kristy Grant, a traveler seeking the radiant coats of the Pesterhide hyenas in Thousand Needles. Lacking combat training herself, Kristy relies on capable adventurers to hunt the beasts and harvest their pelts. Her goal is to send these unique hides back across the sea to her sisters in Stormwind, where they can be fashioned into fine garments and goods. Far from the bustling cobblestone avenues of Stormwind, Kristy Grant finds herself traveling through the arid, sun-baked canyon floor of Thousand Needles. While observing the local wildlife, she is struck by the striking hue and quality of the coats worn by the native Pesterhide hyenas. Recognizing that such distinct pelts are virtually unknown in the Eastern Kingdoms, Kristy envisions sending a shipment of hides back home to her sisters. In her eyes, the pelts represent not only a piece of the Kalimdor frontier, but raw material that skilled family hands in the kingdom can transform into something truly extraordinary.

Pristine Spider Silk. Stormwind mages seek Pristine Spider Silk for robes woven to endure enchantments. The fine thread comes from venomous spiders in Duskwood. Stormwind mages need silk strong enough to bear enchantments and the wear of an adept. Tailors use common spider silk, but the strands gathered from carrion recluses and black widow hatchlings in Duskwood are more resilient. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum send rising adepts into those woods to collect the silk. Master tailor Wynne Larson then weaves it into a robe for an adept.

Pristine Spider Silk. In Stormwind, High Sorcerer Andromath sends rising Alliance mages to Duskwood for pristine spider silk. They bring eight samples to Wynne Larson in the Mage Quarter, where she makes a robe for an adept. High Sorcerer Andromath marks a mage’s passage beyond apprenticeship with vestments fit for an adept. In the Wizard’s Sanctum, arcane mastery is matched by the robes its practitioners wear. Rather than buy finished garments, the mage must show field skill and discernment by taking pristine, unblemished silk from dangerous spiders.

name.frFR: Une peau de yéti en parfait état

text.enUS: Pristine Yeti Hide. You have come into a yeti hide that is unusually thick and tough, tougher even than any you have seen from the yetis of Rage Scar. Pratt McGrubben at Feathermoon Stronghold is looking for yeti hides, and this one may interest him. This hide is pristine, and clearly thicker and sturdier than the hides taken from the yetis of Rage Scar. Pratt McGrubben, at Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas, wants to buy yeti hides, so this one is worth carrying to him.

Prompt Potion Runner. Prompt Potion Runner is an urgent Undercity delivery quest where players must race an unstable concoction across the slime canal to the Apothecarium. The quest highlights the physical infirmities of undeath and the volatile nature of Forsaken alchemical research. In the subterranean corridors of the Undercity, the Forsaken alchemist Alessandro urgently needs a swift courier. Having prepared a highly volatile concoction with an extremely short shelf life, he cannot risk transporting it himself across the city's toxic slime canal due to the fragile state of his undead joints. An adventurer must sprint against the clock to ensure the brew arrives intact before it degrades into useless sludge.

Proof of Demise. Proof of Demise is a military directive issued by Deathguard Burgess in Brill to thin the ranks of the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Initiated on the orders of Varimathras, Sylvanas Windrunner's dreadlord lieutenant, it tests a soldier's loyalty to the Forsaken cause. Recruits are ordered to strip signet rings from fallen crusaders as tangible evidence of their slaughter. The campaign across northern Tirisfal Glades is not merely defensive; it is a coordinated war of eradication. Varimathras, the dreadlord who surrendered and pledged his blade to Sylvanas Windrunner, oversees many of the Forsaken's aggressive military maneuvers against the living. His directives trickle down to commanders like Executor Zygand and frontline officers such as Deathguard Burgess. Burgess makes the directive clear: the human race is viewed as vermin to be purged from Lordaeron, and the zealous crusaders nearby are the immediate target.

Prospect of Faith. Hammertoe Grez, nursing wounds, sends you with the amulet to Prospector Ryedol in the Badlands. Ryedol knows what Hammertoe was seeking, and what the Shadowforge clan must not be allowed to find. Hammertoe Grez, clutching at wounds, pauses to steady himself, then asks you to find Ryedol and hand over the amulet. Hammertoe is sure Ryedol will figure out what to do. Ryedol knows Hammertoe was seeking the origins of their people, and that Hammertoe also meant to thwart the Shadowforge clan, who cannot be permitted to get hold of the scrolls.

Prospect of Faith. Prospector Ryedol sends you to Ironforge with Hammertoe's Amulet. Historian Karnik and Hammertoe were working together to find the lost artifacts of Uldaman, and Ryedol guesses the Shadowforge found out the pair knew more than they let on. Ryedol sorts through who might know what to do next and settles on Historian Karnik, who is in Ironforge. You are to tell Karnik what has happened to Hammertoe and place the amulet in the historian's hands. Karnik will say what needs doing from there.

Prospector Ironband. Prospector Darteus Ironband is an honest, hardworking dwarven surveyor who oversees an archaeological dig in southeastern Loch Modan. Working under the banner of the Dwarven Explorers' Guild, he is determined to uncover the earthen heritage buried beneath Khaz Modan. Despite setbacks and hostile local creatures, Ironband remains committed to sending regular progress reports and uncovered relics back to Ironforge. Darteus Ironband leads the dig at Ironband's Excavation Site nestled in the hills of southeastern Loch Modan. Like many field researchers in the Explorers' Guild, Ironband believes that the soil of Khaz Modan hides vital truths about the origins of the dwarven race. His camp works tirelessly digging trenches and sifting through rubble in search of ancient relics, stone tablets, and earthen artifacts. Despite the slow pace of unearthing buried history, Ironband's resolve remains unshaken, and he is always eager to recruit competent adventurers to safeguard his operation.

Prospector Remtravel. In southern Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel leads an Explorers' League dig among ancient relics. The dwarf's scattered focus and the dangers around camp make his work perilous. The Explorers' League sent Prospector Remtravel across the sea to establish a dig in southern Darkshore. Night elves guard their ancestral lands, yet the League's drive to uncover Azeroth's origins carries its prospectors into forgotten places. Remtravel unearths fossilized history and ancient stones, while aggressive wildlife and hostile local threats make the camp difficult for one scatterbrained dwarf to manage.

Prospector Ryedol. Prospector Ryedol is an Explorers' League surveyor stationed on a dusty rise overlooking the eastern Badlands. Watching over the perilous excavations below, he strives to recover lost dwarven relics and maintain hope in a barren wasteland overrun by troggs and beasts. Perched upon a rugged hill just south of Hammertoe's Digsite, Prospector Ryedol represents the ongoing efforts of Ironforge's Explorers' League in the Badlands. The arid valley is rich in ancient titan secrets and earthen heritage, but field expeditions here are constantly beleaguered by savage troggs, ravenous coyotes, and territorial drakes. Ryedol coordinates retrieval efforts for dwarven gear stolen by the Dark Iron dwarves and seeks signs of hope amid the ruined outposts, determined not to let the League's sacrifices in the wastes be in vain.

Prospector Stormpike. Prospector Stormpike is a blunt, short-tempered dwarf stationed within the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. A member of the renowned Stormpike clan, he oversees logistical support for distant archaeological digs and lends his sharp intellect to deciphering coded missives. Tucked away amid the towering bookshelves of the Hall of Explorers, Prospector Stormpike coordinates excavation efforts across Khaz Modan and beyond. Despite his gruff demeanor and impatience with idle chatter, he is deeply dedicated to uncovering dwarven history, keeping distant sites supplied with essentials like blasting powder. Beneath his rough exterior lies a keen analytical mind skilled at breaking intricate ciphers, making him an unexpected asset to Alliance scouts dealing with clandestine threats.

Prospector Whelgar. Prospector Whelgar is a dwarven archaeologist stationed at an excavation site in the Wetlands east of Menethil Harbor. His mission to uncover titan relics has stalled after vicious raptors overran the dig. He now seeks hardy adventurers willing to brave the beasts to recover ancient artifacts. Sent into the marshy wilderness of the Wetlands to unearth the history of the dwarven race, Prospector Whelgar established an archaeological camp known as Whelgar's Excavation Site. The valley was once rich with ancient stone relics, but the local raptors quickly grew territorial and drove his team into hiding. Despite the danger, Whelgar refuses to abandon his duty.
