He remains focused on recovering valuable relics—including the enigmatic Goaz Stone—before wild predators or rival scoundrels ruin the site entirely.

Protect Kanati Greycloud. Protect Kanati Greycloud is a Horde quest at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Warned that centaur assassins have targeted the tauren Kanati Greycloud, adventurers must make a stand beside him and repel a squad of Galak assassins. While stationed among the towering sandstone spires of Whitereach Post, the tauren Kanati Greycloud learns from intercepted centaur orders of an assassination plot directed squarely at his life. The Galak tribe of centaur, relentless in their hostility toward the nomadic tauren and their Horde allies, are not content merely raiding supply paths; they seek to eliminate those who settle in their canyons.

Protect Kaya. Protect Kaya is a Horde escort quest in the Stonetalon Mountains. After discovering Kaya Flathoof held captive by hostile Grimtotem tauren, adventurers guide her through dangerous mountain trails to reach Camp Aparaje. Returning word of her survival brings immense relief to her anxious father, Makaba Flathoof. The Stonetalon Mountains harbor bitter rivalries among the tauren, none sharper than the tension surrounding the treacherous Grimtotem clan. Deep within hostile territory, Kaya Flathoof was captured and held prisoner. Escaping on foot requires navigating winding trails flanked by opportunistic predators and watchful enemies, making an armed escort her only realistic hope of reaching friendly soil.

Protect the Frontier. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern bridge as predators threaten the frontier. Stormwind's forces are thin here, and wolves and bears have grown bold near the Eastvale Logging Camp. He asks capable adventurers to cull the beasts threatening travelers and workers. Guard Thomas watches the bridge over the river at Elwynn Forest's eastern edge. Goldshire and the Northshire Valley have a visible Stormwind garrison, but this frontier receives far less protection. With Stormwind's forces stretched across the realm, Thomas is one of few sentries between the settled heartlands and the wilderness. Travelers help keep vital supply roads open.

text.enUS: Protecting the Herd. Protecting the Herd is a task given by Rudra Amberstill at the Amberstill Ranch in Dun Morogh. A ferocious predatory beast named Vagash has been attacking the ranch's prized mountain rams in the night, and with Ironforge's military garrison spread thin across the realm, the local breeders must rely on passing adventurers for defense. Amberstill Ranch supplies the mountain rams that serve as iconic mounts and working beasts for the Bronzebeard dwarves. Maintaining these herds is vital to Dun Morogh's rustic economy. When night fell and frantic cries echoed over the paddocks, the Amberstill family discovered two of their prized rams missing. The culprit is Vagash, a notorious and savage beast lurking in the nearby crags above the ranch, known for violently preying on local livestock.

Protecting the Shipment. Protecting the Shipment is an escort quest in southern Loch Modan where adventurers safeguard the courier Miran on his way to Ironband's Excavation Site. Miran carries a crate of volatile blasting powder urgently needed by Prospector Ironband. The journey exposes lingering Dark Iron subversion threatening the dwarven hinterlands. Prospector Ironband's archaeological dig in the hills of southern Loch Modan requires a steady supply of blasting powder to cut through stubborn stone. When supply lines break down and courier wagons come under threat, the courier Miran is left stranded on the road with a heavy load of powder. Guiding Miran safely across the uneven roads to the excavation site ensures Ironband's work does not stall completely.

Proudhorn the Elder. Proudhorn the Elder is an ancestral tauren spirit honored during the Lunar Festival atop the heights of Thunder Bluff. Visiting him is an act of deep reverence, acknowledging the wisdom of the ancestors who watch over Mulgore and the Horde. Perched high on the windblown mesas of Thunder Bluff, Proudhorn the Elder manifests as an ancestral presence during the Lunar Festival. Tauren culture holds the voices of their ancestors in the highest regard, believing that the spirits of ancient leaders and sages linger to offer guidance and strength to the living.

Prove Your Worth. Prove Your Worth is an introductory Horde quest offered by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. To assist the Forsaken campaign against southern human and dwarven territories, adventurers are tasked with thinning the feral worgen prowling near the roadside. It marks the opening step in unraveling the arcane fallout wrought by Archmage Arugal. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, have set their sights on securing the regions south of Tirisfal Glades, including human and dwarven enclaves. However, the path through Silverpine Forest remains fraught with danger. Instead of an open staging ground, the Forsaken find their supply lines and forward bases threatened by feral Moonrage worgen that roam the pine-choked hills.

Proving Allegiance. Proving Allegiance is the crucial trial presented by Gunther Arcanus to determine whether you truly serve the free-willed Forsaken or the Lich King. To earn the solitary necromancer's trust, you are sent to summon and destroy Lillith Nefara, a dangerous Scourge operative lurking near his island. Gunther Arcanus has isolated himself on an island in Brightwater Lake since rising into undeath, fiercely clinging to his autonomy. Though Bethor Iceshard's magical enchantments on Gunther's spellbook confirmed the emissary does not carry the foul taint of the Scourge, words and charms are not enough for the paranoid hermit. To earn his confidence, an outsider must demonstrate active hostility toward the minions of the Lich King through decisive violence.

Proving Grounds. Proving Grounds is an initiation rite given by Lieutenant Haggerdin to Alliance recruits enlisting with the Stormpike Guard in Alterac. To earn an official Stormpike Insignia, aspirants must venture into the harpy-infested Icewing Caverns and recover a planted battle standard. Proving one's courage in the cavern marks the first step toward rising through the expedition's military ranks. The Stormpike Guard wages a relentless campaign in Alterac Valley against the Frostwolf Clan. Lieutenant Haggerdin, coordinating forces from the Alliance encampment in the Alterac Mountains, refuses to send green recruits onto the battlefield without a test. Before granting any soldier an official place in the guard, Haggerdin demands proof of skill and nerve by sending them into the treacherous Icewing Caverns southwest of Dun Baldar.

Proving Your Worth. Proving Your Worth is a crucial step in Sven Yorgen's campaign for revenge in western Duskwood. Before allowing an adventurer to confront the necromancer Morbent Fel directly, the grieving hermit demands proof that they can overcome the undead legions infesting Raven Hill Cemetery. Sven Yorgen hides in a secluded camp north of the howling woods, consumed by grief and fury over the slaughter of his family. He has pieced together that the shadowy Dark Riders who razed his homestead were allied with a sinister necromancer named Morbent Fel. Though Sven hungers for retribution, he is not reckless enough to throw an untried recruit directly into Fel's grasp. He demands a display of sheer combat mastery against the skeletal forces occupying Raven Hill Cemetery.

Prowler Claws. Across the Barrens, Prowler Claws are carried back to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. They show that a hunter can track and defeat the prowlers stalking the plains. Savannah Prowlers hide in the Barrens’ tall grass, waiting to strike with patience and cunning. These large cats ambush creatures that enter their hunting grounds, unlike grazing plainstriders and zhevra. Taking their curved claws means facing predators that rely on stealth and defend their territory. For Horde warriors and scouts, the hunt tests whether they can track a stalker through its own ground and make it the prey.

Prowlers of the Barrens. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after the savannah prowlers. Their claws will show whether you can face the Barrens' greatest beasts. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters who have already faced the plainstriders and zhevras. Southwest of the Crossroads, savannah prowlers vanish into the central Barrens' gold and ochre scrub. These great cats hunt instead of grazing with the herds. They wait in tall grass, then ambush their prey, and unwary travelers can fall to them.

Psychometric Reading. Quintis Jonespyre, still wobbly after reading the knife, passes on visions of Raschal and the Woodpaw gnolls and asks you to take them to Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold. Quintis Jonespyre is still unsteady but has seen something useful. In the vision Raschal pulls two big leather backpacks off the boat, heads inland, and then goes back to the boat. Gnoll scalps appear, and Quintis thinks Raschal met Woodpaw gnolls. Raschal is very worried, almost terrified, and does not notice water elementals forming behind. There the images stop. Quintis must rest and asks you to tell Ginro, who needs to know.

Pure Hearts. Pure Hearts are ritual reagents provided to Forsaken warlocks by Carendin Halgar in the Undercity. They are used to lure and manifest a succubus across the Twisting Nether so the practitioner can defeat and bind the demon. Demonology relies on exploiting base desires and spiritual vulnerabilities. To summon a succubus into the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Carendin Halgar provides warlocks with Pure Hearts. When placed upon the summoning circle, these untainted spiritual essences act as potent bait, drawing the seductive demon across the Twisting Nether into the mortal realm. Once the demon manifests, the warlock must resist her enthralling mind-charms and strike her down in combat. Overcoming the succubus asserts mystical dominance, banishing her back to the Twisting Nether until Carendin teaches the warlock the spell to summon her forth at will.

Purgation Isle. Purgation Isle is a spiraling, rocky island lying off the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Crowned with a cemetery and a ruined scout tower, the desolate rock is cursed and swarming with the restless, condemned spirits of fallen humans and dwarves. Rising abruptly from the sea south of Hillsbrad, Purgation Isle is a grim sight marked by winding paths that lead past tombstones to an abandoned watchtower. No living nation claims it today. Instead, the isle is plagued by condemned souls—former paladins, priests, mages, and judges who wander among the graves, unable to find peace in death.

Purified Kor Gem. A Purified Kor Gem is a rare, consecrated crystal required by the weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell outside Ironforge. Once tainted by dark energies, it must be reclaimed from the depths of Kalimdor and cleansed by elven magic before it can be forged into a holy arm of the Light. The stone begins its journey as a Corrupted Kor Gem in the possession of the vile naga lurking within Blackfathom Deeps, deep beneath the coast of Ashenvale. To cleanse the stone of its aquatic, shadowy taint, a paladin must seek out the night elf Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Drawing upon arcane and natural arts, Thundris purges the corruption from the stone, transforming it into the radiant Purified Kor Gem. Only in this pristine state is it fit to serve as a conduit for holy power.

Putrid Claw. Putrid Claws are the decaying hands severed from mindless undead prowling the woods west of Brill. Deathguard Dillinger collects them as definitive proof that the encroaching Scourge threat near the old bridge is being held at bay. Even in their own homeland, the Forsaken are not entirely safe from the Lich King's reach. Pockets of mindless Scourge—rotting dead and ravaged corpses—regularly wander across the eastern borders into Tirisfal Glades, clustering along roads and near the old bridge west of Brill. To ensure the safety of travelers and garrison supply lines, the Deathguards place bounties on these wandering horrors. A severed putrid claw serves as unmistakable, physical evidence that one more shambling corpse has been put down for good.

Pyrewood Ambush. Pyrewood Ambush is a critical strike coordinated by the Deathstalkers inside the cursed town of Pyrewood Village. By assassinating the local human council, the Forsaken hope to break Archmage Arugal's grip on the cursed inhabitants and weaken his fortress looming above. Perched inside the town hall of Pyrewood Village, Deathstalker Faerleia lies in wait for the village leadership. While Archmage Arugal isolates himself within Shadowfang Keep tending to his dark sorceries, he relies on the local Pyrewood Council as figureheads to maintain order among the afflicted populace. Faerleia intends to wipe out this leadership cadre in a swift ambush, hoping that without the council's mediation, the feral worgen roaming the surrounding woods and village streets will break free from Arugal's dominion.

Pyrewood Shackle. Pyrewood Shackles are enchanted restraints worn by the beleaguered inhabitants of Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest. Imbued with the strange magic of Archmage Arugal, these mysterious bands seem to play a role in whatever dark fate grips the townsfolk when night falls over the settlement.

Pyrewood Village. Pyrewood Village is an isolated human settlement nestled in southern Silverpine Forest beneath Shadowfang Keep. Originally part of Gilneas before being stranded outside the Greymane Wall, its living residents harbor a horrific secret brought upon them by the mad archmage Arugal. Pyrewood was once a prosperous Gilnean settlement. When King Genn Greymane chose to isolate his kingdom behind the massive Greymane Wall following the Second War, Pyrewood was left on the northern side. Cut off from their homeland, the townsfolk were left entirely defenseless during the Third War as the Scourge marched across Lordaeron. Though they managed to survive the initial wave of the undead, their true nightmare began when the mage Arugal took refuge in the fortress above.

Quagmire. The Quagmire comprises the sprawling, treacherous heart of central Dustwallow Marsh. Bound by Brackenwall Village to the north and the Dragonmurk to the south, its waterlogged flats are notoriously difficult to navigate. Hostile beasts and ravenous oozes make any journey through this central fen perilous. Occupying the wide expanse between Lost Point in the west and Dustwallow Bay in the east, the Quagmire represents the wild core of the marsh. Footing is unreliable at best, with solid earth constantly giving way to murky water and clinging mud. Travelers must contend with predatory crocolisks lurking beneath the scum, aggressive spiders nesting in the dead brush, and strange oozes that seep through the muck.

Quartermaster Lewis. At Sentinel Hill in Westfall, Quartermaster Lewis keeps supplies moving to the People's Militia. He serves local defenders and travelers holding the frontier against the Defias Brotherhood. Quartermaster Lewis keeps the militia's supplies in Sentinel Tower. Stormwind's royal leaders offer little aid to impoverished Westfall, so Sentinel Hill depends on local volunteers and whatever provisions they can gather. Lewis hands out field necessities, including dry rations, fresh water, arrows, shot, and throwing blades. The fighters standing watch need these basics to endure Defias raids.

Quel'Lithien Lodge. Quel'Lithien Lodge is an isolated high elven hunting lodge nestled in the forested northern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands near the entrance to Quel'Thalas. Its Farstrider rangers hold out among the blighted woods, surrounded by the Scourge and hunted by Forsaken agents, while guarding old elven archives. Before the Third War, Quel'Lithien was a Farstrider camp on the road toward Quel'Thalas, and it housed elven records of the ranger order. The lodge fell on hard times after the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and into the elven kingdom. Today its rangers keep their vigil in the corrupted forest, one of only two major concentrations of high elves left in Lordaeron.

Quell The Uprising. Deep beneath the cobblestones of Stormwind, the high-security Stockade has fallen into total chaos. Following a coordinated breakout led by incarcerated members of the Defias Brotherhood, Warden Thelwater is urgently commissioning adventurers to cut down the rioting inmates and restore order before the capital learns how compromised the facility truly is. The Stockade was built to contain the most dangerous criminals, conspirators, and outlaws threatening the Kingdom of Stormwind. However, a sudden, violent uprising orchestrated by imprisoned Defias operatives has wrested control of the cell blocks directly from the guards. With the prison thoroughly overrun and corridors choked with armed felons, normal protocol has collapsed entirely. Rather than mounting a structured retaking, prison authorities are relying on visiting champions to fight their way through the riots.

Questioning Reethe. Ogron, whom Krog sent to track the human Reethe, has found him at last after a long search and says he hid well for a human. Ogron worries that so much time in the swamp may have driven Reethe mad, and asks you to come along to get answers from him. Afterward the way leads back to Krog at Brackenwall Village. After a long search, Ogron found Reethe, who by Ogron's reckoning hid well for a human. Ogron fears that so many days in the swamp may have left Reethe crazy, and wants you alongside to get answers from him. Afterward, Krog at Brackenwall Village awaits your return.

Quilboar. Quilboar are aggressive, boar-like humanoids native to central Kalimdor, renowned for their sharp spinal quills and relentless territorial savagery. Claiming descent from the fallen demigod Agamaggan, they dwell within dense mazes of razor-sharp brambles across Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens. Their fierce struggle over water, soil, and sacred ground makes them a constant threat to travelers and Horde settlements. Quilboar revere Agamaggan, the colossal boar Ancient who perished battling the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. According to their sacred traditions, the quilboar are his mortal offspring. Where Agamaggan bled and died across central Kalimdor, enormous thorny vines erupted from the scorched earth, forming sprawling root-mazes that the quilboar treat as holy ground. His crystallized blood endures across the Barrens as crimson Blood Shards, which their geomancers dig up and revere as powerful talismans.

Quinn Yorick. Quinn Yorick is a wounded Forsaken scout sheltering on the upper floor of a ruined farmhouse in the Ivar Patch. Having barely survived an encounter with the ghoul known as Ivar the Foul, he now relies on passing allies to help secure his survival. Tucked away inside an abandoned home at the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick lies gravely injured upstairs. His condition is the result of a vicious clash with Ivar the Foul, a ghoul lurking in the farm's barn in the northern stretches of Silverpine Forest. Sent with his sister Rane to scout Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec, Quinn cannot finish his mission or safely retreat alone, so he remains in hiding while travelers working for the Forsaken bring him healing and deal with the creature that nearly tore him apart.

Quinn's Potion. Quinn's Potion is a restorative draught concocted by Apothecary Renferrel in the Sepulcher. It is brewed to stabilize and revitalize the wounded Deathstalker Quinn Yorick following a disastrous scouting patrol in Silverpine Forest. After Deathstalker Quinn Yorick was severely battered and incapacitated near the Ivar Patch, word reached the Royal Apothecary Society at the Sepulcher. Apothecary Renferrel hastily compounded this specialized draught to facilitate Quinn's recovery. While Renferrel rarely lets minor field casualties distract him from his grander, more sinister research for Lady Sylvanas, he provided the restorative to get the injured scout back on his feet and capable of travel.

Raene Wolfrunner. Raene Wolfrunner is an accomplished Sentinel officer and hunter stationed at the heart of Astranaar in Ashenvale. Accompanied by her loyal wolf and saber cat companions, she coordinates defense efforts across the forest against encroaching Horde forces and corrupted furbolg tribes. She serves as a vital anchor for Alliance champions striving to protect the sacred wilderness. Raene Wolfrunner stands watchful in Astranaar alongside her trusty saber cat Korra and wolf Dagri. As an officer among the Sentinels, she oversees patrols throughout Ashenvale and coordinates intelligence reaching beyond its borders, dispatching scouts like Kaela Shadowspear into neighboring regions such as the Stonetalon Mountains.

Raene's Cleansing. This quest marks the tragic continuation of the search for Teronis, a night elf sentinel sent to Lake Falathim. Upon discovering his remains on the shore, the task shifts to recovering his research journal and retrieving the glowing gem held by local murlocs before reporting the grim news back to Astranaar. Sent to Lake Falathim by Raene Wolfrunner, adventurers discover Teronis dead along the waterside. Rather than a rescue, the mission turns into salvage and investigation. Among his belongings lies an intact journal detailing his assignment and findings regarding the strange disturbances in Ashenvale.

Raene's Cleansing. This intermediate step in the investigation of Ashenvale's corruption sends Alliance adventurers deep into the sacred groves east of Iris Lake. Entrusted with a recovered Glowing Gem, you must consult the dryad Shael'dryn to learn how to restore Dartol's ancient rod. Following the tragic death of the sentinel Teronis, Raene Wolfrunner examines the field notes he left behind. His research indicates that investigating Ashenvale's troubled furbolgs may require an ancient artifact: a rod crafted long ago by a night elf named Dartol. With only a Glowing Gem in hand, Raene admits her tactical expertise as a huntress is ill-suited to deciphering lost arcane and natural mysteries.

Raene's Cleansing. This quest represents a pivotal step in restoring Dartol's Rod of Transformation, an ancient night elf artifact being sought by Raene Wolfrunner. Guided by Shael'dryn at her moonwell, adventurers must venture north toward the foul border of Felwood to recover an iron shaft locked inside a hidden chest. The mission carries a tragic undertone, forcing the Alliance to confront corrupted ancients who guard the key. Following the clues to repair Dartol's Rod, Raene directs the search to Shael'dryn, a knowledgeable keeper watching over a tranquil moonwell deep in Ashenvale. Shael'dryn knows the whereabouts of the rod's iron shaft, yet retrieving it requires confronting the creeping taint threatening the northern woods. The piece lies locked in an old chest tucked away in a quiet glade near the border of Felwood.

Raene's Cleansing. This quest marks the search for the final component needed to restore Dartol's Rod, an ancient relic tied to cleansing Ashenvale. Shael'dryn directs travelers toward the fallen druid sanctuary of Dor'Danil to recover the missing iron pommel. The final piece of Dartol's Rod—an iron pommel—was entrusted to the night elf druids dwelling at the Dor'Danil barrow den. Tragically, the sanctuary fell to disaster, and its caretakers were slain. With the druids dead and their refuge overrun, the exact hiding place of the relic was lost, leaving scavengers and wandering oozes to swallow up whatever was left behind in the ruins east of the southern road.

Raene's Cleansing. This step in the cleansing of Ashenvale tasks you with taking the rebuilt Rod of Dartol to a secluded mountain shrine. Hidden among the ridges southeast of Shael'dryn's retreat, the sacred basin holds the latent magic needed to re-enchant the relic. After assembling the shattered pieces of Dartol's Rod, the dryad Shael'dryn directs travelers away from her moonwell into the untamed slopes to the southeast. The ancient shrines of Ashenvale were often deliberately nestled high in the mountain crags, far from the road and shielded by dense forest canopies. Reaching this quiet sanctum requires navigating unmarked terrain along the rock faces, climbing winding trails known mostly to Sentinels and woodland hermits.

Raene's Cleansing. This step in the long-running Ashenvale investigation sees Dartol's Rod of Transformation fully restored. Entrusted with the completed artifact by the dryad Shael'dryn, you return to Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar to report success and honor the memory of the fallen scout Teronis. After scouring the corrupted reaches of Ashenvale for components and ancient gem fragments, the relic known as Dartol's Rod of Transformation has finally been reforged. Entrusted to the dryad Shael'dryn near Iris Lake, its magical properties were cleansed and renewed. With the craftsmanship complete, she directs you back across the forest roads to Astranaar to present the artifact to Raene Wolfrunner.

Raene's Cleansing. This critical stage of Raene Wolfrunner's mission requires the use of Dartol's newly restored rod to disguise an outsider and initiate contact with an uncorrupted furbolg. Southeast of Mystral Lake, an outcast named Krolg offers a rare glimpse into the surviving furbolgs' deep resentment toward the night elves. With Dartol's Rod of Transformation restored, Raene Wolfrunner suspects the late night elf intended to disguise himself in order to safely approach the furbolgs. The woods of Ashenvale have grown perilous, and the madness spreading through the tribes makes direct diplomacy impossible. By harnessing the arcane relic, an adventurer takes on the appearance of a furbolg, hoping to slip past instinctive territorial rage and find someone willing to speak.

Raene's Cleansing. Disguised by Dartol's Rod of Transformation, adventurers gain the trust of Krolg, an uncorrupted furbolg near Lake Mystral. Disillusioned with both the arrogant night elves and the corruption rotting his own kin, Krolg asks for the death of the depraved chieftain Ran Bloodtooth so that the furbolgs can police their own. Near the waters of Lake Mystral, Krolg keeps a secluded vigil. Displaced and weary, he carries deep resentment toward the night elves, whose ancient hubris he blames for bringing ruin upon Kalimdor and stirring the dark rot festering in Ashenvale. To reach him, seekers use Dartol's Rod of Transformation to walk among furbolgs undetected. Yet despite his bitter hatred of the kaldorei, Krolg does not seek senseless butchery or innocent deaths.

Raene's Cleansing. This quest marks the final chapter in the search to uncover what befell Teronis and halt the furbolg threat looming over Ashenvale. Bearing Ran Bloodtooth's skull from Krolg, an adventurer returns to Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar to report the culmination of their perilous journey. Following the defeat of the fierce corrupted furbolg chieftain Ran Bloodtooth, Krolg sends the champion back to Astranaar. With Bloodtooth's severed skull in hand, you return as proof that the savage threat prowling the forest depths has been decisively struck down.

Raene's Cleansing. This task marks the completion of the Rod of Transformation at the hidden shrine in Ashenvale. With the sacred artifact assembled, it must be returned immediately to the dryad Shael'dryn at her moonwell sanctuary. The arduous effort to assemble the Rod of Transformation reaches a quiet turning point at the secluded shrine hidden deep within Ashenvale's wilds. Piecing together the shaft, pommel, and glowing gem, and re-enchanting the reconstructed rod at the hidden shrine has restored its magic. The artifact is ready to be returned to Shael'dryn for Raene's investigation of the furbolg attacks.

Raene's Cleansing. Raene's Cleansing begins when Raene Wolfrunner asks an adventurer to track down her missing friend, Teronis. Seeking a way to halt the rampant furbolg aggression across Ashenvale, Teronis set off toward Lake Falathim to recover a magic gemstone. Raene Wolfrunner serves alongside the Sentinels in Astranaar, defending Ashenvale against mounting threats. Among her closest companions was Teronis, who took it upon himself to find a potent defense against the increasingly violent furbolg tribes. When days passed without his return, Raene grew deeply worried, unable to abandon her post while fearing the worst.

text.enUS: Rage Scar Hold. Rage Scar Hold is a cavern carved into the wilderness of Feralas, situated on the mainland not far from Feathermoon Stronghold. It is notorious for housing some of the most vicious yetis in the region. Strangely, scattered books, symbols, and traces of night elven architecture deeper within suggest the den once served a far more civil purpose before the beasts claimed it. Carved into the rugged wilds of Feralas, Rage Scar Hold is dominated by savage yetis that attack anyone venturing near their lair. The creatures make the surrounding forest trails hazardous for both Alliance sentinels and passing travelers. While yetis are common to the untamed reaches of Kalimdor, the denizens of Rage Scar Hold stand out for their raw aggression and territorial ferocity.

Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm threatens the Horde from below. Its magma-lit tunnels hold savage troggs, and the Cleft of Shadow gives access to the caverns. Beneath Orgrimmar, dangers threaten the capital from below. While Thrall works to secure Durotar above, Ragefire troggs infest the chasm’s unstable vents and magma rivers. They rose from unknown depths and violently rejected Magatha Grimtotem’s attempts at diplomacy. Left unchecked, their numbers could undermine the city and overrun it.

Ragefire Chasm (Classic). Ragefire Chasm threatens Orgrimmar from beneath its streets, where troggs have broken into the tunnels. The fiery caverns also shelter a cult whose plans reach beyond Durotar. Ragefire troggs have surged into the volcanic tunnels beneath Orgrimmar. They pushed up from deep fissures and now threaten the city's foundations. Magatha Grimtotem, a tauren, tried to make peace with them, but the troggs answered with violence. Their tunnels run below the stone streets and fortified towers, leaving Orgrimmar at risk if the creatures keep digging upward.

Ragnar Thunderbrew. Ragnar Thunderbrew is a dwarven brewer and co-owner of the renowned Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Known across Dun Morogh for serving his family's signature Beer Basted Boar Ribs, he works constantly to keep the busy tavern stocked and its patrons satisfied. Standing inside the Thunderbrew Distillery at Kharanos, Ragnar Thunderbrew manages the establishment's culinary reputation alongside his family's brewing operations. The distillery is a central gathering place for local mountaineers, traveling adventurers, and gnome refugees fleeing Gnomeregan. Chief among his duties is preparing the family's renowned Beer Basted Boar Ribs, a hearty Dun Morogh specialty cooked with stout dwarven ale. However, maintaining steady supplies has become difficult; his usual meat provider enlisted in the King's Army, leaving Ragnar dependent on wandering mountaineers and hunters to keep fresh crag boar flanks coming into the kitchen.

Rahauro. Rahauro is a tauren attendant found on the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, faithfully serving the elder crone Magatha Grimtotem. Acting on her behalf, he recruits brave adventurers to venture into the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. He coordinates efforts to retaliate against the hostile troggs and recover missing possessions belonging to his mistress's fallen agents. Standing loyally near Magatha Grimtotem on the high terrace of Elder Rise, Rahauro acts as her direct intermediary. Magatha often operates through trusted underlings rather than soiling her own hooves with public recruitment. When reports emerge of wild creatures swarming beneath the orcish capital, it is Rahauro who handles the logistical details, dispatching Horde mercenaries to deal with the uprising.

text.enUS: Raid on the Kolkar. After Strange Alliance, Uthek the Wise sends you against the Kolkar centaurs to the northeast. Kill them, take their charms, and bring ten of those charms back to Uthek. Uthek scoffs at the Kolkar centaurs for thinking their magic strong; in Uthek's view they know nothing of magic. You go northeast to the Kolkar, kill them, and take their charms. Uthek wants ten Crude Charms to throw in the fire, laughing as they burn.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands where Tor'gan seeks to lift the spirits of a despondent orc named Gor'mul. When tales of Orgrimmar and Warchief Thrall fail, Tor'gan turns to newly rediscovered shamanic traditions to craft a revitalizing amulet from highland raptor eyes. At the remote outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, the orcs face enemies from without and quiet battles within. One of their own, Gor'mul, has fallen into a deep, unshakable melancholy. His companions attempted to rally him with proud tales of Kalimdor, the mighty fortress city of Orgrimmar, and the visionary leadership of young Warchief Thrall. Yet none of these grand victories or distant wonders could pierce Gor'mul's gloom or give him reason to hope.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest aimed at rekindling the fighting will of Gor'mul, a broken warrior consumed by despair. An emissary delivers a Raptor Talon Amulet in hopes of awakening the fierce spirit he once possessed. However, Gor'mul remains bitter, questioning whether any simple trinket could ever mend his sorrow or restore glory to the Horde. Raising Spirits involves delivering a Raptor Talon Amulet to an orc named Gor'mul. His allies hope that the wild strength and ferocity of raptors, channeled through the talisman, will reawaken the warrior's flame that once burned fiercely within his veins.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest that addresses the lingering emotional trauma of an old orc veteran. Through the guidance of Tor'gan, a shaman attempts to reach the embittered Gor'mul using ancestral magic to restore his lost pride and will to live. In the wake of past wars, many orcish veterans struggle with the burdens of survival and perceived dishonor. Gor'mul is one such warrior, languishing in bitter despondency because he was denied what he considers an honorable death alongside his fallen Warchief. Tor'gan, an empathetic shaman, seeks to alleviate Gor'mul's suffering by reminding him of his people's spiritual strength. Believing that ancestral energies can heal emotional wounds, Tor'gan prepares an enchanted amulet intended to rekindle the old fighter's pride.

Raleigh Andrean. Raleigh Andrean is a Forsaken resident of the Undercity. His requests reveal a callous attitude toward his former human life and those he once knew. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Raleigh Andrean lived an ordinary human life, married to a woman named Deliah and keeping company with his friend Valdred Moray. Like countless others, he fell when the Scourge tore through the kingdom, only to be raised as a mindless thrall in service to the Lich King. He regained his free will following the shattering of the Ner'zhul's grip and Sylvanas Windrunner's uprising, taking his place among the Forsaken in the Undercity.

Raleigh and the Undercity. This quest bridges an investigation from Brill to the Undercity, tasking an adventurer with delivering a recovered heirloom ring to a widower named Raleigh. Found on a woman's stolen corpse bound for Fenris Isle, the jewelry points to a tragedy among Lordaeron's former inhabitants. Delivering it sets into motion a dark pursuit of vengeance. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren pieced together clues surrounding a stolen corpse and an engraved ring that once belonged to a woman named Deliah. Hoping to confirm its origin and see it returned to her family, Sevren directed the finder deep into the subterranean halls of the Undercity to seek Deliah's surviving husband, Raleigh.

Ran Bloodtooth's Skull. Ran Bloodtooth's Skull is a grisly trophy taken from the chieftain of the corrupted furbolgs in Ashenvale. Brought back to the night elves of Astranaar, it serves as tangible proof that a ferocious threat to the woodland realm has been ended. The forests of Ashenvale have suffered immensely from demonic taint and wilderness corruption, driving once-peaceful furbolg tribes into murderous madness. Among the fiercest of these hostile chieftains was Ran Bloodtooth. Recovering his skull provides the night elf Sentinels with definite proof that the brute has fallen, breaking his hold over the local furbolgs and offering a small measure of respite to the beleaguered town of Astranaar.

Randis. In Cathedral Square, Randis waits for a chance to see the world beyond Stormwind. During Children's Week, he eagerly joins willing adventurers across Alliance lands. Randis lives in the orphanage near Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, one of many children left without family by the realm's conflicts. When Children's Week comes each year, Orphan Matron Nightingale gives sympathetic heroes a whistle and entrusts them with his care. Curious and full of questions, Randis dreams of adventure, asks riddles, and declares that he wants to be king of Stormwind when he grows up.

Rane Yorick. Deathstalker Rane Yorick is an operative of the Forsaken intelligence guild stationed deep in Silverpine Forest. Together with her brother Quinn, she was sent to scout the farms of northern Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. The Deathstalkers serve as Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's eyes, ears, and blades across Lordaeron. Operating out of shadows and hidden posts, agents like Rane Yorick monitor the wilderness for threats that could disrupt Forsaken dominion. When sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest, Rane and her brother Quinn found themselves hemmed in by surrounding feral dangers, turning an undercover reconnaissance mission into a battle for survival.

Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea. Near Auberdine's watch, Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea directs the defense of Darkshore. The seasoned night elf sentry sends travelers to meet threats and investigate strange signs along the coast. From Auberdine, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea coordinates scouts as corruption grows and hostile forces press into Darkshore. She watches the wilderness around town and relies on capable travelers to guard the perimeter and protect night elf holdings along the coast.

Raptor Grounds. In the southern Barrens, Sunscale raptors claim a secluded valley in the rocky hills west of Northwatch Hold. Their eerie, tool-using cunning and obsessive theft of bright trinkets set them apart from ordinary beasts. West of Northwatch Hold, Sunscale raptors make their home in the Raptor Grounds. Eerie and far from ordinary beasts, they fashion crude shelters, make primitive tools, and coordinate their hunts. Their obsessive fascination with shiny or unusual things drives them to raid passing caravans and Horde encampments. Coins, trinkets, and supplies disappear into their canyon dens.

Raptor Head. Across the Barrens, Raptor Head trophies answer a bounty from Gazrog at the Crossroads. The guard payroll vanished from a watchtower, and a wild raptor was caught in the theft. A stolen chest of guard payroll has left the Crossroads watchtower without its silver. The defenders caught a wild raptor red-handed, to their disbelief. Gazrog has put a bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the Barrens. Bring their severed heads to the outpost, and the predators will be culled before they can pilfer more Horde supplies.

Raptor Horns. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix wants intact raptor horns for a scheme of his own. The goblin believes the cunning of Barrens raptors lies in their horns and hires travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws. Mebok Mizzyrix looks for fortune in Ratchet, where goblins chase one scheme after another. He has watched the Barrens raptors act with unusual craft and coordination compared with beasts elsewhere. Mebok decided their intelligence must be held in their horns. He has no formal inquiry in mind; he wants to put this idea to profit.

Raptor Mastery. At his expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges travelers to prove their prowess in the wilderness. The famed hunter demands ten Stranglethorn Raptors slain to test whether you possess genuine hunting talent. Following your arrival in the jungle after Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary offers to test your tracking and hunting capabilities. Rather than handing out maps or directions, he insists that finding the Stranglethorn Raptors yourself is half the test, challenging you to venture out into the brush and bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

Raptor Mastery. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges hunters to step up their game against more dangerous quarry. Following an earlier raptor hunt, he directs adventurers to pursue and bring down ten Lashtail Raptors. After proving an initial measure of hunting prowess, Hemet Nesingwary expects more than idly passing time by the camp's fire. To prove true focus and skill, hunters are dispatched into the dense jungle brush just north of Grom'gol Base Camp to track down and slay ten fierce Lashtail Raptors.

Raptor Mastery. Hemet Nesingwary raises the stakes of his hunting expedition by sending you after a elusive breed known as Jungle Stalkers. Tracking down ten of these cunning raptors will prove your mettle as a true stalker of wild beasts in Stranglethorn Vale. Having tested your aim against lesser raptors, Hemet Nesingwary presents a more demanding quarry. Jungle Stalkers are notably cagey and far more difficult to track and slay than the breeds hunted previously. Hemet expects you to venture out into the jungle, fell ten of these wary predators, and return to camp to earn a lead on his finest hunt yet.

name.itIT: La maestria nella caccia al raptor

text.enUS: Raptor Mastery. Deep in Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges seasoned trackers to bring down an elusive predator that has escaped even him. Having proven your mettle against lesser beasts, you are tasked with tracking the cunning raptor known as Tethis and securing its talon. Following your earlier trials in the jungle, Hemet Nesingwary reveals the existence of a particularly vicious raptor named Tethis. While lesser hunters have chased prey across the foliage, Tethis has evaded capture entirely, defying even the expedition leader himself. Ajeck Rouack bestowed the beast with its moniker, marking it as the ultimate prize among Stranglethorn's scaled horrors.

Raptor Ridge. Raptor Ridge is an elevated, rugged expanse in the eastern Wetlands, sitting northwest of the fortified Dragonmaw Gates. It serves as the primary hunting and nesting grounds for packs of ferocious Razormaw raptors, overseen by a particularly vicious matriarch deep within its caverns. Rising above the sodden marshes of the eastern Wetlands, Raptor Ridge is among the most perilous wilderness areas in the region. Vicious Razormaw raptors prowl its crags and rocky trails in large packs, making travel near the foothills of Khaz Modan hazardous for wanderers. At the heart of the ridge lies a brooding cavern dominated by the Razormaw Matriarch, whose aggressive brood aggressively defends their nests against any encroaching predators or foolish travelers wandering too close to the Dragonmaw Gates.

Raptor Thieves. A raptor has stolen the guards' payroll from the Crossroads tower, leaving the defenders baffled. Gazrog calls for a cull to keep the beasts from striking again. The Crossroads depends on mercenary and grunt guards to keep trade routes open across the Barrens. Their pay matters to morale and discipline. When silver vanished from the guard tower, leaders expected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, a raptor was caught stealing in the dead of night, leaving the settlement stunned and short of coin.

Rare Books. Rare Books is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley focused on recovering two stolen magical primers for Brother Paxton. Kobolds have hauled the missing texts into the Jasperlode Mine, where they appear to be studying elementary magic and summoning rituals. Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey faces a crisis in his library: several volumes have been carried off by vermin infesting the valley. Only two books remain missing from his catalog: 'Geomancy for Curious Young Wizards' and 'Arcane Explainer: Magical Stuff in Simple Words'. These educational primers were carted away into the depths of the Jasperlode Mine by the occupying kobolds.

Rare Earth. At Dolanaar, Rare Earth waits for delivery to Denalan's camp near Lake Al'Ameth. The mineral-rich soil came from Darnassus for his botanical experiments on Teldrassil. Rare Earth is late reaching Dolanaar from Darnassus. Denalan, an eccentric botanist on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, requested the parcel to study plants in Teldrassil's young ecosystem. Herbalist Syral Bladeleaf now entrusts the soil to travelers heading south, hoping it reaches Denalan before its potency fades.

Rascally Rodents. Rascally Rodents is a quest in Northshire Valley where Brother Paxton tasks adventurers with recovering stolen books from the local kobolds. Though Paxton initially fears the vermin are devouring his library, retrieving the texts reveals an unsettling mystery behind the creatures' motives. Brother Paxton in Northshire Valley is in distress over the local kobold infestation, which has spilled over from the surrounding hills and mines into the sacred grounds. Convinced that the ravenous creatures have begun devouring the texts from his collection, he enlists the aid of young adventurers to hunt down the vermin and salvage whatever volumes remain before the entire library is lost.

Ratchet. Ships crowd Ratchet's docks on the eastern coast of the Barrens. The Steamwheedle Cartel runs this neutral port, linking central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms by sea. Ratchet gives shelter to anyone who can pay, on the dry coast between Durotar and Dustwallow Marsh. After the Third War, chief engineer Gazlowe founded the port, drawing smugglers, exiles, and daring traders to Kalimdor's frontier. The Steamwheedle Cartel runs the town, which keeps strict neutrality between the Horde and the Alliance. Ships such as The Maiden's Fancy cross the Great Sea to Booty Bay with goods, mercenaries, and raw materials. Ratchet Bruisers watch the docks and beat anyone who starts a fight and disrupts trade.

Rattlecage Skull. Rattlecage Skulls are the shattered remnants of mindless undead roaming the ruined outskirts of Deathknell. Novice Forsaken warlocks must gather these calcified trophies for Venya Marthand to demonstrate their emerging will and qualify for the dark arts of summoning. Within the sunless bounds of Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken with an affinity for dark magic are guided by Venya Marthand. To prove that a fledgling practitioner has the fortitude to bend extraplanar creatures to their command, Venya tasks them with subduing the lingering Rattlecage Skeletons near the ruined smithy. Striking down these lesser undead and retrieving their severed skulls serves as both a practical test of discipline and a ritual foundation before learning to breach the void and enslave a first demonic minion.

Rattling the Rattlecages. Rattling the Rattlecages is an early trial assigned by Shadow Priest Sarvis to newly awakened Forsaken in Deathknell. Tasked with destroying twelve Rattlecage Skeletons, fresh undead prove their resilience against the Scourge and demonstrate that they possess the willpower to defend their newly won freedom. Having culled the mindless zombies stumbling through Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken are immediately pushed into a harsher trial. Shadow Priest Sarvis directs recruits to confront the Rattlecage Skeletons roaming the outskirts of the settlement. These animated bones lack any trace of sapience or self-control, yet they hit harder and fight with greater ferocity than the decaying corpses nearby. Surviving their clattering ambushes demonstrates that a new recruit will not falter when placed under immediate pressure.

Rau Cliffrunner. Rau Cliffrunner is a tauren scout and scholar stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to protecting his people from regional threats, he studies the history and origins of the hostile Galak centaur through their ancient relics. Working closely with allies in Thunder Bluff, Rau coordinates ventures into dangerous enemy strongholds across the canyon. Perched on the perilous bluffs of Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner maintains a watchful eye over the sweeping, sun-scorched expanse of Thousand Needles. The tauren outpost serves as a crucial Horde sanctuary in an otherwise hostile territory teeming with ferocious predators, quilboar, and aggressive centaur clans. Rau acts as both an outpost organizer and a dedicated investigator, keen on neutralizing emerging threats before they can overwhelm the vulnerable mesa settlements.

Ravaged Caravan. The Ravaged Caravan is a smoldering wreck located on the northeastern shore of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Once a supply convoy bound for Supervisor Fizsprocket's mining operations, it was ambushed and destroyed by local tauren determined to halt goblin exploitation of their homeland. Perched on a rise above Stonebull Lake, the Ravaged Caravan marks an early clash between the tauren of Bloodhoof Village and the encroaching Venture Company. Sent to deliver mining supplies, blueprints, and equipment to Supervisor Fizsprocket's dig site, the caravan was cut off and wrecked by tauren defenders before it could reach its destination. Despite the devastation, stubborn Venture Co. survivors still cling to the ruined wagons and smoldering crates, jealously guarding what little cargo remains.

Ravaged Twilight Camp. Tucked away in the secluded Crystal Vale of northwestern Silithus, the Ravaged Twilight Camp sits ruined among towering mineral formations. It serves as an isolated redoubt for the eccentric hermit Highlord Demitrian, a devotee of the Windseeker. While the Twilight's Hammer maintains numerous active outposts across the sands of Silithus, this broken encampment in the Crystal Vale tells a different story. Nestled far from the primary cult fortresses, the camp lies largely ruined and deserted, save for Highlord Demitrian. A servant of Thunderaan, Demitrian lingers amidst the stones, seemingly abandoned by or detached from the wider Twilight hierarchy while brooding over elemental bindings and the lost power of the Windseeker.

name.frFR: Talisman de la griffe du corbeau

text.enUS: Raven Claw Talisman. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Raven Claw Talisman is kept among relics needed to awaken sleeping druids. The sacred night elf relic is one of four Relics of Wakening used to guide the Druids of the Talon safely back from the Emerald Dream. The Raven Claw Talisman rests in a designated chest inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den, where Teldrassil's Druids of the Talon entered deep meditative sleep. Their hibernation is a delicate spiritual threshold. Without the proper ceremonial focus, a druid whose link to the waking world is broken may remain stranded in the Emerald Dream. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs this talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting to perform the awakening ritual and bring the sleepers back safely.

Raven Hill. Reports of shifting shadows and flickering window light in the abandoned settlement of Raven Hill have set the Night Watch on edge. Dispatched by Elaine Carevin in Darkshire, travelers are sent west across the haunted woods to confront whatever sinister presence has taken shelter among the ruins. To the rangers of the Night Watch, the far western edge of Duskwood has long been surrendered to the dead and the wilderness. Yet complete abandonment would be preferable to unexpected activity. Calor, a watcher patrolling the gloomy roads, noticed movement among the silent houses of Raven Hill two nights in a row, punctuated by the unsettling flicker of a lantern in a window. In a land plagued by ghouls, skeletons, and beasts, any unexplained signs of life demand immediate investigation.

Raven Hill. Raven Hill is a desolate, ruined village in western Duskwood sitting in the long shadow of the vast Raven Hill Cemetery. Once a lively human settlement, it lies abandoned by all but a handful of frightened squatters and invisible spirits. Situated along the western thoroughfare of Duskwood just north of Addle's Stead, Raven Hill is a tragic shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living evacuated eastward toward Darkshire or fled the territory entirely. Today, ruined timber homes rot beneath perpetual gloom, avoided by travelers who fear both the restless dead wandering down from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen lurking between the crumbling walls.

Raven Hill Cemetery. Raven Hill Cemetery is a vast, cursed graveyard stretching across the western reaches of Duskwood. Once a peaceful burial ground for local hamlets, the cemetery has been overrun by hordes of walking dead, scavenger spiders, and ruthless grave robbers. Before the darkness engulfed the Dawning Wood, Raven Hill Cemetery served as the primary resting place for the surrounding settlements. As dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead failed to remain in their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors clawed their way out of the soil, swelling the graveyard's grim boundaries. Today, it stands as one of the most perilous blights in Duskwood. The cemetery is prowled not only by rotting abominations and giant spiders, but also by desperate grave robbers eager to plunder ancestral crypts unhindered by local authorities.

Ravencrest Monument. Perched upon the windswept cliffs of southern Azshara, the Ravencrest Monument marks the shattered remnant of an ancient night elven colossus. Once a towering tribute overlooking the Great Sea, the statue has long since broken apart, leaving only towering legs and scattered stone ruins now stalked by hostile Spitelash naga. Standing high above the ocean southeast of the Ruins of Eldarath, the Ravencrest Monument was once an awe-inspiring marvel of Kaldorei stonework. Today, little remains of the majestic colossus beyond its pair of gigantic broken legs rooted to the stone plinth, with the shattered fragments of its torso and head either buried in the cliffside dirt or lost beneath the waves below. Reaching this remote coastal promontory requires trekking across the mainland bridges of Azshara, as sheer, rocky drops prevent any approach from the sea.

Ravenholdt. Ravenholdt, also known as the Assassin's League, is an elite guild of rogues, thieves, and killers based out of a secluded mountain manor above the Hillsbrad Foothills. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the league maintains strict neutrality from faction politics while waging an unending shadow war against their bitter rivals, the Syndicate. They test and recruit only the most cunning operatives across Azeroth, valuing peerless discipline, stealth, and lethal efficiency above all else. Tucked away in the craggy mountains connecting Hillsbrad to Alterac, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the nerve center for Azeroth's premier brotherhood of assassins. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the organization operates far beyond the jurisdiction of kings and warchiefs. Within its walls, master specialists hone every lethal art: Master Kang instructs disciples in close combat and assassination, the Thunderwood brothers brew rare and deadly poisons, and gnome craftsmen engineer intricate locks to test fledglings. To non-rogues, entering the estate is an overt flirtation with death, where an unwary step easily ends with a poisoned dagger in the ribs.

Ravenholdt Manor. Tucked away high in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the secluded headquarters for the guild of thieves and assassins known as Ravenholdt. Overseen by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the estate provides a discreet haven where practitioners of stealth hone their craft far from the eyes of authorities. Hidden behind a narrow mountain pass and a winding cave northwest of Durnholde Keep, Ravenholdt Manor sits isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains. The property belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, a nobleman who maintains a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. The grounds feature a tranquil garden and an outdoor training arena overseen by martial experts like Master Kang, providing a disciplined space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat. While the manor welcomes those with a talent for skullduggery, clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors are treated with cold suspicion by the manor's watchful sentries.

Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat is an ancient night elf outpost perched around a massive great tree in north-central Ashenvale. Guarded by dryads and Cenarion protectors, it serves as a watchful sanctuary monitoring the northern passes toward corrupted Felwood. It is also the sanctuary of Keeper Ordanus, an elder son of Cenarius targeted by sinister outside forces. Nestled between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run, the outpost is fiercely guarded by Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters. Their collective vigilance keeps a wary eye on the encroaching taint descending from Felwood just to the north.

Razor Hill. Razor Hill links the Valley of Trials, the Barrens, and Orgrimmar at a crossroads in central Durotar. Its fortified barracks train young orc and troll warriors for life in the wilderness. Razor Hill joins northern Durotar to the southern coast and the Barrens across the Southfury River. Stone-and-timber barracks and orcish burrows fill the settlement, founded early in Durotar's settlement. After the Third War, human forces from Kul Tiras lured the Horde here with a false offer of an emissary summit. Rexxar went in Thrall's stead and stopped their ambush. Razor Hill now stands fortified against further attacks from the coast.

name.ptBR: Torre de Vigia do Monte Navalha

text.enUS: Razor Hill Watchtower. Furl Scornbrow watches Durotar from the Razor Hill Watchtower. From its red stone bluffs, he keeps an eye on the plains and coast, guarding the settlement below. The Razor Hill Watchtower rises above Razor Hill and the canyons around it. Thick timber and iron framing hold the outpost together. Durotar faces threats from Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders across the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists in nearby crags. From the ridgeline, a lookout can spot warbands, smoke signals, and incursions before they reach the settlement gates.

Razorfen. Razorfen is the collective name associated with the predominant quilboar tribe of southern Kalimdor and their sprawling thorn-choked settlements. Carved into massive briars along the southern border of the Barrens and the edge of Thousand Needles, Razorfen encompasses the strongholds of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs. It serves as both the spiritual heart and the central bastion of quilboar power. According to legend, the colossal thorned brambles that make up the Razorfen sprouted ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. When the giant boar Ancient, Agamaggan, fell in battle against the Burning Legion, his blood seeped into the earth wherever he bled and died. From that divine sacrifice grew massive vines of petrified bramble and iron-hard thorns, creating a natural fortress where his descendants, the quilboar, have dwelled ever since.

Razorfen Downs. Razorfen Downs is the ancestral capital and sacred burial labyrinth of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal brambles bordering the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Once their holiest sanctuary, it has fallen under the sway of the undead Scourge, transforming into a festering bastion of necromancy. Long revered as the ancestral capital city and burial grounds of the quilboar race, Razorfen Downs rests within the colossal petrified briars sprung from the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Legend holds that its arched entryway was carved directly from the Great Boar's very maw. For centuries, the high priests of the Death's Head tribe tended these deep, winding burrows and honored their revered dead. Yet despite its sacred standing among the boar-folk, the maze of bone and bramble has recently suffered a catastrophe far darker than any squabble over Barrens water.

Razorfen Downs (Classic). Deep in the southern Barrens, the Scourge now holds Razorfen Downs, the quilboar's ancestral burial ground and capital. Led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer, its agents have raised the quilboar dead and threaten to spread their power across central Kalimdor. Razorfen Downs shares the towering, petrified vines of nearby Razorfen Kraul. It lies where the boar demigod Agamaggan fell in the War of the Ancients. For generations, this thorn labyrinth was the quilboar's sacred burial ground and seat of power, guarded by mystics of the Death's Head tribe. The quilboar hold its dense briars holy, for they were soaked in their divine progenitor's blood.

Razorfen Kraul (Classic). Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral heartland of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal thorns that sprang from the blood of the fallen boar demigod Agamaggan. Ruled by the ruthless crone Charlga Razorflank, this fortified labyrinth serves as a staging ground for bloody raids across the southern Barrens. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the colossal boar demigod Agamaggan perished battling the Burning Legion to save Azeroth. Wherever his sacred blood seeped into the soil of southern Kalimdor, massive, impenetrable thorn vines erupted from the earth. The quilboar, believing themselves the mortal progeny of the Great Boar, gathered within these dense briars to dwell and venerate his sacrifice. The dense mass known as Razorfen Kraul stands as their most revered redoubt, thick with quilboar warriors, beast trainers, and earth-shaping shamans.

Razorflank's Medallion. Razorflank's Medallion is a personal token carried by Charlga Razorflank, the crone ruling over Razorfen Kraul. Recovered from the heart of the quilboar stronghold, it serves as undeniable proof that the matriarch has been brought down. Carried by Charlga Razorflank herself, this medallion represents the authority of the crone who leads the Razorfen quilboar. When Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar learns of the fates of fallen explorers like Heralath and the dwarf Lonebrow, he tasks Alliance adventurers with striking directly at the quilboar leader. Presenting the crone's medallion confirms her death, reassuring the night elf sentinels guarding the borders of Feralas that the gathered forces within the Kraul have lost their leader.

Razorhide. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Razorhide to those who bring him blood shards. The captive quilboar trades Agamaggan’s life essence for a blessing that hardens the skin before battle. The quilboar trace their power to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who died fighting the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood sank into the Barrens and hardened into crystalline shards, still alive with ancient power. The Horde and quilboar remain sworn enemies, yet Mangletooth, held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, will share sacred knowledge for these fragments.

Razormane Grounds. Razormane quilboar push east from the Barrens into central Durotar. Their thorn-choked camp marks the front of their unending clash with Orgrimmar's orcs. At the Southfury River, the Razormane Grounds threaten travelers beneath central Durotar's red cliffs. The camp marks the furthest east the quilboar have spread from the Barrens. Captain Flat Tusk of the Battleguard and Geolord Mottle lead raids on nearby orc settlements and passing supply lines. Patrols set out from Razor Hill and nearby outposts, but the Razormane keep replenishing their ranks among the briars faster than the Horde can clear them.

Razorwind Canyon. Dustwind harpies threaten travelers on Razorwind Canyon’s road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. The rocky gulch cuts through Durotar, and the harpies make the route north toward the Horde capital dangerous. Razorwind Canyon runs beside the main road from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Its gullies reach into the eastern bluffs and west toward Tor'kren Farm. Dustwind harpies nest among the rocks and attack travelers who stray too close to their roosts. With the canyon so near the capital’s trade route, Durotar’s defenders must keep watch over its gullies.

Razzeric's Tweaking. On the Shimmering Flats, Razzeric adds personal modifications to racers once Pozzik has finished with them. A seaforium booster ordered from Shreev in Gadgetzan was on a zeppelin that Razzeric hears crashed in Dustwallow Marsh, and Razzeric wants it brought back. Razzeric grants that Pozzik is a great mechanic, but thinks Pozzik too wary of loading on firepower and hanging on for the ride. Once Pozzik is done with a racer, Razzeric spends time making personal changes: loosening the controls, removing frame sections and piling on power. A seaforium booster was ordered from Shreev at the Gizmorium in Gadgetzan, but the zeppelin carrying it crashed in Dustwallow Marsh, by Razzeric's account. The booster is needed back on the Shimmering Flats, since showing up at the track without that extra kick would be a travesty.

Razzle Sprysprocket. Razzle Sprysprocket is a gnomish engineer residing in Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Known for his technical tinkering alongside Ozzie Togglevolt, he enlists travelers to help salvage disrupted gnomish machinery and components around the snowy hills. Following the tragedy at Gnomeregan, Razzle Sprysprocket found refuge among the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, setting up his workshop in Kharanos. With a knack for delicate mechanical parts, Razzle works alongside fellow engineer Ozzie Togglevolt. Their efforts frequently involve recovering gyro-mechanisms and cog assemblies that were lost or scavenged during the flight from their irradiated homeland.

Reading the Ley Lines. Reading the Ley Lines is a rite of passage for young Skyborne discovering their Highborne magical heritage. Entrusted by Falorne Fallwind on Zephras Isle, novitiates travel to the standing stones in Thendal Grove to sense and draw upon the raw arcane currents surging through the elemental terrain. Even within the windswept confines of the elemental plane, latent arcane conduits run beneath the earth. While strange elementals and the hostile Al'Aketh drift across Zephras Isle, subterranean ley lines have begun pushing toward the surface. To practitioners of magic, these ruptures provide direct access to untamed arcane reservoirs, offering strength to any who possess the bloodline and knowledge necessary to channel them.

Reagent Pouch (shaman). Burning Blade cultists in Durotar carry reagents for a shaman's first fire sapta. Telf Joolam uses them with fire tar from Razormane quilboar to make the draught that lets a young shaman see the realm of fire. Burning Blade cultists carry reagents for a young shaman's first fire sapta. The hermit Telf Joolam uses the powders and oils in their pouches with fire tar from Razormane quilboar. Together, these components make a draught that grants sight into the realm of fire and attunes the shaman to the spirits of flame.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor is gathering reagents for the gnome mage Leftwitch, who lives in Kharanos, and the Reclaimers are short-handed. He wants claws and horns from the Hatefury satyrs to the east before the rest of the list can begin. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor has another job on his hands: fetching reagents for Leftwitch, the gnome mage who lives in Kharanos. Roetten reckons it is easy coin, since the Reclaimers are already out in Desolace, and Kreldig says he does not care that the crew is short-handed.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Next on Leftwitch's list for Kreldig Ungor is venom from the scorpashi and hides from aged kodo. Kreldig cannot say where to find either, since he does not know Desolace well. Following the first part of Leftwitch's list, Kreldig Ungor turns to the next items. They look simple enough, but the instructions are exact. The mage wants venom from the scorpashi, any of them will do, and hides from kodo, but only aged kodo. Dying and ancient kodo are no use. Kreldig wants seven vials of venom and three hides. Mages, Kreldig muses, ask for some odd things.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor has the last of the items Leftwitch wants, and he admits it is not pretty and will take longer than the others. All of it comes from demons: brains, wings and vials of blood. Kreldig warns that the final set is a grim business, slower to gather than any before it. Leftwitch wants three kinds of parts, ten of each. The brains come from felhounds: mana eaters, mage hunters or ley hunters. The wings come from the nether maidens, sisters or sorceresses. The blood comes from doomwarder captains or lords. Kreldig says he would understand if you passed on this one.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor gives you Leftwitch's package and sends you back to Ironforge. Roetten Stonehammer is the one to see about your pay, and Kreldig promises a kind word about you once back home. Kreldig says your pay waits in Ironforge with Roetten Stonehammer himself. Roetten will be glad to be rid of Leftwitch's package, and handing it over should be enough to get what you are owed. Kreldig expects to be in Desolace only a little longer, and still means to speak well of you once home.

Rear Guard Patrol. Rear Guard Patrol is a military scouting mission tasked by Deathguard Linnea to protect the Forsaken defenses along Tirisfal's eastern border. It directs operatives to purge stray Scourge horrors and lingering spirits haunting the Balnir Farmstead before they can compromise the supply lines supporting the Bulwark. The Bulwark stands as the primary bulwark holding back the pestilence and armies of the Western Plaguelands from spilling into Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Linnea oversees rear-echelon security along this frontier. Because the line cannot afford to divide its forces against ambushes from behind, any undead that bypass the choke point must be destroyed before they can sever the supply lines feeding the front.

Rear Guard Patrol. Rear Guard Patrol is a critical defense assignment given by Deathguard Linnea in Tirisfal Glades. Rather than fighting off mere wandering ghouls, patrollers are tasked with hunting down Riptear, an abomination roaming near Venomweb Vale that should never have made it past the Bulwark. The Bulwark stands as the sole fortified barrier separating Tirisfal Glades from the horrors of the Western Plaguelands. The strategy of the Forsaken military hinges upon a strictly one-front war. If mindless undead slip behind the lines, the supply routes feeding the front can be strangled in an instant. While stray spirits or ghouls occasionally bypass the barricades, reports of an abomination roaming the glades signal a severe failure of containment.

Reassignment. Reassignment is the culmination of Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's campaign to escape his posting in Southshore. Having compiled an exaggerated report of his deeds against the coastal naga, Farren dispatches an adventurer all the way to Stormwind Keep to deliver the documents to his former mentor, Major Samuelson. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle has made no secret of his disdain for his station in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tucked away in Southshore, far from the comforts of the capital and under the stern watch of Marshal Redpath, Farren has spent his days scheming for a transfer back south. By taking credit for clearing out the nearby Daggerspine naga, he hopes to present himself as an indispensable, battle-hardened officer ripe for promotion.

Rebel Camp. Tucked just off the road in northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Rebel Camp serves as a fortified refuge for Alliance soldiers who broke away from Colonel Kurzen. Led by Lieutenant Doren, these troops refused to surrender to the madness gripping their commander's expedition and now fight to survive and undo his descent into tyranny. When Colonel Kurzen's expedition pushed deep into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale on behalf of Stormwind, things rapidly fell apart. Afflicted by the dark jungle magic and the curse of the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, the Colonel and his core loyalists succumbed to madness, turning rogue and terrorizing the wilds. A handful of sound-minded soldiers led by Lieutenant Doren refused to participate in the atrocities. Breaking away from Kurzen's Compound, they established this hidden camp in the north to stage a desperate guerrilla campaign against their former comrades.

Reception from Tyrande. Reception from Tyrande is an Alliance quest that sends adventurers from the embattled slopes of the Stonetalon Mountains directly to the night elf capital of Darnassus. After aiding the Sentinels in securing their precarious foothold in Stonetalon against the Venture Company, you are sent by Sentinel Thenysil in Astranaar to receive formal recognition from High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind herself in the Temple of the Moon. The night elven outposts scattered throughout the Stonetalon Mountains face intense pressure, particularly from the Venture Company ravaging the land. Sentinel Thenysil coordinates efforts from Astranaar, but sustaining these remote bases requires immense resilience. Securing supply lines and intelligence is vital to maintaining an Alliance presence in Kalimdor's interior, making outside aid profoundly impactful to the Sentinels stationed there.

Recipe of the Kaldorei. Zarrin teaches a lesson in balance through the Recipe of the Kaldorei. In Dolanaar, young cooks learn to gather only what they need from Teldrassil's woods. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and teaches young adventurers the traditions of his people. The night elves once called themselves the kaldorei, or children of the stars. Zarrin begins their understanding of that heritage with the bond between a hunter, their food, and Teldrassil's boughs, rather than the battlefield.

name.deDE: Die Geschäfte der Wiederholer in Desolace
name.esES: Los negocios de los Recuperadores en Desolace
name.frFR: Les affaires de Récupérateurs en Désolace
name.ptBR: Trago qualquer coisa em três dias

text.enUS: Reclaimers' Business in Desolace. Reclaimers' Business in Desolace is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers from Ironforge out to the harsh badlands of Desolace. Issued by Roetten Stonehammer, it sends recruits across the sea to meet Kreldig Ungor at Nijel's Point to assist the Reclaimers in recovering lost treasures and relics for a price. While Ironforge bustles with tradesfolk and dwarven affairs, distant Kalimdor remains an untamed frontier. Roetten Stonehammer acts as an urban liaison for the Reclaimers, an enterprising group looking to capitalize on forgotten ruins and barren lands. He recruits eager adventurers passing through the great mountain city, warning them that Desolace is an atrocious expanse overrun by warring centaur clans, yet ripe with profitable opportunity for those brave enough to make the journey.

name.esES: La reconquista de La Vega Carbonizada
name.frFR: À la reconquête du Val calciné

text.enUS: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. Reclaiming the Charred Vale is an Alliance quest offered by Keeper Albagorm atop Stonetalon Peak. It charges adventurers with culling the aggressive Bloodfury harpies who occupy the ruined valley of the Charred Vale, clearing a path so druids and caretakers can begin healing the scorched landscape. To the south of Stonetalon Peak lies the Charred Vale, a once-lush alpine haven reduced to ash and smoldering ruins. The devastation began when a mechanized logging and mining army swept through the sacred crags, stripping trees and fueling uncontrolled blazes. For the guardians stationed around Stonetalon, watching ancient woodland succumb to industrial greed is an intolerable wound upon the wilderness.

name.esES: La reconquista de La Vega Carbonizada
name.frFR: À la reconquête du Val calciné

text.enUS: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. Reclaiming the Charred Vale is a messenger quest tasked by Keeper Albagorm in Stonetalon Peak. Having temporarily suppressed the local harpies, Albagorm sends an Alliance traveler far south to Feralas to recruit the aid of the druid Falfindel Waywarder. The Charred Vale in southern Stonetalon Mountains remains an ash-choked reminder of catastrophic devastation. While Alliance forces under Keeper Albagorm have struck back against the rampant Bloodfury harpies nesting in the ruins, driving them off is merely a holding action. Albagorm recognizes that physical force alone cannot mend the ravaged earth before the harpies rally and reclaim their dominance.

Reconstructed Tome. In warlocks’ hands, the Reconstructed Tome gathers the scattered teachings of the cabal. Its pages hold the rites for summoning and binding a felhunter from the Twisting Nether. Warlocks of the Alliance and Horde search for the torn leaves of the Tome of the Cabal. They piece the grimoire back together and consult occult scholars, who are eager to glimpse its rare teachings before the finished book is surrendered.

Recover the Key!. Elder Torntusk is held at Jintha'alor in shackles. He says Hitah'ya the Keeper has the key to his bindings and is in the nearby cave, well guarded, and he asks you to kill her and bring it back. After Kidnapped Elder Torntusk!, you find Elder Torntusk bound in shackles at Jintha'alor. Hitah'ya the Keeper holds the key to his bindings and is in the nearby cave, well guarded. Elder Torntusk asks you to kill her and fetch the key so his shackles come loose, for only then can he go home.

Recruitment Letter. Takrin Pathseeker sends promising adventurers from Durotar west to serve in the Barrens. His letter directs able-bodied volunteers to the border outpost run by Kargal Battlescar. Takrin Pathseeker watches young warriors and scouts prove themselves around Razor Hill. He chooses those who seem strong enough for frontline service and gives them a letter for duty in the Barrens. Across the Southfury River bridge, recruits leave Durotar’s sheltered red dirt and join the Horde’s guard against quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts.

Red Burlap Bandana. In Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem gathers red bandanas from slain Defias thieves near the abbey vineyards. The cloth marks low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses of the Brotherhood. Red burlap masks mark the Defias Brotherhood's rank-and-file. Cheap, rough cloth dyed red hides a thief's features and signals allegiance to the growing rebellion. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs carry these scarves into the eastern orchards. The local guards recognize the striking red fabric as proof of thieves slain nearby.

Red Jack Flint. Red Jack Flint is a seasoned human mariner stationed within Menethil Keep in Menethil Harbor.
