text.enUS: Return of the Ring. After scouring away layers of subterranean sludge in Gnomeregan's automated cleaning apparatus, an adventurer uncovers a pristine golden ring bearing the seal of Ironforge and the initials 'TdK'. Tracing those markings leads up to the bustling artisan alleys of the dwarven capital to locate its eccentric creator. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan, ancient machinery still whirs in defiance of the trogg invasion. Feeding a grimy, caked bauble into the Sparklematic 5200 strips away years of irradiated toxic grime, revealing a polished Brilliant Gold Ring thrumming with arcane potency. Stamped along its inner band is the distinct hallmark seal of Ironforge, alongside three neatly engraved initials: 'TdK'.

name.ptBR: Ficar ou não ficar... eis a questão!

text.enUS: Return of the Ring. After scouring away the filth of Gnomeregan in the Sparklematic 5200, an adventurer uncovers a ring bearing the seal of Orgrimmar and the engraved letters 'NOG'. Tracing the piece back to the Horde's capital leads directly to the goblin engineer Nogg, who has his own curious theories about the city's fall. Gnomeregan is an Alliance city deep in Khaz Modan, making the recovery of a ring bearing the official seal of Orgrimmar entirely unexpected. Once processed through the gnomes' Sparklematic cleaning rig, the bauble sheds its thick layer of subterranean sludge, revealing a surge of magical power and the partially legible letters 'NOG'. Whether crafted in Kalimdor or brought along on an ill-fated expedition, the trinket clearly has roots in the Horde capital.

Return the Book. Bethor Iceshard enchants Gunther Arcanus's stolen spellbook to prove his own freedom and recruit his former Kirin Tor colleague to the Forsaken cause. Taking the tome back to Gunther's island retreat reveals that neither former wizard is a thrall to the Lich King. After discovering that the renegade necromancer on Brightwater Lake was his old companion Gunther Arcanus, Bethor Iceshard devised an ingenious method of communication. Having previously ordered the theft of Gunther's spellbook to uncover the necromancer's identity, Bethor weaves an intricate dweomer into its pages. Rather than a demand or an armed parley, the enchantment serves as an arcane signature, proving that Bethor is not only active in Lordaeron, but completely liberated from the Lich King's mental yoke.

Return the Comb. Return the Comb is an Alliance errand in Duskwood that concludes the haunting transaction with the spirit Blind Mary. After being presented with a comb to harvest strands of her spectral hair, the tortured ghost is overcome with despair over her lost beauty and casts the implement away. Returning the hair-laden comb to Madame Eva allows the mystic to spin the ethereal Ghost Hair Thread. Blind Mary lingers in a decrepit shack south of Darkshire, eternally mourning her tragic death and changed state. When approached with Madame Eva's comb, the reminder of mundane grooming only deepens her sorrow. Realizing she is now nothing more than an apparition—a monster stripped of mortal grace whom no one will ever love again—she recoils in horror, thrusting the comb and the ghostly hair tangled in its teeth back into the traveler's hands.

Return to Bellowfiz. Return to Bellowfiz is a short delivery quest in Dun Morogh where an adventurer brings a cask of local Evershine to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It concludes a local favor, rewarding the thirsty driver with a welcome drink. Return to Bellowfiz is an errand in the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. After aiding with local hunting, an adventurer receives a freshly brewed cask of Evershine with instructions to carry it straight to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It is a straightforward favor that highlights the informal camaraderie and mutual support that keep the cold frontier running.

Return to Brock. Having delivered Brock Stoneseeker's missive to Ironforge, you are entrusted with a batch of Honorary Picks to carry back to Thelsamar. Taking advantage of the dwarven aerial transit network, you board a gryphon with Gryth Thurden to return quickly across the mountains. The great mountain stronghold of Ironforge relies on a coordinated network of gryphon roosts to maintain communication and trade with outlying settlements like Loch Modan. Gryth Thurden, Ironforge's gryphon master, oversees this transit from the city's central flight master platform. Because travelers must first establish a rapport with an aerie's handler before flying there, Gryth ensures you have already spoken with Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar before saddling a mount for the return trip.

Return to Corporal Kaleb. Krazek has mended the pot and added a second steam whistle, plus a new chopper in the base made to cut through leg bones. The pot now has to go back to Corporal Kaleb at the Rebel Camp. Krazek has finished with the pot you brought in. It now has one more steam whistle and a new chopper set into the bottom, able to cut through leg bones. Krazek calls it a guaranteed cook-pleaser and expects the owner to be happy with it. It must go back to Corporal Kaleb at the Rebel Camp.

Return to Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Return to Denalan carries Rellian's alarming news to the botanist studying corruption in Teldrassil. After examining the mossy tumors on timberlings, you head south to help Denalan with his discovery. Rellian Greenspyre studies the mossy tumors afflicting Teldrassil's timberlings when urgent word arrives from his colleague Denalan. At his camp beside Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan has finally isolated the cause of these unnatural growths on the forest's nature spirits. Rellian recognizes the gravity of this discovery and sends you south at once to lend a hand.

Return to Feathermoon Stronghold. Your search turned up a strange gazebo at the center of the Ruins of Solarsal. Now it is time to head back to Feathermoon Stronghold and tell General Shandris Feathermoon about it. General Shandris Feathermoon waits at Feathermoon Stronghold to hear about the strange gazebo you discovered in the heart of the ruins. Make your way back to the stronghold with your findings.

Return to Fel'Zerul. An exiled Atal'ai in the Hinterlands has looked over the artifacts brought to them and calls them harmless. They have darker worries about Jammal'an the Prophet, and Fel'zerul in Stonard is to hear them. The Atal'ai Exile once held Jammal'an the Prophet to be a worthy high priest. But the prophet's unyielding faith in the prophecy may doom the Atal'ai, if it has not done so already. Speaking up got the exile branded an infidel and driven out of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The artifacts you brought pose no harm. What frightens the exile is the chance that Jammal'an has found the right fetish enchantment for the summoning ritual, which would put the world in great peril. Fel'zerul in Stonard waits to hear what was learned.

Return to Jahan. Return to Jahan marks the concluding leg of an introduction to the Horde's wind rider flight network between Mulgore and the Barrens. After visiting Thunder Bluff to deliver hides to the skinner Ahanu, travelers take a wyvern back to the Crossroads carrying finished leather wares for the merchant Jahan Hawkwing. For many travelers, this errand is their first experience soaring aboard a trained wind rider. Tal, the wind rider master perched high atop Thunder Bluff's central mesa, arranges flights across the plains of central Kalimdor. As long as a traveler has already established contact with the roost at another settlement—such as Devrak's outpost at the Crossroads—these winged beasts can effortlessly cover leagues that would otherwise demand a perilous overland trek through the Red Rocks and northern Barrens.

Return to Jitters. Return to Jitters concludes Chef Grual's culinary errand in Duskwood. Having prepared his infamous 'crab' cakes using the gooey legs of the local venom web spiders, Grual sends you back to the starving, terrified hermit at Raven Hill. Delivering the meal finally satisfies Jitters' desperate hunger. Duskwood is short on conventional livestock and sea life, leaving Chef Grual at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to improvise with whatever the blighted forest provides. His renowned 'Dusky Crab Cakes' contain no actual crab meat at all, relying instead on gooey legs harvested from the venom web spiders creeping through the wood. Grual considers this resourceful cooking; anyone with a delicate stomach might view it with horror.

Return to Kristoff. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Stormwind for a borrowed book to return. After a long search and a delay in Northshire, you bring The Stresses of Iron back to the Cathedral of Light. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Cathedral Square for The Stresses of Iron, a book on metallurgy. Its trail led from Stormwind Keep's Royal Library to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton was copying the text by hand. Paxton ran short of Rethban ore for the scribe's ink, so the work stalled. With the ore retrieved and the copy complete, you bring the original book back to Stormwind.

Return to Lewis. Dungar Longdrink sends armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Osric's Crate crosses Elwynn and Westfall by gryphon, carrying supplies to defenders under pressure. Westfall is slipping from the kingdom's grasp. Defias bandits, ravenous gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers threaten the land. Overland supply routes face harassment, and roads are dangerous for solitary wagons. The flight master network offers a crucial lifeline. Osric, an armorer in Stormwind's Old Town, prepared a heavy crate of armor for the battered volunteers of the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill.

Return to MacKinley. After the scare of the giblets, "Shaky" Phillipe hands you a pouch to carry to "Sea Wolf" MacKinley. Phillipe swears the debt was always meant to be paid and adds that there is no need to get rough. Phillipe presses a pouch of payment on you for Sea Wolf. Phillipe wants MacKinley told that the debt was always meant to be repaid, and swears to it. Phillipe puts it down to getting a little drunk and losing the way, and says MacKinley will understand and that there is no need to get rough.

Return to Marleth. Return to Marleth marks the mischievous conclusion to a heated brewing feud in Dun Morogh. Having infiltrated the Kharanos cellar and swapped in a keg of Marleth's fiery Scalder, an adventurer returns to Brewnall Village with a prize barrel of Thunder Ale as indisputable proof. Dwarven rivalries are rarely settled with diplomacy when there is ale on the line. Marleth Barleybrew of Brewnall Village harbors a fierce competitive grudge against the distillers of Kharanos, creators of the famed Thunder Ale. After having her potent 'Scalder' slipped into the Thunderbrew cellar unnoticed, Marleth demands evidence of the feat. Hoisting a genuine barrel of Thunder Ale from beneath their noses serves as both trophy and leverage.

Return to Narain. Dirge Quikcleave keeps his word and hands over the five-hundred-pound chicken. You carry it to Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris. This comes after Dirge's Kickin' Chimaerok Chops. Dirge Quikcleave gives you the chicken he promised, saying he is a goblin of his word. He cannot imagine what a gnome would want with a bird that large, and grumbles that it must be to sleep in. From here you take it to Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris.

Return to Nessa. You carry Laird's findings from Auberdine back to Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. The journey is an introductory errand that teaches young travelers how to cross between Kalimdor and Teldrassil. Laird sends you back across the water with his written observations. He has found stark differences between the fish caught off Darkshore and those near Teldrassil, and suspects the great World Tree changes the local marine life. You can return to Rut'theran Village by hiring a flight from Caylais Moonfeather, the hippogryph master, or by boarding the regular ferry at Auberdine's pier.

Return to Onu. You carry a page from the Twilight Tome back to Onu in Darkshore. The scribbles are all you could bear to take from the cultists’ book. The Twilight Tome overwhelms anyone who tries to read it. Its words swim across the page, and its ornate scrollwork twists into grotesque figures. You tear out a single page of scribbles before the strain brings on vertigo.

Return to Podrig. Return to Podrig is a logistics quest concluding a courier run between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. After delivering a dispatch to the capital, the courier is entrusted with a crate of weapons to ferry back to Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher using the Forsaken bat handler network. Outposts throughout Lordaeron depend heavily on regular shipments from the Undercity to remain operational. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Deathguard sentries face pressure from local worgen, Dalaran remnants, and Scourge stragglers. Supplying remote garrisons with freshly forged armaments is vital to holding the region under Forsaken control.

Return to Primal Torntusk. Elder Torntusk asks you to return to his mate, Primal Torntusk, at Revantusk Village and tell her that he is coming home. Elder Torntusk is free of his bindings, and he asks you to return to Revantusk Village. There you are to tell his mate, Primal Torntusk, that he is coming home.

Return to Quinn. Return to Quinn is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest where an adventurer delivers a restorative draught concocted by Apothecary Renferrel to the wounded Deathstalker Quinn Yorick. Trapped and weakened at the Ivar Patch north of the Sepulcher, Quinn requires the draught before he can contemplate returning to duty. Following the harvesting of wild beast hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher brews a restorative potion formulated to aid Quinn Yorick. Renferrel has little time for sentimentality or bedside manners, quickly handing off the mixture to return to his own clandestine alchemical research, leaving the adventurer to run the courier run back into the wilderness.

Return to Rorian. Return to Rorian is a mission carrying urgent reports from the field back to Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After aiding Yala Windwatcher against encroaching forces, an adventurer is dispatched to inform Rorian the Dayseeker that the Al'Aketh cult has actively escalated their presence by disturbing the local wind spirits. Following the disruption dealt to the agitators harassing Zephras Isle, Yala Windwatcher stays behind to mop up remaining hostiles while tasking you with an essential duty: delivering intelligence. Thendal Grove needs to know that the mysterious Al'Aketh are no longer operating purely in the shadows.

Return to Sven. This quest marks the moment Sven Yorgen finally learns the truth behind the brutal massacre of his family at the Yorgen Farmstead. After tracking down the runaway Jitters, you return to Sven's isolated camp on the edge of Westfall carrying the vagrant's completed journal. The journal promises answers to the questions that have haunted Sven since the attack. When Sven Yorgen's farm was attacked, Jitters fled into the woods in terror, leaving behind only an incomplete diary amidst the slaughter. Terrified of Sven's wrath and haunted by what he witnessed, Jitters hid deep within Duskwood. When confronted, he hands over his completed journal willingly, desperately hoping that providing the full story of the attack will spare him from having to face the vengeful farmer in person.

Return to Thunder Bluff. This quest charges an operative with carrying a potent chemical agent brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill back across the sea to Thunder Bluff. There, Apothecary Zamah awaits the compound so she can engineer a dispersal apparatus against the Venture Company. It marks a crucial step in the Royal Apothecary Society's clandestine research under the very roofs of their Tauren hosts. After securing the volatile ingredients requested in the Hillsbrad Foothills, Apothecary Lydon successfully synthesizes his virulent concoction. Lydon is thoroughly thrilled to see his biological handiwork tested on live subjects, but the raw toxin alone lacks an effective delivery mechanism. To maximize its effect, the vial must be brought back across the Great Sea to the crags of Mulgore, into the waiting hands of Apothecary Zamah.

Return to Troyas. Daryn Lightwind hands over her book, Feralas: A History, and asks you to take care of it. It goes to Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold, who is surely eager for your return. With the Super Snapper FX behind you, Daryn Lightwind gives you her book and asks that you look after it. She urges you to hurry along, sure that Troyas is eager for your return. The book is bound for Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold.

Return to Vahlarriel. Dalinda Malem is ready to leave Thunder Axe Fortress. She thanks you for what you have done for her and her family, and says the time is yours to choose. You escort her out, then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer. Dalinda asks whether the time has come, and offers thanks for all you have done for her and her family, in case things do not go as hoped. If you are ready, nothing else keeps her here, and she will go when you judge the moment right. You escort her out of Thunder Axe Fortress and then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer in Desolace.

Return to Verner. You carry fifty freshly forged horseshoes from Goldshire back to Lakeshire. Smith Argus has finished the order, and Verner Osgood is waiting across the border in Redridge. Smith Argus has forged fifty horseshoes for Lakeshire, and you carry them east from Goldshire. Redridge faces supply shortages and gnoll attacks. The iron shoes help keep horses and draft animals working on its rugged mountain roads.

name.esES: Vuelve con el médico brujo Uzer'i

text.enUS: Return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i. With the shrunken head delivered in A Strange Request, Neeru Fireblade hands you the herbs and asks you to carry them to Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Feralas, along with word that Neeru is satisfied with the head. After A Strange Request, Neeru Fireblade gives you a pouch of herbs for Witch Doctor Uzer'i. You are also asked to tell Uzer'i that Neeru is satisfied with the shrunken head. The pouch is bound for Uzer'i in Feralas.

name.esES: El regreso a Las Tierras Devastadas

text.enUS: Return to the Blasted Lands. With newly forged weapons in hand, you are directed back from Stranglethorn Vale to the Blasted Lands. The spirit of the Fallen Hero of the Horde awaits your return to set you against the demon Razelikh. Following the completion of your enchanted armaments, Galvan the Ancient proclaims that the hour of redemption is at hand. You carry the newly crafted weapons back to the Blasted Lands, seeking out the Fallen Hero of the Horde. The ghostly warrior asks whether you are prepared to face Razelikh and his minions.

Return to the Crossroads.. Gryshka's reply is on its way from Orgrimmar to Zargh at the Crossroads. A wind rider carries it across the distance between Durotar and the Barrens. You carry Gryshka's written reply to Zargh after bringing her a parcel of prime meat in Orgrimmar. Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's high bluffs, provides a mount for the return to the Barrens. You have already met Devrak at the Crossroads, so the wyverns know the flight path. The ride crosses the desert sky and saves you the long march overland across the Southfury River.

name.esES: Vuelve a las Tierras del Interior

text.enUS: Return to the Hinterlands. Thadius Grimshade tells you where Sharpbeak is kept: in a cage on a high cliff, atop Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. Vile Priestess Hexx, high priestess of the Vilebranch trolls, has the key. You are to carry the news to Gryphon Master Talonaxe. Having done his part, Thadius wishes you fortune and tells you what he learned. Sharpbeak sits caged on a high cliff, atop Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. Vile Priestess Hexx, high priestess of the Vilebranch trolls, possesses the key to that cage. Take word of this to Gryphon Master Talonaxe.

Return to the Magistrate. Return to the Magistrate concludes an urgent reconnaissance dispatch between the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades and the town of Brill. Having reported to Deathguard Linnea at her waystation east of Brill, adventurers are sent back to deliver troubling news directly to Magistrate Sevren. The message confirms that the mindless minions of the Lich King continue to test the borders of the young Forsaken nation. The eastern road out of Tirisfal Glades leads directly into the blighted ruins of the Western Plaguelands, where the Scourge holds devastating sway. To keep the undead hordes from spilling over into their newly claimed homeland, the Forsaken established the Bulwark—a fortified checkpoint watched from a waystation behind the line by grim sentries like Deathguard Linnea. After gathering reports of what presses against the eastern gate, Linnea sends messengers racing back west along the King's Road toward Brill before enemy infiltrators can capitalize on any gaps.

Returning Home. In Goldshire, a novice night elf priest receives a call to return home. The novice has wandered as far as Elwynn Forest, where Priestess Josetta relays an urgent message from Darnassus: return to the Temple of the Moon and continue spiritual training under Priestess Alathea. Night elves are an unusual sight in Elwynn Forest, and a young acolyte among its human settlements draws attention. When you arrive in Goldshire, Priestess Josetta greets you warmly with news. A Sister of Elune has traveled across continents seeking you, bearing an urgent command from the Temple of the Moon. It is time to return to Kalimdor and advance your calling.

Returning Home. In Darnassus, Returning Home brings young night elf priests before the leaders of their faith. After proving themselves in Teldrassil’s wilds, they are summoned to the Temple of the Moon to meet Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Priests tending the wounded and cleansing corruption around Dolanaar draw the Sisterhood of Elune’s notice. Trainer Laurna Morninglight intercepts promising initiates with word that Priestess Alathea has asked to meet them. Aid to local settlements matters, but each devotee must also deepen their communion with the Moon Mother and answer the faith’s higher calling.

Returning Home. A summons reaches wandering night elf priests in Dun Morogh, calling them back to Darnassus. Maxan Anvol, the dwarven priest trainer, directs them to report to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon. In Kharanos, Maxan Anvol takes note of the night elf's fortitude amid Dun Morogh's bitter cold, far from Teldrassil's serene forests. The dwarven priest trainer brings urgent word: a priestess of Elune passed through looking for the elf, carrying orders from Darnassus that demand an immediate return.

Returning Home. In human lands, a night elf priest receives a summons to return to Teldrassil. Brother Joshua delivers the message from Priestess Alathea, who calls the young priest to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for advanced guidance in Elune’s mysteries. Night elf priests sometimes travel to human lands such as Stormwind to share spiritual fellowship with the Church of the Holy Light. Their deepest ties remain with the Sisterhood of Elune. Brother Joshua tells an acolyte that a night elf emissary has come searching for them. Their early travels are over, and their home temple calls them back for deeper training with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind’s inner circle.

Returning Home. Priestess Alathea calls promising night elf priests back to Darnassus. The summons brings them to the Temple of the Moon to be recognized by the Sisterhood of Elune and receive advanced guidance. A messenger from the Sisterhood reaches you while you visit Nara Meideros in Stormwind's Park. You have served your people abroad, and the order's leaders now require you in Darnassus. They have watched your spiritual growth and call you back for an evaluation and a rite of recognition. The journey marks your passage from a new initiate to an active servant of the Mother Moon.

Returning Home. Night elf priests in Ironforge are called back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. A Sisterhood emissary seeks out acolytes abroad and sends them to Priestess Alathea for urgent training and sacred duties. In Ironforge, night elf priests remain tied to the Sisterhood of Elune, though they are far from Teldrassil. Braenna Flintcrag, a dwarven priest trainer in the Mystic Ward, carries a message from a visiting night elf priestess. The messenger sought young disciples traveling abroad and said their mentors needed them back in the capital at once.

name.esES: La vuelta de la cartera perdida

text.enUS: Returning the Lost Satchel. In Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, the search for Maur Grimtotem ends with his satchel. You must carry it back to Rahauro on Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Maur Grimtotem was slain by troggs in the fiery depths of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Even in death, his arms clung to his personal satchel. Freeing it from his grip is the only clue to why a member of the Grimtotem clan entered the volcanic caverns beneath Thrall's capital.

Revenge of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire prepares to strike back at the Bael Modan dwarves. After Prospector Khazgorm's death, he sends Horde allies into the fortress for volatile munitions to fuel his attack. Gann Stonespire knows Prospector Khazgorm's death only slowed the Bael Modan dig site. Dwarven work will resume, and another foreman will soon oversee the machines tearing through Gann's ancestral land. He refuses to watch the earth suffer more excavation. Instead, Gann plans to turn the invaders' demolitions gear against them and rupture their stronghold from within.

Revenge of Gann. At Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire turns the dwarves’ own plans against their flying machine. The Horde agent seeks revenge for the fallen Stonespire tribe. At Bael Modan, the dwarven excavation sits atop the ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. The Prospectors rely on a gyrocopter for their reach and military strength. It is stationed on a watchtower above the dig, where it surveys the surrounding Barrens and protects the dwarves’ supply lines. For Gann, the machine also marks the Alliance’s intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

Rezlak. Along Durotar's roads south of Orgrimmar, Rezlak waits for help with his supply lines. The goblin entrepreneur belongs to the Tinkers' Union and hires travelers to recover missing supplies and drive off harpies. Rezlak waits beside the canyon road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. He represents the Tinkers' Union, a goblin syndicate focused on engineering, supply lines, and practical business. The factional tensions of Kalimdor matter little to him while trade runs smoothly. Dustwind harpies have raided his cargo caravans and made the routes unsafe. Rezlak remains at his post and hires passersby willing to earn a profit by recovering supplies and dealing with the harpies.

Rhahk'Zor. Rhahk'Zor is a hulking ogre serving as the head foreman within the Deadmines. Overseeing Edwin VanCleef's subterranean construction efforts, he keeps the Defias laborers and miners in line through sheer brute force and heavy-handed discipline. Deep beneath the rolling hills of Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood has transformed the abandoned gold mines of Moonbrook into an underground fortress. Coordinating this sprawling construction requires harsh discipline, a role filled by the ogre Rhahk'Zor. Appointed as head foreman, he oversees the excavation crews and laborers, driving them forward to carve out tunnels and assemble VanCleef's secret projects.

Rhapsody Shindigger. Gryphon Master Talonaxe tells of Rhapsody Shindigger, once the finest flyer at the aviary, who took so keenly to liquor that Rhapsody had to be let go. Talonaxe has heard that Rhapsody now keeps a brewing camp east of the aviary, in the Hinterlands. Talonaxe stresses that the dwarves of the aviary all love a good ale, but Rhapsody took to liquor the way a gryphon takes to the skies. No one could fly like Rhapsody, a damned shame as Talonaxe sees it. The first sign of trouble came when Rhapsody stumbled back from the trip with Brohann, and things went downhill fast. In the end Rhapsody had to be let go. The last word is that a brew camp now stands to the east of Aerie Peak.

name.esES: El cubata de Kalimdor de Rapsodio
name.zhCN: 拉普索迪的卡利姆多鸡尾酒

text.enUS: Rhapsody's Kalimdor Kocktail. Rhapsody Shindigger, found in the Hinterlands, will talk about what happened down in the swamp only if given something stiff to drink. A Kalimdor Kocktail needs Roc gizzards from Tanaris and Groddoc and Ironfur livers from Feralas. Rhapsody greets Brohann's messenger with a hiccup. The two of them had quite an adventure, and the tale of what happened down in the swamp, which was not a pretty scene, will only come out with something stiff to drink. Rhapsody has a recipe in mind, the Kalimdor Kocktail, and promises to tell everything once it is brewed.

Rhapsody's Tale. After Rhapsody Shindigger gets his Kalimdor Kocktail, he finally tells his tale of the flight with Brohann Caskbelly. He hands over an Atal'ai Tablet Fragment and asks that it be taken to Brohann in Stormwind. With the kocktail in him, Rhapsody Shindigger finally talks. Before the flight he drank a whole keg of stout, and Brohann followed him through the sky. What he kept from it is a troll souvenir, an Atal'ai Tablet Fragment, and he wants it taken to Brohann Caskbelly in Stormwind.

Rhinag. Among the rocks near Durotar's northwestern border, Rhinag waits, weakened by scorpids' venom. The Darkspear troll depends on passing travelers to find him a remedy in time. Rhinag shelters among the rocks near Durotar's northwestern border after a Venomtail Scorpid stung him. The poison has left the Darkspear troll weak and isolated. He needs a venomtail antidote, and his survival depends on whether a passing traveler can find one before the toxins take their toll.

Ride to Ironforge. Ride to Ironforge is an introductory courier quest that sends newly trained adventurers on their first gryphon flight from Thelsamar in Loch Modan into the dwarven capital. Entrusted with a list of top mining students from Brock Stoneseeker, the traveler carries the dispatch straight to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Great Forge. For many young mountaineers and travelers, the flight from Thelsamar to Ironforge marks their very first journey astride a gryphon. Handled by Gryphon Master Thorgrum Borrelson, this short passage carries travelers over Dun Morogh's snowy ridges and directly into the cavernous entry of the mountain fortress.

Ride to Orgrimmar. A wind rider carries Horde travelers from the Crossroads to Orgrimmar. With Zargh’s fresh cuts of meat in hand, you fly to the capital’s Skytower and deliver them to Innkeeper Gryshka. Devrak sends trained wind riders between the Crossroads and Orgrimmar. The flight crosses the dry Barrens and reaches Durotar’s red cliffs, sparing travelers the hard journey on foot. From high above the dusty canyon trails, the wyverns carry messengers and travelers, along with dispatches and trade goods, straight to the capital.

name.esES: Un viaje a Cima del Trueno
name.itIT: In volo verso Picco del Tuono
name.ptBR: Voo para o Penhasco do Trovão

text.enUS: Ride to Thunder Bluff. This quest sends young Horde adventurers taking their first flight path across Kalimdor aboard a wind rider. Entrusted with a shipment of cured hides, travelers depart the dry crossroads of the Barrens to deliver valuable leatherwork supplies directly to the heights of Thunder Bluff. For many travelers making their way through the Barrens, booking a flight with Devrak marks their first journey through the skies on the back of a wind rider. These winged wyverns provide vital aerial links between the dispersed settlements of the fledgling Horde, avoiding the perilous ground routes prowled by quilboar and centaur packs.

Ride to the Undercity. Ride to the Undercity introduces fledgling Forsaken adventurers to the Horde's aerial flight network across Lordaeron. Carrying weapon requisitions from the embattled outpost of the Sepulcher, couriers take a dread bat directly into the Undercity's Trade Quarter to resupply regional defenders. Maintaining lines of communication between the Forsaken capital and its frontline outposts requires swift, reliable transit. Karos Razok, the bat handler stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, manages the trained dread bats that ferry messengers and supplies across the plagued landscape. With roads crawling with hostile beasts, Moonrage worgen, and remnants of the Scourge, taking to the skies is the safest and fastest way to ensure urgent military requests reach the capital.

Ridgepoint Tower. Stormwind guards watch the eastern frontier from Ridgepoint Tower. They keep vigil over the perilous corridors, valleys, and roads leading into neighboring wilderness. At Ridgepoint Tower, the garrison watches the valleys and roads of eastern Elwynn. The tower stands on high ground, where Stormwind's authority reaches its eastern border and the wilds begin. Its guards keep watch over the routes before threats can reach the farms and settlements nearer Northshire and Goldshire.

Rilli Greasygob. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob is the specialist Wenikee Boltbucket seeks. She sends you there with a damaged samophlange, hoping his knowledge of its Venture Company origins can explain the device. Wenikee Boltbucket examined the samophlange recovered from the Venture Company drilling site in the Barrens. Her extra gauges showed the apparatus nearing collapse. More levers and dials might destroy it, so she stopped and sent the problem to someone with knowledge of its design.

Rime's Wrath. Rime's Wrath is a quest focused on quelling a hazardous outbreak of minor ice elementals. Because methods to peacefully soothe the aggressive frost spirits were unknown, eliminating them became necessary to keep the area safe. Rime's Wrath involves dealing with a localized surge of minor ice elementals. These spirits of biting frost and cold have become an active danger in the area, necessitating swift intervention before their chill spreads further or harms passersby. Rather than a coordinated assault, the response is a containment measure against wild, hostile elemental manifestations.

Rime's Wrath. Following a rockslide, an unusually large elemental named Avala emerged and began triggering erratic weather swings and secondary landslides. An observer tasks adventurers with hunting down the elemental and claiming its core to secure the area. Defeating the creature restores stability to the mountain slopes and safeguards travelers from deadly winter perils. The disturbances began when a sudden rockslide destabilized the mountain pass, opening the way for elemental activity. Among the creatures that surfaced, one particular elemental stood out, towering over its kin in sheer size and raw power. Given the informal moniker "Avala" by the watchful questgiver, this potent entity is not merely an imposing presence—it directly fuels localized atmospheric turmoil and destabilizes the surrounding cliffs. Its presence poses an immediate peril to anyone attempting to navigate the area, as unstable earth and sudden winter chills make ordinary travel lethal.

Rin'ji is Trapped!. Rin'ji, a troll, has lost an axe and been captured in Quel'Danil Lodge, and begs for help to escape. Rin'ji knows that others may not like Rin'ji's kind, but promises something in return and mentions a secret hidden at the Overlook Cliffs. Rin'ji is a captive at Quel'Danil Lodge and badly frightened. The axe is gone, and Rin'ji begs any passer-by to help get away. Rin'ji knows many dislike Rin'ji's kind, but offers something for a kind soul who helps, and says a secret lies hidden at the Overlook Cliffs.

Rin'ji's Secret. After helping Rin'ji, you carry a tablet etched with Witherbark troll markings that nobody has yet read. Oran Snakewrithe, who studies the Witherbark, might decipher it, and lives in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Witherbark troll markings cover the tablet, and what Rin'ji's secret really is remains a mystery. It might be worth a great deal, or it might be worth nothing, because a Witherbark troll in trouble would probably do anything to get out of it.

Ring of Zoram. The Ring of Zoram is an ancient Kaldorei heirloom dating back to the glory days of the sunken city of Zoram before the Great Sundering. Once worn by the city's rulers and the key to the ancient lock of a sunken statuette, it recently fell into the hands of the encroaching coastal naga. Before the Well of Eternity collapsed and the oceans swallowed the western reaches of Kalimdor, Zoram was a coastal jewel of the night elven empire. The Ring of Zoram belonged to the rulers of the city, and a strange code is written upon its inner band in the language of the night elves. When the Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago, the ring sank along with the city, lost beneath the crashing tides of what is now the Zoram Strand.

Ringo. Ringo is an unfortunate goblin explorer who ventured up the blistering heights of Fire Plume Ridge in Un'Goro Crater. Overwhelmed by the volcano's stifling heat and noxious vapors, he collapsed inside a cave, desperate for someone to help him back down. His close friend Spraggle Frock remains worried sick back at Marshal's Refuge. While goblins are known for braving hazardous environments in search of wealth or oddities, Fire Plume Ridge proves harsh even by their standards. Towering in the center of Un'Goro Crater, the active volcano spews ash, magma, and boiling steam. Ringo climbed about halfway up the southern face before the suffocating heat finally proved too much for him. Leaving his belongings scattered just outside, he crawled into a cave to shelter from the sweltering atmosphere, completely incapacitated by heat exhaustion.

Ripped Missive. The Ripped Missive is a blood-spattered letter recovered from Haalien that sheds light on a brutal cultist assault against a druid den in Shadowgale Forest. Its contents expose the callous motives behind the slaughter and hint at dangerous subversion originating from within Valanaar. Tucked behind the bracer of Haalien, this torn and bloodstained document holds grim intelligence concerning the recent violence in Shadowgale Forest. Recovered after a fierce skirmish, the scrap of writing sheds light on the dark intentions of the cultists who fell upon the local druid den, offering vital clues for those seeking justice for the fallen.

Rise of the Silithid. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser urges you to carry the report on the insect threat to Gracina Spiritmight, a night elf scholar and historian in Darnassus. Fizzledowser wants the report to reach someone with working knowledge of such matters. Gracina Spiritmight is a night elf scholar who has spent a lot of time studying the life forms unique to Azeroth's ecology, and she is a historian too. Fizzledowser hopes she can help work out what the danger really is and, above all, how it might be halted. By Fizzledowser's last word, she was living in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.

Rise of the Silithid. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser hands you the report on the insect threat and urges you to take it to Orgrimmar, to a troll scholar named Zilzibin Drumlore. Fizzledowser wants the report in the hands of someone who has working knowledge of such matters. Zilzibin Drumlore is a troll scholar who has spent a lot of time studying the life forms unique to Azeroth's ecology, and is a historian besides. Fizzledowser hopes Zilzibin can work out what the danger really is and how it might be halted, and says all the help available will be needed. Zilzibin lives in a house on the Drag's second tier, in Orgrimmar.

Rise of the Silithid. General Shandris Feathermoon hands you a copy of Raschal's account of the infestation in southeastern Feralas. Darnassus is where the main report is filed, and she wants this copy to reach Gracina Spiritmight, a priestess of the Temple of the Moon who knows a great deal about such creatures. While the main report is filed in Darnassus, Shandris Feathermoon entrusts this copy to you. It is meant for Gracina Spiritmight, an associate of the Protectorate. She is a priestess, and her home is the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, and the General says her broad knowledge of such creatures, and her receiving the report, would benefit everyone. She dismisses you with good wishes and a prayer that Elune watch over all.

Rise, Obsidion!. After Release Them, a dying archaeologist gasps that it was all a trap, and begs you to kill the traitor for them and for Thorius. Both Lathoric the Black and Obsidion must die, and Curator Thorius in Ironforge wants proof of it. The archaeologist is barely able to speak. They say it was all a trap, ask for forgiveness, and plead for the traitor to be killed for them and for Thorius. Lathoric the Black and Obsidion must both fall, and Curator Thorius in Ironforge wants the head of one and the heart of the other.

Rising Spirit. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers a ritual blessing drawn from Agamaggan's ancient power. Bring blood shards taken from his Bristleback rivals, and he strengthens your will and spirit. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth knows the geomancy and ancestral magic of the quilboar. He takes pride in his people's devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. To Mangletooth, an unbroken spirit carries a warrior onward when strength fails and defeat seems near.

Rite of Strength. The Rite of Strength is the initial trial in the traditional Rites of the Earthmother undertaken by young tauren at Camp Narache. To demonstrate their bravery and defense of the tribe, initiates must cull encroaching Bristleback quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine and present their belts to Chief Hawkwind. For a young tauren seeking recognition from tribal elders and eventual acceptance in Thunder Bluff, completing the Rites of the Earthmother is an essential duty. Bestowed by Seer Graytongue, the Rite of Strength serves as the starting trial. It demands physical courage and decisive action in defense of Red Cloud Mesa, testing whether an initiate can face the tribe's mortal foes without flinching.

Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a pivotal coming-of-age trial within the Rites of the Earthmother, testing a young adventurer's spiritual maturity. Initiated by Baine Bloodhoof, the quest directs aspirants to seek counsel from the village seer, Zarlman Two-Moons. Undertaking this journey is essential for anyone seeking the blessings and respect of the elders on the rises of Thunder Bluff. For generations, the nomadic tauren have turned to the Earthmother to guide their people across the plains of Kalimdor. Now gathered within the safe borders of Mulgore, their spiritual traditions remain the cornerstone of their society. The Rite of Vision is one of the ancient trials known as the Rites of the Earthmother. While earlier trials test an initiate's physical strength and connection to the hunt, the Rite of Vision demands an inward journey, directing young tauren and honored allies to commune directly with the spirits.

Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a foundational spiritual trial undergone by young tauren stepping beyond the Red Cloud Mesa into greater Mulgore. To pierce the veil and receive guidance from ancestral spirits, initiates must gather natural reagents to brew the Water of the Seers under the watchful eye of Zarlman Two-Moons in Bloodhoof Village. Before any vision can be granted, the initiate must demonstrate an intimate understanding of the natural gifts found across Mulgore. Zarlman Two-Moons instructs the seeker to collect well stones found near the sacred communal water wells and ambercorn fallen beneath the roots of Mulgore's ancient trees. These natural elements are not merely physical objects; to the tauren, they hold the latent magic and lifeblood of the Earth Mother, ready to be channeled into ritual use.

Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is the spiritual climax of an ancient trial undertaken by young tauren in Bloodhoof Village. By drinking the sacred Water of the Seers beside the tribal bonfire, initiates summon a spectral guide to lead them toward their destiny. After gathering the necessary ritual herbs and passing the initial trials of faith, an initiate is granted the Water of the Seers by the village shaman, Zarlman Two-Moons. This potent draught must be ingested before the roaring tribal fire at the heart of Bloodhoof Village. When consumed with a focused and respectful mind, the sacred waters expand the drinker's perception beyond physical sight, bridging the veil between the material plane and the spiritual realm.

Rite of Wisdom. The Rite of Wisdom is the concluding trial in the traditional Rites of the Earthmother undertaken by young adventurers in Mulgore. After purifying their sight through the Rite of Vision, petitioners travel to the sacred burial grounds of Red Rocks to commune with an Ancestral Spirit and receive the blessing of the dead. Having cleared their perception through the Rite of Vision, young protectors are directed east of Thunder Bluff toward Red Rocks. This ancient burial ground holds the physical remains and lingering spirits of those who fought and died to carve out a peaceful existence in Mulgore. Passing the trial requires approaching the resting grounds with proper reverence and communion, facing whatever territorial threats roam the hills to seek the counsel of the honored dead.

Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the beginning of an initiate's spiritual journey on Red Cloud Mesa. Directed by Chief Hawkwind, travelers seek out Seer Graytongue in the southern hills of Camp Narache. Undertaking these venerable ceremonies is considered a vital trial of passage for tauren coming of age. Upon the Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind directs young tauren seeking to prove themselves to Seer Graytongue. Residing in the quiet hills directly south of Camp Narache, Graytongue oversees the spiritual beginnings of the youth. This simple journey marks the formal threshold between everyday camp life and the serious commitments demanded by tribal custom.

name.esES: Los ritos de la Madre Tierra

text.enUS: Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the transition of a young tauren out of the secluded Red Cloud Mesa and into the wider plains of Mulgore. Having proven your mettle in Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sends you north to Bloodhoof Village with a carved totem to continue the ancient trials under Baine Bloodhoof. For generations, young tauren have tested their strength within the safe cradle of Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Completing the initial trials proves one has the discipline and resolve to survive, but the sacred Rites of the Earthmother require far more than surviving local wildlife. Chief Hawkwind recognizes when an initiate has outgrown the mesa's sheltered hunting grounds and must step into the broader community.

name.esES: Los ritos de la Madre Tierra

text.enUS: Rites of the Earthmother. This trial, set directly by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, tasks rising heroes with hunting down the great kodo beast Arra'chea across the plains of Mulgore. Though an initiate may have completed the traditional rites of passage, Cairne expects his people to continually reaffirm their strength, tracking, and devotion to the tribe. Returning with Arra'chea's horn proves an adventurer is ready to serve the wider Horde beyond the mesas. Reaching Thunder Bluff marks the end of simple youth for a tauren, but High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof does not let young hunters rest on their laurels. To Cairne, earning a place among the high bluffs is merely the beginning of one's responsibility to the United Tauren Tribes. Rather than sending initiates against petty pests, he demands proof of real fieldcraft: the tracking and clean harvest of one of Mulgore's most renowned wandering beasts.

Rivern Frostwind. Rivern Frostwind is a night elf riding instructor stationed high atop Frostsaber Rock in northern Winterspring. Accompanied by his frost tiger companion Glacier, he watches over the native wintersabers and trains riders deemed worthy by his order. Only the most dedicated champions of the Alliance are granted the honor of riding one of his prized mounts. Perched on the icy promontory of Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind oversees the breeding and stewardship of the legendary Winterspring frostsaber. While nightsabers roam the lush forests of Teldrassil and Ashenvale, their sub-arctic cousins are bred to endure the bitter cold of northern Kalimdor. Rivern acts as a gatekeeper for these majestic predators. He demands that outsiders prove their commitment to preserving the beasts—gathering fresh meat from the tundra, clearing out Winterfall furbolgs, and driving back rampaging frost giants—before he will even consider entrusting one of the sabers to them.

text.enUS: Riverpaw Gnoll Bounty. Riverpaw Gnoll Bounty is an official contract issued by Deputy Rainer at Westbrook Garrison to cull the encroaching gnolls threatening Elwynn Forest's western borders. The Stormwind Army offers a reward for painted armbands taken from the Riverpaw packs infesting the woods and waterways. Westbrook Garrison guards the critical borderlands between Elwynn Forest and Westfall. However, depleted garrison forces have left the outpost struggling to contain an aggressive influx of Riverpaw gnolls. These savage creatures have established encampments directly south of the guard tower and further east around the shores of Stone Cairn Lake, encroaching close enough to threaten peaceful travelers and local homesteads.

Riverpaw pack. The Riverpaw pack is a savage clan of gnolls inhabiting the borderlands of Elwynn Forest and Westfall. Known for their brutal raids and ruthless dominance over local kobolds, they have grown increasingly organized and brazen following the Third War. With Stormwind's military stretched thin, their presence threatens vital roads and settlements throughout the heartland. For decades, the Riverpaw clan prowled the fringes of human civilization, but their boldness has surged in recent years. In Elwynn Forest, packs led by the infamous brute Hogger prowl the southern woods around Forest's Edge and roam the shores of Stone Cairn Lake. In Westfall, they roam across the Dust Plains and along the coasts, ambushing solitary travelers and raiding homesteads. Deputy Rainer at Westbrook Garrison and Captain Danuvin at Sentinel Hill rely heavily on mercenary blades to cull their numbers, issuing standing bounties for painted armbands and severed paws.

Riversong the Elder. Elder Riversong is an ancestral night elf spirit honored during the Lunar Festival, found resting beneath a quiet shrine in Astranaar. Bathed in a beam of moonlight, she offers quiet wisdom to travelers and directs pilgrims toward other revered ancestors across the lands of Kalimdor. Amid the ancient boughs and wooden walkways of Astranaar, Elder Riversong appears under an open night elf shrine. Marked by a distinct column of celestial light piercing the Ashenvale canopy, her ethereal presence serves as a focal point for participants in the Lunar Festival seeking communion with past generations.

Rizzle's Schematics. Rizzle's unguarded plans describe the refining of indurium ore. The scrawls point to the dwarves' dig at Uldaman, in the Badlands, as where the ore comes from, and many of the other notes are about heat resistance. A lump of raw ore sits on the plans as a paperweight, and you carry that sample to Pozzik on the Shimmering Flats. This follows Keeping Pace. Rizzle's schematics describe the refining of indurium ore. Rizzle's scrawls point to the dwarves' dig at Uldaman, in the Badlands, as where the ore comes from. Many of the other notes are about how well it resists heat. A lump of raw indurium ore holds the plans down as a paperweight, and that sample is what you take to Pozzik.

Robo-Mechanical Guts. Robo-Mechanical Guts are salvagable gearworks, conduits, and machine innards harvested from the malfunctioning constructs roaming the ruins of Gnomeregan. Gnomish engineers in Stormwind require these specific components to repair heavy tunneling vehicles meant to aid in the reclamation of Gnomeregan in Dun Morogh. When High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the surviving gnomes evacuated Gnomeregan, thousands of automated mechanisms, clockwork sentries, and industrial robots were abandoned inside. In the city's radioactive aftermath, these machines continue to roam the corridors autonomously. In Stormwind City, the tinker Shoni seeks to assemble a fleet of gyrodrillmatic excavationators to pierce the defenses of Gnomeregan and reclaim the lost city. Lacking fresh raw materials, she tasks bold adventurers with braving the contaminated halls of Gnomeregan to carve out functional robot viscera—springs, wires, and gyro-components—to refit the excavation machinery.

Rocket Car Parts. Rocket Car Parts are the scattered, twisted metal remains of high-speed collisions across the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Constantly generated by reckless gnome and goblin racers pushing experimental speeders past their limits, these salvaged scraps are harvested by opportunists looking to turn racetrack accidents into quick coin. The Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats is the staging ground for an unending, combustible rivalry between goblin and gnome engineering. In their pursuit of unmatched land speed, racers regularly suffer catastrophic breakdowns, explosive misfires, and high-velocity crashes that scatter metal across the salt flats. These discarded remnants—ranging from bent cylinders and burnt gears to crushed sheet metal—do not stay abandoned for long. Scavengers and merchants, most notably the opportunistic dwarf Kravel Koalbeard, hire passing adventurers to comb the blinding white expanse and collect the debris. Because both racing teams are perpetually desperate for spare machinery to patch together their next prototype, scavenged wreckage can easily be resold directly back to the very teams that wrecked it.

Rocket Car Parts. Rocket Car Parts is an errand undertaken for the opportunistic dwarf merchant Kravel Koalbeard on the blinding salt pans of the Shimmering Flats. Rather than letting the violently scattered debris of high-speed racer crashes go to waste, Koalbeard pays wanderers to comb the desert floor and recover wrecked mechanisms to resell directly to the rival gnome and goblin pit crews. The Shimmering Flats serve as the proving ground for the fierce technological rivalry between goblin and gnomish engineers. High-velocity experimental rocket cars routinely suffer catastrophic malfunctions, leaving twisted gears, cylinders, and jagged sheets of metal scattered wide across the vast white desert. While the pit crews focus solely on building and tuning the next machine, the desert floor has quietly become a scrap yard of experimental engineering.

Rocktusk Farm. Swine feed Orgrimmar from Rocktusk Farm, just beyond the city gates in northern Durotar. The farm supplies meat and provisions to the capital, where dry, stony ground makes crops hard to grow. Rocktusk Farm raises hardy swine on Durotar’s dry, stony ground. Crops are difficult to grow here, so the farm helps feed Orgrimmar’s growing population. Close to the capital’s fortified perimeter, it is safer than homesteads in the wild red canyonlands.

Rod of Channeling. In the Wetlands, the Rod of Channeling is carried by Dragonmaw spellcasters. Warlocks seeking to summon a felhunter gather three for Strahad Farsan's acolytes to steady the ritual circle in Ratchet. Warlocks need more than willpower to bind a volatile felhunter. Strahad Farsan asks for three matched rods so his acolytes can channel magic together and steady the summoning circle while the warlock binds the beast. Dragonmaw darkcasters carry these rods for their own workings. Bonewarders and shadowwarders bear them at Angerfang Encampment and in the surrounding Wetlands ruins. Combat leaves the rods worn and nicked, but they still focus chaotic nether energy.

Roetten Stonehammer. Roetten Stonehammer is an enterprising dwarf found wandering the Library in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Representing the interests of Reclaimers Inc., he organizes expeditions and recruits adventurers to handle salvage operations in distant lands like Desolace. Amid the ancient tomes and dust of the Hall of Explorers' Library, Roetten Stonehammer keeps his eye on matters of practical recovery. Operating on behalf of Reclaimers Inc., Roetten connects daring mercenaries with lucrative salvage contracts across Kalimdor. Rather than digging purely for historical curiosity, his associates look to reclaim valuable cargo, wreckage, and rare reagents from perilous frontiers like the rugged wastes of Desolace.

Rogue. Rogues are masters of stealth, espionage, and sudden, lethal combat who dictate the terms of engagement from the shadows. Relying on light leather armor, dual-wielded blades, and brewed toxins, they strike unawares before vanishing back into the dark. Across Azeroth, they serve as scouts, assassins, pickpockets, and agents for factions and hidden syndicates alike. Rogues eschew the heavy plate and open confrontation of traditional frontline warriors. Clad in lightweight leather to remain completely silent and mobile, they stalk their quarry unseen. When they engage, they seize the opening moments through precision and surprise, aiming for vital organs or exposed joints. Utilizing an ever-flowing pool of energy and rapid weapon combinations, a rogue softens up an enemy with carefully chained strikes before unleashing a catastrophic finishing blow.

Roguefeather Den. Roguefeather Den is a cavern nestled in the south-central reaches of Thousand Needles. Infested with ferocious screeching harpies, the cave serves as a fortified roost where the flock hoards scavenged provisions deep within its shadowed recesses. Carved into the sheer sandstone bluffs of southern Thousand Needles, Roguefeather Den is the foul nesting ground of local harpies. Known for their feral screeching and aggressive territorialism, the harpies treat the cavern as both a secure haven and a storehouse, vigilantly guarding the gathered food and stolen supplies they pile in the dark recesses at the back of the cave.

Rogues' Quarter. The Rogues' Quarter is a dimly lit district in the southeastern wing of the Undercity. It serves as the staging ground for the Forsaken's scouts, assassins, and underworld operatives, along with the craftsmen who support them. Tucked away in the southeastern quadrant of the subterranean city, the Rogues' Quarter gathers the Forsaken's most cunning and lethal survivors. In life, many were thieves, cutpurses, or silent blades for the Kingdom of Lordaeron; in death, their expertise in stealth, poisons, and misdirection has been repurposed to protect the fledgling nation from the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. The district hums with quiet activity, offering a covert haven where operatives sharpen their daggers, brew deadly toxins, and hone clandestine skills.

Roland's Doom. Roland's Doom is an abandoned, shadow-drenched mine tucked into the southeastern hills of Duskwood, just east of the Rotting Orchard. Once an ordinary delve, it has become infamous as a dangerous den overrun by savage worgen. Cut into the ridges east of the Rotting Orchard, Roland's Doom long ago ceased to be a functioning mine. Instead, it serves as a violent staging ground for the Nightbane worgen pack, led by beasts such as Gutspill and Nefaru. The dark tunnels echo with guttural snarls and the reek of damp earth and blood, making it one of the most perilous corners in all of Duskwood for unwary travelers.

Rolling Plains. The Rolling Plains span the southern expanse of Mulgore, stretching between Bloodhoof Village and the border of the Barrens. These windswept grasslands are home to thriving herds of wildlife, but they are also a point of perpetual vigilance due to prowling centaur raiders and aggressive harpies. Spanning south from Bloodhoof Village toward the natural earthen gates leading into the Barrens, the Rolling Plains embody the vast open ranges of the tauren homeland. The area teems with wild game essential to the tribes, including prairie wolves, kodo herds, flatland cougars, and swift tallstriders. For young hunters proving their worth to the elders, these sweeping savannahs serve as an indispensable proving ground where tracking, patience, and reverence for nature are put to the test.

Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian the Dayseeker is an elder Skyborne figure situated in Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. He oversees the initiation of young fledglings as they discover their calling, step into maturity, and attune themselves to the natural elements of their homeland. Under his watchful guidance, newcomers learn the fundamentals of survival, tradition, and service to their community. Within the serene confines of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker stands as one of the primary mentors for the fledgling Skyborne. Revered for his experience and calm wisdom, Rorian directs youth during their crucial transition into adulthood. It is under his instruction that initiates undertake their traditional rite of passage, marking their readiness to defend and support their island home.

Rot Blossom. Rot Blossoms are foul, necrotic flora found growing among the desecrated graves of Duskwood. Fed by the blighted soil and undead remains, they are sought after for their potent, unwholesome alchemical properties. Duskwood's unnatural corruption breeds bizarre and disturbing plant life, none more unsettling than the Rot Blossom. Rooted in the defiled earth of graveyards such as the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, these morbid blooms thrive in proximity to death. Local rumors claim they can even take root within the cracked skulls of the walking dead, particularly Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends that stalk the barrows. To the locals in Darkshire, harvesting them is both a grim chore and a dangerous necessity, as disturbing their soil means braving the unrested dead.

Rot Hide Clues. Investigating a barge loaded with corpses on Lordamere Lake reveals an engraved ring on a recently deceased woman's hand. Reporting the grim discovery to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher exposes a disturbing operation: Rot Hide gnolls are robbing Tirisfal's mass graves and shipping bodies to Fenris Isle. While examining an abandoned, corpse-laden ferry on the shores of Lake Lordamere, Forsaken scouts discover that not all the dead are ancient remains. Protruding from the pile of carrion is the unwrapped, plague-marked hand of a recently slain woman wearing a simple band inscribed with the words 'For Deliah'. The boat itself points to coordinated logistics rather than senseless scavenger feeding.

Rot Hide Ichor. Rot Hide Ichor is a foul bodily fluid harvested from the undead Rot Hide gnolls infesting Fenris Isle in Lordamere Lake. Apothecary Renferrel collects samples of the substance at the Sepulcher to uncover the origin of the gnolls' corruption and devise a strategy against them. The Rot Hide gnolls of Fenris Isle are not ordinary wild beasts; they are visibly decomposed and twisted by unnatural blight. Rather than normal blood, their veins pump a noxious ichor that sustains their animated flesh. The Royal Apothecary Society suspects that this fluid holds the secret to how the pack was corrupted and who commands them from within the ruined keep of Fenris Isle.

Rot Hide Ichor. Rot Hide Ichor is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest assigned by High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Seeking to understand the unnatural Rot Hide gnolls infesting Fenris Isle before launching an assault, Forsaken leadership tasks adventurers with extracting the foul, mysterious fluid circulating through the creatures' veins for study. The Rot Hide gnolls of Silverpine Forest are far from typical wild humanoids. Decaying, aggressive, and reeking of blight, they occupy strategic positions like Fenris Isle across Lordamere Lake. High Executor Hadrec recognizes that their unnatural resilience stems from whatever strange fluid flows within them, requiring hard specimens before committing soldiers to a costly assault.

Rot Hide Origins. "Rot Hide Origins" is a Forsaken quest bridging the research of the Royal Apothecary Society in the Silverpine forest with the sorcerous expertise of the Undercity. After analyzing putrid fluids taken from gnolls, Apothecary Renferrel sends an adventurer to consult Bethor Iceshard to uncover the magical lineage behind these rotting beasts. While examining the fluid harvested from the rot hide gnolls infesting Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel manages to reduce the foul substance into its basic elements. His preliminary chemical distillation reveals something far stranger than ordinary gnoll disease: the ichor carries the unmistakable dual signature of necromancy and warlock arts. Realizing pure alchemy cannot unravel the full scope of the sorcery at play, Renferrel tasks an agent with taking a prepared sample directly to the capital for esoteric scrutiny.

Rotting Orchard. The Rotting Orchard is a blighted, abandoned fruit grove situated in southern Duskwood. Once a source of harvest for the nearby settlement of Darkshire, it has fallen into ruin and is now overrun by ravenous lupine predators known as the Nightbane pack. Located east of the ruined Yorgen Farmstead and west of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, the Rotting Orchard stands as a grim testament to Duskwood's decline. The trees hang heavy with withered, spoiled fruit, while dilapidated barns and outbuildings have been converted into rough encampments by the Nightbane worgen. Nightbane Stalkers prowl the twisted brush, while dark casters known as Shadow Weavers weave their sinister magic amid the decaying timber. The pack answers to the fierce worgen Gutspill and Nefaru, who lair in the nearby mine of Roland's Doom.

Rough Quartz. In Durotar, a Rough Quartz comes from a Minor Manifestation of Earth. A shaman brings the stone to an elder, who binds it into the first Earth Totem. Rough Quartz is a gift from a Minor Manifestation of Earth to a shaman who communes with the spirits in Durotar or Mulgore. To the untrained eye, it looks like an ordinary desert pebble. The stone represents endurance, patience, and unwavering strength. At the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller binds it into carved wood to make an Earth Totem. The quartz becomes the spiritual focus joining a young shaman to Azeroth's living soil.

Rough Wolf Pelts. Rough Wolf Pelts is an introductory skinning quest in Elwynn Forest offered by Helene Peltskinner near Goldshire. With her husband away assisting near Northshire Abbey, Helene relies on capable skinners to harvest raw hides from local wolves to complete her pending leatherworking orders. Just outside Goldshire, Helene Peltskinner works diligently to supply travelers and residents with cured leather and furs. While her husband typically hunts the prowling timber wolves of Elwynn Forest to keep her workshop supplied, duties near Northshire Abbey have taken him away from the workbench. Left with a backlog of customer orders to finish, Helene enlists the aid of passing apprentices willing to turn their skinning knives toward the local wildlife.

Royal Apothecary Society. The Royal Apothecary Society is an alchemical guild established under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and based in the Apothecarium beneath the Undercity. Composed of Forsaken researchers, its primary mission is compounding a lethal New Plague capable of eradicating the Scourge while claiming vengeance against the living. While Horde allies believe the society seeks a cure for undeath, its researchers actively harvest venoms, slimes, and toxic reagents across Azeroth to perfect weapons of mass destruction. Founded in the wake of the Forsaken's liberation, the Royal Apothecary Society serves as the scientific and alchemical arm of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. From their vats and subterranean laboratories in the Apothecarium, researchers seek to weaponize the very force that damned them. Their preeminent endeavor is the creation of a 'New Plague'—a concoction intended to eradicate the Scourge and destroy the Lich King. Unlike traditional human alchemy, which prioritizes elixirs of healing or transmutation, the Society experiments ruthlessly with foul pathogens, caustic acids, and necromantic blends, raising fallen warhorses as skeletal steeds and brewing deadlier strains of toxic blight.

Royal Gallery. Stormwind Keep's Royal Gallery honors figures from the kingdom's history and the Grand Alliance. Past the courtyard garden, its statues and works of art fill a quiet hall of remembrance. The Royal Gallery lies beyond Stormwind Keep's interior garden, beside the Royal Library. Its statues honor King Llane Wrynn, the fallen ruler of Stormwind; Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras; and Lady Mara Fordragon, patron of the refugees who fled to Lordaeron after the First War. Courtly visitors such as Lady Dena Kennedy come to this quiet hall, where the kingdom's noble heritage is remembered.
