text.enUS: The Only Cure is More Green Glow. Following earlier inconclusive tests on surface troggs, Ozzie Togglevolt tasks adventurers with retrieving pure, high-potency radioactive fallout directly from inside Gnomeregan. His ultimate goal is to understand the toxic radiation that devastated his people and concoct a cure for the afflicted leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt's preliminary trials outside the city were a failure. The irradiated troggs roaming Dun Morogh carried insufficient and impure residue, leaving his lab in Kharanos with more questions than answers. To engineer a true remedy for leper gnomes, Togglevolt concludes that scientific integrity demands a fresh, concentrated sample directly from deep within the city's toxic belly.

The Orb of Soran'ruk. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan sets warlocks to gather the scattered pieces of Soran'ruk. They seek to rebuild an orb that holds a disgraced demon's essence. Failure within the Burning Legion brings an eternal sentence. When lesser demons lose favor with their masters, their spirits are bound inside crystal orbs. The Legion gives these prisons to mortal conjurers and warlocks as vessels for power under demonic control. Shattering an orb does not free its captive; even the shards hold potent magic.

The Orc Report. Sifting through loose dirt in Dustwallow Marsh, you come upon an orc's severed hand clutching a tube carved from bone. Inside lies a dirt-stained parchment in Orcish script, which looks important. It is meant for a Theramore Lieutenant. In the loose dirt lies an orc's severed hand, gripping a tube carved from bone. Inside is a parchment stained with dirt and the writing is Orcish, which seems significant. A Theramore Lieutenant is the one to show it to.

The People's Militia. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle tests your mettle for the People's Militia. Stormwind's throne is distracted, and its army is absent, so local volunteers defend Westfall from the Defias Brotherhood. You begin by driving outlaws from the northern fields and mines. Westfall once fed Stormwind, but outlaws, vagrants, and thieves now overrun the region. With the capital sending no royal soldiers to patrol the countryside, Gryan Stoutmantle organized the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill as a local defense force. He calls for decisive action to reclaim Westfall. Anyone seeking the militia's badge must prove they can fight and will protect innocent settlers.

The People's Militia. Across Westfall, The People's Militia faces a growing Defias threat. Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteers now confront thieves who have moved beyond highway robbery to ransack Moonbrook and the Gold Coast Quarry, and the Militia calls for harsher retaliation. Defias attacks have grown from petty banditry on the roads into a wider threat. Defias Looters and Pillagers, who hurl fire, have overrun Westfall's economic centers. They occupy Moonbrook, strip the Alexston Farmstead, and have taken control of the Gold Coast Quarry. Gryan Stoutmantle sees the danger: if the brigands hold these places, Westfall may become impossible to reclaim without a formal royal army.

The People's Militia. This task marks the culmination of Gryan Stoutmantle's campaign to clear Westfall's roads and farmlands of the Defias Brotherhood. By hunting down the seasoned brigands entrenched in the southern Dagger Hills, volunteers prove their dedication and earn full induction into Sentinel Hill's People's Militia. The northern farmlands of Westfall have suffered greatly under the Defias Brotherhood, but the outlaws who escaped Stoutmantle's early sweeps retreated south into the rocky crags of the Dagger Hills. Operating out of the rugged terrain, Defias Highwaymen, Pathstalkers, and Knuckledusters have continued to raid rural homesteads and intercept travelers. To break their hold over the southern half of the region, the People's Militia sends hardened recruits into the hills to dismantle these raiding bands directly.

The Perenolde Tiara. Count Remington Ridgewell seeks a lost heirloom in the Ruins of Alterac. The Stormwind aristocrat sends mercenaries north to recover the Perenolde Tiara, once owned by Alterac's royal family and now said to be held by an ogre mage. Alterac's royal family wore an emerald-set tiara crafted by master dwarven jewelers in Ironforge. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Grand Alliance and joined the Orcish Horde. His betrayal led to Alterac's conquest and collapse. In the fall of Alterac City, many treasures of the royal family vanished among the snowy rubble of the Alterac Mountains.

The Perfect Stout. Rejold Barleybrew of Brewnall Village is determined to craft the ultimate dwarven stout, combining family brewing tradition with exotic local ingredients. To perfect his experimental recipe, he seeks shimmerweed, a pungent plant cultivated exclusively by the hostile Frostmane trolls atop Shimmer Ridge. Daring travelers are sent into the troll encampment to lift the herb straight from tribal baskets. In Brewnall Village, brewing is more than a trade—it is a way of life, especially for the Barleybrew family. Rejold Barleybrew believes that brewing greatness is in his blood, but achieving the legendary 'perfect stout' demands unconventional innovation. Rather than relying solely on standard hops, malt, and mountain spring water, Rejold looks toward the untamed flora of Dun Morogh to give his ale an unmistakable bite.

The Power to Destroy.... In the Undercity, Varimathras sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner wants two dark tomes held by the Searing Blade cult, hoping their power will aid her war against the Scourge and the Lich King. Thrall's orcs are hunting the Searing Blade cult beneath their capital, while the Forsaken covet the cult's occult stores. On Sylvanas Windrunner's orders, Varimathras sends operatives into Ragefire Chasm to seize two demonic grimoires: Spells of Shadow and Incantations from the Nether. The Dark Lady believes disciplined Forsaken will can put these demonic gifts to better use than the lesser cultists.

The Price of Shoes. Verner Osgood, the smith in Lakeshire, has depleted his supply of iron patching together equipment for the beleaguered town guard. With no metal left to shoe the local horses, he sends a courier across Elwynn Forest to enlist help from Smith Argus in Goldshire. Lakeshire sits directly in the crosshairs of gnolls, orcs, and murlocs, yet Stormwind offers precious little reinforcement. The local garrison has to fight daily to keep the township from falling, and that relentless combat wears gear down quickly. Verner Osgood spends nearly every waking hour repairing dented breastplates, reshaping dulled swords, and keeping the town guards clad in iron, exhausting his raw materials in the process.

The Princess Trapped. The Princess Trapped begins when adventurers uncover an iridescent crystal shard in the Arathi Highlands and hear the plea of Myzrael, a self-styled princess of the earth imprisoned deep underground. Claiming she was trapped by hostile giants, she begs travelers to confront their kobold allies in Drywhisker Gorge and restore power to her crystalline communication network. Scattered across the rolling plains of the Arathi Highlands, strange crystal shards hum with distant power. Approaching them reveals a desperate voice echoing from deep subterranean caverns: Myzrael, a self-proclaimed princess of the earth. She claims that ancient giants cast her down and bound her far beneath the soil, cutting her off from the sunlit lands above. The crystals embedded in the earth represent her sole means of contacting the surface, carrying her pleas for salvation to any adventurer willing to listen.

The Principal Source. At Cliffspring Falls, a sickness among Darkshore's deer draws the Cenarion Circle's attention to the water. Dendrite Starblaze sends young druids from Moonglade to collect a sample for Auberdine naturalist Alanndarian Nightsong. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore with fresh water. When deer began to sicken with a lingering malady, the Cenarion Circle looked to the river for its cause. Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade suspects the water source is tainted and sends novice druids to gather a sample at the cavern mouth beneath the falls.

The Principal Source. Dendrite Starblaze sends Horde druids to Dreadmist Peak for a water sample. From Moonglade, she asks them to bring it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads, where it can help explain the poison harming wildlife. Dreadmist Peak rises northwest of the Crossroads, with springs and pools high above the dry northern Barrens. Their waters shape local weather and moisture. The Burning Blade, a cult devoted to demons, has taken hold on the crags. Dendrite Starblaze fears their foul sorcery may taint the basin around this important mountain.

The Problem With Prideclaws. The Problem With Prideclaws addresses the encroaching threat of wild prideclaw predators in the Shen'dar Highlands. As local settlements already grapple with bandits and cultists, culling the encroaching beasts protects vulnerable villagers while yielding useful pelts for the community. The hills surrounding the Shen'dar Highlands are fraught with peril, pressed not only by roving bandits and unhinged cultists but also by an encroaching population of prideclaws. These fierce beasts have begun pressing inward toward the village perimeter, growing bolder as their territory expands and creating an imminent hazard for the local inhabitants.

The Prodigal Lich. Following your service in Brill against Scourge remnants and rot hide gnolls, Magistrate Sevren directs you south to the Undercity. Bethor Iceshard, a prominent archmage in the Magic Quarter, requires a capable operative for a sensitive mission regarding a wayward lich. Having proven your capability in the ruined town of Brill, Magistrate Sevren deems you worthy of higher-level Forsaken endeavors. Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage dwelling in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, has demanded an agent tested in combat against the Scourge. Sevren hands over official orders, dispatching you beneath the ruins of Lordaeron into the subterranean corridors of the Forsaken capital.

name.frFR: Le retour de la liche prodigue

text.enUS: The Prodigal Lich Returns. The Prodigal Lich Returns marks the conclusion of the effort to recruit Gunther Arcanus into the Forsaken. Having proven your intentions and restored his grimoire, you carry an arcane communion gem back to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Gunther Arcanus spent years isolated on an island in Brightwater Lake, having broken free from the Lich King's grip through sheer force of will, completely unaware that Sylvanas Windrunner had liberated Lordaeron. Bitter and suspicious of outsiders, Gunther distrusted the emissaries of the Undercity until an adventurer returned his spellbook and proved their hostility toward the Scourge. Satisfied that his visitor was not an enemy, Gunther entrusted them with a Nether Gem to establish contact with his former colleague.

The Public Servant. Senator Mehr Stonehallow of Ironforge has traveled directly to Gol'Bolar Quarry to address the sudden trogg invasion threatening Dun Morogh's mining operations. Seeking to reclaim the site, he enlists adventurers to cut down the aggressive Rockjaw Bonesnappers so miners can return to work. It is rare to find a member of Ironforge's Senate standing in the slush and dirt of a contested mine, but Senator Mehr Stonehallow is no typical politician. Holding dual allegiance to the dwarven ruling body and the scholarly Explorers' League, Stonehallow has taken personal responsibility for organizing a response to the trogg infestation at Gol'Bolar Quarry. Rather than waiting for slow legislative measures, he directly contracts capable mercenaries and travelers to cull the invaders.

The Ravaged Caravan. Morin Cloudstalker directs travelers to examine the wreckage of an ambushed Venture Company caravan near the northern shore of Stonebull Lake. Although the tauren torched the convoy in retribution for lost comrades, goblin salvagers returned to recover intact cargo. Investigating the surviving supply crates reveals the true industrial scale of the Venture Company's operations in Mulgore. The charred remnants along the northern bank of Stonebull Lake are the result of a swift strike by the tauren. Grieving the loss of two companions killed in an earlier skirmish, Morin Cloudstalker and his warriors ambushed an armed Venture Company supply convoy. Intending to obliterate the intruders' efforts, the tauren torched the wagons and abandoned the smoking ruin, presuming fire would consume whatever the goblins sought to haul.

The Ravaged Caravan. Investigating a broken transport in Mulgore reveals that goblin industrialists have established an illegal foothold in tauren territory. By recovering documents from a sealed crate, scouts confirm the Venture Company is systematically stripping the land's mineral wealth. This discovery rallies the Bloodhoof Outrunners to mount an active defense of their ancestral plains. The wreckage of a ravaged caravan east of Bloodhoof Village tells an unsettling story. Within a sealed supply crate lies a dense cache of mined ore and minerals alongside a bound sheaf of Venture Company documents. This paperwork provides irrefutable proof that the greedy Venture Company has begun an unpermitted mining operation deep in the tranquil valleys of Mulgore.

The Real Threat. Following Call to Arms, Korin Fel tells you that her husband is unaware of why Hammerfall is under attack, and asks you to slay the ogre Or'Kalar and bring her his head. Korin Fel says you serve her husband well, yet he has no idea why Hammerfall is being attacked. The cause is Or'Kalar, Mug'thol's pawn in Stromgarde, who hates her husband for defeating him years ago and wants him dead. Her auguries tell her the ogre has set a trap for him.

The Red Crystal. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea asks travelers in Auberdine to investigate a red crystal in Darkshore's eastern mountains. Hostile moonkin are multiplying nearby and seem drawn to it, and the Sentinels need to know if the formation is real. Moonkin were long seen as gentle, mystical creatures bound to the wilds of Kalimdor. Now aggressive packs are multiplying along the slopes east of Auberdine. Some night elves still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea puts the town's safety first as the danger grows. Reports place the beasts at a single spot among the eastern peaks.

The Red Messenger. Executor Arren tasks newly risen Forsaken with intercepting a courier dispatched from the Scarlet Monastery to the crusade camp outside Deathknell. Intercepting the messenger secures critical intelligence on local Scarlet movements before the zealots can solidify their presence in the valley. This mission marks one of the earliest offensive operations undertaken to secure the Forsaken's fledgling sanctuary. Word travels quickly through Tirisfal Glades, even among the dead. Superiors in Brill alerted Executor Arren that the Scarlet Crusade sent an emissary from their stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery westward into Deathknell. While the Crusaders maintain an aggressive presence across Lordaeron, dispatching a courier directly to the edge of the Forsaken's waking grounds indicates an organized push to eradicate newly risen undead before they can muster an organized defense.

The Relics of Wakening. At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, an urgent effort is underway to save the sleeping Druids of the Talon. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the sacred mounds, threatening the druids whose spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Four ritual relics are needed to bring the sleepers safely back to the waking world. West of Dolanaar, a swarm of corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs has overrun the winding corridors of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Barrow dens are secluded sanctuaries where night elf druids hibernate while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. A foul taint spreading across Teldrassil has driven these former allies mad. They have desecrated the sanctum, leaving the sleepers unaware that danger threatens their physical bodies.

The Reports. Carry Senir Whitebeard's report on the Frostmane trolls from Kharanos to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Senir warns that the senator is sour and asks you not to mention who helped gather the information. After daring reconnaissance deep inside Frostmane Hold, Senir Whitebeard drafts an urgent report detailing the growing troll threat facing Dun Morogh. Stationed out of Kharanos, the mountaineer needs a courier to deliver these intelligence findings directly to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Eager to preserve his own reputation in the eyes of the government, Whitebeard cheerfully advises his runner not to mention who actually did the hazardous legwork out in the snowy crags.

The Rescue. The Rescue is an early Horde quest initiated by Krusk in Tarren Mill, tasking heroes with infiltrating Durnholde Keep to liberate captured orc scouts. Thrall's scouts were ambushed after being sent to retrieve an object from Durnholde, leaving them captive to the ruthless human criminals of the Syndicate. Warchief Thrall sent a select detachment of orc warriors to the Hillsbrad Foothills with orders to quietly investigate the rising Syndicate threat and retrieve an object from Durnholde Keep. Under the leadership of Gol'dir, the scouting party approached the fortress ruins. However, the Syndicate's sheer numbers overwhelmed them in an ambush. While the warrior Krusk managed to break free and limp back across the river to Tarren Mill, his companions Drull, Tog'thar, and Gol'dir were taken alive into human chains.

The Restless Dead. The Restless Dead addresses an alarming disturbance within the crypts of the Hall of Thanes, where ancient dwarven spirits have been roused from their rest. With the caretakers terrified to enter the vaults, an adventurer must descend into the catacombs to put the angry phantoms and the spirit of Anvilmar back to sleep. Deep beneath the surface in the Hall of Thanes, ancestral crypts hold generations of honored dead. Normally resting in quiet slumber, the spirits have been violently agitated by an unseen disturbance in the vaults. Strange noises echoing up from below have spooked the site's caretakers, who refuse to enter the lower chambers to perform their duties until order is restored. Adventurers are called upon to descend into the shadowed stone halls and quiet the agitated souls.

The Rethban Gauntlet. The Rethban Gauntlet is an eccentric endurance trial devised by the dwarven brewer Yorus Barleybrew in Lakeshire. Challengers must drink a potent swig of his family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder and sprint north into the gnoll-infested Rethban Caverns and back before an hour elapses. In the town of Lakeshire, where grim talk of gnoll raids and missing town guards usually dominates the inn, the dwarf Yorus Barleybrew brings a distinctly dwarven flavor of entertainment. His self-styled challenge, the Rethban Gauntlet, tests an adventurer's mettle, speed, and liver all at once. Participants are required to down a draught of his family's signature concoction, Barleybrew Scalder, right before setting off on foot toward the northern foothills.

The Rise of the Machines. Hierophant Theodora Mulvadania has found initials and a rank marking on the elemental shards, and the machines you brought down in the Burning Steppes bore Rank IV. Theodora sends you with a shard sample to Lotwil Veriatus, a scholar of elemental sciences, in a camp to the east. The shards carry the initials G.L.A., with a rank marking beneath them. The machines you brought down in the Burning Steppes bore Rank IV, which Theodora assumes is a lowly rank. Theodora wants you to bring a sample shard to Lotwil Veriatus, renowned among scholars of elemental sciences. Lotwil is stationed at a camp to the east, and Theodora hopes Lotwil can help the search.

The Road to Darnassus. Along Teldrassil’s western road, corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs threaten the route from Dolanaar to Darnassus. Moon Priestess Amara coordinates scouts and travelers to keep this trade and messenger road clear of ambushes. You travel west from Dolanaar toward Darnassus on Teldrassil’s main overland road. Trade goods, political messages, and travelers use it each day to stay connected with the capital and the boughs of the great tree. Teldrassil is young and wild, so safe roads matter to its kaldorei communities.

The Ruins of Solarsal. Shandris Feathermoon tells you that the Ruins of Solarsal, to the south, are now crowded with Hatecrest naga. You are sent to walk through the ruins and notice whatever seems out of the ordinary. The Ruins of Solarsal far pre-date modern times. Shandris says they explored the place at first, found nothing of note and left it alone. Very recently, though, Hatecrest naga have taken it over in alarming numbers. At first that looked like the prelude to an attack, a threat that is still possible, but Shandris believes something else may be going on. You are to walk through the ruins and notice whatever seems out of the ordinary.

The Ruins of Stardust. Pelturas Whitemoon's desperate quest to heal his daughter Relara continues in Astranaar. While the sacred stone Elune's Tear calmed her terrifying nightmares, a fierce fever still grips her. Guided by Orendil Broadleaf's botanical knowledge, adventurers journey south to harvest a cooling, luminescent dust settled among ancient night elven stones. Pelturas Whitemoon has spent sleepless nights by the bedside of his daughter, Relara, watching a malignant affliction burn through her. Though offering an Elune's Tear provided a temporary respite from the tormenting dreams that plagued her thoughts, the illness remains deeply rooted. Her body is racked by an intense fever that mundane medicines have failed to quench. With the temple healers pushed to their limits, Pelturas turns once more to ancient, nature-infused remedies to preserve his daughter's life.

The Rumormonger. Having done a service for the gnomes, Kravel Koalbeard now wants to do the goblins a favor. He has heard that Nazz Steamboil, the goblin racer pilot, once went by another name, and wonders whether it is a secret worth money. He sends you to Krazek of Booty Bay, who would know. Kravel Koalbeard says the goblins are next in line for a favor. Nazz Steamboil, the goblin racer pilot, once went by another name, he hears, and Kravel wonders why it changed, whether it hides a secret, and whether Nazz cares to keep it hidden. The one who would know the truth, Kravel says, is Krazek, down at the southern tip of Stranglethorn in Booty Bay. Useful information might turn a profit. Look for Krazek at the Salty Sailor Tavern.

The Runed Scroll. A silvery ribbon marks the Runed Scroll found in Kalimdor's wilds as a formal message from across the border. Finding it sends Horde scouts to the Mor'shan Rampart to warn its guards of activity to the north. A fine silvery ribbon binds the scroll, unlike the rough leathers and parchment common in the Barrens. Its craft and script point to the night elves beneath Ashenvale's canopies to the north. With every ridge and road contested, a message taken from the enemy could matter greatly to the Horde's front lines.

The Sacred Flame. The Sacred Flame is a Horde task initiated by Zangen Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff. Seeking to recover an ancient relic guarded by the Galak centaur in Thousand Needles, Zangen sends adventurers deep into Ashenvale to acquire a sacred moonwell phial from the local dryads. The Galak tribe of centaur inhabiting the canyon floor of Thousand Needles fiercely protects an artifact dating back to the creation of their race. To pierce their defenses and extinguish their sacred flames, Zangen Stonehoof requires water touched by lunar divinity, drawing the tauren's gaze northward to the ancestral forests of Ashenvale.

The Sacred Flame. Following a perilous excursion to an Ashenvale moonwell, a phial of sanctified waters must be ferried south to Freewind Post. The tauren mystic Rau Cliffrunner needs this lunar essence to breach an eternal flame warding an ancient centaur relic in Thousand Needles. Zangen Stonehoof's mission demands swift transit through central Kalimdor. With the etched phial brimmed with purified moonwell water, you are instructed to cross the sun-baked expanse of the Barrens, descend the towering Great Lift, and reach the high mesa settlement of Freewind Post. Waiting perched above the canyon floor is Rau Cliffrunner, who monitors the brazen centaur clans below.

The Sacred Flame. The Sacred Flame is the final task in Rau Cliffrunner's investigation into the Galak centaur of Thousand Needles. Armed with blessed waters, a Horde adventurer must penetrate Splithoof Hold, extinguish the tribe's revered brazier, and claim the ancient Cloven Hoof relic. North of Freewind Post lies Splithoof Crag, the heart of the Galak centaur domain in Thousand Needles. Deep within its cavernous den, Splithoof Hold, burns a fire that the centaur hold sacred. After preparing an etched phial filled with purified water, Rau Cliffrunner tasks his allies with penetrating the subterranean stronghold, using the water to momentarily quench the flame, and snatching the prize guarded within: a relic known as the Cloven Hoof.

The Scarlet Crusade. This early mission from Executor Arren tasks newly awakened Forsaken with ambushing a nearby camp of Scarlet Crusade zealots southeast of Deathknell. It serves as a grim introduction to one of the Forsaken's most fanatical and persistent enemies. Once the immediate peril of the Night Web spider infestation is handled, Executor Arren turns Deathknell's attention toward an encroaching threat. A detachment of the Scarlet Crusade has established a foothold just southeast of the settlement. These zealots refuse to acknowledge any distinction between mindless Scourge minions and free-willed Forsaken, meaning their presence on the border poses an existential threat to the newly risen dead.

The Scrimshank Redemption. In Gadgetzan, Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser is troubled: Junior Surveyor Scrimshank, a top assistant sent into the Gaping Chasm, an area of desert southeast of town, has gone missing. You are asked to find out what became of Scrimshank, or at the least to find the surveying equipment. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser is troubled. Junior Surveyor Scrimshank went into the Gaping Chasm and has not been seen since, and the last report from there spoke of more of those weird bugs. Fizzledowser wonders whether the bugs now hold two big regions of the desert at once. You are asked to go in and search for Scrimshank, or failing that, for the surveying equipment, which Fizzledowser fears may be all that is left.

The Scythe of Elune. The Scythe of Elune is an Alliance investigation bridging an ancient night elf relic in Kalimdor with the sudden worgen infestation plaguing Duskwood. Sent by Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, adventurers delve into the haunted depths of Roland's Doom to uncover what brought these ravenous beasts to the Eastern Kingdoms. After tracing the enigmatic Priestess Velinde Starsong across Kalimdor and speaking with the Carevin household in Darkshire, travelers find common cause with Jonathan Carevin. The Nightbane worgen have overrun southern Duskwood, pushing out miners and threatening what little remains of the township. Although Carevin does not fully grasp the supernatural origin of these beasts, he recognizes the value of someone willing to root them out, pointing searchers toward Roland's Doom—the very mine where the fiends were first sighted.

The Second Rebellion. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks help against the overwhelming forces of Colonel Kurzen. Outnumbered ten to one by a cunning tactician, the rebels must rely on swift, covert strikes to survive. Cutting down Kurzen's jungle fighters is the first step toward relieving the relentless pressure on their refuge. The soldiers at the Rebel Camp face dire odds against Colonel Kurzen. Yohwa explains that the Colonel is a brilliant military tactician whose force outnumbers the rebellion by at least ten to one. Unable to wage an open war of attrition, the rebels have no choice but to adopt the Colonel's own covert tactics, launching quick incursions into his encampment to thin his ranks and escaping before heavy reinforcements can retaliate.

The Severed Head. Vigorous digging turns up the head of a male orc, ragged where it was cut from the neck. Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village is the one to bring it to. Digging hard in the loose dirt brings up an orc's head, a male's, ragged where it was cut from the neck. The lips are drawn in a snarl and the dark eyes glare defiantly. Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village is the one to bring it to.

The Shade of Elura. At Auberdine, Elura's shade guards a sunken ship and its Elunite ore. Elanaria sends young night elf warriors into the waters to lay the captain to rest and recover her medallion and ore for a weapon forged by Smith Mathiel. Long ago, a ship carrying rare Elunite ore struck jagged coastal rocks near the Auberdine lighthouse and sank. The captain, Elura, cursed her own soul in despair and out of unwavering duty. Bound to the wreck beneath the waves, her shade guards the lost cargo from anyone who would disturb it.

The Shadowy Figure. Haunted by the massacre of his family, the hermit Sven Yorgen tasks you with discovering the identity of a mysterious stranger seen lurking near his farm on that fateful night. Armed only with an enigmatic book recovered from the ruins, you must consult the residents of Darkshire to trace the stranger's footsteps. Sven Yorgen lives in hiding along the desolate hills of Duskwood, broken by the horrific butchery of his family. While he originally placed blame on the mysterious black riders terrorizing the woods, his memory remains tormented by another detail: a quiet, shadowy figure who was lurking nearby on the night of the massacre. Desperate for answers, Sven entrusts you with the only physical clue recovered from the wreckage—a strange book left behind at the ransacked farm.

name.esES: La búsqueda de la figura continúa

text.enUS: The Shadowy Search Continues. Following Madame Eva's divination, this investigation leads from her parlor to Clerk Daltry in Darkshire. It centers on tracing the origins of the journal recovered from the ruins of Sven Yorgen's ransacked farmstead. After examining the dirt-stained journal salvaged from the tragedy at Sven's farm, Madame Eva discerned that while its author was an outsider, the physical volume itself came from within Darkshire. Clerk Daltry frequently sells blank ledgers and tomes to traveling scholars, spellcasters, and record-keepers. By following the trail of local commerce, investigators seek a mundane paper trail to identify an otherwise elusive and sinister trespasser lurking in the gloomy groves of Duskwood.

The Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, Therzok tests rogues seeking a place in the Shattered Hand. He asks them to open Tazan's recovered satchel with a key taken from an unwitting accomplice. After retrieving Tazan's locked satchel, you find it useless without the key. The Shattered Hand demands skill, not brute force against the complex lock. Therzok sends you to Gamon, a tauren drunkard who frequents Orgrimmar's tavern. Gamon is easily distracted and once helped Tazan, making him a fitting mark for quiet theft.

The Shattered Hand. Therzok tests rogues in Orgrimmar who seek entry to the secretive Shattered Hand. Their trial sends them after Tazan, a troll smuggler, and his locked satchel. The Shattered Hand works from the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. The order of assassins and thieves follows old orcish traditions. Warchief Thrall rules the young Horde with honor, diplomacy, and caution, but the Shattered Hand's leaders believe restraint weakens their people. They seek to restore martial supremacy through covert violence, using knives and poison when a battlefield charge may fail.

name.esES: El saludo de los Mano Destrozada

text.enUS: The Shattered Salute. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul teaches a silent sign to new rogues. The Shattered Hand uses it to recognize its agents safely in the field. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the Shattered Hand works in secrecy as Thrall's Horde intelligence and assassination arm. Its agents cannot use banners or military signs on dangerous, secret assignments. Shenthul teaches newly inducted rogues the Shattered Salute, a silent gesture that lets allies recognize one another.

The Shieldsmith. In Stormwind, Yorus Barleybrew sends warriors back after a harrowing trial in the Redridge Mountains. He gives them a cask of Barleybrew Scalder to take to Furen Longbeard, who will fashion a stout shield. After you prove your mettle against the gnolls and perils of the Rethban Gauntlet, Yorus Barleybrew honors his bargain. The promised reward cannot be hammered out in Lakeshire, so he directs promising fighters back to Stormwind City. A dwarven armorer there stands ready to repay a personal debt.

The Shimmering Frond. Across Teldrassil, a curious plant shimmers among the roots and canopy. Travelers bring a cutting to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, hoping the botanist can explain its origin. In Teldrassil's boughs, a strange plant catches the light. Its fronds twist with a pulsing shimmer unlike the island's usual foliage. The glow draws the eye amid Teldrassil's young forest life.

The Singing Crystals. Kin'weelay seeks a way to rescue young Yenniku from the darkness that has claimed him. Following the revelation of Yenniku's plight, the witch doctor plans to locate a legendary jewel known as the Mind's Eye, sending you to gather resonance shards needed to master its power. After learning the grim fate that befell Yenniku, the medicine man Kin'weelay turns to ancient jungle lore for an answer. Tales speak of the Mind's Eye, a gem hidden within the depths of Stranglethorn that possesses immense magical strength. Kin'weelay believes this stone could hold the secret to freeing the young troll's spirit. While he communally seeks the guidance of the jungle spirits to pinpoint its location, he needs rare catalysts to safely command the jewel's potent sorcery.

The Sisterhood of Elune. The Sisterhood of Elune is an introductory quest directing adventurers to Darnassus to meet Sister Aquinne. Serving as the primary spiritual authority among the night elves, the Sisterhood requires swift outside aid to confront brewing challenges in their lands. "The Sisterhood of Elune" is a summons directing adventurers to seek out Sister Aquinne in the night elf capital of Darnassus. As representatives of Elune's faithful, the priestesses often dispatch calls for reliable champions to assist with urgent matters affecting their people and sacred lands.

The Slaughtered Lamb. This errand directs novice gnome warlocks out of Ironforge to seek advanced instruction in human lands. With King Magni Bronzebeard keeping a vigilant watch on dark practitioners within the dwarven mountain, mentors must rely on Stormwind's hidden networks to complete their disciples' training. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, aspiring warlocks in Khaz Modan studied under their own tinker-mages and demonic scholars deep within the techno-city. The disaster that drove the gnomes into exile scattered those institutions. The surviving practitioners found themselves cramped into Ironforge's gloomy, subterranean caverns, operating under the distrustful eye of King Magni Bronzebeard and the dwarven guard. Unable to practice demonic arts openly or cultivate dangerous rituals in such tight quarters, senior instructors like Lago Blackwrench have little choice but to send their students away.

The Sleeper Has Awakened. Kerlonian Evershade struggles to stay awake on the road from Darkshore to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Newly awakened from a long sleep, he carries the Horn of Awakening and needs help against furbolgs and cultists along the way. Kerlonian Evershade, a Druid of the Claw, has only recently awakened from sleep in the barrows. For millennia, the druids communed with wild spirits through the Emerald Dream. The Third War called them to wake, but centuries of hibernation leave Kerlonian struggling to stay conscious. He set out south from Darkshore to meet Liladris Moonriver in Ashenvale, yet exhaustion soon overtook him. Sudden naps leave him helpless along the wilds, so he depends on a brass Horn of Awakening and passing allies to keep moving.

The Sleeping Druid. Oben Rageclaw lies asleep in Ban'ethil Barrow Den, but his spirit is caught in the Emerald Dream. Gnarlpine shamans have drawn it from his body and set his flesh moving through the den. Night elf druids sleep in barrow dens across Kalimdor while their spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Their bodies rest in stone alcoves, safe through centuries of slumber. Teldrassil's corruption has driven the Gnarlpine furbolgs to desperate savagery. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans found a way to breach Oben Rageclaw's sacred rest and draw his living spirit from his sleeping body.

The Sparklematic 5200!. Deep within the ruins of Gnomeregan, the Sparklematic 5200 is an automated cleaning device that continues to function amidst the chaos. By feeding it a grime-encrusted object scavenged from the subterranean halls along with a nominal coin fee, adventurers can restore salvaged trinkets, gems, and scrap to pristine condition. It stands as a vibrant testament to the enduring ingenuity and eccentricity of gnomish engineering. Amidst the radioactive fallback and trogg infestation consuming Gnomeregan, a pocket of surviving gnomes maintains a secure perimeter near an extraordinary invention: the Sparklematic 5200. Built to scrub the harsh subterranean filth off salvaged valuables, this sturdy contraption promises to put the 'shine back in shine-tastic.' Even while subterranean monstrosities pound on the bulkheads, the machine sits ready for commercial operation.

The Sparklematic 5200!. Deep within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan sits the Sparklematic 5200, an automated cleaning contraption designed to scrub toxic filth from recovered salvaging. Operating the machine strips heavy grime from soiled objects and packages whatever is salvaged in a decorative gift box. Gnomish engineering often prizes efficiency and whimsy in equal measure. The Sparklematic 5200 was built to handle toxic and contaminated refuse, scouring away grime and caustic residue through automated cycles. Once loaded and paid, the contraption rattles through its cleaning routine before emitting a cheerful ding, neatly wrapping whatever remains into a present tied with a bow.

name.ptBR: Os espíritos das Torres de Pedra

text.enUS: The Spirits of Stonetalon. Unrest stirs among the spirits of Stonetalon, and Zor Lonetree sends Horde champions west to learn why. From Orgrimmar, they travel past the Crossroads and report directly to Seereth Stonebreak near Greatwood Vale. In Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree listens to the natural world and feels deep distress from the Stonetalon Mountains. The elemental spirits of its rocky peaks are furious as logging tears into their forests. Horde shamans hear that unrest and fear the devastation in the western highlands will upset Kalimdor's spiritual balance.

The Sprouted Fronds. At Denalan's garden by Lake Al'Ameth, the planted frond has taken root and sprouted. Travelers can see the new growth among the garden beds. You find Denalan's garden near Lake Al'Ameth, where the botanist studies Teldrassil's peculiar plants. After a shimmering frond is planted, new fronds rise from the soil in his planter, ready to be gathered and examined.

The Spy Revealed!. Inside Bookie Herod's strongbox lies a damp piece of parchment detailing the daily routines of Private Thorsen. Bearing only the initial M, this correspondence suggests an informant has embedded themselves among the rebels in northern Stranglethorn Vale. The muddy note is meant for Lieutenant Doren. Opening the strongbox reveals not just valuables, but an itinerary tracking Private Thorsen. The barely legible writing recounts his patrol routes, his companions, and his daily activities around the Rebel Camp, marked only with the signature -M. Such detailed observations could only come from someone living alongside Thorsen, pointing to a traitor within the rebel camp.

The Stagnant Oasis. Tonga Runetotem sends you southeast from the Crossroads to search the Stagnant Oasis. He wants to know if the hidden fissure beneath the Forgotten Pools has a match in its murky waters. Tonga Runetotem sends you to the Stagnant Oasis after a strange fissure is found beneath the Forgotten Pools. He suspects the sudden patches of lush growth across the Barrens have a cause beneath the earth. You search the oasis's murky shallows for another opening, among predators that haunt the water.

text.enUS: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. Gerrig Bonegrip in Ironforge has a spare copy of Yagyin's Digest and will part with it for three items of power. Gerrig will not speak their names aloud, and writes them down in a note instead. Gerrig hears you ask for Yagyin's Digest and wonders whether you are starting a new chapter of their order somewhere, then decides it is not Gerrig's place to ask. Gerrig has an extra copy and believes those of the order must aid each other. In return, three items of power must be brought. Their names stay unspoken, since someone may be listening, and Gerrig writes them down.

text.enUS: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. The Star, the Hand and the Heart is an Undercity quest wherein Keeper Bel'dugur tests an aspiring leader seeking to establish a new chapter of their order. To earn the essential Yagyin's Digest, the petitioner must track down three items of power whose names Bel'dugur dares not speak aloud. Within the shadowed corridors of the Undercity, ambitious practitioners seeking to lead their own circle turn to Keeper Bel'dugur. To establish a new flock and open a chapter of their order, an aspiring leader requires Yagyin's Digest, an authoritative text of ritual lore guarded by the keeper. Bel'dugur stands ready to support his fellow brother, but demands proof of worthiness before yielding such authority.
