text.enUS: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. Stormwind's mages once guarded Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic, but Morganth stole the perilous tome and hid it in the Tower of Ilgalar. Ur of Dalaran wrote a treatise on shadow magic and its subtle, corruptive nature. The mages of the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind feared that such arts could bring doom and ruin to the unwary, so they sealed the volume against readers. After Morganth surrendered to dark arts and Stormwind's magical circle exiled him, he took the tome east into the Redridge Mountains, to his stronghold at the Tower of Ilgalar.

text.enUS: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. In Stormwind, High Sorcerer Andromath seeks the forbidden tome Morganth stole and carried to the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Three promising mages once studied together in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum. Morganth turned to dark arts and shadow magic, despite his peers' desperate warnings to abandon those corrupting powers. The city's magical order formally banished him. Before leaving, he stole a dangerous work by Ur, an infamous archmage whose studies reached beyond orthodox arcana.

Urgent Message. The Urgent Message is a sealed dispatch penned by Brave Moonhorn warning Freewind Post of escalating centaur violence across Thousand Needles. Carried by travelers descending into the canyon, the letter alerts the tauren garrison that their supply lines and scouting parties are under immediate threat. Penned by Brave Moonhorn near the great lift that descends from the Barrens into Thousand Needles, the Urgent Message represents the first line of defense for travelers crossing the border. Moonhorn monitors the jagged canyons below, where aggressive centaur tribes have renewed their relentless raids against Horde travel. Addressed to Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post, the missive sounds the alarm about emboldened attackers striking dangerously close to crucial roadways, urging the local garrison to brace for sustained conflict and guard against secondary threats like the unpredictable Grimtotem clan.

Ursal the Mauler. In Teldrassil, Athridas Bearmantle seeks to wake the Druids of the Talon from their unnatural sleep. Their kin remain trapped in the Barrow Den, and the corrupted Gnarlpine chief behind the disturbance must be slain. The Druids of the Talon withdrew to the Barrow Den of Ban'ethil to sleep and commune with the Emerald Dream. Their peaceful trance became a prison with no way back to waking. Athridas Bearmantle traced the trouble to the gnarlpine furbolgs, and to their vicious leader, Ursal the Mauler, who meddled with the druids' sacred ritual. The sleepers remain caught between waking and the Dream.

Ursangous's Paw. This quest represents the proof of felling Ursangous, one of the most ferocious and legendary predators prowling Ashenvale. Bringing the beast's severed paw to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post earns honor among the Horde's trackers. As part of the Ashenvale Hunt, trackers operating out of Splintertree Post are tasked with pursuing the ancient beasts that dominate the dense forest canopy. Ursangous ranks among the fiercest of these apex predators, known for killing numerous travelers and warriors who crossed his path. Taking down such a beast is no small feat, and claiming his paw serves as undeniable physical proof that the mighty creature has finally met his match.

Ursolan. Ursolan is a sprawling Timbermaw furbolg settlement situated in western Azshara, just east of Timbermaw Hold. Bisected by a deep ravine, the encampment honors the bear Ancient Ursol and serves as a vital stronghold for uncorrupted furbolgs defending their territory from outside incursions. Perched on the rugged bluffs of western Azshara, Ursolan constitutes the eastern branch of the Timbermaw tribe's domain, connecting directly through Timbermaw Hold to Bear's Head in the south. Named after the revered bear Ancient Ursol, this camp represents a rare haven of sanity among Kalimdor's furbolg populations, which have largely fallen victim to demonic corruption. The village spans both rims of a dramatic earthen chasm, where the Timbermaw vigilantly guard their borders against encroaching interlopers, including intrusive researchers from the night elven camp of Talrendis.

Uther's Tomb. Uther's Tomb is the sacred resting place of Uther the Lightbringer, situated atop Sorrow Hill in the Western Plaguelands. Constructed by his surviving followers after his defeat at nearby Andorhal, this monument stands as one of the few remaining bastions of the Holy Light amidst a blighted and haunted region. Perched south of the ruins of Andorhal at Sorrow Hill, Uther's Tomb marks the final resting place of the legendary paladin who founded the Knights of the Silver Hand. Following the collapse of Lordaeron, Uther made his last stand in Andorhal, defending the royal urn holding the ashes of King Terenas Menethil II against Prince Arthas Menethil and the Scourge. Arthas struck down his former mentor and desecrated the urn to carry Kel'Thuzad's remains. Surviving soldiers salvaged Uther's body, laying him to rest within a stone sanctuary. Despite the relentless corruption engulfing the surrounding lands, the tomb remains miraculously untouched by decay, held under the steadfast vigil of High Priest Thel'danis.

Uzzek. Uzzek watches the eastern Barrens from southwest of Far Watch Post. The battle-hardened orc survived many skirmishes across Kalimdor and now tests and trains promising Horde warriors crossing the plains. Uzzek trains young warriors southwest of Far Watch Post, near the eastern edge of the Barrens. He endured brutal combat in the recent wars and now tests those learning to defend themselves. To prove their skill, they face the savage wildlife and raiders that trouble the crossing.

Vahlarriel's Search. Vahlarriel Demonslayer has come to Desolace to learn what became of two missing nobles of House Malem, a Darnassian merchant family. Their father fears the worst, and the last word of the pair places them in the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks back. Vahlarriel asks you to find their wagon. Vahlarriel Demonslayer is looking for Tyranis and Dalinda Malem, whose father fears the worst and has charged Vahlarriel with doing everything possible to find them. The search has barely begun, and Vahlarriel hopes it will not keep them in Desolace long. The pair were last reported crossing the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks ago. Vahlarriel asks you to find their wagon in Desolace and to come at once when you do. Its charred remains lie there, with a chest among them.

Vahlarriel's Search. After the second part of Vahlarriel's Search, Vahlarriel Demonslayer sends you to look for Dalinda and Tyranis Malem, beginning at the fortress. Word of it goes to Vahlarriel's superiors in Darnassus, who worry about Tyranis's motives and want Dalinda brought home safe above all. Vahlarriel Demonslayer wants you to look for both Dalinda and Tyranis, beginning at the fortress, and return with what you learn. Vahlarriel will contact superiors in Darnassus right away. A private word follows: they worry about why Tyranis came to Desolace, and they care most that Dalinda gets home safe. As for Tyranis, they want him gauged first, before any homecoming.

Vahlarriel's Search. Going on with the search of the Malems' wagon, you turn up a pendant and a trail of footprints heading south. Smoke rises from a big fort far off. Vahlarriel Demonslayer at Nijel's Point should be shown the pendant and told about the sign that the Malems may live. Searching the wagon further, you turn up a pendant, and beyond it footprints leading south. Far off, smoke rises from a big fort. A tended fire makes it, not buildings burning, and your instincts say that if the Malems are still alive, they were taken that way.

Valdred's Hands. Valdred's Hands are the severed limbs of Valdred Moray, claimed after his death in southern Silverpine Forest. They are sought by Raleigh Andrean in the Undercity as a morbid trophy and proof of vengeance for the murder of his wife. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, Valdred Moray and Raleigh Andrean were close friends. That bond was shattered when Valdred murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. Though Raleigh succumbed to death and arose as one of the Forsaken—professing an inability to genuinely grieve—the lingering hunger for retribution never left him. When Valdred attempted to flee southward past the Greymane Wall into Gilneas, Raleigh dispatched an emissary to end his former friend's flight, demanding his severed hands as definitive proof that the deed was done.

Valgan's Field. Valgan's Field is an abandoned wheat farm nestled in northern Silverpine Forest, overlooking Lordamere Lake. Once a picturesque homestead, it now lies desolate and overrun by the feral Moonrage worgen unleashed by Archmage Arugal. Situated just west of the Shining Strand and north of the nearby river, Valgan's Field was once a prosperous wheat farm offering scenic views of Lordamere Lake. That peaceful life vanished when the Scourge tore through Lordaeron, forcing its owner, Valgan, to flee or meet his end. Left untended, the ruined structures fell into the claws of feral Moonrage worgen prowling down from Shadowfang Keep. Before the Third War, the mage Arugal spent time here, leaving behind remnants of his arcane research that now draw the attention of the Forsaken.

Valik. Henchman Valik lies injured and dying in a Syndicate camp, confronted by an enemy. Certain you will kill them anyway, Valik strikes a bargain: a mug of Southshore Stout in exchange for answers. Valik is injured and dying, and finds you standing before them as an enemy. Valik expects you to kill them regardless, but offers a bargain: carry a mug of Southshore Stout to the Syndicate camp, and Valik will answer your questions. Valik even wonders aloud whether your kind drinks at all.

Valley of Bones. The Valley of Bones is a desolate canyon along the crags of Shen'dralas, choked with dust, ancient remains, and restless undead. Haunted by the lingering spirits of the Magram centaur clan and patrolled by dark necromancers, it is dominated by the colossal rib cages of mysterious ancient beasts known as the Dead Goliaths. Tucked away in the southern reaches of the region, the Valley of Bones lives up to its grim name. Skeletal horrors walk the dusty ravines, raised and bound by centaur necromancers who draw upon dark sorceries. The spirits of deceased Magram centaur wander the wastes alongside them, bound to this barren earth long after their violent deaths. Adding to the canyon's ominous nature are the Dead Goliaths—two immense skeletons slumped against the rocky cliffs whose true origin remains a total mystery to scholars and wanderers alike.

Valley of Fangs. The Valley of Fangs is a rugged, narrow pass carved between towering rock pillars in the central Badlands. Known for the vicious predators that prowl its dusty floor, it also shelters a small, isolated encampment of wandering tinkerers and exiles. Situated between two imposing stone formations in the heart of the Badlands, the Valley of Fangs earns its name from both the sharp silhouettes of its surrounding cliffs and the dangerous beasts roaming its floor. Feral crag coyotes, prowling cougars, and vicious wolves stalk the dusty corridor, making transit hazardous for lone travelers. Despite the hostile wildlife, a handful of wayward figures—including the banished orc Martek the Exiled and his goblin associates Rigglefuzz and Jazzrik—have pitched an informal camp here, tinkering away in seclusion far from the regional outposts.

Valley of Heroes. Stone statues watch over the Valley of Heroes, where Stormwind's southern road crosses the moat into the city. They honor the leaders of the Alliance Expedition to Draenor, and guards hold this fortified entrance. You cross the moat beneath statues honoring the commanders of the Alliance Expedition. Stormwind's rebuilding after the Second War raised these monuments along the causeway. The champions marched through the Dark Portal into Draenor to seal the rift forever, giving their lives so Azeroth might survive. As you head north toward the Trade District, you pass Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, Ranger-Captain Alleria Windrunner, Force Commander Danath Trollbane, and High General Turalyon.

Valley of Honor. In the Valley of Honor, Orgrimmar's warriors and hunters prepare for battle. Its barracks, guilds, and battlemasters serve the Horde's forces across Azeroth, while forges and training grounds keep its fighters ready. The Valley of Honor holds Orgrimmar's military quarter behind high canyon ridges. Practice weapons clash, and blacksmiths' anvils ring through the day. The Hall of the Brave draws seasoned warriors and battlemasters who coordinate campaigns in places such as Alterac Valley and Warsong Gulch. Training grounds for beastmasters and hunters flank the hall. Across the valley, the Horde equips, drills, and sends out its frontline defenders.

Valley of Kings. The Valley of Kings is a lush canyon nestled in the southwestern corner of Loch Modan, directly south of the passage to Dun Morogh. It serves as a heavily watched gateway into the fiery Searing Gorge, flanked by monumental stone figures carved in memory of the War of the Three Hammers. Travelers venturing here walk beneath ancient dwarven history while facing the immediate threat of Blackrock encroachers and troggs. The valley's most commanding feature is the pair of colossal statues depicting King Madoran Bronzebeard and High Thane Khardros Wildhammer. Carved by joint commission from their sons following their deaths, these stone titans overlook the pass into the scorched southlands. They stand as a lasting monument to the allied victory in the War of the Three Hammers and an eternal warning against the Dark Iron clan, reminding all who look south of the ruin brought upon the southlands by the summoning of Ragnaros.

Valley of Spears. The Valley of Spears is a rugged canyon nestled in western Desolace, serving as the stronghold of the Maraudine centaur clan. Enclosed by steep cliffs and guarded passes, the valley leads directly to Maraudon, the sacred ancestral burial ground of all centaurkind. Carved into the rugged heights of western Desolace, the Valley of Spears is a stronghold of the Maraudine clan. Accessible on foot only through narrow, easily defended mountain passes from the south and east, this enclosed valley provides the centaur with a natural bastion. Travelers who venture past the rocky chokepoints face dense encampments of hostile nomads guarding the approach to their most revered holy site.

Valley of Spirits. Darkspear trolls make their home in the Valley of Spirits, west of Orgrimmar's main thoroughfares. Thatched lodges, tiki poles, and pools mark their place among the city's red stone and iron. The Valley of Spirits branches west from the Valley of Strength, a quiet enclave for the Darkspear trolls. The tribe settled in Durotar alongside Thrall's orcs, and made this pocket among the crags their gathering place in the city. Trollish craftspeople, spiritualists, and practitioners gather around wooden bridges and winding waters, practicing their arts away from the dry heat of Orgrimmar's main thoroughfares.

Valley of Strength. The Valley of Strength is the bustling central commons of Orgrimmar, greeting all who pass through the city's towering front gates. Housing the city bank, the central auction house, and the Broken Tusk inn, it serves as the beating commercial and administrative heart of the Horde capital. Step past the fortified timber gates of Orgrimmar and you enter the Valley of Strength. Carved deep into the red canyon rock of Durotar, this valley serves as the Horde's front square. Adventurers, merchants, and warriors from all allied nations mingle across its dusty plazas, swapping war stories over flagons from the Broken Tusk inn or attending to vital trade at the central bank and auction house. It is a bustling testament to the strength and unity the orcs fought to establish in their new homeland.

Valley of the Watchers. Tucked away in the far southern reaches of the Tanaris desert, the Valley of the Watchers is a sun-scorched canyon defined by monumental stonework. At its end stands a colossal, sealed stone gate leading into the mysterious complex of Uldum, guarded by lumbering giants and ancient stone sentinels. The Valley of the Watchers marks the southern boundary where the shifting sands of Tanaris meet the mountainous edge of the continent. Dominating the canyon is a massive gate crafted from ancient stone, locked tight against the outside world. This sealed portal is believed to guard the entrance to Uldum, a subterranean facility of the enigmatic Titans. Massive Dune Smasher mountain giants roam the dusty approach, ensuring that whatever secrets lie buried beneath the sands remain undisturbed by travelers, tomb robbers, and scholars alike.

Valor's Rest. Valor's Rest is a small outpost and cemetery perched at the eastern threshold of Silithus. Guarded by members of the Cenarion Circle, it is the first point of shelter seen by travelers emerging from Un'Goro Crater into the windswept wastes. Perched on the eastern border of Silithus along the ramp leading down from Un'Goro Crater, Valor's Rest serves as the threshold into this desolate frontier. Maintained as a neutral staging ground by the Cenarion Circle, the camp hosts members of both the Alliance and the Horde who dare to brave the arid wastes. Its prominent graveyard stands as a somber reminder of the danger lurking throughout the desert, where insectoid horrors and ancient threats test even the hardiest expeditions.

Valormok. Valormok is a remote Horde outpost established in the rugged northwest reaches of Azshara. Positioned north of the Haldarr Encampment, this windswept settlement serves as a staging ground for scouts and adventurers braving the cursed, ancient ruins of the coast. Perched among the autumn-colored trees of Azshara, Valormok represents the Horde's tentative interest in a hostile and largely forsaken territory. Life here is bleak and fraught with peril; the camp is lightly fortified and constantly exposed to nearby satyrs, nagas, and prowling beasts. Despite these hardships, its stationed warriors hold the ground, acting as a crucial flight hub and forward bastion connecting Orgrimmar with the wilder stretches of northern Kalimdor.

Valstag Ironjaw. Valstag Ironjaw is an Ironforge dwarven soldier stationed within Menethil Keep in the coastal marshlands of the Wetlands. Facing the pressing dangers that plague the trade passages connecting Loch Modan and the coast, he assists in securing regional routes and keeping the harbor's garrison informed of local threats. Found inside Menethil Keep in Menethil Harbor, Valstag Ironjaw serves as part of the dwarven garrison keeping watch over the lowlands. The surrounding marsh is rife with danger, from hostile Dragonmaw orcs to ravenous wildlife, making communications and supply lines difficult to maintain. Valstag helps coordinate defense efforts along the primary thoroughfares, particularly the treacherous passage cutting through Dun Algaz toward Loch Modan.

Vanndar Stormpike. Vanndar Stormpike is a fierce dwarf mountain king who commands the Stormpike Expedition from the northern fortress of Dun Baldar. Searching the frozen peaks of Alterac Valley for ancient relics and raw resources, he leads the Alliance's unyielding war against the Frostwolf orcs. A veteran mountain king of Ironforge, Vanndar Stormpike spearheads the dwarven excavation into Alterac Valley. Following the Third War, he marched the Stormpike Guard into the northern mountains seeking hidden mineral riches and long-lost titan artifacts. Settling into the fortified redoubt of Dun Baldar, Vanndar views the valley as an ancestral right and rightful Alliance territory. He directs military outposts, defensive bunkers, and frontline pushes with grim dwarven resolve, determined that no retreat will ever be sounded under his watch.

Vanquish the Betrayers. At Tiragarde Keep, Kul Tiran forces hold a coastal foothold in Durotar. Gar'Thok has ordered a Horde strike against Lieutenant Benedict's garrison, whose presence breaks the fragile peace with Theramore. Thrall led the Horde across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, where he joined Lady Jaina Proudmoore against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Peace broke when Jaina's estranged father, Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, brought Kul Tiras's navy to Durotar. He blamed all orcs for the Old Horde's atrocities and seized coastal footholds, including Tiragarde Keep. Daelin died at Theramore, but remnants of his fleet still refuse any pact or surrender their hatred.

Varian Wrynn. King Varian Wrynn is the rightful ruler of the Kingdom of Stormwind, currently missing after vanishing en route to a diplomatic summit in Theramore. In his absence, his ten-year-old son Anduin wears the crown, guided by Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor. Varian was just a boy when the First War shattered his life. He watched his father, King Llane Wrynn, die by the hand of the assassin Garona Halforcen as the Old Horde stormed the capital. Rescued by Anduin Lothar, the orphaned prince fled north with the kingdom's survivors to Southshore. In Capital City, King Terenas Menethil II took Varian in like a second son. The young prince grew up in exile alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, bearing the memory of a burned home until the Alliance of Lordaeron broke the Horde and reclaimed Stormwind.

Varimathras. Varimathras is a dreadlord of the nathrezim race who serves as the chief lieutenant and military advisor to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Forced to pledge loyalty to the Banshee Queen after suffering defeat during the civil war for Lordaeron, he now stands at her right hand in the Royal Quarter of the Undercity. Before the Third War, Kil'jaeden sent Varimathras and his fellow dreadlords to Azeroth as the Lich King's jailors, to make sure the spirit of Ner'zhul served the Legion's plans. Bound alongside his brothers Detheroc and Balnazzar, he oversaw the Scourge in Lordaeron while Archimonde invaded Kalimdor. When the Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, the triumvirate remained entrenched in the ruins of the Capital City, entirely unaware of their master's demise until Prince Arthas returned to drive them into hiding.

Varok Saurfang. High Overlord Saurfang is a legendary orc warrior and a veteran of the Old Horde's wars. Serving as Warchief Thrall's trusted military commander in Orgrimmar, he represents the proud martial spine of the modern Horde. Few living warriors possess a martial pedigree to rival Saurfang. A veteran of the Old Horde's wars, he is considered an unstoppable force on the battlefield. Today he stands in Orgrimmar as High Overlord, a bulwark of Thrall's newborn Horde.

Vault of Ironforge. The Vault of Ironforge is the primary banking house and treasure repository for the dwarven capital. Situated in the bustling Commons directly opposite the Auction House, it serves as a central hub where citizens and travelers across the Alliance securely store their wealth. The vault's operations are overseen by Dinita and the esteemed Stonemantle family. Carved deep into the mountain rock of the Commons, the Vault of Ironforge stands as a symbol of dwarven fiscal security and craft. With the city's trade booming, travelers, soldiers, and merchants gather here daily to deposit coin, relics, and provisions under the vigilant eyes of city guards and tellers. Overseen by Dinita and the trusted Stonemantle family, the institution offers Alliance patrons absolute peace of mind.

Velarok. Velarok Windblade is a lone human swordsman camped amid the ash and cinder of Searing Gorge, flanked by the mutilated corpses of Dark Iron dwarves. He seeks vengeance against the local Dark Irons for the brutal murder of his father, recruiting passing travelers to forge a weapon of retribution. His single-minded hunger for vengeance drives everything he asks of those who help him. Found southeast of Thorium Point, Velarok Windblade presents himself as a grieving human warrior stranded in the perilous wastes of the Searing Gorge. Surrounding his camp are the bloody, battered corpses of Dark Iron dwarves who crossed his blade. According to Velarok, these clan dwarves slaughtered his father in cold blood. Consumed by hatred, he enlists travelers to gather materials to assemble the Torch of Retribution, an enchanted weapon of vengeance against the Dark Irons and the minions of Ragnaros.

Velinde Starsong. This quest bridges an eerie investigation in Ashenvale with the military hierarchy in Darnassus. After uncovering unsettling events tied to the vanished night elf commander Velinde Starsong, adventurers are sent across the sea to consult Sentinel leadership regarding her mysterious fate. Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow holds watch in Ashenvale, but she was not the first to shoulder that burden. Before her stood Velinde Starsong, a priestess tasked with containing the demonic corruption bleeding southward out of Felwood. Though initial reports suggested Starsong had the peril well in hand, her defensive campaign gradually unraveled. Then, without warning or formal relief, she vanished entirely, leaving behind an unfinished war and unanswered questions.

Velinde's Effects. In Darnassus, Velinde's Effects draw the Sentinels into an inquiry. The search concerns Sentinel Velinde Starsong, who vanished after years of service, and the journal Thyn'tel Bladeweaver asks you to retrieve from the Sentinels' quarters. Priestess Velinde Starsong served the night elves for many years and earned their deep trust. When she quietly vanished from her duties, the Sentinels believed she had left for personal reasons and expected her to return. Outsiders later found clues tied to the Tome of Mel'Thandris. Only then did Sentinel leaders allow an inquiry into Velinde's private belongings.

Velinde's Journal. Velinde Starsong's personal journal records her duties and the mystery of her departure from Darnassus. The Night Elf priestess's journal is stored in the Sentinel bunkhouse. When Night Elf priestess Velinde Starsong left Darnassus, her belongings were locked in a footlocker at the Sentinels' bunkhouse in the Tradesmen's Terrace. Among them was her personal journal, a record of her responsibilities and duties. The Sentinels respected Velinde and believed she had left to attend to private matters. Her journal's contents suggest her unexplained absence is more troubling than they first believed.

Velinde's Key. In Darnassus, Velinde's Key guards the writings of a vanished priestess. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver entrusts it to those who bring proof of their interest in Velinde Starsong's fate. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps Velinde's Key in Darnassus. The simple key secures Priestess Velinde Starsong's personal belongings in a footlocker in the Sentinel bunkhouse above the Tradesmen's Terrace. Velinde left night elf lands without warning, and her possessions were set aside. Bladeweaver gives the key only to those who bring genuine evidence of their interest in learning her fate, such as revelations found in the Tome of Mel'Thandris.

Velora Nitely. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Velora Nitely works the forge for the Forsaken and the Horde. Once among Lordaeron's finest armorsmiths, she now makes dry jokes that rarely land. Velora Nitely works near the anvils in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, where she makes armor for the Horde. Before the Third War devastated the north, Lordaeron celebrated her as an exceptional armorsmith. Undeath took her life and warmth, but left her technical skill untouched. She works with Horde crafters across continents, including Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens. Her craft includes reinforcing heavy battle plate and forging the formidable Brutal Legguards from hardened materials such as Dragonmaw shinbones.

text.enUS: Velora Nitely and the Brutal Legguards. Thun'grim Firegaze sends Horde warriors across the Great Sea for Velora Nitely's Brutal Legguards. In the Undercity, the Forsaken smith draws on the craft she kept from her mortal life to forge the armor. Her work helps assemble a durable suit for the Horde's warriors. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east across the Great Sea to find a smith for the Brutal Legguards. You've proved your mettle to the veteran smith at his vigil in the Barrens, and now he points you toward the fabled Brutal Armor. Thun'grim cannot make the whole suit alone, so he relies on skilled allies across the Horde. The greaves call for an artisan whose work was revered before northern humanity fell, in the Forsaken's underground kingdom.

Vengeance on the Northspring. Talo Thornhoof was once a seasoned hunter who feared no creature, until harpies ambushed Talo in the forest. The hate has boiled inside ever since, and Talo asks you to take revenge on the Northspring harpies, found to the west. Talo remembers being a seasoned hunter who feared nothing that lived. Then came a day in the forest, honing a weapon once a hard fight was over, when harpies surrounded Talo. Talo barely dragged to safety, still hears their cries echoing, and was never the same afterward. All this time later the hate still boils, and Talo wants revenge.

Venom Bottles. Bottles of a vile green venom fill a Witherbark village in the Hinterlands. So many of them suggest the Witherbarks value it highly, and an apothecary in nearby Tarren Mill might like a sample. The bottles in the Witherbark village hold a vile, green venom. There are so many that the Witherbarks must consider it very important. A sample could be carried to an apothecary in Tarren Mill, who may want to see it.

Venom to the Undercity. Apothecary Lydon is delighted with the venom taken from the Witherbark's spider god, and wants a sample sent to Lydon's superior, Faranell, at the Apothecarium in the Undercity. A parcel is entrusted to you for the journey. Lydon has killed nearly two dozen rabbits with a single dose of the venom. Some of them were tiny, so their resistance was surely low, but there is no denying the poison is powerful. Lydon is certain that Faranell will want to test it personally, and hands you a parcel to carry to the Apothecarium in the Undercity.

Venomtail Antidote. In Durotar, Venomtail Antidote is urgently needed to save a scout from scorpid poison. Kor'ghan brews the remedy in Orgrimmar for Rhinag, who lies stricken near Durotar's northwestern border. Durotar's venomtail scorpids can kill a warrior within an hour of a deep sting. Rhinag, a troll scout, was envenomed near the northwestern border, far from aid. His only chance is a remedy from Kor'ghan, an apothecary in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow.

Venomtail Poison Sac. In Durotar, a scorpion’s venom can bring a hunter near death, while its poison sac holds what alchemists need to make a cure. Scorpids roam Durotar’s red rocks, including Venomtail Scorpids, Corrupted Scorpids, and the Death Flayer. Their tail sacs hold a fast-acting venom that can overwhelm even seasoned warriors if left untreated. The same sacs contain the primary compounds alchemists need to make an antidote. When a scorpion stung the hunter Rhinag outside Orgrimmar, local alchemists needed four fresh poison sacs to make a remedy and neutralize the venom in his veins.

Venomweb Vale. Venomweb Vale is a shadowed valley in eastern Tirisfal Glades, sitting just south of the Scarlet Monastery. Once a lush woodland teeming with game, the vale has devolved into a blighted nest overrun by aggressive, venomous arachnids. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, this valley was a peaceful retreat of lush grass and verdant trees, favored by local hunters tracking deer and rabbits. Today, rot and creeping gloom dominate the landscape. Giant, venomous spiders swarm among the trees and hollows, led by the monstrous arachnid Sri'skulk. The vale's northern edge borders the territory of the Scarlet Crusade, where darkhounds prowl near the fortified Scarlet Encampment under Lieutenant Sanders.

Ventaari Brightwish. Ventaari Brightwish is a Skyborne resident of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. She greets travelers from across Azeroth and offers the quest The Gift of Skysight. Residing in Thendal Village upon the soaring cliffs of Zephras Isle, Ventaari Brightwish is one of the local Skyborne. While she shares a surname with Belathaan Brightwish, her own duties center around aiding newcomers who find their way to the village, extending hospitality to both the Alliance and the Horde as she initiates visitors into the traditions of her people through tasks like The Gift of Skysight.

Venture Co. Base Camp. Tucked away in the dense jungles of northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Venture Co. Base Camp serves as a forward foothold for the notoriously greedy goblin syndicate. Here, hired overseers and laborers exploit the lush wilderness, focusing their efforts on harvesting timber, hunting local wildlife, and extracting valuable tumbled crystals from the nearby waterways. The Venture Company is infamous across Azeroth for ruthless profiteering and complete disregard for the natural world. At this jungle base camp, steam-powered equipment and makeshift goblin shacks chew into the ancient canopy. Guarded by armed mercenaries, foremen, and field workers, the camp coordinates resource extraction throughout the surrounding valleys, paying particular interest to valuable tumbled crystals found nearby while clear-cutting any jungle that stands in their way.

Venture Co. Documents. These tightly bound papers were recovered from a crate amidst a ruined caravan in eastern Mulgore. They detail the operations of the Venture Company, confirming the predatory cartel's illegal strip-mining ventures within the tauren homeland. Discovered packed atop mined ore and minerals in the remnants of a ransacked wagon, these documents expose the scale of the Venture Company's intrusion into Mulgore. Known across Kalimdor for ruthless deforestation and uncontrolled excavation, the goblin-led cartel has quietly set up drilling and mining outposts in the eastern foothills. Morin Cloudstalker and the tauren Outrunners rely on these seized ledgers to gauge the threat to their sacred ancestral plains and rally hunters to drive the trespassers out.

text.enUS: Venture Co. Engineering Plans. The Venture Co. Engineering Plans are mechanical schematics kept inside the goblin logging mill in Windshear Crag. Recovered by Alliance operatives, they detail the inner workings of the heavy machinery devastating the Stonetalon Mountains. Windshear Crag is choked with smoke and logging machinery as the Venture Company strips the forests of Stonetalon. Hidden inside their lumber mill south of Cragpool Lake, these engineering blueprints lay out the exact construction, strengths, and flaws of their specialized timber-harvesting contraptions.

Venture Co. Letters. The Venture Co. Letters are internal correspondence recovered from Windshear Mine in Stonetalon Mountains. Stolen under the cover of explosive distractions, they provide the night elf Sentinels with crucial intelligence on goblin industrial operations in the region. Windshear Crag has been overrun by the Venture Company, whose logging machines and strip-mining operations tear through the ancient woodland. To uncover the full scope of the cartel's ambitions, Alliance operatives deployed covert sabotage to create distractions and infiltrate Windshear Mine. These retrieved letters contain private communications and logistical records detailing the company's local activities, giving Sentinel leadership insight into how the defilers organize their workforce and supply lines.

Venture Co. Mine. Tucked into the eastern cliffs of Mulgore, the Venture Co. Mine is an unauthorized industrial excavation run by greedy goblin opportunists. Despite being denied rights by the tauren, the Venture Company dug into the hills regardless, threatening the natural balance of the plains. When the Venture Company sought rights to strip Mulgore of its minerals, the tauren flatly refused. The corporate cartel ignored them, tunneling deep into the eastern mountain wall anyway under the direction of Supervisor Fizsprocket. Their sprawling complex features three entrances—a ground tunnel guarded by hired muscle, a sheer cliffside overlook, and an upper passage leading out to a small lumber camp. The encroaching machines, smoke, and slag heaps represent a blatant defilement of sacred land.

Venture Company. The Venture Company is a notoriously ruthless goblin cartel focused on aggressive resource extraction, heavy industrial machinery, and logging. Unaligned with the major goblin ports like Booty Bay or Ratchet, the cartel strip-mines and clear-cuts territories across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms without regard for local populations or the natural world. Led overall by Mogul Razdunk from afar, the Venture Company operates by a simple corporate philosophy: if it can be chopped down, drilled into, or blasted out of a mountain, they will exploit it. The cartel deploys some of the most advanced heavy machinery on Azeroth, including massive lumber-harvesting shredders, drilling rigs, and industrial refineries. Unlike traditional merchant houses that focus on shipping or retail, the Venture Company specializes in seizing raw resources by force, ignoring treaties, borders, and local sovereign rights.

text.enUS: Venture Company Mining. In Booty Bay, the goblin Crank Fizzlebub wants someone to strike at the Venture Company's operations in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Their dig site near Crystalvein Mine continues to produce valuable Singing Blue Crystals from the nearby hills, and Crank asks for ten of those stones brought back to him. Following your earlier collection of Singing Blue Shards, Crank Fizzlebub points toward a larger rival. The Venture Company runs operations across the jungle, cutting into the profits of independent goblins. Though the many basilisks keep the miners from setting foot inside Crystalvein Mine itself, the workers continue digging into the surrounding hillsides to extract Singing Blue Crystals. Crank asks you to take the crystals from these miners and bring them to Booty Bay as proof of their setback.

Verdan the Everliving. Verdan the Everliving is a colossal bog beast lurking deep within the verdant tunnels of the Wailing Caverns. He dwells amid the nightmare spreading from the sleeping druid Naralex, alongside the corrupted Druids of the Fang, and violently attacks any who venture into his damp hollows. Verdan is a hulking bog beast, an elemental of foliage, silt, and mire that lurks in the overgrown depths of the Wailing Caverns. Nothing is known of him from before the caverns fell to corruption; he is simply the largest and most dangerous creature in their lush, flooded hollows.

Verdant Note. The Verdant Note is a summons delivered to novice tauren druids in Camp Narache. Sent on behalf of the druid mentor Gart Mistrunner, it instructs young initiates to report for training and begin learning the rites of the Earthmother. Young tauren who demonstrate a spiritual affinity for nature receive the Verdant Note shortly after beginning their trials in the Red Cloud Mesa. Carried by a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner, the brief missive directs the initiate to present themselves to the mentor at Camp Narache. Restless spirits and shifting elements have begun troubling Mulgore, making the instruction of new druids an urgent duty for the elders.

Verdant Note. The Verdant Note is a formal summons delivered to promising young tauren in the Red Cloud Mesa. Entrusted by Grull Hawkwind, the message bids budding protectors of the wilds to seek out the druidic mentor Gart Mistrunner at Camp Narache. Young tauren stepping into their responsibilities on the Red Cloud Mesa are quickly singled out for their natural gifts. Grull Hawkwind passes along this missive on behalf of a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner. The note acts as an invitation into the ancient fold of tauren druidism, calling the initiate away from basic village errands to heed the whispering balance of the plains.

Verdant Sigil. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives young night elf druids the Verdant Sigil as a summons to begin training. Young night elves in Shadowglen who feel the call of the wild receive the Verdant Sigil from Conservator Ilthalaine. A messenger brings it from Mardant Strongoak, the druid trainer, and it directs novices to climb into Aldrassil's boughs. The token invites them to leave basic chores behind and begin serious study of communion with nature spirits and the mysteries of the Emerald Dream.

Verdant Sigil. A summons reaches newly awakened night elf druids in Shadowglen. Conservator Ilthalaine passes the Verdant Sigil to fledgling shapeshifters, directing them to Mardant Strongoak within Aldrassil. The token marks the start of their formal training in nature and the Emerald Dream. When a young night elf shows promise in keeping Shadowglen's balance, the order calls for a formal introduction. A runner brings the Verdant Sigil to Conservator Ilthalaine, who entrusts it to the initiate. The token shows that the circle in Aldrassil has taken notice and invites the young druid to begin formal training.

Verna Furlbrow. Verna Furlbrow waits beside her broken wagon near Westfall’s northern border. Bandits drove her from her family’s pumpkin patch, and the road to Elwynn Forest has left her stranded. Verna and her husband farmed pumpkins in northern Westfall until lawlessness drove them from their land. After outlaws took the farm, they loaded what they could onto their cart and set out for Elwynn Forest with their horse, Old Blanchy. Their wagon broke down just down the road from the abandoned Jansen Stead. Unable to repair the axle or continue, Verna now faces the elements, bandit raids, and scavengers. She depends on travelers to keep her household fed and guarded.

text.enUS: Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe. Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe travels to Salma Saldean as the Furlbrows prepare to leave their farm. Her handwritten formula carries a familiar comfort for those who remain. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow have homesteaded in Westfall for years, but the Defias Brotherhood and rogue harvest golems now run rampant across the countryside. They wait for their wagon to be repaired so they can escape toward Stormwind. While they wait, Verna writes down her beloved formula for Westfall Stew. She entrusts the recipe to travelers bound for her neighboring friend, Salma Saldean, so the familiar comfort of the stew can endure for those left behind.

Verner Osgood. Verner Osgood is the resident blacksmith of Lakeshire, stationed just outside the town smithy. Balancing local civilian trade with the crushing demands of the Stormwind military, he works tirelessly to keep horses shod and defenders armed amid relentless gnoll raids. Standing by the forge in central Lakeshire, Verner Osgood represents the strained industrial backbone of the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with crafting basic supplies like horseshoes for local mounts, Verner finds his stock constantly co-opted to manufacture weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom stretching its borders thin and local garrisons lacking supplies, independent smiths like Verner must carry the logistical burden of the realm's defense.

Verner's Note. Verner's Note is a written requisition penned by Lakeshire's blacksmith, Verner Osgood, and carried to Smith Argus in Goldshire. It details a critical shortage of iron in Redridge, asking the Elwynn smith for emergency horseshoes. Maintaining the defense of Lakeshire demands a heavy toll in worked metal. With the Stormwind Guard stationed in town stretched thin against invading gnolls and local perils, Verner Osgood has consumed nearly all his iron reserves keeping soldiers armed and armored. As a result, Lakeshire's stables have fallen into neglect, lacking even basic horseshoes for their mounts. This letter represents Verner swallowing his pride to ask Smith Argus in Goldshire for an external shipment of prepared shoes to keep the town's horses mobile.

Verog the Dervish. Across the southern Barrens, Verog the Dervish keeps moving, and Regthar Deathgate seeks to draw him out. The orc directs Horde champions to attack the Kolkar command tent at the Stagnant Oasis, hoping to force the nomadic leader into the open. After Barak Kodobane fell, Regthar Deathgate turned to the remaining Kolkar warlords. Barak had stayed near the northern waters of the Forgotten Pools, but Verog the Dervish roams the sun-baked plains and rarely lingers in one camp. Horde scouts cannot easily track him across that wide territory. Their chance is to make the commander come to them.

Verog's Head. Regthar Deathgate seeks Verog's Head as proof of the Kolkar leader's death. The chieftain commands forces around the Stagnant Oasis, and his defeat is meant to weaken the tribes threatening the Barrens. The Kolkar centaur threaten Horde travelers and supply routes across the northern Barrens. Verog the Dervish roams the arid scrubland, leaving his command tent at the Stagnant Oasis vulnerable. Horde operatives attack his forces around the pavilion until an alarm sounds. Verog rushes back to defend his camp, where he is slain and decapitated. Regthar Deathgate receives his head as proof that another dangerous Kolkar chieftain has fallen. Barak Kodobane's head is already on display beside it.

Veron Amberstill. Veron Amberstill is a dwarven ram breeder residing at Amberstill Ranch in eastern Dun Morogh. He tends to the rugged mountain rams that serve as the traditional mounts of Ironforge and offers them to skilled riders who have earned his trust. Tucked away in the snow-dusted hills of eastern Dun Morogh, Veron Amberstill oversees the celebrated stock of Amberstill Ranch. Mountain rams are perfectly suited for Khaz Modan's treacherous slopes, sure-footed and thick-coated against the bite of mountain blizzards. Veron breeds and trains these beasts to carry dwarven scouts, mountaineers, and traveling adventurers. While he gladly provides standard and swift mounts to fellow dwarves, outsiders must prove their unwavering loyalty to the throne of Ironforge before he will part with any of his prized herd.

Veronica Nials. Captain Veronica Nials is an officer of the Stromgarde military stationed at Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands. Amid the kingdom's collapse, she coordinates defensive operations against the Syndicate and ogres that overrun the fallen capital. Following the Third War, the human kingdom of Stromgarde shattered, leaving its remnants struggling to survive against invading Boulderfist ogres and the treachery of the Syndicate. Captain Veronica Nials stands as one of the central commanders of the surviving Stromgarde defenders at Refuge Pointe. Tasked with holding the line, she directs Alliance champions against key Syndicate leadership, such as Lord Falconcrest and the warlock Marez Cowl, while striving to recover fallen soldiers' badges so their grieving families can find closure.

Vesprystus. At Rut'theran Village, Vesprystus sends travelers between Teldrassil and mainland Kalimdor. He tends the hippogryph roost at the great World Tree's base. At Teldrassil's southern base, Vesprystus tends the Rut'theran roost. Trained hippogryphs carry travelers from the isolated elven boughs toward Darkshore and the mainland. A magical portal also links Rut'theran to Darnassus in the canopy above. Across the strait, Vesprystus works with the flight master at Auberdine to carry sentinels, emissaries, and adventurers into Kalimdor.

Veteran Uzzek. Veteran Uzzek is a Horde quest that sends promising young warriors to seek out a seasoned combat instructor. Stationed just south of Far Watch Post between Durotar and the Barrens, Uzzek teaches new recruits that true martial greatness requires disciplined study as well as strength. In the culture of the Horde, martial strength is unquestioned and revered above all else. Yet brute force alone does not make a champion. Seasoned commanders know that the greatest warriors are also humble students of the craft, willing to hone their instincts through discipline and study. Aspiring fighters ready to advance beyond basic training are directed to seek out those who have survived the crucible of war.

Vial of Innocent Blood. A Vial of Innocent Blood is a grim alchemical reagent gathered by Syndicate shadow mages lurking in the ruins of Durnholde Keep. Sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill, it serves as a key catalyst in brewing experimental toxins. Within the crumbled walls of Durnholde Keep, the fallen human nobles of the Syndicate practice dark and unsavory arts. Among them are shadow mages who systematically harvest the blood of innocents for their own occult rituals. This macabre practice has drawn the keen attention of Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Needing untainted blood to brew an experimental pacifying agent meant to neutralize the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains, the Forsaken apothecary sees the Syndicate's grim stores as a convenient shortcut for his work.

Vial of Phlogiston. A Vial of Phlogiston is an alchemical substance used by master armorers to temper extraordinarily resilient mail. Guarded within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul, it is coveted by both Alliance and Horde smiths forging specialized battle armor for promising warriors. Phlogiston is an intensely volatile, fire-bearing substance prized in esoteric metallurgy. Both the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and the near-blind orc armorer Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens consider it an indispensable component for hardening warrior armor beyond ordinary physical limits. Without this alchemical agent, the specialized forging techniques required for Fire Hardened Mail or the Horde's Brutal Armor cannot be completed.

Vial of Purest Water. In the southern Barrens, Brine blesses a vial of pure water for a shaman initiate. Its contents help Islen Waterseer prepare a water sapta for seeing elemental spirits. Brine guides the initiate through trials of patience and cleansing before sealing the water in the vial. The water holds an uncorrupted elemental purity. Carry it across the Barrens to Islen Waterseer, who keeps watch on a solitary shore. She needs it to brew a water sapta. Without such pure water, a shaman cannot commune with spiritual guardians in places far from the sunbaked flats.

Vial of Spider Venom. A Vial of Spider Venom contains the potent, necrotic poison harvested from the arachnids that infest the darkened woods of Duskwood. Madame Eva of Darkshire uses this dangerous extract alongside undead remains to craft protective wards against incoming harm. The shadowed thickets of Duskwood harbor monstrous arachnids—from skittering pygmy venom webs and green recluses to black widows and the notorious Naraxis. These creatures pump a foul, potent poison through their fangs, potent enough to paralyze travelers and decay flesh. Adventurers brave enough to slay these horrors can extract intact vials of the viscous fluid.

Vice. The Vice is a rugged, desolate expanse of Deadwind Pass situated along the road leading toward Karazhan. It serves as the territory of the Deadwind ogres, who maintain rough mounds and scattered camps in defiance of the land's grim isolation. Travelers passing through must navigate both their crude brutality and their surprisingly adept wielders of dark magic. Stretching across the southern stretches of Deadwind Pass, the Vice is defined by barren earth, jagged rock faces, and crude mounds erected by the Deadwind ogre clan. While the surrounding canyon is largely abandoned to vengeful ghosts and scavenger vultures, these ogres have carved out a stubborn foothold directly beside the main path approaching Karazhan. Why they chose such a bleak and magically scarred waste remains an enduring mystery, but any traveler passing between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows quickly learns they defend their camps with fierce territorial violence.

Vicious Night Web Spider Venom. Vicious Night Web Spider Venom is a potent natural toxin gathered from the arachnids haunting eastern Tirisfal Glades. The Royal Apothecary Society prizes it for its peculiar ability to carry and preserve historical disease strains, making it a critical reagent in the development of the Forsaken's New Plague. According to research conducted by Apothecary Johaan in Brill, ancient texts chronicle a devastating historical plague that wiped out thousands of innocent victims. Curiously, the contagious agent behind that forgotten outbreak managed to endure over centuries by embedding itself within the venom of the local Night Web spiders. By hunting down the vicious breed lurking in Venomweb Vale south of the Scarlet Monastery, the apothecaries extract this preserved virulence to serve as a vital catalyst in their ongoing alchemical experiments.

Vidra Hearthstove. Vidra Hearthstove is a dwarven cook residing in the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Known for preparing local specialties, she frequently relies on traveling adventurers to gather regional ingredients for her famous blood sausages. Within the bustling warmth of the Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove tends the kitchen and helps feed the locals and travelers passing through Loch Modan. Sharing a surname with the innkeeper, she keeps Thelsamar well-provisioned. Her signature dish, Thelsamar blood sausages, is a hearty dwarven staple that requires fresh game meats gathered from the surrounding wilderness, including boar entrails, spider ichor, and bear meat.

Viktori Prism'Antras. Viktori Prism'Antras is an eccentric stargazer residing in a small hillside hut overlooking Darkshire. While the town around him succumbs to dread and looming horrors, Viktori focuses intently on building a telescope to view the heavens clearly. To realize his vision, he relies on adventurous travelers to acquire intricate parts based on gnomish schematics. Perched up the slope just beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras spends his days peering outward from the gloom of Duskwood. Amid undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows, his obsession lies far beyond the suffocating canopy. He dreams of building a magnificent optical telescope capable of bringing the stars into brilliant focus, offering a quiet escape from the dread that engulfs the hamlet.

Vile Familiar Head. Near the Burning Blade Coven, Vile Familiar Heads mark a grim test for young Horde warlocks. Under Ruzan's guidance, they gather the gruesome trophies as proof of readiness to bind their first demonic minions. The test demands discipline and respect for the lethality of the beings they mean to summon. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Ruzan asks novices seeking to learn summoning to bring him six Vile Familiar Heads. Vile familiars are fiery imps with dangerous elemental cunning, found outside the Burning Blade Coven. Novices must face and defeat them, proving they can subdue demonic life rather than be overcome by it. Warlocks are barely tolerated within Thrall's Horde, so their training calls for care. A novice slain by a conjured creature only deepens the dishonor and suspicion cast upon practitioners of the dark arts.

Vile Familiars. Near the Den, Vile Familiars threaten every warlock who seeks the power of demons. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength against them and bring back their heads. This is the humble, dangerous first step toward mastering fel power under the Horde’s watchful eyes. Warlocks live uneasily within Thrall’s new Horde. Demonic corruption and blood pacts once brought ruin to the orcs, leaving deep scars and distrust. Fel magic is tolerated in Durotar, but its practitioners are neither loved nor welcomed. Many warlocks live in seclusion, practicing in shadowed places like the Den, away from prying eyes. There, they teach the few initiates daring enough to follow their path.

Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Ruzan sends warlock initiates against vile familiars. After you slay them, you report to Zureetha Fargaze, who oversees the effort to curb the Burning Blade. Warriors and scouts in the Valley of Trials answer directly to Zureetha Fargaze, who sends them to curb the Burning Blade Coven. Warlock initiates first answer to Ruzan, their shadowy mentor. He demands proof that you can master lesser demons before sending you back to aid the Horde's defense. Your work serves both the warlocks and the safety of the Den.

Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Vile Familiars are creeping out of a nearby cavern. Zureetha Fargaze found a hidden Burning Blade coven while watching over the valley's trials. Recruits are sent to hunt the familiars spreading across Durotar's red earth. The Valley of Trials tests young orcs and Darkspear trolls in strength, discipline, and loyalty to Thrall's Horde. Its trials were meant to pit recruits against scorpids and boars, not demonic corruption. Yet a cave to the northeast shelters agents of the Burning Blade, who have formed a secret coven beneath the valley overseers' watch.

name.ruRU: Чешуя мурлока из племени Злобного Плавника

text.enUS: Vile Fin Scale. Vile Fin Scales are harvested from the murloc tribes prowling the waterways and northern coasts of Tirisfal Glades. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes these resilient biological samples in their ongoing research to engineer a devastating new plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works relentlessly to craft a virulent blight capable of decimating both the living and the Scourge. Simple toxins are easy enough to brew, but creating an infectious disease that spreads effortlessly across populations requires specialized alchemical properties. Apothecary Johaan in Brill studies Vile Fin scales specifically to understand how their natural resilience and mucous coatings can aid in stabilizing and transmitting his experimental contagions.

Vile Reef. The Vile Reef is a submerged, vibrant coral shelf lying off the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale near Grom'gol Base Camp. Beneath its waters, aggressive murlocs make their home among ancient sunken troll ruins, giant clams, and coastal shipwrecks. Stretching beneath the waves of the Great Sea just offshore from Grom'gol Base Camp, the Vile Reef is known for its vivid marine growth and perilous inhabitants. The seabed is dotted with the weathered stonework of submerged troll ruins alongside the enigmatic Altar of the Tides. Flocks of territorial murlocs lurk among the coral shelves and shattered timbers of passing vessels, fiercely defending the shallow waters and preying upon any diver who braves the deep in search of giant clams and rare blue pearls.

name.deDE: Elende Satyrn! Die Dryaden sind in Gefahr!

text.enUS: Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger!. Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger! is an urgent Alliance quest begun in Ashenvale by the dryad Illiyana. Desperate for aid, she recruits travelers to search for her missing sisters who ventured into the corrupted ruins of Xavian to recover a stolen sacred relic. While resting in Ashenvale, the dryad Illiyana finds herself overwhelmed with worry. A band of her dryad sisters departed into the corrupted northern reaches of the forest on a perilous mission to recover the Branch of Cenarius, a holy relic stolen by the vile satyrs. Though they promised to return swiftly, two days have passed in silence, prompting Illiyana to plead with passing Alliance travelers to track them down before it is too late.

Vilebranch Hooligans. Smith Slagtree of Revantusk Village says Vilebranch trolls invaded the village and stole his tools. He keeps spare tools, but the stolen set was a gift from a kind-hearted gnome who saved his life when he was a young orc, and he wants it back. Vilebranch trolls invaded Revantusk Village and stole Smith Slagtree's tools. He has backup tools, but the stolen set was a gift from a kind-hearted gnome who saved his life when he was a young orc. He tells you the tools mean the world to him and asks you to recover them.

Vimes's Report. Captain Garran Vimes rates your work as the best Vimes has seen from an amateur. Lady Jaina Proudmoore asked Vimes to keep her apprised of a delicate situation, and Vimes gives you the report to bring to her in Theramore. Lady Proudmoore asked Captain Vimes to keep her apprised of a delicate situation, and Vimes has not spoken with her for some time. Vimes meant to deliver the report later, but now judges it more fitting for you to speak with her about it, since you may well have better answers for her questions than Vimes would.

Vimes's Report. Lady Jaina Proudmoore has read Captain Garran Vimes's report and thanks you for your help with the investigation. She asks you to return to Vimes and help get to the bottom of the mystery. Going by Captain Vimes's report, Lady Proudmoore sees that you have been a great help to his investigation, and she thanks you for it. She is easier in her mind knowing the matter rests in such capable hands. She asks you to return to Captain Vimes in Theramore and help him get to the bottom of this mystery.

Viscous Fallout. Viscous Fallout is a toxic water elemental wandering the irradiated corridors of Gnomeregan, a living mass of the poison that fouled the city after Mekgineer Thermaplugg's devastating radiation release. When Gnomeregan was flooded with radiation on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's treacherous advice to wipe out the invading troggs, the fallout left the city's lower levels awash in toxic slime and contamination. Viscous Fallout is a water elemental of that poisoned depth, its very substance thick with the city's toxic waste. Where it came from before the fall is not known.

Visit the Herbalist. Following a meal delivery to his remote post, Guard Parker asks a favor before you return to the Lakeshire inn. Hoping to express his feelings for Darcy, he sends you to the local herbalist to purchase flowers. Parker insists that the herbalist not be told who ordered them or who they are intended for. Stationed along the lonely southern approach to Lakeshire, Guard Parker spends his watch keeping an eye out for blackrock orcs and gnolls. When you bring him a warm meal from Darcy at the Lakeshire Inn, he seizes the opportunity to reciprocate her kindness. Instead of letting you simply walk back, he asks you to stop by the local herbalist shop on the west end of town and purchase a bouquet of flowers for her.

Vital Intelligence. Vital Intelligence marks the end of a freshly risen Forsaken's training in Deathknell. Entrusted with intercepted Scarlet Crusade documents, the courier is sent out into Tirisfal Glades to report to Executor Zygand in Brill. Having neutralized local threats and intercepted a courier of the Scarlet Crusade, newly recruited Forsaken are deemed ready for broader service. Executor Arren entrusts the recovered intelligence to the player, directing them out through the sheltered canyon of Deathknell and east along the road toward Brill, past Cold Hearth Manor.

Vol'jin. In Orgrimmar, Vol'jin advises Warchief Thrall while seeking a lasting home for his people. The Darkspear chieftain is a master shadow hunter. Vol'jin leads the Darkspear after his father, Sen'jin, dies on their ancestral island. Sea witch-worshipping murlocs and human forces nearly destroy the isolated tribe, but Thrall's orcs intervene and forge a deep bond with the trolls. After fleeing the ruined islands, Vol'jin pledges his people to the New Horde and brings them across the Great Sea to Kalimdor.

Volcor. Volcor lies wounded in Blackwood Den, deep in southern Darkshore. The night elf scout depends on his bear Grimclaw and Auberdine's defenders to escape the hostile furbolgs. Volcor is a night elf scout wounded inside Blackwood Den. While tracking the corrupted Blackwood tribe through its underground lair, he was ambushed and badly hurt. He could not fight past the hostile furbolgs alone, so he sent Grimclaw, his loyal bear companion, into the wilds of Darkshore to seek help in Auberdine.
Voodoo Charm. In Teldrassil’s barrows, the Voodoo Charm can break the Gnarlpine enchantment holding Oben Rageclaw’s body.

Voodoo Dues. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley in Booty Bay needs to balance his books by collecting outstanding debts from three old associates. Though rumors claim the men were cursed and bewitched into wandering ancient jungle ruins, MacKinley expects their prized possessions retrieved regardless of their grim fate. Following your earlier collection efforts for "Sea Wolf" MacKinley, the pirate still holds an active ledger of unsettled debts. Three particular debtors—Maury "Club Foot" Wilkins, Jon-Jon the Crow, and Chucky "Ten Thumbs"—have let their accounts sit delinquent for months. MacKinley initially assumed the trio merely skipped out of Booty Bay to avoid paying, but he later heard they met a stranger and darker fate deep in the jungle.

Vorlus Vilehoof. In Darnassus, young night elf warriors face a trial set by Elanaria. They must hunt a satyr who has defiled a hidden moonwell near the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Elanaria asks you to prove your dedication and discipline before she teaches advanced martial techniques. She needs more than words from those who defend Kalimdor. A guardian must face corruption and cleanse the sacred boughs of Teldrassil.

Vorn Skyseer. Vorn Skyseer is a peaceful tauren resident of Camp Narache atop Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. Resting among the camp's tents, he greets young adventurers beginning their journeys and introduces them to local life. Situated in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, Vorn Skyseer serves as an informal welcoming presence for young tauren. As they undertake their rites of passage before venturing into the wider valleys of Mulgore, Vorn offers kind words and hospitality, helping new arrivals settle into the camp.

Vorsha the Lasher. Vorsha the Lasher is a violent hydra terrorizing the Horde's foothold at Zoram'gar Outpost along the coast of Ashenvale. Revering the creature's ferocity, the local naga maintain an offering brazier on an offshore island to honor her. By extinguishing this sacred flame, Horde champions provoke Vorsha and draw her ashore to end her predatory assaults. Zoram'gar Outpost sits on a tenuous strip of coast in northwestern Ashenvale, constantly besieged by hostile wildlife, night elves, and serpentine invaders. Among the most destructive threats prowling the Zoram Strand is Vorsha the Lasher, a gargantuan hydra known for brutal, unprovoked strikes against the outpost. The beast emerges from the surf to crush fortifications and butcher warriors before vanishing back into the deep tides.

Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. Vul'Gol Ogre Mound is a sunken basin in southern Duskwood overrun by the Splinter Fist ogres under the brute Zzarc'Vul. Once a cluster of human homesteads, its ruined farmhouses and subterranean cavern are now littered with the carcasses and scavenged plunder of the clan. Tucked away in the shadows southwest of the fork heading toward Stranglethorn Vale, the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound serves as the seat of the Splinter Fist clan in Duskwood. The basin was once peaceful farmland, but its human inhabitants have long since fled or perished, leaving behind hollowed-out cabins now claimed by lumbering ogres and used as crude shelters. Inside the cavern beneath the rise, piles of slaughtered black bears attest to the clan's voracious appetite. Their chieftain, Zzarc'Vul, rules over the encampment, hoarding odd trinkets alongside mundane scavenged goods.

WANTED: Andre Firebeard. A wanted notice in Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port names the pirate Andre Firebeard, who stands accused of crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan. The notice declares that his head, delivered to Security Chief Bilgewhizzle at Steamwheedle Port, counts as a binding contract. The notice calls Andre Firebeard a vile pirate, accused of crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan. The governing counsel has decreed that anyone who reads it may use lethal force in capturing Andre and those who aid him. He is to be found at the pirate enclave a way south along the coast from Steamwheedle Port, where he stands by a campfire inside the walls.

WANTED: Baron Longshore. On Ratchet's docks, Chief Engineer Gazlowe posts a bounty for Baron Longshore. The pirate captain hails from Gilneas and commands vessels of the Southsea Freebooters. His presence along the Merchant Coast threatens goblin merchant shipping across the region. South of Ratchet, the Southsea Freebooters hold fortified camps along the Merchant Coast. Their pirates harass merchant vessels and disrupt the sea lanes the Steamwheedle Cartel relies on between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and points beyond. Under captains such as Baron Longshore, the raids drain the local goblin administration and threaten trade along the coast.

WANTED: Baron Vardus. A notice carrying High Executor Darthalia's order names Baron Vardus, a human and a high-ranking member of the Syndicate, wanted dead for crimes against the Forsaken. Proof of his death is to be brought to Darthalia in Tarren Mill. Darthalia has put a price on Baron Vardus, a human charged with crimes against the Forsaken and counted among the Syndicate's high-ranking members. Last word placed him in the Uplands of the Alterac Mountains, to the north of Tarren Mill. The order is plain: he is to die, and whoever brings Darthalia proof of his death will be paid for it.

WANTED: Bruuz. Bruuz threatens the harbor traffic that keeps Ratchet busy. Gazlowe has posted a bounty for the huge shark prowling the docks and disrupting coastal trade. Ratchet is the primary neutral gateway between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, and its trade depends on merchant ships. Lately, a huge shark called Bruuz has been prowling the bay. Dockworkers gave the shark its name after it began attacking small skiffs, sailors, and cargo being unloaded near the docks. Its presence disrupts the port and puts the ships that keep Ratchet supplied at risk.

name.zhCN: 通缉：卡利夫·斯科比斯汀

text.enUS: WANTED: Caliph Scorpidsting. The Gadgetzan Water Company posts a bounty on Caliph Scorpidsting, who heads the Wastewander outlaws. Proof of his death goes to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan. Notices at Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port announce a high bounty from the Gadgetzan Water Company for Caliph Scorpidsting, who leads the Wastewander outlaws. The charges against him are the murder of company employees, the theft of company resources and the seizure of company property. Proof of his death is to go to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan.

WANTED: Chok'sul. A bounty posted in Thelsamar by Magistrate Bluntnose calls for the death of Chok'sul, an ogre warlord menacing northeastern Loch Modan. Believed to be organizing the assaults against local settlements and critical infrastructure, bringing his head secures a handsome reward from the town's leadership. While troggs and wildlife constantly test the borders of Loch Modan, the arrival of organized ogres represents an escalation that the local dwarven mountaineers cannot ignore. Settling into encampments along the rugged northeastern reaches of the valley, these brutes have moved beyond simple scavenging. According to local scouts and town authorities, their raids are focused, persistent, and dangerous.

WANTED: Incinerator Gar'im. WANTED: Incinerator Gar'im is a bounty posted by the authorities in Lakeshire against a hostile orc commander entrenched in Render's Valley. Gar'im commands a dangerous contingent of shadowcasters and is purported to be working with the Blackrock clan holding Stonewatch Keep. Magistrate Solomon offers a handsome bounty for proof of his demise. The Redridge Mountains have grown increasingly perilous as the Blackrock orcs push out from their mountain bastions. In Render's Valley, Incinerator Gar'im leads an active incursion, spearheading dark sorcery alongside loyal shadowcasters. With the local town guard stretched thin and the crown's armies largely absent, Magistrate Solomon has turned to independent mercenaries to eliminate Gar'im, who is purported to be working with the Blackrock of Stonewatch Keep.

WANTED: Jai'vhanel. WANTED: Jai'vhanel is an Alliance bounty posted by the Auberdine Village Council in Darkshore. The notice calls for the elimination of Jai'vhanel, a maddened black owl known as 'Swordfeather' that has begun ambushing travelers along the road near Auberdine. Adventurers must hunt the creature near the ruins of Ameth'Aran and bring proof of her death to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea. A posted notice from the Auberdine Village Council alerts travelers along the coastal roads of Darkshore to a dangerous menace. A prominent local owl known as Jai'vhanel, nicknamed 'Swordfeather', has succumbed to a sudden madness. Rather than keeping to the dense wilderness, she has begun ambushing travelers and couriers journeying near Auberdine, transforming an ordinary woodland predator into a critical hazard for the settlement.

WANTED: Marez Cowl. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty quest issued against a high-ranking Syndicate operative entrenched within the ruins of Stromgarde. As both an influential advisor and a dark warlock trafficking with demons, Cowl represents a severe threat to the Alliance forces attempting to secure the Arathi Highlands. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty decree posted to eliminate one of the Syndicate's key leadership figures in the Arathi Highlands. Marez Cowl serves as a high-ranking advisor and field operative within the organization, orchestrating their activities in the ruined capital of Stromgarde. By placing a price on her head, Alliance commanders at Refuge Pointe aim to decapitate the Syndicate's local command structure.

WANTED: Murkdeep!. Auberdine posts an Alliance bounty for Murkdeep, blamed for a Sentinel's death and ships lost off Darkshore. The village council wants the dangerous murloc chieftain dead. Find him south along the misty coast. The Greymist murlocs along Darkshore are usually a nuisance, but Murkdeep has turned against Auberdine. The wanted poster outside the inn names him as the killer of at least one night elf Sentinel. It also suspects him of sabotaging or wrecking two cargo vessels offshore. With ships lost and raids along the coast, the Auberdine Village Council has set a public bounty on the murloc leader.
