text.enUS: Whitestone Oak Lumber. Whitestone Oak Lumber is a sturdy crafting timber sourced from the subterranean shipyards beneath Moonbrook. Prized for its strength, it serves as a critical shaft material for sacred armaments forged by Alliance master smiths.

Wild Hearts. Wild Hearts is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest tasked by Rane Yorick. To save her brother Quinn from wounds inflicted by the ghoul Ivar the Foul, you must harvest discolored worg hearts and deliver them to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher for an alchemical remedy. Following the disastrous mission that left the Deathstalkers pinned down at a farm in northern Silverpine, Rane Yorick finds herself attending to her severely wounded brother, Quinn. The feral ghoul Ivar the Foul left Quinn mangled and failing to recover. Knowing conventional rest will not restore an undead body torn by such savagery, Rane looks to the macabre arts of the Royal Apothecary Society to stitch her brother back together.

Wild Shore. The Wild Shore is the southernmost coastline of Stranglethorn Vale, where the jungle meets the waves of the South Seas. It serves as a staging ground and anchorage for the Bloodsail Buccaneers, whose ships lie moored along the shallows. Stretching along the bottom tip of the continent, the Wild Shore marks the border where Stranglethorn Vale plunges into the South Seas. To the northwest lies the fortified inlet of Booty Bay, while a shallow ocean strait separates the mainland beach from Jaguero Isle to the east. The beach continues northeast toward the Crystal Shore. Because of its secluded position away from the Blackwater Raiders' direct cannons, the coast has become a hotbed of piratical activity and wild perils.

Wildbend River. Near the Grove of the Ancients, Wildbend River carries demonic poison toward the sea. Its tainted waters run through southern Darkshore from the corrupted heights of Felwood, endangering the wilderness. Wildbend River brings corruption, not clean nourishment, to southern Darkshore. It flows west past the Grove of the Ancients and empties into the sea. The river continues from Felwood's Bloodvenom River, tumbling through rocky ridges with foul runoff. Night elves watch its banks for twisted wildlife and the spread of demonic blight.

Wilder Thistlenettle. Wilder Thistlenettle is a dwarven miner brooding in a tavern within Stormwind's Dwarven District. The sole survivor of a tragic cave-in deep within the Deadmines, he is haunted by the gruesome fate of his mining company and his brother. Wilder Thistlenettle can be found drowning his sorrows in an alehouse near the southeastern gates of the Dwarven District. Years ago, he joined an expedition into the deep lodes of Moonbrook's Deadmines alongside his brother and their companions. A catastrophic cave-in sealed the rest of the crew in the dark while Wilder barely made it to the surface alive.

Wildhammer clan. The Wildhammer clan is a rugged, nature-dwelling branch of the dwarven race famed for taming wild gryphons and wielding storm-charged hammers. Driven from their ancestral fortress of Grim Batol centuries ago, they carved a fiercely independent home across the wooded peaks of the Hinterlands. Though reclusive by nature, they remain stalwart friends of the Alliance, defending the skies whenever called upon. Before the War of the Three Hammers, the Wildhammers lived in the foothills around Ironforge. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died, civil war fractured the dwarven kingdom, and the victorious Bronzebeards claimed Ironforge for themselves. Thane Khardros led his clan north to establish a magnificent hold inside the peak of Grim Batol. Yet peace was short-lived: the defeated Dark Irons soon laid siege to the fortress. While Khardros personally slew the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud, her dying curse blighted the mountain so deeply that the halls became uninhabitable. Refusing an invitation to move back under Bronzebeard rule, the Wildhammers chose self-reliance, marching north into the forests and rocky crags of the Hinterlands.

Wildmane Cleansing. Wildmane Cleansing marks the culmination of the tauren ritual efforts to purify the vital watering holes of Mulgore. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, heroes take the completed Wildmane Totem north to cleanse the final poisoned well. Driving back goblin pollutants restores balance to the plains and secures the pastoral livelihood of the tauren tribes. Water is sacred lifeblood across the sun-drenched plains of Mulgore, sustaining the herds, the soil, and the nomadic tribes who have recently gathered around Thunder Bluff. When the Venture Company and encroaching goblins began contaminating these aquifers with toxic industrial runoff, the tauren elders recognized an existential threat. Following the purification of the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, the Wildmane Water Well stands as the third and final corrupted site requiring spiritual intervention.

Wildmane Cleansing Totem. The Wildmane Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted to purify the northern water well of Mulgore. Entrusted to young defenders of the land, it serves as the final instrument in driving out the toxic corruption left by encroaching goblin ventures. When goblin ventures began poisoning the land and fouling Mulgore's scarce water supplies, the tauren turned to sacred ritual to reverse the blight. After cleansing both the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn water wells, Mull Thunderhorn crafts this final totem to purge the remaining corruption at the Wildmane Water Well north of Thunder Bluff. Infused with natural spirits, the totem cleanses the fetid waters so pure life can nourish the plains once more.

Wildmane Totem. Wildmane Totem represents the third and final stage in Mull Thunderhorn's efforts to craft cleansing totems for Mulgore's poisoned wells. To restore the Wildmane Well, the ritual demands offerings taken from the territory's fiercest natural predators: prairie wolf alphas. After securing the materials required to consecrate totems for the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, only one afflicted source remains in central Mulgore: the Wildmane Well. The poisoned water across the plains threatens both migrating wildlife and settlements, demanding powerful primal ingredients to restore the earth's natural balance.

Wildmane Water Well. The Wildmane Water Well is the northernmost of the sacred water wells scattered across Mulgore, resting just north of the mesas of Thunder Bluff. Vital to the plains and their herds, it has become a contested flashpoint targeted by goblin opportunists seeking to choke the tauren's lifeblood. For generations, the nomadic tauren have relied on sacred water wells dug across the golden plains of Mulgore to sustain their people and their wandering kodo herds. The Wildmane Well guards the northern expanse just beyond the shadow of Thunder Bluff. Its vital importance makes it an irresistible target for enemies of the tribes. The goblins of the Venture Company have fouled it with their poisons in a bid to control the regional water supply, and only a cleansing ritual with a totem crafted by the tauren can make its waters pure again.

Wiley the Black. At the Lakeshire Inn, Wiley the Black keeps out of sight. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle and shares what he knows of the Defias Brotherhood. Wiley the Black keeps to the Lakeshire Inn, away from Westfall's turmoil and Redridge's gnoll-infested borders. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia, who once saved him. Stoutmantle grumbles that he should have let Wiley rot. When the militia needs insight into the Defias conspiracy, it turns to Wiley. He reluctantly shares covert intelligence to repay his debt.

Wiley's Note. Wiley's Note is a confidential missive penned by the Lakeshire rogue Wiley the Black, paid as a debt to Gryan Stoutmantle. Its contents reveal alarming alliances formed by the Defias Brotherhood and draw Stormwind's intelligence service into the investigation. Penned in Redridge by the shady rogue Wiley the Black, this scribbled dispatch is handed over to settle an old favor owed to Gryan Stoutmantle. Within, Wiley exposes what he knows about the Defias Brotherhood's clandestine ambitions. His intelligence reveals that the brotherhood is not operating alone: they have brokered alliances with regional gnolls, kobolds, and goblin operatives to further their operations across the kingdom.

Willem. Outside Northshire Abbey, Willem sends recruits to meet the valley's threats. He serves under Marshal McBride in the Stormwind Army, with the Defias Brotherhood pressing into Northshire. Deputy Willem watches the gates of Northshire Abbey, where the Stormwind Army keeps a foothold in the valley. The kingdom's soldiers are spread across many territories, leaving local defense to small groups like Marshal McBride's garrison. Willem meets incoming volunteers and sends them to aid residents and guard the valley's edges.

William Pestle. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle gathers supplies for Stormwind's apothecary. He and his brother Morgan run the shop in the Trade District, and William hires travelers to find candles, kelp, and herbs. William works from Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn while his brother Morgan Pestle tends the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind City's Trade District. From Elwynn Forest, William works with local gatherers to secure raw materials the city shops need. He sends regular shipments to the capital, where Stormwind's citizens rely on a steady supply of restorative salves, draughts, and powders.

William's Shipment. In Goldshire, William Pestle packs candles from Elwynn's kobolds for his brother Morgan in Stormwind. William Pestle keeps trade moving between Goldshire and the capital. He gathers materials in Elwynn Forest, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot leave his duties to travel north, so he depends on couriers to carry the parcel of wax and candles into the city.

Williden Marshal. Williden Marshal is the ambitious human leader of Marshal's Expedition, based out of Marshal's Refuge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Driven by the lure of rare flora, mysterious crystals, and profitable scientific research, he brought his team into the crater only to watch their lower camps overrun by the basin's colossal beasts. Williden Marshal brought an entire scientific expedition deep into Un'Goro Crater seeking fortune and discovery. Intrigued by accounts of alien crystals, uncataloged plants, and untapped resources, he established multiple forward camps across the valley floor. However, the primeval wilderness quickly turned against them. The savage beasts of the crater dismantled their research posts, forcing Williden and his survivors to retreat up into the northern cliffs to establish Marshal's Refuge.

Wind Rider. Wind Rider is a Horde quest offered by Elu atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Aspiring to become a wind rider himself, Elu tasks adventurers with climbing into the craggy heights of Highperch to gather wild wyvern eggs to bolster the Horde's aerial mount reserves. Across Kalimdor, the Horde relies heavily on wind riders to ferry couriers, scouts, and warriors across vast distances. At Freewind Post, a young tauren named Elu aspires to join their esteemed ranks. With the demands of the expanding Horde outpacing the availability of mounts, Elu has been charged with helping procure new wyverns to supply the master wind riders, offering eager travelers a chance to assist in this vital effort.

Windbreak Canyon. Windbreak Canyon is a winding gorge along the northern side of Thousand Needles, situated between Freewind Post and the Shimmering Flats. Famous for its harsh drafts and jagged stone, it is heavily infested with nesting wind serpents. Travelers passing along the main road must tread carefully near its mouth to avoid being hunted from above. Carved into the sheer northern walls of the canyon floor, Windbreak Canyon spans a large stretch of territory east of Freewind Post. Rather than offering shelter, the ravine channels whistling winds between the rock spires, creating ideal perches for feral wind serpents. The predators lay their clutches along the stone ledges and strike at unwary travelers drifting off the main road. Those braving the canyon interior will also find the winding trails that climb upward toward the Weathered Nook.

Windfury Ridge. Windfury Ridge is a rugged highland area flanking the pastures of Mulgore. Notorious for harboring vicious harpies alongside predatory wolves and cougars, it poses a constant hazard to travelers while offering prized feathers to tauren artisans. Windfury Ridge rises sharply above Mulgore's serene plains, serving as the hunting grounds of the Windfury harpies. These vicious winged creatures nest high along the crags, readily swooping down upon any unwary wanderers who skirt the hills. The rocky terrain is further populated by prowling prairie wolves and wild mountain cougars, making the ridge one of the more treacherous borders of the tauren heartland. Despite the danger, the harpies are frequently hunted by brave tauren warriors; their vibrant, iridescent plumage is highly sought after across Thunder Bluff to adorn ceremonial garments for lavish feasts and wedding celebrations.

Winds in the Desert. A stolen supply caravan leaves Rezlak waiting in Durotar. Dustwind harpies ambushed it in Razorwind Canyon, scattering the construction materials among the cliffs. Rezlak came directly from Ratchet, sent by Chief Engineer Gazlowe to help the Horde build across Durotar. The harsh, barren land already makes fortification work hard. Now shipments keep vanishing before they reach the building sites, and without the cargo, work stops. The irritable goblin supervisor has nothing to build with.

Windshear Crag. Windshear Crag is a heavily despoiled valley in the central Stonetalon Mountains, stripped of its ancient timber by the Venture Company. Once a lush forest, the region is now an industrial wasteland dominated by whirring shredders, murky runoff, and aggressive logging crews. In the shadows of the machinery, local kobolds burrow for ore while mountain passes connect the scarred landscape to Ashenvale. Not long ago, Windshear Crag was a thick, old-growth woodland flanking the slopes of Stonetalon. That tranquil wilderness vanished when the Venture Company arrived in search of profit. Today, the basin is filled with severed stumps, acrid smog, and clanking machinery. The entire logging enterprise is overseen by Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a leper gnome whose engineering genius produced the Super Reaper 6000—a mechanical terror capable of reducing massive trunks to kindling in moments. From an elevated platform above the polluted Cragpool Lake, Gerenzo directs an unchecked operation that strips the mountain bare, earning the hostility of rival engineers and local inhabitants alike.

Windtotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder receives travelers on a bluff above Ratchet. She welcomes those who honor the wisdom of ages past and offers an ancestral blessing and guidance to other elders across Kalimdor. On a grassy hill just northwest of Ratchet’s flight master, Windtotem the Elder watches over the goblin docks and open sea. Iron, gunpowder, and coin pass through the harbor below, while quiet Barrens winds and a shaft of celestial light reach the elder.

text.enUS: Wine Shop Advert. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina draws passersby to his family's wine shop. He offers a voucher for a free bottle of vintage wine from their canal-side storefront, a small sign of trade in the reconstructed capital. Everyday life in Stormwind revolves around brisk commerce. Renato Gallina walks the Trade District's cobbled streets, promoting Gallina Winery, the small shop he runs with his sister, Suzetta. He hands flyers to thirsty travelers and locals, each offering a free tasting.

Wine Ticket. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina hands out Wine Tickets to bring customers to his family's shop. Present one to Suzetta Gallina for a complimentary bottle of Pinot Noir. Renato Gallina promotes the Gallina Winery with printed tickets near Stormwind's Trade District. The winery is a boutique vintage shop along the nearby canals. Each ticket promises a complimentary sample of Pinot Noir, drawing curious passersby and newly arrived adventurers toward the family business in hopes they become loyal customers.

Winna Hazzard. Winna Hazzard is an eccentric Forsaken researcher stationed at Bloodvenom Post in Felwood. Accompanied by a feline companion and known for bouts of maniacal laughter, she studies the blighted ecosystem and conducts unsettling experiments with the zone's corrupted fauna. Winna Hazzard represents the Forsaken interest in Felwood's unnatural decay. Stationed in the Horde enclave of Bloodvenom Post, she spends her time observing the local wildlife and formulating experiments utilizing tainted waters and venomous samples. Her jovial, manic demeanor often masks callous motives, evident when she uses tainted liquids drawn from the land to corrupt the small kitten that stays by her side.

Winstone Wolfe. Winstone Wolfe is a human operative affiliated with the secretive Ravenholdt organization, stationed at their secluded estate nestled between Hillsbrad and the Alterac Mountains. He keeps watch over the estate's grounds and groundskeepers, serving as one of the trusted contacts within the hidden league of thieves and assassins. Tucked away in the hidden valley of Ravenholdt Manor, Winstone Wolfe operates among the ranks of Lord Jorach Ravenholdt's syndicate. Quiet, watchful, and practical, Wolfe is one of the capable hands who handles business around the manor, ensuring that only those with proper discretion and talent walk the grounds undisturbed.

Winter's Presents. Winter's Presents is an Alliance holiday breadcrumb quest celebrating the Feast of Winter Veil in Ironforge. Joyful revelers and PX-238 Wonderform Operators urge travelers to visit Greatfather Winter beside the Smokywood Pastures market stalls. There, beneath the grand holiday tree, festive gifts await hearty adventurers. As the chill of winter sets in across the peaks of Khaz Modan, Ironforge transforms into the heart of Alliance festivities for the Feast of Winter Veil. Revelers and holiday enthusiasts throughout the city spread word of good cheer, excitedly directing passersby toward the grand decorated tree nestled near the Smokywood Pastures vendors.

Winter's Presents. In Orgrimmar, Winter's Presents await beneath the festive tree during the Feast of Winter Veil. Holiday organizers and goblin apparatus tenders direct Horde heroes to Great-father Winter, where gifts have been prepared for them. The Feast of Winter Veil brings a pause for celebration to Orgrimmar as the chill winds of late year sweep across Durotar. Promoters from Smokywood Pastures and holiday enthusiasts spread word through the capital that gifts wait beneath the decorated tree. Warriors, hunters, and wanderers resting in the city are all invited to share in the season’s generosity.

Winterfall Village. Winterfall Village is a sprawling furbolg encampment nestled in the snowdrifts of eastern Winterspring, just east of Everlook. Once peaceful kin to the other ursine tribes of Kalimdor, the Winterfall furbolgs living here have descended into madness and violent corruption under the rule of High Chief Winterfall. Sprawled across the terraced snowbanks east of the goblin trading post Everlook, Winterfall Village serves as the primary bastion of the Winterfall furbolgs in Winterspring. Like their cousins scattered across northern Kalimdor, these bear-folk were warped and driven mad by the lingering foulness of the Burning Legion's invasion. Led by High Chief Winterfall from a secluded cavern atop the settlement's highest tier, the tribe has abandoned its ancestral ways. Instead of communing peacefully with the wild spirits of the snow, the enraged furbolgs now aggressively assault travelers, patrol the mountain passes, and threaten any who come near their frost-bitten home.

Winterhoof Cleansing. Winterhoof Cleansing is a rite entrusted to Horde adventurers by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. After goblin operations fouled the local springs, a consecrated totem must be carried into the Venture Company's territory to purify the Winterhoof Water Well. Restoring this spring is a vital first step in healing the poisoned waters of central Mulgore. The grassy plains of Mulgore rely on a delicate network of ancestral water wells to sustain both wild game and the scattered tauren tribes. Recently, ruthless industrial mercenaries of the Venture Company moved into the rolling hills southeast of Bloodhoof Village. Their operations have contaminated the local aquifers, leaving the Winterhoof Water Well rank and toxic. Wild beasts shun the tainted water, and the nearby camps face an impending crisis if the corruption spreads further through the earth.

Winterhoof Cleansing Totem. The Winterhoof Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. Carved to undo the toxic blight spread by Venture Company intruders, it channels the Earth Mother's power to purify the polluted Winterhoof Water Well. When the goblin engineers of the Venture Company encroached upon the plains of Mulgore, their industrial operations quickly tainted the land's precious subterranean water tables. In response, Mull Thunderhorn prepared the Winterhoof Cleansing Totem, imbuing the carved wood with protective magic intended to wash out the foreign poisons. Carried past hostile goblin guards to the edge of the Winterhoof Water Well, the totem disperses the contamination through a focused ritual, restoring pure drinking water to the wandering herds and native tribes of the plains.

Winterhoof Water Well. The Winterhoof Water Well is a vital fresh water source situated on the edge of the Rolling Plains in southern Mulgore. Crucial to the local wildlife and nomadic tauren tribes, the well has recently fallen under threat from the exploitative Venture Company, who seek to poison and control the region's water supply. In the arid stretches of central Kalimdor, water is life, and Mulgore's subterranean wells sustain both the herds of the plains and the encampments of the tauren. The Winterhoof Water Well, named for one of the respected tribes of the plains, taps into the deep aquifers beneath the Rolling Plains. Unfortunately, its strategic importance has drawn the avarice of the Venture Company. Rather than sharing the land or negotiating, the ruthless goblin cartel has attempted to poison the water supply to exert leverage over the surrounding territory.

Wisdom of Agamaggan. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth trades the wisdom of Agamaggan for blood shards. The captive quilboar offers Horde spellcasters a ritual drawn from the ancient boar god’s power. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth is held prisoner by the Horde. The quilboar trades his people’s magical secrets for blood shards, crimson crystals said to have formed from Agamaggan’s spilled blood. The towering boar Demigod died in the War of the Ancients. Mangletooth says the geomancers and shaman of his tribes use the shards to channel divine power in their rituals.

Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil is a Darkspear troll mystic dwelling in a cave at Malaka'jin in the southern Stonetalon Mountains. A longtime comrade of Darsok Swiftdagger and the shadow hunter Rokhan, he turns dark voodoo and ritual sorcery against the Horde's local enemies. Secluded inside an eastern cavern above the camp of Malaka'jin, Jin'Zil practices ancient jungle troll arts away from the coastal home of his tribe. Surrounded by bubbling cauldrons and captive prisoners, he gathers exotic reagents from the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains to weave potent blessings and curses in defense of the Horde's mountain encampment.

Witch Doctor Uzer'i. Witch Doctor Uzer'i is a jungle troll mystic residing at Camp Mojache in the primordial forests of Feralas. Dedicated to advancing the magical capabilities of the Horde, he researches techniques to trap and harness the muisek—the spiritual essence of powerful natural creatures. By capturing these ancient forest spirits, Uzer'i seeks to channel the raw primal energies traditionally favored by night elves directly into enchanted weapons. Rooted in traditional troll spiritualism, Witch Doctor Uzer'i has spent considerable effort studying the natural magic inherent to the untamed wilderness of Feralas. He argues that night elves have drawn upon the spirits of forest beasts for millennia, and believes the time has come for the Horde to seize those same primal forces. Central to his study is the concept of muisek: the vibrant spiritual essence that remains within a creature. To harness it, Uzer'i crafts specialized vessels capable of rapidly shrinking fallen beings before their escaping spirit disperses, allowing the essence to be stored and studied.

Witch Hill. Witch Hill is a dreary, mist-shrouded rise in the heart of Dustwallow Marsh along the path toward Theramore. It is best known for the secluded Swamplight Manor, scattered camps of hostile Mirefin murlocs, and sinister rumors of dark hauntings. Rising out of the stagnant waters of Dustwallow Marsh, Witch Hill sits roughly a third of the way along the peninsula leading southeast toward Theramore Isle. The elevated ground provides little refuge from the hazards of the swamp, as aggressive Mirefin murlocs claim the surrounding waters. At its center stands Swamplight Manor, the lonely and unsettling residence of the hermit known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl. Travelers passing through frequently report eerie phenomena and lingering dark presences across the knoll.

Witchwing Talon. In the northwestern Barrens, Witchwing Talons mark dead harpy raiders. Horde scouts at the Crossroads seek them as proof while they work to secure vital caravan routes. Witchwing harpies raid Horde supply caravans from their roosts northwest of the Crossroads. Scout Darsok Swiftdagger coordinates strikes against the flock's hierarchy. Darsok requires physical proof of each dead scavenger, and the talons provide it. With proof that raiders have fallen, the scouts can weaken the flock's ranks before striking higher in its command.

Witherbark Cages. Gryphon Master Talonaxe tells you that Sharpbeak, heir of Swiftwing, the mightiest gryphon, has been lost, and that trolls are believed to have taken the young gryphon. You are asked to look through the cages of the two Witherbark troll villages for any sign of Sharpbeak. Sharpbeak was lost a few days ago while hunting with his parents. Talonaxe and the others believe the trolls took him, and you are asked for your help. Three cages wait to be checked across the two Witherbark troll villages, and Talonaxe wants to hear what you find.

Witherbark Village. Witherbark Village is a forest troll settlement nestled around a secluded lake in the southeastern hills of the Arathi Highlands. Inhabited by the hostile Witherbark tribe, it serves as a staging ground for troll raiders contesting both the Alliance remnants of Stromgarde and the Horde outpost at Hammerfall. Built along the shores of a quiet mountain lake, Witherbark Village houses the fierce forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe. While fishers, axe throwers, and witch doctors occupy the hut-lined waterfront, tribal leaders such as Zalas Witherbark and deadly shadow hunters oversee operations from a massive cavern cavern tucked behind the settlement. The Witherbark maintain an opportunistic alliance with the Boulderfist ogres of Arathi, working together to carve out territory across the highlands—even establishing a firm foothold amidst the ruins of Stromgarde Keep. Fiercely territorial, they lash out at any outsider venturing into their corner of the basin.

Wizbang Cranktoggle. On Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle keeps a network of buzzboxes working from Auberdine. The eccentric gnome engineer lives upstairs at the inn, far from the halls of Gnomeregan and Ironforge. Wizbang Cranktoggle brings Alliance ingenuity to Auberdine. The gnome engineer works on the inn’s upper floor, among tools and spare parts. The night elves here seek harmony with nature and follow ancient customs. Wizbang turns instead to practical mechanical problems, far from the solemn druidic traditions of Kalimdor.

Wizlo Bearingshiner. Wizlo Bearingshiner is a goblin tinkerer stranded at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. The sole survivor of a centaur attack on his caravan, he recruits travelers to recover a valuable Hypercapacitor Gizmo from the wreckage. Staying alongside the tauren at Whitereach Post along the canyon road, Wizlo Bearingshiner faces an unwelcome delay. Centaur attacked his caravan, leaving him as its only survivor. His clients are waiting for their wares, and he worries that he will not deliver them in time.

Wizzle Brassbolts. Wizzle Brassbolts is a gnome engineer stationed alongside his fellow tinkerers out on the salt flats of Thousand Needles. Working with the gnomish racing team at the Mirage Raceway, he seeks durable local materials to reinforce their experimental rocket cars. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between gnomish and goblin engineering takes the form of high-speed rocket car races. Wizzle Brassbolts works as part of the gnomish raceway crew, striving to keep their vehicles intact against blistering speeds and abrasive salt. To bolster their machines, he recruits adventurers to hunt the local wildlife—such as the sturdy turtles wandering the basin—harvesting their hard shells to build new fuel tanks strong enough to hold his brother's corrosive new rocket fuel.

Wizzlecrank's Shredder. In Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank's Shredder sits trapped among Venture Company operators. Pilot Wizzlecrank climbed inside the machine to steal it, but it will not move without a key. Its engine must be started before the goblin can try to escape. Deep in Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank waits inside a motionless shredder. The Venture Company machine is surrounded by hostile mercenaries in the polluted basin. Wizzlecrank climbed aboard to steal it, then learned he needed a key to unlock its movement column. When another shredder operator asked if all was well, he panicked and blamed a mechanical problem. Now he remains sealed inside, with guards and overseers nearby, hoping someone will fetch the key before the Venture Company grows suspicious.

Wolf Heart Sample. Wolf Heart Sample is bound for the Crossroads, carrying diseased wolf tissue from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks to learn what northern toxins do to the Barrens’ native beasts. Wolf Heart Sample began with plagued wolves in Lordaeron’s ruins. Apothecary Renferrel gathered the hearts, and they were packed for the journey across the Great Sea. The Forsaken’s Royal Apothecary Society seeks greater knowledge of venom, blights, and biological reagents. A courier carries the parcel to the Crossroads in the Barrens, linking Undercity’s experiments in the scarred Eastern Kingdoms with Kalimdor’s frontier outposts.

Wolf Heart Samples. Wolf Heart Samples are peculiar organic specimens gathered from corrupted wolves in Silverpine Forest. Despite their lethal toxicity, the hearts beat within the living creatures without killing them, drawing the intense scientific interest of the Royal Apothecary Society. While examining carcasses in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel discovered that certain wolf hearts harbor a deadly compound. Strangely, the level of poison present within the tissue should easily be fatal to the wolves themselves. Recognizing the unique value of a physiology that thrives while saturated in lethal toxicity, Renferrel set aside tissue samples to be dispatched directly to Undercity. For the Forsaken, studying naturally resilient or toxic organisms is a critical step in mastering biological warfare and compounding new reagents.

Wolves Across the Border. Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves prowling Northshire Valley and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where the valley’s needs continue despite the guards’ focus on Defias bandits. Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls with a grudge against the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have limited strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits, while tradesfolk still have daily needs. Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking.

text.enUS: Wolves at Our Heels. Wolves at Our Heels is an Alliance quest offered by Lars at Sven's Camp in western Duskwood. Tasked with hunting the rabid and starving dire wolves stalking the surrounding woods, travelers help clear immediate wilderness threats so Sven and Lars can focus on their vendetta against the necromancer Morbent Fel. Tucked away along the western hills of Duskwood near the Westfall border, Sven Yorgen and his companion Lars maintain an isolated outpost. Living away from Darkshire leaves them entirely reliant on their own foraging and hunting to survive. However, carrying fresh game through these dark woods makes Lars an irresistible target for the ravenous predators stalking the shadowed riverbanks and underbrush.

Wood Pulp. At Bael Modan, Wood Pulp helps the dwarves prepare their blasting charges. The dwarven personnel stationed in the southern Barrens carry it as an absorbent base for stabilizing liquid explosives. At Bael Modan, Ironforge dwarves use earth-moving equipment and chemical explosives to tear into ancestral tauren hunting grounds. Liquid nitroglycerin is unstable on its own, so dwarven engineers soak it into porous wood pulp with sodium nitrate to make stable charges for excavation and combat. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers carry bundles for sapping and field munitions.

Wooden Key. The Wooden Key is a simple carved key carried by the maddened ancients roaming northern Ashenvale near the border of Felwood. It unlocks a concealed chest holding a remnant of Dartol's Rod, an ancient night elven relic. The Wooden Key is held by the Crazed and Withered Ancients wandering the shaded trails north of Raynewood Retreat. Shael'dryn once knew the local treants, but now describes their nature as twisted by corruption. One of them carries the key to a chest holding a piece of Dartol's Rod.

Woodpaw Den. Woodpaw Den is a rugged gnoll stronghold nestled in southern Feralas, just north of the ancient Darkmist Ruins. The settlement serves as a major gathering point for the Woodpaw gnolls and their fiercest pack alphas, making it a dangerous pocket of wilderness within the dense canopy. Situated amidst the towering boughs of Feralas, Woodpaw Den stands as the fortified heartland of the local Woodpaw gnolls. Unlike smaller scout camps scattered along the jungle tracks, this encampment is heavily guarded by the pack's seasoned Alphas. The gnolls here defend their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and the encroaching wilderness. Located just north of the elven remnants at Darkmist Ruins, the den represents an ever-present predatory threat to travelers attempting to traverse the central wilderness of the region.

Woodpaw Hills. The Woodpaw Hills are a rugged, forested stretch of southeastern Feralas claimed by the Woodpaw gnolls. Once a dominant tribal territory, the hills have become an embattled frontline as insectoid terrors tunnel up from below and ancient stone giants stalk the canopy. The dense forests of the Woodpaw Hills serve as the historical territory of the Woodpaw gnoll clan. While the hyena-folk once roamed unchallenged across these slopes, their dominance has crumbled under pressure from multiple fronts. To their southeast, nightmarish silithid swarmers have breached the earth at the Writhing Deep, forcing the gnolls back and compelling their chieftains to retreat deeper into the Woodpaw Den. Adding to the peril, ancient mountain giants—relics summoned down during the Third War to repel the Burning Legion—now wander the hillside woods, crushing any travelers or Horde interlopers who stray into their path.

Woodpaw Investigation. Hadoken Swiftstrider is sure the Woodpaw gnolls follow some written strategy. He sends you to search the gnoll camps south of Camp Mojache for anything resembling battle plans. This comes after Alpha Strike. Hadoken has little respect for gnoll brains, yet he is sure they keep some record of their strategy, as their recent assaults are too well coordinated to be improvised. If he could see those plans, he would better understand what stirred them up. He sends you back to the Woodpaw to find whatever looks like battle plans and bring it to him.

Worgen. Worgen are fierce, lupine humanoids cursed with uncontrollable primal rage, moving upright yet hunting with bestial swiftness. Once thought to be mere nightmares conjured from other planes, these savage pack-hunters now terrorize Silverpine Forest, Ashenvale, and Duskwood. Long before their recent emergence in Lordaeron and Kalimdor, wolf-men were whispered of in folktales and cautionary fables. Their true origins remain a mystery: scholars who have studied the beasts believe they were drawn into Azeroth from another realm, and both Archmage Arugal and the night elves' Scythe of Elune have proven able to call them forth.

Worgen in the Woods. Calor, a disillusioned former guardsman stationed in Darkshire, tasks adventurers with culling the sinister Nightbane Shadow Weavers prowling Duskwood. By taking the hunt to Brightwood Grove and the Rotting Orchard, outsiders can prove their mettle to Master Jonathan Carevin's monster hunters. The Night Watch struggles constantly against the undead, spiders, and outlaws pressing against Darkshire's borders. For some, like Calor, the official guard proved too slow and complacent to cleanse the land. Leaving the Watch behind, Calor threw in his lot with Master Jonathan Carevin, dedicating his blade to the total eradication of heresy and corruption. But Carevin does not accept just anyone into his circle; those seeking to aid their cause must first prove they can survive against the woods' most ferocious horrors.

Worgen in the Woods. As the Nightbane pack encroaches further upon Darkshire, Calor tasks adventurers with striking down the pack's primary rank-and-file stalkers. These ferocious Dark Runners have overrun the nearby Rotting Orchard, threatening to completely surround the besieged town. While scouts first encountered lone worgen weaving shadowy magic on the fringes of the forest, Calor's rangings revealed a far more urgent tactical threat. Larger, swifter beasts known as Nightbane Dark Runners have massed in the Rotting Orchard just southwest of Darkshire. Rather than merely lurking beneath the canopy, these predators form the bulk of the pack's numbers, establishing a staging ground within striking distance of the village gates.

Worgen in the Woods. As the Nightbane pack tightens its grip on Duskwood, Calor directs adventurers to strike against their deadliest ranks. Taking the fight directly to their southern dens and mines, defenders push back the feral threat encroaching on Darkshire. The worgen infestation haunting Duskwood is far from mindless chaos. Having carved out territory in the dark expanse south of Darkshire, the beasts known as the Nightbane have begun establishing fortified camps. Calor watches their bonfires flicker in the distance with growing dread, noting that the creatures have occupied deep caves and abandoned mining shafts. Among them, the Vile Fangs and Tainted Ones represent the most vicious breeds, displaying ferocious savagery and a tenacity that threatens to overwhelm the town's perimeter.

Worgen in the Woods. This errand delivers Calor's letter of recommendation to Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, concluding your pursuit of the savage worgen haunting Duskwood. Impressed by your prowess against the beastly invaders, Calor points you directly to a man fighting deeper threats among the shadows. Having culled the Nightbane pack stalking Roland's Doom and the shadowed glades, you earn the hard-won respect of Calor. Stationed on the darkened frontiers of the woods, Calor is rarely eager to hand out compliments, let alone formal introductions. Handing over a faded scrap of parchment, he directs you to deliver his word directly to Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, remarking that if they had more fighters of your caliber, their small cohort might finally eclipse the town's beleaguered Night Watch.

Workshop Entrance. The Workshop Entrance, commonly known as the backdoor to Gnomeregan, is an access portal situated just beyond the Train Depot. It provides seasoned adventurers and engineers an alternative route into the depths of the irradiated city, bypassing the front gates and opening near the Engineering Labs. Located across the cavernous workshop floor just past the Train Depot, the Workshop Entrance offers a direct approach into the industrial heart of Gnomeregan. Flanked on one side by the opening to the Loading Room, this passage cuts straight through to the Engineering Labs, avoiding the fortified entry gates that leper gnomes and troggs contest near the surface. For strike teams attempting to reclaim the underground capital, bypassing the initial perimeter through this side door can prove vital.

Worn Parchment. At the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, Worn Parchment scraps offer clues to the cultists gathered there. North along Darkshore’s mist-shrouded coast, dark spellcasters and their followers have seized the ruined Tower of Althalaxx. Dark Strand Fanatics patrol the grounds outside and carry scraps of worn parchment among their belongings. One scrap holds only scattered writing and strange symbols. Gathered together, the fragments reveal a previously unknown organization called the Cult of the Dark Strand.

Worn Stone Token. Worn Stone Tokens are small magical talismans carried by personnel and mages associated with Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains. Though their ambient magic has largely faded, they were crafted to help the Kirin Tor bind and command elemental servants. The magi of Dalaran have long possessed a formidable command over elemental entities, using specialized talismans to bend these extradimensional beings to their will. Worn Stone Tokens represent depleted or exhausted versions of these implements. Carried not only by theurgists and summoners but even by Dalaran laborers and guards stationed around the ruins and internment camps of Alterac, they demonstrate how deeply elemental binding is integrated into Dalaran's everyday operations.

Worth Its Weight in Gold. At Refuge Pointe, Apprentice Kryten is after Witherbark tusks, medicine pouches and a shadow hunter's knife, all reagents for Archmage Malin, who sent him and Skuerto to gather them. He asks you to seek them among the Witherbark trolls in the southeast of Arathi. Archmage Malin sent Kryten and Skuerto to Arathi to collect reagents, and Kryten had no idea how to gather them until you arrived. He needs ten Witherbark tusks, four medicine pouches and one shadow hunter knife. The Witherbark trolls make their home in the southeast of Arathi.

Wounded Ancients. Wounded Ancients is an Alliance task given by Kaela Shadowspear in the Stonetalon Mountains. Suspecting that goblin munitions drove the local forest guardians mad, Kaela sends adventurers to recover shrapnel lodged in the corrupted treants so the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle can analyze the taint. The forested groves of Stonetalon were long watched over by towering treants, gentle yet ferocious guardians bound to the health of the land. When the Venture Company moved in with buzzsaws, explosives, and strip-mining operations, nature fought back. The treants successfully repelled the invaders from parts of the vale, but victory came at an insidious cost. The defenders did not return to peaceful guardianship; instead, they devolved into hostile, maddened husks.

Woven Wand. The Woven Wand is a unique enchanted relic crafted long ago by three Dalaran apprentice magi as a pledge of brotherhood. Following the fall of Lordaeron and bitter betrayals among its creators, the wand was hidden away in Fenris Keep before resurfacing in the hands of the Forsaken.

Wrenix of Ratchet. In Orgrimmar, Wrenix of Ratchet draws Horde rogues toward a goblin port far to the south. Zando'zan sends them to aid Wrenix the Wretched, a disreputable goblin in Ratchet. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the rogue guild works out of winding crevices, largely unseen. Zando'zan, a troll who speaks in wild ramblings, greets operatives with ominous portents. His visions include Warchief Thrall struck down by poison and blade. He gives no explanation for the prophecy, and quickly sends agents south to the port town of Ratchet in the Barrens.

Wrenix the Wretched. Beside his strange apparatus in Ratchet, Wrenix the Wretched helps crack tough locks. The goblin tinker offers tools to open secure caches. Wrenix the Wretched works beside his machinery in Ratchet, the goblin port on the Barrens coast. As a tinker of the Steamwheedle Cartel, he knows mechanisms and contraptions, and how to bypass locks and salvage what lies beyond them. Rogues and scouts working the coast can turn to him for help.

Writhing Deep. The Writhing Deep is a massive, insectoid hive complex carved into southeastern Feralas. Inhabited by the Zukk'ash silithid, this subterranean burrow is a growing danger that threatens nearby wildlife and surrounding encampments alike. The relentless expansion of these subterranean predators has upset the regional balance of the lush forest. Tucked away in the humid lowlands of southeastern Feralas, the Writhing Deep serves as the primary colony for the Zukk'ash silithid. Unlike the typical woodland beasts of the valley, these chittering insects dig labyrinthine tunnels and fiercely guard clutches of resinous eggs. The hive's aggressive encroachment into the nearby territories has destabilized the wild fauna and agitated local gnoll packs, pushing displaced and frenzied predators uncomfortably close to both Horde paths and native sanctuaries.

Writhing Haunt. The Writhing Haunt is a blighted farmstead situated east of the Ruins of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands. Once fertile land that fed Lordaeron, it has been seized by the Scourge and transformed into a toxic spreading ground for plague vapors. Like many of the old human homesteads surrounding Andorhal, the farmstead now called the Writhing Haunt fell swiftly during the Third War. Today, the fields do not grow crops but instead harvest rot. The Scourge planted an enormous plague cauldron squarely in the center of the tilled earth, continuously venting noxious, diseased vapors into the air. Rotting ghouls, freezing ghouls, and fetid zombies wander the overgrown furrows, guarding the machinery under the command of Cauldron Lord Razarch.

Wynne Larson. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Wynne Larson supplies mages across the kingdom with robes. Human clothier Wynne relies on local craftsmen since Dalaran and Quel'Thalas fell in the Third War, and points spellcasters toward rare materials for enchanted garments. Before the Third War, Dalaran and Quel'Thalas supplied the finest woven fabrics and enchanted vestments. Their destruction crippled the old trade routes and arcane textile production. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Wynne Larson now works with local tailors and enchanters such as Lucan Cordell. Together, they meet the city's growing demand for robes and spellwoven gear.

Wyrmbog. Wyrmbog is the perilous southern expanse of Dustwallow Marsh, lying just south of the Dragonmurk. Dominated by foul mire and jagged spires of stone, it serves as the staging ground and territorial buffer for the black dragonflight. The caves of ancient wyrms, including the broodmother Onyxia and the elder Emberstrife, are carved directly into its surrounding ridges. Wyrmbog represents the most heavily infested black dragon territory in southern Kalimdor. Where the open waters of Dustwallow give way to scorched muck and towering bones, whelps and mature drakes patrol the fetid air. The bog is choked with toxic fumes and predatory beasts driven wild by the draconic presence. Travelers foolish enough to wander into these reaches find themselves directly in the shadow of Onyxia's Lair and Emberstrife's cavernous den.

Xavathras. Xavathras is a vicious satyr commander residing among the tents at the Ruins of Constellas in Felwood. Leading a band of Jadefire satyrs, he oversees the corruption of an ancient moonwell in service to his master, Xavaric. Within the tainted glades of Felwood, the Ruins of Constellas have fallen into the clutches of the Jadefire satyrs. Stationed in an encampment pitched amidst the elven stonework, Xavathras directs the defilement of a nearby moonwell on behalf of another cruel satyr, Xavaric. By poisoning the pure waters with demonic energy, Xavathras deepens the corruption that grips the forest. His presence poses a direct threat to any attempts to restore the woodland, earning the ire of night elves like Eridan Bluewind who mark him for death.

Xavian. Xavian is an ancient ruined night elf temple complex in northeastern Ashenvale, now overrun and claimed by the satyrs. Serving as the primary seat of satyr influence in the forest, the ruin is foul with demonic corruption and dark rites directed against the woodland. Tucked away in the northeastern hills of Ashenvale, west of Forest Song and north of Satyrnaar, Xavian stands as the foremost bastion of satyr power in the region. Once a sacred elven temple, its stone arches and terraces have been desecrated by followers of the Burning Legion. Leaders among the satyrs, including Prince Raze and Geltharis, oversee their kin from these ruins. They perform defiling rituals across the grounds, even utilizing stolen Warsong oil to further blight the sacred woodland. The area takes its name from Xavius, the highborne councilor who became the first satyr during the War of the Ancients after failing Sargeras.

Xavian Water Sample. A vial of pristine, magically infused water drawn from the base of the highest waterfall in the ancient elven ruins of Xavian. Horde mages in Orgrimmar seek it out to unravel the latent arcane powers preserved in Ashenvale's oldest sacred sites. Xavian is a fabled ancient elven city, and tales of its ancient knowledge are well known among the learned. Even in ruin, its waters are said to hold vast magical powers. Deino, an arcane instructor in Orgrimmar, tasks rising mages with trekking deep into Ashenvale to collect a fresh sample straight from the pool below Xavian's tallest waterfall. Securing it requires braving dangerous territory, as the ruins are now fiercely guarded by corrupt satyrs hostile to any meddling spellcasters.

Yaw Sharpmane. Yaw Sharpmane is an experienced tauren hunter trainer stationed in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He guides young hunters venturing out from Camp Narache, helping them master the wild beasts of their ancestral plains. Positioned amidst the tents and fires of Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane serves the Shu'halo as an instructor in the ways of marksmanship, tracking, and survival. Young hunters who have proven themselves in Red Cloud Mesa are directed to Yaw to hone their craft as they step onto the broader plains of Mulgore.

Yeh'kinya. Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll scholar residing at Steamwheedle Port on the desert coast of Tanaris. Claiming to seek ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers, he dispatches willing adventurers across Azeroth on missions to gather lost troll relics. Lounging among the goblins and dockworkers of Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya presents himself as a quiet student of history and spirits. He recruits travelers to track down obscure magical items across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, from ancient eggs in the Hinterlands to stone prophecy tablets buried in the ruins of Zul'Farrak. While he claims these errands serve peaceful academic inquiry into ancient troll history, his specific focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion from watchful onlookers.

Yojamba Isle. Yojamba Isle is a cluster of small tropical islets off the northwestern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, near the waters leading up to Westfall. It serves as an offshore encampment for the scholarly Zandalar Tribe, who have established a foothold here to observe the growing crisis in the jungle. From these shores, the Zandalari seek willing champions from both the Horde and the Alliance to confront the ancient horrors awakening in Zul'Gurub. While most trolls encountered across Stranglethorn Vale are hostile to outsiders, the Zandalar tribe dwelling on Yojamba Isle maintain an uneasy neutrality. As the ancient priests and lorekeepers of troll civilization, the Zandalari have watched with mounting dread as the Gurubashi trolls within Zul'Gurub turned to Hakkar the Soulflayer. Knowing the world-ending danger a fully summoned blood god represents, the Zandalari have ventured far from their ancestral home to establish this staging ground, calling upon any capable adventurer—regardless of faction—to aid in curbing the threat.

Yorgen Farmstead. The Yorgen Farmstead is a derelict farm nestled in southern Duskwood, fallen into ruin alongside the rest of the troubled region. Formerly owned by the farmer Sven Yorgen, the property has been seized and occupied by brigands of the Defias Brotherhood. Situated amidst the gloomy woodlands of southern Duskwood, the Yorgen Farmstead was once a functioning homestead belonging to Sven Yorgen. Like many isolated holdings in the region, the farm could not withstand the encroaching perils of the territory. Sven was forced to abandon his lands, retreating north to a makeshift camp along the Darkened Bank. In his absence, the abandoned grounds were claimed by outlaws looking for a foothold far from the gaze of Stormwind's authorities.

Yorus Barleybrew. At the Lakeshire Inn, Yorus Barleybrew awaits Alliance warriors bold enough to answer his challenge. Trainers across Alliance capitals send seasoned fighters from Stormwind toward the Redridge borderlands to meet the eccentric dwarf and face his test of arms. Across Alliance capitals, warrior trainers watch fighters who have outgrown their first drills. When an apprentice proves their mettle around their twentieth season, trainers such as Kelv Sternhammer, Wu Shen, and Darnath Bladesinger pass along word of Yorus Barleybrew. The dwarf offers no standard military order. Instead, he has issued an open wager and a test of arms to any Alliance warrior bold enough to answer.

You Too Good.. Lumak sends you from Orgrimmar to find his friend Nat Pagle. Your skill has outgrown ordinary lessons, and Nat camps on a distant islet south of Theramore Isle. Lumak trains fishers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He sees that you have learned all he can teach about rod and reel, and admits you are too good for ordinary lessons. To learn the art of artisan fishing, you must seek knowledge beyond the city and the Horde.

Young Crocolisk Skin. Young Crocolisk Skin is a pliable reptile pelt harvested from juvenile crocolisks throughout the Wetlands. Prized by local tanners like James Halloran of Menethil Harbor, these softer hides are cured and exported to ports across Azeroth. Menethil Harbor serves as a bustling hub of commerce along the western coast of Khaz Modan, exporting marshland goods to distant ports. Among the town's most lucrative exports are the cured hides processed by the harbor's resident tanner, James Halloran. While full-grown crocolisks yield thick, tough scales, their young provide softer, far more workable leather. Because these juvenile skins are delicate and in high demand, Halloran relies on local hunters and passing travelers to scour the boggy marshes just outside town to keep his curing racks stocked.

text.enUS: Young Crocolisk Skins. James Halloran, a prominent tanner based in Menethil Harbor, contracts travelers to supply fresh skins from the marsh's juvenile crocolisks. His cured hides enjoy international maritime demand, making reliable hunting essential to his trade. Supplying these softer materials earns his trust and opens the way to further leatherworking chores. Menethil Harbor is an essential maritime hub connecting the Eastern Kingdoms to distant continents, but it also supports a bustling local economy built around the resources of the surrounding marshland. James Halloran has established an international trade by tanning and curing the tough hides of the region's abundant reptilian predators. Merchants and ships sailing out of Menethil carry Halloran's leather goods to distant ports, creating constant pressure on his workshop to maintain a steady inventory.

Young Lovers. Young Lovers is an Elwynn Forest quest centered on the forbidden romance between Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield. With their rival families locked in a bitter feud, Maybell enlists an adventurer to secretly courier a heartfelt love letter to Tommy Joe by the riverbank. In the pastoral fields of Elwynn Forest, a bitter feud divides two neighboring farming households: the Stonefields and the Maclures. Despite the hostility between their families, young Maybell Maclure has fallen deeply in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield. Unable to visit him openly without igniting family fury, Maybell relies on passing travelers to carry secret correspondence across the boundary lines separating the rival estates.

Your Package Has Arrived. "Your Package Has Arrived" is an urgent courier task concerning misplaced mail intended for delivery in Ironforge. A courier crate sent all the way from the Wildhammer stronghold of Aerie Peak was left abandoned beside a mailbox, addressed specifically to Eldrun Stormbreaker. Travelers who discover the parcel are tasked with completing its journey and seeing that it reaches its rightful owner. A postal mishap leaves several stray parcels abandoned beside a city mailbox, left out in the open rather than carried safely to their destinations. Among this jumbled heap of neglected freight sits an urgent parcel marked for delivery all the way from Aerie Peak, the mountain redoubt of the Wildhammer dwarves in the Hinterlands. Transporting goods between distant outposts across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron can be perilous and chaotic, meaning mislaid parcels occasionally require an alert passerby to step in and finish the delivery route properly.

Your Place In The World. In the Valley of Trials, untested recruits take their first steps toward honor and survival in Durotar. Kaltunk sends them straight to Gornek for basic combat training, beginning their service to the Horde. In Durotar's arid Valley of Trials, young orcs and Darkspear trolls prove their worth before entering the wider world. Under Warchief Thrall, life demands strength, vigilance, and discipline. Kaltunk evaluates every eager recruit, tempering dreams of wrestling demons and dragons with the practical duties ahead. Training begins in the canyon, where recruits learn humility before claiming glory.

Yowler's Paw. Yowler's Paw is the grisly trophy taken from Yowler, the ferocious pack leader of the gnolls menacing the hills above Lakeshire. Brought to the town artisan Verner Osgood, it serves as undeniable proof that the beast leading the local gnoll packs has been put down. The Redridge gnolls have long terrorized the heights surrounding Lake Everstill, their bloodcurdling howls echoing down into the settlement of Lakeshire. Among them, none is more feared than Yowler, the ruthless alpha driving their expansion. Because gnoll ears and paws are customary proof of bounties across the human territories, Verner Osgood asks brave adventurers to bring back Yowler's paw. Severing it marks not just the demise of an unusually cunning predator, but a deliberate move to shatter the chain of command among his disorganized followers.

Yvette Farthing. Yvette Farthing is a Forsaken resident of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, dwelling in the Gallows' End Tavern alongside her father, Coleman. Though she appears as hardened and detached as any of Sylvanas's people, she carries the lingering ghost of a mortal romance cut short by the Scourge. Before the Third War swept Lordaeron into ruin, Yvette was in love with Thurman Agamand, one of the heirs of the prosperous Agamand Mills. When the Scourge plague approached, Yvette and her father, Coleman, begged Thurman to abandon the estate and flee with them. Thurman refused out of devotion to his family's legacy. Both would eventually perish and rise into undeath, but while Yvette found a place among the free-willed Forsaken in Brill, Thurman's tragic final fate remained unknown to her.

Zalashji's Den. Zalashji's Den is a secluded cave tucked along the eastern coast of Tanaris. It serves as the solitary lair of Zalashji, an enigmatic naga who dwells far from the typical gathering grounds of his serpentine kin. Carved into the rugged bluffs along the eastern shoreline of Tanaris, this coastal cavern provides shelter to a single inhabitant: Zalashji. Naga are known across Kalimdor to gather in disciplined war parties or coastal outposts, yet Zalashji resides here entirely alone. Little is known about why he made this isolated cave his domain, far removed from the primary settlements and desert ruins of the region, but any traveler venturing along the surf should approach the cave mouth with caution.

Zalazane. On the Echo Isles, Zalazane's treachery has driven the Darkspear from their home. Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village sends Horde champions to end the witch doctor's rule. Dark magic drove Zalazane mad, and he enslaved his fellow tribesmen, seizing the Darkspear trolls' rightful home and forcing them into exile on Durotar's coast. The Darkspear made a home on the Echo Isles after fleeing their sunken island and following Thrall across the Great Sea. The isles lie just off Durotar's southeast coast. Zalazane, once a respected and powerful witch doctor of the tribe, hungered for power. He used hexes to enslave the minds of his kin and began a violent uprising. Vol'jin led the Darkspear who remained free, but they were driven from their ancestral camps across the water. They had to build a temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village.

Zalazane's Head. Master Gadrin awaits proof that Zalazane has fallen. The Darkspear seek relief from the witch doctor who drove them from the Echo Isles. Master Gadrin asks for proof that Zalazane is dead. The witch doctor betrayed the Darkspear and seized control of their island home with mind-enslaving hexes. His magic drove Vol'jin's people to the shores of Durotar. From the Echo Isles, Zalazane still sends hexed thralls across the water to seize more victims. Sen'jin Village needs proof that his rule has ended. Returning Zalazane's severed head confirms his defeat and gives the displaced tribe a measure of peace, with hope of reclaiming their stolen islands one day.

Zaldimar Wefhellt. On Goldshire's upper floor, Zaldimar Wefhellt teaches young mages their first spells. When they outgrow his lessons, he sends them to Stormwind City for further training. Upstairs at the Lion's Pride Inn, Zaldimar Wefhellt teaches novice mages the first arts of arcane, fire, and frost. When an apprentice outgrows those lessons, he sends them north to the Mage Quarter in Stormwind, where Jennea Cannon can teach them more.

Zamah's Note. Zamah's Note is a written dispatch sent from Zamah in Thunder Bluff across the Great Sea to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. It outlines an urgent request for an alchemical concoction capable of dealing with the Venture Company in the Stonetalon Mountains without relying on direct bloodshed. The goblin operations of the Venture Company have entrenched themselves deeply within the Stonetalon Mountains, deforesting and tearing up the sacred land. Zamah, seeking a specialized solution to dislodge them without inciting outright slaughter, turns to the expertise of the Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society. The note serves as formal correspondence detailing Stonetalon's dire situation to her colleague, Apothecary Lydon, stationed far away in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills of Lordaeron.

Zamek's Distraction. Zamek can create the diversion that Keeping Pace calls for. It comes while you are in the middle of that step, and Keeping Pace cannot be finished without it. While you are working through Keeping Pace, Zamek can create a diversion. When it happens, Rizzle leaves his hut, and the Indurium plans are left behind.

Zamja. In Orgrimmar’s Drag, Zamja teaches Horde travelers to cook. The Darkspear troll trains cooks to make meals from beasts of Kalimdor. Zamja works in the Drag, where she cuts meat and teaches Horde travelers to cook. Cooking helps travelers in the rugged lands of Durotar and the Barrens turn raw game into rations. Cooks who have mastered basic recipes can seek further training in Gadgetzan, to the south.

Zando'zan. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, promising rogues begin training with the Shattered Hand. Trainer Shenthul sends his chosen initiate to meet Zando'zan and enter the Horde's covert ranks. Orgrimmar's rulers know brute strength cannot win every war. Beneath the city, the Cleft of Shadow houses the Shattered Hand, a covert guild that handles espionage, sabotage, and theft for the Horde. When rogue trainer Shenthul sees promise in an initiate, he sends them to report to Zando'zan for dedicated operative training.

Zangen Stonehoof. Zangen Stonehoof is a tauren keeper situated at the High Rise bonfire in the heart of Thunder Bluff. Dutiful and revered among his peers, he faithfully tends to the central flames each evening while coordinating efforts to aid his distant kin across Kalimdor. Perched on the High Rise of Thunder Bluff, Zangen Stonehoof maintains the central communal bonfire that overlooks the city's highest bluffs. As twilight falls over Mulgore, Zangen kindles the fire, providing warmth and an enduring beacon for the tribes assembled beneath High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Beyond keeping the flames alight, he maintains ties with allies beyond Mulgore's mesa, acting as a liaison for spiritual and ritual endeavors taking place across the continent.

Zankaja. In Orgrimmar, young orc woman Zankaja waits anxiously for word of her mate, Dogran. He was assigned to duty at the Crossroads, along the dangerous frontier of the Barrens. Zankaja waits for news of Dogran, her mate, in Orgrimmar. Dogran earned a promotion and went south to bolster the outpost at the Crossroads in the Barrens. The assignment honors a warrior, but the frontier is harsh, with quilboar, centaur, and aggressive beasts. When Dogran failed to send word or return as expected, Zankaja began asking travelers to seek news of him.
